findings.strategy_name: Double Red — two consecutive bearish candles after a resistance test
findings.setup_summary: On a 5-min chart, after price tests a resistance level, wait for two consecutive bearish candles where the second closes lower than the first; enter a short (Put) at the close of the second bar with a horizon of 5-15 bars. Thesis is falsifiable: two lower-lower closes after a resistance tag, no wick or structure-break requirement.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: resistance test followed by two bearish bars, second closing below the first. Invalidated/blocked if the market is highly volatile or a major scheduled news event is imminent (book: 'Not suited for volatile markets. Do not use it when big news events are taking place.'); thesis dead if price reclaims back above the first red bar's high.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: next bar close after the second lower close (book's binary Put). No stop/target given; expiry 5-15 min in binary terms, which translates to an expiry_bars horizon. Regime gate: skip volatile markets and news windows.
findings.quote: The double red strategy is a short-term reversal system based on price action and resistance. The trade is planned on a 5-minute chart and is signaled when two bearish candles form following a test of resistance.
findings.chapter_anchor: Strategies #1: The Double Red Strategy
findings.mechanism: Two lower closes after a resistance rejection confirm seller control and predict continued downward drift; the resistance test gives the level a location anchor.
findings.notes: Candidate behavior family requiring a resistance-label feature (windowed extremes). Closest existing V8 family is failed_breakout (liquidity_vacuum_reentry); Double Red could be tested as a 2-bar-confirmation variant of it, but its mechanism claim (rejection momentum, no prior breakout failure) is distinct. The news/volatility gate is weaker in crypto perps (24/7, no single scheduled event, though high-impact macro releases do hit BTC).
findings.book: Top Binary Options Trading Strategies - Strategies of Pros Explained for Dummies

findings.strategy_name: Pinocchio — long-wick pin bar after an established trend, trade against the wick
findings.setup_summary: On a 1h or 4h chart, after an established trend (book shows an uptrend for the bearish version), a pin bar forms whose wick is at least 2x the size of its real body; trade the opposite direction of the wick (long upper wick after uptrend = short). The bar-level requirement is falsifiable: wick length >= 2 * body length, plus a prior-trend condition.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: long wick (>2x body) appearing after a trend. Invalidated/blocked if the market is neutral/choppy — a valid signal must come after a trend ('Trying to trade the bearish Pinocchio pattern in neutral market conditions can be risky'); also do not use a very short (60-sec) horizon.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: either immediately after the pin bar closes or as a limit at the 50% Fibonacci retracement of the pin bar's range (a limit-entry variant). Expiry 5-15 min in binary terms → expiry_bars in V8. No stop/target given in the book.
findings.quote: A Pinocchio bar is a candlestick bar that has a very small body and a very long wick (nose)... when the wick is longer than the body, this tells us that the market is deceiving us and that we should trade the opposite way!
findings.chapter_anchor: Strategies #2: The Pinocchio Strategy
findings.mechanism: An outsized wick at the end of a trend shows the push was rejected, implying exhaustion of the directional move; the market then reverses toward the body/close side.
findings.notes: Directly transferable to BTCUSDT 1h wicks (wick/body ratio needs an ATR-relative or fixed-ratio measure). Caveat: crypto wicks are frequently liquidation cascades rather than deliberate rejection, so the prior-trend requirement is load-bearing. The claimed 68% win rate in the book has no statistical backing. The 50% fib-retrace limit entry variant maps to a limit-entry option in risk_geometry.
findings.book: Top Binary Options Trading Strategies - Strategies of Pros Explained for Dummies

findings.strategy_name: 1-2-3 trend reversal — failed higher high confirmed by a break of the prior swing low
findings.setup_summary: After an uptrend or strong move up, mark the first peak (1); if a counter-move begins, mark its bottom (2); if the next up-move fails to exceed point 1 and turns down, mark its high (3). Enter short only when price breaks below the point-2 low. All conditions are observable on the pattern timeframe: lower high (3<1) then structure break.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: complete 1-2-3 swing structure (lower high after a peak) plus a close below the point-2 swing low. Invalidated if price reverses back above point 3, or if point 3 exceeds point 1 (no lower high → no pattern).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close through the point-2 low. Expiry set equal to the pattern timeframe; book risk rule: 'better to open two trades with smaller expiry times than 1 trade with longer expiry times' — a risk/lifecycle rule preferring split shorter-horizon exposure over one long-horizon bet. No stop/target given.
findings.quote: If the new move up does not surpass point 1 and starts turning down, mark the highest point of this new move up with (3)... the price must move down to break the low created at point (2). If that happens, all our conditions are met, and we enter the trade with a 'Put'.
findings.chapter_anchor: Strategies #3: The 1-2-3 Strategy
findings.mechanism: A failed higher high signals weakening of the prior trend; the subsequent break of the intermediate swing low confirms trend reversal and provides a clean structure-defined trigger.
findings.notes: Swing-point labeling (points 1-3) can reuse V8's windowed-extreme machinery. The 'two shorter trades over one long trade' rule is a candidate risk_rule/lifecycle_rule for V8 (exposure splitting by horizon) distinct from the one-exposure-per-direction invariant. Symmetric long version implied for downtrends, though the book only draws the bearish case.
findings.book: Top Binary Options Trading Strategies - Strategies of Pros Explained for Dummies

findings.strategy_name: Session-overlap timing — trade high-volume hours, avoid flat off-peak sessions
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable regime claim: when the London/NY and Asia/London sessions overlap there is higher volume, higher volatility and clearer directional movement; during off-peak hours volume is thin and markets are flat/directionless. The book further claims Tuesday/Wednesday are the most active days and Friday's EU/US overlap is high-volatility, with the second half of Friday unpredictable.
findings.trigger_invalidation: This is a filter, not a directional signal: it gates WHEN to trade (overlap hours, Tue/Wed/Fri-EU/US), not direction. Invalidated regime = off-peak / holiday hours where volume and range contract.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target — pure timing regime. Maps to a time-based feature/regime gate on participation.
findings.quote: The binary options market is most active when there is an overlap of the London/New York and Asia/London sessions... During off-peak hours, there is little volume and less price movement, resulting in flat and directionless markets.
findings.chapter_anchor: Fundamentals — Timing: Best time for trading
findings.mechanism: Liquidity and participation cluster at session boundaries, producing cleaner directional moves; thin hours produce noise-dominated, range-bound price action.
findings.notes: Crypto perps trade 24/7 with no session close, so the London/NY overlap framing transfers only partially; however realized volume/volatility on BTC still clusters around US/EU daytime hours and thins on weekends, and funding-period mechanics add their own structure. Claim is stated as 'our research' with no statistics — evidence class NARRATIVE. Candidate input to the existing 'time' feature group.
findings.book: Top Binary Options Trading Strategies - Strategies of Pros Explained for Dummies

findings.strategy_name: Higher-timeframe trend confirmation — confirm trend one or two levels above the execution timeframe
findings.setup_summary: Methodology rule: use a candlestick chart of a bigger timeframe than the expiry/execution timeframe to confirm the trend — at least 1h for pattern recognition, and 1h/4h to confirm the view when trading 15-30 min horizons; the 1-min chart gives entry/exit signals while 15-min and hourly charts confirm trend and support/resistance. Also 'use hourly chart to understand the underlying trend' even for the shortest 60-sec horizon.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not a directional setup; it prescribes the TF hierarchy: entry signals on the execution TF must be aligned with trend context on the next 1-2 TFs up. Falsifiable as a filter: entries taken without higher-TF trend alignment are the negative case.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target. Methodological constraint on signal validity, not a position geometry rule.
findings.quote: In order to confirm a trend, use a candlestick chart with a bigger time frame than the one you use to decide your expiry time. it is usually recommended to use a time frame of at least 1 hour for chart pattern recognition.
findings.chapter_anchor: Fundamentals — Expiry time: What time-frame to use for the pattern recognition
findings.mechanism: Short-horizon price action is noisy; requiring the entry-timeframe signal to align with trend context on a higher timeframe raises the prior probability of continuation and filters counter-trend noise.
findings.notes: Directly supports the existing trend_pullback expert's trend requirement and motivates a MarketState design where trend is computed on the confirmation TF (1-2 levels above the entry TF) as a PIT feature, reinforcing the no-wal-clock / PIT discipline. This is a lesson reinforcing architecture, not a new expert.
findings.book: Top Binary Options Trading Strategies - Strategies of Pros Explained for Dummies

book_title: Top Binary Options Trading Strategies - Strategies of Pros Explained for Dummies

findings.strategy_name: Triple Screen multi-timeframe trend confluence
findings.mechanism: countertrend exhaustion within a dominant higher-timeframe trend reverts to the trend direction
findings.setup_summary: Identify the trend on the timeframe one order of magnitude above the trading chart (factor ~5, e.g. weekly for daily, 4h/1d for a 1h trading chart) using EMA slope and/or MACD-Histogram slope; trade only in that direction or stand aside. On the trading chart, enter countertrend pullbacks when a short-term oscillator (5-day Stochastic, or 2-day EMA of Force Index) is oversold (long) or overbought (short); entry is a stop order above the prior day's high (long) or below the prior day's low (short). The higher-timeframe screen acts as a censor that removes one of the three choices (buy, sell, stand aside).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalidates if the higher-timeframe trend gate flips (weekly MACD-Histogram/EMA slope reverses); countertrend oscillator entries must be refreshed, never chased when already extended; entering when both timeframes trend the same direction is discouraged as 'hopping aboard a moving train'.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: buy-stop above the prior trading-chart bar high (long) or sell-stop below the prior bar low (short), or a limit placed at the depth of the average of recent penetrations below the EMA; stop: in the vicinity of the latest swing low/high; target: the opposite channel line (the book uses a channel containing 90-95% of recent prices); expiry: governed by the higher-timeframe trend gate.
findings.quote: The Triple Screen trading system begins by identifying the trend on a chart one order of magnitude greater than the one you are planning to trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7 (Trading Systems), Q 7-2, 7-5 to 7-9; Answers 7-2, 7-6, 7-8; also Answer 4-7
findings.notes: Canonical Elder multi-timeframe system; the factor-of-5 timeframe rule is directly transferable to 24/7 perp crypto (e.g. 1h trading chart with 4h or 1d gate). Maps onto V8's trend_pullback expert as a refinement: add a higher-timeframe trend gate (EMA/MACD slope) and a short-term oscillator trigger, with a buy-stop above the prior bar high. Book explicitly states the purpose is to resolve conflicting timeframes, which matches V8's multi-clock/regime discipline.
findings.book: The New Trading for a Living (Study Guide) 2014

findings.strategy_name: 2% Rule + 6% Rule + Iron Triangle sizing
findings.mechanism: percent-capped dollar risk per trade and a monthly equity heat cap prevent ruin and force a cooling-off review
findings.setup_summary: Maximum dollar risk per trade is 2% of account equity, and that 2% must also absorb slippage and commissions (Iron Triangle: total acceptable dollar risk / risk-per-share from entry to stop = maximum position size). If realized plus open-trade losses for the month reach 6% of month-start equity, stop trading for the rest of the month, review the system, and return next month at reduced size, scaling back up only after performance goals are met.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not a market-timing rule; the ceiling recomputes each month from month-start equity — profits are not counted against the 6% heat cap, only realized losses and amounts at risk in open trades.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: per trade; stop: defined per trade, the rule sizes so that (entry - stop) x size <= 2% equity including costs; hard lifecycle cap: 6% monthly equity drawdown stops all trading for the month; after a severe drawdown, lower the risk fraction and increase size in steps.
findings.quote: The 2% Rule dictates your maximum dollar risk per trade. Two percent of a $28,000 account is $560, which must cover not only your risk but also slippage and commissions.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9 (Risk Management), Q 9-4, 9-8, 9-12, 9-14 to 9-17; Afterword (monthly 6% stop)
findings.notes: Book asserts these rules are 'proven by experience' (Q 9-6: never meet a margin call, never average down, first mistake is cheapest, liquidate worst position first). The 2% per-trade cap and 6% monthly stop map directly onto V8's RiskGate deterministic admission and heat cap; the 6% monthly rule is a lifecycle_rule candidate. Book also warns stops can gap (Answer 9-11) and that leverage (futures margins as low as 5%, Answer 8-10) makes these caps mandatory.
findings.book: The New Trading for a Living (Study Guide) 2014

findings.strategy_name: False breakout reversion
findings.mechanism: liquidity vacuum left by a failed breakout pulls price back through the level
findings.setup_summary: After a congestion zone, price breaks below support to a new low; when the downmove stalls (stops making new lows) and price closes back inside the zone or above the previously broken support line, go long with a protective stop near the latest low. Symmetric for shorts: a false upside breakout to a new high that fails and falls back below the broken resistance gives a sell signal. Short-bar failures at the breakout indicate the move is losing force and the reversion is more likely.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If price keeps making new lows/highs after the false breakout (real breakout resuming), the reversion thesis is invalid; a breakout that never re-enters the congestion zone is a genuine breakout, not a false one.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close back above the broken support / into the congestion zone (long), or below the broken resistance (short); stop: below the recent low (near the false-breakout extreme), not at the obvious breakout level; target: the opposite edge of the congestion zone; once the re-entry bar stalls, tighten the stop toward breakeven.
findings.quote: False breakouts are the bane of amateurs, but professional traders love them. They often wait until a downside breakout stops making new lows and then trade against it: buy and place a protective stop near the latest low.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3 (Classical Chart Analysis), Q 3-7, 3-8, 3-10; Answers 3-7, 3-8, 3-10
findings.notes: Confirms and refines the existing V8 failed_breakout expert (mechanism liquidity_vacuum_reentry). Book adds two refinements: (1) 'wait for the breakout to stop making new extremes' as the entry confirmation, and (2) trading the re-entry into the congestion zone in both directions (the V8 expert is currently SHORT-only). False-breakout signals are frequent on 24/7 perp markets around technical levels.
findings.book: The New Trading for a Living (Study Guide) 2014

findings.strategy_name: Kangaroo tail recoil
findings.mechanism: a single-bar rejected price extreme protruding from congestion creates recoil back into the zone
findings.setup_summary: A single bar protrudes from a compact congestion area, leaving a long wick (a 'kangaroo tail') that marks a rejected high or low; markets tend to recoil away from the tail. Tail pointing up -> sell (or take profits on longs); tail pointing down -> buy. The stop is placed midway down the tail, not below its tip, because a stop below the tip exposes the trade to too much risk. After the tail, one may add on the next bar that trades in the trade direction and take profits when the move stalls.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalidates if price closes back beyond the tail's extreme (rejection fails and the level holds); recoil is expected away from the tail direction back into the congestion zone.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on the bar trading away from a tail protruding from congestion, with optional add on the next bar in the trade direction; stop: midway down the tail (book explicitly prohibits a stop below the tip as too wide); target: take profits when the move stops making new highs (longs) / new lows (shorts), i.e. opposite side of congestion.
findings.quote: Tails show that either a high or a low price level has been rejected by the mass of market participants. Since markets tend to move away from rejected price levels, it pays to trade in the direction opposite a tail.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3 (Classical Chart Analysis), Q 3-12, 3-13; Answers 3-12, 3-13
findings.notes: Distinct from the existing liquidity_sweep_reclaim expert (which requires the wick extreme to be a windowed prior extreme reclaimed by close): kangaroo tail is a single-bar rejection from within compact congestion with a distinctive stop-at-mid-tail rule. Book notes some vehicles are more tail-prone than others (Answer 3-12). On perp crypto, long wicks are often liquidation cascades rather than pure rejection, so the mechanism may need a venue-microstructure qualifier before formalizing; test as a challenger variant of sweep_reclaim first.
findings.book: The New Trading for a Living (Study Guide) 2014

findings.strategy_name: Impulse system (EMA + MACD-Histogram censorship filter)
findings.mechanism: agreement between market inertia (EMA slope) and market power (MACD-Histogram slope) defines a directional censorship regime
findings.setup_summary: Compute the slope of a fast EMA (market inertia) and the slope of the last two bars of MACD-Histogram (market power). Both rising -> green, shorting prohibited; both falling -> red, buying prohibited; contradictory slopes -> blue, both directions permitted. Used as a censorship/regime gate, not an automatic entry system: its best signals come when the red or green color disappears (e.g., red turning non-red completes a double bottom and suggests buying; green disappearing near the end of an upswing suggests taking profits).
findings.trigger_invalidation: The filter flips when either slope changes sign; the book explicitly warns that automating the color-consistent states produces multiple whipsaws (e.g., between bars C and G in Q 7-12), so the actionable signal is the disappearance of red/green, not sustained color.
findings.risk_geometry: Not an entry-timing system; a gate only. Entries are taken with other tools within the permitted direction; no stop/target specified by the system itself.
findings.quote: The primary role of the Impulse system is not to tell traders when to buy or sell. Rather, it shows them when they're prohibited from buying or shorting.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7 (Trading Systems), Q 7-10 to 7-13; Answers 7-10, 7-11, 7-12
findings.notes: Fully price-derived (EMA slope + MACD-Histogram slope), so directly computable on BTCUSDT 1h perp data. For V8 this is a regime/censorship filter candidate rather than an expert: it could gate which directions existing experts may emit, matching the book's framing. Key methodological caveat from the book: the sustained-color states whipsaw if automated; only the disappearance of red/green is a clean signal - so it should be wired as a state-transition filter, not a level filter.
findings.book: The New Trading for a Living (Study Guide) 2014

book_title: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained: An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading (Michael Thomsett, Ethan Hathaway Co Ltd, 2012/2013)

findings.strategy_name: Failed breakout / failed test of range border reverses
findings.mechanism: A failed test of the trading-range border (resistance or support) shows the controlling side lacks momentum, so price is most likely to move in the opposite direction; a failed breakout above resistance often carries price all the way through the opposite border.
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: after price breaks above a windowed resistance level and then closes back below it within N bars (failed breakout), expect movement in the opposite direction — enter SHORT on the failed-breakout bar close with the prior high frozen as reference; mirror for a failed test of support (LONG). The China Railway example generalizes the book's rule: a failed upside breakout preceded a strong move that broke through the opposite border (support).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close pierces the frozen range border then closes back inside the range within N bars. Invalidation: close re-crosses and holds beyond the failed border (thesis dead); the book also warns any breakout can 'reverse so that prices return to the established trading range', so a false-failure re-breakout must kill the trade.
findings.risk_geometry: entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE on the failure bar; stop just beyond the frozen prior_high/prior_low ref; target 1.0R+ toward the opposite range border; expiry in bars; still_valid = close stays on the failure side of the frozen ref.
findings.quote: A failed test of resistance or support is most likely to lead to price movement in the opposite direction.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 1 Seg 1 (technical indicator areas); Part 2 Seg 4 (resistance and support; China Railway failed breakout)
findings.notes: Directly corroborates the active failed_breakout expert (SHORT variant). Book adds the proximity principle (signals at range borders are strongest) and the double/triple top = repeated failed resistance tests as variants of the same family. No statistical support given; reliability asserted by practitioner narrative.
findings.book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

findings.strategy_name: MA-touch mid-trend entry (pullback to rising average)
findings.mechanism: In a confirmed uptrend with the moving average below price, a pullback that touches the rising MA is a low-risk continuation entry because the MA acts as dynamic support where the controlling side resumes.
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h with an established uptrend (price above rising MA; trend confirmed by another indicator), when price falls and touches the rising slow MA, enter LONG on the next bar close; the book further requires uptrend confirmation and recommends treating the touch as an add-to-position point. Exit signal: when the MA crosses above price / curls, the uptrend is likely over and the position should be closed.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: MA below price, price dips to the MA, uptrend still confirmed. Invalidation: MA line moves through and above price (book: 'sold the entire position... wait for new signals'), or the retracement exceeds the pullback swing low.
findings.risk_geometry: entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after MA touch; stop below the pullback swing low or an ATR multiple; target 1.0R+ or prior high; expiry in bars; still_valid = close holds above the rising MA.
findings.quote: When MA is below price, as price falls and touches the MA, if the uptrend is confirmed, this point may be used to increase the size of the open position.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 8 Seg 4 (mid-trend entry, China Foods); Part 5 Seg 1 (20-day/200-day MA)
findings.notes: Corroborates the active trend_pullback expert (ema_fast>ema_slow and close<ema_slow). The book frames the touch as continuation/add rather than entry, which is a risk-geometry variant V8 can test against the existing pullback trigger. Practitioner heuristic, no statistics.
findings.book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

findings.strategy_name: Fibonacci retracement continuation zones
findings.mechanism: After a primary impulse, counter-trend retracement tends to terminate at 23.6%/38.2%/61.8% of the impulse, after which the primary trend resumes; a reversal signal at a fib level marks the resumption point.
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: after a measurable impulse leg (top-to-bottom extremes), compute 23.6/38.2/61.8% retracement levels of that leg; expect retracement to stall at one of them. Book procedure: look for a reversal signal at 23.6%, if none walk to 38.2%, then 61.8%; enter in the primary-trend direction only when a reversal signal actually appears at the level. No reversal signal anywhere in the pullback suggests it is a retracement, not a reversal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pullback reaches a fib level AND an independent reversal signal prints there. Invalidation: price closes beyond the 61.8% level — the move is likely a trend change, not a retracement.
findings.risk_geometry: entry on reversal-signal bar close at a fib zone; stop beyond the fib level; target trend continuation (next fib level or new extreme); expiry in bars; frozen impulse refs per PIT.
findings.quote: Analysts expect retracement to occur at specific percentages against the prevailing trend. ... the key Fibonacci ratios of 23.6%, 38.2%, and 61.8%
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 4 Seg 1 (Bollinger Bands and Fibonacci Retracement; Radio Shack examples)
findings.notes: Fib levels are self-referential (no independent causal claim) but are widely watched, so they can serve as entry-zone features for the trend_pullback family rather than a standalone expert. Book folds this into the retracement-vs-reversal decision, which V8 encodes as a dead-thesis distinction.
findings.book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

findings.strategy_name: Bollinger band fade: buy lower band, sell middle band
findings.mechanism: Price touching the statistical band (2 std devs) reverts toward the 20-session EMA; band breadth itself measures volatility state, so the trade only makes sense inside a range regime.
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: with Bollinger(20,2), buy when price touches the lower band and sell/exit when price returns to the middle band; sell when price reaches the upper band and buy to close at the middle band. The book notes that when price exceeds the highest average after a period of band narrowing, it 'is expected to level out', i.e. band touch in a narrowing-then-expanding regime flags exhaustion.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close touches the outer band (or wick touches and the body stays inside). Invalidation: trend takeover — price rides the band / closes beyond it with band breadth expanding; then the band is a trend-persistence signal, not a reversion edge.
findings.risk_geometry: entry on band-touch bar close; stop beyond the band edge (e.g., 1 ATR past the band); target the middle band; short expiry; still_valid = price remains inside the band envelope.
findings.quote: a swing trader may buy when the low average is touched by price, and sell when the middle band is touched; or sell when price reaches the top and buy to close at the middle.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 4 Seg 1 (Bollinger Bands)
findings.notes: Mean reversion against a trend is dangerous in 24/7 trending perps; the trade needs a range/regime filter (band persistence), which maps to V8's regime-filter concept. The book itself only frames this inside a range context. Falsifiable and cheap to screen on 1h data once a range regime filter exists.
findings.book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

findings.strategy_name: Over-reaction swing fade (exaggerated move corrects in 1-3 sessions)
findings.mechanism: Reactions to news/events are exaggerated and self-correct: the overshoot beyond the typical range is not a trend, and price reverts to the established range within one to three sessions.
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: when a single session pushes price well outside its recent typical breadth (e.g., >N ATR excursion beyond a short-window range) or away from the established trading range, fade it — enter against the excursion and exit when price returns into the range, expecting completion within 1-3 sessions. The book's swing-timing rule: entry when price moves away from the typical daily breadth, exit on return to normal levels; this works best in moderately volatile names, poorly in highly volatile ones.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: excursion bar close beyond a frozen range threshold. Invalidation: no reversion into the range within the 1-3 session window (trend extension), or a second strong excursion bar in the same direction; book notes swing timing is hard in high-volatility issues.
findings.risk_geometry: entry on excursion bar close; stop beyond the excursion extreme (or 1 ATR past it); target the range re-entry edge; expiry short (1-3 sessions per the book's correction window); still_valid = price has not broken to a new range.
findings.quote: those exaggerated movements tend to self-correct within one to three trading sessions
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 1 Seg 3 (random walk critique); Part 8 Seg 2 (swing timing; CA Inc. entry/exit examples)
findings.notes: Leverage and liquidation cascades in perps generate frequent overshoot wicks, and the 24/7 no-gap tape makes the fade executable at the excursion close. This is the strongest mean-reversion candidate in the book for crypto. Distinct from bollinger_band_reversion (band-instrument trigger vs event/excursion trigger). The book's own caveat (fades work in 'isolated moments when price movement is extreme') supports gating this behind a volatility filter.
findings.book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

findings.strategy_name: Volume spike as reversal warning / climax confirmation
findings.mechanism: A single-session volume spike far above the typical range signals that the controlling side's conviction is exhausted, marking likely reversal when confirmed by price/momentum signals; volume 'precedes a strong reversal'.
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: a session whose volume jumps far above the recent average (e.g., >Mx the 20-session mean) and then immediately returns to prior levels is a reversal warning — not a standalone entry, but a confirmation gate: 'exceptionally high volume in a single trading session is a key reversal warning', to be confirmed by price/candlestick/momentum. Book also defines the spike as non-recurring: volume returns to previous levels and does not repeat.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: volume > Mx windowed mean at/near a trend extreme or range border. Invalidation: spike without any price-pattern or oscillator confirmation (book repeatedly shows confirmed volume signals that failed); treat as no-signal rather than fade.
findings.risk_geometry: no standalone geometry — a participation feature consumed as confirmation for candlestick/breakout candidates and as a trigger feature for the backlog capitulation family; volume comparison must be PIT (no future bars).
findings.quote: exceptionally high volume in a single trading session is a key reversal warning. This should be confirmed by other indicators
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 1 Seg 1; Part 6 Seg 1 (volume indicators; spike definition)
findings.notes: Corroborates the DATA_BLOCKED capitulation backlog family (capitulation_exhaustion). Crypto caveat: volume must be aggregated across venues/derivatives tapes and taker-flow based; single-venue 1h volume is a biased proxy. Book gives no statistics — reliability claims are anecdotal.
findings.book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

findings.strategy_name: ATR contraction as trend-slowdown early warning
findings.mechanism: ATR measures conviction through session ranges; when range declines while the trend continues, the controlling side is losing enthusiasm and trend reversal is likely to precede other reversal signals.
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: compute ATR(14) (or the windowed high-low range); if price keeps making trend-direction extremes but ATR contracts (declining slope over a window), the trend is slowing. The book's Exxon Mobil example: price shows no weakening but the strong ATR decline confirms likely near-term reversal. Operationally: a negative ATR-slope regime while a trend-following candidate is open should weaken/terminate that candidate.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: ATR slope negative over W bars while trend still extends. Invalidation: ATR slope flattens/rises (momentum rebuilding) or price breaks the range decisively (ATR contraction then expansion on the same side = continuation).
findings.risk_geometry: no entry — a lifecycle/regime rule: candidate dead-thesis (still_valid=false) or size/heat reduction for trend_pullback-type experts when the volatility contraction condition holds; frozen ATR window per PIT.
findings.quote: If the range begins to decline as the trend evolves, it provides a forecast that the trend may be slowing down. This 'early warning' often precedes other reversal or momentum signals.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 6 Seg 1 (ATR; Exxon Mobil example)
findings.notes: Cleanly falsifiable: it is a pure function of the price tape already in MarketState (volatility group). This gives V8 a deterministic still_valid refinement for trend-pullback episodes without adding a new active expert. Book asserts ATR ranges rise with 'enthusiasm'; no statistics given.
findings.book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

findings.strategy_name: Oscillator divergence as leading weakness signal
findings.mechanism: When price and a momentum oscillator diverge (price new high, oscillator lower high), the trend is not confirmed and is probably weak; divergence acts as a leading warning that reversal confirmation should be sought.
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: price makes a new high while RSI(14) makes a lower high (bullish divergence = uptrend weak), or price makes a new low while RSI makes a higher low (bearish divergence = downtrend weak). Book rule: divergence alone is a warning to look for confirming price-pattern/candlestick exit or entry signals — 'The failure of RSI to confirm the new high levels in the price movement was the revealing signal that the trend was losing its momentum.' Divergence is most meaningful when it occurs near overbought/oversold extremes (RSI 70/30).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: new price extreme paired with a non-confirming oscillator extreme over the lookback window. Invalidation: oscillator re-confirms price (convergence) or crossover absent — book explicitly warns leading indicators give false whipsaw signals; divergence at mid-range is weaker than divergence near extremes.
findings.risk_geometry: no standalone entry — a confirmation/gating feature (response group) for candlestick and Western reversal candidates; trigger requires the extreme window to be frozen per PIT.
findings.quote: Bullish divergence means that an uptrend is not confirmed by the oscillator, in which case the uptrend is probably weak.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 6 Seg 2 (convergence and divergence; Wal-Mart example); Part 7 Seg 1 (RSI)
findings.notes: On fast 1h crypto tape, RSI divergence is noisy and the book itself flags whipsaw/false-signal risk for leading indicators — so V8 should use it only as a confirmation input, never a standalone trigger. No statistics; the book frames divergence as 'rare enough that when it does appear, it should not be ignored.'
findings.book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

findings.strategy_name: Trailing stop and stop-loss bail-out rules
findings.mechanism: A stop that trails price by a fixed distance protects accumulated profit while capping loss; a fixed stop-loss activates at a preset price but does not guarantee execution at that price.
findings.setup_summary: Book's concrete rules: (a) stop-loss = sell order triggered at a preset price (e.g., 10% below entry); (b) trailing stop = fixed distance below each new extreme (e.g., 10% below each day's high) — while price rises the stop ratchets up; once price retraces the full distance, exit is generated automatically. Partial-exit variant: pre-set exit points (e.g., close 1/10 of position at each +5%, close all at -10%).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price retraces the trailing distance from the most recent extreme; or price hits the fixed bail-out level. Invalidation: no trailing in place / stop distance not updated at each new extreme; book warns the stop-loss trigger price is not a guaranteed fill ('by the time it was executed, the price had declined to 7.50').
findings.risk_geometry: stop distance = 10% of entry or of the running extreme (book default) — in V8 an ATR-multiple variant; stop refs frozen at bar close per PIT; exit on the trailing-stop bar; combined with per-trade exposure limit (book example: no more than ~10% of capital per trade).
findings.quote: If the stock's price rises, the trailing stop is adjusted to a specified percentage or amount below. As soon as it declines to the 10% level, a sale is generated automatically.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 8 Seg 4 (stop loss and trailing stop orders; partial exit; RIM gap example)
findings.notes: In 24/7 crypto there are no exchange overnight gaps, so a resting stop is triggered at (near) its level rather than gapping through — this is a genuine improvement over the book's equity-tape caveat. However, the 10% flat distance is crude for high-leverage perps; an ATR-multiple trailing variant is the natural V8 adaptation. Book's trailing-stop-as-profit-protection concept fits the RiskGate/stop family without expanding the active-expert budget.
findings.book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

findings.strategy_name: Multi-indicator independent confirmation gate
findings.mechanism: No single indicator is reliable; requiring two or more independent signal families to agree raises the hit rate of reversal timing, and contradiction between equally strong indicators is itself actionable (do not act).
findings.setup_summary: The book's central thesis, stated repeatedly: every signal (price pattern, candlestick, volume, oscillator) must be confirmed by an independent indicator before acting. Rules: (1) do not act when two equally strong indicators contradict; (2) weight the stronger indicator; (3) wait for a third confirming indicator when signals conflict. Confirmation can also be continuation confirmation (do not exit a valid trend) — the book treats false exits as a first-order failure mode.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — this is a methodology invariant, not a trade trigger; its falsifiable component is the claim that confirmed signals fail less often, which V8 can test by comparing episode outcomes with vs without cross-feature-group confirmation.
findings.risk_geometry: none — a candidate-generation gate: emit CandidateDraft only when the primary trigger is corroborated by an independent feature group (e.g., candlestick + volume + response), and suppress emission when two equally strong groups disagree.
findings.quote: No signal provides enough by itself to act upon with confidence. Always seek confirmation before you act.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 8 (entire part: 'why is confirmation the key process'); Part 1 Seg 2
findings.notes: Directly relevant to V8's candidate-generation contract: the book's confirmation discipline maps to requiring cross-feature-group confluence in MarketState before CandidateDraft, and 'contradiction -> do not act' maps to an explicit suppression rule. The book repeatedly documents strong confirmed signals that failed anyway (eBay, Kraft, Wal-Mart), which is itself the evidence for V8's stance that no gate removes falsification risk.
findings.book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

findings.strategy_name: Pyramiding / position scaling on continuation
findings.mechanism: Increasing position size on confirmed continuation (at retracement end, breakout-with-continuation, or MA touch) increases profit potential; the added exposure also increases loss risk proportionally.
findings.setup_summary: The book's three timing methods for adding size: (a) add at the recognized end of a retracement; (b) add when price breaks out of the trading range with continuation signals (flip confirms new support); (c) add when price in an uptrend touches the rising MA. The book is explicit that this 'contradicts most technical assumptions of fixed position size' and that 'when open positions are increased, a greater risk of loss also occurs.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A as an active V8 strategy: conflicts with V8 rule 16 (one active exposure per instrument+direction). The compatible subset is partial-profit tranche exits (sell 1/10 per +5% increment) which is a lifecycle exit variant, not new exposure.
findings.risk_geometry: would require adding exposure units to the ExposureBook mid-episode; each added unit needs its own stop/target; rule-16 change would require a registry decision with an authority receipt.
findings.quote: Techniques for increasing position size are called pyramid systems or pyramiding. ... when open positions are increased, a greater risk of loss also occurs.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 8 Seg 4 (mid-trend entry; pyramid systems; greed and panic)
findings.notes: Pyramiding violates the one-exposure-per-direction invariant; it can only enter V8 through a registry experiment that beats the single-exposure baseline on frozen OOS, per rule 16. The partial-profit-tranche exit, however, is compatible today as a lifecycle exit variant and is explicitly in the book ('set two exit points for any position... grows by 5%, one-tenth of the position will be closed').
findings.book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

findings.strategy_name: Support/resistance role flip (breakout validation by retest)
findings.mechanism: A level that previously stopped price becomes the origin of demand/supply after a flip: prior resistance becomes new support after an upside breakout, and prior support becomes new resistance after a downside breakout; the retest of the flipped level validates the breakout.
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: after an upside breakout establishes a new, higher range, the old resistance level should act as support — a retest that holds (close stays above the flipped level) validates the breakout and is the entry; mirror for downside where old support becomes resistance. The Coca-Cola example: 'price levels broke through resistance and established a new, higher trading range. The previous resistance price became the new support price.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: breakout beyond a windowed range border, then price returns to the border zone (retest) and holds on the new side. Invalidation: the retest closes back through the flipped level (the 'failed breakout' branch of the family applies instead — the level did not flip).
findings.risk_geometry: entry on retest bar close on the flipped side; stop beyond the flipped level; target continuation to a new range; still_valid = close remains on the flipped side; frozen flip-level ref per PIT.
findings.quote: It often occurs that previous resistance becomes new support in an upside breakout; or that previous support becomes resistance in a downside breakout.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 1 Seg 1 (b. tests of resistance and support); Part 2 Seg 4 (resistance and support; the 'flip'); Part 3 Seg 2 (flip confirmation)
findings.notes: This is the core thesis of the DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family and is intimately related to the active liquidity_sweep_reclaim expert ('stays on reclaimed side'). The book's flip is the retest-after-breakout validation that gives breakout_retest its still_valid semantics. In perps, the flipped level often coincides with a liquidity wall, so the location+liquidity feature groups are the natural input.
findings.book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

findings.strategy_name: Double Bollinger Band trend/range regime filter
findings.mechanism: Price confinement between the 1-SD and 2-SD Bollinger bands indicates an active trend; confinement inside the 1-SD bands indicates a range, so band-zone residence discriminates trend vs range regimes and their direction
findings.setup_summary: On daily charts, plot two sets of Bollinger Bands (20-period center MA, one at 1 SD and one at 2 SD, excluding center lines). When a pair closes the NY session (4pm ET) between the upper 1-SD and 2-SD bands it is in an uptrend; between the lower 1-SD and 2-SD bands, a downtrend; confined within the 1-SD bands = range. Only band-zone residence is a tradable trend state; when all four bands converge the pair is range trading.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A daily close that exits the trend zone back inside the 1-SD (range) zone signals trend exhaustion; corroborating filter: ADX above 25 and rising confirms trend, ADX falling below 25 implies exhaustion/range.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop on the filter itself; it feeds the retrace-in-trend, new-trend and exhaustion-reversal setups; trend-exhaustion signal = close outside the trend zone.
findings.quote: If the currency pair is trading between the upper one and two standard deviation bands, it is in an uptrend, and if it was trading between the two lower bands, it is in a downtrend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, 'Bollinger Band Basics' and 'Knowing When the Trend Has Exhausted'
findings.notes: Corroborated in the same book by the ADX>25 trend filter (Chapter 7). For 24/7 crypto the 'NY session close' must be replaced by a fixed calendar bar close (e.g., 00:00 UTC) and band zones are computed on rolling windows; no exchange gaps but weekend volume drops must be tolerated.
findings.book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

findings.strategy_name: Bollinger first-band pullback in trend (value entry)
findings.mechanism: In an ongoing trend the mean-reverting pullback to the inner 1-SD band marks a value level where continuation participants re-enter
findings.setup_summary: Daily chart. Uptrend established (price between upper 1-SD and 2-SD bands): wait for price to retrace to the upper 1-SD band, enter LONG on the daily close; stop slightly below the 15-period SMA. Downtrend: wait for rally to the lower 1-SD band, enter SHORT on the close, stop slightly above the 15-day MA. Do not take the trade if the candle closes outside the band.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A close outside the relevant band invalidates the entry; if the pair closes out of the trend zone entirely, the trend thesis is broken.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close (book: daily NY 4-5pm EST close); stop: beyond 15-day SMA; T1 = conservative 30-60 pips, exit half, move stop to breakeven; trail remainder (30-pip trailing stop); T2 further away; positions typically held overnight.
findings.quote: In an uptrend, the way to find value is to wait for the currency pair to dip and retrace to the upper first standard deviation Bollinger Band. At that point, if we were looking to join the trend, we could go long with a stop placed slightly below the 15-day Simple Moving Average.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, 'Finding Value within a Trend'
findings.notes: Anecdotal hit evidence: 8 value buys in a June-July 2010 GBP/USD uptrend, prior trend continued in all but one (small sample). This is a refinement/variant of the existing trend_pullback family: the BB 1-SD band replaces the ema_fast>ema_slow cross as the pullback definition and the stop is the 15-period SMA instead of an ATR multiple; for crypto 'daily close' becomes a fixed-UTC bar close.
findings.book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

findings.strategy_name: New-trend entry on close into the outer band zone
findings.mechanism: A daily close out of the range zone into the 1-SD-to-2-SD band zone marks the start of a new trend that tends to persist for days, but a first occurrence may only be a 24-hour continuation
findings.setup_summary: Daily chart, close of the session. When a pair that was confined inside the 1-SD range zone closes into the uptrend zone (upper 1-SD to 2-SD bands) enter LONG; a close into the lower zone enter SHORT. Book records both a one-day failed continuation and a repeat close that produced a near-month-long trend, so the entry is taken each time but always managed with T1-T2.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If the pair moves ~60 pips against entry it has re-entered the range zone and the new-trend thesis failed (book: when a trade went against her by more than 60 pips it was stopped 97% of the time).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: session-close bar; stop: 60 pips fixed (refined from 70; the 'sweet spot' for this setup); T1 = 30-60 pips on half, stop to breakeven; trail remainder; positions held 1-12 hours, sometimes overnight with stop and both targets set; book also refuses pairs with spread wider than 6 pips.
findings.quote: At some point it had to get into the bands first, and the point where it enters the uptrend or downtrend zones creates an opportunity to join a new trend that could be emerging. When the currency pair ends the NY session (4 p.m. Eastern Time) within the first and second bands, there is a reasonable chance that it will remain within the bands for days to come.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, 'Getting into a New Trend'; Chapter 14 Lesson 1 & 2 (spread and stop refinement)
findings.notes: Includes a rare empirical refinement from the book's own trade log (Chapter 14): a 60-pip stop adopted because >60 pips adverse correlated with a 97% stop-out rate, and a 6-pip spread admission cap. For V8 the 60-pip absolute stop becomes an ATR-relative or fixed-R parameter; the spread cap informs the simulator cost model.
findings.book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

findings.strategy_name: News-surprise momentum with the 5-minute rule
findings.mechanism: A large economic data surprise (actual vs forecast) triggers directional continuation after an initial noise burst; entering on a 5-minute candle close aligned with both the surprise and the prevailing trend raises the probability of continuation
findings.setup_summary: Before a scheduled high-impact release (employment reports, retail sales, ISM/PMI, GDP, CPI/PPI) verify: (1) the data is high-impact; (2) the surprise is large (rule of thumb >5% vs forecast, sometimes 2% suffices; let price confirm); (3) sentiment alignment. Wait 5 minutes after release, then enter only if the 5-minute candle closed in the surprise direction AND price is on the corresponding side of the 50-period SMA on the 5-minute chart. If the first 5-minute candle closes against the data-consistent direction, the trade is void.
findings.trigger_invalidation: 5-minute candle closes opposite to the surprise = no trade; good data but price below the 50-SMA (or vice versa) = sentiment overrides, skip; spreads start widening 5-10 minutes pre-release, so avoid that entry window.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: 5-min close after the 5-minute wait; stop: high/low of the data candle (for shorts/longs), minimum 20 pips, default 30-35 pips; T1 = amount risked (example: 31 pips), exit half, trail remainder 20-30 pips; first target usually hit within the first hour.
findings.quote: The key is to wait five minutes before getting into the trade to make sure that the currency responds the way that it is supposed to.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, 'Sifting through the Headlines' and 'How Fast and Furious Trading Works'
findings.notes: Crypto analog: US CPI/FOMC/NFP and similar macro releases move BTC, so the mechanism transfers, but microstructure differs - perps are 24/7 with millisecond reactions, no retail-broker spread widening, and liquidation cascades instead of stop clustering. Requires a macro-calendar feed as a response-group feature (event/available clock discipline). A second anecdote (USD/CAD, Chapter 9) shows the 5-minute rule filtering out a data-consistent trade that then failed.
findings.book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

findings.strategy_name: Round-number (psychological level) breakout
findings.mechanism: Stop and limit orders cluster at round numbers and 50-pip increments; when a round level breaks, the triggered orders create a sharp burst of directional price action, so break-and-continue in the direction of prevailing sentiment
findings.setup_summary: Identify key round levels (book examples: USD/JPY 105.00, 100.00, 95.00; EUR/USD 1.45, 1.40, 1.35, 1.30) plus 50-increment levels. A sustained break of a round level during active sessions triggers sharp continuation; sell/buy the break in the direction of the prevailing trend or market sentiment rather than fading it. Book notes that during panics one downgrade/level break is often followed by another, so joining beats fading.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The break fails and price closes back through the level; breakouts occurring during the quiet Asian window are predominantly fake-outs (low participation).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the break; stop beyond the round level or the data-candle extreme; short-term target in the direction of prevailing sentiment; for news-driven breaks a stop at the data-candle high/low, minimum 20 pips.
findings.quote: Every 100-pip increment will attract stops, and a break of those levels can trigger a sharp burst in price action as brokers process orders that either get their clients into new positions or out of old ones.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, 'Technicals Matter, Too'; Chapter 1 'Turning Headlines into Opportunities'
findings.notes: Transfers directly to crypto: BTC round numbers (50k, 100k) and perp order clustering behave the same way, and the book explicitly warns that quiet-session breaks are fake-outs (see session-timing finding). Mechanism is the same family as liquidity_sweep_reclaim but without the wick-through-reclaim structure - pure break-and-continue on clustered stop liquidity.
findings.book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

findings.strategy_name: Interest-rate / carry differential following
findings.mechanism: Investors move capital toward the higher-yielding currency, driving its value up while it is funded by low-yield currencies; in risk-off episodes they unwind, selling high-yield and buying low-yield, so the carry trend flips with risk appetite
findings.setup_summary: Long the high-yield currency funded by the low-yield one while risk appetite is on (the book's example: AUD above USD for most of 2010 because Australian rates exceeded US rates). Direction of rates matters more than level - a low-rate country can attract money if its rates are headed up. Unwind (short high-yield / long low-yield) when risk aversion rises, since carry unwinds move currencies in lockstep with equities.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A central-bank policy path reversal, or a risk-off episode (sharp equity sell-off) that unwinds carry before the rate differential itself changes.
findings.risk_geometry: Book gives no entry/stop specifics; multi-day-to-months hold; the stated risk control is position sizing because at 10:1 leverage a 10% adverse move wipes the account.
findings.quote: If I had to pick only one thing to determine where currencies are headed, it would certainly be interest rates.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Interest Rates' and 'Yield'; Chapter 5, 'The Direction of Interest Rates'
findings.notes: For crypto perps the analog is the funding rate: positive-funding regimes behave like carry and funding-carry is a candidate strategy. There is no sovereign yield curve in perps, so this is a feature-group input (flow/funding) and a possible backlog strategy, not an immediate expert. Chapter 12 confirms the fragility: a carry-trade-only system worked 2001-2007 and crashed in 2008.
findings.book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

findings.strategy_name: T1-T2 partial-profit / breakeven / trail exit method
findings.mechanism: Banking half the position at a conservative first target roughly equal to the risk and moving the remainder to breakeven converts floating profit into realized profit while a residual position captures trend continuation
findings.setup_summary: For any position: set T1 approximately equal to the amount risked (example: risk 40 pips, T1 = 40 pips). Exit half at T1, move the stop to the entry (breakeven), and trail the remainder (book: 30-pip trailing stop ratcheted every 20 pips). The method is net-positive if the strategy wins 60-70% of trades even with a slightly negative per-trade expectation, because partial profits are banked and the trade cannot lose money after breakeven.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The book argues strict 2:1 risk/reward targets are unrealistic: on a ~100-pip average daily range a 70-pip target (for a 35-pip stop) demands 70% of a day's move, and a 10-pip stop gets clipped by noise plus 2-3 pips of spread.
findings.risk_geometry: T1 = risk amount; breakeven stop on remainder after T1; trailing stop 30 pips, ratchet every 20 pips; T2 further and achievable; applied to both BB new-trend entries (T1 30-60 pips) and news trades (T1 = risk).
findings.quote: When the target is hit, I would close out half of the position and move my stop to breakeven on the remainder of the position. If the trade continues to move in my favor, then I will trail the stop to lock in more profits.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, 'Bag Your Winners Quickly'
findings.notes: Directly actionable in the V8 lifecycle: partial fill at T1, breakeven move, trailing ratchet. The book explicitly rejects strict 2:1 R:R in favor of a high-hit-rate, per-trade-negative-edge model on psychological grounds - a falsifiable alternative to the current fixed target_r/stop_r geometry worth testing as a VARIANT of an existing family.
findings.book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

findings.strategy_name: Correlated exposure cap (same-dollar-direction pairs)
findings.mechanism: Concurrent longs in two USD-correlated pairs (e.g., AUD/USD and NZD/USD) are one concentrated USD-direction bet, not diversification, because the USD is usually up or down against all majors on a given day
findings.setup_summary: Before adding a second position, check correlation with existing exposure. Since the USD tends to be uniformly up or down across the majors, going long both AUD/USD and NZD/USD on simultaneous breakouts doubles the same underlying bet; treat it as one exposure or size down. Intentional concentration is acceptable only if deliberate.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - admission/risk rule rather than a signal; if one correlated leg collapses the other typically follows.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - gate at exposure admission: reject or aggregate the second correlated position; reduce size if the correlation is intentional.
findings.quote: On most days, the U.S. dollar will be either up against all of the major currencies or down. The magnitude of the moves will be different... rather than being diversified, the exposure is highly concentrated, which creates a hidden risk in the positions.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, Mistake #3: Taking Highly Correlated Trades
findings.notes: For V8: BTC and highly-correlated alt perps double up on the same macro/risk direction, so this extends the existing one-exposure-per-(instrument,direction) rule into a correlation-aware cap in RiskGate; correlation must be computed from PIT history, not live cross-asset data.
findings.book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

findings.strategy_name: Per-trade account risk cap (5% max)
findings.mechanism: Bounding per-trade risk keeps a single adverse move from destroying the account under leverage; offered leverage (50:1) is not a target
findings.setup_summary: Never risk more than 5% of the account on any one trade (the book's hard line: 'risking anything greater than 5 to 10 percent of your account on any one trade is financial suicide'). Even at modest 10:1 leverage a 10% adverse move wipes the account, so position size must be derived from stop distance and account equity, not from the leverage offered.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - permanent risk rule.
findings.risk_geometry: Position size = (risk percent x equity) / stop distance; margin is not a loss cap; margin-call behavior (broker closes positions) must be modeled.
findings.quote: Professional traders who survive in the forex market will usually not risk more than 5 percent of their account on any one trade, and using stops can be a good way to limit the downside risk of leverage.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Leverage' and 'Margin'; Chapter 11, Mistake #8
findings.notes: Crypto perp leverage (commonly 25x-125x) makes this cap more load-bearing than in spot FX; complements the V8 heat cap and one-exposure rule. The book's margin-call description (broker force-closes when equity falls below maintenance margin) is a simulator cost-model input.
findings.book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

findings.strategy_name: Session time-of-day liquidity filter for short-term strategies
findings.mechanism: Breakout and trend strategies need enough participants to fuel continuation; the quiet window (NY close to Europe open, especially the Asian session start) produces fake-outs rather than breakouts
findings.setup_summary: For short-term breakout/momentum strategies, only trust setups when European and U.S. markets are both open (12:00-17:00 GMT overlap); treat breakout signals in the Asian session (approx. NY 5pm-2am) as suspect fake-outs. Book stats: ~70% of the average daily range occurs in European hours and ~80% in U.S. hours. Also: do not range-trade ahead of a big scheduled release - breakout risk is highest there.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A breakout or trend-following signal outside the overlap window is a lower-probability trade; a range break during pre-news dead time is a fake-out risk.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - timing/admission gate applied to short-term strategies; interacts with the news-surprise rule's 5-minute wait.
findings.quote: This is the time when more 'fake-outs' than breakouts occur because the beginning of the Asian session is typically one of the quietest times in the currency market.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Zones'; Chapter 10, 'If You're a Short-Term Trader...'
findings.notes: Maps directly to 24/7 crypto: BTC ranges compress in the Asian window and breakouts there are disproportionately fake-outs, while the London/NY overlap is the high-volume window. Time is a frozen V8 feature group; this becomes a time-gated lifecycle rule (episode admission by session), not a separate expert.
findings.book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

findings.strategy_name: Bollinger trend-exhaustion reversal (band re-entry)
findings.mechanism: When a trend dies the price usually reverts at least to the first SD band on the other side, so entering at the first band after the first exhaustion close gives a counter-trend reversion trade
findings.setup_summary: Daily chart. In a downtrend (price between lower 1-SD and 2-SD bands), wait for the first close above the lower 1-SD band (exhaustion), then go LONG with a stop at the most significant near-term low; the reversion frequently extends to the upper 1-SD band. Symmetric: after an uptrend's first close below the upper 1-SD band, short with a stop at the most significant near-term high.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Price remains inside the trend zone (no exhaustion close) = no setup; a fresh close beyond the band in the original trend direction invalidates the reversion.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: close above/below the first band; stop: most significant near-term swing low/high; target: far first band or T1-T2 with the 15-period SMA as a partial-exit reference; book notes the far band is often a few hundred pips away, so T1-T2 is preferred over a single distant target.
findings.quote: A practical way to pick a bottom would be to wait for the currency pair to close above the lower first standard deviation Bollinger Band with a stop at the most significant near-term low.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, 'Knowing When the Trend Has Exhausted'
findings.notes: Counter-trend, so it ranks below continuation families for V8's trend-favoring evidence base; the book itself frames trend-fading as the contrarian ('Jack Shephard') approach suitable only for range-style personalities. Uses the same band machinery as the regime filter, so it is cheap to add once band features exist.
findings.book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

findings.strategy_name: High-probability setup checklist (five alignments)
findings.mechanism: Converging alignment of trend quality, fundamentals, calendar risk, market sentiment, and key levels raises the conditional probability of a trend-continuation trade
findings.setup_summary: Before any trend-continuation long/short, verify five questions: (1) the retracement is shallow, not deep - deep corrections raise the risk the trend breaks; (2) there is no fundamental reason (e.g., disappointing data) behind the dip; (3) the next 24 hours of scheduled data are expected to support the trade; (4) risk appetite supports it (e.g., no 300-point Dow plunge that would trigger follow-through selling in Asia); (5) key support/resistance levels will not stall the trade.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A deep correction, a fundamental driver behind the move, adverse expected data, adverse sentiment, or a broken key level each veto the trade; when factors conflict, judgment decides weighting.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - pre-trade admission filter; also includes the instrument-selection judgment to express a country-data view through a pair less affected by the USD (e.g., CAD news via AUD/CAD or CAD/JPY when US data is co-released).
findings.quote: The point is to have as many stars aligned in your favor as possible on your trades and not to expose it to unnecessary and amateur risks.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, 'Sticking with High-Probability Trades' and 'If You're a Short-Term Trader...'
findings.notes: This is a candidate-vetting heuristic, not an executable expert: it informs how V8 combines feature groups for setup admission (the 'as many variables as possible' principle) and the idea that a data view should be expressed in the instrument least contaminated by other drivers - a principle for V8's perp universe where USD/BTC macro is the dominant confound.
findings.book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

book_title: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex (Kathy Lien, 2011)
Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0 (Forex Hero)

findings.strategy_name: 30-day moving average trend filter
findings.mechanism: price trading above a trend-defining moving average signals demand accumulation, biasing continuation over reversal
findings.setup_summary: On the daily (or higher) timeframe, when price moves above the 30-day moving average, establish a long bias toward gains; the MA acts as a trend regime filter for entry decisions rather than a standalone entry. Complemented by the book's rule to never trade against the established trend ('wait for a beneficial tendency').
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid while price trades back below the 30-day MA; also 'don't play against the trend' - do not initiate counter-trend positions in the filtered direction.
findings.risk_geometry: Book gives no entry/stop/target for this; treat as a regime filter only - entry/stop/target geometry is inherited from the underlying expert (e.g., trend_pullback).
findings.quote: One of his favorite measures is the 30-day moving average. When prices move above that level, he's more inclined to bet on gains.
findings.chapter_anchor: Section 05, How pros evaluate the market (Wang Bing, commodity trader)
findings.notes: Single practitioner anecdote, no statistics. A price-vs-MA filter is instrument-agnostic and transfers directly to 24/7 BTCUSDT; V8 already consumes MA features in trend_pullback, so this is a cheap regime-filter variant. Folds in the companion tip 'Transactions against a trend usually result in loss. Wait for a beneficial tendency and then make your move!' (Section 08, tip 5).
findings.book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

findings.strategy_name: Scheduled-event volatility risk rule (news stop-outs)
findings.mechanism: volatility and spread expansion before scheduled announcements produce wild whipsaws that hit stops regardless of the eventual direction
findings.setup_summary: Before a scheduled high-impact release (FX: NFP, FOMC, CPI, trade balance, retail sales; crypto analog: CPI/FOMC), either widen the stop by the expected spread-expansion distance (book suggests 5-10 pips for higher TF stops), or reduce position size so the widened stop preserves the originally intended loss, or close the position before the release. Never leave a tight stop near price when an announcement is imminent.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Applies only when a high-impact release is scheduled within the holding period; no adjustment needed when no announcement is pending over the trade horizon.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop width scaled by expected spread widening; position sized so loss-at-widened-stop equals the intended loss (stop_distance_atr variant with an event premium).
findings.quote: The volatility jumps before important anouncements and the drastic movements can hit the stop-losses, resulting in a lost trade and investment.
findings.chapter_anchor: Section 03, When & why do spreads tighten / How to trade during the news events
findings.notes: BTCUSDT 1h produces violent wicks around US CPI and FOMC releases; a deterministic event-calendar stop-widening rule is directly implementable in RiskGate without new data streams (the calendar is knowable in advance). The book warns the widened spread 'will get you' even if the announcement favors you, because price whipsaws a few pips before taking direction.
findings.book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

findings.strategy_name: Break-even stop promotion at +1R
findings.mechanism: once the position has moved in favor by the full initial risk distance, promoting the stop to entry removes tail risk from the winner while leaving the upside intact
findings.setup_summary: As soon as a position has profited by the same amount that was initially risked (1R), move the stop-loss to break-even; some traders also close a partial position at that point. This is an exit-management rule layered on any entry.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Only triggers after price reaches +1R in favor; the original structural stop remains in force before that level.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop promoted from initial stop_r to entry at +1R; target_r unchanged; a standard lifecycle transition on the existing expert's frozen references.
findings.quote: A good habit of more successful traders is to employ the rule of moving your stop to break even as soon as your position has profited by the same amount that you initially risked through the stop order.
findings.chapter_anchor: Section 08, Risk management (trailing stops / break-even)
findings.notes: A canonical lifecycle rule, implementable in src/v8/lifecycle.py for existing experts (trend_pullback, failed_breakout, liquidity_sweep_reclaim) with no new features; perp leverage makes the risk-free-trade property especially valuable. Companion guidance: trailing stops and partial position closure noted as alternatives.
findings.book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

findings.strategy_name: Fixed-percent risk cap per trade (2% / rule of 1/6)
findings.mechanism: capping per-trade risk as a small fraction of equity bounds drawdown so a single loss cannot erase prior profitability
findings.setup_summary: Risk at most 2% of equity on any single trade (pros' consensus); a conservative variant caps risk at 1/6 of free capital when conviction is not complete. Position size = (equity * risk_fraction) / stop distance. The book ties this to survival statistics: 99% of day traders lose money and one oversized loss eliminates any winning streak.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Cap applies unconditionally at admission; both percentages are variants of one sizing family.
findings.risk_geometry: notional = (equity * risk_fraction) / stop_distance; maps directly to V8 RiskGate's heat cap with position size derived from stop_r.
findings.quote: Pros recommend 1:2 risk-reward ratio, and not risking more than 2% of your equity on any single trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Section 08, Risk management + 10 tips from the pros (rule of 1/6)
findings.notes: Pure sizing rule, applies unchanged to BTCUSDT perps; particularly relevant given default high leverage. Companion leverage lesson: 'Using 1:50 leverage means that a 2% adverse move could wipe out all your equity' - book recommends effective leverage of 10:1 or less.
findings.book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

findings.strategy_name: Minimum 1:2 risk-reward admission gate
findings.mechanism: requiring target at least 2x the stop filters out low-expectancy entries before capital is committed
findings.setup_summary: Establish a risk-reward ratio for every trade and admit a candidate only if potential gain is at least 2x the amount willing to be lost (target_r >= 2 * stop_r); otherwise skip the entry as not worth the risk.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Reject candidate when structure-based target yields reward/risk below 2:1.
findings.risk_geometry: target_r >= 2 * stop_r, both derived from market structure rather than fixed pips.
findings.quote: Generally, the risk-reward ratio should be at least 1:2, if not more. Having a solid risk-reward ratio can prevent traders from entering positions that ultimately are not worth the risk.
findings.chapter_anchor: Section 08, Risk-reward ratio
findings.notes: A pure risk-layer admission rule for V8's risk_geometry; applies unchanged to BTCUSDT 1h. Stated as a universal rule across strategies, not an empirical claim.
findings.book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

findings.strategy_name: Thin-market liquidity avoidance
findings.mechanism: low participation widens spreads and degrades fill quality, so execution cost in an inactive market exceeds the small tradable range available
findings.setup_summary: Do not open positions in structurally illiquid windows: Friday afternoon, weekends, session close, bank holidays, end of December, overnight. These windows offer smaller ranges and wider spreads; price can be chaotic and stops unreliable.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Applies when liquidity is structurally low; a rolling spread/liquidity measure could gate admission in place of a fixed clock for a 24/7 market.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry geometry - a time- or liquidity-based admission gate at the lifecycle layer.
findings.quote: An inactive (often called 'thin') market offers smaller movements of rates, thus smaller potential profits. A thin market also comes with higher commissions (spreads) for each trade due to the decreased liquidity.
findings.chapter_anchor: Section 03, When NOT to trade forex
findings.notes: Crypto perps have no weekend close and no central session clock, so the fixed-clock version does not transfer; but BTC weekend books are genuinely thinner, so a liquidity-based (spread/order-book-depth) admission gate is the honest 24/7 adaptation. Book also lists 'when angry or frustrated' and overnight as avoid windows - psychological/execution-state admissions that are harder to formalize deterministically.
findings.book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

findings.strategy_name: Session-overlap volatility timing
findings.mechanism: liquidity and participation cluster at session overlaps, concentrating volatility and tradable range into a few daily windows
findings.setup_summary: Concentrate analysis and entries in the high-participation windows: the London/New-York overlap (~10:00 EST, when London closes and the US opens) provides the biggest returns, with 20-30 pips of opportunity in Euro pairs at the London open; the biggest weekly moves in the four majors occur Tuesday and Wednesday, and Friday is only tradeable until ~12:00.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Timing filter only; invalidated per instrument if no hourly volatility differential is observed.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry geometry - a timing filter to run alongside entries; needs time-derived features (hour of day, session label) on the tape.
findings.quote: The time when the London session intersects with the US session usually provides the biggest returns. ... the biggest movement in the four major currency pairs ... is observed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays.
findings.chapter_anchor: Section 03, What Are the Best Times to Trade Forex
findings.notes: Crypto is 24/7 with no formal sessions, but BTC volatility/volume still clusters around US daytime and the funding-rate window; the overlap concept maps to participation concentration, not the FX session structure. V8's 'time' feature group could host a session/participation feature. Book claims 'according to research' for Tuesday/Wednesday but presents no statistics.
findings.book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

findings.strategy_name: Consensus vs actual news surprise (buy the rumor, sell the news)
