findings.mechanism: large players pre-position for consensus expectations before data release, so only the deviation of actual from consensus moves price - matching news produces reversals, surprising news produces one-way moves
findings.setup_summary: Around scheduled releases, track consensus forecasts: if actual > forecast the currency tends to strengthen (actual worse than forecast => downward pressure); if actual == consensus expect little or reverse movement because positioning was completed pre-release. The 'sell the news' case is a fade of the pre-release run-up.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No trade when actual matches consensus; thesis invalid if price does not move in the surprise direction in the post-release window.
findings.risk_geometry: Book specifies none; news wicks imply entry at bar close after the release with stop beyond the initial spike.
findings.quote: The currency rates often start moving even before the actual data comes out due to forecasts and market sentiment! ... If the actual data comes out worse than expected, it creates a strong downward pressure on the currency.
findings.chapter_anchor: Section 02, Consensus Vs Actual numbers (reference: babypips)
findings.notes: BTC has no own macro calendar but is highly sensitive to US CPI/FOMC releases; the surprise-vs-consensus mechanism is testable in principle, but V8's tape does not carry consensus/surprise data, so this is DATA_BLOCKED until a news/surprise feed exists. Narrative worked example (consensus 9.0%, actual 9.0% => no move; 8.0% => dollar rally; 10.0% => drop), no statistics.
findings.book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

findings.strategy_name: Commodity-currency cross-market flow (gold/USD, oil/CAD/RUB, gold/AUD)
findings.mechanism: commodity prices drive trade balances and flows of commodity-exporter economies, creating persistent cross-asset correlation regimes
findings.setup_summary: Use commodity prices as a cross-market input for currency direction: rising gold => USD weakness (gold is the dollar's safe-haven alternative), AUD/CAD strength; rising oil => CAD and RUB strength, USD/CAD decline (gold breaking an important level is a tradeable signal for dollar-bloc proxies); the free-floating ruble tracks Brent 'in almost-perfect lockstep'.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Correlations are regime-dependent; treat decoupling (e.g., gold up while USD up) as the invalidation signal for the pair.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry geometry - a cross_market feature input to any expert; adds the cross_market feature group to the feature vocabulary.
findings.quote: When Gold Goes Up, the USD Often Goes Down (and Vice Versa) ... the higher the oil prices are, the lower the USD/CAD value will be.
findings.chapter_anchor: Section 06, Commodity currencies
findings.notes: BTC is USD-priced but has no commodity-export mechanism, so the trade-balance transmission does not transfer; however DXY, gold, and equity risk-sentiment features are plausible regime inputs for BTC perps (risk-on/off) and worth testing as cross_market features. The 'almost-perfect lockstep' claim (RUB~Brent) is the strongest falsifiable correlation statement; Morgan Stanley's dollar+5% => oil -10 to -25% is an external citation, not the book's own data.
findings.book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

findings.strategy_name: Carry / interest-rate differential thesis
findings.mechanism: capital flows toward the higher-yielding currency, so the policy-differential trend persists until central banks converge
findings.setup_summary: Hold the currency of the faster-growing economy funded by the slower-growing one; central-bank policy divergence sustains the differential trend (the book's 2016-17 dollar rally is attributed to a Fed tightening while peers eased). For crypto perps the direct analog is the funding rate: hold the perp direction that receives funding while the differential persists.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Carry edge decays when policy converges or the yield/funding differential compresses; the book gives no explicit invalidation metric.
findings.risk_geometry: A holding-period strategy; P&L accrues from the differential rather than price direction - requires funding-rate (derivatives tape) data that V8 does not yet ingest.
findings.quote: It is better to invest in the currency of a country that is growing faster and fund it with a currency of a country that is growing slower.
findings.chapter_anchor: Section 01, Forex trading quick facts + Section 02, Central bank Policy divergence
findings.notes: The perp funding rate is the structural analog of the carry differential and is a documented flow driver on BTC perps, but V8 is DATA_BLOCKED for any derivatives-tape feature (funding, basis) and this stays a backlog candidate until the tape exists. Dollar-strength narrative supported by Bloomberg consensus quotes in the text, no statistical test presented.
findings.book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

findings.strategy_name: Trend persistence / hold-winners discipline
findings.mechanism: trends are self-reinforcing because each new follower's flow extends the move, so premature profit-taking truncates the edge and counter-trend entries lose
findings.setup_summary: When holding a winning position in an established trend, resist closing early: 'trends last longer than they might seem' and they develop quickly because participation grows as traders follow. Let targets be structure-based and keep losers closed early ('close the unsuccessful ... early').
findings.trigger_invalidation: Qualitative exit discipline, not a falsifiable entry signal; the herding-continuation claim is a candidate mechanism for the simulator/expert exit modeling.
findings.risk_geometry: Exit-side lesson: keep target at structure rather than manual early close; complemented by 'don't hold unsuccessful positions open for a long time'.
findings.quote: Trends last longer than they might seem at first! ... when trends start, they develop quickly because they are increased by the number of traders following them.
findings.chapter_anchor: Section 08, 10 tips from the pros (tips 2, 9, 10)
findings.notes: Motivational framing with no data. The herding/self-reinforcement mechanism is plausible on perps (funding + leverage flows add momentum), but the claim is qualitative; useful as an exit-behavior hypothesis and a simulator lesson, not a standalone signal. Pairs with 'close unsuccessful positions early' and 'don't stop the profit'.
findings.book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

findings.strategy_name: Multiple time frame context (higher TF trend, lower TF entry)
findings.mechanism: higher-timeframe structure dominates lower-timeframe noise; a lower-TF signal read in isolation misreads routine pullbacks as reversals
findings.setup_summary: Analyze 2-3 time frames spaced 4-8 bars apart (Month=>Week=>Day, or Day=>6h=>1h, or Day=>4h=>1h): the higher timeframe sets the trend (daily charts), the lower timeframe sets entry/exit (hourly). The book's worked example shows a daily downtrend that is a mere blip within a longer upward tendency - the canonical single-timeframe misread.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Methodology, not a signal; applies to how any expert reads context on the 1h bar.
findings.risk_geometry: None.
findings.quote: For successful and precise market analysis, you must use at least 2-3 time frames! ... use daily charts to identify the overall trend and then use the hourly charts to determine specific entry levels.
findings.chapter_anchor: Section 04, Multiple time frame analysis
findings.notes: Directly relevant to V8's single-timeframe (1h) MarketState: a higher-TF trend context (e.g., 4h/1d trend feature) is a concrete, low-cost marketstate refinement candidate for the trend_pullback family and any regime filter. Practitioner consensus claim ('all good traders I know use 2-3 time frames'), no statistics.
findings.book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

findings.strategy_name: Magic Formula: two-factor rank on quality (ROC) + value (earnings yield)
findings.setup_summary: Rank the tradable universe by (a) EBIT / tangible capital employed (return on capital) and (b) EBIT / enterprise value (earnings yield), sum the two ranks, and buy the ~30 highest combined-rank names, holding each one year and rebalancing annually. On 17 years of US data (Compustat Point-in-Time, controlling for look-ahead/survivorship bias) the top-ranked ~30-stock portfolio returned ~30.8%/yr vs 12.3% for the equal-weighted market; decile analysis shows monotonic returns from Group 1 (17.9%/yr) to Group 10 (2.5%/yr). Perp analog (only if V8 expands beyond single-instrument): rank perp instruments by a quality proxy and a carry/value proxy (e.g., funding-adjusted yield normalized to notional), select the top-ranked basket, hold on a long cycle.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: rebalance at a fixed calendar interval (annually in the study); entry when an instrument is in the top combined-rank group. Invalidation: the thesis fails if the top-ranked decile stops beating the bottom-ranked decile over multi-year frozen OOS, or if crowding pushes ranked bargains to fair value so the rank spread collapses.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at market on the screen date; no price stop (margin of safety is the buffer); target is reversion toward fair value; exit after a fixed ~1-year hold (time stop / scheduled rebalance); risk is controlled by holding 20-30 names (diversification) rather than by per-name stops.
findings.quote: Rather, the formula looks for the companies that have the best combination of those two factors.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 p.54 (also Ch.6 p.51-52, Table 6.1; Ch.7 Table 7.2; Appendix p.139-144)
findings.notes: Cross-sectional ranking across multiple perps is a ranker, which V8 keeps ABSENT by default (rule 6) - so this enters only as a registry experiment beating a simple baseline on frozen OOS. Requires a multi-instrument derivatives tape with funding (DATA_BLOCKED today, same gate as breakout_retest/capitulation). The earnings-yield-vs-risk-free-hurdle idea (buy only when yield exceeds ~6%) is part of the same ranking mechanism.
findings.book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

findings.strategy_name: Mr. Market / margin of safety: buy at a large discount to intrinsic value, wait for reversion
findings.setup_summary: Estimate intrinsic value per share; buy only when price trades at a large discount (the book's example: estimated value $70-72 vs purchase price $37, i.e. roughly half to 60% of value); expect Mr. Market to pay a fair price within 2-3 years as smart money, buybacks, or takeovers converge price to value. Short-term price swings (the 'wide range of prices' each year for GE/IBM/GM) are treated as Mr. Market's mood, not value changes.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price drops to a pre-defined large discount to estimated value. Invalidation: the value estimate itself was wrong (earnings fade, business deteriorates), or price fails to converge to fair value after ~3 years - the book explicitly warns a bargain can 'remain a bargain forever (or worse)'.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at market when price < ~50-60% of estimated value; no price stop (margin of safety is the loss buffer); target = fair value; expiry = ~2-3 years (time-based reversion horizon); the smaller the discount, the closer to a no-trade.
findings.quote: This means that if you buy shares at what you believe to be a bargain price and you are right, Mr. Market will eventually agree and offer to buy those shares at a fair price.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 p.98 (framework in Ch.4 p.32-34)
findings.notes: Requires an intrinsic-value anchor for BTC that the behavior-only feature stack cannot supply (the natural perp analog is a realized-cost-basis / MVRV-style floor, which is this book's mapping, not its text). The 2-3 year reversion claim is asserted, not tested in the book - the tested claim is the value factor's multi-year efficacy. 24/7 trading removes gap risk but not the slow reversion; leverage shortens the survivable horizon.
findings.book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

findings.strategy_name: Graham net-net basket: buy assets priced below net liquidation value
findings.setup_summary: Buy a basket of 20-30 names whose market price is below the proceeds of a fire-sale liquidation of the business's net current assets (Graham's 'bargain issues'). The book reports Graham used the formula successfully for 30+ years, that results were satisfactory with no further analysis, and that few if any stocks qualify today.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any name trades below its estimated net liquidation value. Invalidation: the basket stops reverting to (or above) liquidation value over long horizons; in practice the current market rarely offers qualifying assets, which is itself an invalidation of the screen's capacity.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at market; no price stop; target = reversion toward asset value; long/no fixed expiry but effectively multi-year; risk controlled by holding a basket so individual names can fail.
findings.quote: the purchase price was actually lower than the proceeds that would be received from simply shutting down the business and selling off the company's assets in a fire sale
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 p.49 (Ch.6 p.55-56 summary)
findings.notes: No book-value/liquidation-value analog exists for a token; the nearest crypto equivalent is a realized-cost/floor feature that is not part of this book. Keep as a gated backlog idea only if a realized-cost flow family is ever built; the transferable core is 'buy below a hard asset-backed floor and hold a diversified basket'.
findings.book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

findings.strategy_name: Evaluation-horizon gate: expect multi-year underperformance from a genuine edge; measure risk as long-run loss probability
findings.setup_summary: A strategy with a real long-run edge still underperforms the market in 5 of every 12 months, in 1 of every 4 one-year windows, and in 1 of every 6 two-year windows; only on a 3-year horizon does the edge show (the Magic Formula beat the market in 160/169 three-year periods and was profitable in 169/169). Definition of risk: (1) probability of losing money long-term and (2) probability of underperforming alternatives long-term - not short-horizon volatility.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any evidence-based claim about a strategy must use multi-year horizons before a verdict. Invalidation: a strategy judged failed on <3-year evidence may actually be a live edge mid-drawdown; conversely short-horizon outperformance is not evidence of edge.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a - methodology for the lab/registry, not a tradable setup.
findings.quote: Following the formula for any three-year period in a row, the magic formula beat the market averages 95 percent of the time
findings.notes: Directly governs V8's registry gates (SCREENING -> REPLICATION -> SHADOW) and lab verdicts: demand frozen-OOS evidence spanning multiple years and expect months-to-years of underperformance from legitimate families. 'Magic formula did poorly for more than two years in a row in one of every six periods' (Ch.8) quantifies how long a false-failure window lasts. The 1h BTC frame only increases episode counts per calendar year - this does NOT shorten the horizon needed for an economic verdict.
findings.book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

findings.strategy_name: Crowding-capacity persistence: edges survive because investors abandon them mid-drawdown and chase recent winners
findings.setup_summary: A strategy's long-run edge persists partly because of human behavior: if it worked all the time, everyone would use it and the bargains would disappear, so genuine value strategies must have long lumpy underperformance stretches. Case studies: a bestselling author's formula fund underperformed 2 of its first 3 years (one year by 25%) then became a top fund; a disciplined manager lost most clients after 3-4 slow years then went on to trounce the market. Most investors switch to whatever worked in the past few years (performance chasing), which is exactly the wrong rotation point.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: evaluate a strategy's practical viability by its drawdown-tolerance requirement, not just its mean return. Invalidation: if adoption/crowding is high (edge widely followed), the edge decays toward zero even with correct execution.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a - behavioral constraint on strategy selection and holding, not a tradable setup.
findings.quote: if the magic formula worked all the time, everyone would probably use it. If everyone used it, it would probably stop working.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.8 p.73 (Ch.8 p.71-72 fund/manager case studies; p.74 'most people look for a new strategy-usually one that has done well over the past few years')
findings.notes: For V8: systematic, belief-independent execution is an advantage over human managers because it will not quit mid-drawdown (the registry, not the operator, decides). But the lesson cuts both ways: promotion criteria must include crowding/capacity monitoring, and naive rotation into recently-hot families (momentum in strategy space) is a known failure mode the lab should not encode as evidence.
findings.book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

findings.strategy_name: Coverage/neglect premium: value works best in lightly analyzed names; earnings-based cheapness stays robust in large caps
findings.setup_summary: Mispricing is more frequent among names too small to justify analyst coverage, so simple value screens find more bargains there; in the book's decile tests the smallest-cap group did NOT itself outperform (12.1% vs 11.9% for largest decile) - the outperformance comes from the value screen applied inside the universe, not from size alone. The Magic Formula stays discriminative in large caps (best-decile 18.88%/yr vs worst 4.66%, spread >14 pts) where price/book fails (low P/B best-vs-worst decile spread only ~2 pts among $1B+ names).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: prefer a value/quality screen to locate bargains; expect concentration of bargains in low-coverage instruments. Invalidation: the coverage/neglect premium collapses if the market becomes fully efficient in the target universe (e.g., after broad retail/institutional adoption).
findings.risk_geometry: n/a beyond the underlying value strategy - this is universe-selection guidance.
findings.quote: companies that are too small for professionals to buy and that are not large enough to generate sufficient commission revenue to justify analyst coverage are more likely to be ignored or misunderstood. As a result, they are more likely to present opportunities to find bargain-priced stocks.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix p.149-151
findings.notes: If V8 ever expands beyond BTCUSDT, alt perps are the low-coverage analog - more mispricing but thinner liquidity (capacity check). The large-cap robustness result favors fundamental/flow-based cheapness over raw price screens, which supports a flow/carry feature program over pure price-pattern work when ranking instruments.
findings.book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

findings.strategy_name: Signal averaging: trailing-window inputs are noisy per name but informative across a portfolio
findings.setup_summary: The Magic Formula deliberately uses trailing (last-year) earnings even though value depends on future earnings, because a noisy proxy becomes an unbiased average across 20-30 names: 'on average, last year's earnings will often provide a pretty good estimate for normal earnings going forward.' For the few who can project normal-year earnings 3-4 years out, 5-8 high-conviction names in different industries can replace the 20-30-name basket; for everyone else the diversified basket is mandatory.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: evaluate any per-name signal in aggregate across many candidates before judging it; a trailing-window feature that is weak per episode may still rank families well in aggregate. Invalidation: aggregation across too few candidates, or across a non-stationary universe, re-introduces per-name noise.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a - aggregation/evaluation methodology for the lab.
findings.quote: using last year's earnings is often a good indicator of what earnings will look like in the future. Of course, for individual companies, this may not be the case.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.11 p.104 (Ch.11 p.102-103 normalized-earnings ideal; p.105 5-8 stocks rule)
findings.notes: V8 already evaluates families across many candidate episodes; this finding argues for pooling episodes when scoring an expert hypothesis rather than promoting on single episodes, and for preferring normalized/window-robust features over single trailing snapshots where possible. Also motivates the registry's multiplicity unit (variants, not re-fits).
findings.book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

findings.strategy_name: Phased portfolio entry + fixed-cycle rebalance (5-7 names every 2-3 months; replace only matured names)
findings.setup_summary: To reproduce the tested average, do not buy the full 20-30-name portfolio at once: add 5-7 names every 2-3 months over the first ~9-10 months, then each cycle replace only the 5-7 names that reach the one-year holding mark with fresh top-ranked selections; stay committed for a minimum of 3-5 years regardless of results.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: enter the portfolio in tranches on a calendar schedule rather than all at once; exit names on a fixed holding cycle. Invalidation: the schedule assumes the average (not single-name) result, so deviating to concentrated timing or abandoning the cycle re-introduces timing luck.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry in calendar tranches (every 2-3 months), each name held ~1 year, replaced on schedule; no price stop; risk governed by the schedule plus basket diversification.
findings.quote: we will have to work into our magic formula portfolio over the course of our first year of investing. That means adding 5 to 7 stocks to our portfolio every few months until we reach 20 or 30 stocks in our portfolio.
findings.chapter_anchor: Step-by-Step Instructions p.132-135
findings.notes: Reuse starter slug position_scaling. V8's 'one active exposure per (instrument, direction)' rule (rule 16) conflicts with phasing into a single position, so the phased-entry lesson applies at portfolio/backtest scale (staggering candidate entries and scheduled rebalancing in the lab) rather than per-position. The 1-year hold is the book's cycle; a perp analog would need its own calibrated cycle.
findings.book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

findings.strategy_name: Leverage/tax-neutral cheapness metric: EBIT/EV instead of P/E or E/P
findings.setup_summary: When comparing how cheap assets are, deflate operating earnings by enterprise value (equity price + net interest-bearing debt), not by equity price alone: P/E and E/P are distorted by differing debt levels and tax rates, while EBIT/EV is not. The book's worked example: two identical businesses (same EBIT 10, Company A no debt at $60, Company B $50 debt at $10) have the same EBIT/EV yield (10/60) despite P/E of 10 vs 3.33.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any cheapness/rank comparison across assets with different leverage must normalize to a leverage-neutral yield. Invalidation: raw price- or margin-based yield ranking misranks assets whenever leverage differs across the universe.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a - metric-construction methodology feeding any cross-asset ranker.
findings.quote: P/E and E/P are greatly influenced by changes in debt levels and tax rates, while EBIT/EV is not.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix p.143-145 (definitions p.139-142)
findings.notes: Perps embed leverage by construction (margin vs notional), so a funding/carry-based cheapness ranking across instruments should normalize yield to total notional exposure rather than to mark price or margin - the direct analog of EBIT/EV vs P/E. Applies only if V8 adds cross-instrument carry ranking.
findings.book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

findings.strategy_name: Moat persistence: high return on capital signals a durable advantage and reinvestment-driven growth
findings.setup_summary: A company that earns a high return on capital even for one year likely has a temporary special advantage (new concept/product, brand, network position) that keeps competition from eroding profits; such firms can reinvest profits at high rates, driving earnings growth (the Jason Gum Shops example: 50% ROC reinvested lifts earnings 50%/yr). Competition grinds ROC down toward average over time, so high ROC is a persistence signal, not a permanent state.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: prefer assets whose 'capital employed' earns a high return as a quality screen. Invalidation: ROC mean-reverts faster than expected (competitive entry), or the high-ROC year was a one-off that does not persist - the book itself concedes mediocre businesses can have a good year or two.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a beyond the composite value strategy - this is the quality pillar's causal claim.
findings.quote: In short, companies that achieve a high return on capital are likely to have a special advantage of some kind. That special advantage keeps competitors from destroying the ability to earn above-average profits.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.9 p.84 (Ch.9 p.79-83 reinvestment/growth argument)
findings.notes: Kept separate from the composite two-factor finding because it is an independently falsifiable claim (ROC persistence / moat). There is no 'capital employed' for a token in the behavior-only stack; only usable as a cross-instrument quality filter if network-level fundamental data (revenue, active users, fees) is ever added. No short side exists in this book.
findings.book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

book_title: Come Into My Trading Room — Study Guide (Elder, 2002)

findings.strategy_name: Impulse System (EMA slope + MACD-Histogram slope alignment)
findings.mechanism: when trend inertia (EMA slope) and momentum (MACD-Histogram slope) point the same way, the move is likely to continue until one leg flips
findings.setup_summary: On the trading timeframe (1h for V8), go long when the EMA slope is rising AND the MACD-Histogram is above its prior bar and rising together; short when both are falling together. Clusters of same-direction signals carry more weight, and a higher-timeframe uptrend (weekly-equivalent) adds extra weight to bullish clusters. Falsifiable: both slope signs are computable from price; entry on the next bar after a confirmed cluster.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = EMA slope up + MACD-Histogram rising together (or both falling for short). Thesis invalidated when either component flattens or flips; book: 'both EMAs turn down, canceling the buy signal altogether.'
findings.risk_geometry: Entry next-bar close on signal cluster; stop below recent swing low (week's low on daily scale); the book advises tightening stops when the trend gets old and MACD-Histogram weakens.
findings.quote: Buy signals emerge when both the EMA and MACD-Histogram are rising together; sell signals emerge when both are falling.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part Two, Answers 54-56; also Trade 4/8 entry answers
findings.notes: Distinct from V8 trend_pullback: this is a momentum-alignment entry rather than a price pullback. Heavily corroborated by the 8 case studies, which award points for 'Impulse buy' signals. A candidate new family once the active-expert budget allows.
findings.book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

findings.strategy_name: Buy the pullback to a rising EMA (value trade); sell near the upper channel
findings.mechanism: prices oscillate around value; buying near the rising EMA (value) and selling above value (channel wall) harvests the oscillation inside a trend
findings.setup_summary: In an uptrend (rising EMA slope), buy when price pulls back into the value zone at/near the rising EMA ('sweet zone' between fast and slow EMAs); the book's entry is a limit order placed at the projected next-bar EMA value. Take profits when price touches the upper channel/envelope wall. Stop below the recent swing low (week's low on the daily scale).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = pullback into rising EMA in a confirmed uptrend. Invalidate = EMA flattens or turns down ('both EMAs turn down, canceling the buy signal'); stop hit.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit at projected next-bar EMA (book: 'estimate tomorrow's EMA value each day and place a buy order there'), or bar-close near EMA; stop: below recent swing low / week's low; target: upper channel line (a well-drawn channel contains ~95% of recent prices).
findings.quote: Buying near the rising EMA is a value trade... If we buy near the moving average, near value, then our goal is to sell when the stock or commodity becomes overvalued, near the upper channel line.
findings.chapter_anchor: Answers 27, 28, 30, 59; Trade 2 (SUNW) and Trade 7 (IBM) exit answers
findings.notes: Directly corroborates V8 trend_pullback. Two concrete refinements: (a) limit-entry at projected next-bar EMA value instead of NEXT_BAR_CLOSE; (b) channel-wall target (EMA-anchored envelope) as an alternative to fixed target_r. In 24/7 crypto the daily bar is a 24h aggregation; EMA projection has no session dependency.
findings.book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

findings.strategy_name: False breakout / no-follow-through reversal
findings.mechanism: penetrating a significant extreme without follow-through exposes a vacuum of resting orders on the original side, so price reverts into the range
findings.setup_summary: When price penetrates a significant prior extreme (new low / new high) but fails to follow through and closes back inside within a short window, trade the reversal: buy a false downside breakout, short a false upside breakout. Book examples: wheat penetrated a historic low and 'ticked up instead'; BVF took out its July low with 'no follow-through.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = penetration of a prior extreme with no follow-through (close back on the original side). Invalidate = follow-through continues through the level; close beyond the swept extreme.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry next-bar close after failed breakout; stop beyond the failed-breakout extreme ('tight stop immediately below the latest lows'); target = return into range / opposite channel wall.
findings.quote: Wheat failed to follow through on that downside breakout and ticked up instead.
findings.chapter_anchor: Trade 5 (Wheat) entry answer; Answer 21 ('a false upside breakout B was followed by a false downward breakout D'); Trade 8 (BVF) entry answer
findings.notes: Corroborates V8 failed_breakout (SHORT variant). The book adds the mirror long side and an explicit short timing window ('within a week'). Crypto has no exchange gaps, so penetrate-and-reclaim is cleaner to detect on 1h bars.
findings.book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

findings.strategy_name: Kangaroo tail / tested-and-rejected level (wick rejection)
findings.mechanism: a long wick through a level that closes back on the other side shows the level was swept and rejected, trapping the sweepers and fueling the recoil
findings.setup_summary: A 'kangaroo tail' — a bar whose wick spikes through a support/resistance level and closes back on the reclaimed side — marks a level that has been tested and rejected; prices recoil from tails. Buy the rejection of a downside wick through support; short the rejection of an upside wick through resistance. A tail can also serve as the first low of a double bottom.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = wick through a windowed prior extreme with close back on the reclaimed side. Invalidate = close stays beyond the level (sweep not rejected / reclaim fails).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry next-bar close after reclaim; stop beyond the tail's extreme (the swept wick); target = opposite structure (double-bottom objective / channel).
findings.quote: Tails... show what levels prices have tested and rejected. Prices recoil from kangaroo tails.
findings.chapter_anchor: Answer 22; Answer 28 ('The kangaroo tail B serves as the first low of a double bottom'); Answer 33
findings.notes: Corroborates V8 liquidity_sweep_reclaim. High-leverage perp markets produce abundant wick-through-reclaim tails (liquidation sweeps) on 1h bars; funding-mark boundaries may cluster sweep events and are a time-feature to test.
findings.book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

findings.strategy_name: Indicator/price divergence reversal (MACD-Histogram, MACD-lines, Force Index)
findings.mechanism: a shallower indicator extreme against a deeper price extreme shows the driving side is exhausting, so the price move is due to reverse
findings.setup_summary: Bullish divergence: price makes a lower low while the indicator (MACD-Histogram, MACD-lines, or Force Index) makes a higher bottom — buy. Bearish divergence: price makes a higher high while the indicator makes a lower top — sell. A confirmed higher-timeframe divergence is strong enough to override a declining EMA trend signal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = divergence completes (indicator ticks up from a higher bottom at a lower price low, or ticks down from a lower top). Invalidate = the indicator confirms price by printing a new extreme ('if Stochastic does not turn up... it will confirm the strength of the downtrend').
findings.risk_geometry: Entry next-bar close after divergence confirmation; stop below the recent swing low (month's low in the case studies); 2% risk sizing applied on top.
findings.quote: Divergences are the strongest signals of MACD-Histogram... a bullish divergence of MACD-Histogram allowed us to override the signal of the EMA.
findings.chapter_anchor: Answers 32-33, 35, 39; Trade 1 (ORCL) and Trade 5 (Wheat) entry answers
findings.notes: 'Strongest signals' is asserted, not statistically demonstrated. Divergence is an early-signal trade that whipsaws in persistent crypto trends, so pair it with the higher-timeframe trend-override gate. Needs frozen prior-extreme refs like existing V8 experts.
findings.book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

findings.strategy_name: Elder-ray countertrend power exhaustion (Bear/Bull Power tick)
findings.mechanism: in a trend, the countertrend side exhausting its power (Bear Power negative then ticking up in an uptrend) marks the pullback's end and a resumption entry
findings.setup_summary: In an uptrend (EMA slope up), buy when a bar's low pierces below the EMA (Bear Power = low − EMA becomes negative) and Bear Power then ticks upward; in a downtrend, short when Bull Power (high − EMA) rises to or above zero and then ticks down.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = countertrend power negative then ticking up (long) / Bull Power ticking down from zero (short). Invalidate = EMA slope flips, or the countertrend power keeps printing new extremes (trend is breaking, not merely pulling back).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry next-bar close on the tick; stop beyond the signal bar's extreme (below the bar's low for longs); target = upper channel line (sell above value).
findings.quote: When the trend, identified by the slope of the EMA, is up and Bear Power becomes negative but then ticks upward, it gives a buy signal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Answers 36-37
findings.notes: A concrete oscillator trigger for pullback-in-trend; could alternatively be implemented as an alternative trigger variant of trend_pullback rather than a standalone family. Fully falsifiable with EMA plus bar high/low.
findings.book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

findings.strategy_name: Force Index (volume x price change) countertrend exhaustion entry
findings.mechanism: a negative smoothed Force Index during an uptrend shows the pullback was driven by shrinking/one-sided selling that is exhausting, so the trend resumes
findings.setup_summary: In an uptrend, buy when the 2-day EMA of Force Index (today−yesterday price change times today's volume) becomes negative; in a downtrend, sell when it turns positive. Force Index spikes identify exhaustion moves near reversal areas.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = smoothed Force Index crosses zero against the trend (negative in uptrend / positive in downtrend). Invalidate = the EMA trend flips.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry next-bar close after the zero-cross; stop below the swing low; exit on Force Index spikes or at the channel wall.
findings.quote: Force Index gives buy signals when it declines below zero during uptrends.
findings.chapter_anchor: Answers 34-35
findings.notes: Volume on crypto perps is exchange-reported and wash-trade-inflated, so the participation feature needs audit. Best framed as a volume-confirmed variant trigger for trend_pullback rather than a new family.
findings.book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

findings.strategy_name: SafeZone noise-based stop (Average Penetration x coefficient)
findings.mechanism: bar-to-bar penetration of prior extremes measures current market noise; placing the stop one coefficient-of-noise beyond recent extremes keeps it out of noise without using ATR or swing points
findings.setup_summary: Stop placement rule: in an uptrend, market noise = the extent today's low extends below yesterday's low (Downside Penetration); stop = lows − (Average Downside Penetration over the lookback period x coefficient). In a downtrend, stop = highs + (Average Upside Penetration x coefficient). Pure noise measurement — no ATR, no swing point.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Applies to any open position: stop is hit -> exit. If the trend flips, switch which penetration side (upside vs downside) is used for stops.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry per the trend method; stop = Average Downside Penetration x coefficient below lows (long) or Average Upside Penetration x coefficient above highs (short); lookback window and coefficient are the only parameters; stop is sized to clear recent noise.
findings.quote: Market noise is the extent by which today's extreme price extends outside yesterday's extreme... multiply Average Downside Penetration by the coefficient and subtract it from the lows to place stops in uptrends.
findings.chapter_anchor: Answer 61; also BVF exit answer (buy orders 'as many points below the EMA as the average depth of past penetrations')
findings.notes: Strong candidate for a V8 stop-placement rule alongside atr_stop: uses bar-to-bar extreme penetration, robust in 24/7 markets with no gaps. Complements the V8 dead-thesis exit: SafeZone handles normal noise stops, trend-flip handles thesis invalidation.
findings.book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

findings.strategy_name: 2% Rule — per-trade risk cap
findings.mechanism: capping per-trade dollar risk as a fixed fraction of equity keeps a losing streak from breaching survival thresholds regardless of stop distance
findings.setup_summary: Never risk more than 2% of account equity on any single trade, including commissions and slippage; position size = (2% x equity) / (risk per unit = entry − stop). Far stops force smaller size; tight stops allow larger size. When losing, keep size consistent or reduce it — never increase size to recoup losses.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A trade is rejected if its dollar risk (size x stop distance + costs) exceeds 2% of equity; reduce size to fit, or skip the trade.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry/stop come from the method; size is derived so that risk <= 2% of equity; this is the admission gate applied to every trade.
findings.quote: The 2% Rule, the most important rule of money management, protects you from ever losing more than 2% of your account equity on any single trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Money Management chapter, Answers 70-75, 81-82
findings.notes: Maps directly to V8 RiskGate deterministic admission and position sizing. In high-leverage perp crypto, per-trade risk as a % of equity is the key scaling input and must respect the one-exposure-per-direction rule.
findings.book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

findings.strategy_name: 6% Rule — monthly loss cap with hard stop for the month
findings.mechanism: anchoring the heat budget to start-of-period equity and freezing new admissions once realized + open risk consumes the budget protects capital across consecutive losses
findings.setup_summary: Record equity at the start of the month. If equity dips 6% below that level (realized losses plus risk on open trades), stop trading for the balance of the month. Total risk in open trades plus realized losses never exceeds 6% of start-of-month equity.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rule blocks new trades once month-to-date realized + open risk >= 6% of start-of-month equity; risk budget can only be freed by closing trades to breakeven/winning (moving stops to breakeven removes that trade from the risk pool).
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop geometry — a period admission gate. Breakeven-stop moves free risk budget (trades C/D in Answer 78).
findings.quote: To observe the 6% Rule, you must stop trading as soon as your equity dips 6% below that level. Stay out for the balance of the month.
findings.chapter_anchor: Answers 77-80
findings.notes: Refines V8's heat cap into a fixed period budget anchored at period start with a hard stop-for-period admission rule. In 24/7 crypto the 'month' is an arbitrary anchor — test calendar-month vs rolling-window variants. Companion lifecycle rule from the same chapter: 'We may move stops only in the direction of the trade, never against it.'
findings.book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

findings.strategy_name: Triple Screen — three-timeframe hierarchy (strategic/tactical/execution)
findings.mechanism: higher timeframes set the strategic direction that trades on lower timeframes follow; conflicting signals across timeframes are filtered out rather than averaged
findings.setup_summary: Make the strategic (bullish/bearish) decision on the highest timeframe, the tactical entry/exit decision on the middle timeframe, and execution on the lowest (weekly -> daily -> intraday, factor-of-five between timeframes). Filter conflicting signals between timeframes, keeping only aligned signals; combine one trend-following indicator group with oscillators so their messages are balanced.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No trade when timeframes conflict; the method prescribes standing aside or reducing size on conflict. The strategic decision must be made before looking at the tactical chart.
findings.risk_geometry: Methodology layer — no direct geometry; risk sizing still governed by the 2%/6% rules.
findings.quote: If you work with weekly, daily, and intraday charts, then make your strategic decision... on the weekly chart, then tactical on the dailies, and find entry and exit points using intraday charts.
findings.chapter_anchor: Answer 45; Answer 44 (factor-of-five); Answer 26
findings.notes: V8 is single-timeframe (BTCUSDT 1h). The transferable lesson is the regime-filter pattern: higher-timeframe trend (e.g., 4h/1d EMA slope) as a gate on 1h expert admissions — a refinement candidate for trend_pullback's trend requirement. 24/7 crypto has no session boundaries, but bar aggregation is arbitrary (weekly-equivalent = 7x24h aggregation).
findings.book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

findings.strategy_name: Opening-range breakout (narrow range expands; wide range caps the day)
findings.mechanism: a narrow opening range concentrates participants and sets up an expansion; a wide opening range has already absorbed the day's flow and caps the day
findings.setup_summary: Define the opening range (first ~30-60 minutes of the session). A narrow opening range tends to produce an important breakout; a wide opening range may set the day's high and low. In an established trend, a breakout from the opening range in the trend direction is the first high-quality intraday signal (book example: downside breakout from the opening range confirms a downtrend and gives the day's first short).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = price breaks the opening range in the trend direction. Invalidate = wide opening range (fade or stand aside); breakout fails and price returns into the range.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on range breakout; stop on the far side of the range; intraday target (channel / day's projection); day-trade only — no overnight risk.
findings.quote: A wide opening range may define the high and the low of the day, but prices are likely to break out of a narrow opening range.
findings.chapter_anchor: Answers 51-52, 56
findings.notes: Crypto has no opening bell; anchor the reference range to the daily UTC open (funding-mark boundary) or a fixed session window on 1h bars. The same chapter's U-shaped intraday volume curve (Answer 51 — pros dominate near session close) is a flow/time feature input if a session is defined.
findings.book: Come Into My Trading Room (Study Guide) 2002

findings.strategy_name: Hammer bottom-reversal at support
findings.mechanism: long lower wick shows the market sold off intra-session then was bought back to close near the high; buyers rejected lower prices at the hammer's low
findings.setup_summary: After a downtrend (ideally confirming a prior support level or an oversold condition), a 1h bar prints a small real body (black or white) at the top of the bar's range, little or no upper shadow, and a lower shadow at least 2x the height of the real body. Buy on the hammer bar's close with a stop under the low of the hammer's lower shadow; the hammer low acts as support, and the first bounce may fail and retest it.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Dead-thesis is a close under the hammer's low (an intraday wick under is not enough); a hammer not preceded by a downtrend is not a hammer (shape alone is insufficient - the trend defines the pattern).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close of the hammer session (V8: NEXT_BAR_CLOSE). Stop: below the frozen low of the hammer's lower shadow (swing ref). Target: prior resistance / falling resistance line / prior pivot high - candles give no targets. Expiry not stated; book notes first bounce after a hammer often fails and retests the hammer's low before a real rally.
findings.quote: A hammer gives a potent signal when it appears after a significant downtrend or in an oversold market... there may be selling on a rally from the hammer. Therefore, the first bounce after the hammer may fail, and the market may return to test the hammer's support.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch2 S1 (pp.30-41) + Ch4/Ch6 worked examples (buy on hammer close, stop under hammer low, p.117, p.191)
findings.notes: Distinct from existing liquidity_sweep_reclaim: hammer is defined by body/shadow ratios (lower shadow >= 2x body, small body at top of range), not by sweeping a windowed prior extreme. The hammer low is a natural frozen ref usable as both stop and still_valid pivot. Fills-at-close make the 'buy on hammer close' entry clean.
findings.book: The Candlestick Course 2003

findings.strategy_name: Engulfing-pattern top/bottom reversal
findings.mechanism: one session's real body completely wraps the prior opposite-color real body, showing supply overwhelmed demand (bearish) or demand overwhelmed supply (bullish)
findings.setup_summary: Bearish: in an uptrend, a black bar's real body completely wraps the prior white bar's real body (only the real body must be engulfed, shadows may exceed). Short on that bar's close; the high of the pattern is resistance. Bullish: in a downtrend, a white bar wraps the prior black bar; long on close; the pattern's lows are support. Context rule is strict: the engulfing combination after the wrong trend is not a reversal signal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A close beyond the engulfing bar's opposite extreme negates (e.g., close above pattern high for a short = resistance broken). Engulfing after a decline (not a rally) for the bearish variant is explicitly NOT a signal - context, not shape, makes the pattern.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: close of the engulfing bar. Stop: beyond the opposite extreme of the pattern (above pattern high for shorts, below pattern lows for longs). Target: structure (box bottom/top, prior S/R, falling resistance line) since candles give no targets. The book's real-world demo shorts a box range from a gravestone-doji/engulfing top at 420 to the box bottom at 370.
findings.quote: If the market is solid, the lows of the bullish engulfing pattern should be support. Thus, for those who are long based on this pattern, there should be a stop under the lows of this pattern.
findings.notes: The book repeats the context rule many times and shows cases where the exact same candle combination is NOT a reversal because the prior trend was wrong - a strong spec-level lesson for pattern classifiers. Volume confirmation (light volume on the engulfed bar, spike on the engulfing bar) strengthens the signal.
findings.book: The Candlestick Course 2003

findings.strategy_name: Morning/evening star three-bar reversal
findings.mechanism: trend bar, then an isolated small-body bar showing indecision, then a strong counter-trend bar that closes well into the first bar's body = control handed over
findings.setup_summary: Morning star (bottom): in a downtrend, a long black bar, then a small real body (spinning top or doji) that gaps away from the prior body (ideally no body overlap; shadow intrusion allowed), then a white bar closing well into the first black bar's real body. Evening star is the mirror in an uptrend (long white, isolated small body, black bar closing into the first body). Entry on the close of the third bar.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Third bar fails to close well into the first bar's body (pattern incomplete); second (star) body overlapping the first body weakens/voids the pattern; opposite move beyond the third bar's extreme negates.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: close of the third bar. Stop: beyond the third bar's low/high (or pattern extremes). Target: structure. Volume rule: light volume on the first bar plus heavy volume on the third bar intensifies the signal.
findings.quote: A long, black candle develops, assuring the bears that they continue to be in command. Then a small real body or spinning top appears, gapping down at the open... The final candle of the morning star pattern is a white real body that moves deeply into the first session's black candle.
findings.notes: The 'gap away' between the star and the first body requires non-overlapping bodies, which is structurally rarer in continuous 24/7 perp markets than in exchange sessions. The doji-star variants (morning/evening doji star) overlap with the doji finding. Lower priority than hammer/engulfing.
findings.book: The Candlestick Course 2003

findings.strategy_name: Doji top-exhaustion (Northern doji at resistance)
findings.mechanism: open equals close after an extended move shows balance/indecision; in an overbought rally the bulls can no longer sustain the highs, leaving the market 'tired' and vulnerable to a turn
findings.setup_summary: After an extended/overbought rally (ideally after a tall white bar and/or at a prior resistance zone), a doji (open approx equal to close) forms. It is a top-exhaustion alert, most meaningful when doji are rare and when it confirms a resistance area. Action needs follow-through; a close above the doji's high (or the highest high of the doji and prior bar) invalidates.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Close above the doji's high = 'bulls are refreshed', signal dead. Doji mid-range or inside a box range = no signal (no trend to reverse). Southern doji in a decline is weak unless it confirms a support level. Doji frequent on the chart = diminished significance.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: at confirmation (doji is an alert; book's worked example waits for follow-through). Stop: above the frozen doji/prior-bar high. Target: structure. Gravestone doji (open/low/close at session low) is the stronger top variant.
findings.quote: When the market is rising and overbought, and then a doji appears after a tall, white candle, the Japanese say that the market is tired... A close over the doji's high could be a signal that the bulls have regained a foothold.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch2 S2 (pp.43-53), Ch4 (gravestone doji confirming box-top resistance, p.115)
findings.notes: Doji are frequent on 1h crypto bars, and the book itself says doji lose meaning when common - so the family needs a rarity/context gate (confirm resistance, follow tall white bar, overbought). Clear invalidation semantics (close over the frozen high) fit V8's still_valid pattern.
findings.book: The Candlestick Course 2003

findings.strategy_name: Change of polarity: old resistance becomes new support
findings.mechanism: price memory: once a level is broken by a committed close, participants who missed the move buy the first retest of the flipped level; old S/R inverts role
findings.setup_summary: After the market closes above a multi-tested resistance area, that prior resistance zone becomes new support; buy the first retest that holds on a close basis. Symmetrically, a close below prior support turns that zone into resistance; sell the retest that fails to close above it.
findings.trigger_invalidation: For a long on flipped support: a close back inside/under the old resistance zone invalidates the flip (close-based, not intraday poke).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: retest of the flipped zone holding on a close (V8: NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after the retest bar). Stop: below/above the flipped zone (a defined swing ref). Target: next S/R level or structure.
findings.quote: Once a market breaks over a multitested resistance area, the prior resistance area is converted into new support. In contrast, markets that fall through prior support have trouble climbing back through it again since that previous support is frequently converted into resistance.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch1 S3, pp.23-24 (Exhibit 1.7)
findings.notes: Nison explicitly labels this not a Japanese technique but a core principle of technical analysis. Horizontal level flips are directly constructible from 1h BTCUSDT marketstate location features and are corroborated across the library. Candidate family: supply_demand_zone.
findings.book: The Candlestick Course 2003

findings.strategy_name: Close-based break of support/resistance
findings.mechanism: a close beyond a level reflects committed willingness to hold the price there, unlike an intraday poke; therefore break validity, window support, and S/R holding are all defined on closes
findings.setup_summary: A break of resistance/support is only confirmed by a close above/below the level; an intraday break that closes back inside is not a break and is not a signal. A bar that dips below support but closes back inside the box range is 'not as bearish' - buyers returned before the close.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A close back inside the range voids the break signal and keeps the level intact; the level is not dead until a close beyond it confirms.
findings.risk_geometry: Methodology rule feeding V8's breakout_retest backlog and failed_breakout family: entry on the close-based break (NEXT_BAR_CLOSE), stop back beyond the level, dead-thesis on close back inside.
findings.quote: An intraday break of support or resistance does not have the same significance as a severing of support or resistance on a close... Resistance or support is not considered broken unless by a close.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch1 S3 (p.22) + Ch4 Trading Guidelines (p.122)
findings.notes: Directly reinforces V8's failed_breakout (close below windowed prior high) and the close-based semantics already in the spec. In 24/7 crypto the 'close' is the 1h bar close; no exchange-gap nuance applies.
findings.book: The Candlestick Course 2003

findings.strategy_name: Major-trend direction filter for reversal signals
findings.mechanism: reversal signals aligned with the major trend have better base rates; counter-trend reversal signals are exits or alerts, not new-position triggers
findings.setup_summary: Initiate a new position on a bullish candle signal only when the major trend is up (e.g., signal arriving after a pullback to support in an uptrend); a bullish signal in a downtrend is used only to cover shorts or as an alert to sell the bounce. The more overbought/oversold the market, the more vulnerable it is to reversal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - an admission gate; a violation means 'do not initiate', not invalidation of a position.
findings.risk_geometry: Gate applied before risk_geometry construction (RiskGate-level admission rule); counter-trend signals remain usable for cover/exits, never for new entries.
findings.quote: If you see a reversal signal, consider initiating a new position only if that signal is in the direction of the major trend... A bullish candle signal in a bear trend should be used either to cover shorts or as an alert that the market may rally and to use that rally to sell.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch1 S3 (pp.20-21) + Ch4 Guidelines (p.122)
findings.notes: Strong candidate for a RiskGate admission rule or expert-level regime filter in V8. Note the book's softer definition of 'reversal' (up to neutral, not up to down) which aligns with V8's evidence-bound framing.
findings.book: The Candlestick Course 2003

findings.strategy_name: Mandatory risk/reward gate before any candle-signal trade
findings.mechanism: even a perfect pattern is not a trade unless expected reward exceeds defined risk; candles provide no price targets, so targets must come from Western structure (pivots, trend lines)
findings.setup_summary: For any candle-signal trade: define risk as entry close to stop (e.g., under the hammer low), define the target from structure (prior high, falling resistance line, pivot). Skip the trade when risk approx equals reward (book example: $2 risk vs $2 target = no trade); only take it when the R multiple is attractive (book's worked hammer example accepts 1:2.5).
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - a gate, not a signal.
findings.risk_geometry: This gate is what produces V8's target_r/stop_r pairs; it explicitly recommends skipping ~1:1 setups and taking the trade only when reward exceeds risk. Risk measured from the signal bar's close to the stop ref; target from location features.
findings.quote: NEVER PLACE A TRADE WITH A CANDLE SIGNAL UNTIL YOU HAVE CONSIDERED THE RISK/REWARD OF THE POTENTIAL TRADE... Bullish hammer or not, if the risk is $2 and the target is also $2 from the hammer's buy signal, this is not a trade that warrants action.
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's risk_geometry spec and its 'no economic claim without a gate' philosophy. Two limitations stated by the book: candles do not give price targets, and no signal should be traded standalone - targets come from location features (prior pivots, trend lines).
findings.book: The Candlestick Course 2003

findings.strategy_name: Hanging man top with next-bar close-under confirmation
findings.mechanism: a hammer-shaped bar after an uptrend shows an intraday sell-off that was bought back; longs who entered near the close are vulnerable, and a next-bar close under its real body traps them, risking a cascade of selling
findings.setup_summary: After an uptrend (preferably at or near the high of the move), a bar forms with a small real body at the top of the range, little or no upper shadow, and a lower shadow at least 2x the real body - the same shape as a hammer but in an uptrend. Do not short on the pattern bar: only short on a subsequent bar that closes under the hanging man's real body.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No confirmation close under the hanging man's real body = no sell signal (the book's worked exhibits explicitly conclude 'we did not get any sell signals'); a close above its high negates.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: close of the confirming bar (the close under the hanging man's real body). Stop: above the frozen hanging-man high. Target: structure. This is a trigger-lag design: the entry fires on a confirmation close, not on the pattern bar close.
findings.quote: For the hanging man's bullish long lower shadow one must wait for a close under the hanging man's real body before becoming bearish... if the market closes lower the next day, those who bought on the close of the hanging man day are now left 'hanging' with a losing position.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch2 S1 (pp.30-31, 40), Ch4 Guidelines (p.122)
findings.notes: Directly informs V8 trigger semantics: some candle reversals require a confirmation bar (entry on the confirmation close / NEXT_BAR_CLOSE), not the pattern bar itself. This is a lifecycle/trigger design lesson generalizable to doji and high-wave tops.
findings.book: The Candlestick Course 2003

findings.strategy_name: Small real bodies / long-shadow series as trend-losing-force alert
findings.mechanism: shrinking real bodies and mounting rejection shadows show the controlling side can no longer sustain closes at the extremes, so the prior trend is losing force
findings.setup_summary: During an ascent, a series of small real bodies (spinning tops) or long upper shadows implies the bulls do not have full control - a warning not to follow longs, and near overextension/resistance a reversal may be forming. During a descent, a series of long lower shadows implies the bears lack full control. Inside a box range these carry no signal (there is no trend to reverse).
findings.trigger_invalidation: No trade implication inside a box range; a single small body alone is insufficient - it is a contextual alert, not an entry signal.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry geometry; used to scale back existing positions, defer entries, or gate continuation (e.g., do not add longs in a channel showing consecutive long upper shadows).
findings.quote: If there are small real bodies (either black or white) during an ascent, caution is warranted from the long side... Such spinning tops are a warning not to follow this market from the long side... A series of long upper shadows as the market is ascending implies that the bulls do not have full control.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch2 S1 (pp.28-30) + Ch4 Trading Guidelines (p.121-122)
findings.notes: Propose as marketstate features: small-body frequency and shadow-dominance ratios over a recent window, feeding exhaustion alerts or entry gating. Corroborates the existing 'trend losing force' concept already used informally in V8 design.
findings.book: The Candlestick Course 2003

findings.strategy_name: Volume-confirmed reversal patterns
findings.mechanism: the force behind a reversal is credible only when volume dries up on the trend/pattern bar and expands on the confirmation bar; low-volume moves lack conviction and often fail
findings.setup_summary: For a reversal pattern (engulfing, star, belt-hold), treat the signal as stronger when the first/trend bar prints light volume and the final/confirmation bar prints heavy volume (e.g., light volume on the black bar of a bullish engulfing plus a volume spike on the white turnaround candle; a belt-hold off support 'on strong volume' has more fuel).
findings.trigger_invalidation: A confidence filter, not a standalone signal; absent volume data means a weaker signal, not an invalidation.
findings.risk_geometry: Confidence filter on pattern-based entries; no geometry of its own.
findings.quote: Light volume develops on the first candle line, followed by heavy volume on the third candle line. The light volume tells you that the force propelling the initial trend was weakening... Strong volume shooting into the third candle fuels the force that ignites the new trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch3 S2 Side Light (p.85); Ch2 S3 (p.57, belt-hold volume); Ch3 S1 Q21 answer
findings.notes: Perp volume (taker/notional) is available and point-in-time constructible for BTCUSDT; implementable as a participation-feature filter on new/existing candle experts. The book repeatedly stresses merging volume with candles.
findings.book: The Candlestick Course 2003

findings.strategy_name: Windows (gaps) as continuation and S/R zones
findings.mechanism: a window is a price vacuum where no trades occurred; unfilled price levels magnetize price and act as support/resistance on corrections - 'corrections stop at the window'
findings.setup_summary: A rising window (gap up: no overlap between the prior bar's high and the current bar's low) is a bullish continuation whose entire zone is support, most critically the window bottom; a falling window is bearish continuation with resistance at the window top. Size is irrelevant - even a 1-tick window counts. Break of window support requires a close under the bottom; once breached, the window is voided.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A close through the window's critical edge voids it (once a rising window's support is broken, it is no longer support on a later rally); the book explicitly warns against fading large gaps (high risk).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on a pullback into the window holding on a close. Stop: below window bottom (rising) / above window top (falling). Break by close voids the level and shifts attention to the next window or structure.
findings.quote: 'Corrections stop at the window.' That means windows often become support and resistance areas... the most important area of a rising window is the bottom of that window.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch3 S4 (pp.101-110), Ch5 (breakaway-gap exhibits), Ch4 Guidelines (p.122)
findings.notes: In continuous 24/7 perp markets, true price vacuums between consecutive bars are rare except during liquidation cascades or venue halts; funding does not create gaps. The vacuum logic overlaps the liquidity_vacuum mechanism already used by failed_breakout. Defer; if ever implemented, treat the window as a vacuum level rather than an exchange gap.
findings.book: The Candlestick Course 2003

book_title: The Candlestick Course (2003) — Steve Nison
Dave Landry on Swing Trading (2001)

findings.strategy_name: Trend pullback (simple/shallow pullback)
findings.mechanism: Markets thrust, correct, then resume; entering only on resumption avoids tops and false reversals
findings.setup_summary: Strong uptrend (ADX>=30 and +DMI>-DMI, or Trend Qualifiers) that has made a two-month (~43-bar) new high; price then makes 3-7 consecutive lower highs (width) without retracing more than ~15% (shallow depth). Enter next bar on a trade 1/16 above today's high; protective stop 1/16 below the lowest bar of the pullback, capped at 5% of price.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price trades above the prior bar's high after a 3-7 bar pullback from a two-month high. Thesis invalidated: trade below the pullback low, or pullback exceeding ~50% retracement of the prior trend / width beyond ~7 bars (momentum negated).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: stop-order 1/16 above prior bar high (next-bar trigger, valid ~2 bars). Stop: 1/16 below lowest bar of the setup, capped at 5% risk if wider. Target: partial profits at 1R (2-for-1), trail remainder; typical holding 2-7 bars. Expiry: time-stop ~7 bars unless strong trend.
findings.quote: The width should be wide enough so the market has enough time to correct but not too long as to negate the market's initial momentum. Three-to-seven bars is a good rule of thumb here.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, Pullbacks (pp. 33-58)
findings.notes: Confirms the existing trend_pullback expert and adds concrete parameters: width 3-7 bars, shallow depth <=15%, two-month (43 trading-day) new-high location. The book also warns early pullbacks in a stair-step are superior to later ones. On BTCUSD 1h, 'trading day' maps to 1h bar; a two-month high is ~43*24=1032 bars, which is a viable frozen location reference.
findings.book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

findings.strategy_name: Deep pullback snapback (knee-jerk rebalance)
findings.mechanism: A sharp deep pullback in a strong trend creates an out-of-balance situation; panicked shorts and shaken longs force a violent snap-back in the trend direction
findings.setup_summary: Strong trend (ADX>=30 or Trend Qualifiers) with a two-month new high; then a sharp sell-off of >=15% (deep pullback) over 3-7 bars. Enter next bar 1/16 above today's high expecting a short, sharp knee-jerk snap-back toward the original trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade above prior bar high after a >=15% deep pullback in a strong trend. Invalidation: trade below the setup low (stop); if the deep pullback does not reclaim quickly the 'snap-back' thesis is dead.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: 1/16 above prior bar high. Stop: book uses a fixed 5%-of-price stop for deep pullbacks (setup low often >8% away). Expected holding: short and sharp (days not weeks). Target: 2-for-1 scale-out, windfall capture on the parabolic move.
findings.quote: Like a rubber band being stretched to extremes, the market often violently “snaps back” in the direction of the longer-term trend as shorts scramble to cover and longs jump back in.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, Pullbacks - Snapbacks (pp. 46-51)
findings.notes: Depth-threshold variant of the pullback family (a parameter variant = one multiplicity unit in V8), but with a distinct payoff profile: short sharp knee-jerk vs smooth longer continuation. Highly relevant to perps where leveraged longs get liquidated on deep 1h dips before mean reversion - falsifiable and screenable, not to be assumed.
findings.book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

findings.strategy_name: Trend Knockout (stop-hunt re-entry)
findings.mechanism: In a strong trend, a two-bar low knocks out weak hands and stop holders; the resulting vacuum lets the trend resume
findings.setup_summary: Strong trend (ADX>=30 with +DMI>-DMI, or Trend Qualifiers). The market makes at least a two-bar low (trades below the prior two bars' lows). Buy next day or the day after, 1/16 above today's high; protective stop below the low of the knockout bar, capped at 5% of price.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade above the prior bar's high within 1-2 bars after a 2+ bar low in a strong trend. Invalidation: trade below the knockout-bar low; deeper 3+ bar knockouts are considered stronger but less fillable.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: stop-order 1/16 above current bar high, valid up to 2 bars. Stop: 1/16 below low of the knockout bar, max 5% risk. Target: trend continuation; 2-for-1 scale-out, ~7-bar time stop.
findings.quote: Trend Knockouts (TKOs) identify strong trends from which the weak hands have already been knocked out. By placing your order above the market, you have the potential to capture profits as the trend resumes.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, Fakeouts and False Moves - Trend Knockouts (pp. 62-67)
findings.notes: New expert family; mechanism matches V8's liquidity lexicon ('stop-run creates vacuum'). Complementary to liquidity_sweep_reclaim but close-based (2-bar low) rather than wick-through-extreme. Corroborated by the book's repeated lesson that second entries after being stopped out are often the best entries.
findings.book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

findings.strategy_name: Double Top Knockout (false-reversal continuation)
findings.mechanism: A false double-top reversal attracts eager top-pickers and shakes out nervous longs; when the reversal fails, trapped traders' covering and re-entry fuel trend resumption
findings.setup_summary: Strong trend; market makes a new two-month high; makes another new high no sooner than 3 bars later (allowing the false double top to form); then makes at least a two-bar low that 'confirms' the double top. Buy next bar 1/16 above today's high; stop 1/16 below yesterday's low (max 5%).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade above today's high after the 2-bar low pullback from the second high. Invalidation: trade below the setup low; a genuine reversal would not trigger the buy-stop.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: 1/16 above today's high (next bar). Stop: 1/16 below yesterday's low, capped at 5%. Target: continuation above the double top; 2-for-1 management.
findings.quote: Reversal patterns of markets in strong uptrends attract eager top pickers. These patterns also shake out the nervous longs. When the reversal fails to follow through, these players are trapped on the wrong side of the market or knocked out.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, Fakeouts and False Moves - Double Top Knockout (pp. 68-74)
findings.notes: Continuation-side complement to V8's failed_breakout: it buys the failure of a counter-trend reversal instead of shorting a failed trend breakout. Requires a two-month-high location feature. On BTC 1h the 'two-month calendar high' is a ~43-day windowed extreme - implement as a frozen reference.
findings.book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

findings.strategy_name: Trend Pivot Pullback (false-rally shakeout re-entry)
findings.mechanism: A one-day false rally inside a pullback shakes out fast money; re-entry above the failed rally high catches the true trend resumption
findings.setup_summary: Strong trend; two-month new high; 1-5 lower highs; then a one-day rally (high greater than prior day's high) followed by a lower high, forming a pivot high. Buy tomorrow or next day 1/16 above this pivot high; stop 1/16 below the lowest bar in the setup (max 5%).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade above the pivot high within 2 bars. Invalidation: trade below the setup low; pivot high must sit below the two-month high or it is not a pullback. Strictly safer than a Simple Pullback at the cost of missed fills.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: 1/16 above the pivot high, order valid 2 bars. Stop: 1/16 below lowest bar in the setup, max 5%. Target: resumption toward/through the old high; 2-for-1 scale-out.
findings.quote: Trend Pivot Pullbacks seek to identify pullbacks that have had this false rally. This rally draws in, and subsequently shakes out the “fast money”—traders without staying power (money) and/or patience.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, Fakeouts and False Moves - Trend Pivot (False Rally) Pullbacks (pp. 75-81)
findings.notes: Second-entry variant of the pullback family with a distinct trigger (pivot-high retest) that filters false first entries. On 1h crypto the pivot definition is bar-based and fully executable via a stop order above the pivot high.
findings.book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

findings.strategy_name: Bow Tie (MA proper-order rollover with countertrend confirmation)
findings.mechanism: Multiple moving averages converging then re-spreading marks a major trend-regime shift; entering only after a countertrend bar filters false starts
findings.setup_summary: With 10-SMA / 20-EMA / 30-EMA: the averages converge and re-spread, shifting from proper downtrend order (10<20<30) to proper uptrend order (10>20>30) over ~3-4 days; then a lower low (longs) / higher high (shorts); buy next bar 1/16 above today's high; cancel the order if the market trades back to the 20-EMA.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade above today's high after the countertrend confirmation. Invalidation: price trades back to the 20-EMA before fill - order cancelled (trend-shift thesis dead). Pulling back to the 10-SMA is considered normal/healthy.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: 1/16 above today's high. Stop: below lowest bar in the setup, max 5%. Target: new trend; 2-for-1 management; order-cancel rule tied to 20-EMA.
findings.quote: In spite of what many books on technical analysis will tell you, moving-average crossovers do not work... You often avoid false moves by waiting for a countertrend by only entering if the trend re-asserts itself.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, Bow Ties (pp. 83-91)
findings.notes: Book explicitly rejects naive MA crossovers and requires countertrend confirmation - a methodological lesson for any MA-based family. Higher signal latency than pullback/knockout families; on 1h crypto the 10/20/30 convergence needs ~30+ bars of lookback. Could serve as a trend-regime-shift detector feeding other families.
findings.book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

findings.strategy_name: High-Level Micro Double Bottom (continuation)
findings.mechanism: In a strong trend, a brief two-pivot-low consolidation (micro double bottom) resolves upward; the twice-tested level becomes strong support
findings.setup_summary: Strong trend (ADX>=30 or Trend Qualifiers) that has made a two-month high; the stock makes a pivot low (low surrounded by two higher lows), then another pivot low at or near the same level; buy next bar 1/16 above the high of the right side of the second pivot low; stop below the lowest bar of the setup (max 5%).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade above the high of the second (right) pivot formation. Invalidation: trade below the setup's lowest bar; the two pivot lows must be at or near the same level.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: 1/16 above the right pivot high. Stop: below lowest bar of the setup, max 5%. Target: trend continuation; 2-for-1 management.
findings.quote: We define the pattern as two pivot lows which form at or near the same level.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Micro Patterns - High-Level Micro Double Bottom (pp. 93-99)
findings.notes: The book admits micro patterns are 'discretionary in nature,' so formalization requires a precise pivot-window definition (a low surrounded by two higher lows). The 'tested level becomes support' mechanism corroborates V8's location feature group and liquidity-sweep ideas.
findings.book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

findings.strategy_name: Trend Qualifiers (multi-factor trend-strength composite)
findings.mechanism: A composite of observable trend clues - base breakout, new two-month high/low, strong/weak closes, wide-range bars, gaps/laps with the trend, MA proper order/slope/daylight - indicates trend quality and trend direction
findings.setup_summary: A market is in a strong uptrend when several qualifiers coincide: base breakout (wide-range bar after sideways), new two-month high, closes in the top 25% of range, range wider than prior 5 bars, gaps/laps in trend direction, 10-SMA>20-EMA>30-EMA with positive slope and 'daylight' (lows above the MAs). Standardized proxy: ADX>=30 with +DMI>-DMI. Markets trend only ~30% of the time.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - this is a filtering/methodology construct, not a standalone trade. Conflicting qualifiers (low ADX, no daylight, improper MA order) argue against trend-assuming entries; ADX>=25 for early trends vs >=30/35 for strong trends is the stated trade-off.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target. Used to gate admissible setups (trend filter) and for scanning: ADX>=30, historical volatility >=40%, 10-day avg volume >=100k, price >=$20-30, spread <=1/4 point.
findings.quote: Strong Closes—When a stock closes within the top 25% of its range, it suggests that traders were willing to carry the position overnight.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, Trend Qualifiers (pp. 17-27); Chapter 4 Stock Selection (pp. 29-31); Appendix ADX (pp. 224-233)
findings.notes: Direct input for V8's trend feature group: ADX/DMI, MA proper-order + slope + daylight, close-location-in-range, wide-range-bar, and new-high features. These can refine the trend qualification every trend-following expert consumes and act as a regime gate. 'Markets only trend about 30% of the time' is a regime-mix warning for any trend family.
findings.book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

findings.strategy_name: 6/100 HV ratio volatility compression (mean reversion)
