findings.mechanism: Realized volatility is mean-reverting: when short-term (6-bar) HV drops below half of long-term (100-bar) HV, an outsized move is imminent (direction unknown)
findings.setup_summary: Compute 6-bar and 100-bar historical volatilities (annualized stdev of log returns). When the 6/100 HV ratio drops below 0.50 while price consolidates, a large move is likely as volatility reverts to its mean; pair with a directional setup (pullback, TKO, DT-KO, micro pattern) to pick the side.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 6/100 HV ratio <0.50 (volatility compression). The signal carries no direction - a directional expert must supply the side; if no setup forms, the signal is not tradeable. Exit when vol reverts / the directional setup completes.
findings.risk_geometry: Filter/regime only; no entry/stop of its own. Book examples pair it with existing setups using the standard 5%-capped stops.
findings.quote: when shorter term HV readings dropped below 50% of their longer-term HV readings, a large market move was prone to ensue as volatility reverts back to its mean.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, Finding Explosive Moves (pp. 111-121)
findings.notes: Attributed to Connors & Hayward (Investment Secrets of a Hedge Fund Manager); the book stresses it does NOT predict direction. For V8 this is a volatility feature + regime filter that can gate or enrich directional families. Volatility mean reversion is strong in 24/7 crypto; on 1h the 6/100 windows map to 6 and 100 bars.
findings.book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

findings.strategy_name: Oscillator Swing System (3-10 oscillator stretch + open-to-close reversal)
findings.mechanism: A five-bar stretch of the 3-10 price oscillator marks a short-term overbought/oversold extreme; the same-day open-to-close reversal confirms the snap back
findings.setup_summary: On a market NOT in an ADX-confirmed opposite trend: when the 3-SMA-minus-10-SMA oscillator has 5 consecutive down days (oversold) and the market closes above its open, go long on the close; exit on the close 3-7 days later. Mirror for shorts after 5 consecutive up days and a close below the open.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 5 consecutive oscillator-down days + close above open (long side). Invalidation: ADX>=30 with -DMI>+DMI (downtrend) prohibits longs; the 3-7 day close exit is mandatory. Book: short-side results much weaker than long side in the 1990-2000 bull regime.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on the close of the signal day. Exit: fixed on the close 3-7 days later. Published backtest used no stops or money management.
findings.quote: The 3-10 oscillator must have at least five consecutive down days. If the market closes above the open, go long on the close. Exit on the close three to seven days later.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, Market Timing for Swing Trading - Oscillator Swing System (pp. 129-132)
findings.notes: Published 10-year S&P futures backtest: 143 trades, ~65% winners, profit factor 2.28 (long side much stronger - regime-dependent). The '5 consecutive days' stretch and open-to-close reversal are bar-based and executable on BTC 1h, but must be rescaled (5 bars vs 5 days) and frozen-registered. V8 currently has no active mean-reversion family, so this is a backlog candidate, not a formalization.
findings.book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

findings.strategy_name: CVR III-Modified (fear-index extreme reversal)
findings.mechanism: An implied-volatility/fear index is mean-reverting; an extreme reading that begins to reverse intraday precedes a 3-7 day market reversal
findings.setup_summary: For longs: the VIX low is above its 10-day MA, the VIX closes >=10% above its 10-day MA, and the VIX closes below its open -> buy the market on the close; exit on the close the day the VIX trades back below its prior 10-day MA (vol reversion). Mirror for shorts (VIX high below 10-day MA, close >=10% below, close above open).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: all three VIX conditions on the same day. Invalidation: the fear index keeps extending away from its MA (no reversion); the exit event is itself the reversion to the 10-day MA.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: close of the signal day. Exit: close on the day the vol index reverts to its MA (typically 3-7 days). Published backtest used no stops.
findings.quote: once the VIX was 10% or more away from its moving average, the stock market had a nearly 70% chance of reversing over the next three-to-seven days as the VIX returned to more average levels.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, Market Timing for Swing Trading - CVR III-Modified (pp. 138-141)
findings.notes: Published backtest: 76% reversal accuracy over 3 days, profit factor 3.83 (long 84% / short 56%, bull-market biased). No VIX exists for BTCUSD; analogues are Deribit DVOL or funding-rate extremes, which sit outside current V8 data scope, and this is a market-level timing overlay that V8 keeps ABSENT by default under the complexity budget - hence DEFER_GATED. The mechanism is already partially captured by the realized-vol feature (finding NEW_volatility_mean_reversion).
findings.book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

findings.strategy_name: 2-for-1 money management and swing-trade risk rules
findings.mechanism: Skewed payoff (many small losses, few home runs) requires capping initial risk, banking partial profits at 1R, and protecting the remainder at breakeven so no single trade can be damaging
findings.setup_summary: Protective stop on every trade, placed below the setup's lowest bar (longs) / above the highest bar (shorts), never risking more than 5% of price and ~2% of account. Once profit >= initial risk, sell half and move the remaining stop to breakeven (2-for-1). Then scale out further and trail below the lowest low of the prior two bars. Exit positions not profitable within 1-2 days; time-stop out by ~7 bars unless in a strong trend; take most of a parabolic move; never add to losers; if pyramiding, 3-2-1 ratio with largest position first.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - rules apply to every position. 'No tickie, no tradie': no entry without a confirmed trigger (never fade by picking tops/bottoms).
findings.risk_geometry: Initial stop: 1/16 below setup low, capped at 5% of price; account risk ~2%. Scale-out at 1R to breakeven; trailing stop = lowest low of prior 2 bars; time stop ~7 bars; windfall rule on parabolic moves; drawdown table motivates caps (50% loss needs 100% gain to recover).
findings.quote: as soon as your profits (a) are equal to or greater than your initial risk (b), you should lock in half of your profits and move your protective stop on your remaining shares to breakeven (c) (near your original entry).
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, Landry's Rules and Money Management (pp. 11-16); Chapter 15-16 position management (pp. 191-206); Chapter 1 Drawdown (pp. 7-9)
findings.notes: Direct inputs for RiskGate (5% initial-stop cap, ~2% account risk, one-direction discipline, never average down) and lifecycle (scale-out at 1R -> breakeven stop, 2-bar-low trailing, ~7-bar time stop). For 24/7 perps all these clocks must be bar-counted, not calendar-dated, to preserve V8 determinism; the drawdown-recovery asymmetry justifies the heat/cap discipline.
findings.book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

book_title: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis (Patel, 2010)

findings.strategy_name: Ideal Ichimoku confluence trend-following (foundation strategy)
findings.setup_summary: On the reference timeframe (book: daily), LONG when (a) close is above the Kumo Cloud formed by Senkou A=(Tenkan+Kijun)/2 and Senkou B=52-bar midpoint, both shifted +26 bars; (b) Tenkan Sen (9-bar midpoint of high/low) > Kijun Sen (26-bar midpoint); (c) Chikou Span (close shifted back 26) is above price-from-26-bars-ago in 'open space'; (d) future Kumo bullish (future Senkou A > future Senkou B); (e) price within a bounded distance of Tenkan (200 pips) and Kijun (300 pips); (f) no Kumo shadow overhead and at least 50 pips of room to next resistance. Mirror for SHORT. Entry at next bar close or limit alert at resistance+buffer (40 pips).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = all five components aligned in one direction. Invalidation = close back into/through the Kumo Cloud, or Tenkan Sen crossing Kijun Sen against the position (trend change), or Chikou entering the cloud. Author's backtest shows trades last weeks-months and capture only ~30-50% of max profit (by design).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar close or limit above resistance/below support plus buffer (40 pips bullish, 35 bearish). Initial stop = Kijun Sen minus exit buffer; in 'Preserve mode' at +300 pips profit stop migrates to Tenkan Sen. Target: structure/alerts, no fixed R; expiry: none, trend trade. Gap risk acknowledged as reason stops are mandatory.
findings.quote: Price has to be above Kumo Cloud; Tenkan Sen is greater than Kijun Sen; Chikou is showing strong bullish momentum ("Open Space"); There should be at least 50 pips to the next major support or resistance value; Kumo Future is bullish
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2 'Ichimoku Trading Plan' strategy description (pp.42-44); Chapter 5 'Ideal Ichimoku Strategy' (p.150)
findings.notes: The five-component confluence is directly computable on 1h bars (26-bar Kijun ~= 26h window). 24/7 trading removes the weekend/close distortion the book frets about for FX, so bar counts are cleaner. The book supports it with a manual 2-year EURUSD daily backtest (8-11 trades, R/R improved from 1.51 to 0.88 after rule tweaks), but it is discretionary (alerts re-placed by eye, acknowledged errors), so DESIGN_INFERENCE not LITERATURE_SUPPORTED. The bounded-distance entry gate and preserve-mode exit are the load-bearing sub-rules to test.
findings.book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

findings.strategy_name: Tenkan Sen/Kijun Sen crossover with cloud + momentum filters
findings.setup_summary: Enter LONG at next bar close when Tenkan Sen (9-bar midpoint) crosses above Kijun Sen (26-bar midpoint), AND price is above a thin Kumo Cloud (or within ~50 pips below it for FX, accepting price will slice through a thin cloud), AND Chikou Span is in 'open space', AND price/Tenkan/Kijun/Chikou are not inside a thick cloud. Optional filters: future Senkou A >= future Senkou B and future cloud not thick. Mirror for SHORT. Book positions this as the Ichimoku analog of the 10/30 SMA crossover with a 200-SMA-style trend gate.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = TS/KS cross with thin-cloud + open-space conditions. Invalidation = cross back (TS recrosses KS against position) or price closes back through the cloud. Book shows this captures more of the trend than the ideal strategy but with more whipsaw ('you will learn the consequences as you backtest').
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: next bar close at cross. Stop: Kijun Sen minus buffer (plan-dependent). Target: ~250-400 pips in the book's example trade; no fixed expiry. The book intentionally omits full money management for advanced strategies.
findings.quote: If the 10 period SMA crosses over the 30 period SMA when price is above the 200 period SMA then a bullish trade is entered... The Tenkan Sen/Kijun Sen crossover strategy is similar to this strategy.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5 'Tenkan Sen/Kijun Sen Cross Strategy' (pp.150-154)
findings.notes: A midpoint-of-high/low cross is a volatility-aware relative of an EMA cross; both TS/KS and ema variants can coexist as variants of one moving_average_cross family in V8's variant model. 24/7 bars make the 9/26 structure unambiguous. Note: author's least-favorite 'Kumo Cloud Breakout' is a separate strategy (see failed_breakout finding); do not merge.
findings.book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

findings.strategy_name: Chikou Span 'open space' momentum/regime filter
findings.setup_summary: Compute Chikou Span = close shifted back 26 bars. Trend momentum is strong ('open space') when, projecting forward 5-10 bars, the Chikou line would NOT run into price-from-26-bars-ago either horizontally (price consolidates) or vertically (price moves 5-10%). If it would collide, momentum is weak and the trend is suspect. Usable as a regime gate on trend experts rather than a standalone entry.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = Chikou in open space (no collision within the forward 5-10 bar / 5-10% box). Invalidation = Chikou enters/collides with historical price, or Chikou crosses price-from-26-bars-ago (trend flip).
findings.risk_geometry: No entry geometry; pure filter/feature. The book's 'visual square box' heuristic is a forward-looking probe, inherently look-ahead-free if computed only from the shifted series at time t.
findings.quote: If the Chikou Span runs into price, then there is not much of a trend momentum... If the Chikou Span is in "open space" then the trend momentum is strong because today's price is not going to run into any price support/resistance from 26 periods ago.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 1 'Chikou Span' (pp.19-25)
findings.notes: This is a falsifiable, look-ahead-free momentum feature: distance of the shifted close to historical price over a forward window. Maps cleanly to a history-group feature feeding trend experts (e.g. trend_pullback, ichimoku confluence). In perps, 26h and the 5-10% vertical probe are directly meaningful given 24/7 bars.
findings.book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

findings.strategy_name: Kumo Cloud breakout with fake-break rejection (refinement of failed_breakout)
findings.setup_summary: Book's 'Kumo Cloud Breakout Strategy': enter on close above (below) the Kumo Cloud with the same TS/KS/Chikou alignment filters. Author explicitly rates it weakest of the five strategies because close-throughs frequently reverse within the next bar or two ('fake' break of major S/R) - one observed pair of breakouts looked identical ex-ante, one ran 1,000 pips and one failed under 100. The cloud edge (esp. a long flat Senkou B or Kumo shadow behind price) is a well-defined, precomputed level usable as the prior-high/level reference for the existing failed_breakout family.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = close through cloud edge with alignment. Invalidation = close back inside/through the other side within 1-2 bars (fake break) -> stand aside or flip. The book's lesson: breakout signal alone is weak; confirmation (retest held) is required.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry above cloud edge + buffer; stop below Kijun or below cloud; target prior extreme. No fixed expiry.
findings.quote: there are many times where prices break out of the Kumo Cloud and then the next bar or bars reverse right away. It was basically a "fake" break of a major support or resistance.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5 'Kumo Cloud Breakout Strategy' (pp.155-156)
findings.notes: Directly corroborates the existing failed_breakout expert (mechanism liquidity_vacuum_reentry): fake breaks create the reentry short. The Kumo/Senkou B edge is a deterministic, frozen-reference candidate for the windowed prior-high ref; cloud thickness is a volatility-group input. In perps, close-through semantics and 1-2 bar reversal windows map to 1h bars.
findings.book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

findings.strategy_name: Kijun-distance 'equalize' entry gate and extended-price retraction
findings.setup_summary: Do not enter a trend trade while price is 'far' from the Kijun Sen (26-bar midpoint); wait for equalization. The book operationalizes 'far' as >200 pips from Tenkan / >300 pips from Kijun (fixed-pip, per instrument) and suggests a volatility-scaled alternative: price >= 1.5x ATR away from Kijun counts as far and historically preceded a pullback (Fig 1.24, June 8 2009). Conversely, when price is far from a FLAT Kijun, high probability of retraction to Kijun -> major pullback or trend reversal. A 2-year backtest showed this distance rule kept the plan out of several major moves; removing it added 4 trades and nearly doubled max profit.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = trend aligned (TS>KS, Chikou open space) AND price within gate distance of Kijun. Invalidation = price stays outside gate (no equalization) -> no trade; the rule is a filter, not a standalone signal. Warning in book: 'far' values vary with volatility, must be volatility-scaled.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry only when within distance; stop = Kijun minus buffer; if entry risk exceeds cap, skip. This refines the existing trend_pullback family's entry condition (add a max-distance-from-baseline gate).
findings.quote: When price is far away from the Kijun Sen it shows that price has moved at a faster rate than the Kijun Sen... there is a high probability that price will retract toward the Kijun Sen causing a major pullback or even a trend reversal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 1 'Kijun Sen' (pp.14-17); entry-distance rules in Chapter 2 (p.43); optimization in Chapter 4 (p.141)
findings.notes: The 1.5x ATR 'far' threshold is the falsifiable, volatility-scaled form and is directly usable in V8 with atr_ref. The fixed-pip thresholds do not transfer to BTC; scale by ATR or %. Refinement direction: trend_pullback variant gated on distance-to-Kijun, and a dead-thesis variant: far + flat Kijun = pullback risk.
findings.book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

findings.strategy_name: Multi-touch Chikou-peak / Kumo-shadow support-resistance levels
findings.setup_summary: Draw horizontal levels through Chikou Span peaks (close-shifted-26): 2+ peaks touching one level = major S/R (author: often coincides with a Fibonacci retracement). Similarly, Kumo shadows (past clouds behind price) and flat Senkou B plateaus are major S/R; the longer the flat Senkou B, the stronger the level. A strong trend cannot occur until it breaks through the price of the shadow peak.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = price approaches a 2+ touch level or shadow peak. Invalidation = clean close through the level; shadow weakens as price consolidates away from it. Zone map, not a standalone entry.
findings.risk_geometry: No geometry; the level itself anchors entries/stops/targets for other strategies (e.g. alert placement below resistance for breakout entries).
findings.quote: If you draw a horizontal line through a Chikou peak, it represents a support/resistance value. If you get many Chikou peaks hitting that horizontal line then it is a major support/resistance value. In most cases, if you get two or more peaks, this typically represents a Fibonacci value.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 1 'Chikou Span' (p.24); 'Kumo Cloud Components' (pp.35-39)
findings.notes: Location-group feature: count of touches on a shifted-close-derived level is computable deterministically. On 1h BTC, 26-bar-shifted close levels may be noisier than in FX dailies (faster regime rotation), so treat as a candidate feature for zone-weighted S/R rather than a level to hard-trade. Useful as an anchor for alert placement in the ichimoku confluence family.
findings.book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

findings.strategy_name: Preserve mode: stop migration Kijun->Tenkan and break-even protection
findings.setup_summary: Exit-management ladder for trend trades: (1) initial stop = Kijun Sen minus buffer; (2) when open profit >= threshold (book: 300 pips FX) enter 'Preserve mode' and migrate stop to the Tenkan Sen to tighten it ('we do not want to give back all our profits'); (3) 'free trade' when the stop is at/above entry (breakeven) - profit guaranteed even on stop-out. Book notes Preserve mode is a conservative choice that foregoes some tail profit by design (captures ~30-50% of max profit); the day-trade plan adds 'once 12 pips profit reached, change stop to break even' and 'once 20 pips reached use Tenkan as stop'.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = open profit >= preserve threshold while TS trending with position. Invalidation = TS is flat/higher than Kijun (keep Kijun as stop) or price retraces to stop. Also: if price is >200 pips from a FLAT Tenkan, exit (book's 'pip rule for flat conditions' - only fires when TS flat, not when trending).
findings.risk_geometry: Stop: Kijun - buffer -> Tenkan - buffer after preserve threshold -> break-even. No target; expiry none. All distances volatility-scaled in crypto.
findings.quote: Preserve mode is where we move our stop from the Kijun Sen to the Tenkan Sen to tighten our current stop. We do not want to give back all our profits... With this conservative strategy, we are going to get stopped out for a profit or get stopped out for a minimum loss when we are wrong.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3 backtest, Preserve mode (p.63, pp.83-88); day-trade stop ladder in Chapter 8 (pp.185-187)
findings.notes: This is a lifecycle rule (stops vs dead-thesis are separate exits in V8): a deterministic stop-migration ladder driven by realized profit in R/ATR units. The 'free trade' state is an explicit break-even lifecycle state. The flat-vs-trending qualifier on the 200-pip exit is a good dead-thesis discriminator.
findings.book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

findings.strategy_name: Portfolio risk framework: allocation cap, mandatory stop, R/R<1 target
findings.setup_summary: Book's trading-plan risk layer: never allocate more than 20% of funds to one position; a stop order is mandatory on every entry ('people lose all their money because they forget or did not want to place a stop order'); never risk 100% of portfolio at once because of gap risk; keep system-level risk/reward < 1.0 (avg winner > avg risk); cap max entry risk (daily FX: 250-300 pips, including buffer, per trade); risk per month = drawdown budget; no add-ons for the base plan; weekly re-placement of alerts.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rules are admission/position gates, not signals: entry rejected if risk budget violated; trade exited same-day if post-fill risk exceeds plan allocation. Book optimizes entry-risk cap 300->250 pips and adds a 550-pip profit exit to roughly halve R/R from 1.51 to ~0.44.
findings.risk_geometry: Position size bounded by 20% allocation and per-trade risk cap; stop always present; targets structure-based.
findings.quote: we always use a stop and never risk 100 percent of our portfolio at one time (money management)
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2 'Components of a Trading System' (pp.41-44); Chapter 3 (p.73); Chapter 4 'Post-Analysis' (pp.137-147)
findings.notes: Directly portable to V8 RiskGate as deterministic admission rules: hard stop required, per-trade risk cap (in R not pips), 20% gross allocation cap, system R/R<1 objective. For perps, 'no margin' becomes a leverage cap; funding costs should enter the R accounting. Corroborates general risk literature (Tharp quote at book's opening).
findings.book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

findings.strategy_name: Day-trade session circuit breakers (max losses/trades per day)
findings.setup_summary: Intraday plan caps: only two losing trades allowed per day, after which no more trades that day ('some days day trading is just not going to work... we have to trade at least two trades to determine if that day is a nontradable day'); max five trades per day; max loss per trade 25 pips including spread; realistic monthly profit targets scaled to contract size (not fixed dollar greed). Day session assumed 7am-4pm EST for FX.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Stand-aside trigger = 2nd losing trade of the day or 5th trade taken. Not a market signal; a session risk governor.
findings.risk_geometry: Per-trade risk 25 pips incl. spread; stop Kijun - buffer unless that exceeds 25 pips, in which case use Tenkan - buffer; break-even after +12 pips.
findings.quote: Only two losses per day are allowed. No more than five trades per day can be taken. Maximum loss per trade is 25 pips (including the spread).
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8 'Day Trading with Ichimoku' (pp.185-186)
findings.notes: 24/7 perps have no natural session; implement as a rolling UTC-day or event-time window counter (deterministic in replay). The two-loss circuit breaker is an emotional-discipline device more than an edge claim; in V8 it maps to a max-consecutive-loss / max-daily-loss RiskGate counter. Per-trade 25-pip cap transfers as an R or bps cap.
findings.book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

findings.strategy_name: Cost-structure constraint on short-horizon strategies (spread/fee dominance)
findings.setup_summary: Book restricts the 5-minute Ichimoku day-trade plan to EURUSD specifically because its ~2-pip spread is the lowest available; 'a spread of 10 pips can wipe out our day trading profits especially if we are targeting 15 pips per trade'. For daily-framework trades targeting 200+ pips, higher spread is tolerable. Lesson: expected target must be a large multiple of round-trip cost; strategy viability is cost-regime dependent.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Admission test for a horizon/strategy: round-trip cost (spread + fees + funding) must be a small fraction (book implies <= ~10-15%) of the expected target; else the plan must be restricted to venues/timeframes with lower cost.
findings.risk_geometry: Cost enters trade accounting directly; book even subtracts spread from profit in trade stats tables.
findings.quote: We choose the EURUSD instrument because the spread that most brokerage firms offer is 2 pips. We need the spread to be low because we are day trading... A spread of 10 pips can wipe out our day trading profits especially if we are targeting 15 pips per trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8 'Day Trading with Ichimoku' (pp.185-186)
findings.notes: For BTCUSDT perps this is the taker-fee + funding + spread dominance check: 1h-target strategies (R~1%) must clear fee/funding drag; high-leverage notional-amplified fees make this stricter than the book's FX case. Directs the Binance USDM cost model calibration: verify R-multiple targets are >= ~10x round-trip cost before any short-horizon candidate is screened.
findings.book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

findings.strategy_name: Multi-strategy signal confluence (2+ Ichimoku strategies agreeing within a few bars)
findings.setup_summary: Book's cross-strategy observation: 'the high probability of success is seen when two or more strategies show entry signals in price close to each other' (e.g., Kijun cross then Tenkan/Kijun cross; or Kumo breakout then TS/KS cross). The largest cited example: four strategies firing within four days preceded a 2,000-pip move over seven months. Individual strategies are described as weak (Kumo breakout 'by itself is weak. If you combined this strategy with others then it is strong').
findings.trigger_invalidation: Testable claim: conditional win rate rises when >=2 signal families agree within a lookback window vs single signals. Falsifiable only with a fixed, pre-registered signal set.
findings.risk_geometry: No geometry; a signal-aggregation hypothesis.
findings.quote: the high probability of success is seen when two or more strategies show entry signals in price close to each other
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5 'Ichimoku Strategies' - strategy combinations (p.159)
findings.notes: Evidence-class NARRATIVE: based on chart anecdotes, no statistics. IMPORTANT for V8: a cross-expert agreement feature is a shared-scorer/router mechanism, which rule 6 keeps ABSENT by default; it enters only via a registry experiment beating the simple baseline on frozen OOS. Falsifiable form inside the budget: a within-family composite (multiple sub-conditions of the same family) rather than a cross-expert ranker.
findings.book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

findings.strategy_name: Ichimoku bar-count time elements (9/17/26/33/42/.../257 cycles) and Gann square-of-odds
findings.setup_summary: Place vertical lines at swing-reversal bars (>=2 bars of higher-highs/lower-lows), then measure bar-count distances between all reversal pairs; count a match if the distance equals one of the derived numbers (9,17,26,33,42,51,65,76,83,97,101,129,172,200,257) or +/-1. Book author admits he does not even use these (prefers W.D. Gann), that during a sustained 18-week trend there was 'really no match', that ranges around the values cover almost all numbers ('do not use a range'), and that 'time elements by themselves are not too valuable'.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No reliable trigger; author uses them only as calendar alerts then applies discretionary technical analysis. Poor falsifiability: +/-1 tolerance plus many candidate numbers near-guarantee hindsight matches (multiple-comparisons problem).
findings.risk_geometry: None.
findings.quote: The time elements indicate a possible price reversal. Time elements by themselves are not too valuable.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 6 'Ichimoku Time Elements' (pp.161-170)
findings.notes: REJECT for V8: (a) author self-reports weak performance and non-use; (b) weekend/calendar dependence is ambiguous in a 24/7 market where every hour trades; (c) the +/-1 tolerance + 15 candidate numbers make the pattern unfalsifiable ex-ante. If anything, keep only as a lesson against multi-hypothesis cycle fitting. W.D. Gann square-of-odd-number time projections share the same falsifiability problem.
findings.book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

findings.strategy_name: 21-day, 3 percent rule
findings.setup_summary: The book defines a named per-trade risk rule, the '21-day, 3 percent rule' (Ch.2, p.29): a percentage-based cap on loss per trade tied to a 21-day window. This part carries only the index entry; the exact parameter semantics (3% of equity per trade, and how the 21-day window is applied) are detailed in Part 1.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any new position taken without computing its loss-at-stop against the 3% equity cap. Invalidation: positions whose stop distance would exceed the cap are rejected.
findings.risk_geometry: Risk per trade capped at 3% (of equity, per Part 1 text); the glossary confirms stops are placed at a specific price.
findings.quote: 21-day, 3 percent rule, 29
findings.chapter_anchor: Index p.29 (3 percent rule; 21-day, 3 percent rule)
findings.notes: Corroborated by the equity-management chapter cluster (pp.187-199). Maps directly to V8 RiskGate per-trade risk cap; percentage-of-equity sizing is venue-agnostic and applies cleanly to leveraged perps.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Equity management / capital preservation
findings.setup_summary: Chapter 12 (pp.187-199) is titled 'Learning the Rules of Equity Management'; the index shows it covers an equity management formula (p.193), risk versus reward (p.195), and the failure mode of a margin account being wiped out (p.198). Falsifiable claim: there exists a formula-based equity cap whose violation leads to account loss.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: cumulative losses approach the equity-management threshold. Invalidation: continuing to trade at the same size after breaching the capital-preservation cap.
findings.risk_geometry: Equity-level management formula (p.193); reward-to-risk accounting (p.195); protective stop-loss reference at p.192.
findings.quote: Capital preservation, 197
findings.chapter_anchor: Index pp.187-199 (Ch.12 Learning the Rules of Equity Management); p.198 'Margin account loses'
findings.notes: Supports V8 heat cap / drawdown floor logic in RiskGate. In 24/7 leveraged perp trading, margin-call risk is the direct analogue of the 'margin account loses' failure mode.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Protective stop-loss order
findings.setup_summary: Glossary definition: a stop-loss order automatically liquidates an open position at a specific price to minimize exposure if the market moves against the position (e.g., long USD at 156.27 with a stop at 155.49). Falsifiable: every open position carries a resting protective stop at a defined price level.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: position opened. Invalidation: no protective stop present, or stop not executable by venue.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at market/limit; protective stop at a specific price (e.g., 78 pips below entry in the glossary example); stop is an automatic liquidation, distinct from a discretionary exit.
findings.quote: Stop Loss Order Order type whereby an open position is automatically liquidated at a specific price. Often used to minimize exposure to losses if the market moves against an investor's position.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary entry 'Stop Loss Order'
findings.notes: Directly reinforces V8 risk_geometry stops and the simulator STOP_FIRST semantics; perp venues support resting stops natively.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Support and resistance level role-flip
findings.setup_summary: Support is defined (glossary) as a price floor at which the exchange rate 'automatically corrects itself'; the index shows the book formalizes the game of scoring points at highs/lows (Ch.5, pp.71-87) including 'Past Resistance can Become Future Support' (p.83) and 'Past Support can Become Future Resistance' (p.84). Falsifiable: after a prior high is broken, that level flips from resistance to support and price is expected to halt/bounce there.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price approaches a prior extreme that has been broken in the direction of travel. Invalidation: price closes cleanly through the flipped level without a reaction.
findings.risk_geometry: Level-based entries at prior swing extremes; stops beyond the flipped level (structure), target at the next prior extreme.
findings.quote: Support Levels A technique used in technical analysis that indicates a specific price ceiling and floor at which a given exchange rate will automatically correct itself.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary 'Support Levels'; Index pp.75-84 (Ch.5 The Financial Game of Support and Resistance)
findings.notes: Role-flip of levels is the same behavioral claim V8's location feature group feeds; 24/7 trading with no exchange gaps makes level tests cleaner (no gap-through ambiguity), though high leverage increases stop-run frequency at these levels.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Buy zone / sell zone entries
findings.setup_summary: Chapter 7 (pp.113-127) splits the chart into a sell zone (short the market when price enters it, p.121) and a buy zone (go long when price enters it, p.126), with zones divided by trend lines (p.117). Falsifiable: entries are only taken at the zone edge defined by the prevailing trend line, not mid-zone.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price enters the zone of interest against the trend. Invalidation: price trades back through the zone's defining trend line (trend-line break, p.126).
findings.risk_geometry: Zone-edge entry; index references 'trend line division of, 117' and bullish-candle entrance for buy zones (p.122); stop on the far side of the trend-line divider.
findings.quote: Shorting the Market When It Enters the Sell Zone, 121
findings.chapter_anchor: Index pp.113-127 (Ch.7 Buy and Sell Zones)
findings.notes: Zone-plus-trend-line structure is implementable on 1h BTC, but trend-line construction is discretionary; the exact zone definitions are in Part 1. Corroborates the location feature group and the supply_demand_zone backlog.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Fibonacci retracement/extension levels
findings.setup_summary: Chapters 8-9 (pp.129-159) cover the 'Fibonacci retracement and extension ratio relationship' (pp.140-146), with retracement levels cited in reference to support and resistance (pp.142, 144) and 'fibonacci levels' (pp.143, 149). Falsifiable: price tends to halt or reverse at Fibonacci ratios (retracements) and project to extensions (targets) of prior legs. Notably, the book itself titles Ch.9 'The Reality of the Fibonacci Secret', signaling a self-critical, potentially falsifying chapter.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price pulls back to a Fib level of a prior leg. Invalidation: price closes through the Fib level with no reaction, or level spacing is violated by the observed data.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at Fib retracement levels; extensions used as targets; the index notes Fibonacci ratios in reference to both support and resistance.
findings.quote: The Fibonacci Retracement and Extension Ratio Relationship, 140
findings.chapter_anchor: Index pp.129-159 (Ch.8 The Fibonacci Secret; Ch.9 The Reality of the Fibonacci Secret)
findings.notes: Fibonacci is a self-fulfilling/probabilistic heuristic with no causal microstructure claim; V8 should test it only as a location-feature hypothesis with a falsification gate. The book's own 'Reality of' chapter is a warning label.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Consolidation / bracketing range trade
findings.setup_summary: Chapter 11 (pp.175-186) is titled 'Consolidating, Bracketing, Accumulation, or Sideways Movement' and contains three explicitly numbered trading strategies (Strategy 1 p.178, Strategy 2 p.181, Strategy 3 p.183) plus 'Bull and Bear Traps'. The index references the 'trading range of, 181' and 'small trading range, 177'. Falsifiable: during bounded sideways movement, the range has definable boundaries that can be traded both directions.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price within a defined horizontal range (consolidation). Invalidation: the range resolves directionally (trend resumes) or a trap produces a false break.
findings.risk_geometry: Range-boundary entries; stop beyond the opposite range edge; the range top/bottom serve as both entry and exit references.
findings.quote: Consolidation, 175-186
findings.chapter_anchor: Index pp.175-186 (Ch.11 Consolidating, Bracketing, Accumulation, or Sideways Movement); p.181 'trading range of'
findings.notes: Range/consolidation structure is observable on 1h BTC, but the three strategies' exact definitions live in Part 1; the 'trading range of' (p.181) suggests a range-width characterization usable as a volatility-compression feature.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Bull and bear traps
findings.setup_summary: The index shows the book's consolidation chapter ends with 'Bull and Bear Traps' (pp.184-186): a false breakout of a range that traps breakout traders and then reverses. This is the classic failed-breakout/false-break mechanism: price pierces a range boundary, fails to follow through, and re-enters the range, squeezing the trapped side. Falsifiable: a candle closes beyond the range boundary and then closes back inside within N bars.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close beyond a defined prior boundary followed by a close back through it. Invalidation: the breakout follows through (no close back inside within the expiry window).
findings.risk_geometry: Counter-entry at the close back through the boundary; stop beyond the trapped extreme (the false-break extreme); target back to the opposite range edge.
findings.quote: Bull and Bear Traps, 184-186
findings.chapter_anchor: Index pp.184-186 (Bull and Bear Traps; 'traps, 184-186')
findings.notes: Mechanism matches V8's formalized failed_breakout family (liquidity_vacuum_reentry) and liquidity_sweep_reclaim; consolidation-phase traps in 24/7 perp markets are frequent and stop-hunt-like. Part 1 likely supplies the detailed setup; this entry corroborates the existing expert rather than proposing a new one.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Fundamental-announcement whiplash risk
findings.setup_summary: Chapter 10 (pp.161-174) covers fundamental announcements; the index shows the book distinguishes 'Trading Days Versus Trending Days' (p.167), warns of 'Increased Risk with Trading Fundamental Announcements' (pp.167-169), and references 'Whiplashes' (p.169) and 'Not All Fundamental Announcements Move the Market' (p.183). Falsifiable: price around high-impact scheduled announcements is subject to two-sided whipsaw that raises stop-out probability versus normal sessions.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: a high-impact scheduled announcement window. Invalidation: if a given announcement class shows no elevated volatility/whipsaw in the local venue data, the rule does not apply.
findings.risk_geometry: Risk-reduction rule rather than entry rule: reduced size, wider stops, or no new entries during event windows; 'trading fundamental announcements' carries increased risk (p.167-169).
findings.quote: Increased Risk with Trading Fundamental Announcements, 167-169
findings.chapter_anchor: Index pp.167-169 (Ch.10 Fundamental Analysis); p.169 'Whiplashes'
findings.notes: BTC reacts to scheduled macro events (FOMC, CPI, NFP) with genuine whipsaw, but not all FX-centric announcements matter, and 24/7 crypto trading has no session close to hide in; implement as a time-gated lifecycle/risk rule, not a directional expert.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Multiple time frame trading
findings.setup_summary: Chapter 3 includes the section 'Using Multiple Time Frames to Trade' (p.44): trade direction is established on a higher timeframe and entries/exits are timed on a lower timeframe rather than trading a single chart. Falsifiable: entries taken against the higher-timeframe trend underperform those aligned with it.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: a lower-timeframe entry signal. Invalidation: higher-timeframe trend context is neutral or opposes the lower-timeframe signal.
findings.risk_geometry: Direction filter only; entry/stop/target still per the lower-timeframe setup.
findings.quote: Using Multiple Time Frames to Trade, 44
findings.chapter_anchor: Index p.44 (using multiple frames, 44)
findings.notes: Methodology lesson for V8: any candidate expert on the 1h BTCUUSDT should condition on the higher-timeframe (4h/1d) trend as a regime filter; cheap to implement and likely corroborated across the library.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Roll-over cost as carry input
findings.setup_summary: Glossary definition of Roll-Over: settlement of a deal is rolled forward to another value date, and the cost of this process is based on the interest-rate differential of the two currencies. This is the FX roll-over concept; in crypto perpetuals the direct analogue is the funding rate paid to hold a position across funding intervals. Falsifiable: holding-cost differential is observable and priced into the instrument.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - structural cost definition rather than a trigger; applies whenever a position is held across a roll/funding event.
findings.risk_geometry: Cost of carry: interest-rate differential (FX) / funding rate (perps); affects PnL of held positions and discourages long holding when carry is adverse.
findings.quote: Roll-Over Process whereby the settlement of a deal is rolled forward to another value date. The cost of this process is based on the interest rate differential of the two currencies.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary entry 'Roll-Over'
findings.notes: Direct structural mapping to crypto perp funding; motivates funding-rate as a feature (flow group) and as carry-cost input to expert PnL in the simulator's cost model.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: OCO bracket exits
findings.setup_summary: The index shows the book covers One-Cancels-Other (OCO) orders (pp.27, 43): a bracket where two resting orders (typically take-profit and stop-loss) are attached to a position and the filling of one cancels the other. Falsifiable: an OCO pair guarantees a single terminating exit at either the target or the stop.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - order-management structure; requires both resting orders valid simultaneously.
findings.risk_geometry: Bracket exit: target above (long) and protective stop below attached at entry; first fill cancels the counterpart order; glossary 'Stop Loss Order' provides the protective leg.
findings.quote: One cancels other (OCO) orders, 27
findings.chapter_anchor: Index pp.27, 43 (OCO orders; trading of, 43)
findings.notes: OCO is natively supported by major perp venues; informs V8 lifecycle/exit semantics (target OR stop, first hit) and the simulator's STOP_FIRST behavior for the candidate-draft-to-exit path.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Funding carry trade and carry unwind (Icelandic krona carry)
findings.mechanism: Leveraged carry positions are paid to hold an appreciating, high-yield asset funded in a cheap currency; the position is self-reinforcing while the target appreciates, but unwinds violently and herding-driven when the funding mismatch reverses.
findings.setup_summary: Book setup (falsifiable on perp data): households borrowed yen at ~3% and Swiss francs to buy krona-yield assets paying 15.5% while the krona rose; the trade was profitable until the carry target collapsed, at which point the funding-currency obligations became multiples more expensive (gap-like repricing; krona removed from the market). Perp analog: when perp funding is persistently and unusually positive while price trends up, leveraged longs are collectively paid to hold; the falsifiable claim is that such carry crowding is fragile and the unwind is a liquidation cascade once price breaks the carry-trend low or funding flips sharply negative.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Carry thesis invalid when the carry target stops appreciating (price breaks its carry-trend support) or the funding/carry spread reverses; book event: krona collapsed and yen/Swiss-franc obligations repriced multiples higher.
findings.risk_geometry: No explicit stop or target in the book; the documented failure mode is gap-like repricing (FX market suspended), which in perps maps to a funding-driven liquidation waterfall rather than a price gap (24/7 venue).
findings.quote: With local interest rates at 15.5 percent and the krona rising, they decided the smart thing to do, when they wanted to buy something they couldn't afford, was to borrow not kronur but yen and Swiss francs. ... in October, after the krona collapsed, the yen and Swiss francs they must repay became many times more expensive.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part I, 'Wall Street on the Tundra' (Icelandic carry-trade section, ~44/396)
findings.notes: Funding carry is first-class perp microstructure (funding rate, leverage, 24/7). Requires funding-rate data; funding is not currently a frozen feature group, so this is DATA_BLOCKED/backlog until a funding feature group exists. Distinguish from the simpler 'collect funding while long' trade: the edge claim here is that extreme carry crowding predicts its own violent unwind.
findings.book: Boomerang - Travels in the New Third World 2012

findings.strategy_name: Sovereign short on banking-system size vs fiscal capacity
findings.mechanism: When an economy's banking/aggregate obligations dwarf its capacity to service them (government revenues), credit is mispriced as risk-free; historically such ratio extremes precede default, and repricing arrives as a confidence-driven step-change, not a gradual decay.
findings.setup_summary: Compute the ratio of a system's banking-sector obligations (or total debt) to its government revenues; when the ratio exceeds historical danger thresholds (Ireland >25x annual tax revenue; Spain and France >10x), short the credit. Bass validated the heuristic against Reinhart-Rogoff's sovereign-default history before positioning. Transferable perp-application: an aggregate-leverage regime filter — when venue-wide OI or system leverage reaches extreme multiples of spot cashflow/volume, tail-deleveraging risk is underpriced.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid if the entity actually runs sustained primary surpluses (Bass: 'the only way things can work out... If they start running real budget surpluses') or if confidence never reprices despite the ratios.
findings.risk_geometry: Bet sizing is probability-weighted (11bps premium paid on Greek default insurance vs ~70% expected loss); no stop specified; counterparty rule — trade only with firms least likely to fail and demand daily collateral posting.
findings.quote: The first thing we tried to figure out was how big these banking systems were, especially in relation to government revenues. We took about four months to gather the data. No one had it. ... Historically, such levels of government indebtedness had led to government default.
findings.chapter_anchor: Preface, 'The Biggest Short' (~14/396)
findings.notes: Not directly tradeable in BTC perps (no sovereign credit market); kept as a regime-filter/methodology transfer: the ratio heuristic (obligations vs capacity to service) is a falsifiable tail-risk indicator that could gate V8 risk or the simulator regime.
findings.book: Boomerang - Travels in the New Third World 2012

findings.strategy_name: Position before confirmation on slow-resolving tail theses (confirmation reprices the tail)
findings.mechanism: For an event that is slow and uncertain to resolve, the moment the market acknowledges the possibility is the repricing event itself (Greek default insurance went 11bps to 2300bps); waiting for 'the whites of their eyes' means paying the already-expanded premium. Confidence is path-dependent: 'Once you lose confidence, you don't get it back.'
findings.setup_summary: Methodology rule for tail/convexity theses: enter when the thesis is pre-registered and the premium is cheap, not after confirmation, because confirmation is the repricing event. Directly testable implication for V8: on deleveraging/cascade episodes, measure the entry-price gap between confirmation-gated triggers (e.g., first confirmed break after a crash) and thesis-first triggers (pre-registered level); the confirmation-gated entries are predicted to systematically overpay. Also: the position must survive chronology/timing error, since being wrong about ordering is the main residual risk.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Residual risk is chronology, not outcome: 'My biggest fear. That I'm wrong about the chronology of events.' Being early is survivable only if sizing and carry cost allow it (2-3 year horizon at 11bps carry).
findings.risk_geometry: Cost of early position (premium/carry while the thesis is unresolved) is the price of optionality; sizing must survive being early for years.
findings.quote: Should I wait until I see the whites of their eyes before I position myself, or should I position myself now? The answer is now. Because the moment people think it is a possibility, it's expensive. ... Once you lose confidence, you don't get it back. You just don't.
findings.chapter_anchor: Preface, 'The Biggest Short' (~18/396)
findings.notes: The single most relevant methodology lesson for V8's backtest design: confirmation-gated candidate-episode entry is a systematic overpayment on tail events. Recommend an audit of how candidate entries are triggered against this bias. Direction NONE because it is an entry-timing/measurement lesson, not a side.
findings.book: Boomerang - Travels in the New Third World 2012

findings.strategy_name: Iron law of price-to-fundamental reversion (Kelly)
findings.mechanism: A bubble is inflated by nothing firmer than expectations; once price untethers from its fundamental anchor, the deviation is not a new regime and the magnitude of the subsequent fall scales with the size of the deviation.
findings.setup_summary: When an asset's price rises far above its fundamental anchor, the fall is proportional to the deviation. Kelly's falsifiable claim on housing: 'the more house prices rise relative to income and rents, the more they will subsequently fall' (predicted 40-50%, up to 66%, fall relative to income; price/earnings ratio above Google's). Crypto analog requiring an on-chain/value anchor: price-to-realized-price (MVRV-type) or price-to-miner-cost extremes as a reversion signal; perp price can be measured against the spot-anchored value.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Reversion thesis invalid only if fundamentals actually grow into the price (Kelly: 'Where would this growth come from?' — the implied growth rate was implausible).
findings.risk_geometry: No stop in the book; the documented failure mode for the short is being early — the deviation can keep widening for years before reverting, so the position is not time-boxed.
findings.quote: There is an iron law of house prices: The more house prices rise relative to income and rents, the more they will subsequently fall.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part III, 'Ireland's Original Sin' (Morgan Kelly section, ~186/396)
findings.notes: A falsifiable statistical claim made in 2007 and borne out with unusual accuracy (documented in the book). For crypto there is no income/rent analog, but BTC has realized-price/hash-cost anchors; requires a value-anchor series not in the frozen feature vocabulary, hence backlog. The reversion is to an anchor, not to a rolling band.
findings.book: Boomerang - Travels in the New Third World 2012

findings.strategy_name: Paper exposure vs deliverable supply (futures OI vs physical / perp OI vs spot depth)
findings.mechanism: When open interest in a derivatives contract far exceeds deliverable/spot supply, a crisis can seize up the paper market and decouple it from the underlying; holders of 'paper' exposure own a claim, not the asset — settlement and venue choice are part of the position.
findings.setup_summary: Bass's venue rule: hold physical gold, not gold futures, because outstanding futures contracts exceeded available gold and the futures market was likely to seize up in a crisis ('people who thought they owned gold would find they owned pieces of paper instead'). V8 analog: when perp open interest is a large multiple of spot depth/volume, the perp can dislocate from spot under liquidation cascades — funding and basis blow out, insurance-fund risk materializes; the simulator cost model should represent perp-spot decoupling in high OI-to-depth regimes rather than assuming clean convergence to spot.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Venue/risk rule, not a directional thesis; no invalidation beyond the OI-to-deliverable ratio regime itself.
findings.risk_geometry: Hedging/venue selection: prefer the settlement-robust exposure; monitor OI-to-spot-depth as a regime gate on the cost model and on perp-vs-spot basis assumptions.
findings.quote: You need physical gold. ... when the next crisis struck, the gold futures market was likely to seize up, as there were more outstanding futures contracts than available gold. People who thought they owned gold would find they owned pieces of paper instead.
findings.chapter_anchor: Preface, 'The Biggest Short' (~21/396)
findings.notes: The 'more contracts than gold' phenomenon is structurally identical to perp OI exceeding liquid spot depth. Feeds the simulator's basis/funding dislocation model and a risk rule on venue exposure; it is a cost/settlement lesson, not a signal, hence direction NONE.
findings.book: Boomerang - Travels in the New Third World 2012

book_title: Boomerang: Travels in the New Third World (2012) — Michael Lewis

findings.strategy_name: Potential Reversal Zone (PRZ) Fibonacci-convergence reversal
findings.mechanism: 3+ independent Fibonacci projections/retracements of a 5-point structure converging in a narrow price zone mark a high-probability trend-change area
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h, fit a 5-point XABCD swing structure and compute XA retracement at D, the BC projection (paired reciprocally to the C retracement), and the AB=CD completion. The PRZ is the band where >=3 of these levels converge tightly (book: within a few points/ticks on index charts; suggest <=1 ATR band on 1h perp). Enter in the zone on the initial test; a valid reversal requires the whole range to be tested and price to stabilize/reverse, not just touch the nearest number.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The entire PRZ must be tested on the initial test and price must react; a price gap/displacement THROUGH the whole PRZ without any reaction (book: 'blowout') invalidates the setup; if price continues in the prior trend after the full test, the reversal thesis is dead.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry is a zone/limit order around the pattern completion (book: 'executing in the zone'); stop = Stop Loss Zone (SLZ) just beyond the PRZ (for retracement patterns, violation of the X point itself is an explicit stop trigger); initial target = IPO at 0.382 or 0.618 retracement of the pattern range (A-to-D); expiry per the time projections (min 0.382 time, see time finding).
findings.quote: Specific price structures that possess three or more numbers within a defined area are the basis for defining these harmonic zones.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3 'Potential Reversal Zone (PRZ)', pp. 39-40; Ch 9 execution pp. 174-176
findings.notes: The definitive falsifiable core of the book: exact ratio alignments, no statistical support (chart examples only). On perps, 'gap through the PRZ' translates to a fast displacement/liquidation-cascade bar since 24/7 tape has no gaps. Book also notes larger price legs make more significant zones and psychological levels (50/100/1000) complement harmonic levels - both minor notes for the zone-significance feature.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: AB=CD equidistant-leg pattern with reciprocal C-to-BC ratios
findings.mechanism: after a leg AB and pullback to C, an equidistant CD leg completes at a predictable D where the BC projection converges with the C-point retracement via a fixed reciprocal-ratio table
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h, after swing AB, the C point must retrace AB by one of 0.382/0.50/0.618/0.707/0.786/0.886. The BC projection is the reciprocal of the C retracement (0.382->2.24/2.618; 0.50->2.0; 0.618->1.618; 0.707->1.41; 0.786->1.27; 0.886->1.13). The PRZ is where the projected D (CD length == AB length) converges with the BC projection; D completion is a mandatory requirement before entry. Alternate (1.27/1.618) AB=CD structures complement extension patterns.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The AB=CD completion point is the mandatory trigger; a trade is invalid if CD diverges materially from the AB=CD completion area, or if the reciprocal BC projection fails to converge with it.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at/just beyond the AB=CD completion point; for retracement patterns the X point is the stop reference; initial targets are the 0.382/0.618 pattern-range retracements; no expiry stated other than time-symmetry preference (equivalent leg duration).
findings.quote: a 0.618 retracement at the C point typically will possess a 1.618 BC projection that converges closest with the completion of the AB=CD
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 4 'The AB=CD Pattern', pp. 41-69
findings.notes: Book warns 'the idea of trading every AB=CD that completes is absurd' - structure needs confirmation (other converging Fibonacci levels). Reciprocal-ratio table is a concrete, testable rule for the D-zone feature set.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Bat pattern - deep 0.886 XA retracement reversal
findings.mechanism: a shallow B retracement (<0.618) sets up a deep 0.886 retest of the XA leg, catching longs/shorts at extreme support/resistance with a tight stop
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: B must retrace <0.618 of XA (prefer exact 0.50, or 0.382); D point at the 0.886 XA retracement; BC projection must be >=1.618 (ideal 1.618 or 2.0; 1.27 invalidates); AB=CD minimum completion, Alternate 1.27 AB=CD most common; C retrace 0.382-0.886. The 0.886 is the defining PRZ level. Book claims smaller stop loss than most patterns and sharp, quick reversals; the full PRZ tends to be tested in valid Bat reversals.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A BC projection under 1.618 invalidates the structure; valid reversals typically test the entire PRZ (bearish Bat 'tends to test its entire PRZ in valid structures more than most other patterns'); standard blowout rules (full PRZ violation on initial test) invalidate.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the 0.886 retracement (book: 'typically the optimal area to execute a trade'); stop tighter than other patterns, just beyond PRZ; targets = IPO 0.382/0.618 retracements of pattern range.
findings.quote: The pattern incorporates the powerful 0.886 XA retracement, as the defining element in the PRZ.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 5 'The Bat Pattern', pp. 71-96
findings.notes: 0.886 (4th root of 0.618) is a genuine numerical anchor that can be implemented as a frozen-ratio retracement feature. The B-point (<0.618) vs Gartley (0.618) distinction is the family-differentiator the book stresses most.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Gartley pattern - precise 0.618 B point with 0.786 D retracement
findings.mechanism: a mandatory precise 0.618 B retracement of XA validates a 5-point correction whose D completes at the 0.786 XA retracement overlapped by an equivalent AB=CD
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: B must be a precise 0.618 retracement of XA (most precise B point requirement of all patterns - deviation produces a 'deeper' Bat-like structure); D at 0.786 XA retracement; BC projection must NOT exceed 1.618 (1.13-1.618); equivalent AB=CD completion is mandatory and its overlap with the 0.786 retracement typically defines the critical PRZ level; C retrace 0.382-0.886.
findings.trigger_invalidation: BC projection >1.618 indicates a Bat, not a Gartley; the equivalent AB=CD + 0.786 overlap is the defining zone, and the reversal often fires off that overlap even before the full PRZ is tested; blowout rules apply.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry in the PRZ (book: 'a distinct window of opportunity'); the AB=CD completion and 0.786 retracement are the most critical numbers; X-point stop for retracement patterns; IPO 0.382/0.618 targets.
findings.quote: the Gartley must possess a precise 0.618 B point retracement to validate the structure
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'The Gartley Pattern', pp. 97-120
findings.notes: The B-point tolerance band is the falsifiable parameter: book says anything below ideal 0.618 alignment favors a Bat completion instead. Useful as a variant-of-family discriminator in V8's one-family-one-multiplicity-unit model.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Crab / Deep Crab extension pattern - 1.618 XA projection with extreme BC
findings.mechanism: an extreme 1.618 XA extension marks oversold/overbought exhaustion; the extreme price action into the zone signals the reversal
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: Crab - B <=0.618 retrace of XA, D at the exclusive 1.618 XA projection, extreme BC projection (typically 2.618/3.14/3.618; Deep Crab min 2.24), Alternate 1.27 or 1.618 AB=CD, C retrace 0.382-0.886. Deep Crab: B at 0.886 retracement, D still 1.618 XA projection. Book: Crab completions show the most extreme price action of all patterns and 'frequently experience sharp price action and dramatic reversals'.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The 1.618 XA projection is the minimum completion requirement (BC projection convergence is the floor); slight overshoot of the 1.618 on the initial test is tolerated but the completion point should mark the turn; severe overshoot/continuation invalidates.
findings.risk_geometry: IMPORTANT book-stated difference: extension patterns have no clean X-point stop reference ('the initial point (X) is a less significant point in the extension structure'), so stops are 'more subjective' and may require more risk than retracement patterns; wait for the 1.618 to be tested before entering.
findings.quote: The Crab is a distinct 5-point extension structure that utilizes a 1.618 projection of the XA leg exclusively. This is the most critical aspect of the pattern and the defining level in the Potential Reversal Zone (PRZ).
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7 'The Crab Pattern', pp. 121-148
findings.notes: Deep Crab (0.886 B point, both B and X violated during CD leg) is explicitly a distinct pattern from Crab and Butterfly. Extension-pattern stop subjectivity is a risk-rule caveat for V8: a frozen X-ref stop does not exist here.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Ideal Butterfly pattern - 0.786 B point with 1.27 XA projection
findings.mechanism: a mandatory 0.786 B retracement sets up a milder 1.27 XA extension with a compact BC projection; strongest at all-time high/low territory where it can end the predominant trend
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: B at precise 0.786 of XA; D at the exclusive 1.27 XA projection (NO 1.618 XA projection); BC projection >=1.618 but compact (1.618/2.0/2.24 best; 2.618 sometimes); equivalent AB=CD minimum, Alternate 1.27 AB=CD most common and rarely exceeded; C retrace 0.382-0.886 (0.618 preferred). Book: 'The ideal Butterfly works well in new high/low territory' - valid patterns frequently end the predominant trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A 1.618 XA projection means it is a Crab, not a Butterfly; BC projections should complete 'in a compact area' with the 1.27 XA; blowout of the PRZ invalidates.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the 1.27 XA projection (defining limit of PRZ); tighter structure than Crab ('tame' BC projection); IPO 0.382/0.618 targets; X-point stop for retracement-class treatment applies to the retest-of-extreme nature of the pattern.
findings.quote: a mandatory 0.786 retracement of the XA leg as the B point is the defining element of an ideal Butterfly pattern
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8 'The Ideal Butterfly Pattern', pp. 149-169
findings.notes: The book's exemplars are regime-end reversals (SPY 2009 low, Citigroup 2008 top). For BTCUSDT 1h, the 'new-high/low territory' context is common; the 0.786-B / 1.27-XA ratio pair is the falsifiable signature.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Terminal Price Bar (T-bar) initial-test reaction validation
findings.mechanism: the initial bar that tests the entire PRZ defines the reference for validity; a valid reversal must react to the zone on/near that bar, and the T-bar extreme sets the invalidation level
findings.setup_summary: After a pattern completes in the PRZ, identify the T-bar = the first bar whose range tests the full set of harmonic numbers. Valid reversal: price stabilizes on the T-bar (bullish) or the T-bar closes below the harmonic range (bearish), then continues in the reversal direction. Violation of the T-bar extreme = dead reversal thesis (and, per Ch 12, the trigger level for the failed-pattern continuation trade).
findings.trigger_invalidation: No reaction on the initial test, consolidation then resumption of the prior trend ('a common sign of a failed setup'), or close beyond the T-bar extreme/PRZ - each invalidates the reversal.
findings.risk_geometry: T-bar extreme is a frozen reference used both for the reversal stop and for the continuation entry 1-2 bars beyond it (see failed-pattern finding); no other exit geometry stated.
findings.quote: In an ideal reversal, the price bar that tests all of the numbers in the PRZ is called the Terminal Price Bar (T-bar).
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10 'Price Action in the Potential Reversal Zone (PRZ)', pp. 185-190; Ch 12 p. 234
findings.notes: Operationalizes as a still_valid-style lifecycle condition for any zone-reversal family: 'close stays on the reversal side of the T-bar extreme'. Falsifiable and cheap to compute from 1h bars.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Failed-pattern continuation - reverse the trade on PRZ/T-bar violation
findings.mechanism: when a reversal zone is blown out (gap/displacement or extreme expansion through the entire PRZ and T-bar), the failure signals overwhelming trend strength and the continuation of the predominant trend becomes the trade
findings.setup_summary: After a harmonic reversal setup is entered and the T-bar extreme is violated (book: typically 1-2 bars beyond the T-bar, often confirmed by a gap/expansion close through the zone), cover/flip and trade continuation in the prior trend direction. Stop just beyond the violated zone (book example: prior week high for a failed bullish pattern; 'a simple 1-bar stop loss would have been more than adequate').
findings.trigger_invalidation: Requires the entire PRZ to have been tested with only a nominal initial reaction first; the violation must be a clear, confirmed signal (convincing continuation after the T-bar break) - 'frequent stop-outs can occur before the price continues in the predominant trend'.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry 1-2 bars beyond the T-bar; tight stop at the extreme of the violated PRZ / T-bar; stop then trails per subsequent bars (book: 'after confirming the violation, the stop loss is usually determined by the prior price bar(s) beyond the Terminal Price Bar'); targets not specified for the continuation leg.
findings.quote: Because pattern failures are a sign of an overwhelming predominant trend, these technical events can serve as important continuation signals.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 12 'Pattern Violations', pp. 233-250
findings.notes: Direct refinement of the existing V8 failed_breakout expert (liquidity_vacuum_reentry, frozen prior_high_ref, SHORT): adds (a) both directions, (b) T-bar-based entry timing, (c) harmonic-zone context. Blowouts map naturally to perp liquidation cascades; tight stop discipline is mandatory.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Prior harmonic support/resistance polarity flip after violation
findings.mechanism: violated harmonic PRZs flip polarity: prior support becomes future resistance and prior resistance becomes future support on the retest
findings.setup_summary: After a harmonic PRZ is clearly violated, record the full PRZ band as a frozen level; on the eventual retest (book: 'it is common for price action to retest these harmonic levels'), the band acts as the opposite-polarity S/R. Book example: NQ intraday bullish Bat violated at 1780, later retested and acted as resistance; SMH gapped through a Deep Bearish Crab, retraced, and the prior resistance zone acted as support while the gap filled.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Only well-defined prior patterns count ('these situations are most commonly found when a pattern has been clearly violated'); retest must behave like the opposite-polarity level (reject on first touch) or it is not a valid flip.
findings.risk_geometry: Zone-based retest entries; no explicit stops/targets stated beyond standard PRZ management.
findings.quote: When support is violated, that price level becomes future resistance. When resistance is violated, that price level becomes future support.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 12 'Prior Harmonic Support and Resistance', pp. 246-250
findings.notes: Classic S/R flip, corroborated across many TA books; for V8 this is a location-feature input: frozen violated-zone bands (like failed_breakout's prior_high_ref) plus a polarity flag. Gap-fill note is perp-relevant: SMH example = gap fill at prior resistance, analogous to funding/liquidation-driven fills back to levels.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Harmonic Trade Management System - IPO/PPZ/SLZ/0.382 trailer
findings.mechanism: all trade parameters (entry, initial profit, protection, stop) are defined relative to the pattern structure in advance, letting price signals rather than emotion manage the position
findings.setup_summary: After a PRZ entry: (1) Initial Profit Objective (IPO) = 0.382 or 0.618 retracement of the pattern range (pattern high to reversal low for bullish); if the reversal blows through 0.382, target 0.618. (2) Split the position and bank partial profit at the IPO so half 'rides for free'. (3) Profit Protection Zone (PPZ) - 'never let a profit become a loss': defend small profits until the equivalent time projection is reached. (4) Stop Loss Zone (SLZ) beyond the PRZ. (5) 0.382 trailing stop after the IPO: cover when price retraces past the 38.2% level of the reversal move. Trend-line breaks are additional exits; stalling at an IPO with no continuation = cover.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Book rule: 'If in doubt, get out'; lack of continuation at an IPO is 'a sign of temporary exhaustion that must be respected'; the 0.382 trailer violation is the make-or-break cover trigger.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry per pattern; initial target = 0.382/0.618 of pattern range; protection = PPZ (defend profit until 1.0 time); stop = SLZ beyond PRZ then 0.382 trailer; book-stated partial-position scaling (2-3 portions) at the IPO levels.
findings.quote: Never let a profit become a loss.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11 'The Harmonic Trade Management System', pp. 203-232 (IPO p. 205, PPZ p. 206, SLZ p. 207, 0.382 trailer p. 207)
findings.notes: Directly transferable to V8 risk_geometry: targets as structure-relative retracements (not R-multiples), frozen-ratio trailing stop, and partial scaling. The IPO-at-0.382/0.618 rule gives V8 a concrete alternative target rule to the current fixed target_r=1.0. Book admits the same pattern yields different outcomes - management rules, not pattern accuracy, are the edge claim.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Fibonacci time projections - minimum 0.382 time filter and 1.0 equivalent time
findings.mechanism: a pattern's CD leg should not complete before the minimum 0.382 time projection (relative to X-to-B duration), and significant reversals often accelerate only after the equivalent (1.0) time projection is reached
findings.setup_summary: Measure the X-to-B time duration (bars); project Fibonacci time targets (0.382...1.0) from B to the D completion. Rule 1: a pattern completing before 0.382 of projected time is suspect ('a red flag... the validity of the setup must be considered suspect'). Rule 2: price is primary - never require time for entry, only filter ('the key is to execute in the PRZ, as long as the minimum 0.382 time objective has been reached'). Rule 3: defend small profits until the 1.0 equivalent time is reached, after which breakouts tend to accelerate.
findings.trigger_invalidation: CD leg completes in far less than 0.382 of the XB time -> invalidate/suspect; no meaningful move by the equivalent time -> cover the small profit.
findings.risk_geometry: No price geometry; pure expiry/validity timing: min 0.382 bar-count floor and a 1.0-count decision gate for defending the PPZ.
findings.quote: At a minimum, a pattern should not complete until it has reached the 0.382 time projection.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11 'Time Considerations', pp. 208-209; worked examples pp. 213-225
findings.notes: For 24/7 continuous tape this is cleanly computable from bar counts (no session/gap distortion). Book explicitly subordinates time to price: 'the time requirement for a pattern's completion is not as important as the price objective.' Maps to V8 expiry_bars with a minimum-bar-count validity filter.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Pattern differentiation and price-over-time discipline ('all patterns are not the same')
findings.mechanism: similar-looking 5-point structures are distinct technical entities with different ratio alignments and different management; trading them via a pre-defined rule system (entry/stop/target all set in advance) removes emotional discretion
findings.setup_summary: Methodology lessons: (1) do not treat Bat/Gartley/Crab/Butterfly as interchangeable - B-point ratio and D-point ratio define the family; (2) price is primary, time secondary - execution follows the price zone not the time projection; (3) every possible outcome (reversal, stall, blowout) has a pre-planned response (the Action/Task model); (4) keep a written trade journal + execution checklist (pattern present? AB=CD? >=3 numbers converging? warning signs? stop level? risk willing?).
findings.trigger_invalidation: No setup-level trigger; the lesson is that missing the exact alignment (e.g., labeling a Bat as a Gartley) is itself the failure mode the book warns against.
findings.risk_geometry: All parameters defined relative to structure before entry; 'the price of the next tick' as the cost of waiting for confirmation.
findings.quote: all patterns are not the same
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3 'Fibonacci Pattern Alignments', p. 37; Ch 9 'Trade Execution' (checklist p. 180, journal p. 179)
findings.notes: V8 already encodes this: one behavior family per expert, ratio-alignment variants as multiplicity units. The actionable lessons: enforce a ratio-tolerance band before formalizing a family, and require all risk_geometry to be frozen at candidate-generation time. Also book's honesty note ('not end-all-be-all... most pattern completions yield sizeable but temporary price moves') is directly compatible with V8's NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM stance.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

book_title: Harmonic Trading, Volume One: Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets (2010)
How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology (3rd edition)

findings.strategy_name: ABCD pullback continuation
