findings.setup_summary: On a 5m chart of a high-relative-volume instrument: a strong rally from A makes a new session high at B; price pulls back to C which holds above the A origin (a higher low) for at least one consolidation period; enter long near C-close, stop below C, target the D extension (new high). Never chase at B.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = C holds as support (buyers defend C). Invalidation = close below point C; also do not enter if pullback has no definable floor (stop cannot be placed).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry near C (bar close); stop below C (structure, not a fixed ATR multiple); target D (structure/new high); sell half at D and move stop to break-even; remainder exits on target, on 5m new-low weakness signal, or when buyers exhaust.
findings.quote: If the price moves higher, I sell half of my position at point D, and bring my stop higher to my entry point (break-even).
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 1 (ABCD Pattern), lines 1163-1192
findings.notes: Directly corroborates the existing trend_pullback expert family (ema_fast>ema_slow, close<ema_slow): ABCD replaces the EMA filter with a structural higher-low (C above A). Refinement input: frozen C-support ref, half-out-at-D break-even, still_valid = price holds above C. Book's self-fulfilling-prophecy rationale (many traders watch the same level) is the stated edge mechanism.
findings.book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

findings.strategy_name: Moving Average trend ride (9 EMA as moving support/resistance)
findings.setup_summary: After the high-volatility session open, a trend establishes around the 9 EMA on 1m/5m charts; enter long on a pullback to the 9 EMA that holds as support (short below it when it holds as resistance), buying as close to the MA as possible; ride until a 5m candle closes through the MA.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = EMA holds as support/resistance with price respecting it. Invalidation = 5m candle CLOSE through the EMA (wick breaks with low volume are false breakouts and do not stop the thesis); for shorts a close above the MA.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at/near MA; stop 5-10 cents below MA or on 5m candle close below MA; no fixed R target — exit on MA break; optional half-profit at extended moves (no trailing stops; manual monitoring).
findings.quote: My stop will usually be 5 to 10 cents below the moving average line or, if a candlestick, close below the moving average (for long positions).
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 5 (Moving Average Trend Trading), lines 1345-1387
findings.notes: Refinement input for trend_pullback: (1) close-based (not wick-based) EMA break as the still_valid termination — this is exactly the close-through-EMA exit discipline V8's NEXT_BAR_CLOSE semantics can express; (2) low-volume false-breakout filter (a wick through the EMA on low relative volume is not a thesis kill). Book notes trend trades hold hours and work best mid-session, i.e., a time-of-day regime dependency.
findings.book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

findings.strategy_name: Bull Flag momentum breakout with volume confirmation
findings.setup_summary: On a short timeframe (1m-5m): a vertical pole of large up-candles is followed by a sideways consolidation of small candles; enter when price moves over the high of the consolidation candlesticks, with share volume significantly higher after consolidation as confirmation; stop below the consolidation low. Trade only the first and second consolidation periods of a run.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = close above the consolidation high with volume expansion. Invalidation = close below the consolidation low (breakdown); third-and-higher consolidation periods are not traded (buyers likely losing control).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on consolidation-breakout (scalp style); stop = breakdown of consolidation; target = next resistance / profit target, book recommends quick scalp for low-float under-$10; exit half, move to break-even, remainder on loss of steam (new 5m low).
findings.quote: As soon as prices are moving over the high of the consolidation candlesticks, I enter the trade. My stop loss is the break below the consolidation periods.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 2 (Bull Flag Momentum), lines 1196-1238
findings.notes: Low-float-stock manipulation dynamics do not map to BTCUSDT 1h, but the pole-consolidation-breakout-with-volume-confirmation pattern is transferable to high-relative-volume episodes. Book flags this as the riskiest strategy requiring fast execution and scalping exits — the canonical L1 fill-at-close simulator can express it only coarsely, hence BACKLOG_CANDIDATE rather than PROPOSE_NEW_EXPERT.
findings.book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

findings.strategy_name: Extreme-RSI reversal at significant intraday support/resistance (Bottom/Top Reversal)
findings.setup_summary: On a 5m chart: at least 4-5 consecutive candles in one direction (extreme move), 5m RSI below 10 (bottom) or above 90 (top), price at or near a significant intraday support (bottom) or resistance (top) level, and an indecision candle (Doji/spinning top) or strong reversal candle at the extreme with high volume; enter on the first 1m or 5m candle making a new high (bottom) / new low (top).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = new-high/new-low candle near the level after the extreme + indecision signal. Invalidation = price resumes the prior trend (new 5m low for longs); if price goes sideways/flat for a few minutes after entry, exit immediately (likely consolidation for another leg down); never catch a falling knife without confirmation.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry = first 1m/5m candle to new high (long) or new low (short); stop = low of previous candle or low of day (long) / high of previous candle or high of day (short); target = next support/resistance level, or VWAP / 9 EMA / 20 EMA (whichever closer), or opposite-direction new 5m extreme; trail stop to break-even then to prior candle lows.
findings.quote: The key to your success with Top and Bottom Reversals is trading the extremes at or near a significant daily support or resistance level.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategies 3 & 4 (Reversal Trading), lines 1242-1341
findings.notes: Concrete and falsifiable (RSI threshold, candle-count, level proximity, entry candle). Crypto caveat: 24/7 liquidation cascades produce frequent RSI extremes on 1h bars, so the level-anchor and indecision-candle confirmation are load-bearing; without them the setup degenerates to catching falling knives. Mechanism sits adjacent to the DATA_BLOCKED capitulation backlog (capitulation_exhaustion) — proposed as a distinct exhaustion_reversal family anchored on location, not on volume climax.
findings.book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

findings.strategy_name: VWAP rejection/support trading (institutional anchor)
findings.setup_summary: On a 5m chart, price action against the session VWAP: short when price tries but fails to break/close through VWAP (rejection) or when VWAP breaks and price closes below it; long when VWAP holds as support; enter as close to VWAP as possible; stop = 5m candle close through VWAP on the opposite side; target = next support/resistance level or previous day close.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = VWAP rejection (short) or VWAP support hold (long), ideally with institutional flow visible. Invalidation = 5m candle close through VWAP (stop); if price trades sideways near VWAP (no institutional interest), stand aside.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at/near VWAP (minimize risk); stop = 5m close through VWAP; target = next level; sell half at target and move stop to break-even.
findings.quote: I usually short stocks when traders try but fail to break the VWAP on 5-minute charts.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 6 (VWAP Trading), lines 1393-1424
findings.notes: Mechanism claim: VWAP is the benchmark where institutional traders execute large orders, so failed attempts through it attract follow-on flow (self-fulfilling crowd). VWAP is directly computable on perp tapes (session-anchored or rolling); this is a strong new expert family candidate. The MOH worked example (short below VWAP, stop above VWAP, 1:3 R/R) is a clean falsifiable template.
findings.book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

findings.strategy_name: Horizontal support/resistance level trading
findings.setup_summary: Draw horizontal S/R from DAILY-chart extreme wicks (not closes, not diagonal trendlines); levels are AREAS (5-10c band), validated by a clear prior bounce and by elevated volume near the level; on the intraday chart buy near support (long) or short near resistance (short), entering on an indecision candle at the level; stop = 5m candle close below support / above resistance; target = next level.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = bounce at the level with volume and/or indecision candle. Invalidation = 5m close through the level; levels only count if they are near the current price range and have clear prior bounces.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry as close to the level as possible; stop = 5m close through the level; target = next level (or half-dollar/round-dollar if none); sell half at target, move stop to break-even; short side mirrors with a close-above-resistance stop.
findings.quote: Traders buy at support and sell at resistance, making their effectiveness a self-fulfilling prophecy.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 7 (Support or Resistance Trading), lines 1428-1486
findings.notes: Strong new expert family candidate: frozen daily-wick extreme levels are deterministic (can be computed PIT from daily bars), and the level-as-area + close-through invalidation maps cleanly to frozen-ref + still_valid semantics. Book's methodological claim: the market 'remembers price levels' not trendlines; volume near the level confirms significance. KMX worked example provides exact level/target/stop structure.
findings.book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

findings.strategy_name: Red-to-Green / previous day close rotation
findings.setup_summary: For a gapped/directional instrument: when price extends away from the previous day close and then moves back toward it with rising volume, trade the rotation — short from VWAP with target the previous day close (gapped-up case) or long toward the previous day close (gapped-down case); stop = nearest technical level (VWAP break or MA break); the move should work immediately.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = high-volume move toward the previous day close from an extension. Invalidation = break of the nearest technical level (VWAP/MA); 'Red-to-Green moves should work immediately' — if price stalls, exit (implicit time-stop).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry near VWAP or the anchoring level; stop = break of nearest technical level (VWAP/MA/support); target = previous day close; sell all at target, or bring stop to break-even once in profit.
findings.quote: The previous day close is a powerful level of support or resistance and traders should trade toward it when there is rising volume.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 8 (Red-to-Green Trading), lines 1490-1516
findings.notes: The previous day close is a well-defined daily anchor (00:00 UTC candle close) and is widely watched in crypto, but with no overnight gap the 'fill the gap' psychology is weaker than in equities — hence MEDIUM. Could be implemented as a variant of the supply_demand_zone family with a frozen previous-day-close ref, or as its own expert; the 'must work immediately' rule implies a short expiry/time-stop.
findings.book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

findings.strategy_name: Opening Range Breakout (5/15/30 min)
findings.setup_summary: Define the first 5m (or 15m/30m) candle range at session open; REQUIRE the range width to be significantly smaller than the daily ATR (else the stock is too volatile to give a catchable directional move); enter in the breakout direction when price breaks the range high (long) or low (short); stop = close back through VWAP (close below VWAP for longs, break above for shorts); target = next technical level, daily MA, or previous day close.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = close outside the opening range in a clear direction. Invalidation = close back inside the range or through VWAP; if the opening range is near/above daily ATR, do not trade (no directional signal).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on range-break; stop = close through VWAP; target = next technical level (intraday level, daily MA, PDC); if no level, exit on weakness (new 5m low for longs) / strength (new 5m high for shorts).
findings.quote: The opening range must be significantly smaller than the stock's Average True Range (ATR).
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 9 (Opening Range Breakouts), lines 1520-1559
findings.notes: Equities version relies on the 9:30 opening auction and overnight-gap psychology that crypto lacks, but a session-open range is definable (e.g., first N bars of the UTC day or after a funding-settlement window). The range-width-vs-ATR filter is a falsifiable, high-value addition to any breakout family. ORB is described as an entry signal only — target and stop must come from other levels, so it is a candidate behavior family more than a standalone edge.
findings.book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

findings.strategy_name: 2% risk cap + minimum 2:1 R:R + three-step position sizing
findings.setup_summary: Pre-trade risk protocol: (1) maximum dollar risk on any trade = 2% of account equity, computed before the session; (2) per-share/per-contract risk = stop distance from the strategy (technical level, not arbitrary); (3) max position = max_risk / risk_per_share. Do not take any trade with reward:risk below 2:1 (a logical stop that would risk >2% of equity means skip the trade).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = setup with R:R >= 2:1 and stop inside the 2% cap. Invalidation = stop placement requires >2% equity risk or R:R < 2:1 — pass on the trade regardless of attractiveness.
findings.risk_geometry: Position = (2% x equity) / (entry - stop); min reward:risk 2:1; stop always at a reasonable technical level (VWAP, MA, level), never tightened below the technical level to force a ratio.
findings.quote: The absolute maximum traders may risk on any trade is 2% of their account equity.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3 (Risk and Account Management; Three-Step Risk Management), lines 345-424
findings.notes: Corroborates V8 RiskGate design: 2% fixed-fractional cap, R-multiple targets, stop-at-technical-level admission, skip-trade-on-over-risk. Book adds the breakeven math: with a 2:1 R:R gate a trader can be wrong 40% of the time and still profit — a rationale V8 can encode as a minimum-R:R admission check. Directly transferable to perp sizing (notional/leverage-adjusted).
findings.book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

findings.strategy_name: Never average down a losing position; scale into winners only
findings.setup_summary: If the thesis level is lost (e.g., support breaks), exit — do not add to the losing position to lower average cost; averaging down wins ~85% of the time but the ~15% of trades that fail blow up the account, and the one bad trade can end the career. Scaling is permitted ONLY into winners (add on validated continuation, e.g., re-adding shorts after a failed retest of a broken level).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = thesis invalidation (level/MA/VWAP break). Invalidation: any add-on-a-losing-position is prohibited; re-entry is allowed only when the setup re-forms (e.g., price returns below the broken level).
findings.risk_geometry: Honor stop at the technical level; position added only on favorable confirmation; LABU and Amaranth/Brian Hunter case studies are the cautionary evidence (margin call / forced liquidation).
findings.quote: Averaging down does not work for day traders... 85% of the time you will profit when you average down. But the 15% of the time you are wrong, you will blow up your account.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7 (Trade Management and Position Sizing), lines 1103-1157
findings.notes: Maps to V8 lifecycle/risk rules: ONE exposure per direction, dead-thesis exit (stops vs still_valid), no re-entry until setup re-forms. Especially load-bearing in perps where leverage turns 'averaging down' into a liquidation event (margin-call dynamic = funding + leverage amplification). Note the author reports a distribution asymmetry (85/15) that is the classic martingale ruin argument — falsifiable only as a risk-behavior rule, not as an edge claim.
findings.book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

findings.strategy_name: Stocks-in-Play universe filter (high relative volume + catalyst episodes)
findings.setup_summary: Universe/regime gate before any strategy applies: pre-market gap >=2% or intraday move >=$1, average relative volume >=1.5x normal, ATR >= $0.50 (min volatility), average daily volume >=500k (min liquidity), short interest <30% (avoid squeeze exposure), and a fundamental catalyst (news/earnings/FDA/M&A). Trade only instruments in this state; a stock trading at normal volume is dominated by HFT and not tradeable.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = high-relative-volume episode with catalyst. Invalidation = relative volume returns to normal / no catalyst / moves are choppy without directional foreshadowing — stay out.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A (universe selection filter, not an entry geometry); feeds instrument and episode selection before strategy-specific stops/targets apply.
findings.quote: Retail traders trade only Stocks in Play, high relative volume stocks that have fundamental catalysts and are being traded regardless of the overall market.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 4 (How to Find Stocks for Trades; Rule 7), lines 497-706
findings.notes: For a single-instrument BTCUSDT tape this is an episodic regime filter rather than a cross-sectional stock screen: the participation feature group should capture relative-volume spikes, ATR expansion, and catalyst windows (news, ETF flows, funding spikes). The book's anti-correlation principle ('independent of sector and overall market') maps to a cross-market feature (BTC vs alt/market beta) — candidates for the participation and cross_market feature groups.
findings.book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

findings.strategy_name: Session time-of-day regime + daily giveback bracket
findings.setup_summary: Session segmentation with strategy-to-session mapping: Open (first ~1.5h, highest volume/volatility) is the most profitable period — trade momentum/VWAP with full size; Mid-day (low liquidity) is the most dangerous — cut size, tighten stops, only reversal/VWAP/MA/S-R setups, never momentum; Close (last hour) is directional — trade with the institutional flow. Hard daily bracket: stop trading (or move to simulator) after giving back 30% of Open-session profits during Mid-day/Close.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = session regime transition (liquidity expansion/contraction). Invalidation = daily giveback bracket exceeded (loss of 30% of Open profits) — trading stops for the day.
findings.risk_geometry: Position size tiered by session (largest at Open, smallest mid-day); stops tight mid-day; the 30% giveback bracket acts as a daily P&L stop independent of per-trade stops.
findings.quote: I am not allowed to lose more than 30% of what I have made in the Open during Mid-day and the Close.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7 (Trading Based on the Time of Day), lines 1599-1615
findings.notes: Crypto is 24/7 with no 9:30 bell, but session structure exists (UTC daily boundary, Asia/Europe/US liquidity, funding-settlement windows at 00:00/08:00/16:00 UTC). Maps to the time feature group (session regime) plus a daily-equity giveback bracket in lifecycle — a deterministic daily stop on realized session P&L that is fully implementable in the replay clock model (no wall clock needed).
findings.book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

findings.strategy_name: AB=CD measured-move completion
findings.mechanism: harmonic swing legs repeat in length; CD completes at a price that can be projected from AB and the BC retracement ratio
findings.setup_summary: On any timeframe (book examples 5m to daily), identify three swing legs: AB impulse, BC retracement that completes between 0.382 and 0.786 of AB (measured on swing highs/lows), then CD resuming the AB direction. Project D = C +- (AB x 1.00/1.272/1.618). Pattern is valid only if BC does not exceed 1.00 x AB and D exceeds B. Enter with a limit order just beyond the projected D (shaded), expecting price to reverse and trade back to retracements of the AD swing.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches projected D after a valid ABC structure. Invalidations: BC retracement exceeds 1.00 of AB; D fails to exceed B; warning signs at C (gap in direction of D, wide range bar ~2x normal, CD made in far fewer bars than AB) signal D will overshoot to 1.272/1.618 rather than 1.00.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit order shaded just beyond D. Stop: fixed points (e.g., 5 points on S&P E-mini) or beyond a swing point. Targets: first = .618 retracement of AD, second = .786 retracement of AD; scale out 2-3 parts, move stop to breakeven after first target. Typical legs 5-8 bars; CD in fewer bars implies extension.
findings.quote: The AB=CD pattern is a measured move where the CD leg is similar in length to the AB leg.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 4, AB=CD Pattern Structure
findings.notes: Fully implementable on BTCUSDT 1h OHLCV with swing-pivot detection and Fibonacci projection; no gap dependency (the gap-based CD-extension warning sign is absent in 24/7 markets, but the wide-range-bar variant remains measurable). The book cites Gartley's ~70% correctness claim and '40 years of testing' but presents no reproducible statistics.
findings.book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

findings.strategy_name: Gartley 222 retest entry
findings.mechanism: a four-leg X-A-B-C-D structure containing a valid AB=CD retests a prior extreme and offers a low-risk trend-direction entry before the bigger move
findings.setup_summary: X is the anchor (recent swing high/low, possibly on a higher timeframe). Leg XA forms, AB retraces to a Fibonacci level, the embedded AB=CD completes at D. Primary D completion is at .786 of XA (also .618/.50/.382; .382 in strong trends). Buy a higher low / sell a lower high - a retest entry into the established trend. Invalidations: D cannot exceed X; C cannot exceed A; B cannot exceed X (then it becomes a Butterfly).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches D at the .786 retracement of XA with the internal AB=CD valid. Invalidated: D exceeds X, C exceeds A, or B exceeds X; wide-range bar or gap at D (warning sign) -> wait for confirmation.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit just beyond D (.786). Stop: beyond X (1.00) if risk acceptable, else fixed dollar amount (e.g., 8 cents/soybeans, $5.50/GOOG). Target 1 = amount risked (breakeven stop after), target 2 = .618 of AD. Trailing: stop below the .786 of the most recent retracement after price makes .382 off AD. 2-3 part scale-outs.
findings.quote: By definition, it is buying a higher low or selling a lower high, which is ideal for trading with the trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 5, Trading the Gartley "222" Pattern
findings.notes: Trend-following retest with limit entry and quantified risk - well suited to 24/7 perps where retests of swing extremes are frequent and limit fills are reliable. Distinct from existing EMA-based trend_pullback (different trigger: harmonic swing completion vs EMA cross). Gartley's 'profitable in 7 out of 10 cases over 30 years' is an assertion, not a presented study.
findings.book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

findings.strategy_name: Butterfly extension reversal
findings.mechanism: a failed Gartley where D extends beyond X to the 1.272/1.618 expansion of XA marks an overbought/oversold extreme where a reversal becomes probable
findings.setup_summary: Four legs X-A-B-C-D with D beyond X (the Gartley failure point) at the 1.272 or 1.618 expansion of XA; must contain a valid AB=CD within the AD swing; AB retraces .618/.786 (deeper first retracement is a clue). Countertrend entry at a major top/bottom. Negations: D beyond 2.618 of XA (trend continues), B beyond X, C beyond A, D not beyond X, or no internal AB=CD. Max risk is generally at the 1.618 level.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: D completes at 1.272/1.618 expansion of XA. Invalidated/negated: extension beyond 2.618 of XA; B above X (sell) or below X (buy); C beyond A; D fails to exceed X; gap toward completion is an overshoot warning.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit at D (1.272 or 1.618). Stop: just beyond the 1.618 expansion of XA (or fixed dollar amount if 1.618 too far - e.g., $500/contract euro). Targets: first .618 of AD, second 1.272 of AD; 3-part scale-outs used on reversals. Book warns failures are fast and violent - stops mandatory.
findings.quote: The Butterfly pattern is best described as an extension pattern. It is also a failed Gartley pattern where the D completion point completes above the X.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6, Butterfly Pattern Description
findings.notes: Contrarian top/bottom-picking at extremes is inherently high-risk with perp leverage ('when this one fails it usually fails in a big way'). No gaps in 24/7 markets removes one completion-side signal. Would need extra risk gating (heat cap, forced stop) and is a candidate for a later registry experiment, not an active expert.
findings.book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

findings.strategy_name: Three Drives exhaustion
findings.mechanism: three evenly spaced, successively higher/lower drives with 1.272/1.618 inter-drive extensions mark the final push before a reversal or a deeper correction
findings.setup_summary: Three evenly spaced tops (uptrend) or bottoms (downtrend), each drive-to-drive distance a 1.272 or 1.618 extension of the prior; contains an embedded AB=CD with retracements at A and C ideally at .618/.786; near-perfect time symmetry (legs ~equal bars or a Fibonacci ratio of bar counts). Entry at drive 3 completion; signals either a major reversal or the end of a swing/correction.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: drive 3 completes at the projected 1.272/1.618 level. Invalidated: drive ordering broken (drive 2 not between 1 and 3); C beyond A / B beyond D; extensions past 1.618 while forming; large gaps toward drive 3 completion (trend not exhausting).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit at drive-3 completion (1.272/1.618). Stop: below recent swing low / beyond the 1.618, or fixed (e.g., $2.00/share QQQQ, 5 points E-mini). Target 1 = amount risked; then .618 retracement of the swing; reversal setups allow 3-part scale-outs with extension targets.
findings.quote: It consists of three evenly spaced tops in an uptrend or three evenly spaced bottoms in a downtrend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Three Drives Pattern Description
findings.notes: Structurally distinct from Butterfly (three-drive spacing symmetry vs single XA-extension) but same exhaustion-reversal family and same failure mode (continuation moves when it fails, e.g., gold failed-sell setup where price rose $125). Falsifiable via swing labelling but contrarian profile warrants backlog status.
findings.book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

findings.strategy_name: Fibonacci retracement entry in an established trend
findings.mechanism: in a trend, pullbacks find support/resistance at Fibonacci retracement levels of the prior impulse leg, so entering at .382-.786 of XA is a trend-continuation entry
findings.setup_summary: Two legs only (XA impulse, AB retracement) - no AB=CD required. In an established trend, enter with a limit at the .382/.50/.618/.786 retracement of XA, in the trend direction. Strongest trends retrace only .382/.50; bar-count symmetry between XA and AB (equal bars or Fibonacci ratio of bar counts) adds confluence. Rapid 2-3 bar AB completion is a warning sign to wait.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price trades into the Fib retracement zone of XA in a trend. Invalidated/stand-aside: long wide-range bar just before the level (wait for .786 or momentum slowdown); AB completes in far fewer bars than XA; deep retracement beyond 1.00.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit at Fib level. Stop: just beyond X (1.00) or beyond swing low/high. Target 1 = amount risked (e.g., $1.45 INTC), then opposite Fib levels or the D of a forming AB=CD. Refines V8 trend_pullback: replaces EMA-cross trigger with swing-based Fib retracement level + bar-count confluence.
findings.quote: A retracement-type pattern gives the trader an advantage of not having to try to pick a top or a bottom - it is an entry into a trade in the direction of the trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8, Fibonacci Retracement Pattern Structure
findings.notes: Directly testable on BTCUSDT 1h (swing detection + retracement levels + bar-count symmetry). Closely related to existing trend_pullback; a shallow-retracement variant (.382/.50 in strong trends) with Fib-level entry is a natural family variant, keeping the one-family-one-unit multiplicity rule.
findings.book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

findings.strategy_name: Opening Price Retracement day-trade setup
findings.mechanism: the day's opening price acts as a magnet/decision anchor; a .618/.786 retracement of the off-open range in the direction of the open yields a high-probability intraday trade
findings.setup_summary: Stocks only in the book. Price above the opening price 30-60 min after the open -> wait for a .618 or .786 retracement of the day's off-open range (low-to-high) and buy; below the open -> sell the .618/.786 retracement of the high-to-low off-open range. Only the current day's open is used. Claim: opening price sits in the upper/lower 20% of the day's range >60% of the time and price above (below) the open gives >60% long (short) win probability.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: .618/.786 retracement of the off-open range reached after an open-direction move. Invalidated/stand-aside: gap-through open with no retracement; warning signs (wide range bars); price consolidating sideways instead of moving to a retracement level.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit at .618/.786 of the off-open range. Stop: just below day low / above day high (e.g., 55c CTX, 85c GS). Target 1 = .618 of the first swing off entry, then move to breakeven; second target can use a forming pattern (e.g., Butterfly 1.27). Day trade - close flat by day end.
findings.quote: if the price is above the opening price, the probability of a winning long trade is above 60 percent
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8, Opening Price Retracement Setups
findings.notes: The mechanism is tied to equity/futures session microstructure (overnight order accumulation around the auction open). 24/7 perps have no single auction; a UTC-day-open anchor could be tested but the '>60%' statistic is asserted, not demonstrated. Low-priority candidate; requires a session-anchor decision before any experiment.
findings.book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

findings.strategy_name: NR7 trend-day regime filter with shallow-pullback entries
findings.mechanism: volatility contraction (NR7) precedes expansion; trend days open near one extreme, hold gaps, and produce shallow repetitive corrections, so pullback entries have tight quantifiable stops
findings.setup_summary: Regime filter: NR7 (narrowest range of the past 7 sessions) precedes trend days; confirmation of a trend day = open at/near one extreme, gap held with no fill attempt, wide range bars in the first 15-30 minutes, neutral closes. On a confirmed trend day: enter shallow pullbacks/consolidations (corrections 1.25-3.5 points, rarely beyond 5.5 points; .382/.50 retracements using the opening price) in the trend direction. Trend is over when new highs stop being made or support breaks.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trend-day conditions confirmed; enter on the next 2-3 point pullback or consolidation. Invalidated: correction exceeds the 5.5-point pullback rule; failure to make a new high after a pullback (trend over). Countertrend entries on a trend day are the book's primary warning.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit 2 points into a shallow pullback / just above a consolidation level. Stop: 3 points initial, placed below the wide-range-bar low or below the trend pullback level; trail above/below last small swing. Targets: retest of last high, then hold core into the close; add on subsequent patterns. Scale out into the close.
findings.quote: A narrowing of range, referred to as an NR7, which is defined as the narrowest range in the past seven trading days.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10, Identifying a Trend Day
findings.notes: NR7 and shallow-repetitive-correction behavior are measurable on 24/7 crypto (UTC-day candles replace the session; 'gap held' becomes 'opening range held'). Directly usable as a regime filter + variant of trend_pullback (shallow .382/.50 pullback entry, tight stop). Book cites Crabel and Raschke statistical research without reproducing it.
findings.book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

findings.strategy_name: Warning-sign/confirmation-bar entry filter
findings.mechanism: momentum overshoot at pattern completion: wide-range bars, gaps, tail closes, and steep final legs indicate price will exceed the completion point, so delaying entry one time bar filters the overshoot
findings.setup_summary: Methodology applied to all pattern completions (AB=CD, Gartley, etc.). Warning signs (gap in the CD leg, wide range bar ~2x normal at/near completion, tail closes, very steep CD vs AB) -> pass or wait. Confirmation signs (tweezer top/bottom, gap in the trade direction, close at range extreme in trade direction, or waiting one full time bar after the trigger) -> low-risk entry with a stop under the confirmation bar.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - this is an entry-timing filter on pattern completions, not a standalone setup. Both branches (warning -> stand aside; confirmation -> enter next bar) are implementable as a variant of any pattern expert.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after trigger (matching V8 simulator convention) or after a confirmation bar; stop just below the tweezer/confirmation low. Waiting one bar is the core rule: 'daily time frame waits one daily bar, 5-minute time frame waits one 5-minute bar'.
findings.quote: Waiting one time bar can be used when the trader has reason to believe, based on price behavior, that price may exceed the completion point of a pattern.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11, Warning Signs and Confirmation Signs
findings.notes: Feeds bar-range, tail (close vs high/low position), and wick features into marketstate; 'wait one bar' is a cheap entry-delay variant in the simulator. The overshoot claim (price exceeds D when momentum is extreme) is a falsifiable feature test across all pattern experts.
findings.book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

findings.strategy_name: 1-3% risk-per-trade sizing with risk-free scaling
findings.mechanism: risk control dominates the trading equation because wins/losses/order are unpredictable; sizing by stop distance and a small % of capital keeps drawdowns survivable
findings.setup_summary: Risk 1-3% of trading capital per trade (novices 1%); position size = (capital x risk%) / stop distance, rounded down; never risk more than ~10% of the instrument price as a stop (about 5% is reasonable); never widen a stop; always place a stop (Rule #1/#2). After taking a first profit equal to the amount risked, move the stop to breakeven (risk-free trade) and scale out remaining units at further Fib targets. Recompute sizing when the account shrinks/grows; cap concurrent open positions.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - a position-sizing and stop policy, not an entry setup.
findings.risk_geometry: Position sizing formula: shares/contracts = risk_dollars / stop_distance. E.g., $100k account x 3% = $3000 / $2.00 stop = 1500 shares. Stop never exceeds ~10% of instrument price. First target = risk amount, then breakeven stop, then trailing to .618/.786 levels.
findings.quote: We suggest using a risk in the range of 1 percent to 3 percent of total trading capital on any one trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11, Money Management
findings.notes: Directly maps to V8 RiskGate (deterministic admission, heat cap, one exposure per instrument/direction, position sizing by stop distance). Critically relevant to perps where margin-based sizing at 10-50x leverage ignores true risk. 'Risk-free trade' (breakeven after first target = risk) is a lifecycle-rule candidate.
findings.book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

findings.strategy_name: Head and Shoulders neckline break with measured target
findings.mechanism: a three-swing reversal structure (left shoulder - head - right shoulder) whose neckline break resolves the pattern; height projection gives a measured target
findings.setup_summary: Left shoulder, head, right shoulder; the countertrend rally into the right shoulder usually retraces .618/.786 of the head swing (lower right-shoulder ratio = more bearish for a top). Entry on the neckline break (sell-stop below neckline for a top, buy-stop above for a bottom) or by fading the right-shoulder retracement. Measured target = pattern height projected from the broken neckline; alternate target = 1.272 extension of the internal AB=CD. Failure point = above the head (top) / below the head (bottom), where the move reverses and continues the original trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: neckline break after the right shoulder forms. Invalidated: price exceeds the head (pattern fails); right shoulder retraces beyond the left-shoulder extreme. Stand-aside if pattern is only visible late.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: sell/buy-stop at neckline or limit at right-shoulder .618/.786. Stop: above head (top) or visual point/dollar amount; manage to breakeven after partial. Target 1: pattern-height projection from neckline; target 2: 1.272 extension of AD of embedded AB=CD, then trail.
findings.quote: Another traditional way to measure a profit objective with this pattern is to take the height of the pattern and project it down from the price level of the broken neckline.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 9, Trading the Head and Shoulders Top Pattern
findings.notes: Swing-structure pattern implementable on 1h BTC (shoulder/head/neckline detection + measured projection). Note in crypto the neckline is often tested repeatedly and stop placements cluster there, so the breakout quality signal matters. Book notes left shoulders often contain Butterfly/AB=CD structures that can be traded directly.
findings.book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

findings.strategy_name: Double Top/Bottom stop-run excess penetration
findings.mechanism: in double tops/bottoms the second extreme slightly exceeds the first to take out clustered stop orders placed at/beyond the level, then reverses; the excess penetration is a liquidity artifact
findings.setup_summary: Classical Double Bottom/Top: the second low just barely ticks through the first low (or the second high through the first high) before reversing - stops placed just at/beyond the extreme are 'taken out just as the market reverses'. Trend clues: wide range bars on the reversal side, first retracement only reaching .382 (sign of a trend). Trade the reversal long after the stop-run on the second low, or trade the failure point (break beyond the pattern extreme = explosive continuation) via buy-stop/sell-stop orders.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: second extreme wicks through the first and reverses with wide bars. Invalidated: the extreme breaks cleanly without reversal (failure point), which then becomes a continuation entry in the breakdown direction.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit at .618 retracement of the reversal move or buy-stop above the failure point; a smaller timeframe can time the entry. Stop: below the pattern low / beyond the failure level; profit taken at .382 retracement, stop to breakeven. Failure point of double top = the pattern high; double bottom = the pattern low.
findings.quote: It is not unusual for the second low on a Double Bottom pattern to be exceeded by a small amount... stops are placed just at or slightly beyond these levels and are taken out just as the market reverses.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 9, Pattern Recognition (Double Top and Bottom)
findings.notes: Directly corroborates the V8 liquidity_sweep_reclaim family mechanism (liquidity_vacuum_reentry): a wick through a prior extreme that is reclaimed by close. 'Second low ticks through first low' is a concrete, testable feature on 1h BTC. Stop clusters near swing extremes are prominent in perps with liquidation cascades.
findings.book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

findings.strategy_name: Harmonic-number swing-amplitude stop placement
findings.mechanism: each market has a reproducible dominant swing amplitude ('harmonic number'); the dominant swing size on the traded timeframe is the natural stop distance and pullback target
findings.setup_summary: Empirical methodology: measure the most common recurring swing amplitude on the traded timeframe (e.g., S&P 5.4 pts, euro 70 pips, gold 11/17, crude 44/88) from a sample (book suggests ~100 swings); use it as the stop distance (or 3% of instrument price as a proxy harmonic, e.g., IBM $99.48 -> $2.98 harmonic used as a stop) and as a pullback target. Harmonics on smaller timeframes relate to larger ones by 1/2 or .618. Expansions (2x-3x the harmonic) signal trend mode.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - a stop/target calibration methodology applied within pattern experts.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop distance = dominant harmonic swing amplitude (or 3%-of-price proxy) placed beyond the swing high/low; profit target = harmonic projection down/up from the extreme; replaces a universal ATR multiple with an instrument-specific amplitude calibrated per timeframe.
findings.quote: The 3 percent harmonic would be approximately $2.98... We can use $2.98 for placing a stop-loss order if buying the pullback.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3, Using the 3 Percent Rule for Finding a Harmonic Number
findings.notes: The usable core for V8 is 'dominant swing amplitude per timeframe as stop distance', which is testable as a robust percentile of swing ranges on BTCUSDT 1h. The fixed 3%-of-price variant transfers poorly to crypto (regime-varying volatility), and the harmonic-number mysticism (Gann/astrology lineage) is not evidence. More natural as a stop-calibration input to atr_stop than as a standalone strategy.
findings.book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

book_title: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading: The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns into Profit (Part 1) — Jared F. Martinez, 2007

findings.strategy_name: New-high pullback short (stop-cluster retracement)
findings.mechanism: protective stop-loss orders clustered just beyond prior highs get absorbed by the breakout, then sellers exceed buyers and price pulls back after every new high is scored
findings.setup_summary: After price takes out a significant prior high (book example: a multi-month GBP high), switch to a 15-min chart and short on the bar close of a bearish candlestick formation (evening star, bearish engulfing, tweezer top); book cites a 200-pip drop in ~45 minutes. Mirror going long at new lows with bullish formations.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid if price keeps making new highs after entry (bulls keep scoring points / channel shifts up): 'If the bulls take out the high, they will more than likely keep on going.'
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: next bar close after a bearish candle at/just after the new high. Stop: a little beyond the last high of resistance (last low for longs). Target: first pullback support — past support, uptrend line, or Fibonacci retracement; no explicit R-multiple or expiry stated.
findings.quote: most of the time, after the bulls achieve a new high, frequently prices start to retrace, or fall back down
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 5 'Resistance and Support' / 'How Do Bulls and Bears Score Points?' (pp.73-81)
findings.notes: The book explicitly roots the pullback in stop-order clusters near last highs — a liquidity mechanism, not just mean reversion. In crypto perps, leverage + 24/7 trading concentrate stops at prior highs/round levels; testable as a location+response family. Distinct from V8 liquidity_sweep_reclaim (no wick-through-close sweep required; entry is the rejection candle after a clean new high).
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Trend-line cascade bounce (inner -> outer -> long-term)
findings.mechanism: correctly drawn trend lines act as floors/ceilings; the market bounces off each line in the trend direction and only a full cascade of breaks signals major reversal
findings.setup_summary: In an uptrend, buy the bounce when price retraces to the inner or outer uptrend line (lines drawn across wick lows; outer at ~45 degrees) while price remains above the outer line ('80 percent chance' of continuation, asserted). If the inner line breaks, expect price to travel to the outer line and bounce there; if the outer breaks, to the long-term line; a long-term line break implies major reversal. Mirror for downtrends.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid on a decisive close beyond the respective trend line; long-term line break = major reversal, do not re-enter.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close at/after the trend-line touch. Stop: just beyond the trend line (below it for longs). Target: next higher trend line / prior high; no explicit R-multiple or expiry. Book's probability claims (80% continuation) are asserted, not measured.
findings.quote: If the inner trend line is broken, the market usually moves to the outer trend line and will bounce back up from there... If the long-term trend line is broken, as a rule there will be a major reversal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'Finding and Drawing Inner, Outer, and Long-term Uptrend Lines' (pp.96-104); Ch 6 'The Value of Trend Lines' (pp.111)
findings.notes: Distinct from the existing trend_pullback family (EMA-based): this is a geometric trend-line family. Falsifiability requires a deterministic line-fitting rule (regression across wick lows/highs), which the book only describes qualitatively — formalize before coding. The 80% figure is practitioner assertion.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Zone-break angle filter (buy/sell zone entry)
findings.mechanism: after a trend line is broken, the position of the line's extension ('backside') relative to the last swing extreme determines whether the break is a true reversal or a channel shift
findings.setup_summary: When price closes through an uptrend line into the sell zone, compare the trend-line extension to the last swing high: if the backside of the line is lower than the last high, short with a claimed 80% probability of continued dip/reversal; if higher than the last high, expect continued rally (channel shift). Mirror for downtrend lines entering the buy zone. Require the breaking candle itself to be a bearish (or bullish) decision candle — a counter-candle at the break means the trend is still intact.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if a bullish candle appears immediately at the break of an uptrend line (market 'still potentially bullish'), or if price reclaims the last high.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: after bar close into the zone (next bar). Stop: 'above the last high of resistance' for shorts / below last low for longs. Target: next support/resistance; no explicit R-multiple or expiry.
findings.quote: If the backside of the trend line is lower than the last high, there is an 80 percent chance of a continued dip and a trend reversal. If the backside of the trend line is higher than the last high, there is an 80 percent chance of a continued rally.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7 'The Sell Zone' and 'The Buy Zone' (pp.117-125)
findings.notes: Gated on subjective line placement + angle measurement; needs a precise line-fitting spec to be falsifiable, hence backlog not formalize. Crypto: bar-close zone breaks are clean (no exchange gaps), but BTC trend lines are noisy vs FX 45-degree norms.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Fibonacci retracement C-entry / D-extension (A-B-C-D wave)
findings.mechanism: after an A->B rally the market retraces into the AB boundary and bounces at a Fibonacci retracement level; shallow retraces (0.382-0.618) imply strong follow-through to the 1.618 extension, while a deep 0.786 retrace implies weak follow-through to only the 1.27 extension
findings.setup_summary: In an uptrend, take the latest A-B move, draw the Fibonacci retracement/extension grid, and enter long at the C bar close when price bounces at a 0.382/0.50/0.618 retracement, ideally at a convergence (Fib level + uptrend line + past support + bullish candle). Target the D extension (1.27 or 1.618) or the nearest of four past resistance levels, placing a limit exit 10 pips in front of the level. Mirror for downtrends.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if price continues through the next Fib level without a bounce candle — retracement beyond 0.786 signals the trend is likely broken.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close of the confirming bounce candle at the retracement level. Stop: sized by equity management (book's typical 30-50 pips) or beyond the C swing extreme. Target: D extension (1.27/1.618) or nearest of four past resistance/support levels, limit order 10 pips before the level; no explicit expiry.
findings.quote: Should the market bounce at the 0.382, 0.50, or 0.618, it will predominately rally and go to a 1.618 extension... If it retraces all the way down to the 0.786, it will only go to the 1.27 extension.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8 'The Fibonacci Retracement and Extension Ratio Relationship' + 'Steps to Be Followed When Trading an Uptrend' (pp.140-149)
findings.notes: The book's C-entry is explicitly a convergence stack (Fib + trend line + candlestick) — its cleanest articulation of 'multiple reasons to enter'. Fib levels are widely watched (self-fulfilling component). The shallow-vs-deep retrace-to-extension mapping is the falsifiable core. Fully implementable from OHLC alone.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Consolidation range fade with candlestick confirmation
findings.mechanism: inside a sideways range, institutional sellers at resistance and buyers at support push price back to the opposite side of the range; a missing reversal candle at the boundary is itself a signal of imminent breakout
findings.setup_summary: Identify a consolidation (equal highs/lows; book: ranges ~150-300 pips on larger TFs, market is sideways 50-60% of the time). Sell at resistance on the close of a bearish candlestick formation; buy at support on a bullish formation; ride to the opposite side of the range and repeat until breakout. If no candlestick formation appears near a boundary, the market is likely about to break out — stand aside.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if price closes beyond the range boundary (by construction no reversal candle formed) or the range expands.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close of reversal candle at the range boundary. Stop: beyond the range boundary (past resistance for shorts, past support for longs). Target: the opposite side of the range; no explicit R-multiple or expiry.
findings.quote: you need to sell at the level of resistance and buy at a level of support when you find a consolidation in the market.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11 'Strategy 1' (pp.178-181); Ch 3 sideways-market discussion (p.40)
findings.notes: Book insists trend systems bleed out in sideways markets and a trader needs BOTH a trend system and a range system — a direct argument for a range_reversion family in V8's portfolio (complexity budget still gates to 3 active). Crypto ranges frequently; equal-high/low detection is mechanical.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Pre-announcement consolidation straddle breakout
findings.mechanism: immediately before a scheduled macro announcement traders stand aside, compressing price into a tight range; the release triggers a directional breakout whose expected magnitude scales with range duration
findings.setup_summary: Five minutes before a scheduled fundamental announcement, with price in a 20-60 pip tight range, place a buy stop 15 pips above resistance and a sell stop 10 pips below support (spread-adjusted: +5 pips); the longer the pre-announcement range, the more aggressive the expected breakout. If a triggered order is stopped out and price returns into the range, the book says the market tends to then go the other way — keep the second order live.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If the market returns into the range after triggering one side, favor the opposite direction; on a no-change announcement expect continuation of the prior trend rather than a breakout.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: resting stop orders (buy 15 pips above resistance, sell 10 pips below support). Stops: sell stop 15 pips above last high, buy stop 10 pips below last low. Target: next past support/resistance levels; book warns of 30-100 pip slippage on fills and 200-pip/20-second spikes.
findings.quote: Place a buy order 15 pips above or north of the resistance level and 10 pips below or south of the level of support, or the trading range.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11 'Strategy 2' (pp.181-183); Ch 10 'Trading Days versus Trending Days' (pp.167-170)
findings.notes: The book notes brokers largely eliminated straddling because of slippage — the same failure mode applies to fast crypto macro candles (CPI/FOMC/NFP) and liquidation cascades. The spread-adjusted stop math is venue-specific (Binance USDM taker fees differ from FX pip spreads). Needs the crypto macro-calendar feature before it is testable.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Bull/bear trap fade (false breakout of consolidation)
findings.mechanism: with no scheduled catalyst, a breakout out of consolidation is a false move ('fulfilling the natural numerical sequence') and price U-turns back in the direction of the prior trend toward the D extension
findings.setup_summary: After a consolidation with no scheduled fundamental announcement, a breakout to the south (bull trap) or north (bear trap) that fails and closes back inside the range signals reversal back toward the prior trend; enter on the return close in the prior-trend direction.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the breakout continues beyond the fake-out extreme (genuine breakout), or if an unscheduled catalyst/announcement appears.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close back inside the range after the false breakout. Stop: beyond the fake-out extreme. Target: direction of the prior trend toward the Fibonacci D extension; no explicit R-multiple or expiry.
findings.quote: bull traps are false breakouts to the south out of that consolidation, doing nothing more than fulfilling the natural numerical sequence of the market, then U-turning back in the direction of the previous trend
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11 'Bull and Bear Traps' (pp.184-185)
findings.notes: Conceptually adjacent to V8's failed_breakout (liquidity_vacuum_reentry) but contextually distinct — it happens at a consolidation boundary rather than a prior high, and its precondition is 'no scheduled announcement'. Best handled as a variant of the failed_breakout family (one multiplicity unit). The 'no announcement' precondition maps to the crypto macro calendar + funding/expiry windows.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Trend-filtered candlestick reversal patterns
findings.mechanism: reversal candlestick formations (morning star, bullish engulfing, tweezer bottom / evening star, bearish engulfing, tweezer top) signal U-turns only when they appear in the direction of the prevailing trend and only after the final candle closes with confirmation
findings.setup_summary: In an uptrend (candles above the outer uptrend line) buy only bullish formations: morning star (large bearish decision candle -> 1-4 indecision candles -> bullish close beyond the 60% mark of the first candle), bullish engulfing (opens below prior close and engulfs 1-3 prior candles), or tweezer bottom (two+ indecision candles with long lower wicks at near-equal lows, forming support). Mirror the three bearish formations in a downtrend. Ignore all formations inside a 20-40 pip (ATR-scaled for crypto) sideways range.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the confirming candle fails to close beyond the 60% mark of the first candle, or the pattern forms in a flat/consolidating range (book: these 'should be ignored').
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: only after the last candle of the formation closes ('wait until the last candle closes before you enter the market'). Stop: protective stop beyond the pattern extreme / last support. Target: not explicitly defined beyond trend continuation.
findings.quote: in a downtrend, only trade bearish candlestick formations, not bullish... In trading any candlestick formation, you must wait until the last candle closes before you enter the market
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 4 'Bullish/Bearish Candlestick Formations' and 'Trading Candlestick Patterns' (pp.57-69)
findings.notes: The tweezer bottom/top is a double-test of support/resistance — related to V8 liquidity_sweep_reclaim but without the wick-through-close sweep. The candle-close rule matches V8's NEXT_BAR_CLOSE convention. Requires a 'response' feature (candle body/wick geometry) plus the trend filter; the 20-40 pip exclusion must be ATR-scaled for BTCUSDT.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Per-trade equity risk cap (equity management formula)
findings.mechanism: quantifying worst-case loss per trade before entry and capping it as a fraction of equity preserves staying power, so a sub-50% win rate can still be profitable
findings.setup_summary: Never risk more than 5% of trading equity on any single trade (0.5-2% for professional money managers); typical protective stops are 30-50 pips; require risk:reward at least 1:1 and habitually 1:1.5 ($500 risk -> $750 planned gain); the book demonstrates that a 30% win / 70% loss record with $300 losses and $2,000 wins still nets a profit.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rule violation (not a trade thesis): a trade that cannot meet the RR floor or per-trade risk cap must be declined regardless of setup quality ('if the trade does not meet the equity management requirements, you need to have the discipline to pass on the trade').
findings.risk_geometry: Sizing: risk per trade = stop distance x position size; stop distance 30-50 pips typical; risk cap <=5% of equity (0.5-2% pros); RR floor 1:1, habit 1:1.5; book's loss-endurance table: 1 loss survivable at 50% risk vs 19 losses at 5% risk.
findings.quote: The rule of survival at trading is to never risk more than 5 percent of your equity on any given trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 12 'The Equity Management Formula' and 'Risk versus Reward' (pp.192-197)
findings.notes: Direct input to V8 RiskGate: per-trade risk cap, RR minimum, and the loss-endurance table. Crypto's high leverage makes the cap more binding (a 1% adverse move is ~3x the book's 30-pip stop on typical FX majors). Note the book's formula is expressed on margin, which for perps should be equity-normalized.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Pre-submitted protective stop at entry (no mental stops)
findings.mechanism: mental stop-loss orders fail under drawdown because hope and fear override discipline; a pre-submitted protective stop placed at the same instant as the trade is the only reliable loss boundary
findings.setup_summary: Every entry must be accompanied by a protective stop placed at the moment of entry — a little beyond the last major support (longs) or last major resistance (shorts) — managed as an OCO pair with the profit limit so a fill on one cancels the other; never rely on mental stops and never move the stop after entry.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rule violation: trading without a pre-submitted stop is treated as exposure to financial self-destruction; moving a stop after entry is prohibited ('do not move it if you are trading an OCO order').
findings.risk_geometry: Stop: pre-submitted at entry, beyond last major support/resistance (book's narrative re-entry example: '10 pips below the low of the morning star'); every buy order carries a sell limit (profit) + sell stop (loss), and vice versa; OCO cancellation so no working order is left exposed.
findings.quote: protecting yourself as you trade is called placing a protective stop-loss order in the market at the same time as you execute the trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 12 'What Is Equity Management?' (pp.188-192); Ch 2 'Types of Orders' (p.27)
findings.notes: Maps to V8's lifecycle invariant: stops are frozen refs set at candidate creation, never moved — matching 'do not move it'. 24/7 crypto makes unmonitored mental stops especially fatal (no session close to save a runaway position; leverage can liquidate in hours).
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Trading-day vs trending-day regime filter
findings.mechanism: on days with scheduled macro announcements the market consolidates before the release, then trends 120-240 pips in the first hours; on quiet days it drifts only 60-90 pips, and a consolidation with no catalyst is thin late-session drift
findings.setup_summary: Classify sessions by scheduled macro releases: announcement days => pre-release consolidation then a 120-240-pip directional move in the first five hours (trending day); no-announcement days => 60-90 pip drift (trading day). Novices should avoid entering in the announcement window (30-100 pip slippage, 200-pip/20-second spikes); a consolidation with no announcement scheduled should be traded in the direction of the prior trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Regime filter, not a trade thesis: the classification flips on the economic calendar; unscheduled events (assassination attempts, surprise rate changes, 9/11-type shocks) can override the calendar.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a — regime/risk filter; the book recommends standing aside during the announcement window and warns of extreme slippage and whipsaws (Ch 10 figures 10-4, 10-5).
findings.quote: Trading days are when there are no fundamental announcements. Currency charts move typically 60 to 90 pips... Trending days are fundamental announcement days, when the market will generally take off in a direction after the announcement and move 120 to 240 pips within the first five hours.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10 'Trading Days versus Trending Days' (pp.167-170); Ch 11 'Strategy 3' (pp.183)
findings.notes: Do not default to HIGH: FX announcement behavior (interest-rate/employment releases) is not identical to crypto macro moves, but FOMC/CPI/NFP demonstrably move BTC. Implementable as a MarketState feature flag 'scheduled_macro_event' + consolidation state; also relevant to funding-rate settlement windows.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Higher-timeframe trend controls lower-timeframe entries
findings.mechanism: moves on lower timeframes are corrections of higher-timeframe moves, so a signal taken off a single timeframe often lands at the end of that timeframe's trend right when the higher timeframe reverses
findings.setup_summary: Before trading a lower timeframe, establish the higher-timeframe regime: a 200-pip retracement on the daily chart is a complete downtrend on the 60-minute chart, so a 60-min-only bias enters at the end of the move just as the daily hits its trend line and reverses. Use the larger timeframe's trend line/regime as the admission filter for lower-timeframe signals, and check that smaller-TF candles are on the correct side of the larger-TF trend line.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a — methodology rule governing signal admissibility, not a trade thesis.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a — methodology; the book's corollary is that trend systems lose money in sideways regimes (market consolidates 50-60% of the time), so a two-system split (trend + range) is needed.
findings.quote: the movement on smaller time frames will always respond to the trend lines on larger time frames.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'Finding and Drawing Inner, Outer, and Long-term Uptrend Lines' (pp.100-101); Ch 3 'Using Multiple Time Frames to Trade' (pp.44)
findings.notes: Direct architectural input: each V8 Expert's MarketState should include the higher-timeframe trend/regime as context (e.g., 4h trend line side as a filter for 1h signals) rather than each Expert re-deriving regime from a single TF. Also grounds the book's claim that trend-following systems need a separate range system.
findings.book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

findings.strategy_name: Cost drag arithmetic: net return equals gross return minus all-in costs, compounded
findings.mechanism: Every fee, spread, slippage and financing point taken from each trade compounds against gross edge over time, so a strategy only has net edge if gross per-trade expectancy exceeds the all-in cost hurdle, and the hurdle grows with turnover (costs ~= 1% per 100% annual turnover).
findings.setup_summary: For any strategy, compute net per-trade expectancy = gross expectancy - all-in cost rate (taker/maker fees + spread + slippage + funding + financing). A strategy is net-negative regardless of win rate if gross expectancy per trade does not clear the all-in cost per trade; the 2.5pp/yr cost gap consumed ~70% of the potential market accumulation over 50 years (Exhibits 4.1-4.2). Falsifiable: simulated net return must equal gross minus modeled all-in costs on every trade.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If gross per-trade expectancy does not exceed all-in cost per trade, the strategy is net-negative regardless of win rate; if turnover rises without edge rising proportionally, net edge decays. 'We get precisely what we don't pay for.'
findings.risk_geometry: Cost layer, not entry/stop: book's equity baseline ~0.5% per side round-trip (turnover cost rule), plus expense ratio, sales charges, taxes; in perp terms funding (8h), taker/maker fee, spread, slippage per holding period; no stated stop/target.
findings.quote: Gross market return, minus costs, equals net return for investors as a group.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4 (The Relentless Rules of Humble Arithmetic), Chapter 17 (reprise, QED 3)
findings.notes: Direct input to V8 simulator cost model. Perps add a 24/7 funding stream absent from equities and leverage multiplies notional cost; the 'tyranny of compounding costs' argument is the strongest, most falsifiable claim in the book.
findings.book: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing - The Only Way to Guarantee Your Fair Share of Stock Market Returns 2007

findings.strategy_name: Hyperactivity drag: returns decrease as motion increases
findings.mechanism: Overtrading burns edge: the most active traders pay costs on every round trip and their net returns lag the market by the cost of their motion; the empirical reference is the most-active 1/5 of traders turning portfolios >21%/month and netting 11.4% vs the 17.9% market return in 1990-96.
findings.setup_summary: Bin any strategy's trades by frequency; if net expectancy per unit of turnover is not positive, reducing trade frequency raises net return. Buffett's maxim: 'For investors as a whole, returns decrease as motion increases.' The book's prescription for clients: 'Don't do something. Just stand there.' Falsifiable on perp data by bucketing accounts/holders by turnover and measuring net PnL after all costs.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If per-trade net expectancy is positive, frequency per se is not the problem; the penalty exists only where turnover costs exceed the edge added by the extra trades.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop; a portfolio-level trade-frequency/turnover cap, plus full cost charging in the simulator for every extra trade; aligns with V8's buy-and-hold-style low-turnover baseline.
findings.quote: For investors as a whole, returns decrease as motion increases.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 1 (A Parable, Buffett's fourth law), Introduction (active-trader study, 1990-96)
findings.notes: 24/7 low-friction markets and instant leverage maximize the temptation to overtrade; a per-instrument frequency cap in the risk/lifecycle layer directly encodes this finding.
findings.book: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing - The Only Way to Guarantee Your Fair Share of Stock Market Returns 2007

findings.strategy_name: Reversion to the mean of speculative return (valuation expansion compresses future returns)
findings.mechanism: Total return = investment return (dividend yield + earnings growth) + speculative return (change in valuation multiple); speculative return is mean-reverting, so after large multiple expansion future returns are below the fundamental rate until valuation compresses back to the norm.
findings.setup_summary: On a long dataset, when the valuation multiple (P/E; crypto analog: price vs realized-price/cost-basis anchor, funding premium) has expanded well above its long-run norm over the trailing N periods, forecast below-normal forward returns; when compressed, forecast above-normal. Every decade of significantly negative speculative return was immediately followed by a positive decade of correlative size (1910s-1920s, 1940s-1950s, 1970s-1980s).
findings.trigger_invalidation: The pattern broke in the 1990s with a second consecutive expansion decade - reversion has no fixed clock; the book itself (Ch.7) uses it as a forward-return forecast tool, not a trade entry.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop; a regime overlay that reduces long exposure after large speculative expansion and restores it after contraction; horizon is decadal, far longer than V8's 1h-bar scale.
findings.quote: Reversion to the mean (RTM) writ large.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2 (Rational Exuberance, Exhibits 2.1-2.4), Chapter 7 (When the Good Times No Longer Roll)
findings.notes: Crypto has no dividend/earnings anchor, so the analog is price-vs-realized-price (MVRV-type), funding premium, and cost-basis metrics; usable only as a regime filter at V8's horizon, not as a trade trigger.
findings.book: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing - The Only Way to Guarantee Your Fair Share of Stock Market Returns 2007

findings.strategy_name: Performance-chasing penalty: dollar-weighted investor returns lag asset returns
findings.mechanism: Crowd flow follows recent performance: money flows into funds after good performance and out after bad, so the average participant buys high and sells low; dollar-weighted investor returns lag time-weighted fund returns by ~2.7pp/yr industry-wide and ~8.3pp/yr for the hottest aggressive funds.
findings.setup_summary: After large recent gains, inflows spike and subsequent dollar-weighted returns fall short of reported returns; hot sector ETF shareholders lagged their funds by ~5pp/yr (only 1 of 20 top ETFs 2003-06 gave shareholders the reported return). A falsifiable fade: measure flow proxy (funding premium, OI growth, net taker buy-flow) after a large N-bar rally; strongly positive flow while price is extended predicts below-average forward returns.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Setup does not apply when flow is neutral or negative after the rally (crowd already rotated); if the move is genuinely fundamental, the chase continues and the fade loses.
findings.risk_geometry: Contrarian fade: entry on flow-extreme signal after extension, stop beyond the move's structure, target = reversion to mean flow level; the penalty scales with how hot the chased asset is (index fund investors lagged 2.0pp vs 8.3pp for aggressive funds).
findings.quote: Hint: money flows into most funds after good performance, and goes out when bad performance follows.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5 (The Grand Illusion, Exhibits 5.2-5.3), Chapter 15 (ETFs: shareholder shortfall ~5pp/yr)
findings.notes: Funding rate, OI delta and taker flow are directly observable perp analogs of fund flows; this is the book's most directly tradeable phenomenon, though it is documented as a penalty, not a prescribed fade - keep as backlog candidate until flow tape exists.
findings.book: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing - The Only Way to Guarantee Your Fair Share of Stock Market Returns 2007

findings.strategy_name: Past performance does not persist: star funds revert and long streaks are luck on skill
findings.mechanism: Performance RTM: fund returns are near-random across ranks; top-20 and #1 funds revert toward and below the peer mean the following year, and survivorship bias inflates apparent long-run records (223 of 355 funds from 1970 died; only 3 of 355 beat the S&P 500 by >1%/yr over 36 years).
findings.setup_summary: Top-20 funds each year reverted to average rank the next year (avg follow-up rank 284/681 in 1982-92; 619/1,440 in 1995-2005), and the #1 funds reverted worst (avg 949/1,440, beating only 34% of peers). For V8: any backtested expert showing star performance must be stress-tested for RTM risk and survivorship bias before registry advancement; long streaks are 'extraordinary luck imposed on great skill'.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Small samples cannot separate luck from skill - Aronson: 20-800 years of monitoring needed for 95% statistical confidence; Miller's 15-year streak shows rare skill can persist, so the rule is probabilistic, not deterministic.
findings.risk_geometry: No trade geometry; a research-process rule: frozen OOS, registry gating, never promote on in-sample/backtest performance alone.
findings.quote: In fund performance, the past is rarely prologue.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8 (Selecting Long-Term Winners), Chapter 9 (Yesterday's Winners, Tomorrow's Losers)
findings.notes: Applies directly to V8's own expert funnel (BACKLOG->FORMALIZED->SCREENING->...) and to crypto factor persistence, which decays faster than equity factor persistence.
findings.book: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing - The Only Way to Guarantee Your Fair Share of Stock Market Returns 2007

findings.strategy_name: Data-mined paradigms decay: backtested strategies are promoted only after they worked and edges get arbitraged away
findings.mechanism: Paradigm decay: any factor or weighting scheme promoted as a new paradigm (fundamental indexing, value/small tilts, January effect, Nifty Fifty, new-economy funds) was marketed only after its best days; past backtested margins (~1-2%/yr) are eroded by costs and by investors bidding away the claimed systematic mispricing.
findings.setup_summary: A backtested strategy is introduced only after it has already outperformed; the promoters never explain why the factor is structurally underpriced. Test the persistence claim: if the strategy was right in the past because of a transitory mispricing, investor demand prices it away ('if these paradigms actually have been right in the past, won't they therefore be wrong in the future?'). For V8: a PROPOSED expert whose edge rests on backtest alone is suspect until it clears frozen OOS, because selection-on-past-winners is the promotion mechanism itself.
findings.trigger_invalidation: An edge with a stated structural cause for persistence (a real, unrepaired market friction) can persist; without such a mechanism the backtest is data mining.
findings.risk_geometry: No trade geometry; a governance rule: no promotion on in-sample/backtest results; registry experiments must beat the simple baseline on frozen OOS (aligns with V8 constitution rules 6/14/15).
findings.quote: No one would have the temerity to promote a new strategy that has lagged in the past. ... if these promoters of the purported new paradigms actually have been right in the past, won't they therefore be wrong in the future?
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 14 (Index Funds That Promise to Beat the Market)
findings.notes: Crypto factor decay is fast; this is the book's argument for why V8's evidence-bound falsification program exists. 'There have been many new paradigms over the years. None has persisted.'
findings.book: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing - The Only Way to Guarantee Your Fair Share of Stock Market Returns 2007

findings.strategy_name: Serious Money vs Funny Money: cap speculative allocation
findings.mechanism: Speculative capital cap: at most ~5% of assets may go to speculation (funny money) while >=50-95% stays in a low-cost, low-turnover, diversified core, so that active or leveraged bets cannot destroy the portfolio regardless of outcome; the speculative sleeve is measured against the core at 1/5/10 years.
findings.setup_summary: Allocate at most ~5% of capital to speculative/active/leveraged strategies and the rest to a passive diversified core; re-measure the two sleeves on fixed dates and compare. Falsifiable: over long windows the core is expected to win; if the speculative sleeve cannot beat the core net of costs, the cap is the binding constraint.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If the speculative sleeve demonstrates verifiable positive net edge after costs and taxes, more than 5% may be justified; the cap is the default for unverified edge.
