findings.risk_geometry: Cap on total speculative capital, not per-trade R; per-trade risk still sized within the capped sleeve; maps to V8 heat cap in RiskGate.
findings.quote: Not with one penny more than 5 percent of your investment assets. That can be your Funny Money account.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 18 (What Should I Do Now?)
findings.notes: Perp leverage is the archetypal funny-money vehicle; the 5% cap is a practitioner heuristic that supports a strict heat/leverage cap in V8's RiskGate admission.
findings.book: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing - The Only Way to Guarantee Your Fair Share of Stock Market Returns 2007

findings.strategy_name: Broadest possible diversification: eliminate stock/style/manager risk, only market risk remains
findings.mechanism: Diversification is the consummate risk-reduction strategy: holding the market in cap weights eliminates idiosyncratic, style and manager risk, leaving only undiversifiable market risk; concentrated or correlated bets retain exactly the risks that a diversified holder pays nothing to shed.
findings.setup_summary: Any concentrated or correlated exposure set (a single perp, or several perps in one direction) retains idiosyncratic and correlation risk; risk gating should cap correlated exposure across instruments so no single name or style factor can dominate the book. The book's QED: individual businesses come and go via creative destruction, but the aggregate grows - only broad economic risk is undiversifiable.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If a concentrated bet has verifiable, stable, cost-adjusted edge, concentration could be justified - exactly the claim the book says has been falsified for >99% of funds over 35+ years.
findings.risk_geometry: Portfolio-level exposure limits, correlation-aware; aligns with V8 rule 16 (one active exposure per instrument-direction) and the correlated_exposure_cap risk rule.
findings.quote: Owning businesses in the aggregate through an all-market index fund is the consummate risk-reduction strategy. (Broad economic risks to corporate earnings and dividends, however, cannot be diversified away.)
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 17 (Relentless Rules, QED 2), Chapter 3 (Cast Your Lot with Business)
findings.notes: Crypto is dominated by one factor (BTC beta), so naive diversification across alts is not diversification; the cap must be computed on realized correlation, not asset count.
findings.book: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing - The Only Way to Guarantee Your Fair Share of Stock Market Returns 2007

findings.strategy_name: Mr. Market discipline: quotations are for convenience - react to thesis, not price noise
findings.mechanism: Short-term prices are a voting machine (emotions), long-term a weighing machine (fundamentals); the investor who reacts to every quote converts a winner's game into a loser's game by trading on emotion instead of on thesis validity - 'market quotations are there for his convenience, either to be taken advantage of or to be ignored.'
findings.setup_summary: Separate the expectations market (short-term price/emotion) from the real market (fundamental value); exit a position only when the underlying thesis is invalidated, not when the quote moves against it. In V8 terms this is exactly the separation between stop-loss (risk) and dead-thesis still_valid (thesis) exits, and the rule that the still_valid condition is computed from structure, not from noise.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If a quote move reflects genuine thesis invalidation (fundamental change), ignoring it is wrong; the discipline is about not being driven by transitory emotion.
findings.risk_geometry: Exit logic: risk stop and thesis still_valid are different exits; no noise-based triggers; the book adds that speculation's contribution washes out long-term, so noise exits are pure cost.
findings.quote: In the short run the stock market is a voting machine . . . (but) in the long run it is a weighing machine.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2 (Rational Exuberance, Graham quote), Chapter 16 (What Would Benjamin Graham Have Thought about Indexing?)
findings.notes: 24/7 trading and leverage amplify the cost of noise-driven exits; this book independently motivates V8's existing still_valid vs stop separation as a lifecycle invariant.
findings.book: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing - The Only Way to Guarantee Your Fair Share of Stock Market Returns 2007

findings.strategy_name: The passive index is the null hypothesis every active strategy must beat net of all costs
findings.mechanism: Zero-sum-after-costs arithmetic: the aggregate active investor must earn the market gross return minus all costs; a low-cost passive portfolio is the guaranteed baseline, so the probability an active manager beats the index decays with horizon (Monte Carlo: ~29% at 1yr, ~15% at 5yr, ~9% at 10yr, ~5% at 25yr, ~2% at 50yr given 0.25% vs 2% cost).
findings.setup_summary: The index fund is 'guaranteed to win ... every year, and every month and week, even every minute of the day' because gross market return minus intermediation cost equals net investor return. For V8: every expert's results must be measured against a passive benchmark of the traded instrument, net of funding + fees + slippage, not just against 'edge > 0'; the low-turnover baseline is the null hypothesis.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If the passive baseline itself is structurally weak in an instrument (e.g., holding a perp long pays funding), the bar is lower - but the baseline must still be computed and reported honestly.
findings.risk_geometry: Benchmark construction: low-turnover, all-in-cost-inclusive, stated in the experiment protocol; measure every candidate stream against it.
findings.quote: The index fund is guaranteed to win not only over time, but every year, and every month and week, even every minute of the day.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3 (Cast Your Lot with Business), Chapter 12 (Profit from the Majesty of Simplicity, Exhibit 12.1)
findings.notes: In perps there is no free passive index - a long perp pays funding and decays, so the benchmark must be constructed (e.g., spot-hold net of funding) and stated; this is the cost floor every V8 expert must clear.
findings.book: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing - The Only Way to Guarantee Your Fair Share of Stock Market Returns 2007

book_title: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing (2007)

findings.strategy_name: Round Number Fade (Fading the Double Zeros)
findings.mechanism: Take-profit orders cluster at psychologically round numbers while stops sit just beyond them, so price is magnetized to the level and stop-gunning by banks produces a contra-trend bounce.
findings.setup_summary: On a 10-15 minute chart (adapt to 1h), price trades well below (long side) its 20-period SMA and approaches a psychological round number (book examples 105.00 USD/JPY, 1.2800 EUR/USD; in BTC, 100000/50000-style levels); enter a few pips (<=10) before the figure, stop <=20 pips, first-half target 2R, then trail. Filter: level gains weight when it coincides with a Fibonacci retracement, moving average, or Bollinger band, and when no major scheduled economic release is imminent.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches the entry zone while 20-SMA displacement is intact. Invalidation: stop hit (decisive move through the round number by >20 pips with momentum, implying real orders rather than cluster-fades); thesis dead if the figure breaks cleanly.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit a few pips (<=10) before the figure; initial stop 20 pips; take half at 2x risk, move stop to breakeven, trail remainder (book uses two-bar low / five-bar low); intraday expiry.
findings.quote: While stop-loss orders are usually placed just beyond the round numbers, traders will cluster their lake-profit orders at the round number.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, 'Fading the Double Zeros', p. 81-85
findings.notes: Round-number psychology survives in crypto (100k BTC, prior structural round levels) but the 'bank dealer guns clustered stops' mechanism is weaker in an all-visible central-limit order book; the magnet/reversal frequency around round levels is falsifiable on BTCUSDT. Needs sub-1h bars or a 1h adaptation (20-SMA displacement + round-level proximity).
findings.book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

findings.strategy_name: Waiting for the Real Deal (session-open stop-hunt fake-out)
findings.mechanism: At the London open the initial range-break is a deliberate stop-hunt to clear books; once those stops are run, the real directional move follows.
findings.setup_summary: Define the Frankfurt-London 'power hour' range (1-2 a.m. EST). Long setup: GBP/USD makes a new range low at least 25 pips below the range high, then reverses and penetrates the range high; enter buy 10 pips above the range high with a stop <=20 pips; first-half target 2R, then trail by two-bar low. Short is the mirror. Works best following the U.S. open or after a major economic release once the noise has settled.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: range low/high made by >=25 pips then reclaimed. Invalidation: stop hit; no reversal penetration within the session.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: 10 pips beyond range high/low; stop <=20 pips; first lot at 2R, move to breakeven, trail remainder (two-bar high/low).
findings.quote: Once these stops are taken out and the books are cleared, the real directional move in the GBP/USD will begin to occur.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, 'Waiting for the Real Deal', p. 85-88
findings.notes: Crypto has no discrete London open; the pattern must be re-expressed as 'first range-break is a fake-out, reversal then real move' around high-volume transition windows (Asia->Europe, UTC 6-12). Session ranges map to ATR-scaled ranges; needs a time-of-day feature group.
findings.book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

findings.strategy_name: Inside Day Breakout (volatility compression expansion)
findings.mechanism: Two or more inside days compress the daily range; expansion releases the compression, and the breakout direction can be biased by the contraction's location within a triangle or by momentum.
findings.setup_summary: On the daily chart, identify at least two consecutive inside days (each day's high/low contained within the prior day's range). Place a buy stop 10 pips above the prior inside day's high and a sell stop 10 pips below its low; stop-and-reverse 10 pips beyond the inside-day extreme. Target 2R or trail. Bias direction with formation geometry (ascending-triangle contraction near range top favors upside) and MACD histogram sign.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: break of prior inside-day high/low by 10 pips. Invalidation: stop-and-reverse triggered (first move was a false breakout) - thesis flips to the opposite direction.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: 10 pips beyond inside-day high/low (daily bars); stop-and-reverse 10 pips past the inside-day low/high; target 2R or trailing stop; daily-bar expiry.
findings.quote: There need to be at least two inside days before the volatility play can be implemented. The more inside days, the higher the likelihood of an upside surge.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, 'Inside Day Breakout Play', p. 88-92
findings.notes: Cleanly portable to perps: no overnight/exchange gaps, so inside-day containment is well-defined; compression-to-expansion is frequent in BTC. The both-sided stop-and-reverse structure maps naturally to a V8 candidate hypothesis in the breakout family.
findings.book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

findings.strategy_name: The Fader (fade false breakouts in range)
findings.mechanism: In a range-bound environment with weak ADX, breakouts beyond the prior day's range are traps; fading the failed breakout captures the reversion (liquidity vacuum then refill).
findings.setup_summary: Range-bound regime (ADX(14) < 35, ideally declining; daily chart defines the range, hourly charts for entries). Long: wait for a break below the previous day's low by >=15 pips (false breakout), then buy 15 pips above the previous day's high; stop <=30 pips; target 60 pips (2R). Short is the mirror. Stand aside around major scheduled economic releases and on volatile pairs.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: prior-day level violated by >=15 pips then reclaimed; entry on reclaim 15 pips beyond the other side. Invalidation: 30-pip stop; 2R target; skip if ADX >35 or a scheduled release looms.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: 15 pips beyond prior-day high/low; stop 30 pips; target 2R (60 pips); fixed 2R, no trailing prescribed.
findings.quote: Wait for the market to break below the previous day's low by at least 15 pips. Place an entry order to buy 15 pips above the previous day's high.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, 'The Fader', p. 92-94
findings.notes: Directly refines V8's failed_breakout expert: adds the ADX<35 range filter, the 15-pip false-break threshold, the 30-pip stop and 2R target, and the no-news-day filter. The existing V8 variant covers the SHORT-after-failed-high case; the book adds the symmetric long side and the same-side re-entry rule.
findings.book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

findings.strategy_name: Filtering False Breakouts (20-day high shakeout re-break)
findings.mechanism: A 20-day high followed by a fast flush to a 2-day low shakes out weak longs; re-break of the 20-day high confirms real-money re-entry and strong trend continuation.
findings.setup_summary: Daily bars: pair makes a new 20-day high (or 20-day low for the short side); within the next 3 days it reverses to a 2-day low (or 2-day high); buy if it takes out the 20-day high within 3 days of the 2-day low. Stop a few pips below the 2-day low; target 2R or trail (two-bar low).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 20-day extreme made, then a 2-day counter-extreme within 3 days, then re-break within 3 days. Invalidation: stop below the 2-day counter-extreme; no re-break within the 3-day window.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: re-break of the 20-day extreme; stop a few pips beyond the 2-day counter-extreme; target 2R or trailing stop.
findings.quote: Look for a currency pair that is making a 20-day high. Look for the pair to reverse over the next three days to make a two-day low. Buy the pair if it takes out the 20-day high within three days of making the two-day low.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, 'Filtering False Breakouts', p. 94-96
findings.notes: Distinct from failed_breakout (which trades the reversal) and from a plain pullback-to-support: this is a continuation entry after a shallow flush in a strong trend. Well-defined, fully falsifiable time windows (3-day / 2-day / 20-day) make it a strong backlog candidate.
findings.book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

findings.strategy_name: Perfect Order (stacked MA trend regime)
findings.mechanism: Sequential stacking of 10/20/50/100/200-day SMAs aligns momentum with the trend direction and marks a persistent trending regime (momentum alignment = trend persistence).
findings.setup_summary: Uptrend: 10>20>50>100>200-day SMA stacked in descending order (mirror for short). Treat perfect order as a trend-state condition: enter when the stack first forms (book's examples enter ~5 bars later), stay long while it holds, exit when the order breaks (20-day SMA crosses below the 10-day SMA); require ADX >20 and rising for confirmation.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: full MA stack in order with ADX rising. Invalidation: stack order broken (e.g., 20-day SMA below 10-day SMA).
findings.risk_geometry: No fixed stop/target in the book; position held while the perfect order persists, exit on order break. Book examples: +410 pips risking 97 pips (long), +443 pips risking 149 pips (short).
findings.quote: A perfect order is when the moving averages line up perfectly; that is for an uptrend, the 10-day SMA is greater than the 20-day SMA, which is greater than the 50-day SMA.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, 'Perfect Order', p. 97-98 (mechanism defined in Ch. 7 trend profiling, p. 70)
findings.notes: Best used as a trend-state feature / regime gate for the trend_pullback family (only take pullbacks while the stack is in perfect order) rather than a standalone entry. ADX >20 rising confirmation per the book.
findings.book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

findings.strategy_name: Option Volatility Term-Structure Timing (short vs long vol)
findings.mechanism: When short-term (1M) volatility is well below long-term (3M) volatility, compression precedes a breakout; when short-term volatility is well above long-term volatility, expect reversion to a trading range.
findings.setup_summary: Compute the spread between short-term (one-month) and long-term (three-month) volatility. If short << long, expect an imminent breakout (direction undefined) - favor breakout-family setups and tighten range-trade exits; if short >> long, expect reversion to range - favor mean-reversion entries. Book uses 1M vs 3M option volatilities; a realized-vol term structure is the tape-computable proxy.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: ST/LT vol divergence beyond normal. Invalidation: vol gap returns to neutral, or a suspected breakout fires against an open range position - book rule: if the break is likely against you, close the range trade.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry geometry; it is a regime gate that also tells range traders when to exit (close range positions when short-term vol falls well below long-term vol).
findings.quote: if short-term option volatilities are significantly lower than long-term volatilities, one should expect a breakout, though the direction of the breakout is not defined by this rule.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, 'Using Option Volatilities to Time Market Movements', p. 114-117 (also Ch. 7, p. 68-70)
findings.notes: Directly implementable with realized-volatility term structure on the current tape; implied vol (Deribit) would be an options-data feature. This is a falsifiable regime gate that selects between breakout and mean-reversion behavior families.
findings.book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

findings.strategy_name: Risk Reversal Extremes as Contrarian Sentiment
findings.mechanism: 25-delta risk reversals embed market positioning; at extreme values (one standard deviation from the average) they signal overcrowding and give contrarian reversal signals.
findings.setup_summary: Track the 25-delta call/put risk reversal (IV skew) for the instrument; readings at or beyond 1 std dev from the rolling average mark overbought/oversold positioning and favor fading the direction of the skew; near-zero readings indicate no bias (range conditions).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: RR extreme reached. Invalidation: RR continues to extend, implying positioning is still building rather than reversing (trend confirmation).
findings.risk_geometry: No price geometry in the book; contrarian directional filter only.
findings.quote: We identify extreme levels as one standard deviation plus or minus the average risk reversal. When risk reversals are at these levels, they give off contrarian signals.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, 'Fundamental Trading Strategy: Risk Reversals', p. 112-114 (also Ch. 7, p. 68-69)
findings.notes: Crypto analog is Deribit 25-delta options skew for BTC; V8's current tape has no options data, so this is data-blocked until an options/skew feed lands. Would be a participation-group positioning feature.
findings.book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

findings.strategy_name: Leveraged Carry Trade / Funding Carry
findings.mechanism: Buying the high-yield currency and shorting the low-yield one harvests the interest differential plus appreciation; the trade profits only while risk appetite is high and unwinds violently when risk aversion spikes (carry unwind to safe havens).
findings.setup_summary: Long the high-rate currency and short the low-rate currency (e.g., long AUD / short CHF, 4.50% yield pickup at zero leverage; 5x leverage makes it 22.5%). Profitability is conditional on the risk-appetite regime: profitable when investors have low risk aversion, unprofitable when risk aversion is high. Commit to a >=6-month horizon and avoid excessive leverage. Crypto analog: harvest funding on BTCUSDT perps (or long-basis carry); treat funding flips and risk-off spikes as the unwind trigger.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: persistent rate differential + risk-on regime. Invalidation: risk-aversion spike (credit event, crisis) - capital flows to safe-haven currencies and the carry turns sharply negative (book: yen +20% in two months in summer 1998; CHF +7% in 10 days after 9/11).
findings.risk_geometry: Long-horizon (>=6 months) position; no tight stops (stops kill the carry); keep leverage low so fluctuations are survivable.
findings.quote: Carry trades will generally be profitable when investors have low risk aversion, and unprofitable when investors have high risk aversion.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, 'Leveraged Carry Trade', p. 100-104
findings.notes: Funding-rate carry and long-basis are directly implementable on Binance perps once funding data joins the tape; the risk-aversion dependence maps to crypto's funding/basis regime and flash-deleverage episodes (carry_unwind mechanism).
findings.book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

findings.strategy_name: Economic Release Timing and Event-Window Discipline
findings.mechanism: Scheduled macro releases produce a concentrated, fast price adjustment (most of it within the first 20 minutes); reactions beyond 15-30 minutes are overreaction/flow, and trading systematic strategies through high-impact releases is negative-expectancy.
findings.setup_summary: Rank scheduled releases by historical post-release range (book's 2004 EUR/USD table: NFP 124 pips in first 20 min / 193 pips daily vs GDP 43/110; FOMC 74/140). No new systematic exposure during the release window; disable system strategies ahead of the highest-mover releases (NFP). Breakout traders can weight position size by expected release range (50% size for a GDP-day breakout vs NFP-day).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: scheduled-release calendar event. Invalidation: window closes (15-30 min post-release) and the move has been made.
findings.risk_geometry: No price geometry; lifecycle rule: flat ahead of high-impact events, re-enable after the adjustment window.
findings.quote: many system traders turn their systems off ahead of big releases such as the U.S. nonfarm payrolls reports.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 4, 'What Moves the Currency Market in the Short Term?', p. 46-49
findings.notes: The book's 2004 study of post-release pip ranges is a falsifiable empirical case (LITERATURE_SUPPORTED). In 24/7 crypto perps there is no closing bell to protect you, so a scheduled-event lifecycle rule (flat through FOMC/CPI/NFP windows) is directly applicable and reinforces the event/available/ingested clock discipline.
findings.book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

findings.strategy_name: Core Risk Management Discipline (RR, stops, break-even, scaling)
findings.mechanism: Fixed risk controls (min 1:2 reward:risk, 2% per-trade risk cap, break-even at 1R, never add to losers, max-loss rules) convert a raw edge into positive expectancy by keeping losses small and letting winners run.
findings.setup_summary: Rules: (1) minimum 1:2 risk:reward before entry; (2) risk <=2% of equity per trade; (3) move stop to breakeven once profit equals initial risk (1R); (4) never add to losing positions; (5) treat any add-on to a winner as an independent new trade with its own risk (per-lot stops); (6) maximum loss / drawdown cap; (7) stop placement methods: two-day low minus 10 pips, or 20 pips below support, or parabolic SAR trailing; (8) keep a trading journal as enforcement.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any new position. Invalidation: 1R stop, 2R target, or break-even relocation; the journal is the enforcement mechanism.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop: two-day low minus 10 pips (or 20 pips below support); target at least 2R; breakeven at 1R; trailing via parabolic SAR or two-bar extreme; risk fraction 2%.
findings.quote: the rule of moving your stop to break even as soon as your position has profited by the same amount that you initially risked
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 7, 'Risk Management', p. 71-75
findings.notes: Mostly already present in V8 RiskGate (risk_percent_sizing, break_even_stop, volatility-based stops, max_drawdown_cap). Confirms existing rules; the explicit 'never add to losers' and 'add-ons are independent trades' rules are candidate RiskGate refinements.
findings.book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

findings.strategy_name: Currency Correlations Change Over Time (exposure management)
findings.mechanism: Pairs/assets move together in time-varying correlations; 'diversified' portfolios of correlated instruments are actually concentrated, and correlation magnitudes/directions drift with economic regimes.
findings.setup_summary: Compute rolling correlations over 1-month, 3-month, 6-month and 1-year windows (book examples: USD/CAD vs USD/JPY 0.06 at 1-month vs 0.80 at 1-year; GBP/USD vs AUD/USD -0.87 at 1-year flipping to +0.24 in early 2005). Treat two strongly correlated instruments as one position for exposure/heat purposes and recalculate at least monthly; do not take offsetting positions on correlated pairs as a hedge.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: correlation regime shift (typically interest-rate changes). Invalidation: correlation reverts to near zero - the exposure cap can loosen.
findings.risk_geometry: No price geometry; portfolio-level exposure cap across correlated instruments.
findings.quote: the most important aspect to remember when analyzing currency correlations is that they can easily change over time.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, 'What Are Currency Correlations and How Do Traders Use Them?', p. 56-60
findings.notes: For BTCUSDT-focused V8 this is a cross-market exposure rule (BTC-ETH, BTC-risk-asset correlations), reinforcing correlated_exposure_cap with rolling-window correlation rather than static coefficients; most relevant when the instrument universe expands beyond a single perp.
findings.book: Day Trading the Currency Market - Technical and Fundamental Strategies To Profit from Market Swings 2005

book_title: Sentiment in the Forex Market — Indicators and Strategies to Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes (Jamie Saettele, 2008)

findings.strategy_name: Composite COT positioning extreme contrarian
findings.mechanism: Errors of optimism/pessimism: speculators' net positioning peaks at tops and troughs at bottoms; commercials (hedgers) are the exact mirror, so their divergence quantifies where the crowd sits in the optimism-pessimism oscillation
findings.setup_summary: Compute Composite COT = net speculative positioning - net commercial positioning on weekly data, then percentile-rank it over 52 weeks into a COT Index. A reading of 100 (specs extremely long / commercials extremely short) marks a bullish sentiment extreme; 0 marks a bearish extreme. Do not act on the index alone: filter with the speculative %-long ratio (long contracts / (long+short)), acting only when it is also extreme (above ~90% or below ~20%), i.e., when COT Index, Spec Ratio Index, and Comm Ratio Index all line up at 0 or 100.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: COT Index hits 0/100 AND spec %-long ratio is extreme (>90% or <10%). Thesis invalidated if price fails to turn within several weeks — extremes persist (May 2005 DXY: COT Index 100 held until July; book quotes Keynes 'the market can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent'). Blind entry on the extreme alone produced poor results in Oct 2004 and May 2005.
findings.risk_geometry: No explicit entry/stop/target; book says to keep risk tight and examine the chart for a reversal trade once the three indicators line up. Positioning data lags ~3-6 days (weekly report) so entries are delayed.
findings.quote: Commercial positioning is on the wrong side of the market for the meat of the move but is correct at the turn.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 5, The Approach (Composite COT, COT Index, ratios), pp. 83-91
findings.notes: Crypto analog is real-time funding rate + exchange open interest / long-short positioning, which has no weekly lag. Requires derivatives/positioning data beyond the base BTCUSDT tape; the 52-week percentile index must be computed point-in-time with a frozen window to avoid lookahead.
findings.book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

findings.strategy_name: Retail speculative flow contrarian (FXCM SSI)
findings.mechanism: The retail crowd extrapolates the trend and is systematically wrong at turns; aggregate retail long/short positioning moves inversely to price, and the flip of the ratio (not the extreme) is the most accurate turn signal
findings.setup_summary: Track the aggregate retail long/short ratio (% of open orders long). More than 50% long favors weakness, less than 50% long favors strength; SSI moves inversely to price. The flipping of the ratio is a more accurate turn signal than extreme positioning. A big fall in net positioning while price rises is bearish because short-covering is fueling the rally and price will decline when covering ends.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger on a flip in retail positioning near a multiweek extreme or on rising price with falling net positioning. Invalidated if retail positioning continues to extrapolate and price keeps trending (crowd can remain wrong for extended periods).
findings.risk_geometry: None stated in book; indicator is a filter/overlay, not an entry.
findings.quote: The SSI works as a contrarian indicator during trending markets. The flipping of the ratio is a more accurate signal of a turn in prices than extreme positioning.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 5, Other Sentiment Indicators — FXCM Speculative Sentiment Index, pp. 94-97
findings.notes: Crypto analog: exchange-published long/short ratios, taker buy/sell flow, and funding rate. The 'rising price + falling net positioning = short-covering rally' claim is directly testable on perp OI/funding data. Evidence is interpretive guidance on a proprietary indicator (no public statistics).
findings.book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

findings.strategy_name: Extreme-language news headline and magazine-cover contrarian
findings.mechanism: Media only grants extreme coverage (headlines with surge/plummet/plunge/crash, cover stories, directional predictions) when the crowd is at a sentiment extreme; the media extrapolates the trend and is therefore wrong at the turn
findings.setup_summary: When headlines about an asset use extreme language or take a directional stand (e.g., 'Dollar Surges...', 'Euroshambles', 'The Disappearing Dollar'), expect a short-term reversal over days-to-weeks (short-term) or weeks-to-months (magazine covers). Mundane headlines ('Euro rallies against Dollar') signal trend continuation. Google Trends news-reference volume spikes coincide with major turns ('weak dollar' search peaked at DXY bottoms in Dec 2004 and Nov 2006).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger on an extreme-language headline or directional media prediction for the traded asset. Invalidated if the trend continues — many headline examples preceded further trend (e.g., 'At Last, the Euro Looks Ready to Climb' preceded a further 14-month euro decline), so the signal is a warning, not a guarantee.
findings.risk_geometry: Book calls it 'a risky trade outright' — no clean stop placement at multiweek/month/year extremes; use wave principle structure or pivot points for timing; can also be used as an exit overlay on existing positions.
findings.quote: headlines that contain strong language and/or that take a directional stand are fantastic contrarian signals
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 4, Using News Headlines to Generate Signals, pp. 53-68; Ch. 3, The Power of Magazine Covers, pp. 31-51
findings.notes: Book cites a peer-reviewed study (Arnold, Earl & North, FAJ 2007) of 2,080 Business Week/Fortune/Forbes cover stories (1982-2002): cover stories follow extreme performance and signal its end. Crypto analog: mainstream Bitcoin 'crash'/hype coverage and search-volume spikes. Needs an external news/search-volume corpus not present in the perp tape.
findings.book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

findings.strategy_name: Consecutive up/down closes exhaustion trail (sentiment-extreme exit)
findings.mechanism: x consecutive closes in one direction indicate near-complete agreement (too many on one side of the boat); the run is at a sentiment extreme and reversal/at-least consolidation follows
findings.setup_summary: After 8 consecutive closes in the same direction (weekly or daily), treat the trend as at a sentiment extreme: if long, place a stop just below the low of the last up-bar and trail it one bar at a time as the streak extends; exit when stopped. If the streak ends without the prior bar's extreme being taken out, continue holding. Exit is the primary use — this is an exit/timing rule, not an entry rule.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Activation after an 8-bar streak; trail continues while each new bar extends; invalidated/exit when a bar takes out the prior bar's extreme. The '8' threshold is a starting point to be recalibrated per timeframe.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: none (exit rule). Stop: prior bar low (long) / prior bar high (short), trailed each bar. No target — exit at the extreme. Book examples: DXY bottom after 11 consecutive down weeks (Dec 2004); EURUSD tops after 9 and 8 consecutive up weeks (Jan/Dec 2004); USDCAD turns after ~9-week streaks.
findings.quote: Use 8 as a starting point. For example, once a pair has rallied for 8 weeks (or days), place a stop just below the low of the last week.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, When to Get Out — Consecutive Up and Down Periods, pp. 146-149
findings.notes: On BTCUSDT 1h, 8 consecutive up-hours occurs frequently; the streak threshold and bar size must be recalibrated (book uses weekly/daily). Best used as a stop-trailing rule inside an existing trend-following expert rather than a standalone entry.
findings.book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

findings.strategy_name: Overbought/oversold as trend-continuation bias (anti-reversal RSI)
findings.mechanism: Strong trends remain overbought/oversold for extended periods; an oscillator cross into extreme territory marks the start or middle of a trend, not its end — the bias flips only on an opposite-side cross
findings.setup_summary: Maintain a bullish bias while weekly RSI has crossed above 60 (or 70) and has not yet crossed below 40 (or 30); bearish while crossed below 40 (or 30) without crossing above 60 (or 70). Repeated overshoots do not flip the bias. In the book's EURUSD weekly equity-curve tests (2001-2007), the trending interpretation of RSI 70/30, RSI 60/40, slow stochastics 80/20 and 70/30, and Bollinger 1/2-stdev all beat the corresponding reversal interpretations; the book's EURUSD weekly examples show RSI>70 marked the start of bull phases (Jun 2002, May 2006) and RSI<30 the start of bear phases.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Bias flips only when the oscillator crosses the opposite threshold (bullish bias ends only on a cross below 40/30). Trading reversal on overbought/oversold is explicitly refuted by the equity-curve comparisons.
findings.risk_geometry: Trend tests: stop-buy at the bar high when the bias flips long, stop-sell at the bar low when short. For entry refinement while bias is bullish: 'buy intra-week weakness by placing orders near the calculated weekly pivot supports'.
findings.quote: RSI moving above 70 was much closer to the beginning of a bull trend than to the end. Similarly, RSI moving below 30 was much closer to the beginning of a bear trend than to the end.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Fancy Momentum Indicators and Overbought/Oversold, pp. 125-141
findings.notes: Directly refutes the naive rsi_oversold_reversal usage. In V8 this is a regime filter that keeps trend-following experts (trend_pullback) engaged while oscillators are extreme, and a candidate refinement: overbought is confirmation of trend, not a fade signal.
findings.book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

findings.strategy_name: Divergence and momentum-extreme caveats (methodology warning)
findings.mechanism: Momentum (rate of change) peaks at the beginning or middle of a trend, not its end; divergence is present at every turn but does not always lead to a turn; arithmetic momentum distorts at tops/bottoms versus geometric rate of change
findings.setup_summary: Use rate-of-change (geometric, log-scale) rather than arithmetic momentum for divergence: at the Dec 2004 EURUSD top, ROC identified bearish divergence while arithmetic momentum did not. Trade in the direction of a momentum extreme (ROC greatest over lookback), which marks the start/middle of a move (July 2002 EURUSD momentum extreme was mid-trend). A valid reversal fade requires a momentum extreme in the direction OPPOSITE the prior trend (USDCAD Nov 23 2007 bullish extreme after a downtrend).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Do not treat divergence as a standalone reversal signal — divergence persisted through EURUSD 2002-2004 with only pauses/corrections; a divergence-based reversal entered early loses. Only momentum extremes opposite the prior trend direction are valid reversal candidates.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated; bias-definition tool.
findings.quote: Divergence is present at every turn, but divergence does not always lead to a turn.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Divergence and Using Momentum Extremes to Trade a Reversal, pp. 121-125
findings.notes: If V8 ever formalizes an rsi_divergence expert it must be computed on log/ROC basis and treated as a gated confirmation signal, not a standalone entry; divergence as a reversal alone is high-risk per this book.
findings.book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

findings.strategy_name: Single moving-average cross with breakout-entry filter (SMA vs EMA)
findings.mechanism: Close-versus-MA is an objective trend division; a 1-tick breakout entry beyond the bar filters false signals; on tested FX data SMA performed at least as well as EMA
findings.setup_summary: On EURUSD daily 1998-2007: if close > MA(n) buy at 1 pip above the bar high; if close < MA(n) sell at 1 pip below the bar low (filter for false signals). Parameter sweep of 10-21 days: best input is 13 days for both SMA and EMA; SMA slightly better (13-SMA: 250 trades, 33.2% profitable, win/loss 2.39, net profit $32,305 vs 13-EMA: 28.2%, $16,620). Weekly sweeps (4-12) similar with SMA more consistent. Classic trend-following payoff shape: ~30-40% win rate with win/loss ratio > 2.
findings.trigger_invalidation: 'Moving average strategies get destroyed in range bound markets' — the method requires a trend/regime filter and is invalidated by whipsaw in ranges; switching methods after losses is explicitly warned against (consistency is the edge).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: stop-buy at high+1 pip (long) / stop-sell at low-1 pip (short) after the close crosses the MA; position is flipped on the opposite signal (no separate stop/target in the test).
findings.quote: Buy when price crosses above the moving average and sell when price crosses below the moving average. There is no simpler trending strategy and it works well.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Moving Averages, pp. 109-112
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's trend_pullback EMA signal. Adds: (1) 1-tick breakout entry filter, (2) SMA >= EMA on this data, (3) 13-period optimal on daily FX — all are testable refinements on BTCUSDT. The win-rate/win-loss structure is a useful prior for expected trend-following PnL shape in the simulator.
findings.book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

findings.strategy_name: Pivot-point support/resistance with hit-rate statistics
findings.mechanism: Pivot levels derived from the prior period's H/L/C are pre-planned reference points; measured hit rates let stops and targets be placed with known probabilities
findings.setup_summary: Compute pivot = (H+L+C)/3 and S1/R1-S3/R3 from the previous period. EURUSD daily study Jan 1999-Oct 2006: the daily low averages 1 pip below S1 and pierces S1 44% of days; the daily high averages 1 pip below R1 and pierces R1 42% of days; S2/R2 pierced 17%, S3/R3 3%. Use these statistics to place stops below S1 (favorable odds) and take profits just below R1.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Pivots are probabilities, not certainties; 'the high will exceed R1 4 days out of the next 10' is NOT implied by the 42% pierce rate. Hit rates are instrument-specific and must be re-measured per market.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop: below S1 (long) / above R1 (short); target: just below R1 (long) / just above S1 (short).
findings.quote: If you know that the pair slips below S1 44 percent of the time, then you can place a stop below S1 with confidence, knowing that probability is on your side.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Pivot Points, pp. 112-114
findings.notes: 24/7 crypto perp: pivots are computable on any fixed UTC period with no session-gap distortion; hit rates must be re-measured on BTCUSDT 1h. Supplies location features and empirically-grounded stop/target placement for risk_geometry.
findings.book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

findings.strategy_name: Pivot-zone breakout (Fisher pivot zones, tight-zone expansion)
findings.mechanism: A pivot zone between PivotHigh and PivotLow concentrates reference levels; zone width encodes the prior period's close-location (tight zone = breakout ahead, wide zone = range ahead); buying above PH / selling below PL avoids whipsaw
findings.setup_summary: Calculate PivotHigh (PH) and PivotLow (PL) from (H+L+C)/3 and (H+L)/2 (add/subtract their difference). If price is above the zone, take a bullish bias with a stop below the zone; enter only on a breakout above PH (buy) or below PL (sell). Zone width is informative: a tight zone warns of a breakout period; a wide zone indicates range-bound conditions. A rolling pivot zone (highest high / lowest low of the last x periods + last close) is used for trailing stops.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Do not trade inside the zone ('by only playing breakouts from the pivot zone... you have a method to avoid frustrating whipsaw market action'); a breakout is invalidated if price re-enters the zone.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: stop-buy above PH / stop-sell below PL; stop: below/above the pivot zone; trailing: rolling pivot zone (book: 3-, 4-, 5-day; scalpers can try 12/24-hour).
findings.quote: A tight pivot zone warns of a breakout period and a wide pivot zone indicates a higher probability of a range bound period.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Pivot Zones and Rolling Pivot Zone, pp. 114-117
findings.notes: Crypto perp is 24/7, so period boundaries are arbitrary — recompute zones on fixed UTC windows. Range compression followed by expansion is a documented BTC behavior; candidate expert or location/volatility feature feeding breakout_retest.
findings.book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

findings.strategy_name: Elliott 1-2 Base deep-pullback entry (variant of trend_pullback)
findings.mechanism: After a completed 5-wave impulse off a significant low/high, the wave-2 (or B) correction retraces roughly 50-61.8% and shakes out remaining crowd traders; shorts must cover, fueling the wave-3 (or C) explosion
findings.setup_summary: Identify a completed 5-wave impulse from a significant high/low; on the ensuing 3-wave correction, wait for a retrace of ~50-61.8% (corrections off significant extremes 'usually retrace at least 50 percent of the preceding impulse, and often end near the 61.8 percent level'); enter half the position on the pullback and half via a stop above the wave-1 (or wave-A) extreme; stop below the origin of the impulse. Highest reward-to-risk when the impulse begins from a significant low/high; the trade is invalid if the correction retraces 100% of the impulse.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if wave 2/B retraces 100% of wave 1/A (motive-wave rule) or if a triangle unfolds before wave 5 (stop gets triggered — book's own example of the flaw). Also a sharp wave-2 correction is a feature (more bears to cover), not a bug.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: half on the deep pullback (50-61.8% retrace), half stop-entry above wave-1 high / below wave-1 low; stop: below origin of wave 1/A; target: Fibonacci extension (wave 3 = 1.618 x wave 1; wave C = 1-1.618 x wave A).
findings.quote: If the rally happened in five waves, then buy the ensuing correction (this is the 1-2 Base).
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 7, Specific Setups — 1-2 Base, pp. 170-172
findings.notes: Elliott counting is subjective and hard to make deterministic in V8; the falsifiable core is 'deep pullback (~50-61.8%) after a strong impulse, continuation through the impulse extreme'. This is a variant of the existing trend_pullback family (which currently uses a shallow close<ema_slow pullback) — a deep-retrace variant plus split entry is a candidate parameter-variant family.
findings.book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

findings.strategy_name: Round-number and prior-cluster support/resistance with role reversal
findings.mechanism: Traders who traded a level before re-enter at it on retests (longs add, shorts cover) making it support; after a break both groups flip to sellers, so the level reverses role; round numbers act as psychological anchors
findings.setup_summary: Mark horizontal levels at round numbers and prior swing clusters; buy close to support, sell close to resistance; a broken level flips role (former support becomes resistance). Book examples: USDJPY 101-102 was a multi-decade support zone (1993 low 101.10, 1999 low 101.26, 2005 low 101.67); USDCAD 1.1700 was support in Nov 2004 and became resistance in Jan/Mar 2006 and Jan/Mar 2007.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A level holds only while sentiment supports it ('bearish sentiment ensured that the buying was not sufficient enough to hold 1.1700'); invalidated on a decisive break-and-reversal-of-role, at which point the level trades as its opposite.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: at/close to the zone; stop: beyond the zone; no explicit target in book.
findings.quote: The zone surrounding 2.0000 was resistance for the GBPUSD as the 1991 high was at 1.9990, the 1992 high was at 2.0035, and the January 2007 was at 1.9914.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Support and Resistance, pp. 105-108
findings.notes: BTC round levels (100k, 50k, etc.) are widely watched in perp order books and produce clustering; add round-number proximity and prior-swing-cluster proximity as location features. Role-reversal after a break is a falsifiable behavior for the location feature group.
findings.book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

findings.strategy_name: Open interest extremes at major turns
findings.mechanism: Major tops/bottoms occur when open interest is the highest within a specific period (crowd fully committed); but OI alone is backward-looking and, in futures, polluted by contract-roll cycles
findings.setup_summary: Track open interest relative to its recent range: major tops and bottoms tend to occur when OI is at its highest within a specific period, coinciding with Composite COT extremes. The book is skeptical of OI as a real-time trend-strength gauge ('increasing OI + increasing price = strong bull market' is backward looking) and notes FX futures OI tops recur on a 3-month contract cycle (March/June/Sept/Dec expiries), making mid-trend readings noisy.
findings.trigger_invalidation: OI extremes alone do not time turns; the 3-month roll cycle produces false OI tops in futures. Requires confluence with positioning extremes (COT) or price structure.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated.
findings.quote: major tops and bottoms do tend to occur when open interest is its highest within a specific period. In this sense, open interest is valuable at the same time as the Composite COT.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 5, Open Interest, pp. 91-93
findings.notes: Crypto perp OI is continuous (no roll cycle), real-time, and OI-at-highs plus positive funding is a standard crowding read. Testable flow features: OI percentile over window, and the SSI-derived claim 'rising price + falling net positioning = short-covering rally (bearish)'.
findings.book: Sentiment in the Forex Market - Indicators and Strategies To Profit from Crowd Behavior and Market Extremes 2008

findings.strategy_name: Fixed Fractional Money Management
findings.mechanism: risking a fixed fraction of equity per trade keeps per-trade risk constant in capital terms so that losing streaks compound geometrically but never wipe the account
findings.setup_summary: Position size is computed so the capital at risk on each trade equals a fixed percentage of account equity; the trading plan must state the maximum percentage of capital risked per trade and a reward-to-risk ratio target. This is an admission-time rule applied to every CandidateDraft regardless of direction.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the risked fraction scales with conviction or recent win rate (that is a different, adaptive sizing rule); the fraction must be a frozen registry constant.
findings.risk_geometry: risk per trade = fixed % of equity; stop distance defines risk; notional derived from equity, risk %, and stop distance; reward-to-risk target set in plan
findings.quote: reward-to-risk ratios, fixed fractional money management, and potential trailing stop-loss strategies. These all have to do with the proper placement of stop losses in relation to the larger goals of preserving capital, reducing risk...
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 Chapter Summary (p.216-217); plan element 'Maximum percentage of trading capital risked on each trade' at Ch.6 Plan the Trade (p.214); Index: Fixed fractional money management 200-201
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's RiskGate admission and risk_geometry. Crypto perp leverage (up to 100x+) makes per-trade risk fraction the binding constraint; funding and taker fees slightly erode the fixed fraction if not modeled in cost.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Trailing Stop-Loss
findings.mechanism: ratcheting the protective stop in the profit direction locks in gains and converts winners that reverse into smaller wins instead of round-trips
findings.setup_summary: After entry, the protective stop follows price in the direction of profit by a defined distance (the book's technical repertoire names Parabolic SAR as the canonical trailing device, p.90-92); the stop never moves back toward entry or widens.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the stop is moved away from price or back toward entry; only ratchet in the profit direction.
findings.risk_geometry: entry per strategy; stop trails by a defined (volatility-based) distance; no fixed target — exit is stop-driven
findings.quote: a trader can then turn attention toward reward-to-risk ratios, fixed fractional money management, and potential trailing stop-loss strategies.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 Chapter Summary (p.216-217); Index: Trailing stops 30, 145, 201-202; Parabolic Stop-And-Reverse indicator 90-92
findings.notes: Crypto's 24/7 no-exchange-gap tape makes mechanical trailing stops well-defined (no overnight gap jumps that plague equities/FX); in V8 this is a lifecycle exit option distinct from dead-thesis (still_valid) exits.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Technical-Structure Stop Placement
findings.mechanism: placing the stop at a technical reference (swing point, ATR band, Parabolic SAR) makes the stop distance a quantified risk measure rather than an arbitrary fixed amount
findings.setup_summary: Each trade's stop is set at a level derived from technical analysis (support/resistance, ATR, chart structure per the book's indicator repertoire) so stop placement itself is the mechanism for quantifying and controlling risk.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the stop is placed at an arbitrary fixed percentage or pip amount unrelated to market structure.
findings.risk_geometry: stop at technical reference; stop distance defines 1R; target set by the reward-to-risk target
findings.quote: With regard to the analytical side of trading, technical analysis excels as a method for quantifying and controlling risk through stop loss placement.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 Chapter Summary (p.217); Index: Stop losses 28-30, 36, 155-156, 200-201, 208-209
findings.notes: Corroborates V8 risk_geometry's atr_ref / frozen swing-reference stop design. Crypto volatility is regime-dependent, so structural (ATR/swing) stops dominate fixed-% stops; no gaps mean stops trigger at exactly the reference level.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Correlated-Exposure and Overload Cap
findings.mechanism: overloading positions under leverage builds a nondiversified, highly correlated book where many small bets act as one large bet, so total exposure must be capped and sizing kept prudent
findings.setup_summary: Total open exposure is capped to prevent margin overextension and concentrated, correlated positions; sizing is explicitly 'prudent' and avoids overloading, with diversification and pair correlation treated as risk controls.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if exposure aggregation ignores correlation between simultaneously open positions; cap must be deterministic, not advisory.
findings.risk_geometry: portfolio-level cap on total risk units/margin used; correlation-aware aggregation of open exposures
findings.quote: the trader must additionally address the prudent sizing of trades, which, in turn, also means an avoidance of overloading on positions. Overtrading in this respect carries the danger not only of margin overextension, but also potentially precarious exposure to a nondiversified, highly correlated portfolio of currency holdings.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 Chapter Summary (p.217); Index: Overtrading 205-207, Correlation currency pair 205-207, Diversification 205-207
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's ONE exposure per (instrument, direction) and heat cap. Crypto majors are strongly correlated (BTC leads, alts follow) and leverage magnifies overextension; cross-market feature group is where correlation evidence would live.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Periodic Loss Limit (Stop Trading for the Period)
findings.mechanism: a pre-committed periodic loss threshold halts all trading for the period at the point of monetary loss, forcing reassessment instead of revenge trading
findings.setup_summary: The trading plan fixes daily, weekly, and monthly loss limits: at the point of monetary loss the trader stops trading for the given period, regardless of subsequent setups that appear.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if trading continues after the limit is breached; the halt must be pre-committed, not discretionary.
findings.risk_geometry: portfolio-level loss threshold per period; halt in force until period boundary
findings.quote: Specific daily, weekly, and monthly loss limits (the point of monetary loss at which a trader stops trading for the given period)
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6, 'Plan the Trade and Trade the Plan' (p.214-215)
findings.notes: Concretely falsifiable. V8 determinism forbids wall-clock NOW() in replay, so a calendar-day limit cannot be encoded literally; the analogue is a bar-count or episode-based loss halt in the lifecycle. 24/7 perp trading makes time-period loss limits unusually relevant because there are no session boundaries to reset discipline.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Reward-to-Risk Floor
findings.mechanism: requiring a minimum reward-to-risk ratio on every trade preserves positive expectancy even at modest win rates
findings.setup_summary: Every trade is admitted only if its projected reward-to-risk ratio meets the target fixed in the trading plan; the reward-to-risk ratio target is a minimum admission condition, not an aspiration.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if a trade is admitted below the target ratio or if the ratio is computed with unrealistic stop/target distances.
findings.risk_geometry: target = reward-to-risk floor; stop and target distances set to satisfy it; size derived from fixed-fraction rule
findings.quote: Maximum percentage of trading capital risked on each trade • Reward-to-risk ratio target
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6, 'Plan the Trade and Trade the Plan' (p.214-215); Index: Risk/reward ratio 32, 146, 198-200
findings.notes: Maps directly onto V8 risk_geometry's target_r/stop_r. In perp crypto the ratio must net out taker fees and funding erosion, otherwise the realized ratio is lower than the chart ratio.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Master Trading Plan and Journal
findings.mechanism: recording the full plan (capital, leverage, max risk per trade, reward-to-risk target, profit goals, loss limits, strategy description, exact entry/exit criteria) and journaling daily actions makes deviations auditable and enforceable
findings.setup_summary: Before trading, a written plan specifies starting capital, lot size and leverage, max % risked per trade, reward-to-risk target, profit goals, loss limits, a full strategy description, and specific entry and exit criteria; a daily journal records actual activity so conformance to the plan can be checked.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Methodological; the loop is invalid if the plan is unwritten or deviations are not recorded.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: Every detail of the trading plan should be recorded in a dedicated journal... Besides maintaining this written trading plan, successful traders also take notes every day, recording the trading activities of the day.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6, 'Plan the Trade and Trade the Plan' (p.214-216)
findings.notes: Not directly tradable. Maps to V8's audit-trail discipline: registry decisions, CHANGELOG, and frozen spec versions are the machine form of 'plan the trade and trade the plan.'
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Positive-Expectancy Backtest Gate
findings.mechanism: only strategies with demonstrated positive expectancy, verified by backtesting on past price data, are admissible to live use; money management presupposes a positive-expectancy strategy
findings.setup_summary: A strategy is deployed only if manual or automated backtesting against past price data shows significant positive expectancy; this gate precedes any money-management or live application.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if a strategy reaches deployment without demonstrated positive expectancy, or if the backtest uses in-sample data only.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: any trading strategy employed must ultimately have a significant positive expectancy in order to contribute to a viable money management system and potential net profitability. The expectancy of a strategy can be determined through backtesting, whether manual or automated, where the strategy is applied to past price data in order to evaluate its hypothetical historical performance.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 Chapter Summary (p.217); Index: Positive expectancy 209-210, Backtesting 187-190, 210
findings.notes: Directly corroborates V8's evidence-bound stance (no economic claim without authority receipt, frozen-OOS gating). In perp crypto the backtest must include the funding and Binance USDM fee cost model or expectancy is overstated.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Discipline: Fidelity to the Tested Plan
findings.mechanism: relaxing a tested strategy's prerequisites under impatience/greed destroys the edge the backtest measured, and hoping/wishing delays loss cuts; discipline is the binding constraint on expectancy
findings.setup_summary: Trades are taken only when all of the tested strategy's prerequisites occur simultaneously; relaxing conditions 'close enough' invalidates the backtest, and hoping for recovery instead of cutting losses is identified as a primary account destroyer.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if any prerequisite is relaxed for convenience, or if a stop is deferred while hoping for a recovery.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: If the conditions are close enough, the trader may just take the trade. This type of undisciplined trading completely invalidates any backtesting work... failing to follow a tested strategy faithfully is virtually the same as gambling on an untested strategy.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6, Discipline section (p.213-214)
findings.notes: V8's frozen-spec, no-wall-clock determinism is the machine analogue of this discipline: candidate episodes must be generated strictly by frozen expert hypotheses, never by relaxing prereqs at run time.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Capital Preservation First
findings.mechanism: ordering risk control and preservation of capital ahead of profit maximization; capital preservation is the first constraint on any trade and begins with adequate capitalization
findings.setup_summary: Risk management is treated as the highest-priority attribute of a trader in a highly leveraged market; preservation of capital is considered even more important than a focus on making profits.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a (design principle)
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: In order to manage this risk, experienced traders make their highest priority the preservation of capital. In many respects, this can be considered even more important than a focus on just making profits.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 Chapter Summary (p.216)
findings.notes: Philosophy that underpins V8's RiskGate deterministic admission and heat cap. Not itself a falsifiable setup; high perp leverage makes it first-order.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Reject Trading-for-Excitement
findings.mechanism: opening positions purely to relieve boredom or seek excitement turns trading into gambling with worse odds than casino games and is detrimental to the account
findings.setup_summary: No position is opened when the motive is boredom, action, or thrill rather than a tested setup; recreational trading is to be avoided at all costs as harmful to the account.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not tape-falsifiable (motive is unobservable); treated as a psychology discipline, not a trigger rule.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: When these types of traders treat forex trading as gambling, it can actually become very similar to gambling. If positions are opened purely for the purpose of creating excitement and avoiding boredom, forex can have even worse odds than many casino games.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6, Discipline section (p.213)
findings.notes: 24/7 crypto markets are always open, giving a perpetual excuse to trade; the lesson lands as a methodology/flow discipline (trade only on tested setups), not an observable feature.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

book_title: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading (2009)

findings.strategy_name: Trend-following pullback entry (buy the dip / short the rally) with trailing stop below last swing
findings.mechanism: Trends persist; countertrend retracements (dips in uptrend, rallies in downtrend) offer high-probability entries in the direction of the prevailing trend.
findings.setup_summary: Identify an intact trend (higher lows/higher highs for uptrend via trendline or channel). Buy dips (temporary downward retracements) within the uptrend, or short rallies within the downtrend. Hold while the trend is intact; manage with a trailing stop moved to just below the last swing low; the break of the last swing low invalidates the uptrend thesis.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: retracement within a technically confirmed trend reaches support (trendline/channel floor or swing low). Invalidation: price breaks below the last swing low (uptrend) — trailing stop exits; trend-stage logic warns against late-stage entries when higher highs fail or volatility collapses.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar-close on dip/rally. Stop: below last swing low (manual trailing stop); alternatively below trendline/channel floor. Target: multiple R (reward-to-risk 'as high as possible', 'several times the magnitude of the initial stop loss'); trailing stop preferred over fixed profit target. Expiry: none — hold while trend intact. Scaling in/out (fractional positions) supported.
findings.quote: trend traders generally prefer to enter into a trend at high probability locations within the trend... buying on the dips in an uptrend... selling short on the rallies.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 'Trend Trading—Going with the Flow', pp.140-146 (Exhibit 5.1, p.143)
findings.notes: Directly corroborates the existing V8 trend_pullback expert (ema_fast>ema_slow + close<ema_slow, target_r 1.0/stop_r 1.0/expiry 8). Book suggests richer geometry for this family: trailing stop below last swing low rather than fixed ATR stop, and scaling in/out. 24/7 crypto: no gaps, 1h BTCUSDT trends well; whipsaw on late-stage entries flagged by the book's trend-stage discussion.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Moving average crossover system (single-price and 5/20 dual-MA variants)
findings.mechanism: Moving average direction and crossovers describe the prevailing trend; price crossing a MA (or short MA crossing long MA) is a buy/sell signal; systems are typically always-in-market.
findings.setup_summary: Price crosses above a single MA (e.g. 20) -> buy; crosses below -> sell. Or 5-period MA crosses above 20-period MA -> buy, below -> sell. Always-in-market: each opposite crossover closes the prior trade and opens the opposite one. Whipsaw losses are the known cost; profits must come from letting winners run in trending periods.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: crossover at bar close. Invalidation: opposite crossover; whipsaw strings in nontrending sideways markets are the expected failure mode (no trend filter).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar-close on crossover. Stop: none specified (always-in-market system; losses capped by opposite crossover). Target: let winners run. Whipsaw count is the main cost. Book's day-trading example adds filters: 14-RSI above 30 and rising MACD histogram as confirmation (explicitly 'not tested').
findings.quote: If the shorter-period moving average crosses above the longer one, it would be considered a signal to buy. Conversely, if the shorter moving average crosses below the longer one, it would be considered a signal to sell.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch3 'The Magic of Moving Averages', pp.72-77 (crossovers pp.75-76); Ch5 'Day Trading' p.138
findings.notes: Refines the existing trend_pullback family's trend filter (currently ema_fast>ema_slow) with an explicit always-in-market crossover variant. Book warns whipsaws are unavoidable — a regime/volatility filter (ADX mentioned p.89, p.141) is the natural guard. Applicable to 1h perps; taker-fee churn cost of repeated crossovers must be modeled in the simulator.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Breakout with pullback/throwback retest entry (breakout-hold-then-bounce)
findings.mechanism: A true breakout carries directional momentum; if price retraces to the breakout level (pullback after down-break, throwback after up-break) and bounces off it, the break is confirmed and the retest is a higher-probability entry than the initial break.
findings.setup_summary: Price breaks a horizontal support/resistance, trendline, pattern, or pivot level. Wait for the return to the breakout level (pullback/throwback). If price bounces at that level, enter in the breakout direction. Entering beyond the breakout point trades off false-break avoidance against early-entry profit.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: retest of a broken level that holds and bounces. Invalidation: price fails back through the breakout level — the break is declared false/premature and a hard stop (just before the breakout point) exits.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on retest bounce (bar close). Stop: hard stop just before/below the breakout point ('right before the breakout point where... the price move will have proven itself to be a false or premature breakout'). Target: next support/resistance level; for all-time breaks, new extremes beyond the broken level. Patience cost: many true breakouts never retest.
findings.quote: if the break is true (which means it carries real directional momentum) price should hit and bounce off the point of breakout, and then surpass the point at which breakout momentum waned and price turned.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 'Breakout Trading (and Fading)', pp.150-157 (pullback/throwback p.156)
findings.notes: Corroborates the existing V8 backlog family breakout_retest (DATA_BLOCKED, location/volatility/history). Book adds concrete risk geometry: hard stop below the breakout point, target = next structure level. In 24/7 perps there are no exchange gaps, so retests of broken 1h levels are cleanly observable — no gap-fill ambiguity.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Fade the false breakout (slingshot against a fakeout / premature break)
findings.mechanism: Most major breakouts are false: a level is breached slightly then price reverses, trapping breakout traders; a false breakout against the prevailing trend has a high failure rate and sets up a slingshot move in the opposite direction (vacuum created by trapped stops).
findings.setup_summary: Observe a breakout of a significant horizontal support/resistance, trendline, or pattern. If the break fails — price reverses back through the level with no follow-through (fakeout) or reverses after a premature break and then re-breaks — fade it: trade opposite the failed break. Ed Ponsi specifically favors false breakouts that move against the prevailing trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: false/premature break with price back through the level. Invalidation: the break proves true and carries real directional momentum; stop must be placed beyond the false-break extreme.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close back on the original side of the broken level. Stop: beyond the false-break extreme/high-water mark of the trap. Target: opposite side of range or prior structure; book stresses proper risk controls because fading 'goes directly against the trend and momentum'.
findings.quote: One of my favorite situations is a false breakout that moves against the trend. These types of breakouts have a high failure rate, and they also set the stage for a 'slingshot' trade in the opposite direction.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 'Breakout Trading (and Fading)' pp.150-153; Ed Ponsi Executive Insight pp.157-158
findings.notes: Matches the existing V8 failed_breakout family (liquidity_vacuum_reentry, SHORT, close-below-windowed-prior-high, frozen ref). Book's additional claim: a false break AGAINST the prevailing trend (not just any false break) is the highest-quality slingshot — a candidate refinement: require the fakeout to oppose higher-TF trend. Highly relevant to crypto where leveraged stop cascades amplify the vacuum.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Horizontal range trading at support/resistance with minimum-range-height filter
findings.mechanism: In nontrending markets price bounces repeatedly between horizontal support and resistance; entering at the boundaries with a stop beyond the boundary and a target at the far side has positive skew when the range is tall enough.
findings.setup_summary: Establish a horizontal range with at least two approximate touches of both support and resistance (or Bollinger Bands with a flat/near-flat middle SMA). Enforce a minimum range height so the target far side justifies the stop risk (e.g. 20-pip GBP/USD Asian range not worth trading; 300-pip range is). Buy near support, sell near resistance; confirm turns with oscillator exits from overbought/oversold (Stochastics/RSI) or an intra-range trendline break.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price near range boundary + oscillator turn confirmation (crossing out of overbought/oversold). Invalidation: range broken (stop beyond the boundary level); flatness of the range violated.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: at/near boundary (bar close). Stop: just beyond the support/resistance level from which the trade is initiated. Target: other side of the range; a tighter stop is possible if an intra-range trendline break confirms the turn. Expiry: none stated; swings typically 1h-4h-daily timeframe.
findings.quote: If stop losses are always placed just beyond the support or resistance level from which a range trade is initiated... a prudent range trading approach should include some minimum criteria for the height of the range.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 'Range Trading—Between a Rock and a Hard Place', pp.147-150
findings.notes: New mean_reversion family with a falsifiable minimum-height filter. Crypto 1h ranges exist but trend phases dominate and range-breakout risk is elevated by leverage; the range-height threshold is the key testable parameter. No time-of-day bias claim (unlike FX session ranges); 24/7 market means no session-open boundary effects.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Technical carry trade: positive-yield position entered only near long-term support/resistance
findings.mechanism: Capital flows toward higher-yielding currencies when risk appetite is not extreme; a carry trader earns the (leveraged) interest differential daily. Technical carry adds a location filter: entry near long-term support (long carry) or resistance (short carry) is the high-probability zone, cutting adverse-move risk.
findings.setup_summary: Screen pairs for a large current interest-rate differential (threshold ~300 bp) and its likely future direction from central-bank policy. Then select only pairs whose price is in the bottom third of the long-term vertical range (for long carry) or near long-term resistance (for short carry). Scale entry with multiple fractional positions spaced evenly across the support zone; target the top third of the range; stop below long-term support.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pair with positive carry differential and price in the high-probability location (near support/resistance). Invalidation: differential shrinks/reverses (rate-cycle turn); stop below long-term support; adverse price moves can erase all daily interest gains.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: scaled/fractional entries across the bottom-third support zone. Stop: just below long-term support. Target: top third of the long-term range (technically based). Holding period: long-term (weeks to months); daily interest settled at rollover on the FULL leveraged notional, not just margin.
findings.quote: if a substantial positive interest rate differential can be achieved by buying a currency pair... the highest probability entry would be near long-term support. When price on the pair is near long-term support, the historical probability is that price should eventually rise.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch4 'Carried Away with Trading' pp.108-110; Ch5 'Technical Carry Trade' Tips & Techniques pp.181-182
findings.notes: In perps, the interest differential maps to the funding rate (paid on full notional, continuous, no central-bank cycle). Key differences: funding is small, sign-flips, and long-carry is exposed to deleveraging cascades. The transferable piece is the location filter (enter near long-term support) — a candidate REFINE for trend_pullback requiring a cross_market funding feature (derivatives tape, DATA_BLOCKED today).
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Contrarian fade of extreme speculator net positioning (COT / positioning extremes)
findings.mechanism: When large speculators' net positioning reaches an extreme, the marginal buyer/seller is exhausted — there is little uncommitted capital left to push price further, so price is prone to reverse.
findings.setup_summary: Monitor net speculator positioning (CFTC COT report for FX futures; mass-media consensus as a proxy). When major speculators are drastically and increasingly net long at a recent peak, prepare to short; when net short at an extreme, prepare to buy. The contrarian premise: media and consensus are usually wrong or extremely late at market extremes.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: positioning at a recent extreme peak/trough. Invalidation: positioning keeps extending (contrarian trades can step in front of a trend); book explicitly warns this is risky and needs strict risk controls — 'do not step into the path of a speeding train'.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on positioning extreme (bar-close after confirmation). Stop: not specified (book defers specific COT methods 'beyond the scope'); V8 geometry must be added (ATR/swing-based). Target: mean-reversion toward prior range; no expiry stated.
findings.quote: if the COT report shows that major speculators have been drastically and increasingly net long in the British pound against the U.S. dollar... traders may begin looking for the next opportunity to short the pound in a classic contrarian maneuver.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 'Contrarian Trading—The Majority Doesn't Rule', pp.184-187 (COT report p.185, Exhibit 5.16 p.186)
findings.notes: No COT equivalent in perps; proxies are venue long/short ratios, aggregate open interest, and funding-rate extremes — noisy, venue-specific, and not yet in the V8 tape.
