Best use is a participation/flow feature input and a regime-level contrarian filter, not a standalone expert. Class sentiment (positioning extremes), maps to existing V8 vocab flow/participation feature groups.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Bollinger Squeeze volatility breakout (contraction-to-expansion) with head-fake caution
findings.mechanism: Volatility is cyclical: periods of high volatility follow periods of low volatility; when bands narrow dramatically (squeeze), the stage is set for a violent breakout in either direction — but a short fake-out move ('head fake') often precedes the real surge.
findings.setup_summary: Observe Bollinger Bands (20-period SMA, 2 std) tightening to historically low bandwidth around a consolidating price structure. Expect an imminent expansion. Trade the eventual directional break, allowing for a possible head-fake fake-out first; manage risk so a fake-out does not stop the position out before the real move.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: band bandwidth at historical low + price structure consolidating. Invalidation: direction-agnostic — the trade must survive the head-fake; a clean expansion in the wrong direction invalidates the chosen side.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on the post-squeeze breakout (bar close) with allowance for the fake-out. Stop/target: not specified by the book; V8 would add ATR-based stop and R-target. Expiry: none stated; squeeze resolution typically within a handful of bars on the trading timeframe.
findings.quote: periods of high volatility generally follow periods of low volatility. When the Bollinger Bands narrow dramatically, volatility is drastically decreased. The subsequent expectation, then, is for price to breakout violently in either direction.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch3 Tips & Techniques 'The Bollinger Squeeze', p.91
findings.notes: Volatility clustering is pronounced in crypto and the 24/7 market resolves squeezes without gap discontinuities, making the contraction-expansion pattern cleanly measurable on 1h BTCUSDT. The head-fake warning is a falsifiable sub-claim (fake-out precedes true break in a measurable fraction of squeezes). New expert family under complexity-budget rule 14.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Price-oscillator divergence as reversal timing signal
findings.mechanism: When price makes a higher high while the oscillator makes a lower high (bearish divergence), price momentum is fading and a reversal is more likely; a few accurate divergences can offset many false ones because reversal entries are so profitable.
findings.setup_summary: On the trading chart (book recommends longer timeframes for reliability), compare price swings with an oscillator (RSI, Stochastics, MACD). Bearish divergence: price higher high + oscillator lower high -> expect down move. Bullish divergence: price lower low + oscillator higher low -> expect up move. Book stresses divergence is a confirmation/hint tool, not a standalone strategy.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: confirmed divergence at a swing extreme. Invalidation: momentum resumes (divergence fails); no defined failure threshold in the book — V8 must add one (e.g., oscillator making a new extreme with price).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: at the swing extreme after divergence confirmation (bar close). Stop: beyond the swing extreme. Target: prior structure / swing; no R-multiple stated. Expiry: none.
findings.quote: bearish divergence (which hints at an impending reversal back down) occurs when price hits a higher high while the oscillator hits a corresponding lower high.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 'Divergence Trading—Separate Paths', pp.170-172 (Exhibits 5.13/5.14)
findings.notes: The book explicitly demotes divergence to a confirmation tool ('much less often are they employed exclusively as a full-fledged, self-sufficient trading strategy'), which argues for integrating it as a confirmation in the mean-reversion/range family rather than a standalone expert. Medium applicability on 1h perps; better on 4h+. Momentum as a feature group is absent from the frozen V8 vocabulary — divergence needs trend+response-style features.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Fixed-fractional risk and reward-to-risk ratio discipline
findings.mechanism: Risk a fixed percentage of equity per trade by construction: stop distance and position size are chosen so max loss equals the percentage cap; a high reward-to-risk ratio (3:1 ideal, 2:1 practical) lets a trader be right less than half the time and still profit.
findings.setup_summary: Per trade, cap risk at a fixed fraction of account equity (book example: 3% -> 30-pip max stop on a $1/pip mini-lot for a $1,000 account; recommends the cap as a flexible maximum, e.g. 'no single trade can have a stop loss that exceeds 4% of total equity', not a rigid per-trade %). Set profit targets to a multiple of the stop (2:1 practical, 3:1 ideal, 4:1 aggressive), adapting to market conditions; require positive expectancy overall and ~10x required margin as account capital.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — risk rule; invalidation is a capital-preservation constraint, not a market signal.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop: distance chosen so that stop-magnitude x pip-value x size <= equity % cap. Target: 2-4x the stop distance. Position sizing: micro/mini/standard lots scaled to the cap; the book explicitly warns against setting stops at arbitrary pip values that ignore market conditions (e.g. 30-pip stop inappropriate for a weekly head-and-shoulders).
findings.quote: a more adaptable rule might be to require that no single trade can have a stop loss that exceeds, for example, 4% of total equity.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch6 'Fix Your Fractions' pp.200-201; 'Risk and Reward' pp.198-200; 'Fatter Is Healthier' pp.197-198
findings.notes: Maps directly to V8 RiskGate admission rules: per-trade equity-% cap, reward-to-risk admission threshold, and the 10x-margin capitalization guideline. Transferable to perps with taker-fee-aware risk (spread handicap cited for day trading scales with perp maker/taker fees). Book is unambiguous that risk management precedes edge ('risk and money must be managed... to survive to trade another day').
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Position-overload cap: limit concurrent positions because instruments are highly correlated
findings.mechanism: Overtrading multiplies correlated exposure: the handful of tradable pairs all depend on the same underlying (USD, then EUR/JPY/GBP crosses), so holding many positions is not diversification; a strict cap on concurrent positions and per-position size reductions control this risk.
findings.setup_summary: Impose a strict maximum on the number of concurrently open positions; when fewer instruments are tradable and they are closely correlated (all USD pairs, then crosses), additional positions mostly add correlated exposure rather than diversification. Reduce per-position size (multiple fractional positions) as an alternative to reducing count. The book rejects broker hedging and synthetic-pair quasi-hedging as risk controls (long EUR/USD + long USD/CHF == long EUR/CHF).
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — risk rule limiting exposure concentration; no market trigger.
findings.risk_geometry: Cap: max concurrent positions. Sizing: fractional positions (e.g. 10 mini-lots instead of 1 standard lot) so each unit can be scaled out at different prices. No stop geometry — this is an exposure-concentration constraint.
findings.quote: The most obvious way is to place a strict maximum on the number of positions entered at one time.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch6 'Position Overload', pp.205-207
findings.notes: Corroborates V8 rule 16 (ONE active exposure per instrument-direction) and the heat cap. In perp crypto the correlation argument is even stronger (altcoins co-move with BTC; venue-wide liquidation cascades); a strict concurrent-position cap plus aggregate-correlation guard is directly implementable in RiskGate. High leverage in perps magnifies the overextension risk the book describes.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: News/data trading on consensus deviation (expectation vs surprise), including secondary-reaction entry
findings.mechanism: Price moves on the surprise, not the number: the market has already priced in the consensus, so trades are taken on how far actual data deviates from consensus; initial reactions are unreliable, so a secondary reaction (reversal or pullback-continuation) can be a cleaner entry.
findings.setup_summary: Before a scheduled release (NFP, CPI, FOMC, GDP, retail sales, PMI, trade balance...), memorize consensus. When the actual print deviates from consensus by at least a trader-set threshold, trade in the direction implied by the deviation. Variant: skip the initial spike (deemed unreliable, with gaps/widening spreads) and enter on the secondary reaction — a full reversal of the initial move or a continuation after pullback/consolidation.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: |actual - consensus| >= threshold at release time. Invalidation: price already priced-in (a 'bad' number that rallies the dollar means consensus was worse); no clear deviation direction; whipsaw/nondirectional volatility is the known failure mode. Data revisions can move markets more than the original release.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: market order within milliseconds (speed variant) or bar-close on secondary reaction (patient variant). Stop: not specified; book notes spreads widen and price gaps occur in fast markets, so fills are less reliable. Target: 'a few pips' quick scalp or continuation of the one-way run. Expiry: seconds-to-minutes (scalp) for the speed variant.
findings.quote: trading can take place based on how far the actual numbers deviate from the consensus numbers. In this way, news trading is based almost entirely on relative values rather than absolute values.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch4 'No News Is Bad News for News Traders' pp.121-124; Ch5 'News Trading' p.183
findings.notes: The expectation-surprise mechanism transfers to crypto (scheduled US macro releases and FOMC move BTCUSDT at 1h scale; 24/7 trading means releases land in-session), but it requires a scheduled-release + consensus data feed absent from the V8 OHLCV tape and conflicts with deterministic replay (no wall clock, event/available/ingested clocks never collapsed). The secondary-reaction variant is the most implementable fragment and could inform a response-behavior feature.
findings.book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

findings.strategy_name: Join-the-crowd trend continuation (DITM/ITM trade)
findings.mechanism: a confirmed strong trend persists; buying the high-probability leg (deep in-the-money) monetizes persistence with a ~2% buffer against reversal
findings.setup_summary: On 4h/day charts, confirm a strong trend via: price above the daily trend line in the trade direction, price through its 50-period MA, and a sequence of new daily highs (or lows), with trend-line angle ~37-45 deg. Buy the deep-in-the-money leg (premium $75-85, ~2% distance from spot) betting settlement stays on the trend side. Falsifiable on BTCUSDT 1h: after a streak of new N-bar extremes plus close > 50-EMA, P(close higher in next 24 bars) exceeds the premium-implied ~80% threshold.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: strong-trend confirmation (new-high streak + MA/trend-line alignment). Invalidation: trend fails to keep making new highs/lows; close back through the 50-period MA; dead-thesis if trend angle steepens past ~45 deg (overextension).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close on confirmation; risk limited to premium; target = fixed $100 payoff (equivalent R ≈ 0.18-0.33R per trade, high win-rate); expiry = end-of-period (weekly in book -> 24-168 bars in V8); still_valid = trend persists.
findings.quote: If the trend is strong and the headlines seem to be screaming at you... such conditions provide confirmation for an in-the-money strategy, which is a trend-following approach. ... a DITM trade makes a lot of sense.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 7 (pp. 128-129); trend checklist Ch. 5 (pp. 76-78)
findings.notes: Same mechanism family as existing trend_pullback (trend_continuation); a new behavior variant (join-on-strength rather than buy-the-dip) with high win-rate/low-payoff geometry. Book's own week-2 occurrence analysis (Ch 2, p. 21) found buying everything priced >80% won that week, but warns it will not always work - exactly the evidence-bound caution V8 needs.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Compression breakout (triangles, narrow channels, wedges)
findings.mechanism: range compression squeezes sentiment into an apex; the subsequent expansion resolves the range, so a breakout leg placed outside the range wins
findings.setup_summary: On 4h/30m charts, identify a triangle (ascending/descending/symmetrical), narrow sideways channel, or wedge where the high-low range narrows progressively; place a breakout leg just outside the range (buy above resistance / sell below support), betting settlement occurs outside the range. Strongest when timed to scheduled data releases (NFP, central bank statements) or after a doji cluster. Falsifiable: normalized range (e.g., (high-low)/ATR) below a threshold is followed by a range-expanding move within N bars.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: compression (range/ATR ratio falling across >=2 successive windows, e.g., triangle apex). Invalidation: price breaks then closes back inside the range (false break); expiry passes without the break.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close on range break; risk = premium (OTM leg $15-46 -> ~5:1-2:1 payoff); target = $100 payoff; expiry = end of week in book; direction-agnostic straddle variant allowed (breakout either way, same payout).
findings.quote: Triangles can be considered preludes to breakouts. The binary option trader, when seeing a triangle, should locate the strike prices outside of the triangle and play a breakout. ... The breakout trade is essentially a play on volatility.
findings.notes: Crypto perps are prone to range-compression-then-expansion on 1h; needs a definable compression measure (range/ATR or Bollinger width). Corroborated by the Bollinger 'narrow band = breakout precondition' claim (Ch 6, p. 99).
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Failed-breakout retry
findings.mechanism: a range that has already resisted one breakout is range-exhausted; the next attempt is more likely to succeed because markets do not stay sideways indefinitely
findings.setup_summary: After a breakout attempt fails (price breaks a range high/low then closes back inside), re-enter the breakout in the same direction on the next attempt at the same level. Book claim: 'if the previous week's breakout trade failed, the probability that the next one will work is actually greater.' Falsifiable: conditional on at least one failed break of level L, P(successful break within N attempts) versus unconditional base rate.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: prior failed breakout at level L (touch-and-close-back-inside) followed by a fresh approach to L. Invalidation: second failure closes deep inside range; the retry thesis dies if the range itself breaks on the far side.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close above (below) L; stop = back inside the range (structural); target = measured move / structure beyond L; expiry in bars; no premium analog in V8 (perps).
findings.quote: Sometimes the trader is timing the breakout too early. In fact, if the previous week's breakout trade failed, the probability that the next one will work is actually greater because markets don't stay sideways too long.
findings.notes: Distinct from V8's failed_breakout expert (which SHORTs the failure); this is the opposite leg - retry the break. Both could coexist as variants; test the 'failure increases next-attempt success probability' claim as an empirical conditioning question.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Channel bounce / ATM bounce (mean reversion to mid-range)
findings.mechanism: inside a defined channel, price oscillates between support and resistance; fading the extremes with a mid-range target monetizes the oscillation
findings.setup_summary: On a sideways channel (or near a well-tested support/resistance zone), buy the bounce off the bottom / sell the bounce off the top, targeting the middle of the range. Book tactic: enter at $45-55 premium, close at a $75-80 objective (~77% return) rather than riding to expiration. Falsifiable: in a range regime, touch of a 3-touch S/R level followed by close back inside predicts a move back to range-mid within N bars.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price probes a confirmed S/R level inside a range and shows a rejection close. Invalidation: price closes through the level (level breaks -> becomes supply_demand_zone role-switch signal instead); range regime degrades into trend.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close on rejection; stop = beyond the tested level (swing); target = mid-range or fixed R (~0.6R of the range width); expiry short (book: within hours-to-days).
findings.quote: Bounce plays are in the lingo of technical analysis: mean reversion plays betting that the price will move back toward the middle of the range. ... A good method for a bounce trade is not to go to expiration but to select a target price to close the position.
findings.notes: Requires a regime filter (range vs trend) to avoid fading trends; V8 has no active mean-reversion expert, so this is a genuinely new family candidate. The 'vibrating your way to profits' variant rides oscillation with strike mid-range.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Extended Bollinger Band reversal
findings.mechanism: price beyond the ~99% outer band is an extreme-value state; re-entry inside the band confirms the crowd has exhausted and a reversal follows
findings.setup_summary: Use two band settings: standard (20, 2) capturing ~96% and an Extended Bollinger Band (13, 2.618) capturing ~99%. A strong sell signal occurs when price goes beyond the upper EBB then closes back below it; a strong buy signal when price goes beyond the lower EBB then closes back above it. Falsifiable on 1h: close beyond the (20,2.618) band followed by close inside predicts an N-bar reversal at better than base rate.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close outside outer band then close back inside, direction opposite the extreme. Invalidation: price walks the band and keeps extending (book: don't assume price stops at a band - it can stay there); band ride without reclaim is not a signal.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close back inside the outer band; stop = beyond the extreme (structure); target = middle band or 1R; expiry moderate; narrow-band condition is instead the breakout prelude (see volatility_breakout).
findings.quote: If the price goes beyond the EBB and then returns below it, this is a strong sell signal. ... If the price goes beyond the bottom EBB and then returns above it, it is a strong buy signal!
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6 (pp. 104-105); Do's and Don'ts pp. 99-101
findings.notes: Cleanly implementable from ATR/std band math on 1h closes; the 'reclaim by close' structure matches V8's liquidity_sweep_reclaim style (frozen ref + close reclaim). Book also states price at extreme bands is a high-probability pause/reversal zone (p. 99).
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Support/resistance role-switch after break
findings.mechanism: broken S/R flips polarity: tested-and-broken resistance becomes new support, so a pullback to the old level finds fresh buyers
findings.setup_summary: Mark support/resistance with >=3 touches on 4h/day timeframes (higher timeframes = stronger evidence); after price breaks through, the old level flips role - buy the pullback to former resistance (now support) in an uptrend, or sell the rally to former support (now resistance) in a downtrend. Falsifiable: P(bounce at flipped level) > P(bounce at untested level), conditioned on >=3 prior touches.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: break and close through a 3-touch level, then price returns to the level. Invalidation: close through the flipped level (no bounce); fewer than 3 touches = weak level, do not trade.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close at the flipped level; stop = beyond the level by an ATR cushion; target = prior structure / measured move; expiry in bars; book uses S/R to place the binary strike just above/below the level.
findings.quote: When these events occur... the support line begins to act as a new resistance line. The resistance line begins to act as a new support line. ... Many traders use three touches to confirm that the lines are good lines to locate possible entry positions.
findings.notes: Foundation pattern, likely corroborated by many books in the library; cleanly testable on 1h perps. Book couples it with Bollinger coincidence to strengthen level confidence (Ch 6, p. 101).
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Price-break persistence and streak exhaustion
findings.mechanism: trend = persistence of new highs/lows; the streak length of consecutive new extremes measures trend strength, and streaks approaching their historical maximum signal exhaustion and a defined reversal level
findings.setup_summary: Replace subjective trend lines with price-break (three-line break) charts: a new 1h/4h high paints a block, a new low paints a down block; no new extreme = nothing drawn. Trend strength = run length of same-direction blocks; a reversal block appears only if price gives back N previous extremes (3-line rule), so the reversal LEVEL is known in advance even if the time is not. Small new-extreme increments (small blocks) signal a tired trend and an impending breakout; streaks approaching the instrument's observed max block count (book example: ~21) signal likely reversal. Falsifiable: conditional distribution of streak lengths; P(reversal within K bars once streak >= local max).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: streak length reaches local historical maximum percentile, or reversal block prints (N prior extremes given back). Invalidation: streak extends beyond observed max (trend strengthens); small-block compression resolving as breakout continuation rather than reversal.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on reversal block print or streak-max condition; stop = beyond the reversal block high/low; target = prior block cluster / Fibonacci-confluent level (book: fib lines often coincide with reversal points); expiry in bars.
findings.quote: If a series is in place that is approaching 21 blocks, there is a high probability that a reversal is about to occur... Price break charts actually and precisely define and project where, not when, such a price reversal will appear.
findings.notes: Directly implementable as a marketstate feature: count of consecutive new 1h extremes + its rolling percentile; feeds trend-strength scoring and a potential exhaustion-reversal expert. Book also uses it to match durations (1m-renko for 1m binaries etc., Ch 2 p. 25) - a timeframe-linking methodology V8 can borrow.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Surprise-event shock, reaction, and retracement
findings.mechanism: an exogenous surprise produces an immediate one-direction reaction, then the shock wave diffuses and price retraces toward pre-event levels, so the retracement leg is tradable
findings.setup_summary: When a scheduled or surprise event (data release, central bank statement, geopolitical shock) drives a sharp one-direction move, do not chase the initial impulse; enter the opposite direction once the reaction stalls or visibly reverses, with an expiry covering the retracement. Book cases: Japan quake yen surge then BOJ-stopped bounce (4:1); Paris attacks gold spike then weekly decline; Ukraine Monday risk-off -> Friday risk-appetite. Falsifiable: for BTCUSDT, macro-shock candles (FOMC/CPI/NFP) with |return| > k*ATR are followed by a partial retracement (measurable mean reversion fraction) within N bars.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: large shock move (event candle > threshold ATR multiple) followed by stall/reversal bar. Invalidation: news creates genuinely new conditions and the move extends (book: 'if the news was so strong, it creates new conditions, and therefore, the price is likely not to reverse that quickly'); reversal fails and impulse resumes.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close after reaction stalls; stop = beyond the shock extreme; target = 38.2-61.8% retracement of the shock move (fib-of-shock); expiry short-to-medium (book: hours to end-of-week).
findings.quote: These events also have in common surprise followed by the reaction of the markets similar to a chemical reaction diffusion process. The markets react and then the initial shock wave is diffused out. It is in the reaction phase when binary option trading opportunities occur.
findings.notes: BTC reacts to scheduled macro events and flash news; 24/7 markets and high leverage make stop placement critical. Requires an event-labeling layer (economic calendar + surprise magnitude) not currently in V8 - DEFER until calendar data is wired.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Text-mining sentiment polarity and risk-appetite/aversion ratio
findings.mechanism: crowd opinion is measurable from text; sentiment crossovers mark opinion shifts and sentiment peaks (positive or negative) are milestones for subsequent price reversals
findings.setup_summary: Mine headlines/keywords for a market (seed terms: 'risk appetite', 'risk aversion', + market + emotional adjective/adverb), score each hit -5..+5, and build a positive/negative sentiment ratio; treat polarity crossover and extreme sentiment peaks as regime/shift signals. Book cites research: topic-based Twitter sentiment improved next-day S&P 100 prediction; WSJ text mining claimed >55.7% accuracy on daily direction. For crypto perps the analog is funding/OI/extreme positioning plus social sentiment, but the book's own caution applies: Twitter-grade data is at best a confirming indicator.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: sentiment polarity crossover, or sentiment score at a rolling extreme. Invalidation: sentiment continues to diverge from price (no confirmation); the polarity signal is treated only as confirming, never standalone.
findings.risk_geometry: Not a price-geometry trade in V8; input to regime/direction filters only. Book uses it to choose binary moneyness (OTM when central-bank statement due, since surprise risk is high).
findings.quote: sentiment peaks, whether positive or negative, are the key milestones relating to subsequent price changes and offer great potential as a source of trading signals.
findings.notes: LITERATURE_SUPPORTED because the chapter cites peer-style studies (Si et al. 2013 Twitter; Wong, Liu, Chiang 2014 WSJ >55.7%; Hafez/RavenPack). V8 has no 'sentiment' feature group in the frozen vocabulary - would need a registry decision to add one, or proxy via funding/OI (flow). Book's 'binaries misprice OTM ladders because market makers cannot price extremes' (Ch 1, pp. 16-17) is an edge claim specific to the $100-payoff market and NOT transferable to perps.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Carry trade via interest-rate differentials
findings.mechanism: capital flows to where expected yields are highest; selling low-rate and buying high-rate instruments harvests the differential (the 'jet stream' of currency flows)
findings.setup_summary: Currencies strengthen when their central bank's rates are expected to rise and weaken when expected to fall; the carry trade sells low-rate currencies (JPY, CHF, USD) and buys high-rate (AUD, NZD), with the warning that an overextended high-rate currency eventually self-corrects. Crypto-perp mapping: funding rate is the closest analog - sustained positive funding signals crowded longs paying carry (fade candidates), negative funding the reverse; venue-to-venue funding spreads can be traded. Book adds: when a central-bank statement is due, prefer OTM (surprise risk), and rate expectations, not current rates, drive price.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: sustained funding/rate differential regime. Invalidation: central-bank policy shift flips expectations; crowding self-correction unwinds the carry (see carry_unwind).
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop geometry in V8 terms; a flow/regime feature rather than a per-trade setup. Book: high-rate carry is cyclical and self-correcting - do not hold extreme positions.
findings.quote: This leads to a strategy called the carry trade. This strategy involves selling low interest rate currencies... and then buying high interest rate currencies. ... interest rate differentials can be considered the jet stream of the currency market!
findings.notes: The FX-rate-differential mechanism is not directly tradeable in single-instrument perps, but funding-rate regimes are a real, measurable perp feature (crowding signal + carry cost); propose as a flow-group input and a regime filter, not an expert.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: 2% risk per trade, rule of three, and premium breakeven math
findings.mechanism: fixed-fraction sizing bounds ruin while position sizing in multiples of three and premium-aware breakeven math keep one loss from erasing a winning streak
findings.setup_summary: Never risk more than 2% of equity on any single trade; size positions in multiples of three (all-in three lots or legging one lot at a time, all-out/leg-out exits); compute the required win rate from the premium - a $95 premium needs 19 winners per loser, a 5:1 payoff needs >=1 win in 5, and >80% accuracy is required to profit buying $80 premiums. Book also flags time-of-week risk asymmetry: an $80 premium position Monday is riskier than the same on Thursday (more time for things to go wrong). V8 mapping: RiskGate max-risk-per-exposure as % equity + breakeven-aware evaluation of each expert's required win rate.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - standing risk rule, not a trigger-based setup.
findings.risk_geometry: Sizing rule only; book confirms no margin/leverage in binaries (position capped by cash), which differs from perps where leverage must be capped explicitly; V8 RiskGate should enforce the % cap independent of leverage.
findings.quote: Another risk-control approach... is not to risk more than 2 percent of equity on any binary option trade. ... An $80 binary option price on Monday is far riskier than an $80 binary option trade on Thursday. There is more time on Monday for things to go wrong.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9 (pp. 181-183); breakeven math Ch. 10 (pp. 186-187)
findings.notes: Matches starter vocabulary risk_percent_sizing. The premium-to-breakeven table (Ch 10, p. 187) is a clean win-rate/payoff ladder V8 can reuse to set required-accuracy gates per expert before promotion.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Deep-out-of-the-money (DOOM) weekly tail insurance
findings.mechanism: cheap convexity on extreme ladders pays off disproportionately in the rare large moves, acting as portfolio insurance against selloff surprises
findings.setup_summary: Hold one deep-out-of-the-money play ($10-20 premium, ~5-6:1 payoff) each week as an insurance policy for unexpected selloffs, mixed with high-probability legs (book mixes: 3 DITM + 1 DOOM, or thirds DITM/ATM/DOOM). DOOM pays when markets move big (book: 'black Monday' 2015, oil crash 2015 - DOOM and breakout plays catch the moves); it will not pay off most weeks, so expectancy must be evaluated over many weeks. Falsifiable: a constant DOOM-like tail basket on an index has positive net expectancy over periods containing >=1 tail event.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: none - continuous standing position. Invalidation: none per-trade; strategy-level risk is that it never pays while costs accumulate - book: 'it will not pay off all the time'.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: market on the extreme ladder (premium $10-20); risk = full premium; target = $100 payoff (5-6:1); expiry = end of period; book warns selling the extreme ladders (the reverse leg) is dangerous because 'markets that are extended become extended for a fundamental reason'.
findings.quote: It's not a bad idea to put on one DOOM play each week as an insurance policy for when the unexpected occurs. The only caveat with such an approach is it will not pay off all the time.
findings.notes: The $100/0 fixed-payoff structure does not exist on perps; the transferable lesson is portfolio-level: mixing low-probability high-payoff legs with high-probability legs, evaluated over many weeks, and the warning against fading extended markets. V8's one-exposure-per-direction rule conflicts with the multi-leg book framing - record as methodology, not an expert.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Bollinger Band mean-reversion (regression to the mean / Extended Bollinger Bands)
findings.mechanism: overextension reverts: price touching the lower (or an extended) Bollinger Band in a non-trending market mean-reverts to the middle band
findings.setup_summary: In a ranging market (no confirmed trend), when price touches and then closes back inside the lower Bollinger Band (or an Extended Bollinger Band for deeper overextension), go LONG targeting the middle band; mirror-short at the upper band. Falsifiable on 1h: price closes inside band after a band touch in a flat regime.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: band touch followed by close reclaim inside the band in a range regime. Invalidation: strong trend regime (trend feature says trending) or a band-walk where price rides the band without reverting.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after reclaim; stop beyond the touch bar extreme (or 1 ATR below low); target mid-band (0.5 R) or opposite band; expiry in bars bounded by mean reversion horizon; band width = ATR-based.
findings.quote: Regression to the mean, 98; Price action on lower Bollinger Band, 104; Extended Bollinger Bands (EBB), 104-105, 106
findings.chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 98-106 (Bollinger Bands, Low Bollinger Band, Extended Bollinger Bands)
findings.notes: No exchange gaps in 24/7 perp makes a clean band-touch bar observable (no overnight gap past the band); needs a regime/trend feature gate to avoid catching trends (band-walks). This is the strongest new-family candidate from this book.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: ATM (at-the-money) bounce / near-the-money mean reversion
findings.mechanism: strike-anchored mean reversion: price that drifts to the at-the-money region tends to bounce because dealer/structural flows around the strike absorb extremes
findings.setup_summary: Price trading near the at-the-money strike (for perp: a round number / prior-session anchor level) after a drift into overextension bounces back rather than continuing through; enter the bounce at the level with a tight invalidation. Book example: West Texas oil Jan-Feb 2011 bounce.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: drift into the anchor level without a decisive break. Invalidation: close beyond the level by >1 ATR (level broken, thesis dead); strong trend context.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on bar close at/inside the anchor zone; stop beyond the level or 1 ATR; target ~1R back toward the prior range; expiry ~8 bars.
findings.quote: ATM bounce strategy, 140-142; Mean reversion plays, 141
findings.chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 140-142 (ATM bounce strategy, mean reversion plays, West Texas oil examples)
findings.notes: For perp futures the 'strike' anchors to psychological/round levels and prior-session extremes; this is a level-bounce variant, related to but distinct from band-based reversion. Keep as backlog until location feature + level definition formalized.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Breakout plays (range/consolidation break with event catalyst)
findings.mechanism: consolidation break continuation: a decisive break of a range or prior high/low, especially with an event/volume catalyst, continues; failed breaks revert (feeds the existing failed_breakout family)
findings.setup_summary: After sideways consolidation (or pre-event), a close beyond the range extreme with expansion triggers a continuation trade in breakout direction; the book documents FOMC-related breakout plays and lists breakout trades among high-risk performance challenges. Retest of the broken level validates; failure to hold the break = failed breakout (existing SHORT family).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close beyond consolidation extreme. Invalidation: close back inside the range (break failed) or rejection at the broken level = flip to failed_breakout.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after break; stop back inside the range / 1 ATR; target measured move of the range (1R+); expiry tied to event follow-through.
findings.quote: breakout plays, 142-144; FOMC, breakout plays and, 143; breakout trades, 131, 190
findings.chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 131, 142-144, 190 (breakout plays, performance challenges)
findings.notes: Directly refines the existing failed_breakout expert and the breakout_retest backlog family; 24/7 perp means no overnight-gap ambiguity on break bars. Event-catalyzed breakouts (CPI/FOMC) are perp-relevant and tie into the scheduled-event finding.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Volatility/fear index as contrarian indicator
findings.mechanism: fear-extreme contrarian: when a fear/volatility index (VIX; perp analog: DVOL/BVOL or funding-spike gauge) reaches an extreme, the crowd is positioned one way and the underlying tends to reverse rather than continue
findings.setup_summary: When the fear index registers an extreme (very high = capitulation-fear, very low = complacency), fade the extreme: high-fear readings bias LONG reversal, low-fear/extreme-complacency readings bias SHORT. Falsifiable as a threshold regime filter on the fear gauge.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: fear gauge crosses an extreme threshold. Invalidation: fear stays/extends (no reversion within N bars) or underlying makes a new extreme in the fear direction.
findings.risk_geometry: Regime/filter, not a standalone entry: gates direction admission; no direct entry/stop geometry from the book.
findings.quote: VIX index, 109-115; as contrarian indicator, 109; herding behavior, 109; risk aversion, 109
findings.chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 109-115 (VIX as fear index and contrarian indicator)
findings.notes: VIX-as-contrarian is an empirically documented claim; perp analog is a crypto vol index (DVOL/BVOL) or funding-rate extreme gauge. Use as a regime filter in the risk-admission path, not an expert.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Day-of-week risk (weekday edge patterns around weekly expiration)
findings.mechanism: calendar flow rotation: day-of-week microstructure (weekly expiration cycle, weekend behavior) creates systematic weekday-specific edge patterns
findings.setup_summary: The book documents a day-of-week cycle for binary options: contrarian Mondays, ATM Wednesdays, deep-in-the-money Thursdays, very-deep-in-the-money Fridays, Tuesday trade initiation, and 'Missing Monday' as a risk day. Falsifiable as a per-day-of-week conditional filter on entries/expiry selection.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: current weekday matches a documented edge regime. Invalidation: day-of-week effect absent after the weekly cycle shifts (needs periodic re-test).
findings.risk_geometry: Timing filter: which weekday entries/expiries are favored; interacts with weekly expiry in options, not directly transferable to perp expiry (no weekly option expiry for spot perp).
findings.quote: Day of the week risk, 174-176; contrarian Mondays, 175; Missing Monday, 175; at-the-money (ATM) Wednesdays, 175; deep-in-the-money (DITM) Thursdays, 176; very-deep-in-the-money Fridays, 176
findings.chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 174-176 (day of week risk, timing and managing trades)
findings.notes: Derived from binary-option weekly expiration microstructure; perp analog is weekend liquidity/vol thinning and Friday positioning. A weak but falsifiable calendar filter; belongs in the time feature group, gated for re-test since 24/7 perp lacks the weekly expiry driver.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Scheduled data-release / event-risk trades (NFP and macro releases)
findings.mechanism: scheduled-event flow spike: markets price in advance of scheduled high-impact releases and move sharply on surprise vs consensus (consensus error bias), creating anticipatory and post-release flow
findings.setup_summary: Around scheduled high-impact releases (book: NFP, elections, central-bank/FOMC statements; perp analog: CPI, FOMC, jobs), either (a) trade the post-release directional move with defined risk, or (b) blackout/stand aside because surprise risk dominates. Book documents the anticipation phase (170-174) and consensus error bias (169-170).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: scheduled release within N bars / release print differs from consensus. Invalidation: release matches consensus (no surprise -> no edge); position thesis invalidated by the actual print.
findings.risk_geometry: Lifecycle rule: no new entries or size-down during a blackout window around high-impact releases; entries only with tight stop (spike slippage), expiry past the release bar.
findings.quote: Data release trades, 65, 170-172, 190; anticipation of data release, 170-174; consensus error bias, 169-170; NFP report, tactics for trading, 170-171
findings.chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 163-177 (NFP, data release trades, event risk analysis)
findings.notes: Very actionable for 24/7 perp: crypto trades through CPI/FOMC prints (no exchange close to hide in), so an event blackout/size-down lifecycle rule is a high-value, deterministic risk addition. Aligns with V8's no-wall-clock determinism if event times come from the tape, not NOW().
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Correlated vs non-correlated trades (co-movement and diversification)
findings.mechanism: cross-market co-movement: correlated underlying markets move together on shared shocks (S&P/Nikkei co-move on the 2011 earthquake; Shanghai selloff hits AUD/USD), so correlated directional bets stack risk and non-correlated trades diversify it
findings.setup_summary: The book shows markets co-move on shared macro shocks and argues for choosing non-correlated trades to spread risk. V8 translation: BTC/ETH correlated directional exposures (or BTC vs NASDAQ/BTC vs gold) count as one effective exposure; cap correlated exposure so two correlated experts do not stack to twice the intended heat.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: two active exposures on correlated instruments with the same direction. Invalidation: realized correlation breaks (correlation regime change) - monitored, not a trade signal.
findings.risk_geometry: Risk-rule geometry: correlated_exposure_cap in the RiskGate - one effective exposure per direction across correlated instruments; no direct entry/stop geometry.
findings.quote: correlation trades, 156-158; Noncorrelated trades, 158-159; Nikkei and S&P 500 Co-Movement in Reaction to Earthquake, 148, 149
findings.chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 148-159 (surprise event risks, correlation trades, non-correlated trades)
findings.notes: Directly supports a correlated_exposure_cap risk rule across BTC/ETH/alt perps; cross_market feature group exists in V8 vocabulary. This is a risk-management finding more than a signal.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Candlestick reversal/hesitation patterns (hammer, engulfing, doji, spinning tops, tweezers)
findings.mechanism: reversal-candle context: specific candle shapes (hammer, engulfing, tweezers) after a trend, and hesitation candles (doji, spinning tops) at structure, mark potential reversal or pause points
findings.setup_summary: Candle patterns alone are weak standalone signals; the book treats them as context/confirmation (hammer at support after a down-move, doji inside a triangle showing hesitation). V8 translation: candle-shape features (hammer/engulfing/doji at key levels) as confirmation inputs to existing experts, not new standalone experts.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pattern appears at a significant level in the expected context. Invalidation: pattern fails (close through the pattern extreme); context (level, trend) absent.
findings.risk_geometry: Feature-input only: adds confirmation strength to existing families; no own risk geometry.
findings.quote: Hammer (candle pattern), 71; Engulfing candles (candle pattern), 73; Spinning tops (candle pattern), 72; Tweezers (candle pattern), 73; Doji (candle pattern), 80; doji shows hesitation, 92
findings.chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 69-73, 80, 90-93 (candlestick patterns, hesitation patterns)
findings.notes: Candle shapes are cheap, deterministic features computable from the 1h bar. Low standalone edge; best used to strengthen the still_valid/confirmation path of existing experts rather than as a new family.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Fibonacci resistance/retracement levels (incl. at data releases)
findings.mechanism: retracement-level anchoring: price reacts to Fibonacci retracement/resistance levels (38.2/50/61.8 of a swing), pausing or reversing there; the book applies Fibonacci levels to data-release trades
findings.setup_summary: Draw Fibonacci retracement/resistance levels from a completed swing; expect reaction (pause or reversal) at the 38.2/50/61.8 levels; the book documents Fibonacci resistance lines and a Fibonacci strategy used around data-release trades (pp. 94-96, 172-174). V8 translation: fib levels as location features (distance-to-fib-level) for existing level-reaction families.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price at a fib level with context. Invalidation: decisive close through the level (level broken, re-draw or reject).
findings.risk_geometry: Feature-input: fib levels as location features; no standalone risk geometry in the book.
findings.quote: Fibonacci resistance lines, 84, 94-96; Fibonacci strategy, data release trades and, 172-174
findings.chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 84, 94-96, 172-174 (Fibonacci resistance, Fibonacci strategy at data releases)
findings.notes: Fib levels are deterministic and computable from swing extremes; they fit the location feature group and could enrich the failed_breakout / breakout_retest families. Weak standalone; better as a level-set definition.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Triangle/compression with hesitation (doji) before breakout
findings.mechanism: compression-energy accumulation: consolidation (triangles: symmetrical/descending/equilateral) with hesitation candles (doji, spinning tops) compresses range and energy, setting up an expansion/breakout; doji after a move shows hesitation before continuation or reversal
findings.setup_summary: Detect a triangular/range compression (declining range width over N bars) with hesitation candles inside; the compression resolves with an expansion breakout. Falsifiable: range-width compression quantified by ATR/range percentile, then breakout direction. Book: triangles + doji hesitation patterns (pp. 89-93), including parabolic patterns warning.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: compression state detected (range/volatility contraction). Invalidation: range expands without a directional break, or false break flips to failed_breakout logic.
findings.risk_geometry: Compression is a pre-breakout state feature; entry follows the existing breakout family (close beyond compression extreme); stop inside the compression; target measured move.
findings.quote: Triangles, 89-90; triangle and [doji], 90-93; Hesitation patterns, 90-93; Parabolic patterns, 93
findings.chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 88-93 (patterns for trading analysis, triangles, hesitation patterns)
findings.notes: Range compression is highly measurable on 24/7 perp (no gaps disrupt the compression); feeds the breakout/breakout_retest families as a precondition detector. Strong backlog candidate, corroborated across the library.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Lot-size / loss-streak discipline: rule of three, offsetting trades, leverage control
findings.mechanism: fixed-fraction discipline: cap per-trade and per-streak risk (rule of three: after three losing trades, stop or reduce), size lots so a single day cannot inflict unacceptable damage, use offsetting trades to hedge, and treat leverage/margin as risk amplifiers
findings.setup_summary: Deterministic risk rules: (1) rule of three - consecutive-loss cap that pauses/reduces after 3 losses; (2) lot-size management so max single-day loss is bounded; (3) offsetting trades as hedge; (4) explicit leverage/margin awareness. V8 translation: RiskGate heat cap + loss-streak circuit-breaker + position sizing bound.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 3 consecutive losing episodes or per-day heat cap hit. Invalidation: N/A (risk rules; re-arm after reset condition defined in the rule).
findings.risk_geometry: RiskGate rule: heat cap, max drawdown bound, consecutive-loss circuit breaker; interacts with the one-exposure-per-direction invariant.
findings.quote: Rule of three, 181-182; Lot size management, 181-182; Offsetting trades, 182-183; Leverage and margin, 183; Losing streaks, 4, 188
findings.chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 179-183 (risk management, rule of three, lot size, leverage and margin)
findings.notes: High-leverage 24/7 perp makes loss-streak and heat-cap discipline critical; the rule-of-three circuit breaker is a simple deterministic RiskGate addition corroborated across the trading literature.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: Put/call ratio as contrarian sentiment/positioning gauge
findings.mechanism: positioning-extreme contrarian: extreme put/call ratios (heavy bearish options positioning) mark contrarian-bullish conditions and extreme call-heavy readings mark complacency/contrarian-bearish conditions
findings.setup_summary: Track sector/index put/call ratios as a positioning gauge; extreme readings are contrarian signals. Perp analog: funding rate + open interest positioning as the perp-native crowd-positioning gauge (heavy long positioning via high positive funding = contrarian-short; flush to negative funding = contrarian-long).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: positioning gauge crosses an extreme threshold. Invalidation: positioning stays/extends (no mean reversion of the gauge within N bars).
findings.risk_geometry: Feature/filter input; no own entry geometry - feeds a regime filter or confirmation for direction.
findings.quote: Put/call ratios, 115-117; Sector put/call ratios, 115-117; Fear and Greed index, 115
findings.chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 115-117 (put/call ratios, option volatility and sentiment)
findings.notes: The options put/call ratio maps imperfectly to perp (no put/call tape), but funding rate + OI is the perp-native positioning gauge with the same contrarian logic; fund-flow group already in vocabulary. Keep as feature input; the contrarian claim is falsifiable on funding extremes.
findings.book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

findings.strategy_name: QMAC moving-average queue alignment trend filter
findings.mechanism: a trend is only trustworthy when price and its moving averages fall in strict sequential order of alignment; any rally/retracement that occurs while the averages are out of sequence is expected to be short-lived
findings.setup_summary: On a fixed timeframe compute a stacked set of MAs (book uses 50/90/200-day; short set 5/5/13). Bullish regime = close above shortest MA above next above longest (positive queue); bearish = exact reverse. Entry only when price and MAs are sequentially aligned after a disorderly phase; when averages are NOT in queue order, do not trust counter-trend rallies/corrections to persist (stand aside or treat as short-lived). Falsifiable: after a disorderly-alignment rally, price reverts within the swing horizon more often than after a queued-alignment rally.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = full positive/negative queue established; thesis invalidated when any MA breaks out of sequential order (e.g. 50-day crossing back below 90-day while queue was positive) or price closes through the shortest MA against the queue.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on bar close after queue confirmed; book gives no numeric stop but states longer-term MAs mark probable support/resistance zones usable to compute risk/reward against entries.
findings.quote: whether the outlook of the market is bullish or bearish, price and its various multiple averages should fall in an orderly alignment
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 2 'Price and Moving Averages'; Ch 6 'Queuing Theory of Moving Average Crossovers (QMAC)'
findings.notes: Core regime concept of the book; no optimization claimed ('parameters ... are not optimized'). Works on any continuous timeframe; 24/7 crypto has no session alignment to distort MA stacks. Natural V8 use: marketstate trend-alignment feature gating all entries.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: higher-timeframe trend gating ('look at the weekly, trade on the daily')
findings.mechanism: trades executed on the daily time frame have higher win probability when the next-higher time frame (weekly) is trending in the same direction and is not overbought
findings.setup_summary: Before any daily entry check the weekly chart: (1) weekly momentum not overbought and not bearish, (2) weekly price vs moving averages at a support level gaining strength, (3) daily momentum shows a bullish reversal. Enter daily trades only when weekly and daily trend in tandem; all entries/exits executed from daily patterns. Falsifiable: daily signals taken while weekly momentum is bearish or overbought underperform daily signals taken in weekly alignment.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = daily bullish reversal while weekly trend positive; invalidated when weekly momentum turns bearish/overbought or weekly price closes below its supporting MA.
findings.risk_geometry: In worked example: entry at next trading day open (or next bar close), protective stop at low of preceding bar, target sized to 3:1 reward/risk against weekly support/resistance, swing holding period of weeks.
findings.quote: The rule is to trade in the trending direction of the next higher time frame of the daily price, that is, weekly
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7 'Trade on Daily Signals'; Ch 2 'Combining the Four Dimensions'
findings.notes: Maps directly to V8 lifecycle gating (trade only in direction of higher-timeframe regime) and to the one-exposure-per-direction rule. On BTCUSDT 1h the analogous stack would be 1h vs 4h/1D.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: ADX trend-strength regime with peak-turn warning
findings.mechanism: rising ADX indicates trend strengthening, a declining ADX indicates weakening trend, and a downward turn in ADX from an extreme peak presages a change in price trend
findings.setup_summary: Use 14-period ADX as a regime filter: ADX crossing above ~20 = trending market (directional, either way); crossing below 20 = non-trending. Watch for ADX making an extreme high and turning down - this implies a change of trend strength and therefore a probable price-trend/direction change soon. Falsifiable: after ADX turns down from a multi-week peak, price trend direction changes within the next several bars more often than a baseline.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = ADX turns down from a high; invalidated if ADX resumes making new highs (trend strength restored).
findings.risk_geometry: Filter/regime only; book explicitly warns ADX 'should not be used as a buy or sell signal' and lags by about 30 bars to establish.
findings.quote: The turning of direction in the ADX implies that there is going to be a change of trend strength
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'Average Direction Index'
findings.notes: Book recommends using a short ADX period and focusing on its peak turning points, and pairs it with the 50/90/200 MA stack (Ch 6 Fig 6.17).
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: ATR-multiple protective/trailing stop
findings.mechanism: stop distance is scaled to volatility via average true range, and the stop ratchets up (long) using the highest-high of the stop value over a lookback so it can never loosen
findings.setup_summary: Long: stop_line = close - AtrX*ATR(period) with example AtrX=1.3, period=13; take HHV(stop_line, 13) as the active stop so it ratchets. Exit when price closes below the stop line; for a long position a close above/at the stop line may also justify entry if other indicators support the trend. Falsifiable: in choppy regimes too-close ATR stops trigger early; in strong trends too-far stops fail to lock profit - the correct ATR multiple is regime-dependent.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trailing stop is always active; ratchet prevents loosening.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop = close - ATR multiple, ratcheted via HHV lookback; exit on bar close below stop; stops act as last-resort exits ('protective stops').
findings.quote: Average true range is commonly used in the calculation of protective stops (or stop losses)
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'Protective Stops' (formula given: AtrX=1.3, Period=13, Lookback=13)
findings.notes: Directly maps to V8 risk_geometry atr_ref stops; 24/7 crypto means stops can trigger at any hour and ATR scaling is critical because vol is regime-heavy.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: minimum 3:1 reward-to-risk gate and per-position risk cap
findings.mechanism: taking trades only when expected reward is at least three times the possible loss, and risking a bounded fraction of portfolio per position, preserves capital so that the trend edge compounds
findings.setup_summary: For every candidate setup, measure the stop distance (risk) and target distance (reward) against the next-higher-timeframe support/resistance; require reward >= 3x risk before entering (worked example: a 1:3 ratio was rejected as 'no new position'). Cap per-position risk between 1% and 5% of portfolio value. Falsifiable: trades accepted with reward:risk < 3 underperform accepted trades on realized R-multiples.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Gate condition; trade skipped when the ratio fails regardless of signal quality.
findings.risk_geometry: Reward/risk computed from entry, stop, and target; 3:1 used because HK equities 'tend to go into consolidation after a rise of 30 percent' (30% reward vs 10% risk).
findings.quote: Many professional traders do not take a trade unless the potential profit is at least three times greater than the possible loss
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8 'Risk Management'; Ch 7 'Trade on Daily Signals'
findings.notes: Maps to V8 RiskGate admission logic; 3:1 is a heuristic floor, not an edge claim.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: volume-trend confirmation and price-volume divergence warning
findings.mechanism: volume expanding with price confirms trend; price rising on falling volume signals weakening; price falling on rising volume signals more decline; volume on breakout separates true from false breakouts
findings.setup_summary: Compare price trend to volume trend using fast/slow volume averages (book: 2-day vs 10-day). Uptrend valid while volume expands with rising price; expanding range + rising volume = aggressive continuation; contracting range with unimpressive volume = vulnerable to reversal; a narrow-range stall on heavy volume marks strong support/resistance. VZO variant: positive/negative volume flow, above 50% = positive; cross above 30% = entry signal, cross below 70% = exit signal. Falsifiable: breakouts accompanied by volume above its recent average outperform breakouts without it.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Price-volume divergence (price advancing while volume trend declining) invalidates continuation.
findings.risk_geometry: Confirmation/filter only; 'a single volume bar by itself will not be meaningful' - must be read against recent history.
findings.quote: we want to see good volume on a breakout as confirmation of the entry/exit signals and to distinguish a true breakout from a false breakout
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 2 'Volume'; Ch 5 'Reading Volume' and 'Money-Flow Indicator'
findings.notes: Crypto perp venues report volume but wash-trading can inflate it; use venue-quality caveat and prefer notional volume.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: classic and hidden price-momentum divergence
findings.mechanism: momentum oscillator failing to confirm price reveals hidden strength/weakness: classic divergence precedes reversal, hidden divergence (in trend direction) signals continuation and re-entry
findings.setup_summary: Track a momentum oscillator (book uses ROC-type 10/21-period) against price. Bullish divergence: price makes a lower low while oscillator makes a higher low (accumulation) -> buy at oversold. Bearish divergence: price higher high, oscillator lower high -> sell. Hidden bullish: in an uptrend correction, price higher low while oscillator lower low = underlying strength, re-entry. Hidden bearish: in a downtrend, price lower high while oscillator higher high = exit. Multiple concurrent divergences strengthen the signal. Falsifiable: after a divergence is completed, price reverses from the extreme within the swing horizon more often than after no divergence.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = divergence completed at an oscillator extreme; invalidated if the oscillator confirms price on the next swing (no divergence).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on confirmation of reversal; stop beyond the extreme pivot; divergence warns of trend change but 'does not necessarily take place at the exact turning point'.
findings.quote: The more divergences that are occurring, the more significant they become
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3 'Divergence Patterns'; Ch 6 'Momentum Oscillator'
findings.notes: Divergence detection is computable on 1h crypto bars; hidden-divergence continuation variant is the less-crowded edge candidate.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: long-MA-slope-filtered crossover (Edwards & Magee Eight Rules)
findings.mechanism: crossover signals between a fast and slow MA are only reliable when the slower MA is flat or turning in the new direction; a cross against a steeply sloped longer MA is a false signal
findings.setup_summary: Buy when price or the 50-day average penetrates the 200-day average on the upside AND the 200-day is flattening or rising (Eight Rule 1/5 adapted); sell on the mirror downside penetration with the 200-day flattening or falling. Worked counter-example: two identical 50>200 Golden Crosses on the Shanghai index - the first (200-day flat/rounding) produced a bull run, the second (200-day in steep straight decline, MAs not queued, bearish diagonal) reversed the next day. Falsifiable: crossovers executed with the longer MA in steep adverse slope lose more than those with a flat/turning longer MA.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Longer MA slope does not confirm the cross direction (steep in the opposite direction) or price retraces >61.8% of the prior decline at the cross.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on cross confirmation (bar close); stop at the recent swing; target at structure; a buffer (e.g. 57.5% line, or 10% band) can be used to avoid whipsaws.
findings.quote: when the 50-day average crosses with the 200-day average, it is important to note the direction and slope of the 200-day average also
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'Queuing Theory of Moving Average Crossovers' (Eight Rules; Golden/Dead Cross)
findings.notes: Concrete falsifiable refinement of a moving_average_cross family: add longer-MA slope as a validity condition; rescales to 1h BTC (e.g. 50/200 on hourly bars).
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: Fibonacci retracement/projection support-resistance
findings.mechanism: price tends to retrace or rebound to Fibonacci ratios of the prior swing, and clusters of projection lines mark stronger support/resistance; the 50% level acts as a gravity zone
findings.setup_summary: After a significant swing, mark retracement levels 23.6/38.2/50/61.8/78.6 of that swing; expect price to hold at the first test of each level (book Fig 4.29 shows a rebound at every first test). Use Fibonacci projections (61.8/100/161.8/200/238.2 of Wave A/B swings) and treat areas where multiple projection lines cluster as stronger SR. Falsifiable: first-touch reaction at a fib level (measured as a multi-bar reversal) occurs more often than chance.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A close through the level with increased volume voids the level (support/resistance flip).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the fib level; stop beyond the level; targets at the next cluster of projections.
findings.quote: at every first test of prices at these support levels, prices make a rebound
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 4 'Fibonacci Retracement and Projection' and 'Appendix: Ratios and Wave Relationship'
findings.notes: Self-fulfilling component (many traders use the same levels); crypto reacts to round/psychological numbers, so stickiness is plausible but needs evidence-gated testing.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: neckline/range breakout patterns with volume and measured target
findings.mechanism: a break of a structural neckline or range boundary with volume activates a reversal/continuation, and the broken level becomes support/resistance on retest; target is a measured projection
findings.setup_summary: Double top: two peaks; activated when price declines below the low between the tops; target = distance from the high point to the neckline projected downward. Double bottom: must close above the intervening high point before acting; target projected upward by the same distance. Head and shoulders: complete when price breaks the neckline (line across the two troughs) with volume sharply higher on the break; target = head-to-neckline distance projected from breakout. Rectangle/box: consolidation between parallel support/resistance; breakout with volume = trend in breakout direction; pattern not complete until the breakout occurs; post-break the neckline becomes support (bullish) or resistance (bearish). Falsifiable: a neckline break with above-average volume follows through to the measured target more often than a break on weak volume.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Price re-enters the pattern/back above the neckline after a bearish break (or below after bullish) - pattern fails.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on neckline break (bar close); stop inside the pattern or just beyond the neckline; target = measured head-to-neckline / height-of-range projection; volume on breakout is the key confirmation.
findings.quote: A head and shoulders pattern is completed when prices break below the neckline
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3 'M and W Patterns', 'Head and Shoulders Patterns', 'Rectangle Patterns', 'Saucer Patterns'
findings.notes: Pattern labeling has subjectivity; the falsifiable core is 'breakout with volume + measured target + broken-level retest' which is computable with windowed extremes.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: two-bar candlestick reversals at oscillator extremes
findings.mechanism: single candles are meaningless; two-or-more-candle confirmation at overbought/oversold extremes flags reversals, and breakouts from these patterns are typically short-lived (~10 trading days)
findings.setup_summary: At momentum extremes (oscillator overbought/oversold), a bullish engulfing, harami, hammer, or piercing line after a downtrend = buy setup; bearish engulfing, dark cloud cover, hangman, or evening star after an uptrend = sell setup. Hammer with a long lower shadow at the low of a long downtrend is the most dependable; confirm with the next bar (strong open/gap up) before entry. Harami: follow the break when the previous day's high/low is exceeded. 'A breakout from an engulfing pattern generally is short term, lasting no longer than 10 trading days.' Falsifiable: two-bar reversal patterns appearing at oscillator-extreme after a trend produce a reversal within 1-3 bars more often than the same patterns in mid-range conditions.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Next-bar action fails to confirm direction (e.g. hammer followed by a down close).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on next-bar confirmation close; stop below the pattern extreme (shadow low); horizon ~10 bars for engulfing breakouts.
findings.quote: Hammer with a long shadow shows that the bears have failed to push price lower and is more reliable, especially when its shadow is much longer than its body
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3 'Candlestick Patterns' (cites Caginalp & Laurent 1996 'The Predictive Power of Price Patterns')
findings.notes: 1h crypto candles are standard; the 'extremes + two-bar confirmation + short horizon' structure is a well-scoped candidate family distinct from existing V8 experts.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: lunar-phase buy-sell cycle (new moon buy, full moon sell)
findings.mechanism: the first half of the lunar month is an accumulation phase and the second half a distribution phase; index returns are systematically higher from new moon to full moon than the reverse
findings.setup_summary: Buy at the new moon (Sun-Moon 0-degree conjunction) and sell at the next full moon (180-degree opposition, ~14-16 days). Cited RBS study: FTSE new->full moon trading turned GBP 1,000 (1984) into GBP 12,116 vs GBP 5,130 buy-hold; DAX/HSI 'even more profitable'; S&P higher since 1928. Mikula backtest: new-moon entry + full-moon exit combined with stochastic on soybean futures, 44 trades, 66% profitable (longs 54%, shorts 88%). Book advises using it only as a filter: buy when the new moon coincides with a technical buy (e.g. stochastic < 20), sell when the full moon coincides with a technical sell (stochastic > 80), and stand aside otherwise. Falsifiable: the new->full moon half-period of the synodic month has positive average return vs the full->new half.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Lunar timing 'can become a trap if the market enters a bear phase'; if no accumulation occurs in the first half of the lunar month, treat as a larger-trend change warning.
findings.risk_geometry: Fixed ~14-16 day swing hold; protective stops via technical analysis; book says 'the intention is not to trade on the basis of moon-phased buy-sell signals only'.
findings.quote: buying FTSE on the new moon and selling on the full moon, this would result in GBP12,116 overall figure for the same period
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 9 'Using Lunar Cycles in Trading'; Ch 2 'Financial Astrology'
findings.notes: Secondhand bank-report correlation, no controlled test; V8 forbids wall-clock in replay and the claim is equity-index based, so it is gated on a calendar/cycle feature group with low prior. Lunar phase is computable from bar date metadata if ever admitted.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012
