findings.strategy_name: Fade the Break (false-break candle at support/resistance)
findings.mechanism: A wick through a level that fails to hold on close is an institutional trap that catches retail breakout traders (liquidity-vacuum reentry), so the reclaiming close predicts reversal back inside the level.
findings.setup_summary: On M15/M30, identify a clear support/resistance level (at least two touches). A candle's wick pierces the level but closes back on the inside (bull candle above support / bear candle below resistance) = false-break candle. Enter at the opening of the next candle in the reclaim direction; stop 5 pips beyond the false-break candle's extreme; two targets at 1:1 and 1:2 R.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the candle closes beyond the level (genuine close-through, not a wick) or no candle forms a wick-through-reclaim; dead thesis if price closes decisively through the level on a subsequent candle or the 5-pip-beyond-extreme stop is hit.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry next-bar-open; stop 5 pips beyond the false-break candle high/low; dual targets 1R and 2R; no expiry stated (intraday M15/M30 day-trade profile).
findings.quote: Markets often reverse after a failure to break above the resistance level or below the support level. ... the failure is characterized by the shadow of the candle that goes above the resistance level but fails to close above it.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, Strategy 3 'Fade the Break', pp. 126-131
findings.notes: Refines the existing V8 failed_breakout expert (currently SHORT-only, windowed-prior-high basis) to both directions and pins the setup: false-break candle definition (wick through, close reclaim), next-bar entry, and stop 5 pips beyond the candle extreme. In 24/7 perps with no gaps, wick-through-reclaim is cleaner than in FX; the S/R level maps to a frozen windowed-prior-high ref.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Trade the Break (close-confirmed breakout with range-fraction stop)
findings.mechanism: A close beyond a range boundary confirms momentum has resolved the supply/demand imbalance; counter-moves against a fresh breakout retrace at most partway into the prior range, so the stop can sit inside the range at a fixed fraction of its height.
findings.setup_summary: On M15/M30, define support/resistance with at least two touches each side. Wait for a candle that CLOSES above resistance (long) or below support (short) - the breakout candle. Enter at the opening of the next candle. Stop at the 60% mark of the prior range measured from the broken level (e.g., 41-pip range -> stop 25 pips beyond resistance); two targets at 1:1 and 1:2 R.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No trade on a wick-only touch (close-based confirmation required); trade invalid if the computed stop lands inside the wrong geometry; dead thesis if price closes back inside the prior range.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry next-bar-open after breakout close; stop at 60%-of-range mark beyond the broken level; dual targets 1R and 2R; no expiry stated (intraday M15/M30).
findings.quote: When prices close above resistance, that candle is called the breakout candle. ... The stop loss is placed below the midpoint of the prior range because we do not expect prices to fall back below that point.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, Strategy 4 'Trade the Break', pp. 131-137
findings.notes: Feeds the DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family. The 60%-of-range stop geometry is a concrete, deterministic stop rule (book text slightly inconsistent: concept says 'below the midpoint', setup says 60% mark - pin to the setup). Close-based confirmation distinguishes it from failed_breakout; both strategies are designed to work 'hand in hand' (take a trade regardless of market direction).
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Piranha (Bollinger band-touch mean reversion, range regime)
findings.mechanism: In a range regime, price touching a band extreme reverts toward the mean; the tight stop loss doubles as the regime detector - a stopped-out trade signals the range thesis failed and a trend is starting.
findings.setup_summary: On M5 GBP/USD, long when price touches the lower Bollinger band (MA12, dev 2), short when it touches the upper band; stop 10 pips, target 5 pips (2:1 risk-to-reward, so viability hinges on a high win rate). Do not trade during major U.S./U.K. news releases. If stopped, the book's rule is to look for the next trade in the opposite direction (a stopped range trade implies a trend started).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid in trending regimes (book: strategy 'fails badly when the market goes into a strong trend'); hitting the 10-pip stop invalidates the range thesis; avoid major news windows.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on band touch (market); stop 10 pips; target 5 pips (unfavorable 2:1 risk:reward); expiry: scalper holds minutes; ~15-20 opportunities/day.
findings.quote: Long trades are taken when market prices touch the bottom band; short trades are taken when market prices touch the upper band.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, Strategy 2 'Piranha', pp. 118-124
findings.notes: M5 scalping with 5-pip targets is dominated by taker fees and 8-hour funding in perps; the band-mean-reversion mechanism is more viable at H1+. Two transferable pieces: (1) explicit regime dependence (range-only, requires a regime filter), (2) the post-stop direction flip as a regime-change signal.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Trend Bouncer (Bollinger-band pullback in trend)
findings.mechanism: Trends move in waves; a pullback that retraces to the mean of the recent wave (Bollinger center MA12) after a band-extension offers an entry with the trend at better price, with the outer dev-4 band as a volatility-scaled stop.
findings.setup_summary: On H1/H4, when price hits the upper Bollinger band (MA12, dev 2) in an uptrend and then pulls back to touch the center MA12, go long at the MA12 touch; stop at the lower band of the dev-4 Bollinger set; three targets at 1:1, 1:2, 1:3 R. Symmetric short for the lower band (example: NZD/USD H1 short, risk 46 pips / reward 138 pips).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if price never reaches the dev-2 band (no momentum-wave confirmation) or never retraces to the center; stopped if the opposite dev-4 band is breached (wave deeper than expected); dead thesis if price closes beyond the band structure.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at center MA12 touch (market); stop at opposite dev-4 band (volatility-scaled, analogous to atr_ref); laddered targets 1R/2R/3R; expiry: swing 2-5 days.
findings.quote: When the candlestick hits the upper band of Bollinger Bands (MA 12, Dev 2), it indicates an upward momentum, and we prepare to go long. As prices retrace back to the MA 12 (the center line of the Bollinger Bands), a significant retracement has occurred, and it is a good time to enter for a long trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Strategy 8 'Trend Bouncer', pp. 163-169
findings.notes: A volatility-anchored variant of the existing trend_pullback expert: entry trigger is the band-extension-then-mean pullback rather than ema_fast>ema_slow; the dev-4-band stop is a deterministic volatility-scaled stop. Laddered 1R/2R/3R targets are a lifecycle (partial-target) variant distinct from trend_pullback's single 1R target.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Trend Rider (EMA cross with ADX momentum-exhaustion exit)
findings.mechanism: A fast/slow EMA cross detects an early momentum change; trend strength (ADX) rising above a threshold then collapsing marks exhaustion, so the profit exit is a momentum-decay event rather than a price target, letting winners run (book example shows a 1:5.4 R trade).
findings.setup_summary: On H1/H4, long when EMA12 crosses above EMA36, then enter when price pulls back to touch EMA12; stop at EMA36 (minimum 30 pips from entry); NO fixed profit target; exit when ADX14 rises above 40 and then falls back below 40. Symmetric short on the downside cross (example: AUD/USD H1, risk 38 pips / reward 155 pips).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Entry skipped if price never returns to EMA12 (momentum runs without a pullback); stopped if EMA36 (or 30-pip minimum) is breached; the ADX-above-40-then-below event is the only profit exit.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at EMA12 touch after cross; stop at EMA36, min 30 pips; no fixed target - exit on ADX 40 round-trip; expiry: swing 2-5 days.
findings.quote: Once the ADX crosses above 40 and comes back below, it is telling us that the momentum is losing steam and it's time to exit the trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Strategy 7 'Trend Rider', pp. 155-163
findings.notes: Distinct from trend_pullback and trend_bouncer because there is NO fixed target: the exit is a momentum-decay event (ADX>40 then <40), which maps to a new behavior family (adx_exhaustion_exit) under a trend-exhaustion mechanism. Book's stated rationale: retail traders exit too early; targetless exits keep riders on the 1:5+ R trades. Book claims 'trend following is statistically valid' but offers no statistics - DESIGN_INFERENCE.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Fifth Element (MACD histogram momentum confirmation)
findings.mechanism: A MACD histogram sign flip indicates a momentum shift; requiring five consecutive same-sign histogram bars filters whipsaw sign flips and confirms the shift is sustained before entry, with a known future entry time (the 5th bar).
findings.setup_summary: On H1/H4, after the MT4 MACD histogram switches from negative to positive, wait for four positive bars and enter long at the opening of the fifth bar; stop at the last low of the histogram (the last high for shorts); two targets at 1:1 and 1:2 R. Symmetric for short (example: EUR/USD H4, risk 147 pips / reward 294 pips).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the histogram flips sign again before five bars accumulate (count resets - no trade); stopped if the last-histogram-extreme is breached; dead thesis if histogram sign reverts after entry.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry next-bar-open on the 5th histogram bar; stop at the last swing extreme of the histogram (last low for longs); dual targets 1R/2R; expiry: swing.
findings.quote: We wait for five positive bars on the histogram to confirm the momentum before entering a long trade on the fifth bar.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Strategy 9 'Fifth Element', pp. 169-177
findings.notes: The five-bar count is a deterministic anti-whipsaw confirmation and gives a scheduled future entry time (5th bar = 5h on H1), attractive for low-monitoring mechanical execution. Must pin the indicator definition: the book uses the MT4 MACD histogram (raw EMA12-EMA26 line), not the traditional histogram (MACD line - signal). Computable from OHLC.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Power Ranger (trend-gated stochastic range trade)
findings.mechanism: In a range forming after a trend, the stochastic locates the range extremes; gating the extreme trade by prevailing momentum (buy oversold only in uptrends) avoids fading the trend - the book's explicit warning against trading stochastic extremes without the gate.
findings.setup_summary: On H1/H4, draw the prevailing trend line. In an uptrend, wait for stochastic %K and %D (10,3,3) to fall below 20, then go long when they cross back above 20; in a downtrend, go short when they exceed 80 then cross back below. First target at the 75% mark of the range, second beyond the range (breakout anticipation); the stop is sized at 1:1 R to the first target and MUST fall beyond the range extreme or the trade is declared invalid.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trade invalid if the computed stop does not sit beyond the range extreme (support for longs / resistance for shorts); never trade the stochastic extreme against the trend direction; dead thesis if the range breaks.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on stochastic cross back out of the extreme zone (20/80); stop = 1:1 R to first target and must clear the range extreme; two targets (75% of range, then range extension); expiry: swing.
findings.quote: Always determine the momentum of the market first before deciding whether to look for the overbought or oversold region of the stochastic. In an uptrend, look for the oversold region.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Strategy 10 'Power Ranger', pp. 177-185
findings.notes: The transferable insight is the trend gate: buying oversold in a downtrend 'can be risky' (the book names it as the failure mode of naive stochastic trading). The second target beyond the range anticipates breakout, combining range fade with a breakout continuation in one position.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: The Pendulum (range-fraction mean reversion)
findings.mechanism: Range price oscillates around a midpoint under a mean-restoring force; entering only after price has turned back 10% of the range from the extreme avoids catching a falling knife and gives objective 50%/90% exit zones.
findings.setup_summary: On H1/H4, define a range from at least two confirmed support/resistance touches. Enter long when price bounces off support and has retraced 10% of the range back up (short when it turns 10% down from resistance); targets at the 50% and 90% marks of the range; stop at 1:1 R from entry. Example: AUD/USD H4, 269-pip range, enter 27 pips above support, targets 135 and 243 pips above support.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the range breaks before the 10% turn trigger fires (pendulum 'string snaps' - momentum wins); stop = 1:1 R; dead thesis if price closes through support/resistance.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the 10%-of-range turn confirmation (market); stop at 1:1 R (e.g., 108 pips in example); targets at 50% and 90% of range; expiry: swing.
findings.quote: We do this by executing a trade only at the 10% mark after prices turn back from either support or resistance. The first target is set at the 50% mark of the range, and the second target is set at the 90% mark of the range.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Strategy 11 'The Pendulum', pp. 185-190
findings.notes: Fully parameterized range fade (10%/50%/90% fraction geometry) - easy to encode deterministically with frozen range refs. Complements Power Ranger (early range formation) vs Pendulum (formed range); the two are designed to run together across a range's lifecycle. Stop is R-based (1:1 to first target), matching V8 risk_geometry conventions.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Gawk and Balk the Talk (Rule of 20 news-surprise trading)
findings.mechanism: Traders price expectations, not prints; only a news surprise large enough to breach the forecast-error band (20% of the forecast, or 20bp for rates / 50bp for PMI) changes positioning, so price moves in the direction of the surprise.
findings.setup_summary: On M15/M30 around the top scheduled macro releases (NFP, CPI, rate decisions, GDP, trade balance, PMI, retail sales), compare actual vs forecast. If actual exceeds forecast by >=20% (20bp rates / 50bp PMI), go long the affected currency pair (direction depends on whether the currency is base or counter); if actual falls short by >=20%, go short. Stop 20 pips, target 40 pips (1:2 R).
findings.trigger_invalidation: No trade if the deviation is under the 20% threshold; stop 20 pips; trade only on the named high-impact releases (color-coded red flags on the economic calendar).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the news-release candle (market, after the print); stop 20 pips; target 40 pips (1:2 R); expiry: intraday.
findings.quote: The Rule of 20 states: If the deviation between the actual and forecasted figures exceeds 20%, trade in the direction of the deviation.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, 'Trading the News' + Strategies 5 & 6 'Gawk the Talk' / 'Balk the Talk', pp. 138-153
findings.notes: The 20% deviation threshold is a concrete, falsifiable surprise filter, and BTC perp is macro-sensitive (US CPI/NFP/FOMC). Requires an economic calendar with forecast/actual series - a data prerequisite (analogous to the DATA_BLOCKED state until that exists). 'Traders trade based on expectations' is the stated mechanism. Event timestamps keep the design deterministic (no wall clock needed in replay).
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Swap and Fly (carry with break-even stop)
findings.mechanism: Holding a position in the direction of a positive interest-rate differential accrues swap daily; once the trade moves 1R, shifting the stop to break-even converts it into a risk-free swap accumulator whose P&L turns positive purely from the accrual.
findings.setup_summary: On D1/W1, select the pair with the highest positive swap in the trade direction (book: long AUD/JPY, short GBP/AUD on FXPRIMUS). Enter at the opening of the next candle after a three-white-soldiers (long) or three-black-crows (short) pattern; stop at the recent significant low/high; once the trade reaches 1:1 R, shift the stop to break-even; hold until stopped, accruing swap daily (example: AUD/JPY long accrued 302 pips of swap over 36 weeks). Optional full exit at a minimum 1:3 R.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Stopped at the significant swing before reaching 1:1 R (no break-even shift); the carry accrual is the thesis, so it fails if swap/funding direction reverts (book: swap 'moves in tandem with central banks' rates').
findings.risk_geometry: Entry next-bar-open after 3-candle pattern; stop at recent significant swing; dynamic stop shift to break-even at 1R; no fixed target (swap accumulation); expiry: weeks-months.
findings.quote: The swap and fly strategy is a slow but steady technique that helps you to accumulate interest every day. You can even come out with a positive return after a period of time, even though the trade exits at breakeven.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, Strategy 12 'Swap and Fly', pp. 192-199
findings.notes: The break-even stop shift at 1R is the transferable lifecycle rule (consistent with V8's separation of stops vs dead-thesis exits). In crypto perps the analog is funding, but funding settles every 8h, is frequently negative for longs in BTC, and has no central-bank persistence - so this is NOT the same edge; a crypto funding_carry expert is data-blocked until funding data exists and would need an inverted-direction handling.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Guppy Burst (quiet-window range breakout with dual pending orders)
findings.mechanism: After the US close, liquidity thins and price compresses into a tight range; the subsequent Asia-open breakout is a genuine liquidity release, so resting buy-stop at the range high and sell-stop at the range low catch whichever side resolves, with the stop at the opposite extreme.
findings.setup_summary: On M5 GBP/JPY, in the ~3-hour window after the US market close (before Asia opens), record the highest high and lowest low of the window. Place both a pending buy-stop at the high and a pending sell-stop at the low; stop at the opposite side of the range; target = 2x the range height (1:2 R, e.g., 30-pip range -> 60-pip target). When one pending order triggers, cancel the other immediately.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Range must come from the quiet window only; once one pending fills, the other must be deleted (no double exposure); stopped if price reverses through the full range; trade only during the 3-hour gap (one setup per day).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: pending buy/sell stop at range extremes; stop at the opposite extreme; target 2x the range (1:2 R); expiry: intraday session.
findings.quote: The guppy burst seeks to identify the trading range during this 3-hour window and anticipate a potential breakout of the trading range.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, Strategy 15 'Guppy Burst', pp. 217-223
findings.notes: The dual-pending-order pattern is a deterministic structure worth encoding, but the exact '3-hour gap after US close' session anchor does not exist in 24/7 perps (no close/open, no gaps). The adaptable analog is a low-liquidity/low-volatility window (e.g., late weekend, funding-time compression). Without session boundaries, this is a compressed-range breakout rather than a true opening-range trade.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Fixed-fraction 3% risk per trade
findings.mechanism: Capping each trade's dollar risk at a fixed fraction (3%) of equity makes per-trade outcome variance a constant fraction of the account regardless of instrument or stop distance; combined with a mandatory stop it bounds ruin.
findings.setup_summary: Every strategy in the book sizes the position so the pip-distance to the stop risks 3% of account capital; returns are consistently quoted as 'X% return if we take a 3% risk' (e.g., a 15-pip risk at 1.5:1 R yields a '2% return'). The corollary rule is unconditional: 'Always put a stop loss for every trade' - the stopless ('naked') trade is named as the primary account-blowing behavior.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not a market-trigger rule but a sizing/admission constraint: violated if a trade is sized so its stop exceeds the 3%-of-equity budget, or if a position is entered without a stop.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry/stop/target per strategy; this rule fixes size such that (entry - stop) distance x position size = 3% of equity.
findings.quote: The risk for this trade is 15 pips, and the reward is 10 pips. The risk to reward ratio is 1.5:1, which yields a 2% return if we take a 3% risk.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2 'Three Points in Every Trade' pp. 17-23; sizing convention used throughout Chapters 6-10
findings.notes: Maps to V8 RiskGate as a deterministic admission/sizing rule: per-trade risk capped as a fixed fraction of equity, plus the mandatory-stop rule. Also ties to the book's psychology evidence: the Chapter 5 'Mike and Amanda' experiment shows identical entries but 10% vs 2% monthly returns because Amanda meddled with exits - a methodology lesson (rule adherence over discretion) that supports V8's rule-based, no-discretion expert design, though it is NARRATIVE-grade evidence on its own.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Queuing Theory of Moving Average Crossovers (MA-stack trend regime)
findings.mechanism: When price and a stack of longer-period MAs align in sequential order (shortest above longest), the market is in a durable trend regime; when the stack is unaligned, any rally or retracement is short-lived.
findings.setup_summary: On the daily timeframe, enter LONG when price closes above the 50-, 90-, and 200-day moving averages AND the MAs are stacked in sequential bullish order (shortest above mid above longest); enter SHORT on the mirror image. If price and MAs are not aligned in sequential order, do not expect new trend entries (any short-term rally/retracement is short-lived).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close above all three MAs with bullish stack order. Invalidation: price closes back below the long MA or the stack order breaks (short MA crosses below mid MA).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at bar close after MA-stack confirmation. No stop, target, or expiry stated in this part (back-matter only); treat as a regime/trend filter rather than a full trade recipe.
findings.quote: A bullish market is initiated when price crosses above its respective averages (e.g., 50-day, 90-day, and 200-day moving average lines) and the moving averages also follow in a sequential order with the shorter period moving average crossing above the longer period.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Queuing Theory of Moving Average Crossovers; Index: Queuing Theory of Moving Average Crossovers (eight principles, using to trade)
findings.notes: Systematic, fully falsifiable MA-stack rule; directly reusable as the trend filter that gates existing trend_continuation experts (trend_pullback's ema_fast>ema_slow is a 2-MA special case). Detailed daily-signal rules live in Part 1 (applied systems).
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: Price/oscillator divergence as trend-reversal signal
findings.mechanism: When price's directional movement disagrees with the oscillator's, the impulse is losing internal confirmation; divergence generally indicates an impending trend reversal.
findings.setup_summary: With any momentum oscillator (index references MACD, momentum oscillator, Blau's Momentum Direction and Divergence, plus hidden bullish/bearish divergence): price makes a higher high while the oscillator makes a lower high (bearish divergence) in an uptrend, or price makes a lower low while the oscillator makes a higher low (bullish divergence) in a downtrend; expect a trend reversal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence of oscillator extreme vs price extreme on the same leg. Invalidation: price breaks beyond the prior price extreme (divergence denied) or oscillator crosses back through the level of its prior divergence extreme.
findings.risk_geometry: Not stated in this part; book treats divergence as a warning ('generally indicates trend reversal') needing confirmation, not an instant entry.
findings.quote: Divergence occurs when the directional movement of the price disagrees with that of the oscillator. Divergence generally indicates trend reversal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: divergence; Index: Bullish/bearish divergence patterns, Hidden bullish/bearish divergence pattern, MACD, Momentum indicator
findings.notes: Corroborated across the library (RSI/MACD divergence reversal). V8 has no divergence expert yet; candidate backlog family. Hidden-divergence continuation variant also indexed, giving BOTH reversal and continuation behavior branches.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: Outside-day range expansion / inside-day momentum-waning
findings.mechanism: A day whose range engulfs the prior day's range represents a range expansion; the market tends to continue in the direction of that day's close. An inside day after a large move signals momentum is waning.
findings.setup_summary: On the daily bar, if today's high-low range fully contains the previous day's range (outside day), expect the following move in the direction of today's close (LONG if the close is in the direction of the breakout leg, SHORT otherwise). Conversely, an inside day (today's range inside yesterday's) is a consolidation signal, and after a big prior move indicates waning momentum for that move.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: full engulf of prior day's range. Invalidation: subsequent bars fail to follow the outside day's close direction and price closes back inside the prior day's range.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry in direction of outside-day close; no stop/target/expiry stated in this part.
findings.quote: A day in which the previous day's price range is within the range of today's price range. This is often a signal that the market is about to make a move in the direction of the close.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: outside day; Glossary: inside day
findings.notes: Daily-bar structure transfers to 24/7 perps (UTC daily bars are contiguous, so 'engulf' is well-defined). In 24/7 markets there are no session gaps, so the daily-range semantics are cleaner but the edge may be weaker; map onto any bar horizon as an N-bar range-expansion signal.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: Volume confirms price-move validity
findings.mechanism: Volume and price agreeing (volume rising together with price) validates the move; the book's applied systems use a Volume Zone Oscillator and volume-ratio-compressed indicator to gauge this participation.
findings.setup_summary: A trend move is considered valid/confirmed only when accompanied by rising volume (price up + volume up in an uptrend; price down + volume up in a downtrend); a move on flat or falling volume is treated as suspect. Volume zone oscillator and money-flow indicators are the book's operationalizations.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: directional move with expanding volume. Invalidation: new price extreme printed on contracting volume (confirmation absent).
findings.risk_geometry: None stated; this is a confirmation condition, not an entry geometry.
findings.quote: Volume is said to confirm the price action if volume is rising together with the price.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: confirmation; Index: Volume as indicator of price move validity, Volume zone oscillator (VZO), volume ratio compressed indicator formula, Money-flow indicator
findings.notes: Perp volume is exchange-reported trade volume and can include wash/spoofing artifacts; use as a confirming feature (participation group), not a standalone entry. Corroborated across the library (volume-price analysis books).
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: Never-trade-against rule + MA failure in sideways markets
findings.mechanism: The prevailing trend (HH/HL or LH/LL) defines the tradable regime; trading against it is disallowed, and indicator-based signals (especially moving averages) are unreliable in sideways/non-trending regimes.
findings.setup_summary: Define the regime by higher highs/higher lows (uptrend) or lower highs/lower lows (downtrend); only take entries in the direction of that regime (never-trade-against rule). In a sideways/non-trending regime (no HH/HL or LH/LL), suppress signal-driven entries because moving averages behave as lagging indicators there.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: established trend regime. Invalidation: regime flips to non-trending (range), which suspends entries.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated; regime gate applied before any entry.
findings.quote: in an uptrend when prices are making higher highs and higher lows, and as in a downtrend when prices are making lower highs and lower lows
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: trend; Index: Trends: never-trade-against rule; Moving averages: as lagging indicators, sideways markets and; Sideways markets; Nontrending market
findings.notes: Maps directly onto V8's regime_filter role: all experts should inherit a trend-regime gate. The 'MAs fail in sideways markets' caution is a documented failure mode to encode as a suppression rule.

findings.strategy_name: Double top (M) / double bottom (W) reversal
findings.mechanism: A double top is 'generally caused by flats' and a double bottom by 'failures' - the second peak/trough failing to exceed the first marks rejection of the prior trend and a reversal away from the range.
findings.setup_summary: In an uptrend, price prints two conspicuous peaks at a similar level (double top, 'M'); if the second peak fails to exceed the first, anticipate a reversal (SHORT). Mirror for double bottom ('W') in a downtrend (LONG on the failure to make a new low).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: second test of the prior extreme fails to exceed it. Invalidation: price breaks above the first peak (for the top) / below the first trough (for the bottom), negating the failure premise.
findings.risk_geometry: Not stated in this part; conventional geometry would place stops beyond the pattern extreme, but the book text here gives none.
findings.quote: Double top is generally caused by flats, double bottom by failures. Also known as 'M' and 'W' patterns.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: double top/bottom; Index: Double tops/double bottoms ('M' and 'W' patterns)
findings.notes: Structure-based failure-at-level pattern; mechanically expressible with a windowed prior-high/low ref (similar machinery to failed_breakout). Edwards & Magee cited in bibliography gives cross-book literature support.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: AB=CD / Gartley harmonic retracement
findings.mechanism: Harmonic price structures complete at Fibonacci ratio levels (0.382/0.618/1.618); the AB=CD structure projects a target completion where the CD leg equals AB, creating a reversal point at D.
findings.setup_summary: Identify a four-leg swing structure: leg AB, retracement BC, and leg CD where CD equals AB in length (and BC retraces AB at a Fibonacci ratio, commonly ~0.618); the completion point D is the reversal/entry zone. Gartley pattern is the indexed variant.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: D completes at the AB-equality projection and/or Fibonacci retracement of the larger leg. Invalidation: price extends through D by a defined threshold (structure failed).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at completion point D; standard stop beyond D (not stated in this part); targets from Fibonacci ratios 0.382/0.618/1.618.
findings.quote: The important ratios are 0.382, 0.618, and 1.618.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Fibonacci ratios; Glossary: A-B-C correction; Index: AB=CD patterns, Gartley Pattern (AB=CD pattern)
findings.notes: Requires swing-point labeling; concretely falsifiable once peaks/troughs are programmatically identified. Gartley book is cited in the bibliography (Profits in the Stock Market), giving literature corroboration.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: Rule of Equality: extended-wave target projection
findings.mechanism: In Elliott Wave five-wave structure, when one impulse wave extends, the remaining two impulse waves tend to be equal in length - a Fibonacci-ratio equality that yields objective price targets for the non-extended waves.
findings.setup_summary: After labeling a five-wave impulse in which one wave (commonly wave 3) is extended, project the length of the extended wave onto the other impulse waves as equality targets (Rule of Equality); use 0.382/0.618/1.618 retracement and projection levels as entry/target zones.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: extended impulse wave identified. Invalidation: subsequent waves fail to approximate the equality projection (structure invalidated by a new extreme beyond the projected target).
findings.risk_geometry: Target-setting only: projection = length of extended wave mapped to remaining impulse waves; levels 0.382/0.618/1.618 as retracement/projection anchors.
findings.quote: When one impulse wave is extended in a five-wave structure, the remaining two waves tend to be equal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Equality, Rule of; Glossary: extended wave; Index: Fibonacci Retracement and Projection, Elliott Wave Theory
findings.notes: Objective target-projection tool, but gated on subjective wave labeling; V8 should treat it as a location/target feature input (fib levels), not an autonomous expert. Rule of Alternation (Wave 2 simple -> Wave 4 complex) is the companion EW heuristic in the same glossary.

findings.strategy_name: Gap types: breakaway/common/runaway/exhaustion
findings.mechanism: A day whose range sits entirely above or below the prior day's range creates a gap; the indexed taxonomy (breakaway, common, runaway, exhaustion) classifies gaps by position in the trend, each with distinct follow-through or fill behavior.
findings.setup_summary: A gap is defined as a daily range completely above or below the prior day's range. The book's taxonomy (breakaway gap at trend start, common gap in ranges, runaway gap mid-trend, exhaustion gap late in trend) drives gap-continuation and gap-fill plays.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not applicable - finding rejected for V8.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated in this part.
findings.quote: Refers to a trading day in which a daily range is completely above or below the previous day's range, displaying a gap between today's low and yesterday's high or today's high and yesterday's low.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: gap; Index: Breakaway gaps, Common gaps, Runaway gaps, Exhaustion gaps
findings.notes: Rejected for crypto perps: 24/7 trading with no exchange sessions means consecutive bars are contiguous and exchange-level gaps do not form; the gap taxonomy and gap-fill logic have no clean perp analog. Documented as a REJECTED_OPTION mapping.

findings.strategy_name: Protective stops + predefined risk:reward + position sizing
findings.mechanism: Loss containment is mandatory: a protective stop liquidates the trade to cap loss, and risk:reward must be defined and positions sized accordingly before entry.
findings.setup_summary: Every position carries a protective stop at which the trade is liquidated to prevent further loss; risk and reward are defined and managed before entry, and position size is determined as part of the plan (index: 'risk and reward: definitions, managing of'; 'position sizing, determining'; 'money management planning').
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: position opened. Invalidation: stop level reached - liquidation is automatic; the trade thesis is over.
findings.risk_geometry: Protective stop mandatory on every position (book does not specify ATR multiple vs swing point in this part); risk:reward and position size predefined.
findings.quote: protective stops A risk management technique in which the trade is liquidated to stop further loss.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: protective stops; Index: Risk and reward: definitions/managing of, Position sizing: determining, Money management planning, Exit strategies: determining
findings.notes: Confirms V8's RiskGate design (deterministic stop admission, one exposure per instrument/direction, heat cap). Adds the book's emphasis that risk:reward and position sizing are defined pre-entry and that exit strategies (not just entries) are a distinct planned component.
findings.book: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders - Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology 2012

findings.strategy_name: Ichimoku charting technique (Tenkan/Kijun/Senkou/Chikou applied system)
findings.mechanism: Ichimoku overlays the Queuing Theory MA relationships onto one chart: Tenkan-sen and Kijun-sen crosses, the Senkou cloud (spans A and B) as dynamic support/resistance, and Chikou-span confirmation of price position - an applied system for trading daily signals.
findings.setup_summary: Ichimoku applied system trades daily signals: price above the Senkou cloud is bullish, below is bearish; Tenkan-sen (short) crossing Kijun-sen (mid) provides trigger, and the Chikou span (lagging line) confirms the signal against historical price. Built on the same sequential MA logic as the Queuing Theory.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: Tenkan/Kijun cross aligned with price vs cloud. Invalidation: price re-enters the cloud (regime ambiguity).
findings.risk_geometry: Not stated in this part; cloud structure acts as dynamic support/resistance.
findings.quote: eight principles of interpreting, Ichimoku charting and, period groups, reading probable trends with, using to trade
findings.chapter_anchor: Index: Ichimoku charting technique (Tenkan-sen, Kijun-sen, Senkou spans A and B, Chikou span); Index: Queuing Theory of Moving Average Crossovers: Ichimoku charting and
findings.notes: This part only establishes Ichimoku as an applied system tied to MA-stack logic (detail in Part 1); index confirms the standard cloud framework. Backlog candidate; cloud-lag in 24/7 chop is the main perp risk.

findings.strategy_name: Financial astrology / lunar-cycle timing (lunar buy-sell strategy)
findings.mechanism: No causal price mechanism; claims that market cycles correlate with planetary/lunar cycles - lunations, new/full moon, Sun-Moon aspects, transits, and first-trade horoscopes - used to pick timing windows.
findings.setup_summary: The book's central thesis: time entries around lunar/planetary cycles - e.g., a 'lunar buy-sell strategy' keyed to lunations (new moon = Sun/Moon conjunction, full moon = 180-degree opposition), transits, and Sun-Moon aspects (index: 'lunar buy-sell strategy', 'lunar cycles', 'choosing best trading periods').
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not applicable - finding rejected for V8.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated; timing overlay only.
findings.quote: lunar buy-sell strategy
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: lunation, new moon, full moon, transit, eclipse, aspect; Index: lunar buy-sell strategy, lunar cycles, financial astrology, Sun-Moon aspects
findings.notes: No falsifiable causal mechanism; lunar phases are deterministic calendar data, but the book offers no statistical case (RBS 'Sheer Lunacy' skeptical paper is cited in the bibliography). V8 rejects as an autonomous expert; if ever examined, only as a pure calendar-correlation study under the astrology-for-timing framing, which V8's determinism rules do not preclude but the complexity budget does not justify.

book_title: Timing Solutions for Swing Traders: Successful Trading Using Technical Analysis and Financial Astrology (2012) — Part 2 (Glossary/Bibliography/Index)
Beyond Candlesticks: New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed (Steve Nison, 1994) — Part 2 (Glossary + Index)

findings.strategy_name: Spring (break of support then reclaim); mirror upthrust
findings.setup_summary: After an important support area, price breaks under it then 'springs' back above the broken level — the reclaim is the trigger (LONG). The mirror 'upthrust' setup: price breaks through important resistance, fails to hold the new highs, and pulls back under the pierced resistance (SHORT).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = bar close back above the broken support (spring) or close back under the pierced resistance (upthrust). Thesis invalid if the reclaimed side is re-crossed.
findings.risk_geometry: Book gives no numeric geometry in this section; freeze the swept extreme as reference, entry on close of the reclaim bar, stop beyond the swept extreme.
findings.quote: a bullish signal where the market breaks under an important support area and then 'springs' back above the broken support area.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Spring / Upthrust (p.268, 270)
findings.notes: Directly corroborates the existing formalized V8 expert liquidity_sweep_reclaim (mechanism liquidity_sweep_reclaim, behavior sweep_reclaim). The book's 'spring' is the canonical statement of the stop-run-then-reclaim thesis.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Upthrust (failed breakout of resistance)
findings.setup_summary: During an uptrend, price breaks through an important resistance area, fails to hold the new highs, and pulls back under the previously pierced resistance. Enter SHORT on the close back below the pierced level.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = close back under the pierced resistance; thesis invalid if price closes back above the reference (breakout level reclaimed).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE; stop above the failed-breakout extreme; freeze the pierced-resistance reference (per V8 convention); exit on R-multiple target or dead-thesis.
findings.quote: a bearish signal insofar as the market breaks through important resistance, but then fails to hold the new highs and pulls back under the previously pierced resistance area.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Upthrust (p.270)
findings.notes: Maps exactly to the existing formalized V8 expert failed_breakout (SHORT, close below windowed prior high after a failed breakout); the book supplies the resistance-pierce precondition.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Hammer / Hanging man / Shooting star (single-candle rejection lines)
findings.setup_summary: After a downtrend, a candle with a small real body near the upper end of the range, lower shadow >=3x the real body, and little/no upper shadow (hammer) is bullish. The same shape after an uptrend is a hanging man and is only bearish when the next session closes under its real body. A shooting star (long upper shadow, small body near the bottom of the range) after an uptrend is a top-reversal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Hanging man requires next-bar close under its real body as confirmation; the pattern candle alone is not a signal. Hammer/shooting star likewise need next-bar confirmation in the reversal direction.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the confirmation bar's close, not the pattern bar; stop beyond the shadow extreme; book only references risk/reward broadly (Index p.133-137) without numeric multiples here.
findings.quote: a long lower shadow usually three times or more the length of the real body... The hanging man and hammer have the same shape. What differentiates one from the other is that the hammer follows a downtrend while the hanging man is after an uptrend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Hammer / Hanging man (p.259-260), Shooting star (p.267)
findings.notes: Shape-only patterns are abundant on 1h crypto and false-positive-prone at high leverage; the trend precondition and the next-bar confirmation rule are the load-bearing, falsifiable parts.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Engulfing / Piercing / Harami / Last engulfing (dual-candle reversal family)
findings.setup_summary: After a trend, a real body that fully engulfs the prior opposite-color body is a reversal (bullish engulfing after a decline, bearish after a rise). Weaker/exhaustion variants: piercing line (white close >=50% into the prior black body after a new low), last engulfing (the engulfing pattern that appears as the final move of the trend), and harami (small body held inside the prior long body = indecision, trend fuel fading).
findings.trigger_invalidation: All variants need a prior trend to reverse; harami is an indecision signal requiring subsequent confirmation; invalidation = next bar continues the original trend.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE; stop beyond the engulfing pattern's extreme; no numeric R given in this section.
findings.quote: thisa bullish candle pattern that has the same group of candle lines that form the bearish engulfing pattern (a large black candle that engulfs the prior white candle). However, the bearish engulfing pattern appears after a rising market while the last engulfing pattern appears after a falling market.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Engulfing / Last engulfing / Piercing / Harami (p.258-263, 266)
findings.notes: The 'last engulfing' variant frames the engulfing candle as the final thrust of the trend — a usable trend-exhaustion reading for the reversal thesis.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Morning star / Evening star (three-candle star reversals)
findings.setup_summary: Bottom (morning star): during a downtrend a long black body, then a small real body that does not touch the first body, then a long white body that closes well into the first black body. Mirror at top (evening star): long white, small non-touching body, long black closing well into the first white. Doji variants (morning/evening doji star) when the middle candle is a doji.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Pattern completes only when the third candle closes well into the first body and the middle candle does not touch the first body; if the third candle fails to close into the first body the pattern is void.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry after completion of the third candle's close; stop beyond the pattern's extreme; book itself flags subjectivity (Index: 'Subjectivity, morning star and, 119,120').
findings.quote: The last session of the morning star is a long white real body that ideally should not touch the second real body. This long white real body should close well into the first candle's black real body to complete this pattern.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Evening star (p.258), Morning star (p.263)
findings.notes: Composite 3-bar pattern with strict gapping constraints; requires hard thresholds ('close well into', body-length ratios) to be falsifiable on 1h data.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Disparity / divergence index (percentage distance from moving average)
findings.setup_summary: Disparity index = (close - MA)/MA as a percentage (e.g., 25-day disparity of -10% = price 10% under the 25-day MA). Book-specified uses: overbought/oversold fade at extremes, trend-direction filter, and divergence gauge (price makes a new high while disparity makes a lower high = momentum loss).
findings.trigger_invalidation: An extreme disparity reading is a condition, not a trigger; needs a confirmation. Divergence between price and disparity flags loss of trend momentum.
findings.risk_geometry: No geometry in this section; trading use is in the book's moving-averages chapter (Index p.157-166) in Part 1.
findings.quote: a 25-day disparity index of -10% means that today's price is 10% under the 25-day moving average. Some of the ways the disparity index can be used include: as an overbought/oversold indicator, as a signal of trend direction, and as a tool to gauge divergence.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Disparity index / Divergence index (p.257)
findings.notes: Scale-free, PIT-computable percentage distance from MA is a natural V8 feature (trend/volatility groups) and its divergence reading is a momentum-signature input. Book states the divergence index is the same series differently scaled (110% = +10%).
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Three-line break chart trend-reversal system
findings.setup_summary: On a time-independent three-line break chart: a decline has started when the low of the last three rising lines is broken on the downside (sell / white-to-black turnaround); a decline has ended when the highest price of the last three declining lines is exceeded on the upside (buy / black-to-white turnaround). Variants: 'black shoe / white suit / neck' trades, record sessions, and uptrend support lines (Index p.174-190).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Reversal requires breaking the extreme of the last three opposite-direction lines; moves smaller than that are ignored by construction; book acknowledges whipsaws in ranging markets (Index p.184).
findings.risk_geometry: No numeric stop/target in this section; the chart construction itself defines trend state; signals per Index p.174-176.
findings.quote: To determine if the market has started down, the low price of the last three rising lines must be broken on the downside during the fall. On the other hand, to determine if a decline has ended, the highest price of the last three declining lines must be exceeded on the upside.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Three-line break (p.268-269); Index p.279
findings.notes: Deterministic, PIT-constructible trend filter equivalent to a 3-bar-fractal trailing reference; candidate trend-following expert family, but whipsaw-prone without a volatility-scaled reversal threshold.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Record sessions overextension (8-10 consecutive new highs/lows)
findings.setup_summary: A market reaching eight to ten consecutive (or nearly consecutive) record-session highs or lows is overextended; gravestone doji at such record sessions is cited as a top-reversal signal. The consecutive-new-extreme count is a scale-free overextension measure.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Count >= 8-10 is an overextension flag, not a standalone entry; a reversal signal needs a confirming candle (e.g., gravestone doji); invalidation = trend persists past the count without reversal.
findings.risk_geometry: Not specified in this section; book references record-session techniques in kagi (p.235-239) and three-line break (p.186-187).
findings.quote: a market that reaches eight to ten consecutive (or almost consecutive) record session highs or record session lows is a time when the market is overextended.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Record sessions (p.264)
findings.notes: Trivially computable on 1h BTCUSDT; best used as a fade/take-profit/overextension filter rather than a standalone entry; corroborates exhaustion logic in the book's kagi record-session techniques.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Windows (gaps) as continuation patterns and support/resistance
findings.setup_summary: A rising window (top of the prior session's upper shadow below the low of the current lower shadow) is a bullish continuation pattern; a falling window opens when the prior session's low is above the current session's high. The window edge acts as support (rising) or resistance (falling); 'close under top of window keeps downtrend in force' is the stated invalidation line. Variants: three windows, gapping doji, two black gapping candles.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Continuation thesis invalid when the window fills (price closes back through it); the window-edge line is the stated invalidation reference.
findings.risk_geometry: Window edge used as a stop reference (Index: 'rising window, stops, 130-132'); volume cited as confirmation (Index: 'Volume, windows and, 96').
findings.quote: A rising window is a bullish continuation pattern that is formed when the top of yesterday's upper shadow is under the low of the current lower shadow... Close under top of window keeps downtrend in force.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Windows (p.270-271)
findings.notes: Crypto perps trade 24/7, so classic overnight gaps are absent, but shadow-gaps between consecutive candles occur at session boundaries and event shocks; window levels remain PIT-computable S/R.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Long real-body candles as support/resistance zones
findings.setup_summary: A long white candle (real body >=3x recent bodies, close near high) defines a support area from midway of the body down to the bottom of the lower shadow; a long black candle (body >=3x recent bodies, close near low) defines a resistance area from 50% within the candle up to the top including the upper shadow. Zones confirm support/resistance and breakout validity; change-of-polarity applies (support becomes resistance).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Zone valid while intact as S/R; a close through the zone flips its polarity to the opposite role.
findings.risk_geometry: Zone boundaries give concrete stop references; zone extent defined by '50% within the candle' (black) and 'midway of the candle' (white).
findings.quote: The resistance set up by a long black candle should be from 50% within the candle up to the top of the candle (including the upper shadow)... The support should be from midway of the white candle down to the bottom of the white candle (this includes the bottom of the lower shadow).
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Long white candle / Long black candle (p.262-263)
findings.notes: Concrete, PIT-computable zone definitions that feed V8's location feature group; corroborates the change-of-polarity principle (Index p.275).
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Kagi / renko new-price charts as deterministic denoising
findings.setup_summary: Kagi and renko charts ignore time: the line/brick extends in the trend direction and only reverses after a predetermined amount (fixed price or percentage). On kagi, line thickness changes when price penetrates a prior high/low (yang/yin), generating buy/sell signals; shoulders/waists form double-window (M/W) top/bottom reversals; tweezers tops, three-Buddha (head-and-shoulders analog), multi-level breaks, and a correction-stop-location technique (p.225-227) are the tradable patterns.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a — methodology finding. Reversal-amount choice controls sensitivity (Index: 'sensitivity of, 154'); larger amounts produce fewer, later signals.
findings.risk_geometry: Kagi correction stop location (Index p.276) anchors stops at prior inflection/swing levels.
findings.quote: If the market continues to move in the direction of the prior kagi line, that line is extended. However, if the market reverses by a predetermined amount, a new kagi line is drawn in the next column in the opposite direction.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Kagi chart (p.261), Renko chart (p.265)
findings.notes: V8 lesson: a fixed-reversal (ATR-scaled) denoised series is a deterministic, PIT-safe source for trend state and M/W reversal detection; kagi double-window bottom is structurally a double-bottom, corroborating pivot_reversal-style patterns.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Candlestick reversal signals require a prior trend (trend gate)
findings.setup_summary: Candle theory: most candle signals are reversals, so a pattern or candle line only has meaning with a prior trend to reverse. A doji in the middle of a trading zone is not a trading signal; the same physical candle (hammer vs hanging man) is bullish or bearish purely on the direction of the prior trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trend gate is a precondition: no prior trend (flat/range regime) suppresses reversal candidates from being emitted.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a — this is an admission gate, not a setup.
findings.quote: since most of the candle signals are reversals, there must be a prior trend to reverse for a candle pattern or candle line to have meaning. For instance a doji in the middle of a trading zone would not be an important trading signal since there is no trend to reverse.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary: Trend (p.269)
findings.notes: Cross-cutting lifecycle rule for every candlestick-reversal family candidate above: encode a trend precondition at admission and a range-regime suppression; consistent with V8's existing still_valid/dead-thesis design.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

book_title: Forex Patterns and Probabilities: Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets (Ed Ponsi, 2007) — Part 2: Chapters 20-22, Glossary, Index

findings.strategy_name: Win-rate is not expectancy (asymmetric payoff trap)
findings.mechanism: Cutting winners at a small fixed gain while holding losers until they recover produces a high win rate but negative expectancy, because loser size is unbounded while winner size is capped.
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable claim: any rule that (a) exits winners at a small fixed gain and (b) holds losers until they turn positive produces a win rate near 95% but a net loss, since average loss dwarfs average win. The author demonstrates this with a 20-trade demo (19 winners, 1 loss) that nets a loss. V8 implication: expert evaluation and registry (Screening) verdicts must be computed on expectancy / profit factor and payoff geometry, never on win rate.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If a >90%-win-rate strategy shows positive expectancy and positive risk-adjusted metrics on frozen OOS, the trap claim is not violated; but win rate alone is inadmissible as an admission metric either way.
findings.risk_geometry: Anti-pattern as described: entry anywhere, take-profit very small (near 0R), stop effectively absent (hold to positive). The book states this geometry loses despite a 95% win rate.
findings.quote: I placed a total of 20 trades, with 19 "winners" and 1 loss, resulting in a success rate of 95 percent... this so-called strategy resulted in a loss, despite the lofty winning percentage.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 20 'What You Don't Know Can Hurt You' — 'The 95 Percent Winners Strategy' (pp. 229-230)
findings.notes: Book states 'The percentage of winning trades has nothing to do with the ultimate success of the trader.' With 25-100x perp leverage the unbounded-loser geometry becomes a liquidation event. Also implies RiskGate should reject any risk_geometry with an effectively unbounded stop (hold-to-positive).
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Drawdown as the controlling performance metric (return-to-drawdown)
findings.mechanism: A trader who risks a 50% drawdown to make 100% is closer to ruin than one who makes 20% with a 2% drawdown; institutional capital is allocated on largest drawdown, not headline return.
findings.setup_summary: Decision rule: performance is judged first by worst drawdown ('What is your biggest drawdown?') and by return-to-drawdown ratio, not raw return. Author compares Trader A (100% gain / 50% max drawdown) with Trader B (20% gain / 2% max drawdown) and concludes B is superior and A is 'an accident waiting to happen.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: A strategy whose largest drawdown exceeds the risk-of-ruin bound for its leverage and capital base is inadmissible regardless of gross return.
findings.risk_geometry: Account-level rule only — no entry/stop/target; governs drawdown ceiling, exposure cap, and capital allocation.
findings.quote: the question you'll hear from a hedge fund is more likely to be, "What is your biggest drawdown?"
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 21 'A Tale of Two Traders' (pp. 233-235)
findings.notes: Motivates a V8 RiskGate/lifecycle drawdown cap and registry evaluation on risk-adjusted (return/drawdown) metrics. In perps, leverage converts a 50% mark-to-market drawdown into forced liquidation, so the cap is binding earlier than in spot FX.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Willingness to take small losses prevents large losses (mandatory stop)
findings.mechanism: Deliberate early acceptance of small losses is what prevents account-destroying losses; failure to take a strategic loss is the common genesis of major trading disasters.
findings.setup_summary: Risk rule: every trade must have a predefined retreat level; an accepted small loss now beats an unbounded loss later. The book cites Nick Leeson/Barings and Long-Term Capital Management as disasters rooted in unwillingness to take a loss.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Any expert whose lifecycle allows a position to run without a deterministic stop or a dead-thesis (still_valid) exit violates the rule.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop is mandatory and predefined; the book specifies no target geometry here.
findings.quote: you have to be willing to deal with small losses to prevent the creation of a large loss.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 20 'What You Don't Know Can Hurt You' — 'Know When to Retreat' (pp. 228-229)
findings.notes: Supports V8's mandatory deterministic stops and the distinct dead-thesis exit. In 24/7 perp trading there is no overnight reprieve, so an unstopped position is a liquidation position; loss containment is a first-order risk rule.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Backtest overoptimization and hypothetical-returns skepticism
findings.mechanism: Markets are nonstationary; any strategy can be curve-fit to history, so in-sample/hypothetical excellence is not evidence of future edge, and hypothetical results are routinely marketed as actual.
findings.setup_summary: Methodology rule: 'the past does not equal the future'; overoptimized backtests are easy to construct in hindsight and are marketed deceptively (book cites a CFTC complaint for misrepresenting backtested returns). Trading plans must be validated out-of-sample, and hypothetical results must be explicitly distinguished from actual results.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If an expert's advantage survives out-of-sample and forward simulated replication on frozen OOS, nonstationarity alone does not disqualify it; claims of edge without such evidence are inadmissible.
findings.risk_geometry: None — methodology.
findings.quote: Since markets are not static, and are constantly evolving and changing, back testing is not a panacea. The past does not equal the future.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 20 'What You Don't Know Can Hurt You' — 'Beware the Back Tester' and 'Hypothetically Speaking' (pp. 230-231)
findings.notes: Validates V8's challenger + frozen-OOS + registry-decision evolution protocol (no in-place evolution, no NOW() in replay) and the NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM gate pending an authority receipt. Crypto regime drift (funding regimes, leverage cycles, venue microstructure shifts) makes nonstationarity severe.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Good trade versus winning trade (evaluate process, not outcome)
findings.mechanism: Single-trade outcomes are noise; a strategy is judged by whether the predetermined plan was followed, because a winning outcome can follow broken rules and a losing outcome can follow perfect execution.
findings.setup_summary: Evaluation rule: episode attribution goes to adherence to the plan (stop placed correctly, defined exit), never to the realized PnL of the trade; the trader should 'strive to be a good trader,' not a lucky one.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If a plan is followed perfectly and still loses over a large frozen-OOS sample, the fault is with the plan and the plan is modified — not the execution.
findings.risk_geometry: None — evaluation principle.
findings.quote: a winning trade is not always a good trade, and a good trade is not always a winning trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 22 'Some Final Thoughts' — 'A Good Trade Is Not the Same Thing as a Winning Trade' (pp. 237-238)
findings.notes: Supports V8 rule 15 (outcome data never mutates an active expert) and the episode/registry separation: single episodes neither promote nor kill a family; frozen-OOS aggregates do.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Plan fidelity: execute the plan; rule-breaking breeds failure
findings.mechanism: Randomly altering or abandoning a plan because it 'doesn't work' makes it impossible to know whether the plan was ever valid; systematic rule-breaking eventually 'breaks you'.
findings.setup_summary: Methodology rule: a good plan is useless if executed improperly; parameter and rule changes must be deliberate and governed, never on-whim, and execution failures must be separated from plan failures before a plan is discarded.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Plans are discarded only after proper execution shows the plan itself fails on frozen OOS; if execution was improper, the plan is retained.
findings.risk_geometry: None — methodology.
findings.quote: A good plan is useless if it's being executed improperly.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 22 'Some Final Thoughts' — 'Proper Execution Is Critical' (p. 238)
findings.notes: Supports V8's rule that parameter/threshold changes are VARIANTS of one family and version changes require a registry decision — no silent in-place tweaks. Execution (simulator/cost-model) fidelity must be audited before blaming the plan.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Simplicity: fewer moving parts, fewer failure modes
findings.mechanism: Complexity does not imply efficacy; a machine with fewer parts has fewer parts that can break, and simple plans work when executed properly.
findings.setup_summary: Methodology rule: prefer the simplest falsifiable expert; simple techniques can work just as well as complicated ones, and added complexity must buy measurable OOS improvement or be rejected.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Complexity is justified only if it beats the simpler baseline on frozen OOS; otherwise complexity is a liability.
findings.risk_geometry: None — methodology.
findings.quote: Think of a trading strategy as if it were a machine; if it has fewer moving parts, then there are fewer parts that can break, and fewer things that can go wrong with it.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 22 'Some Final Thoughts' — 'Keep It Simple' (p. 239)
findings.notes: Corroborates V8 complexity budget (rule 14: max 3 ACTIVE experts, at most one learned component, absent-by-default router/scorer/ranker/shared scorer).
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: No stops + quick profits + leverage = margin-call ruin
findings.mechanism: Trading without stops while taking profits quickly defers all risk to a single catastrophic loss; in a leveraged 24/7 market the deferred loss becomes a margin call / liquidation.
findings.setup_summary: Explicitly stated anti-pattern: 'trade without stops... and take profits quickly' so that every trade is held 'until it either turns profitable or creates a margin call.' Accounts show nice early returns, then 'blow a hole in the account with one big loss' while the win rate stays impressive.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A no-stop, quick-profit configuration is still inadmissible per risk rules regardless of any shown backtest; the general trap claim is not conditional on OOS results.
findings.risk_geometry: Anti-pattern geometry: stop absent, target near 0R, leverage-driven; the book notes this 'is exactly how many people try to trade' (p. 228).
findings.quote: Why not simply trade without stops... and take profits quickly? That way, we can hold on to every trade until it either turns profitable or creates a margin call.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 20 'What You Don't Know Can Hurt You' — 'Sarcasm Alert' (p. 228)
findings.notes: In crypto perps with 25-100x leverage, no exchange gaps, and deterministic liquidation engines, the 'one big loss' is automatic liquidation. RiskGate must reject experts whose risk_geometry lacks a deterministic stop; this also motivates modeling forced liquidation in the simulator cost model.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Payoff asymmetry, not win rate, is the engine of successful trend trading
findings.mechanism: Successful traders often lose more trades than they win; edge resides in letting winners run so the average winner exceeds the average loser (R:R > 1), not in forecast accuracy.
findings.setup_summary: Design inference from the book's claim that 'many successful traders place more losing trades than winning trades': trend-following experts should be designed and evaluated as payoff-asymmetry systems (many small losses, fewer large gains). Implication for V8 trend-family geometry: target_r/stop_r asymmetry is a first-order design variable, and low win rate must not be treated as a defect.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If a trend expert with R:R > 1 shows positive expectancy on frozen OOS, the mechanism is corroborated; the book states no specific optimal win rate.
findings.risk_geometry: Refinement input: consider variants with target_r > stop_r (asymmetric R) with correspondingly smaller per-trade risk; the book itself gives no numeric values.
findings.quote: there are many successful traders who place more losing trades than winning trades. The percentage of winning trades has nothing to do with the ultimate success of the trader.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 20 'What You Don't Know Can Hurt You' (pp. 227-228)
findings.notes: Candidate refinement for trend_pullback / failed_breakout geometry variants (e.g., target_r 2.0 / stop_r 1.0) and for how Screening reports results (expectancy and R:R profile, not win rate). Guards against penalizing low-win-rate trend following at registry review.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Take responsibility; blame deflection blocks learning
findings.mechanism: Attributing losses to external causes ('market maker manipulation', 'institutions') removes the need to change; accepting responsibility for every trade is a precondition for improvement.
findings.setup_summary: Methodology lesson for the research program: an evidence-bound program must accept responsibility for each expert's falsification rather than attributing failure to manipulation or venue unfairness — 'your account balance' does not care who is at fault.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not a tradeable setup; applies to research governance and honest reporting.
findings.risk_geometry: None.
findings.quote: If we deflect blame, then there is no need for us to change. The fault lies with someone else, so therefore there is no need for us to grow and learn.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 22 'Some Final Thoughts' — 'Take Responsibility for Your Actions' (pp. 238-239)
findings.notes: Reinforces V8's honesty obligations: falsified hypotheses are recorded as REJECTED/QUARANTINED on the evidence, never dismissed as 'market manipulation'; consistent with the evidence-bound falsification program and rule 12 (no fabricated or promoted claims).
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Window (gap) continuation: reaction stops within window, close-through voids trend
findings.mechanism: an unfilled window stores directional pressure; a close through it voids the prior trend
findings.setup_summary: Detect a rising window (current bar low above prior bar high) or falling window. The trend is presumed to continue; a pullback that holds inside the window (no close through the far edge) is the entry. Rising window: long on a pullback close that stays above the window bottom; falling window symmetric short. If the window is not filled within three bars, that confirms continuation.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A close through the far edge of the window voids the trend thesis; intra-session wicks through do not count. After 3 consecutive windows in one direction the market is 'overextended' - offset positions, do not add; only go countertrend after the last window is filled on a close.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at bar close (pullback into window or continuation); stop on a close through the window far edge; targets come from other tools (change-of-polarity levels, prior S/R) since candles give no targets; ~3-bar expiry for window-fill confirmation.
findings.quote: The reaction will go until the window... if the price closes through the window, I then view the prior trend as being voided.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'The Window', pp.93-104
findings.notes: On 24/7 BTCUSDT 1h, bar-to-bar windows are intermittent (continuous auction, overlapping ranges), so signal frequency is low on the most liquid pair but higher on alt perps and higher timeframes. The close-through invalidation rule maps cleanly onto V8's fill-at-close simulator. Folded-in sub-patterns: two black gapping candles (falling window + 2 black bodies = 'rout of the bulls'), gapping doji, and the three-windows overextension rule.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Change of polarity: broken support becomes resistance and vice versa
findings.mechanism: a level tested often accumulates resting orders; once broken those orders flip side and magnetize price back for a rejection test
findings.setup_summary: Identify a level tested at least twice as support (or resistance). After a close below it, the level flips to resistance; a bearish candle (hanging man, dark cloud cover, shooting star, long upper shadow) forming at the flipped level is a short entry. Mirror for broken resistance flipping to support. The more tests before the break, the stronger the expected flip.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A close back beyond the flipped level invalidates the thesis; if no rejection signal appears at the flipped level within a few bars, abandon the setup.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the candle-signal close at the flipped level; stop on a close beyond the flipped level; target = next support / prior congestion / measured move.
findings.quote: a penetrated resistance area should then be converted to support and a broken support area should be resistance... the more often a support or resistance area is tested before prices break them, the better the change of polarity principle should work.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'The Hanging Man' (change of polarity), pp.62-64
findings.notes: This is the location mechanic behind V8's existing failed_breakout and liquidity_sweep_reclaim families; the falsifiable increment is that flip reliability scales with the number of prior tests of the level. Continuous 24/7 markets and high leverage make rejections at flipped levels directly tradable; no gaps interfere.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Disparity/divergence index: close-to-MA ratio as overbought/oversold and divergence gauge
findings.mechanism: the more price stretches from its moving-average mean, the lower the probability the move continues
findings.setup_summary: Compute disparity = (close/MA(N)) - 1, or divergence = close/MA(N) as a ratio. Estimate per-market overbought/oversold zones empirically (book's stock example: +10%/-10% on a 13-week disparity; cited Nikkei study: 200-day divergence 102-110% in rising markets, 90-99% in falling markets within 2 standard deviations). Use the zone to gate other signals: a reversal candle (doji, hammer) in the oversold zone is a higher-value long; avoid fresh longs in the overbought zone; price new high with a lower disparity peak = bearish divergence.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Zones are market-specific and must be re-estimated per market; the book warns 'high divergence does not necessarily mean that prices will reverse'.
findings.risk_geometry: Filter/confirmation only - no entry, stop, or target given in the book.
findings.quote: when the 13-week disparity index reached the +10% area, the market became overbought... if the 200-day divergence moves above 110%, it is considered excessive and there is increased likelihood that the market is vulnerable to a correction.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 'The Disparity Index', pp.159-166
