findings.notes: The 2-sigma divergence bands come from a cited NTAA (1986) Nikkei study - the book's only explicit statistical evidence; transferring those bands to BTCUSDT is an inference and the zones must be re-derived from data. A disparity-extreme feature would also weight the golden/dead cross and candle signals. Computable deterministically from any OHLC series on 1h BTC.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Three-line break trend regime with turnaround lines
findings.mechanism: a close beyond the far extreme of the last three same-direction closes flips the trend regime
findings.setup_summary: From closing prices, add a white line on a new high and a black line on a new low; once three consecutive same-color lines exist, a reversal requires a close beyond the low of the last three white lines (black turnaround) or beyond the high of the last three black lines (white turnaround). Three white lines = bull regime: use bullish candle signals as longs and treat bearish candle signals as cover-only; a black turnaround line flips the regime to bear. Regime changes are close-confirmed and lag, so scale in lightly intra-session and add on confirmation.
findings.trigger_invalidation: An opposite turnaround line flips the regime; 8-10 consecutive same-color lines mark overextension (record-session concept) and warn of a bounce.
findings.risk_geometry: No explicit stops in the book; the turnaround line / last-three-lines extreme is the structural level; exits on the opposite turnaround.
findings.quote: once three consecutive white or black lines appear... the market is in a trending mode. A basic trend reversal signal is produced when a turnaround line moves under three consecutive white lines or above three consecutive black lines.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'Three-Line Break Charts', pp.167-190
findings.notes: Deterministic and close-only, so it ports cleanly to V8 replay. The book uses it explicitly as a trend filter for gating candle entries - a REGIME_FILTER role. Sensitivity adjusts from 2-line (faster) to 5/10-line breaks. 'Black shoe / white suit / neck' is a buy-on-second-confirmation variant of the turnaround signal.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Kagi yang/yin: buy on line-thickening, sell on line-thinning, with shoulders/waists and midpoint rule
findings.mechanism: penetration of a prior extreme flips the line's structural state (thin/thick), marking a regime control change
findings.setup_summary: Build a kagi chart with a fixed or percentage reversal amount (3% is the NTAA-expert default, 5% for longer-term). Buy when the line turns thick (yang - a thin line penetrated the prior high/shoulder); sell when it turns thin (yin - a thick line broke a prior low/waist). Rising shoulders plus rising waists = healthy bull; first lower shoulder or lower waist = weakening. A pullback holding above the midpoint of a long kagi line is bullish; a rally failing to pierce the midpoint in a downtrend is bearish.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Opposite line-thickness change; a two- or three-level break provides extra confirmation at the cost of later entries.
findings.risk_geometry: Structural stop below the last waist (longs) / above the last shoulder (shorts); midpoint of long kagi lines acts as support/resistance; intraday kagi (e.g., 5-minute) is explicitly supported.
findings.quote: the most basic is to buy when the kagi line goes from thin to thick, and to sell when the kagi line changes from thick to thin.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.8 'Kagi Charts', pp.213-239
findings.notes: Fully computable and deterministic from closes; a percentage reversal auto-scales to BTC's changing volatility where fixed-dollar reversals would not. Folded-in sub-mechanisms: shoulders/waists structure, yang-vs-yin length comparison, midpoint support of long lines, double-window reversal patterns, tweezers (double top) and three-Buddha (head-and-shoulders) on kagi.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Record sessions: 8-10 new extremes = overextension, countertrend caution
findings.mechanism: trend extension beyond ~8-10 new extremes exhausts the overbought/oversold condition, raising reversal odds
findings.setup_summary: From a confirmed low, count record highs: each new high (including the upper shadow) is one record session; 2-3 sideways sessions between records are tolerated but a sharp countermove resets the count. After 8-10 record highs, stop adding longs and take a bearish candle signal there as a short/liquidate signal. Mirror with 8-10 record lows. The count is a guidepost - some markets turn at 6, others at 12.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A sharp 2-3 session countermove or lateral relief of the overbought condition resets the count; do not go countertrend without a candle signal.
findings.risk_geometry: No explicit stop in the book; relies on the confirming candle signal's structure; the count is deliberately non-consecutive.
findings.quote: when there are eight to ten record sessions (that is, eight to ten almost consecutive higher highs or lower lows), it increases the possibility that the preceding trend will change.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Record Sessions', pp.121-126; reused in Ch.6 and Ch.8
findings.notes: Deterministic and cheap to compute; the same count extends to kagi shoulders/waists and three-line-break lines. 24/7 trading produces many new highs/lows, so the count fires frequently on 1h BTC - a natural overextension feature for the trend group.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Hammer / hanging man / shooting star: long-shadow rejection lines gated by prior trend
findings.mechanism: a long shadow rejecting an extreme after a one-sided move reveals exhaustion of the losing side
findings.setup_summary: After a significant downtrend, a bar with a long lower shadow, a small real body near the top of the range and little/no upper shadow is a hammer (bullish): buy at the close or on a successful retest of the hammer's low. The identical shape after a rally is a hanging man (bearish) and needs confirmation - the next bar closing under the hanging man's real body; a close above the hanging man's high voids it. A long upper shadow with a small body near the bottom after an uptrend is a shooting star (bearish). The same shape inside a sideways range has no reversal meaning.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Hammer: close below the hammer's low. Hanging man: close above its high (unconfirmed) or confirmed by a next-session close under its real body. Shooting star: close above its high. No prior trend = pattern void.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at bar close or on retest; stop under the hammer's low (close-based); hanging man confirmation = next close under its real body; book suggests scaling in - light on signal, add after successful retest.
findings.quote: If it appears from below, buy, and if appears from above, sell... as reversal signals; they need a prior trend to reverse.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Single Candle Lines', pp.56-68
findings.notes: The trend-context gate (pattern void in ranges) is exactly a still_valid condition for a V8 expert. Springs (failed breakdown below support that reclaims) and upthrusts (failed breakout above resistance that fails) are the Western names for the same probe-and-reject action and pair naturally with the existing sweep-reclaim family.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Doji at extended moves: equilibrium bar, doji-as-S/R, next-session confirmation
findings.mechanism: open approximately equals close at an extreme of a mature move: supply and demand in balance and the directional drive has stalled
findings.setup_summary: A bar whose open and close are equal (doji) after a steep advance - especially directly after a tall white candle - is a transition signal, not an outright sell: wait 1-2 sessions for bearish confirmation. The doji's high acts as resistance; a buy stop sits above it (a close above means the market is 'refreshed' and the uptrend resumes). Symmetric for a doji after a steep decline: a subsequent white candle resolves the balance bullishly; stop under the doji's low. A doji early in a young trend or in a range is weak/neutral.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Close above the doji high voids the bearish doji; close below the doji low voids the bullish one; a near-doji amid a run of small bodies is not significant.
findings.risk_geometry: Confirmation wait of 1-2 bars; stop under the doji's low (bullish scenario) or above its high (bearish); the doji extreme becomes structural S/R.
findings.quote: a doji that emerges after the mature part of an uptrend or sell-off has a greater chance of a market turn... a doji provides 'a hint of tops and bottoms'... traders should view the doji as echoing a market in transition rather than being an outright reversal pattern.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.2 'Doji', pp.45-50; Ch.3 'Gapping Doji', pp.106-109
findings.notes: Gravestone doji (open/high/close near the low of the range) is the stronger top variant; the book pairs doji with ROC/divergence corroboration. On 24/7 crypto the 'next session' is simply the next 1h bar, making the confirmation rule mechanical. The confirmation gate is a strong lifecycle-rule candidate.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Engulfing patterns: body-size asymmetry determines reversal vs consolidation
findings.mechanism: a large body fully enveloping a small opposite body demonstrates a decisive shift in supply/demand control
findings.setup_summary: Bearish engulfing: during a rally, a black body whose range wraps the prior white body's range; bullish engulfing is the mirror after a decline. The strictest version has a small first body and a very large second body whose range includes the first candle's shadows. Reliability scales with size asymmetry - two nearly equal bodies typically resolve into a lateral band rather than a reversal (a volatility-fade signal). A bearish engulfing following a doji is especially bearish. Engulfing extremes become support/resistance.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Close above the top of the bearish engulfing (including shadows) voids it, flipping to bullish; the same shape in a downtrend is a last-engulfing bottom (bullish), not bearish.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on pattern-completion close; stop on a close above/below the engulfing extremes; book example: buy pullback to bullish engulfing support, target = prior resistance, stop under the engulfing lows.
findings.quote: the strictest definition of an engulfing pattern would be if the first candle is small and the second candle very large, and the second real body wraps around the entire first candle-including its shadows... if there are two almost equal size candles... the market may move into a lateral band, rather than reverse.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'The Engulfing Patterns', pp.76-85
findings.notes: The size-asymmetry condition and the equal-size-to-consolidation prediction are both falsifiable. The stock-vs-futures definitional flexibility is moot on perps (opens are arbitrary); the after-doji warning and engulfing-as-S/R rules port directly. Harami (inverse engulfing) and last-engulfing are closely related variants kept in the same family.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Dark cloud cover / piercing pattern: depth of counter-candle penetration
findings.mechanism: how deep a counter-candle closes into the prior body measures how completely the opposing force has reversed control
findings.setup_summary: Dark cloud cover: after an uptrend, a tall white bar followed by a black bar that opens above the white bar's high (futures) or above the white bar's close (stocks/perps) and closes below the midpoint of the white body. Deeper penetration = more bearish; a close short of the midpoint is incomplete and requires next-session weakness for confirmation. The pattern becomes resistance (stop on a close above its high). The piercing pattern is the bullish mirror: a white bar closing more than halfway into a prior black body after a decline.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Close above the dark-cloud high voids it; incomplete (<50% penetration) needs confirmation; the preceding trend is required for either pattern.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on completion close; stop on a close above the dark cloud's high; targets from Western tools (change of polarity, prior S/R); the book explicitly demonstrates skipping a trade where risk approximates reward.
findings.quote: As a general rule, the deeper the close of the dark cloud cover's second session pushes into the white candle, the more bearish the signal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Dark Cloud Cover' and 'The Piercing Pattern', pp.68-76
findings.notes: The midpoint penetration rule is precisely quantifiable for a rule-based expert. The book notes dark cloud covers are more frequent than piercing patterns (fear/greed asymmetry at tops vs bottoms). Both patterns become structural S/R after completion.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Accumulation/distribution: high-volume stagnant-price sessions at extremes
findings.mechanism: high volume with stagnant price at an extreme reveals absorption: one side's ammunition is spent
findings.setup_summary: At a low price level after a decline, a session with heavy volume and a tiny real body (spinning top) that pushes a new low but cannot sustain it = accumulation (bears sell into full force yet price stagnates; all supply absorbed) - long bias, confirmed by a following rally. Mirror at highs = distribution - topping bias. The small body is required to establish 'stagnant prices'.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Accumulation fails if price closes below the absorbing session's low; distribution fails if price closes above the absorbing session's high.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on confirmation after the absorbing session; stop below the accumulation low (or above the distribution high).
findings.quote: Accumulation occurs when, at a low price level, there is a high volume session with stagnant prices... All that the bears have tried to sell has been accumulated by the bulls.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.2 'Accumulation and Distribution', pp.42-44
findings.notes: The price geometry (high volume + tiny body at an extreme) is deterministic, but exchange-reported perp volume is a weak signal (wash trading, aggregate prints), so this stays backlog until the participation feature is trusted. Conceptually overlaps Wyckoff accumulation/distribution, likely corroborated by other books in this library.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Risk/reward gating and close-confirmed structural stops (candles + Western tools)
findings.mechanism: a signal's tradability is conditional on the ratio of structural risk to a reachable target, not on the pattern alone
findings.setup_summary: Never execute a candle signal in isolation: define risk as a structural stop (pattern high/low, window edge, doji extreme, flipped level) and reward as a target from a Western tool (prior support/resistance, change-of-polarity level, Fibonacci/50% retracement, moving average). Only trade when the risk/reward is attractive - the book skips a morning star with $36 risk vs $15 target, and prefers a dark cloud over a 'stronger' bearish engulfing purely on risk geometry. Stops trigger on a close through structure, not on intra-session wicks.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - an admission gate, not a position; the same discipline extends to a pre-committed invalidation price for the whole market opinion ('market chameleon').
findings.risk_geometry: Stop = structural level, close-confirmed; target = non-candle tool level; skip trades at ~1:1 or worse; candles rarely give targets so a target source must be external.
findings.quote: unless there is an attractive risk/reward ratio at the time the candle pattern is completed, stay away from the trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.4 'Stops' and 'Risk/Reward', pp.130-137
findings.notes: This is the book's central methodology lesson and matches V8's RiskGate + risk_geometry design: entry gated by reward/risk, and thesis invalidation (still_valid) on a close through a frozen structural reference rather than an intra-bar wick. Leveraged perps make the gate more binding, not less.
findings.book: Beyond Candlesticks - New Japanese Charting Techniques Revealed 1994 (1) - annotated

book_title: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies: How to Profit in the Forex Market (2013) by Mario Singh

findings.strategy_name: Trend Rider (EMA12/36 pullback with ADX momentum-exhaustion exit)
findings.mechanism: After a momentum-confirmed trend shift, buy the pullback to the fast EMA and ride until momentum exhausts; no fixed target prevents premature profit-taking
findings.setup_summary: On H1 or H4, wait for EMA12 to cross above EMA36 (long bias). Enter long when price pulls back to touch EMA12. Stop at EMA36 (minimum 30 pips from entry). No predetermined profit target; exit when ADX(14) crosses above 40 and then drops back below 40.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Stop at EMA36 (min 30 pips) hit; EMA12 re-crosses EMA36.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on EMA12 touch (next-bar); stop at EMA36, minimum 30 pips; target = ADX-40 exhaustion exit (no fixed R); no fixed expiry; book example achieved 1:5.4 R.
findings.quote: Once the ADX crosses above 40 and comes back below, it is telling us that the momentum is losing steam and it's time to exit the trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Strategy 7 (Trend Rider), pp. 155-163
findings.notes: Nearly identical to the existing V8 trend_pullback expert (ema_fast>ema_slow, close<ema_slow). Adds two concretely falsifiable refinements: (1) entry only at the EMA12 touch rather than any below-EMA bar; (2) an explicit momentum-exhaustion exit (ADX14 >40 then <40) that could serve as a dead-thesis/still_valid rule. Book explicitly argues premature exit is the main retail failure mode.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Piranha (Bollinger band-touch scalping with regime-flip-on-stop rule)
findings.mechanism: In a range, price touching the outer Bollinger band reverts toward the mean; a stop-out at the band is itself a regime signal that the market has left the range and begun trending
findings.setup_summary: On M5 GBP/USD with Bollinger Bands (MA 12, Dev 2), go long when price touches the lower band and short when it touches the upper band. Stop 10 pips, target 5 pips (risk:reward 2:1, negative expectancy per-trade compensated by high frequency). Avoid trading during major US/UK news releases.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Stop-out indicates the band is no longer holding; the next trade should be the OPPOSITE direction of the stopped-out trade.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on band touch (market order at touch); stop 10 pips fixed; target 5 pips fixed; no expiry.
findings.quote: hitting a stop loss is a telltale sign that the market is no longer trading in a band and it is starting to move into a trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, Strategy 2 (Piranha), pp. 118-124
findings.notes: Fixed 10/5-pip geometry does not transfer to BTC (scale by ATR instead). The transferable mechanism is the stop-out-as-regime-change lifecycle rule: when a mean-reversion band strategy is stopped out, that bar-level event is evidence the regime switched to trend - a candidate lifecycle/regime rule for V8. M5 frame is outside V8's 1h focus.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Fade the Break (false-break candle close-rejection at support/resistance)
findings.mechanism: Institutional traders trap retail break-out chasers; a wick through a level that fails to close through it reveals lack of momentum and the level reverts
findings.setup_summary: On M15/M30 at a prior swing support, wait for a candle whose shadow wicks below support but which CLOSES back above (bull close) - the false-break candle. Enter long at the open of the next candle. Stop 5 pips below the false-break candle's low. Two targets at 1:1 and 1:2 R. Short mirror at resistance.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Close stays beyond the level (breakout is real, not false).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at next-bar open; stop 5 pips beyond the false-break candle's extreme; two targets at 1R and 2R.
findings.quote: Markets often reverse after a failure to break above the resistance level or below the support level.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, Strategy 3 (Fade the Break), pp. 126-131
findings.notes: Directly refines existing V8 liquidity_sweep_reclaim / failed_breakout experts: specifies candle-close confirmation, next-bar-open entry, a 5-pip buffer stop beyond the false-break candle extreme (scale to ATR for BTC), and dual 1:1/1:2 targets. Book frames the mechanism as retail-vs-institutional battle at S/R.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Trade the Break (close-confirmed breakout with in-range 60% stop)
findings.mechanism: A candle CLOSE beyond resistance/support is the market's confirmation that momentum is sufficient to continue; the stop placed deep inside the prior range survives the common whipsaw back into the range
findings.setup_summary: On M15/M30, define support/resistance from at least two swing highs and two swing lows. When a candle closes above resistance (breakout candle), enter long at the open of the next candle. Place the stop at the 60% mark of the prior range BELOW resistance (i.e., deep inside the range). Two targets at 1:1 and 1:2 R. Short mirror at support.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Stop (60% into range) hit; opposite-side close breaks the level first.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at next-bar open; stop at 60% of range measured from the broken level into the range; targets 1R and 2R.
findings.quote: The stop loss is placed below the midpoint of the prior range because we do not expect prices to fall back below that point.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, Strategy 4 (Trade the Break), pp. 131-137
findings.notes: Distinct from the V8 backlog breakout_retest (no retest wait - enters next bar after close confirmation). The distinctive risk-geometry contribution is the in-range stop placement at 60% of the range, which directly addresses breakout whipsaw. No-gap perps make the stop placement unambiguous.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Swap and Fly (carry capture with breakeven-shifted stop)
findings.mechanism: Holding a position that earns positive interest/funding generates profit by time alone once the trade reaches breakeven; the carry accrual replaces the need for price appreciation
findings.setup_summary: On D1/W1, select the pair with the highest positive swap on the intended side (book: long AUD/JPY, short GBP/AUD). Enter on a three-white-soldiers (long) or three-black-crows (short) candle pattern at the open of the next candle; stop at a recent significant low/high. When price reaches +1R, shift the stop to entry (breakeven); hold until the breakeven stop is hit - swap accrued over weeks makes the exit profitable (book example: ~1.2 pips/week swap, breakeven after 36 weeks).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Stop hit before price reaches +1R (no breakeven shift possible).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at next-bar open after pattern; stop at recent swing; shift stop to entry at +1R; no target (hold for carry); optional full exit at >=1:3 R.
findings.quote: After a period of time, even if our 'new' stop-loss level is hit, the trade is exited with a profit because of the swap earned.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, Strategy 12 (Swap and Fly), pp. 192-199
findings.notes: The perp analog is funding: hold BTCUSDT long while funding is positive (or short when negative), shift stop to BE at +1R, let funding accrue. Directly uses the V8 'flow' feature group (funding). DATA_BLOCKED until a funding-rate feed is added to the tape. Swap rates are broker/time-varying - same caveat applies to perp funding.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Commodity Correlation (oil->CAD/JPY; Dollar Index->gold XAU/USD)
findings.mechanism: Commodity price action leads a correlated currency: oil breaks out -> CAD/JPY follows (positive correlation, Canada net oil exporter, Japan net importer); Dollar Index breaks support -> gold rallies (inverse correlation)
findings.setup_summary: On D1, use the lead instrument's support/resistance: if a candle closes above oil resistance, go long CAD/JPY at the next day's open; if a candle closes below Dollar Index support, go long XAU/USD at the next day's open (inverse). Stop at 2x ATR of the prior candle; target at 1:3 R.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Stop (2x ATR) hit; correlation regime shift (book cites gold-Dollar Index correlation of -0.6 to -0.8 during 2011-2012, i.e., not stable).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at next-day open; stop 2x ATR of previous candle; target 3R.
findings.quote: The price movement on the oil chart is used as a reference to trigger a trade on the CAD/JPY.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, Strategy 13 (Commodity Correlation Parts 1 & 2), pp. 199-210
findings.notes: The FX proxy mappings (oil->CAD/JPY, DXY->gold) do not transfer to BTCUSDT, but the cross-market-lead mechanism and the 2x-ATR stop / 3R target geometry are usable once V8 ingests gold/DXY/equity data (cross_market feature group). Correlation instability is the main risk; book itself reports a range, not a stable coefficient.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Fifth Element (MACD histogram 5-bar momentum confirmation)
findings.mechanism: A MACD-histogram sign flip is only reliable once confirmed by N consecutive same-sign bars; the delayed 5th-bar entry filters false flips and makes the entry time predictable
findings.setup_summary: On H1/H4 with MT4-style MACD (12,26,9): when the histogram flips negative->positive, wait for four positive bars, then enter long at the OPEN of the fifth positive bar. Stop at the last histogram-swing low. Two targets at 1:1 and 1:2 R. Short mirror on positive->negative flip.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Histogram re-crosses to the prior sign before five bars accumulate.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at 5th-bar open; stop at last swing extreme of the histogram; targets 1R and 2R.
findings.quote: We wait for five positive bars on the histogram to confirm the momentum before entering a long trade on the fifth bar.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Strategy 9 (Fifth Element), pp. 169-177
findings.notes: Pure deterministic price/indicator mechanics on 1h BTC. The generalizable idea is the N-bar confirmation delay as a false-signal filter for momentum flips (relates to V8 momentum_signature starter id). Book's 'know your entry 5 bars ahead' property is a scheduling convenience, not an edge.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Power Ranger (trend-aligned stochastic pullback in a forming range)
findings.mechanism: In an uptrend, an oversold stochastic reading is a pullback to buy, not a reversal signal; entry at the stochastic re-cross, with the admission gate that the stop must sit beyond the range edge
findings.setup_summary: On H1/H4, establish trend direction from a series of higher highs/higher lows (long bias). In an uptrend, when stochastic %K/%D go below level 20 and cross back above 20, enter long; short mirror in a downtrend with level 80. TP1 at the 75% mark of the range; stop at 1:1 R; TP2 at 1:2 R beyond the range (anticipating breakout). Trade is INVALID if the computed stop is not below support (longs) / above resistance (shorts).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Stop would sit inside the range (invalid trade); stochastic re-cross fails to trigger.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on stochastic re-cross; stop 1R and must be beyond the range edge; TP1 at 75% of range; TP2 at 1:2 R beyond range.
findings.quote: In an uptrend, look for the oversold region. In a downtrend, look for the overbought region.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Strategy 10 (Power Ranger), pp. 177-184
findings.notes: The key transferable rules: (1) never trade the oscillator signal against trend momentum (buy oversold in uptrend only); (2) the invalidation gate - stop must be beyond the range edge or the trade is skipped - is a clean, deterministic admission rule for V8.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: The Pendulum (fraction-of-range mean reversion)
findings.mechanism: In a formed range, price that is rejected from support/resistance snaps back toward the range midpoint; entering only after a 10% retracement filters weak bounces, and fraction-of-range targets quantify the reversion
findings.setup_summary: On H1/H4, identify a formed range (support + resistance). After price turns back from support, enter long once price has retraced 10% of the range upward off support. TP1 at 50% of the range, TP2 at 90% of the range; stop set at 1:1 R. Short mirror off resistance.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Price breaks support/resistance instead of turning (the pendulum string snaps -> range breaks into a trend).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at 10% retracement off support/resistance; stop 1R; targets at 50% and 90% of the range.
findings.quote: We do this by executing a trade only at the 10% mark after prices turn back from either support or resistance.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Strategy 11 (The Pendulum), pp. 185-190
findings.notes: The 10/50/90 fraction-of-range geometry is precise and deterministic on 1h BTC. Complementary to Power Ranger (same range, later stage). Range identification is the fragile input; perps' lack of gaps makes range definition cleaner than in FX.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Guppy Burst (quiet-window range breakout via dual pending stops)
findings.mechanism: Volatility compression during a quiet session window precedes expansion; the compression-range edges act as objective breakout triggers, and the mechanical pending-order structure removes timing discretion
findings.setup_summary: On M5 GBP/JPY, in the ~3-hour window after the US market closes (before Asia opens), record the range: highest high = resistance, lowest low = support. Place a pending buy stop at resistance and a pending sell stop at support. TP = 2x the range distance (1:2 R). When one trigger fires, immediately cancel the other pending order.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Opposite pending order triggers first; window expires without a trigger.
findings.risk_geometry: Pending stop entries at range edges; stop at the opposite edge; TP 2x stop distance; intra-window expiry.
findings.quote: The guppy burst seeks to identify the trading range during this 3-hour window and anticipate a potential breakout of the trading range.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, Strategy 15 (Guppy Burst), pp. 217-223
findings.notes: The compression->expansion mechanism and dual-pending-stop structure transfer to crypto, but the '3-hour window after US close' is FX-session-specific; in 24/7 perps the quiet window must be defined by volatility percentile (e.g., lowest-ATR hours) rather than clock time. M5 frame is outside V8's 1h focus.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Rule of 20 news trading (Gawk the Talk / Balk the Talk)
findings.mechanism: Markets price expectations, not levels; only surprises beyond a deviation threshold move price in the direction of the deviation, so trade actual-vs-forecast deviations, not the number itself
findings.setup_summary: Around scheduled news on M15/M30, compare actual vs forecast. If actual exceeds forecast by >=20% (special cases: PMI >=50 bps; interest rates >=20 bps), trade the affected currency in the direction of the deviation - long if the affected currency is the base, short if it is the counter currency. Stop 20 pips, target 40 pips. Short (Balk the Talk) when actual falls short of forecast by >=20%.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Deviation below the 20% threshold - no trade (previous and forecast values alone carry no weight).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry after release (next candle); stop 20 pips; target 40 pips (1:2 R).
findings.quote: If the deviation between the actual and forecasted figures exceeds 20%, trade in the direction of the deviation.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, Trading the News + Strategies 5 & 6 (Gawk the Talk / Balk the Talk), pp. 138-153
findings.notes: BTC reacts to CPI/FOMC surprises, so the mechanism is testable, but V8's tape contains no macro calendar with forecast/actual - the strategy is gated on external data (DEFER_GATED). Fixed 20/40-pip geometry does not transfer to BTC vol. The claim that 'traders trade based on expectations' is trader folklore, not statistically validated in the book.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Exit discipline and mandatory stop-loss (The Experiment / three points in every trade)
findings.mechanism: With an identical strategy, results diverge because of exit meddling - premature manual exits destroy expectancy; and a trade without a stop loss is an account blow-up risk
findings.setup_summary: Methodology lesson (not a tradeable signal): (1) every trade has three points - entry, profit target, stop loss - and a stop loss is mandatory on every position; (2) after entry, do not interfere: let the trade hit either its stop or its target. In the book's controlled experiment, two traders with identical capital, entries, and trade count diverged to 10% vs 2% monthly return solely because one meddled with exits (exited 'too impatiently').
findings.trigger_invalidation: None - this is a discipline rule, not a directional setup.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - stop loss mandatory on every position; exit only at the pre-set stop or target (no manual premature exits).
findings.quote: the biggest reason for the difference in their accounts was that Amanda constantly meddled with her trades
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, The Experiment, pp. 88-107; Chapter 2, Three Points in Every Trade, pp. 17-23
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's design: stops/targets execute without manual interference, dead-thesis (still_valid) is a separate exit from stops, and RiskGate mandates a stop on every admission. The 'naked trade' prohibition (no stop loss) maps directly to V8's RiskGate admission rule. n=2 experiment is anecdotal; treat as methodology corroboration, not empirical evidence.
findings.book: 17 Proven Currency Trading Strategies - How to Profit in the Forex Market 2013

findings.strategy_name: Swing Rule Projection
findings.mechanism: swing symmetry target projection: the retracement height from a swing peak to the pullback valley projects the height of the next swing in the trend direction
findings.setup_summary: In an uptrend (daily bars), take the drop from peak 1 to valley 2 (height X) and add it to peak 1 to get the target for the next rise: e.g. A peaks at 29.17, B bottoms at 25.02 (height 4.15), target 33.32, actual peak 32.83. Mirror for downtrends by subtracting the rise height from the peak. Falsifiable: in the book's 2000-2011 US-equity test (32,042 up-trend / 24,620 down-trend samples) the target landed within +/-5 percent of projection 80% of the time in uptrends (86% for swings under 10% in height), 67% in downtrends (78% for small swings).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Projection is invalidated when price reverses before reaching the symmetry target (undershoot) or overshoots through it; accuracy degrades for swings larger than about 10% in height.
findings.risk_geometry: Target-only method: the book specifies no entry/stop/expiry; target = peak + prior retracement height (minus for shorts); the most reliable inputs are small swings (<10%).
findings.quote: In up trends, it accurately predicts when price is going to peak 80 percent of the time.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 28 'Swing Rule' (pp. 299-302)
findings.notes: Measured on daily US equities, so the 80% hit-rate is instrument-specific and must be re-tested on BTCUSDT. In 24/7 perps swing points form continuously with no session gaps, so the projection is computable on any bar size. Best V8 use: a target-projection feature to refine risk_geometry target selection rather than a standalone entry expert.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Chart Pattern Breakout Hold
findings.mechanism: pattern breakout continuation: an upward breakout from a completed chart pattern starts a position held until a different chart pattern breaks downward or the structure stop is hit
findings.setup_summary: Buy when price closes above a chart-pattern boundary (17 pattern types tested; ascending and symmetrical triangles excluded as buy signals, used only for exits). Place a stop a penny below the bottom of the pattern, hold until a downward breakout from another chart pattern or the stop, with no trailing stop. Tested on 500 stocks: 1,333 in-sample trades (win/loss 59%, avg +27%, avg hold 325 days) and 4,185 out-of-sample (win/loss 48%, avg +25%, avg hold 254 days).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Close back below the pattern bottom after the breakout (bust or stop); worst observed trade was -72% when a tall double bottom retraced through the pattern.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry = breakout bar close; stop = one tick below the pattern bottom (structure stop, not ATR); no trailing; exit = next pattern downward breakout or stop; hold horizon measured in months (254-325 days).
findings.quote: Buy when the stock breaks out upward from a chart pattern... place a stop loss order a penny below the bottom of the chart pattern. Hold until price breaks out downward from another chart pattern or price hits the stop.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 29 'A Tale of Two Trades' (pp. 305-306)
findings.notes: Hold horizon of ~300 days is far outside the V8 1h-expert envelope (expiry_bars ~8); best translated to a longer-bar swing horizon or mined for its methodology (structure-defined stop below pattern). The book adds 'Chart patterns work only when the market trends' - trend conditionality is a family prerequisite. On perps, multi-month funding drag must be modeled.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Breakout regime filter: entries below 200-day SMA outperform above
findings.mechanism: long-term trend regime conditions breakout outcome: chart-pattern breakouts occurring below the 200-day SMA performed equal or better than those above it, contradicting the common assumption
findings.setup_summary: For chart-pattern breakout entries, add a buy rule: enter only if the breakout price is below the 200-day simple moving average. Out-of-sample (1996-2012, 1,685 trades in the <200 SMA column): win/loss 50%, average profit +26%, average hold 247 days, versus worse performance for breakouts above the SMA. The author's instruction is to test both ways rather than assume the naive 'above = better' belief.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - a filter, not a standalone strategy; it gates entries of the breakout-hold family.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A
findings.quote: Patterns with breakouts above the 200-day SMA performed worse.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 29 'A Tale of Two Trades', FAST FACTS + results table (p. 306)
findings.notes: On 1h BTC a 200-day SMA is a 4,800-bar lookback - computable but slow-moving; crypto trend regimes are longer-tailed and funding-linked. The claim is falsifiable on crypto data and directly testable as a V8 regime filter, but the conclusion must be re-tested, not ported.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Trendline Break Requires 1-2-3 Confirmation
findings.mechanism: a single close through a trendline is insufficient evidence of trend change; reversal is confirmed only by the first counter-trend peak and valley (1-2-3 sequence)
findings.setup_summary: When price closes below an up-trendline (or above a down-trendline), do not declare a trend change on that bar; require the 1-2-3 sequence: first lower peak then first lower valley to confirm an uptrend reversal, first higher peak then first higher valley to confirm a downtrend reversal (the book's Test Yourself marks the 'higher peak + higher valley = change' reading as False). Related: triangle trendlines extended into the future act as future support/resistance areas (apex pivots), a location feature.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - the rule is itself the confirmation criterion for declaring a trend thesis dead.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A (lifecycle); informs the V8 separation of stop-out (price level) from dead-thesis (structure) exits.
findings.quote: When price closes below a trendline, it is often not sufficient evidence of a trend change.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 27 'Trendline Sell Signals' (p. 297-298); Chapter 28 Test Yourself (p. 301): 'The trendlines of a triangle, extended into the future, can act as support and resistance areas.'
findings.notes: Directly relevant to 24/7 crypto: 1h BTC produces frequent false trendline breaks, so a lifecycle rule requiring peak/valley confirmation before marking a thesis dead (as opposed to a stop-out) should reduce whipsaw and matches V8's stops-vs-dead-thesis principle.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Measure Rule Pattern-Height Target
findings.mechanism: pattern-height projection: the chart pattern's height (highest peak minus lowest valley) projected from the breakout level estimates the post-breakout move
findings.setup_summary: For a descending triangle with a downward breakout: target = value of the bottom trendline minus the pattern height. Price reaches or exceeds that target only 42% of the time (book stat). The measure rule is applied across many patterns (triangles, double tops/bottoms, H&S, rectangles, flags/pennants, triple tops), making it a general structure-target method; the ch. 29 day-trader use is 'enter on pattern breakout, exit at the measure rule target.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: Target undershoot is the norm for descending-triangle down-breakouts (missed >58% of the time), so the projected level is an aspiration, not a guaranteed fill.
findings.risk_geometry: Target = structure-projected price level; entry/stop are not specified by the rule itself.
findings.quote: Subtract the height from the value of the bottom trendline to get a price target. Price reaches or exceeds the target 42 percent of the time.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 29, DEFINITION box 'The measure rule' (p. 304)
findings.notes: Related to but distinct from the swing rule (ch. 28) - the book's own test question 'The swing rule is the same as the measure rule except that it applies to trendlines' is marked False. Both are height-projection target methods usable as structure-based targets in risk_geometry; the low 42% hit-rate argues for using them for scaling/partial exits rather than a single target.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Busted Pattern (Failed Breakout) with Bust Counting
findings.mechanism: liquidity vacuum reentry: a pattern that breaks out its normal way, fails, and closes through the opposite boundary re-enters with momentum; single/double/triple bust counts quantify how often and how reliably
findings.setup_summary: A chart pattern that breaks out, then price closes back into the pattern and breaks out the other way is a 'busted' pattern. Falsifiable claims from the book: single busts occur ~23% of the time for double tops in bull markets, double and triple busts ~5% each; single-busted patterns perform as good as or better than their non-busted counterparts; rectangles that single bust gain on average more than non-busted ones. This is the book's name for V8's failed_breakout mechanism, with bust-count as an added variant dimension.
findings.trigger_invalidation: On the first bust, a stop placed beyond the original pattern boundary takes the loss; re-entry only on a confirmed opposite-direction close-through, with the bust count (1st/2nd/3rd failure attempt) gating the trade.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on confirmed opposite breakout (close through the boundary); stop beyond the opposite side of the pattern; bust-count acts as a variant parameter that can gate entry quality.
findings.quote: Single busted chart pattern performance is as good as or better than their non-busted counterparts.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 22 'Busted Pattern Buy Setups' (pp. 229-240) and Chapter 25 'Busted Pattern Sell Signals' (pp. 271-287); index references in Part 2 (pp. 322-328)
findings.notes: Failed breakouts are a core crypto microstructure behavior (liquidity-run driven). The bust-counting framework maps directly onto a multi-attempt variant of the existing failed_breakout expert: variant = attempt number, with the claim that later attempts are rarer and lower quality being falsifiable on BTCUSDT. Full chapter text is in Part 1; Part 2 carries the index/structure.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Rectangle Range Ping-Pong (Reversion Between Boundaries)
findings.mechanism: range reversion at boundaries: in a tall rectangle, price alternates between the two near-horizontal trendlines and reverts at them
findings.setup_summary: In a tall rectangle (two near-horizontal trendlines containing price), buy near the lower boundary and sell near the upper boundary as price ping-pongs between them; reverse for the short side. The book presents this as the swing-trader's use of rectangles, complementary to the breakout use.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rectangle bust: a close through either boundary ends the ping-pong regime and triggers the breakout treatment.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry near lower boundary (LONG) / upper boundary (SHORT); stop beyond the opposite boundary; target = the far boundary.
findings.quote: Swing traders can benefit from trading tall rectangles as price ping-pongs between the two trendlines.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 29 'Closing Position' (p. 306); rectangle identification in Chapter 7 (Part 1)
findings.notes: No statistics are given for the reversion side (the book's rectangle numbers are breakout-based), so this is a heuristic. Crypto ranges are persistent but funding can bias one boundary and liquidation cascades can punch through; needs explicit boundary definition and a bust exit. V8 has no mean-reversion family yet - candidate backlog family.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Broadening Bottom Lower-Trendline Bounce
findings.mechanism: broadening range expansion: two diverging trendlines (top rising through peaks, bottom hugging valleys) with bounces off the lower line; upward breakout 53% of the time
findings.setup_summary: Identify a broadening bottom: the top trendline slopes upward through a series of peaks while the bottom trendline hugs the valleys (diverging lines). Buy two days after price bounces off the lower trendline. Falsifiable stat: broadening bottoms break out upward only 53% of the time - near coin-flip, so the directional edge is thin.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Close below the lower trendline / recent valley invalidates the bounce setup.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry = 2 days after the bounce off the lower trendline; stop = below the recent valley or lower trendline; target = upper trendline or upward breakout.
findings.quote: Broadening bottoms break out upward 53 percent of the time.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 29 'A Tale of Two Trades' (pp. 303-304); Visual Appendix p. 311
findings.notes: The 53% upward-breakout rate is barely above chance and no reward/risk stats are given, so this is a low-priority backlog candidate. The pattern does form in crypto (expanding ranges after liquidation cascades) but offers no demonstrated edge.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Gunning / Running the Stop (Stop Hunt)
findings.mechanism: stops clustered just below well-known support (round numbers, pattern bottoms, prior lows) are triggered by a price dip that overshoots the level, creating the fuel for a reversal
findings.setup_summary: Stops placed a small distance below prominent support levels (round numbers, pattern boundaries, prior lows) are vulnerable to being 'gunned' or 'run': price dips through the level to trigger the resting stops, then reverses. The book treats this as a hazard to naive stop placement under its support/resistance chapter (pp. 34-37), corroborating the stop-hunt mechanism.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - mechanism note; a run becomes tradable only when price reclaims the level (see the existing liquidity_sweep_reclaim geometry).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - supports V8's existing sweep/reclaim risk geometry (wick through the level, close back on the reclaimed side).
findings.quote: Gunning the stop, 34, 37 / Running the stop, 34, 37
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4 'Support and Resistance' (pp. 34-37); index entries in Part 2 (pp. 325-327)
findings.notes: In 24/7 crypto perps, stop clusters below round levels and liquidation cascades make stop-runs a core microstructure behavior; the mechanism corroborates the existing liquidity_sweep_reclaim expert. Part 2 only carries the index references; the full treatment is in Part 1, Chapter 4.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

book_title: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns (Bulkowski, 2012) - Part 2

findings.strategy_name: FX-Ed Trend Technique (10-day EMA pullback in strong trend)
findings.mechanism: institutional traders add positions at the 10-day EMA during runaway trends, so pullbacks to the EMA become high-probability continuation entry points; the longer the trend the more self-sustaining it becomes
findings.setup_summary: Daily chart: moving averages in 'proper order' (10>20>50>200 SMA/EMA for an uptrend, reversed for a downtrend) AND price has been above (uptrend) / below (downtrend) the 10-day EMA for at least 10 consecutive candles (the filter proving the EMA genuinely acts as support/resistance). Enter long when price dips to the 10-day EMA in an uptrend, short on a rally to it in a downtrend. Initial stop = 50% of daily ATR(14) beneath the EMA; trail the stop once per daily close, never lower it; no target — exit only when the trailing stop is hit.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No trade if MAs are not in proper order, or price cuts the 10-day EMA back and forth (EMA not acting as support/resistance); thesis invalid when a daily close breaches the trailed stop (0.5*ATR under the moving EMA).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at EMA touch (no candle-close wait); initial stop = 0.5*ATR(14) daily below EMA; stop trailed once per daily close under the moving EMA; no fixed target (let winners run); optional partial exit at the upper channel line with the remainder trailing.
findings.quote: there is considerable evidence that in extremely strong trends, pullbacks (in the case of an uptrend) or rallies (in the case of a downtrend) to the 10-day exponential moving average make particularly effective entry points for forex traders. This is because the big players are using this moving average to determine their entry points as well.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9 'The FX-Ed Trend Technique', pp.99-130
findings.notes: Refines the existing trend_pullback family with a stricter regime filter (proper-order MAs + 10-candle EMA-support proof) and a volatility-scaled trailing stop that converts a fixed expiry to a trend-exhaustion exit. CAVEAT from the book: the institutional-adds-at-the-10-day-EMA claim is explicitly daily-timeframe-specific ('there is no evidence that the big players add to positions at the 10-hour moving average'); a BTCUSDT 1h EMA-pullback expert is therefore a NEW variant (long-lookback EMA, e.g. 100-200 bars), not a replication of the book's claim.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: The Stop Run: fade the false breakout against the trend
findings.mechanism: a pool of stop orders above a well-tested resistance acts as a magnet; banks/institutions push price through the level to execute the order cluster, the breakout then fails once the orders are consumed, and trapped breakout longs covering at a loss supply the fuel for trend resumption
findings.setup_summary: In an established trend (the book's example: USD/CAD downtrend with repeated rejections at Fibonacci resistance 1.1250), a stop-run pushes price above the resistance level; if price falls back beneath the breakout point within a short window (two hours in the example), enter in the direction of the primary trend. The unwinding of breakout traders' losing longs supplies selling pressure.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No entry if the breakout succeeds and holds above the level; thesis invalid if price re-crosses back above the broken level after entry.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the return below the broken level; stop above the failed-breakout high (and above the resistance/Fibonacci level); exits via the multi-exit scheme (partial at 1R, stop to breakeven, remainder at prior support).
findings.quote: Breakouts that run in the opposite direction of the trend have a greater likelihood of failure... I would consider the breakout to have failed if the exchange rate falls back beneath the breakout point of 1.1250.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8 'The Stop Run', pp.91-97
findings.notes: Directly matches the existing failed_breakout expert (liquidity_vacuum_reentry). The book adds the causal mechanism: stop clusters above resistance attract execution pushes (more likely during quiet/low-liquidity times), and the trapped breakout longs' covering is the continuation fuel. On crypto perps this mechanism is amplified by liquidation cascades and the absence of exchange gaps; the 'pool of orders' magnet argument is a liquidity feature, not just a location pattern.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Multiple time frame strategy: higher-TF direction gate + oscillator neutral-flip entry + soft-target partial exits
findings.mechanism: trends persist across time frames, so trading only with the higher-timeframe direction and buying pullbacks (never entries at extremes) stacks probabilities; an oscillator leaving overbought/oversold back to neutral signals the counter-move has begun
findings.setup_summary: Daily chart trending (trendline, ADX, or proper-order MAs) -> trade ONLY in that direction; reject all counter-trend setups. On the hourly chart, enter long when price pulls back to prior hourly support or to a Fibonacci retracement (38.2/50/61.8%) of the daily move that coincides with a prior S/R level, AND a 14-period RSI (or slow stochastic) has flipped from overbought back into neutral territory. Stop above the recent swing high and above the Fibonacci level.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No trade if no discernible daily trend (technique is for trending markets only); never enter on the oscillator signal alone without the price-level confluence; invalid for shorts if price makes a new high beyond the stop level.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at Fibonacci/prior-support confluence when RSI crosses back to neutral; stop above recent high and above the Fibonacci level; exits: partial at 1R with stop moved to breakeven, remainder at prior support levels; book's 'soft target' tweak: raise S/R-based exits by ~10% of the support-resistance range so exits land ahead of round numbers and above the bottom of support.
findings.quote: First, we'll determine the direction in which we want to trade from the long-term chart; then, we'll look to the short-term chart to locate our entry point, stop, and exits.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8 'Forex Multiple Time Frame Strategy', pp.69-98
findings.notes: Adds two refinements to the existing trend_pullback family: (1) a hard higher-TF direction gate (phantom-signal discipline - do not take counter-trend setups even when they 'would have worked'), and (2) the 'overbought does not equal sell' rule - wait for the oscillator to flip to neutral before entry, sacrificing the exact top/bottom for confirmation. Its exit scheme (partial at 1R -> stop to breakeven -> remainder at prior support, with soft targets) is the book's recurring lifecycle pattern and is a candidate lifecycle_rule refinement for V8.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: The Squeeze Play: volatility-cycle breakout from compression
findings.mechanism: volatility runs in cycles - high-volatility trends are followed by low-volatility consolidation; once compression is confirmed, the next expansion is imminent, and traders caught on the wrong side of the breakout fuel it (longer consolidation -> stronger breakout)
findings.setup_summary: Daily chart: price consolidates into a narrowing range; 20-period EMA flattens; ATR(14) is falling; Bollinger band width is near its lows. Draw trend lines forming a symmetrical triangle; go long on a break above the upper trendline or short below the lower trendline. Exits are mapped IN ADVANCE in both directions (prior support/resistance, Fibonacci retracements of the prior move, round numbers).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Setup only valid if all three contraction confirmations agree (flat 20-EMA, falling ATR, falling band width); if volatility is not compressing, no trade. A false break: stop placed on the far side of the trendline; thesis invalid if price closes back inside the triangle.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on trendline break (either direction); stop on the far side of the trendline; exits pre-mapped at prior S/R, Fibonacci, round numbers; partial exit at first target with stop moved to breakeven.
findings.quote: The longer the amount of time spent in the consolidation phase, the stronger the breakout tends to be... there are likely to be a large number of traders who are caught on the 'wrong side' of the market... As these traders cover their positions, they provide fuel for the breakout.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 13 'The Squeeze Play', pp.169-180
findings.notes: Volatility compression-expansion is pronounced in BTC perps (funding + leverage amplify the trapped-position fuel). Fully specifiable: ATR/Bollinger-width contraction thresholds, triangle-break entry, pre-mapped exits - fits V8's frozen-ref discipline. The 'longer consolidation = stronger breakout' claim is a falsifiable hypothesis to test on BTCUSDT 1h/4h. Register as new expert_family proposal (data-ready, no block).
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Flag and pennant continuation with flagpole-measured geometry
findings.mechanism: a sharp directional thrust (flagpole) expresses committed aggressive buying/selling; the small counter-slope consolidation (flag) or converging consolidation (pennant) is weak hands unloading; the aggressor side resumes and the pattern resolves as a continuation breakout in the pole's direction
findings.setup_summary: Intraday chart: a sharp 100-200 pip thrust (flagpole) is followed by a small consolidation (pennant = two lines converging like a symmetrical triangle; flag = two parallel lines sloping against the pole). Entry order = 10% of flagpole height above the pole top (long) / below the pole bottom (short); stop = 25% of pole height below/above the ENTRY (not the pole top); first exit = 1R (partial, stop to breakeven); second exit = pole height measured from the pole top.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No entry if price clears the flag's line but fails to reach 10%-above-pole-top (filtered example: the flag breakout that cannot clear the pole top is an inferior entry that fails); if the initial move is not sharp/sudden, the pattern's reliability is void.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: resting order at pole_top + 0.10*pole_height; stop: entry - 0.25*pole_height; exit1 = +1R with stop to breakeven; exit2 = pole_top + pole_height. Geometry is pole-scaled (fixed-percent, volatility-adaptive).
findings.quote: Our entry will be at a point above the flagpole, by an amount equal to 10 percent of the flagpole... the stop will be placed a number of pips equal to 25 percent of the height of the flagpole.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 12 'Flags and Pennants', pp.153-168
findings.notes: Fully mechanical and falsifiable (impulse + consolidation geometry prices entry/stop/targets), corroborated by the classic Edwards-Magee continuation-pattern literature. The 10%/25% pole-relative parameters are tuned to FX intraday scales and untested on BTC 1h; main cost is the pattern-detection feature (pole + consolidation shape) in marketstate. Backlog candidate; impulse-pullback-continuation is common in crypto.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: The Round Trip: fade extensions to round-number order clusters
findings.mechanism: traders place entries, stops, and exits at round numbers, so order clusters pool at those levels (psychological support/resistance); each test consumes the pool - the first bounce is best - and once the pool is depleted the level finally breaks
findings.setup_summary: On a 5/10/15-minute chart, price that had been tracking the 20-period MA suddenly runs at least 20 pips away from it toward a large round number (further extension = better setup). Enter long at the round number if price is falling toward it (short if rising); stop = 15 pips + spread from entry; first exit = 1R with stop moved to breakeven; second exit at prior support/resistance. Do not trade if the pair's spread exceeds 5 pips.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Only trade a FRESH round-number bounce (first bounce best; each subsequent test diminishes the order pool and the odds); invalid if price closes through the round number; the 'no spread > 5 pips' constraint is a hard rule because every pip matters in a small playing field.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at round number via limit order; stop = 15 pips + spread; exit1 = +1R, stop to breakeven; exit2 = prior S/R level; fixed-pip geometry only valid for narrow-spread pairs; max hold is intraday (the move is 'swift and brief').
findings.quote: The first bounce off of round number support or resistance is usually the best bounce... with each subsequent test, the pool of orders is diminished and the chances for a successful trade are decreased.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 14 'The Round Trip', pp.181-192
findings.notes: Round-number clustering exists in BTC (100k/70k/50k and perp liquidation walls near round levels), but the 5-15-min FX scale, the '20 pips extension' threshold, and the spread-relative stop do not transfer - a perp variant needs ATR-scaled thresholds and liquidation-cluster awareness. The 'first bounce is best' + pool-depletion claim is a falsifiable hypothesis. The S/R role-reversal (finding supply_demand_zone) explains why the ping-pong effect forms.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: The Interest Rate Edge: carry the interest-rate differential with a forward-looking exit
findings.mechanism: in every pair trade one is long one currency and short the other; being long the higher-yielding currency collects the interest-rate differential daily, and leverage magnifies the yield on capital; carry entrants' buying pressure can accelerate the trend, and markets are forward-looking so the trade unwinds when policy signals say the differential will stop widening
findings.setup_summary: Long the higher-yielding currency versus the lower-yielding one (e.g., long USD/JPY when the Fed is hiking and BoJ is at ~0%) when the differential is positive and expected to widen. Hold for months collecting the differential daily; exit on central-bank forward guidance that the differential will stop widening - the USD/JPY 2005 example dissolved into a range while the differential was still at its 4.25% peak because markets priced the expected peak.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Exit when policy signals (central-bank statements/forward guidance) indicate the differential will narrow, even if the differential itself is still large - 'financial markets are forward looking'.
findings.risk_geometry: No fixed stop; hold for months; risk is differential narrowing and adverse exchange-rate moves; leverage (50:1 to 200:1 in the book) is the risk multiplier - carry is the 'double-edged sword'.
findings.quote: The trader who is long the higher yielding of the two currencies collects interest on the trade... This creates a 'chicken-and-egg' scenario; is the pair rising because traders are entering to collect the interest, or is the relative strength and weakness of the two economies causing the pair to rally?
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 15 'The Interest Rate Edge', pp.193-200
findings.notes: The perp analogue is funding: the perp-vs-spot funding rate is the carry yield and funding expectations are forward-looking (corroborates the starter ids funding_carry / carry_unwind). But a single BTCUSDT 1h expert cannot 'go long the high-yielder, short the low-yielder' - the idea becomes a cross-sectional funding/short-basis signal (cross_market feature), not a standalone directional expert. Also relevant to the simulator cost model: funding accrual must be modeled for hold-forever style experts.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: The Boomerang: fade low-volume breakouts in the FX dead zone
findings.mechanism: in the thin window between the US close and the Asian open, orders too small to matter in normal volume can move the market; such moves are unreliable and likely to retrace to the opening price
findings.setup_summary: EUR/USD only, just after 17:00 NY (after most market makers' interest rollover): place a sell order 15 pips above the 5-minute 'opening' price and a buy order 15 pips below it; stop 15 pips (1:1 risk-reward); target = the opening price; cancel BOTH orders if neither fills within 2 hours (before Asian volume arrives).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Cancel both orders after 2 hours - the 'moves are false' thesis only holds inside the low-volume window; a 15-pip stop invalidates the trade if price sustains a 30-pip move (15 to trigger + 15 to stop, called 'a rarity' at this time of day).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: both-sided resting limit orders 15 pips from the open; stop = 15 pips; target = the open; max hold 2 hours; fixed-pip parameters valid only for EUR/USD (narrow spread, specific volatility).
findings.quote: Breakouts that occur during these hours are notoriously unreliable, because they almost always occur on very low volume... Since any movement that occurs at this time is unreliable and likely to retrace, we can create a strategy that is designed to capitalize on these false breakouts, by 'fading' or trading against them.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 16 'The Boomerang', pp.201-206
findings.notes: Rejected for V8 as a standalone expert: the premise (a US-close dead zone with market-maker interest rollover at 17:00 NY) has no crypto-perp equivalent - BTCUSDT is 24/7 with hourly funding and no settlement-rollover cliff. The closest crypto analogue (weekend/Sunday low-liquidity windows) is neither as deep nor as clock-deterministic. Its kernel - low-participation breakouts are suspect and fadeable - survives only as the participation/time regime filter in the time_of_day finding; the fixed-geometry trade itself does not transfer.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Support becomes resistance: the S/R role-reversal mechanism
findings.mechanism: traders who bought at a repeatedly-holding support level are conditioned to buy again; when support finally breaks, those traders hold losing positions, and when price returns to the former level they exit at breakeven out of relief - that selling turns former support into resistance (and vice versa)
findings.setup_summary: After a well-tested support level breaks (or a well-tested resistance breaks), expect the old level to act as the opposite pole on the return: place shorts near former support that has flipped to resistance, longs near former resistance that has flipped to support; treat S/R as AREAS not exact prices (soft targets).
findings.trigger_invalidation: If the level is never re-tested, no trade; if price breaks back through the flipped level, the role-reversal thesis is void - 'if the reason for entering the trade is no longer valid, then the trade itself is no longer valid'.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry via resting order above support / below resistance (don't stand in front of the freight train - never place the entry directly on the level; wait for the bounce and enter as price rises/falls away from it); stop on the far side of the level.
findings.quote: If enough selling occurs as the price nears the former support level, the exchange rate will reverse and begin to fall. Now, the former area of support has become an area of resistance.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 10 'The Ultimate Indicator', pp.133-144
findings.notes: This is the causal engine behind the location feature group and the failed_breakout/liquidity_sweep_reclaim experts in V8: prior-tested-and-broken levels as opposite-pole magnets, driven by trapped-position unwinding (the 'pleasure principle' - traders escape at breakeven). On perps, liquidation clusters at broken levels amplify the flip. Propose a location feature: 'windowed role-flip of prior extreme (was support, now overhead resistance)' frozen at entry.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Three-regime doctrine: proper-order MAs + ADX for trend/range classification
findings.mechanism: markets are in one of three states (trending, range-bound, consolidating) and each requires different techniques; MA proper order and ADX classify the state; traders who 'fall in love' with a technique that worked in one regime lose when the regime changes
findings.setup_summary: Classify regime per instrument: UPTREND if 10>20>50>200 SMA/EMA order holds, DOWNTREND if 200>50>20>10, RANGE if the MAs are jumbled/flat ('spaghetti'), CONSOLIDATION if price is trapped in a narrowing area. ADX >35 and rising = strongly trending. Use trend techniques only in trending regimes, range techniques only in ranges, and switch when the regime changes.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Re-evaluate regime continuously; the 2004 USD/CHF example shows a trend regime decaying into consolidation while traders who kept trading trend technique got hurt; a false tendency (e.g., 'euro strong on Thursday') is a coincidence, not a tendency, and has coin-flip odds minus the spread.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry geometry - this is a gating filter that decides WHICH expert family may fire.
findings.quote: The 10-period simple moving average (SMA) is located above the 20-period SMA, which is above the 50-period SMA, which is above the 200-period SMA: 10 > 20 > 50 > 200... the ADX indicator's giving a reading above 35 and rising would be an indication of a strongly trending market.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4 'Trends' pp.39-42; Chapter 6 'Understanding Trends and Tendencies', pp.53-62
findings.notes: This is the book's central methodology thesis and maps directly onto V8's need to gate trend vs range experts (rule 14 complexity discipline and regime-dependent expert activation). Propose trend/regime features in marketstate: proper-order MA alignment flag, ADX(14)>35 rising, and a jumbled-MA range flag; use as a hard gate (e.g., trend_pullback only fires in trending regime). Also the 'don't fall in love with a technique' lesson is a lifecycle/portfolio-level methodology note.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: The playing field: spread drag and target-sizing game theory
findings.mechanism: the spread is the house edge (roulette zero pockets); with a fixed spread, small targets suffer massively worse raw odds than large targets, because the spread is a larger fraction of the move - target size is a first-order determinant of win probability before any strategy
findings.setup_summary: Quantitative lesson, not a trade: with a 3-pip spread, a trader targeting +10 pips needs a 13-pip favorable move but loses 10 pips on only a 7-pip adverse move (raw odds 1.857:1 against); targeting +100 pips needs 103 vs 97 (raw odds 1.06:1). Larger targets and longer holds shrink the spread's relative drag; traders are also paid the spread less often. A 6%/month goal compounds to ~100%/year; use a monthly 'account stop' (stop trading for the month when gains retrace to the goal level).
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - methodology lesson; applies to how experts are sized and how the simulator cost model treats fees.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A. Sizing/odds lesson: never accept spreads >5 pips for small-target trades; prefer R-multiples large enough that fees/funding/spread are a small fraction of the target.
findings.quote: in order to turn a profit of 10 pips, the trader actually needs the exchange rate to move 13 pips in his or her favor: 10 + 3 = 13... an adverse move of just 7 pips will result in an equivalent loss of 10 pips... The 'raw odds' of 10-pip win versus a 10-pip loss... 13/7 = 1.857 : 1
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 18 'The Forex Playing Field', pp.215-222
findings.notes: Directly relevant to V8's economic verdict discipline: the simulator's Binance USDM cost model (taker/maker fees ~2-10bps + funding) is the crypto analogue of the spread, and it must be an explicit term in expert evaluation. Supports V8's target_r>=1.0 R-multiple convention and argues against low-target variants. Also a caution for the funding_carry expert: leverage magnifies the carry yield on capital (collecting 3.5% on the full notional while posting a fraction) - the same math that makes funding collection on perps attractive.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

findings.strategy_name: Session-volume breakout filter: trade high-volume breakouts, fade low-volume ones
findings.mechanism: high-volume moves are real because significant capital is committed; in low-volume windows, orders that normally could not move the market now can, and institutions may push price to execute order pools for commission - so low-volume breakouts are suspect and fadeable
findings.setup_summary: For intraday breakouts of triangles and S/R levels: breakouts during high-volume sessions (London open / London-New York overlap) are treated as legitimate; breakouts during low-volume windows (late Asian session, late US session) are suspect and should not be traded in the breakout direction - they may be faded instead. The EUR/USD 1.2000 example: the false break came late in the Asian session (June 24), the real break at ~14:30 GMT during the London/NY overlap (July 1). Combine with the ascending/descending-triangle directional bias and the prior-trend filter (breakout in the direction of the prior trend is more compelling).
findings.trigger_invalidation: A breakout in a low-volume window is invalidated as a breakout signal (fade instead); after ~14:00-15:00 NY or when volume dissipates, breakout signals are unreliable.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on triangle-break; use prior-trend filter and volume/session filter as gates; stop beyond the broken level.
findings.quote: a breakout is considered to be significant if it occurs on high volume, and is considered less reliable if it occurs on low volume... if a breakout does occur during a low-volume time of day, it would be acceptable to 'fade' – or trade against – the breakout.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 11 'Keys to Intraday Breakouts', pp.145-152
findings.notes: Crypto perps have no session bell, but they do have a participation/volatility clock: the UTC 0:00 funding boundary, Asian/European/US overlap hours, and weekend low-participation windows. Propose a participation feature (rolling volume/volatility percentile or a session-clock label) used to gate breakout experts (volatility_breakout, NEW_flag_pennant, failed_breakout) - trade breakouts when participation is high, treat low-participation breakouts as suspect. This is the transferable kernel of both Chapter 11 and the rejected Boomerang.
findings.book: Forex Patterns and Probabilities - Trading Strategies for Trending and Range-Bound Markets 2007

book_title: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns (Bulkowski, 2013) — Part 1 (Ch 1-27)

findings.strategy_name: Throwback/Pullback Completion Reentry (Breakout Retest)
findings.setup_summary: After an upward (downward) breakout from any chart pattern, price returns to the breakout price or pattern boundary within 30 days (throwback/pullback). Enter long once the throwback completes: (A) close back above the pattern top, or (B) a higher peak and higher valley, or (C) close above the highest peak between the breakout and the throwback low. Throwbacks occur ~58% of the time (10,305 patterns; 60% for ascending triangles); in 65% of cases price resumes the breakout direction and rises, and in 25% of ascending-triangle throwbacks price drops below the pattern bottom.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: breakout close beyond the pattern boundary, then a loop back to the breakout level within 30 bars, then a completion signal (close back through the pattern top / higher peak+valley / close above the highest peak between breakout and throwback low). Invalidation: throwback dips too deep and closes below the pattern bottom (thesis fails — stop out; this is the main risk of the setup), or no throwback ever forms (missed move).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar open after throwback-completion signal (Option C usually gives the best results in the book's scan). Stop: penny below the throwback low or pattern bottom. Target: measure-rule projection; note patterns WITH throwbacks underperform those without (ascending triangles avg 28% vs 42%; head-and-shoulders bottoms 33% vs 42%).
