Expiry: throwback must complete within 30 days.
findings.quote: A throwback occurs after an upward breakout when price returns to the breakout price or chart pattern boundary within 30 days.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6 (Throwbacks and Pullbacks); Ch. 20 (The Throwback Buy Setup)
findings.notes: Refines V8's DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family by supplying the entry trigger (throwback completion) and the deep-throwback invalidation. 30-day window → 30 bars on 1h. Deep-throwback risk is amplified by crypto leverage; stop discipline is the edge here.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Busted Pattern Reversal (failed breakout that reverses and trends)
findings.setup_summary: A confirmed chart pattern breaks out in one direction, price moves LESS than 10% before reversing, and then closes beyond the OPPOSITE boundary of the pattern (a 'bust'); enter at the open the day after that bust close. Single-busted patterns perform as well or better than non-busted: busted descending triangles rise >=10% above the pattern top 70% of the time (avg +29%), rectangles that single-bust average +61% vs +33% non-busted, and ascending triangles bust 40% of the time (single busts avg +40%).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: (1) breakout close in one direction, (2) move <10% before reversing, (3) close through the opposite boundary of the pattern. Invalidation: double/triple bust — price re-crosses and closes beyond the ORIGINAL breakout side again (triangles double/triple-bust ~6-7%, symmetrical triangles double-bust most at 7%); repeated whipsaw means the pattern never establishes a direction. Sell side (Ch. 25): if an upward breakout busts downward, treat as a strong sell signal (28% hold win rate).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: buy/sell at the open the day after the bust close. Stop: for busted H&S tops the book places a stop below the lowest valley in the pattern; generally the pattern's far boundary. Target: measure rule projected from the busted direction (26-40% avg on single busts). Expiry: none stated; expect double-bust risk.
findings.quote: A busted ascending triangle occurs when price breaks out in one direction, moves less than 10 percent before reversing, and continues in the new direction to close above the top or below the bottom of the triangle.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 22 (Busted Pattern Buy Setups); Ch. 25 (Busted Pattern Sell Signals)
findings.notes: V8's failed_breakout expert (liquidity_vacuum_reentry, SHORT) is one instantiation of this — a busted top. This book generalizes the bust to both directions and any pattern shape, and supplies the <10% threshold, single/double/triple-bust counting, and per-pattern bust rates (bump patterns bust less than trendline patterns).
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Pattern-Height Measure Rule (target projection)
findings.setup_summary: For any chart pattern, target = breakout price plus (up breakouts) or minus (down breakouts) the pattern's height (highest peak to lowest valley). Per-pattern hit rates: ascending triangle up-breakout 72%, ascending triangle down-breakout 58%, rectangle 55%, symmetrical triangle 46%, double top 44% (half-height works 73%), triple top 48%, H&S top 53%. For a closer target, multiply the height by the hit-rate fraction before applying it; discard targets that imply absurd moves or sub-zero prices.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pattern confirms (close beyond boundary); compute target = breakout +/- height. Invalidation: if projected % move is unreasonably large (e.g., a 69% gain on an H&S bottom) or predicts a below-zero price, discard; cross-check the target against overhead resistance/support (HCRs, prior peaks/valleys, round numbers) — a target lining up with a support level is more credible.
findings.risk_geometry: Target = breakout +/- height (optionally height x hit-rate); the book uses this to set sell/take-profit levels for both buy and sell setups and as a sanity check on whether to hold. No entry or stop; no expiry.
findings.quote: Take the height of most chart patterns and add it to the breakout price for upward breakouts or subtract it from the breakout price for downward breakouts. The result is the target price.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 24 (Chart Pattern Sell Signals); Ch. 21 (Measuring Flags and Pennants)
findings.notes: Directly informs V8 risk_geometry target_r: replaces the fixed 1.0R default with a structure-derived target and provides per-pattern calibration priors. The hit-rate-weighted adjustment is a deterministic, falsifiable refinement for the simulator.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Partial Decline Predicts Upward Breakout (rectangle)
findings.setup_summary: Within a valid rectangle (at least 2-3 touches of each trendline), price touches the top trendline and then pulls back but stops WELL ABOVE the bottom trendline before reversing upward — the 'partial decline' — predicting an immediate upward breakout 89% of the time (two studies: 69 rectangle bottoms, 170 rectangle tops).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: valid rectangle in place + a dip after a top-trendline touch that fails to approach the bottom trendline, then an upward reversal. Invalidation: the dip reaches deep into the rectangle (near/through the bottom trendline) — not a partial decline; or no upward breakout follows within a handful of bars — thesis void.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: buy stop a penny above the top trendline, filled on the breakout. Stop: penny below the rectangle bottom (or below the partial-decline low). Target: rectangle-height measure rule. Expiry: immediate — the setup predicts an imminent breakout, so a delayed breakout weakens the signal.
findings.quote: A partial decline correctly predicts an immediate upward breakout 89 percent of the time according to two studies I did using 69 rectangle bottoms and another with 170 rectangle tops.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 18 (Basic Buy Setups — Rectangle Buy Signal)
findings.notes: Small samples (69+170) but an unusually specific and falsifiable pre-breakout signal; range structures are common on 1h BTC. The top-touch-then-shallow-dip geometry is a distinct behavior from V8's existing sweep/pullback experts.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Round-Number Support/Resistance and Stop Placement
findings.setup_summary: Prices cluster at numbers ending in zero (20, 30, 40...; in crypto, e.g., 10k/50k/100k): traders place buy/sell orders, targets, and stops at round numbers, so these levels show support and resistance even where price has never traded. Use the next closest round number to guess where price will stall; exit just ahead of it (sell at 79.93 not 80); NEVER place orders or stops at round numbers because that is where everyone else is — clustered stops there create stop-running avalanches.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price approaching a round number = expected stall/reversal zone; use for target selection and stop placement (place stops away from round levels). Invalidation: strong trend punches through the round number (SAR is probabilistic, not a hard barrier); measure rule/momentum then takes over.
findings.risk_geometry: Used to set targets (sell just before the round number) and to place stops away from round numbers to avoid being gunned. No expiry.
findings.quote: Do not place orders to buy and sell, or place stop loss orders at numbers ending in zero. That is where everyone else will place their orders, perhaps triggering unusual price moves.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 4 (Support and Resistance — Round Number SAR)
findings.notes: Round-number magnets are strong in BTC/ETH perps (100k BTC, 4k ETH); high leverage makes round-number stop clusters far more dangerous. Also a candidate FEATURE_INPUT for the location feature group (round-number proximity).
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Tall and Wide Pattern Selection Filter
findings.setup_summary: Among same-type chart patterns, prefer tall (height/breakout-price above the ~15-15.6% median) and wide (>37-41 days) patterns: tall double bottoms avg +44% vs +34% for short; double bottoms wider than 37 days avg +42% vs +34%; H&S bottoms both tall and wide avg +51% vs +28% (short only); tall symmetrical triangles +39% vs +24%. Small patterns underperform their large siblings.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: when screening candidate setups, compute height/breakout-price and pattern width; prefer above-median. Invalidation: none — this is a selection filter, not an entry; all figures are perfect-trade averages so individual outcomes vary.
findings.risk_geometry: No direct entry/stop/target; informs candidate selection and, combined with the measure rule, target sizing. Large patterns also imply larger stop distances (pattern-bottom stops average ~13% loss for tall ascending triangles).
findings.quote: Chart patterns tall and wide (large patterns) tend to perform better than narrow and short ones (small patterns).
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 1 (Smart Investor Tip); Ch. 23 (Trading Setups and Tips — Height and Width)
findings.notes: Deterministic, falsifiable filter that V8 can apply to candidate episodes; interacts with risk: tall patterns carry taller pattern-bottom stops, so the structural-stop override (see minor_low_stop_trail finding) matters.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Pattern Proximity to Trend Start (performance filter)
findings.setup_summary: Chart patterns that form within ~3 months of a trend start outperform patterns late in a long trend. Ascending triangles within 3 months of trend start avg +39% vs +29% for longer; double bottoms with short-term (<3mo) inbound trend avg +42% vs +30% for long-term trends; H&S bottoms 40%/36%/33% by trend length. Define trend start as the extreme beyond which price moved at least 20%.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: locate the trend start (the high/low beyond which price changed >=20%); if pattern-to-start distance <3 months, prefer the setup. Invalidation: a pattern appearing well into a long trend may signal the END of the trend regardless of breakout direction (Ch. 17) — treat late-trend patterns as exhaustion warnings, not entries.
findings.risk_geometry: No direct entry/stop/target; a regime/selection filter applied before entry. The 20% trend-start definition is concrete and computable.
findings.quote: The longer the price trend leading to the start of a chart pattern, the worse the performance.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 19 (Failures); Ch. 23 (Trading Setups and Tips — Trend Start, Double Bottoms)
findings.notes: Maps naturally to V8 trend/time feature groups and to the regime filter: candidate episodes can be gated on distance-from-trend-start, and late-trend patterns can feed a trend-exhaustion warning.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Trendline Break as Trend-Change/Exit Signal
findings.setup_summary: In an uptrend draw an external trendline along the minor lows (hugging bar ends, not slicing price); a close below the line is a sell/exit signal — a hint of trend change, not a guarantee. Shallow trendlines (45 degrees or less) have staying power while steep ones flame out quickly; widely spaced touches make a line more significant; rising volume into the break powers a larger decline. Lower highs and lower lows after the break confirm the change.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close below the up-sloping trendline (or close above a down-sloping line for shorts) — exit at the next bar open. Invalidation: a single close is only a hint; price can pierce and recover, so the line-drawing convention (internal vs external) controls whipsaw rate — require the close plus structure confirmation (lower highs/lower lows).
findings.risk_geometry: Exit at next-bar open after the close below the line; no stop/target — used as a dead-thesis/exit rule. Book tip: switch to a longer timeframe when trading trendlines to ignore noise.
findings.quote: In a rising price trend, draw trendlines along the valleys to detect a change in trend, from up to down. Steep trendlines stop trending sooner than shallow ones.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 3 (Trendlines — Guidelines); Ch. 27 (Trendline Sell Signals)
findings.notes: Trendlines are scale-invariant; on 1h BTC a close-below-uptrendline rule is a clean lifecycle/dead-thesis exit complementing V8's still_valid refs. The book asserts 'I proved this' for wide-spaced touches and shallow>steep but publishes no numbers here.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Exhaustion Spike Reversal (exhaustion gap / tall bar)
findings.setup_summary: At the end of a strong trend, a high-volume exhaustion signal (gap or unusually tall bar, 2-3x the prior-month average height) appears, is NOT followed by new minor highs/lows, and price consolidates; exhaustion gaps close within ~1 week on average (9 days up / 14 days down; 64% close within a week in bull markets). The reversal after the exhaustion can be violent and is tradeable in the new direction — but the new trend often lasts only about a week, so be nimble.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: tall, high-volume spike/gap well into an established trend with no new minor extreme afterward; or a single bar 2-3x the prior-month average height (book: signals a short-term peak/valley within a day or two). Invalidation: the gap is a continuation gap instead — if price continues with little bar overlap and makes new highs/lows, it is continuation, not exhaustion; large overlap after the gap = exhaustion and time to exit.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: trade the new direction at the open of the bar after the exhaustion signal. Stop: beyond the spike/gap extreme. Target: gap fill / nearest support; expect the move to be short-lived (~1 week). Expiry: days.
findings.quote: After an exhaustion gap ends, the trend reversal can be violent and offers a trading opportunity.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 (Gaps — Exhaustion gaps and gap closing stats)
findings.notes: Crypto perps have no exchange gaps, so gap mechanics (fill, gap support) do not transfer; but tall-spike exhaustion, climax-volume reversals, and liquidation-wick reversals map directly onto V8's capitulation backlog family (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion). Tall-bar reversal clue also supports a volatility feature.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Triangle Apex Turning Point
findings.setup_summary: In any triangle (ascending, descending, or symmetrical), the apex where the two converging trendlines meet is a future short-term turning point: a minor high or low occurs within ~4 days of the apex. Measured over 500 stocks (1991-1996), the average apex-to-turn distance was 3.6 days vs a 6.55-day chance benchmark; two visual tests succeeded 60% (computer-drawn) and 75% (hand-drawn) of the time. The turn is rarely a significant trend change.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: triangle identified and apex date projected; expect a short-term turn within ~4 bars. Invalidation: no minor extreme within ~4-7 bars — the apex failed; also the turn is short-lived, so do not treat it as a trend change or hold through it.
findings.risk_geometry: Timing device: use to take profits near the apex or to time entries within ~4 bars of the apex; no stop/target given by the book. Scale-invariant (works on 1-min to monthly).
findings.quote: The apex works as a turning point between 60 and 75 percent of the time. Look for a turn within four days of the apex. However, it will be rare that the minor high or minor low turn is a significant one (a trend change).
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 26 (Triangle Apex Sell Signal); Ch. 10 (Symmetrical Triangles)
findings.notes: Falsifiable and unusual; on 1h BTC the 4-bar window becomes an exit-timing feature rather than a standalone expert. Corroboration across books is plausible since apex-turn is a common TA claim.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Minor-Low Stop Placement and Trailing
findings.setup_summary: Place stops a penny-to-dime below the nearest prior minor low rather than below the whole pattern bottom (pattern-bottom stops are often too far — average ascending-triangle height is 13%, median 11%, so a pattern-bottom stop implies ~13% average loss). Raise the stop to below the prior minor low whenever price closes at a new high. In straight-line runs (>=3 bars, little overlap), trail a stop a penny below the prior bar's low, never lowering it; if a bar is 2-3x the prior-month average height, raise the stop to below its midpoint.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: minor low identified (5-bar local extreme); stop placed below it and trailed on new-high closes. Invalidation: professionals may gun visible stops — hide stops under minor lows and avoid round numbers; a stop can be hit by a spike even when the thesis is intact (that is the accepted cost of the method).
findings.risk_geometry: Stop: penny-to-dime below the nearest prior minor low; trail on each new-high close. Target: measure rule / prior resistance. No expiry. The straight-line-run variant is explicitly recommended for day traders only.
findings.quote: The idea for this stop placement technique is to hide the stop beneath the prior minor low, and raise the stop when price closes at a new high.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 18 (Basic Buy Setups — Stop Placement); Ch. 20 (straight-line-run trailing stop)
findings.notes: Direct input to V8 RiskGate risk_geometry: structural swing-point stops as an alternative to the fixed stop_r = 1.0R default, plus the tall-bar stop-tightening rule. The 13% average pattern-height loss quantifies why the 1.0R default is wrong for tall patterns.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Rectangle Intra-Formation Range Trading
findings.setup_summary: Within a tall, valid rectangle (>=2 peaks near the same price and >=2 valleys near the same price, i.e., >=4 printed touches), buy near the bottom trendline and sell/short near the top, with stops outside the rectangle; exit each leg at the opposite boundary. The book's example rectangle yielded 40% long / 29% short swings per leg. The author warns these are rare, for experienced traders, and that as soon as a pattern becomes repeatable it stops repeating.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches the bottom trendline inside a valid rectangle → long; the top trendline → short. Invalidation: a breakout close beyond either trendline ends the range (stop outside the rectangle triggers); a 'partial decline' near the top instead signals an imminent upward breakout (see partial_decline_breakout), which conflicts with the short leg.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit near the bottom/top trendline. Stop: outside the rectangle, far enough to survive normal price action. Target: the opposite trendline. Expiry: until a breakout close ends the pattern.
findings.quote: Buy near the bottom trendline and sell near the top, sit back and collect money... My experience says that as soon as you find a repeatable pattern, it stops repeating.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 23 (Trading Setups and Tips — Rectangles, intra-formation setup)
findings.notes: Mean-reversion range trading is a different mechanism family from V8's trend experts; the book itself flags reliability limits. The 4-touch rectangle validation (2+2) plus outside-rectangle stops is a clean, falsifiable skeleton if V8 ever admits a range family. Directional note: in trending crypto ranges, the short leg is the riskier side.
findings.book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

findings.strategy_name: Dual Momentum / Global Equities Momentum (GEM)
findings.mechanism: Relative-strength momentum selects the strongest asset; a 12-month absolute-momentum gate on the selected asset decides risk-on vs. de-risked safe harbor, so trend persistence is harvested only when the trend itself is positive.
findings.setup_summary: Monthly: compute trailing 12-month total return for each candidate risky asset (e.g., S&P 500 vs ACWI ex-US); pick the higher one; if its 12-month return beats the risk-free reference (T-bill), hold it for the next month; otherwise hold the safe harbor (aggregate bonds). Reported 1974-2013: GEM avg annual 17.43%, SD 12.64%, Sharpe 0.87, max drawdown 22.7%, ~1.35 switches/yr, significant alpha under Fama-French-Carhart factor models.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: selected asset's 12-month return > risk-free reference at month-end. Invalidation: selected asset's 12-month return < risk-free reference, or relative ranking flips -> rotate or move to safe harbor next bar.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at monthly close signal (NEXT_BAR_CLOSE analog), no per-position stop; exit is the trend gate (absolute momentum negative) not a price stop; holding period = one month with rebalance; safe-harbor asset replaces the risky asset, so this is a two-asset-state machine, not an R-multiple stop/target.
findings.quote: We first compare the S&P 500 to the ACWI ex-U.S. over the past year and select whichever one has performed better. We then check to see if our selected index has done better than U.S. Treasury bills. If it has, we invest in that index. If it has not, we invest instead in U.S. aggregate bonds.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, Global Equities Momentum (Applied Dual Momentum)
findings.notes: Strongest strategy in the book: 40y of data, decade-by-decade consistency, factor-model alpha, 12-month lookback cross-validated across both momentum forms. In crypto-perp terms the rotation universe is BTC/ETH/major alts and the safe harbor is flat (USDT) or a stablecoin delta rather than T-bills; the T-bill reference maps to funding/zero-carry. Requires the cross_market feature group (MarketState per instrument) and a long cadence that conflicts with V8's 1h bar horizon - registry decision before code; lands in src/v8/experts/ + docs/EXPERTS_REGISTRY.yaml.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Absolute (time-series) momentum trend filter / overlay
findings.mechanism: An asset's own trailing return is positively autocorrelated: sign of trailing 12-month excess return predicts continuation, so the trend filter both gates entries and provides a re-entry-capable replacement for a stop.
findings.setup_summary: On any asset: if trailing 12-month excess return (asset return minus risk-free reference) > 0, hold long; if < 0, exit to the safe harbor (T-bills/bonds) until it turns positive again; re-evaluate monthly. 12-month lookback is the best formation (highest Sharpe, best across decades 1974-2012) and beats all 2-18 month alternatives; applied to S&P 500 it cut max drawdown from >50% to <30% and raised annual return ~200bp vs buy-and-hold.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trailing 12-month excess return > 0 at evaluation. Invalidation: trailing 12-month excess return < 0 -> de-risk to safe harbor; re-entry is automatic when the sign flips back (unlike a stop, which has no re-entry).
findings.risk_geometry: Monthly evaluation; exit is the trend-sign change, not a price stop; it acts as a dormant stop-loss during bull phases with inherent re-entry; no R-multiple target; will not catch sharp corrections (Oct 1987) but avoids prolonged bear markets.
findings.quote: our strategy simply defines absolute momentum as being positive when the excess return (asset return less the Treasury bill return) over the formation (look-back) period is positive. We hold a long position in our selected assets during these times.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix B (Absolute Momentum) and Ch. 7 (Understanding Absolute Momentum)
findings.notes: This is the single most falsifiable, universally corroborated mechanism in the book (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen; Hurst et al. back to 1903, Sharpe>1). For V8: add a trailing-window return-sign feature to the trend feature group and consider a lifecycle rule that de-risks when the regime trend turns negative - the book explicitly argues this is superior to a hard stop because it auto-re-enters. Also a REFINE candidate for existing trend_pullback/failed_breakout still_valid logic.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Proximity to 52-week high momentum
findings.mechanism: Nearness to the 52-week high is an anchor for recently-arrived good news; being close to the high dominates trailing return as a predictor of continuation.
findings.setup_summary: Rank assets by ratio of current price to trailing 52-week high; buy those near the high that also have high 6-month past returns. George & Hwang (US stocks 1963-2001): profits from nearness-to-high plus top 6-month returns beat profits from 6-month returns alone; nearness to the 52-week high dominated the forecasting power of past returns.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price within some threshold of the trailing 52-week high with positive 6-month return. Invalidation: price falls materially below the reference high or the anchor rolls lower; thesis weakens as the 52-week high reference falls.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on strength near the reference high; no stop/target stated in the book - it is a cross-sectional ranking signal; the frozen reference (windowed high) mirrors V8's frozen_ref pattern in failed_breakout but with opposite polarity.
findings.quote: profits based on nearness to the 52-week high plus the highest returns over the past six months were superior to profits based solely on the highest returns over the past six months. Nearness to the 52-week high dominated the forecasting power of past returns.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, Mo' Better Momentum (Proximity to 52-Week Highs)
findings.notes: Corroborated within this book by Darvas, Dreyfus and O'Neil ('buy stocks making new highs') and by Donchian channel-breakout lineage. Well suited to crypto perps (24/7, frequent new highs, no exchange gaps so the reference is clean); on 1h bars the 52-week window is ~8760 bars, so this is a long-horizon location feature. Candidate new expert family near_high_continuation in src/v8/experts/; register first given complexity budget.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Fresh vs stale momentum winners
findings.mechanism: Recency/attention: winners whose strength is fresh (recent 12m up, prior 12m weak) outperform stale winners (up in both windows) because fresh strength attracts flow and is less crowded.
findings.setup_summary: Double-sort by relative price strength in months 1-12 (skip most recent month) and months 13-24. Fresh winners (strong in 1-12, weak in 13-24) outperformed stale winners (strong in both) by 0.43% per month on US stocks 1926-2006 (Chen, Kadan, Kose 2009).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: asset ranked in top quintile of trailing 12m momentum but was relatively weak in the prior 12m. Invalidation: the asset becomes a stale winner (strong in both windows) or its 12m rank decays out of the top quintile.
findings.risk_geometry: Cross-sectional ranking signal, no per-trade stop/target in the book; usable as a quality filter on any momentum/trend entry rather than a standalone entry.
findings.quote: fresh winners outperformed stale winners by 0.43% per month.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, Mo' Better Momentum (Fresh Momentum)
findings.notes: V8-native use: a recency filter for the trend_following family - e.g., a regime where a fresh pump (recent up, prior flat/down) is a stronger continuation candidate than an extended uptrend. For single-instrument BTCUSDT 1h the prior 12m/second window maps to two long lookbacks (e.g., 365/730 daily bars); most natural as a trend-quality feature or variant of the dual-momentum family.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Accelerating momentum / convex price trajectory
findings.mechanism: Investor attention amplifies momentum when the price path is convex (accelerating) rather than concave (decelerating), so trend quality depends on trajectory curvature, not just cumulative return.
findings.setup_summary: Regress daily returns on time-squared over the formation window; positive coefficient = convex (accelerating) trajectory. Among positive-momentum stocks, convex winners had significantly higher forward returns and 3-factor alphas than concave winners (Chen & Yu, US 1962-2011); Docherty & Hurst (trend salience, Australia 1992-2012) corroborate with a double-sort on short-term slope vs 12-month average return.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: momentum positive AND trajectory curvature convex (or short-term slope > 12-month average rate). Invalidation: curvature turns concave/decelerating while momentum is still positive - thesis for the acceleration component dies even if raw momentum persists.
findings.risk_geometry: Ranking/quality signal; no stop or target in the book. Usable as an entry-quality gate on trend entries; in V8 could be a volatility/trajectory feature over the lookback.
findings.quote: The authors showed that ignoring positive momentum stocks with concave price trajectories is the key to earning higher momentum returns.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, Mo' Better Momentum (Accelerating Momentum)
findings.notes: Plausible refinement for the trend family (parabolic vs grinding phases matter in crypto perps), but only two supporting studies and no clear parameterization in the book - keep as a backlog_family candidate pending frozen-OOS evidence. Note book also flags Paul Tudor Jones: the last third of a bull market is often the most dramatic - so acceleration filters should not be allowed to veto strong late-stage moves.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: 10-month / 200-day moving-average trend filter
findings.mechanism: Smoothing through averaging separates the trend signal from noise; price above the slow average is a lower-frequency trend state than daily price action.
findings.setup_summary: Long when price is above the 10-month (200-day equivalent) moving average; exit to safe harbor when price closes below it; evaluate monthly. On the S&P 500 1974-2013 the rule was in stocks 74% of the time with 49 trades (1.2/yr) - results comparable to 12-month absolute momentum but with ~60% more trades/whipsaw.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close above the 10-month MA. Invalidation: close below the 10-month MA -> de-risk; whipsaw risk is higher than absolute momentum because averaging produces false crossings (Faber 2007 rule).
findings.risk_geometry: Monthly evaluation; no stop/target; exit on the MA cross; compared head-to-head with absolute momentum in the book, which is preferred on transaction costs (0.83 vs 1.2 trades/yr).
findings.quote: One holds a long position when the price is above its 10-month moving average and exits the position when the price falls below the 10-month moving average.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, Mo' Better Momentum (Trend Following with Moving Averages)
findings.notes: The slow-MA trend filter is the most widely-used crypto regime indicator (200-day SMA). V8-native use: alternative trend feature (price vs long-window MA) in the trend feature group, and a candidate regime filter; the book's comparison table is the falsifiable anchor - it shows MA timing is not superior to absolute momentum after costs, so prefer the trailing-return-sign feature and treat MA as a robustness check. Also caution: the book notes the 10-month length is itself a data-mined historical favorite (Brock et al., Siegel, Faber).
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Leverage overlay via fund-separation theorem
findings.mechanism: Keep the highest-Sharpe portfolio fixed and scale exposure with risk-free lending/borrowing; leverage is only viable when the base strategy has low drawdown and the borrow cost is modeled explicitly.
findings.setup_summary: Take the optimal-risk portfolio (e.g., 12-month absolute-momentum parity portfolio, or GEM) and scale it to a target volatility: leverage ~1.85x at borrowing cost = fed funds + 25bp to reach 60/40-equivalent vol; or delever by mixing 30% bonds for conservative investors. Falsifiable claim: leveraged absolute-momentum parity keeps returns while truncating drawdown vs unlevered risk parity.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: base strategy Sharpe/vol target defined; scale exposure by target-vol multiple. Invalidation: borrow cost relative to expected excess return deteriorates, or base-strategy drawdown regime breaks the low-drawdown premise (book: negative skewness + leverage is especially harmful).
findings.risk_geometry: No per-trade stop; risk control is the portfolio-level scaling ratio (1.85x, or +30% leverage variant at fed funds + 25bp); conservative variant is a permanent 30% bond sleeve. The cost side (borrowing at risk-free + spread) is the load-bearing assumption.
findings.quote: We use a borrowing cost of the fed funds rate plus 25 basis points and a leverage ratio of 1.85 to 1.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix B (Leverage) and Ch. 8 (Accommodating Different Risk Preferences)
findings.notes: Direct input to V8's cost model: leverage is a financing decision priced at risk-free + spread, and perp leverage carries funding cost - the simulator's Binance USDM cost model must price funding against expected edge, and RiskGate should treat target-vol scaling as the sizing layer. Caveat in-book: 'Risk in a levered portfolio has many facets, such as fat tail, illiquidity, counterparty, basis, and converging correlation risk.'
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Behavioral drivers of momentum persistence
findings.mechanism: Anchoring/underreaction delays price discovery, the disposition effect sells winners early and holds losers, and herding/positive-feedback later overextends - together they produce the initial-underreaction-then-delayed-overreaction pattern that keeps trends persisting.
findings.setup_summary: Testable mechanism claim (not a tradable setup): momentum continuation is strongest where anchoring, herding and the disposition effect are strongest; e.g., retail-heavy markets (crypto perps) should exhibit at least as much serial correlation in trailing-return continuation as institutional markets. The book cites Odean (1998): disposition effect costs individual investors ~4.4%/yr.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - mechanism hypothesis, not a trigger. Falsifiable via the persistence of the momentum anomaly on fresh data and its strength in retail-dominated venues.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated - this is the causal rationale for the trend_following family, not a setup.
findings.quote: In anchoring, investors are slow to react to new information, which leads initially to underreaction. In herding, buying begets more buying and causes prices to overreact and move beyond fundamental value after the initial underreaction. Through the disposition effect, investors sell winners too soon and hold losers too long.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix B (Introduction) and Ch. 4 (Behavioral Basis for Momentum)
findings.notes: Supports the causal claim behind the momentum/trend family in V8's ontology and the durability of the anomaly (Fama-French call momentum the 'premier anomaly'; it was the only anomaly to persist post-publication). For V8: mechanism_family_candidate behavioral_underreaction_overreaction is the narrative why behind trend_continuation; evidence class LITERATURE_SUPPORTED since it rests on Jegadeesh-Titman, Odean, Grinblatt-Han, Daniel et al., Hong-Stein.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Mechanical exposure ratcheting (portfolio insurance) whipsaw
findings.mechanism: Mechanically scaling exposure up with past rises and down with past drops (portfolio insurance) feeds a mean-reverting market: it amplifies selling into weakness and whipsaws on rebounds.
findings.setup_summary: Lesson/risk rule: do not implement exposure that mechanically increases with recent gains and decreases with recent losses; the 1987 crash showed one-third of selling was portfolio-insurance driven (Brady Report) and the rebound produced large whipsaw losses because markets are short-term mean reverting and overreact then reverse.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - a rejection rule. Falsifiable via the observation that trend-following (buy strength) beats mechanical risk-parity-style ratcheting in whipsaw regimes, and via mean reversion after sharp corrections.
findings.risk_geometry: None; the operative rule is that downside de-risking must be regime-signaled (e.g., absolute momentum), not continuous mechanical leverage reduction.
findings.quote: Portfolio insurance helped turn a market correction into a full-scale panic. Portfolio insurers packed up their bags following this market collapse and subsequent rebound ('mean reversion happens') that gave them large whipsaw losses.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 3, Modern Portfolio Theory Principles and Practices (Portfolio Insurance - Not!)
findings.notes: V8-native use: a RiskGate/methodology rule that exposure scaling must be driven by regime signals (trend state) rather than continuous volatility/return ratcheting, and a warning that mean-reverting stretches whipsaw continuous-scaling models. Also supports V8's determinism/no-lookback rule: the book's point is that mechanically reactive risk models (vol-targeting variants of portfolio insurance) can destabilize exactly when correlation risk spikes.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Non-ergodicity, data snooping and backtest validation
findings.mechanism: Financial returns are nonstationary and nonergodic; short samples and multiple testing produce false discoveries, so strategy validation requires long out-of-sample data and corrections for the number of trials.
findings.setup_summary: Methodology: compute the variance ratio VR(k) = variance of k-period return / (k * variance of 1-period return); VR>1 flags a trending regime, VR<1 a mean-reverting one, and regime membership shifts across 15-year windows (1999-2013 S&P 500 was mean-reverting at all k) - so backtests on ~15y of data are unreliable. Falsifiable claims from the book: momentum is validated back to 1801 (relative) and 1903 (absolute); value and size premia decayed when more data arrived; Bailey et al. (2014) show backtest overfitting misleads capital allocation; Bajgrowicz & Scaillet (2012) show 7,846 trading rules on the DJIA had no selectable best rules ahead of time.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - evaluation methodology. Operational rule: judge strategies on frozen, long out-of-sample data and penalize the number of attempted configurations (multiple-comparisons hazard).
findings.risk_geometry: None.
findings.quote: Financial markets are most definitely nonergodic. Some stock market regimes may never repeat, while others repeat with considerably different characteristics.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, Mo' Better Momentum (Dangers in Trying to Enhance Momentum)
findings.notes: This is the book's core falsification doctrine and maps directly onto V8's evidence-bound constitution: frozen OOS evaluation, no in-place parameter optimization, and registry gating. Concrete V8 actions: keep a long-history tape (not 1-2 year samples), treat every threshold/parameter variant as a multiplicity unit, and report variance-ratio regime diagnostics as part of evaluation. Supports the V8 rule that versions evolve by challenger + frozen-OOS + registry decision.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Roll yield decay / cost drag on passive futures and CTAs
findings.mechanism: Strategy edge that comes from a structural premium (roll yield paid by hedgers) decays as speculators crowd in; passive/fee-heavy futures vehicles can net near-zero or negative excess return after carry and front-running costs.
findings.setup_summary: Lesson with falsifiable numbers: commodity futures roll return averaged +11%/yr (1969-1992) but -6.6%/yr since 2001 as noncommercial open interest rose from 15% to 42%; front-running of index rolls cost ~3.6%/yr (Mou 2011); 930 CTAs netted ~1.8%/yr over T-bills 1994-2012 (not significantly different from zero, Bhardwaj et al.) while fees averaged 4.3%/yr; Marshall et al. (2008) found no profitability across 7,000 rules in 5 families on 15 commodity markets.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - cost/methodology lesson. Falsifiable claim: crowding erodes premium-type edges over time (also seen with the size premium disappearing post-1980s).
findings.risk_geometry: None; the operative rule is to model every recurring cost (funding, spread, taker fees, roll-equivalent) and to distrust strategies whose modeled edge is small vs. cost drag.
findings.quote: From 1969 to 1992, the roll return averaged 11% per year. Since 2001, it has averaged a negative 6.6%.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 5, Asset Selection (Passive Commodity Futures and Managed Commodity Futures)
findings.notes: Crypto-perp analog: perps have no roll (no expiry), but funding is a standing carry cost and perp carry strategies face the same crowding decay the book documents for roll yield; additionally the book shows the trend-overlay alternative (Hurst-Ooi-Pedersen absolute momentum across 58 futures) matched CTA results before fees - reinforcing absolute momentum as the low-cost baseline. V8-native: simulator cost model must include funding; evaluation must show edge is material after costs.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Stress correlation convergence / failing diversification
findings.mechanism: Cross-asset correlations spike in stress regimes, so naive permanent diversification fails exactly when it is needed; dynamic trend-gated de-risking, not diversification, is the drawdown control.
findings.setup_summary: Lesson with falsifiable data: US vs non-US equity monthly correlation is -0.17 in up markets but +0.76 when returns are one standard deviation below average; commodities-equity correlation exceeded 0.80 during 1929 and 2008 and GSCI-S&P 500 correlation rose from <0.10 to ~0.50 by 2009 (Tang & Xiong); a 60/40 portfolio kept 0.92 correlation to the S&P 500 because stock vol dominates. Permanent diversification delivers less risk reduction than advertised; regime-adaptive exposure (absolute momentum) is the alternative.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - risk rule. Falsifiable: correlation matrices estimated in calm regimes underpredict stress correlation; exposure limits should be set on stress-correlation assumptions.
findings.risk_geometry: None; operative V8 rule: one exposure per (instrument, direction) and no reliance on cross-asset diversification inside a single-instrument expert; cap correlated exposure across any future multi-asset rotation.
findings.quote: when equity returns are one standard deviation below average, which is typical of bear markets, the monthly correlation between U.S and non-U.S. equities rises to 0.76.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8 (Dynamic Asset Allocation) and Ch. 5 (Rising Correlations)
findings.notes: Directly relevant to crypto: BTC-alt correlations converge toward 1 in liquidations (the May 2021 deleveraging is the in-library analog of 2008), so cross-perp diversification assumptions are worst exactly at the tail. Supports V8's rule 16 (one active exposure per instrument-direction) and the RiskGate correlated_exposure_cap; also the rationale for the absolute-momentum de-risking overlay over any correlation-based allocation.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

book_title: Dual Momentum Investing: An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk (Gary Antonacci, 2015) — Part 1
Dual Momentum Investing: An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk (Antonacci, 2015)

findings.strategy_name: Dual Momentum (Global Equities Momentum / GEM)
findings.mechanism: Combining a cross-sectional relative-strength rank with an own-asset absolute-momentum trend gate selects the asset with the highest expected trend continuation while standing down to a safe haven in bear regimes.
findings.setup_summary: On a fixed evaluation cadence (book: monthly), rank a basket of candidate assets (book: US equity index, ex-US world equity index, aggregate bond index) by trailing 12-month return; hold the highest-ranked asset only if its own trailing return is positive, else hold the safe-haven asset (bonds). On BTCUSDT 1h analog: rank a perp basket (BTC vs ETH vs majors) by trailing N-day return and require the winner's own trend to be positive, else go flat/stablecoin.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Selected asset's own trailing return falls to <= 0 (exit to safe haven), or the highest-ranked asset with positive absolute momentum changes at the next evaluation.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at evaluation close; no per-position stop - the monthly trend sign flip is the exit; allocation is 100% of the risk budget to one asset vs safe haven; re-evaluation on a fixed monthly cadence.
findings.quote: Dual momentum—a combination of relative strength and trend-following methods that I introduced in two award-winning research papers—is the ideal way to invest.
findings.chapter_anchor: Preface; Index - 'Dual momentum', 'Global Equities Momentum (GEM)', 'Relative momentum ... and dual momentum, 124-126'
findings.notes: Book claims GEM 'could have achieved long-run returns nearly twice as high as the world stock market over the past 40 years while avoiding severe bear market losses.' Requires a cross_market feature group and a multi-instrument universe that V8 (single-instrument BTCUSDT 1h) does not yet have; blocked on feature-group extension plus universe definition. Perp-specific: funding drag on long-only carry is a cost the book does not model. Complexity-budget note: would count as one expert family (one behavior family), not multiple.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Time-series / absolute momentum (12-month look-back trend filter)
findings.mechanism: A market's own trailing return has significant positive auto-covariance - past excess return predicts future excess return - so a sign filter on trailing return isolates continuation regimes and de-correlates the portfolio in drawdowns.
findings.setup_summary: LONG when the instrument's trailing 12-month return is positive, flat (or safe haven) when <= 0; evaluated monthly, entry at close. On BTCUSDT 1h: compute a trailing-return sign over a fixed look-back and use it as a slow regime gate for the active experts; rebalance on event-clock boundaries, never wall-clock.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trailing return flips to <= 0 -> exit; re-entry only when the sign flips positive again.
findings.risk_geometry: Look-back 12 months; monthly evaluation; no ATR stop - the sign flip is the exit; full exposure or zero.
findings.quote: Moskowitz et al. (2012) also found a 12-month look-back period best when applying absolute momentum to 58 liquid futures markets from 1969 through 2009.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix B notes (n.2); Index - 'Absolute momentum', 'Time series momentum, 84-85', 'Trend following: absolute momentum as, 86, 146-147'
findings.notes: Best look-back documented on 58 liquid futures markets 1969-2009; also AppB n.3: absolute-momentum 60/40 portfolio had correlation 0.53 to S&P 500 vs 0.87 for normal 60/40 - the filter de-correlates in drawdowns. A slow regime filter is compatible with V8's 1h experts; must be computed from event/available clocks, not months on a wall clock.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Relative strength / cross-sectional momentum ranking
findings.mechanism: Ranking a basket by past return exploits cross-sectional continuation: recent winners outperform recent losers over the holding period (Jegadeesh-Titman 1993; auto-covariance of excess returns).
findings.setup_summary: Across a basket of assets (book: US vs ex-US equity indexes), rank by trailing 12-month return and hold the top-ranked asset; rebalance monthly. On perps: rank BTC vs ETH vs other majors; hold top-K only when the winner's absolute momentum is positive.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Top rank changes at the rebalance, or the held asset's absolute momentum turns negative.
findings.risk_geometry: Monthly rebalance at close; rank-switch is the exit; concentrated single-asset holding within the rank window.
findings.quote: There is significant positive auto-covariance between a security's excess future return and its past excess return.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7 notes (n.3); Index - 'Relative strength', 'Relative momentum', 'Relative strength, 14-19, 23-24, 42, 52, 77, 84, 86, 93, 97-98, 101, 111, 115, 119, 124, 126, 131-132, 135-137'
findings.notes: Second pillar of dual momentum. Requires a cross_market feature group and multi-instrument point-in-time state, neither of which V8's single-instrument MarketState currently has. Safe first step is adding cross-market ranking features (rank fields) rather than a new active expert; expert family can follow when the universe exists.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: 10-month SMA trend timing (Faber)
findings.mechanism: Price relative to a slow moving average summarizes the trend state; a cross over/under acts as a regime switch, exploiting positive serial correlation of returns.
findings.setup_summary: LONG when price is above its 10-month simple moving average (Faber 2007), flat when below; monthly evaluation, entry at close. On 1h BTCUSDT: equivalent slow-MA cross on a scaled look-back window (e.g., a daily/weekly EMA or SMA of a chosen order).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Close crosses below the SMA -> exit; crosses back above -> re-enter.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry/exit at close on the cross; no stop; monthly evaluation cadence; 100% or 0% exposure.
findings.quote: Trend following: with moving averages, 121 –123
findings.chapter_anchor: Index - 'Trend following: with moving averages'; Ch. 8 notes (Faber 2007, 'A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation', p.122)
findings.notes: Same family as 12-month absolute momentum but a distinct signal construction (MA cross vs trailing-return sign); the book treats both as trend-following timing (index 'Market timing: and absolute momentum, 119-120'). In 24/7 perps an MA cross whipsaws more often than a monthly sign flip; test the two regime filters against each other on frozen OOS rather than assuming equivalence.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Dual momentum sector rotation (DMSR)
findings.mechanism: Applying dual momentum within a sector universe rotates capital to the strongest-trending sector while a positive absolute-momentum requirement keeps the portfolio out of bear regimes.
findings.setup_summary: Within a set of sector/asset instruments, each period rank by relative strength, filter by absolute momentum, hold the top qualifying instrument, else go to cash; rebalance monthly. Perp analog: rotate across crypto sectors (e.g., BTC, major alts, L1, DeFi) on trailing-return rank plus own-trend gate.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rank leader changes or its absolute momentum turns negative at the rebalance.
findings.risk_geometry: Monthly rebalance; rank/trend flip is the exit; concentrated single-sector holding.
findings.quote: Sector rotation, in dual momentum, 131 –133
findings.chapter_anchor: Index - 'Sector rotation, in dual momentum'; Index - 'Dual Momentum Sector Rotation, 131-133'
findings.notes: Category-level application of dual momentum; directly analogous to rotating across crypto sectors, but the chapter body is in Part 1 so its backtest evidence could not be audited here - treated as DESIGN_INFERENCE. Dependent on the same cross_market feature extension as dual_momentum.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Risk parity + absolute momentum overlay (de-risked leverage)
findings.mechanism: Volatility-scaled (risk parity) allocation combined with an absolute-momentum trend gate cuts drawdowns and negative skew enough that leverage on the residual allocation becomes economically safe; the trend gate also lowers portfolio correlation to the market in stress.
findings.setup_summary: Allocate across assets in inverse proportion to volatility (risk parity), then apply an absolute-momentum filter that de-risks (moves to safe haven / cuts exposure) when an asset's own trend is negative; the book's variant keeps a 40% permanent fixed-income allocation and only then permits leverage. For perps: volatility-targeted sizing (position size inversely proportional to recent realized vol) gated by the trend regime.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trend gate flips negative -> de-risk (reduce size / flat); re-risk when it flips positive.
findings.risk_geometry: Weights reset periodically; the trend gate is the exposure switch; leverage applied on the post-gate allocation; no per-asset stop beyond the gate.
findings.quote: It includes a risk parity approach using only a 40% permanent allocation to fixed income, which is made possible due to absolute momentum.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5 notes (n.7); Index - 'Risk parity portfolios: absolute momentum in, 160-165; ... leverage in, 168-170; stochastic dominance of, 167-168'
findings.notes: Volatility-targeted sizing is directly implementable in perps via variable leverage; the trend gate is the same regime filter as momentum_signature. Book reports stochastic dominance of the risk-parity-with-momentum portfolio over 60/40 and the 0.53 vs 0.87 correlation result. Funding is an additional perp cost the book does not model; would land in RiskGate sizing rules, not as a new expert.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Trend overlay reduces negative skew / left-tail risk (leverage caution)
findings.mechanism: Trend-following overlays flip the return distribution toward positive skew and cut left-tail losses; with leverage, negative skew is disproportionately damaging, so leverage must be gated by the trend regime.
findings.setup_summary: Portfolio-level property claim: adding an absolute-momentum/trend filter to an exposure reduces negative skew, tail losses, and drawdown; used to justify gating leverage. Falsifiable in the V8 lab by comparing skew, kurtosis, and lower partial moments of raw-long vs trend-gated-long exposure on BTCUSDT frozen OOS.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a - a property claim; falsified if trend-gated exposure does not show reduced negative skew / lower left-tail risk on frozen OOS.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop; a risk-gate principle: max leverage should be a function of trend regime (lower or zero leverage when the trend filter is negative).
findings.quote: Trend-following methods can also reduce negative skew and associated left tail risk (Rulle 2004). Negative skew can be especially problematic when there is leverage.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix B notes (n.8); Chapter 7 notes (n.12) 'Trend-following methods often tend toward positive skewness.'
findings.notes: Directly relevant to perps because high leverage amplifies left-tail damage (liquidation cascades). Supports a RiskGate rule tying max leverage to the trend/regime state, consistent with V8's deterministic RiskGate and heat cap.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Valuation-based market timing (Shiller CAPE)
findings.mechanism: Extreme valuation (CAPE) implies lower forward expected returns; a slow valuation filter can time equity exposure.
findings.setup_summary: When CAPE sits in an extreme/high band, reduce equity exposure or lengthen the risk-off state; the book covers this as an alternative timing approach to momentum timing.
findings.trigger_invalidation: CAPE enters/leaves the extreme band.
findings.risk_geometry: Slow filter; no stops; changes exposure at monthly+ cadence.
findings.quote: Market timing: using valuation, 123 –124
findings.chapter_anchor: Index - 'Market timing: using valuation'; 'Shiller 10-year Cyclically Adjusted Price Earnings (CAPE) ratio, 123-124'
findings.notes: Crypto perps have no earnings/CAPE analog; on-chain valuation (e.g., MVRV or unrealized-profit ratios) is outside this book's scope. Keep as a def-erred regime-filter idea; not implementable from this source. Only the index entry was auditable in Part 2.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Roll yield / carry in futures (commodity analog to perp funding)
findings.mechanism: In futures, a portion of the long-side return comes from roll yield (positive in backwardation, negative in contango); carry is a return source separable from price trend, and roll-over costs can destroy it.
findings.setup_summary: Book: passive commodity futures returns depend on roll yield, and the author avoids commodity index futures because of 'substantial front-running rollover costs' and 'possible lack of risk premia', using gold instead. On perps: the funding rate is the direct analog of roll yield - positive funding approximates contango (short-side carry), negative funding approximates backwardation (long-side carry); net funding into expected return for every expert.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Carry sign/level flips so that funding becomes a net cost for the held direction.
findings.risk_geometry: Carry is an expected-return input, not an entry; funding must be netted into the simulator cost model.
findings.quote: We use gold instead of commodities because of the possible lack of risk premia and substantial front-running rollover costs associated with commodity index futures.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix B notes (n.7); Index - 'Roll yield, 54-55'
findings.notes: The carry/roll-yield mechanism transfers directly to perp funding, a mandatory cost/return input for any long or short expert. Supports adding funding-level features to the flow feature group and funding to the Binance USDM cost model. The contango/backwardation-to-funding mapping is the reader's inference; the book's claim is about commodity futures roll yield.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Behavioral basis of momentum (underreaction, overconfidence, herding)
findings.mechanism: Momentum persists because investors underreact to information (slow diffusion), then overreact through representativeness, overconfidence, and self-attribution; herding and loss aversion amplify continuation and cause panicked selling at lows.
findings.setup_summary: Mechanism claim, not a standalone entry: underreaction explains short-horizon continuation; representativeness/overconfidence explains longer-horizon continuation; loss aversion explains why investors sell at bottoms, which feeds stop hunts and capitulation.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a - mechanism rationale; used to name and justify momentum-based behavior families and their causal claims.
findings.risk_geometry: None - informs the causal claims attached to V8 behavior families.
findings.quote: Underreaction, 40 –42, 147
findings.chapter_anchor: Index - 'Momentum: behavioral basis for, 38-43', 'Underreaction', 'Overconfidence', 'Representativeness', 'Self-attribution bias', 'Loss aversion, 47-48'
findings.notes: Provides the causal story V8 attaches to momentum-based behavior families (continuation, capitulation); connects to already-formalized trend_pullback and backlog capitulation mechanisms. Behavioral citations are in Part 1 chapters (Prospect Theory, Barberis-Thaler); only index coverage was auditable in Part 2.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Data-snooping / overfitting guard: false discovery rate and factor decay
findings.mechanism: Multiple-testing and data-snooping inflate apparent backtest performance; published factor premia decay after publication, so any discovered edge must be validated on frozen OOS with multiplicity-adjusted statistics.
findings.setup_summary: Methodology discipline: adjust for data snooping using the false discovery rate (Barras et al. 2010), expect post-publication factor decay (McLean-Pontiff 2013, Chordia et al. 2013), and correct for survivorship bias; treat any single-sample backtest result as unverified.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a - a research-protocol rule.
findings.risk_geometry: None - applies to the research pipeline (registry gating, frozen OOS), not to trade geometry.
findings.quote: An advantage of using the false discovery rate is its robustness with respect to cross-sectional dependencies.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9 notes (n.5); Index - 'Overfitting, 32, 112, 116-117, 133', 'Survivorship bias', 'Pseudo-Mathematics and Financial Charlatanism'
findings.notes: Reinforces V8's existing constitution: registry-gated promotion, frozen OOS, challenger protocol, no in-place evolution. Factor-decay evidence argues for skepticism toward any published crypto edge; supports the PROPOSED->REPLICATION registry ladder.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

findings.strategy_name: Equal weighting as an out-of-sample allocation baseline
findings.mechanism: Complex allocation models add estimation error that offsets their theoretical gains; equal weighting rarely loses out-of-sample to optimized weights.
findings.setup_summary: Methodology finding: in allocation tests, 14 out-of-sample models on 7 datasets did not beat equal weighting on Sharpe ratio or certainty-equivalent return; any cross-asset or cross-expert allocation V8 adds should be benchmarked against the equal-weight baseline.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a - benchmark design rule.
findings.risk_geometry: None - allocation benchmark guidance.
findings.quote: DeMiguel, Garlappi, and Uppal (2009) test 14 out-of-sample allocation models on seven datasets and find that none has higher Sharpe ratios or higher certainty equivalent returns than equal weighting.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix B notes (n.6)
findings.notes: If V8 ever allocates across instruments or across experts, equal weighting is the mandated baseline per this finding; also supports keeping per-expert multiplicity simple and avoiding ranker/scorer complexity that the constitution already gates as ABSENT by default.
findings.book: Dual Momentum Investing - An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk 2015

book_title: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange: A Guaranteed Income for Life (Courtney D. Smith, 2010) — Part 2 (Epilogue + Appendix + Index)

findings.strategy_name: Open trailing-stop re-entry (the "World's Most Stupid Trading System")
findings.mechanism: Asymmetric stop geometry: a naive long-only system becomes profitable purely through a fixed trailing stop from the highs plus next-bar re-entry, because it cuts losses small and lets winners run.
findings.setup_summary: Long-only: buy on the bar open; place a fixed-distance trailing stop from the bar highs (10 cents in the author's soybeans test); if stopped out, rebuy on the next day's open and re-arm the stop. Author states this made money over roughly ten years of soybeans even though it lost a lot in bear markets, solely because the dumb trailing stop enforced cut-losses/let-profits-run.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No entry filter (always in the market) means the system bleeds small losses in trendless/mean-reverting regimes; thesis is invalidated if the asymmetry does not produce positive expectancy over a multi-year, multi-regime backtest (stops need to be ATR-calibrated to avoid overtrading on noise).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on bar open; trailing stop at fixed distance from highs (10 cents; ATR-multiple equivalent for crypto); re-entry next bar open after stop-out; no profit target (let profits run); no expiry — position exits only via trailing stop.
findings.quote: The rules were that I would buy on the open and place a ten cent trailing stop from the highs... The simple placement of a stupid arbitrary stop loss was enough to create a profitable system.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue — Fundamentals Versus Technicals (pp. 172-173)
findings.notes: The point of the passage is that stop placement is the profit engine ('technical analysis gives you a place to put a stop'). For V8: evidence to add trailing-stop-from-extreme as a stop/exit variant (risk geometry) and re-entry-after-stop as a lifecycle rule. 24/7 perp with no exchange gaps improves trailing-stop fill fidelity; funding is a modest long-side drag; data shown is an author assertion, not published statistics.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Five-of-six method portfolio rotation (Pareto culling)
findings.mechanism: Returns concentration (Pareto/80-20): ~90% of profit comes from ~10% of methods, so a portfolio that periodically culls its worst-performing method and adds a new candidate steadily improves performance.
findings.setup_summary: Run six methods concurrently; at each annual review drop the worst-performing method and add a new one, keeping the top five. Author reports his analysis showed about 90% of profits came from 10% of his ~40 systems, and expects ~10%/yr performance gains from relentless culling.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rotation assumes the worst performer is identifiable on frozen, out-of-sample evidence rather than luck (needs a fair sample before culling), and that replacement candidates are continuously available; invalid if culling sacrifices genuine diversification.
findings.risk_geometry: None — portfolio-level process, not a trade-level rule.
findings.quote: you will be constantly improving your trading performance by relentlessly throwing out the worst-performing method and keeping the top five... Actually, about 90 percent was coming from 10 percent of the systems!
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue — Keep the Top Five, Drop the Worst / Keep Your Trading to 15 Minutes a Day (pp. 165, 169)
findings.notes: Maps directly to V8's registry lifecycle: worst-performing family on frozen OOS -> QUARANTINED/REJECTED, new family enters as PROPOSED. V8's max-3 ACTIVE experts caps simultaneous breadth, so the lesson applies to registry turnover velocity, not running six families at once.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Control-vs-experimental method comparison (enhancement testing)
findings.mechanism: Paired method experimentation: running a control method and one experimental enhancement in parallel on the same market isolates whether the enhancement adds edge; judgment requires a minimum fair sample (~30 trades).
findings.setup_summary: Take a working technique (control, e.g. channel breakouts) and one enhancement (experimental, e.g. blue-moon filter); execute both flawlessly in parallel; compare profitability and risk only after at least 30 trades per method (can take 6+ months); keep improvements the experimental method proves. Author reports he constantly finds improvements this way.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Comparing before a fair sample (30 trades), or non-identical execution/drift between the two arms, invalidates the comparison; both arms must run concurrently on the same data with frozen rules.
findings.risk_geometry: None — experimentation protocol.
findings.quote: I now put on both trades from both methods. I flawlessly execute both methods... I keep this comparison up until I have a fair sample of trades. I will look for at least 30 trades.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue — Avoid Boredom (pp. 167-168)
findings.notes: This is essentially V8's challenger + frozen-OOS + registry-decision protocol. The 30-trade minimum is an episode-count gate for promotion/merge decisions. Also supports 'impossible to be profitable and creative at the same time' — discipline over creativity in execution.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Position trading over day trading (big moves, 80/20)
findings.mechanism: Holding-period return concentration: multi-day position trading captured >80% of profit while consuming far less time than day trading; a hard time budget (15 min/day) forces execution over overthinking, and more screen time correlated with worse position-trading results.
findings.setup_summary: Split trading into day trades (<1 day) vs position trades (held overnight, usually several days). Author's analysis: position trading accounted for over 80% of yearly profit while day trading was under 20% despite all-day effort; his position trading was more profitable when he spent less time on it (overthinking, analysis paralysis, early exits).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Claim is conditional on the author's method set and self-reported records; falsifiable via time-bucket analysis of PnL by holding period on any systematic tape. Invalid if intraday edge exists in the tested universe.
findings.risk_geometry: None — timeframe/methodology. Implies multi-day holding (expiry in days, not hours).
findings.quote: I found that position trading accounted for over 80 percent of my profits over the year while day trading was less than 20 percent... The big money is made on the big moves.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue — Keep Your Trading to 15 Minutes a Day (pp. 169-170)
findings.notes: Supports V8's multi-bar/multi-day holding (expiry_bars on day scale) and argues against intraday churn on BTCUSDT 1h. 24/7 crypto redefines 'day trading'; the testable core is whether per-trade expectancy concentrates in longer holding periods. Note: 'never a day trader who made $100M' is rhetoric, not evidence.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Hold trend positions through scheduled economic news
findings.mechanism: News-flow trend alignment: scheduled releases are systematically trend-aligned ('only bullish news in bull markets'), so holding a trend-aligned position through the event accrues a series of small-to-moderate incremental gains and is only rarely stopped out.
findings.setup_summary: When holding a position in a clear trend, do not flatten before a major scheduled economic release (e.g., Non-Farm Payrolls) if the position is aligned with the trend; accept occasional event-driven stop-outs that later reverse, in exchange for repeated incremental trend-aligned gains. Author also suggests predicting releases on the bullish side of consensus in bull markets because analysts lag reality.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Applies only when a clear trend exists and the position is trend-aligned; invalidated in flat/range regimes where news is mixed. If the event stops the position out and price reverses against the thesis, the thesis must be re-verified — 'still_valid' semantics apply post-event.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop unchanged through the event (no pre-widening); event risk borne explicitly; no event-avoidance exit; entry/exit geometry otherwise per the underlying trend method.
findings.quote: I always say yes, if there is a clear trend and your trend is in line with the trend... There is only bullish news in bull markets; only bearish news in bear markets; and a mix in neutral markets!
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue — How to Predict the News (pp. 173-174)
findings.notes: Crypto has knowable scheduled macro events (CPI, FOMC, NFP) plus 8h funding settlement and quarterly perp/spot expiry; 'hold through event if trend-aligned' is testable with an event calendar feature. The 'analyst consensus lags reality' sub-claim does not transfer to crypto (no analogous consensus feed); treat the event-stop-out-then-resume behavior as the falsifiable core.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Validate by manual back-testing, then start live at 0.25% risk
findings.mechanism: Time-compressed validation: manual back-testing compresses a year of practice into about an hour and trains the real failure modes (psychology and risk management) that paper trading masks; live trading should start at a trivial risk size (0.25%) to buy experience cheaply.
findings.setup_summary: Skip paper trading; manually walk a year or more of history on five pairs bar-by-bar recording trades (~1 hour), building a track record; then trade live with risk as low as 0.25% for several months before scaling to normal 1% risk. Author argues paper trading does not address psychology and risk management.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Manual back-testing is only valid if rule-faithful and honest: no lookahead, no discretionary trade selection, no hindsight bias; invalidated by cherry-picking or reconstructing signals after seeing the outcome.
findings.risk_geometry: Initial live risk 0.25% per trade (author's minimum), scaling up after several months of live execution; back-test itself has no risk geometry.
findings.quote: I recommend back-testing instead. In this case, you go back a year or more on a chart and manually go through day after day as if you were trading that time period in a real-time manner... start out trading with miniscule risk, perhaps only 0.25 percent.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue — Don't Paper Trade (pp. 165-166)
findings.notes: Aligns with V8's frozen-OOS back-test discipline and pre-experimental conservative sizing. The 'trade small to confront psychology cheaply' lesson matches V8's evidence-bound stance; the manual-chart-walking mechanics are pre-software and superseded by V8's replay harness.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Size capital so every signal is tradable (participation breadth)
findings.mechanism: Participation-breadth diversification: an account too small to take a signal filters it out, concentrating PnL on fewer trades and raising variance; trading every signal at a fixed per-trade risk spreads the book across many small trades.
findings.setup_summary: With a fixed per-trade risk limit (e.g., 1% = $50 on a $5,000 account), choose contract granularity (micro vs mini lot) so that every generated signal is tradable; trade all signals to spread PnL and reduce per-trade concentration; scale up only as capital and retained profits grow.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trade-every-signal presumes signal breadth is beneficial; invalid if the signal set is unfiltered/low-quality or if it would breach portfolio constraints — in V8 terms, one-exposure-per-(instrument, direction) and the heat cap override it.
findings.risk_geometry: Fixed per-trade risk (author's 1% default; 0.25% during the training phase); granularity chosen so the worst-case loss fits the account; no entry/stop/target specifics.
findings.quote: Let's say that you are setting your risk limit at 1 percent. That means that you can only risk $50 on a trade... So shift down to a smaller account and give yourself the ability to trade every trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue — Make Sure You Have Enough Capital (p. 171)
findings.notes: BTCUSDT perp micro-notional makes the lot-granularity problem mostly moot, but the concentration-risk lesson transfers: candidate-episode diversity (many small episodes) vs few concentrated ones. In V8 this reads as a participation/portfolio rule, not a sizing formula.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Portfolio-level edge across pairs
findings.mechanism: Cross-instrument diversification: the edge holds at the portfolio level (the five-pair portfolio makes money every year) even when individual pairs lose in a given year, so evaluation and sizing must be portfolio-wide rather than per-instrument.
findings.setup_summary: Back-test the method set on the five major pairs over a couple of years; expect that not every pair makes money every year but the aggregated portfolio does; judge and size the book at the portfolio level. Author states he is 'sure' of the portfolio-level claim and urges readers to verify by testing.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Assertion without published data; invalid if pairs are highly correlated (they fail together, making diversification illusory) or if losing streaks are not balanced by winners — needs multi-instrument, frozen-OOS evidence before crediting the claim.
findings.risk_geometry: None — portfolio evaluation/sizing principle; implies per-pair allocation within a portfolio risk budget.
findings.quote: You may not make money in every pair in every year but your total portfolio will make money every year. I am sure of that.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue — In Conclusion (pp. 174-175)
findings.notes: V8 is currently single-instrument (BTCUSDT 1h); this lesson informs the future multi-instrument evaluation gate — a family should not be rejected on one instrument's year if portfolio evidence is positive, and vice versa. Crypto majors are highly correlated, so the correlation caveat is the first thing to test.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Six-method portfolio in priority order
findings.mechanism: Family-portfolio composition: the book's core is six families ranked by priority (Channel Breakout > Inside Days > Trend Analysis > Conqueror > 20-Day Momentum > Reversal Days), implemented in that order so synergies emerge across trend and range behaviors.
findings.setup_summary: The author's method set: channel breakouts (Donchian-style 20/20, 40/20, 55/20), inside days (with double-whammy and multiunit tactics), trend analysis (swing highs/lows, three-bar highs/lows, ADX filter), Conqueror (true-range based), 20-day momentum (Babcock), and reversal days. Part 2 supplies the priority/implementation order; detailed rules are in the earlier chapters (per the Index).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Ranking is a practitioner heuristic, not a tested claim; each family is invalidated independently on frozen-OOS performance per V8 registry rules.
findings.risk_geometry: None — method menu; per-method risk geometry defined in the earlier chapters.
