findings.quote: I like the methods in this order: 1. Channel Breakout 2. Inside Days 3. Trend Analysis 4. Conqueror 5. 20-Day Momentum 6. Reversal Days
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue — Priority Order Your Methods (p. 171); Index entries for Channel breakouts, Inside days, Reversal days, Conqueror
findings.notes: Cross-reference to the shared starter vocabulary: Channel Breakout ~ donchian_breakout / turtle_entry, Inside Days ~ tight_consolidation, 20-Day Momentum ~ momentum_signature, Reversal Days ~ pivot_reversal, Trend Analysis ~ regime/trend definition. These are candidate backlog families for V8; rules must be read from Part 1 chapters before formalization.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

book_title: Harmonic Trading: Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets (2010), Part 2 of 2

findings.strategy_name: RSI BAMM divergence reversal with harmonic pattern confluence
findings.setup_summary: On the 1h bar: (1) RSI first tests an extreme limit (overbought >70 / oversold <30); (2) an M-type (bearish) or W-type (bullish) complex RSI structure completes; (3) RSI retests the 50 limit at minimum; (4) a Trigger Bar is defined - if the Trigger Bar is the extreme price high/low the Confirmation Point completes at the 1.618 extension (usually Crab/Deep Crab), otherwise at 1.13 (Bat/Butterfly/5-0/Gartley); (5) RSI diverges from price as price makes a new extreme while the impulsive RSI retest does NOT exceed the prior complex-structure extreme; (6) entry when price simultaneously completes the harmonic pattern at its PRZ at the RSI BAMM Confirmation Point.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid if the impulsive RSI retest exceeds the reading of the prior complex structure (no divergence), or if price violates the extension stop zone - beyond 1.618 for a 1.13 setup, beyond 2.0 for a 1.618 setup - especially on the first test, which instead flags strong primary-trend continuation.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at bar close after the harmonic pattern completes at the PRZ/Confirmation Point; stop beyond the defining extension (1.618 for 1.13 setups; 2.0 for 1.618 setups); reversal expected to be quick after the zone test ('most valid reversals will occur quickly after this area has been tested'); no expiry specified beyond the acceleration window of a few bars.
findings.quote: The execution of the trade is triggered at the completion of the relative harmonic pattern that completes at the appropriate RSI BAMM extension level.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 RSI BAMM, pp.255-270 (Final RSI BAMM Review and RSI BAMM Tips)
findings.notes: The signature strategy of this book: quantified RSI divergence (Wilder) fused with harmonic Fibonacci completion. Computable on BTCUSDT 1h (RSI extremes, complex structure, divergence, extension levels all derived from price history), but exact ratio precision (0.886/1.13/1.618/2.0/3.618) is fragile in 24/7 crypto with funding-driven extension, and the book offers chart examples, not statistics. The 7-step process (pp.269) gives a falsifiable trigger sequence. Would need a new expert file src/v8/experts/rsi_bamm.py + registry decision; candidate must also satisfy the RSI BAMM stop rule (see NEW_harmonic_extension_stop).
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: RSI BAMM Reversal Acceleration Trigger (M-type indicator breakdown)
findings.setup_summary: Following a valid RSI BAMM Confirmation Point, RSI forms a brief corrective pause (typically 1-2 bars) after the impulsive retest of the extreme limit, then breaks below the 70 level (bearish) or above the 30 level (bullish) in an M-type (or inverted) structure; the price bar that completes that indicator breakdown marks the acceleration point of the new reversal trend and serves as the final confirmation trigger.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If price action languishes after the Confirmation Point without a decisive indicator breakdown, the setup fails - exit at small loss or break-even rather than holding for the reversal.
findings.risk_geometry: Confirmation sub-trigger only: delays execution until the RSI structure breaks; no new stop level introduced; adds an exit-if-languish rule; timing property is 'within a few price bars' of the breakdown.
findings.quote: the price bar that completes the breakdown of the M-type structure in the RSI reading will typically mark the acceleration point of the new reversal trend
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6, pp.261-265 'RSI BAMM Confirmation Point-Reversal Acceleration Trigger'
findings.notes: Described by the author as 'the most sophisticated technical setup within the entire Harmonic Trading approach.' In V8 terms it is a confirmatory timing feature for the NEW_rsi_bamm family (indicator-structure breakdown derived from the RSI series in marketstate), not an independent strategy. Also acts as a false-signal filter: it prevents executions where the extreme test flounders without decisive reversal continuation.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Harmonic/RSI-BAMM extension stop and first-test invalidation rule
findings.setup_summary: For any harmonic reversal with an RSI BAMM extension: a 1.13-extended setup must not experience price beyond the 1.618 level of the final divergent move; a 1.618-extended setup must not exceed the 2.0 projection. The PRZ + RSI BAMM Confirmation Point together define a 'do or die' price level; price exceeding the stop zone - especially on the first test - invalidates the reversal and flags that the primary trend is strong.
findings.trigger_invalidation: This IS the invalidation rule: stop zone = next extension beyond the setup's defining extension; no discretionary buffer around the level.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop beyond the next harmonic extension (1.618 for 1.13 setups; 2.0 projection for 1.618 setups); combined with pattern PRZ violation as the earlier warning; book frames these as guidelines whose exact level depends on the pattern's PRZ.
findings.quote: the key invalidation point truly occurs beyond the 1.618 extension of the final divergent move. The validation of the technical phenomenon becomes questionable beyond the 2.0 extension
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6, pp.265-268 'Bearish RSI BAMM Failure-Stop Loss Considerations'
findings.notes: Cleanly portable to perp crypto: the rule is a deterministic first-test violation of a frozen level (like the frozen refs in existing V8 experts), needing no exact ratio precision. Maps to RiskGate/lifecycle: stop distance defined by structural extension rather than fixed ATR multiple; also doubles as the invalidation semantics for NEW_failed_pattern_continuation.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Failed harmonic pattern / RSI BAMM violation -> decisive trend continuation
findings.setup_summary: When price violates a harmonic pattern's PRZ (or the RSI BAMM Confirmation Point) on the first test - or when both price and RSI decisively violate their respective technical levels - the reversal thesis has failed and a significant continuation of the predominant trend typically follows; trade in the direction of the prior trend instead of the failed reversal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If price respects the PRZ and reverses at the Confirmation Point, the pattern has not failed - do not enter a continuation trade.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry after first-test PRZ violation (bar close beyond the zone); stop beyond the failed pattern's opposite extreme; target is measured continuation; book refers to its Volume One failure chapter for full specifics (not reproduced here).
findings.quote: price action that violates these price levels, especially on the first test, should raise a red flag that the primary trend is quite strong.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6, pp.265-268; Index 'failed harmonic patterns against trends', pp.133-139
findings.notes: Sibling of the formalized failed_breakout expert (mechanism liquidity_vacuum_reentry): a reversal attempt fails at a defined level, counter-trend interest converts to continuation fuel. High applicability to 24/7 crypto perps because it does not depend on exact Fibonacci ratios - only on first-test violation of a frozen zone, which is computable from MarketState. Should be a variant/behavior under the liquidity_vacuum_reentry mechanism family, subject to the 3-active-expert cap.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Multi-method confluence as a validity gate (pattern + indicator must agree)
findings.setup_summary: Do not execute a reversal setup on a single technique: require both structural completion (harmonic pattern at PRZ) and indicator confirmation (RSI BAMM Confirmation Point) to agree before entry; when independent methods converge on the same price level the probability of a valid reversal is treated as much higher. Author explicitly states he would not execute an RSI BAMM setup without a pattern.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not a tradeable trigger; this is a lifecycle/validity gate - a candidate missing either the pattern completion or the indicator confirmation is not executed.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated; methodological only.
findings.quote: When techniques of multiple approaches come together and yield the same result, the probability for a successful trading opportunity is extremely high.
findings.chapter_anchor: Conclusion, p.272
findings.notes: A design lesson for V8's lifecycle: validity gates should require agreement of independent observable conditions (here: structural PRZ completion AND indicator divergence), not a weighted scorer (which is ABSENT by default in V8). Also encodes the ordering lesson that the pattern is primary and the indicator secondary. Corroborates the existing V8 practice of confluence across independent features rather than scoring.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Harmonic retracement/extension patterns within trends as continuation signals (AB=CD)
findings.setup_summary: In an established trend, harmonic retracement patterns (AB=CD, reciprocal AB=CD, Gartley/Bat/extension variants) that complete at their Fibonacci retracement against the trend act as continuation signals rather than reversals: the pattern's completion point defines a pullback entry in the trend direction. Full rules in the book's Ch.5 (pp.111-139); this part's prose states that harmonic pattern completion typically marks a critical point within the predominant trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If the pattern's PRZ is violated on the first test, the continuation thesis fails and the trade converts to the failed-pattern-continuation logic (NEW_failed_pattern_continuation) in the dominant direction.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at pattern completion (bar close); stop beyond the pattern's extreme; target is an extension in the trend direction; book details in the chapters covered by Part 1 (pp.111-139).
findings.quote: When harmonic patterns develop in specific technical situations, their completion typically represents a critical point within the predominant trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Index 'harmonic patterns within trends', pp.111-139 (Ch.5); Conclusion p.272
findings.notes: Sibling of the formalized trend_pullback expert (mechanism trend_continuation): the pullback-completion definition here is a Fibonacci/harmonic structure rather than EMA conditions. Full behavioral detail (reciprocal AB=CD, retracement vs extension variants by trend) lives in Part 1 chapters; this part contributes the confirmation that pattern completion is trend-anchored, and the trend-context rule (pattern direction must align with the dominant trend to be a continuation, else a failed pattern).
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Donchian 55/20 channel breakout (Turtle) with rejection-rule and last-bar enhancements
findings.mechanism: new fundamentals or order imbalance push price through a multi-week channel extreme; entry on the breakout is aligned with momentum and captures the big move
findings.setup_summary: On daily bars, buy stop 3 pips above the 55-day high / sell stop 3 pips below the 55-day low; on fill, initial protective stop is the 20-day channel on the opposite side (exit and go flat on a 20-day opposite breakout, not a reversal). Take entries only while ADX is rising; layer exits in order: rejection rule (first 2 days), last-bar stop (low of the breakout bar), then 20-day channel; Bishop (ADX>40 turning down) exits all positions. Parameters robust from 50-60 days for entry; 20 days for exit.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Entry triggers on 55-day high/low break. Thesis invalidated if price closes back through the breakout level within 2 days (rejection rule), or 20-day opposite channel / last-bar stop is hit; Bishop overrides all trend exits.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: buy/sell stop 3 pips beyond 55-day high/low (stop/breakout entry). Initial stop: opposite 20-day channel extreme, then last-bar stop (low of the breakout bar), then 20-day channel. No R-multiple target; profit taken by 20-day exit or Bishop exit. Known weakness: wide stop forces small size; rejection rule and last-bar shrink realized risk to near-entry.
findings.quote: Entries are made using 55 days but exits are made with 20 days.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, Channel Breakouts, section Better Channel Breakouts (pp. 35-39)
findings.notes: The book asserts Donchian 4WR 'consistently profitable since the 1960s' and that Turtles used 55/20. On BTCUSDT 1h, rescale the bar count (55 daily bars on a 24/7 perp = ~55 hours or 55 1h bars, much shorter than intended; daily-equivalent bars are preferable). No FX weekend gaps removes the Monday true-range complication, which is favorable. Perp funding is a carry drag on long holds of a 55-day trend trade; include in the Binance cost model. ADX rising filter (only trade when ADX higher than prior bar) is an entry regime filter; Bishop is the exit component.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Riding the Rejection Rule (RRR) - trade the failed 55-day breakout
findings.mechanism: a watched multi-week breakout level that fails (no follow-through, rejection) exhausts the breakout side's power and reverses; a failed signal is a signal
findings.setup_summary: When a 55-day (or 20-day) breakout is rejected - price closes back below the breakout level within the first two days (the rejection rule condition) - enter in the opposite direction at the close of the rejection bar; protective stop at the opposite extreme of the entry bar; exit at the close of trading. The book prefers 55-day levels because 'false breakouts are more significant' at longer channels. Lineage: Raschke/Connors 'Turtle Soup'.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: rejection of a channel breakout within 2 days while the five-day flat condition holds. Invalidated when the stop (opposite extreme of the entry bar) is hit; position exits at the close of the day regardless.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: close of the rejection bar. Stop: opposite extreme of the entry bar. Exit: close of the day (1-day holding). Risk is limited to the entry bar range.
findings.quote: We are looking for a breakout that fails and then profiting from that failure.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, Pattern Recognition, section Riding the Rejection Rule (pp. 101-103)
findings.notes: Maps directly onto V8's existing failed_breakout expert (mechanism liquidity_vacuum_reentry, behavior failed_breakout_reentry). The book adds: (1) the failure must follow a flat/declining channel (five-day condition), (2) entry at close of rejection bar with stop at the entry bar's opposite extreme, (3) 1-day holding, (4) 55-day levels yield stronger failures than 20-day. 24/7 perp markets with high leverage and crowded stop clusters plausibly manufacture frequent false breakouts, but that is a falsifiable claim to test, not an assumption.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Rejection rule - breakout follow-through monitor
findings.mechanism: a breakout with no follow-through within the first two days, after a flat channel, reveals insufficient power to sustain the new level; early exit converts large channel stops into small losses
findings.setup_summary: For any breakout entry: if the channel was flat or declining for at least 5 days prior to the breakout (the five-day condition, so the rule only applies to sideways markets), liquidate if price closes back through the initial breakout level on the breakout day or the next day. The book claims this eliminates roughly half of normal stop-outs and converts ~$1,000 channel losses into ~$200 exits; same rule applied to other methods (RRR, slingshot).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close back through the initial breakout level within 2 days while the five-day condition holds. Invalidation: price holds above the breakout level for both of the first two days - rule no longer applies, shift to last-bar or 20-day stop.
findings.risk_geometry: No new entry; pure exit filter applied to existing breakouts. Realized loss is close to entry (a few pips in the book's example). Effect: higher trade count, smaller losers, comparable winners.
findings.quote: If a five-day condition is in place, liquidate a 55-day buy signal if the price of the market closes below the initial breakout level on the day of the breakout or the next day.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, Channel Breakouts, section Rejection Rule (pp. 46-50)
findings.notes: This is the book's most distinctive, falsifiable risk mechanism and a general 'principle of instant gratification': winning trades show profit in the first days; trades that fail immediately should be exited rather than hoped back to profit. For V8 this is a risk_geometry/lifecycle rule (dead-thesis check on breakouts) and a candidate REFINE of the existing failed_breakout/liquidity families' still_valid logic. On 24/7 crypto the two-day follow-through window maps cleanly to a fixed-bar window.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Swing high/low trend analysis ('123') with objective swing significance and ADX filter
findings.mechanism: price moving in higher highs/higher lows (bull) or lower highs/lower lows (bear) persists; breaking the first swing point in the trend direction guarantees a new swing extreme, so entry needs only three of the four pivot points
findings.setup_summary: Objectively define swing highs/lows (a bar whose high is above the bar on each side; significance = number of bars to the left, 3-bar highs/lows treated as significant, 1-2 bar ignored - DeMark-derived). Long when a higher low is confirmed and price breaks the first swing high; short on the mirror. Stop at the most recent significant swing low/high, trailed to each new swing point; exit when the market returns to neutral. Take trades only when ADX is higher than the prior day (filter claimed to cut ~half of losers while keeping ~95% of winners).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: break of first swing high after confirmed higher low (long) / first swing low after confirmed lower high (short). Invalidated when the recent significant swing low/high is hit, or the market transitions to neutral (e.g., higher low after lower highs = megaphone/no-trade zone).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: stop order at the first swing point (breakout entry). Stop: most recent 3-bar swing high (shorts) / low (longs), trailed to each new swing extreme. No fixed R-target; exit on neutral transition or trailing stop. Stops intentionally wide - 'only stopped out when we are wrong' and only on significant moves.
findings.quote: Go long when the market turns into a bull market, go short when the market turns into a bear market, and stand aside when the market is in any other condition.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, Trend Analysis, sections How to Profitably Trade Bull and Bear Markets / How to Trade the Trend / The Bishop (pp. 18-30)
findings.notes: The book's core contribution is making swing significance objective (3-bar rule) and entering on the break of the FIRST swing point without waiting for the confirming extreme - a concrete, falsifiable rule. The ADX rising regime filter is a candidate REGIME_FILTER feature for V8's trend family. The stop-trail-on-each-new-swing-point logic is a lifecycle rule candidate. Note V8's existing trend_pullback expert is a different mechanism (pullback-in-trend); this is the swing-structure breakout variant and should be its own family.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Bishop exit - ADX trend-exhaustion liquidation signal
findings.mechanism: when ADX (trend strength) is above 40 and turns down, the strong trend is exhausting; exiting all trend-following positions at this point captures profits near major highs/lows instead of giving back trend-following profits
findings.setup_summary: Exit ALL open trend-following positions (swing trend analysis, channel breakouts, Conqueror) on the first down day of ADX whenever ADX is above 40; no other condition or pattern matters. Rare signals: about half get you out at or near the end of the trend, the rest get you out early to re-enter later. Claimed net effect in the GBP example: adds ~1,000 pips/year to channel-breakout results.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: ADX > 40 and first lower day. Invalidation: none during the trade - it is a one-shot exit; a subsequent ADX re-acceleration is a re-entry opportunity via the base method.
findings.risk_geometry: Exit-only signal, no entry geometry. Replaces or precedes the 20-day channel exit for trend positions.
findings.quote: I look for the ADX line to be above 40 and then turn down. I then exit my trend-following positions in all the techniques that I teach in this book.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, Trend Analysis, section The Bishop (pp. 28-30); applied to channel breakouts in Chapter 3, The Bishop (pp. 40-43)
findings.notes: A clean, falsifiable lifecycle rule for V8's trend families: add an ADX-exhaustion exit variant to trend_pullback / donchian / swing families. Caveat: ADX behavior on BTC 1h (long alternating trend/range regimes, high vol persistence) may differ from FX daily; the >40 threshold must be re-estimated. Also the book pairs it with the ADX-rising entry filter - a coherent ADX regime pair (rising gates entries, peak>40 gates exits).
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Conqueror - three-timeframe moving-average confluence with adaptive ATR stop
findings.mechanism: a move is only tradable when short (10d), medium (10d MA momentum) and long (40d) trend readings are aligned; sitting out until all three agree avoids whipsaw, and an adaptive stop that tightens as conditions weaken gives a strong reward-to-risk ratio
findings.setup_summary: Compute three conditions: (1) close minus 10-day MA of close, (2) 10-day MA minus 10-day MA 10 days ago, (3) close minus close 40 days ago. Long if all three positive, short if all three negative, stand aside otherwise. Entry at the close of the triggering bar. Stop: disaster stop sized to a fixed $2,000 loss, plus 2x ATR above the lowest close in the move (Conqueror I; 12x ATR for Conqueror II), reduced by one-third each time one condition flips sign; re-enter only after a condition flips positive then negative again. Backtest (Freeburg/CTCR 1972-1998, 4 currencies): 46% profitable trades, avg win/avg loss ratio 3.31, avg trade +$1,580.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: all three conditions same sign. Invalidated when the reduced ATR stop is hit, or the money-management stop; sideways markets never trigger all-three alignment, so the system sits out.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: close of the day all three conditions align. Stop: 2x ATR above lowest close (trailing), cut by 1/3 per flipped condition; disaster stop fixed $2,000. No target - exits on stop/tightening or re-alignment logic; notable for using a different exit technique than entry (rare).
findings.quote: Go long if all three conditions are positive. Go short if all three conditions are negative. Stand aside on any other condition.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, The Conqueror, sections Enhancing the Conqueror / Adjusting the Stop (pp. 57-65)
findings.notes: Concrete 10/20/40-day triple-trend alignment with published backtest stats - strong candidate for a momentum/moving-average family expert (related to starter ids moving_average_cross, dual_momentum). The adaptive-stop rule (shrink ATR multiple by 1/3 per condition flip) is a distinctive risk_geometry refinement. On BTC 1h, MA windows would need rescaling; 24/7 noise may chop the all-three alignment more than FX, a testable hypothesis.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Stochastic divergence - daily (countertrend) vs weekly (trend change) with quantified lead times
findings.mechanism: when price makes a new extreme close but stochastics (%K/%D) do not, momentum is weaker than price - the move is at risk of reversal; divergence magnitude scales with timeframe
findings.setup_summary: Divergence = new price extreme (measured close-to-close) not confirmed by stochastics. Daily divergence predicts a short countertrend move: study of 58 daily divergences across ~30 futures found mean lead 4.5 days (SD 5.7) but mode 1 and median 2 days, mean retracement 5.9% (median 5%). Weekly divergence predicts an intermediate-term trend change: 124 cases, mode = the exact turning week, mean lead 2.8 weeks, mean retracement 15.3% (max 80%). Use daily divergence to trim 1/4 to 1/2 of a position, weekly divergence to exit longs / enter shorts aggressively on a reversal bar; Lane's stop = two bars below the two previous lows.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: unconfirmed new price extreme on stochastics. Invalidated if the divergence fails (the %K resumes the original direction - 'failure' signal, which the book trades WITH the trend); lead time is noisy, so a standalone divergence buy/sell is not mechanical without a confirmation bar.
findings.risk_geometry: No fixed entry/exit: used as a partial-profit overlay on trend positions or as entry timing with a reversal-bar confirmation. Stop: low of the countertrend move (author) / two bars below two previous lows (Lane). Countertrend expected window 1-5 days (daily).
findings.quote: In other words, the momentum of the price is less strong than the price itself.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, Stochastics, section The Best Way to Make Money Using Stochastics (pp. 76-82)
findings.notes: The most quantitatively honest part of the book: the author openly reports noisy daily lead times (mean 4.5, mode 1, SD 5.7 days) and even flags that divergences may be 'illusions' (markets retrace at least a day within two weeks ~98% of the time). The weekly-divergence trend-change claim (mode = exact turning week, mean 15.3% retracement) is the testable core. For V8: a momentum-divergence overlay/partial-profit signal, or a feature (close-in-range percentile) for existing families; daily version is weak as a standalone entry. Stochastics %K/%D map cleanly to 1h bars.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Inside day (bar) breakout - one-bar consolidation breakout with lemonade reversal
findings.mechanism: an inside bar is a day of balance; following whoever wins the breakout of the inside bar's range captures short-term directional momentum
findings.setup_summary: An inside bar has high < prior bar's high and low > prior bar's low (whole range inside prior bar). Place a buy stop above the inside bar's high and a sell stop below its low; on fill, stop at the opposite side of the inside bar and exit at the close of the breakout bar. Book claims ~55% win rate with average winner much larger than loser. Enhancement - 'lemonade' trade (a failed signal is a signal): when the initial fill is stopped, reverse to the opposite side for a claimed 70-75% win rate; multiunit tactic: take 20 pips on one unit, hold the rest to the close.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price trades through an inside bar extreme after the bar completes. Invalidated when the opposite inside-bar extreme is hit (stop); position exits at close of the breakout bar regardless of P&L.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: buy/sell stop at the inside bar extremes (breakout entry). Stop: opposite inside-bar extreme (contained risk = inside bar range). Exit: close of the breakout day (same-day hold); 20-40 pip quick-profit variant via multiunit tactic.
findings.quote: An inside day is any day that has its whole range inside the range of the previous day.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, Pattern Recognition, sections Inside Days / Double Whammy / Multiunit Tactic (pp. 91-96)
findings.notes: Highly portable to BTC 1h: 'inside day' becomes an inside bar, and 24/7 trading with no gaps makes the containment definition clean. The lemonade reversal (reverse on stop-out) is a lifecycle/psychology-relevant mechanism - 'a failed signal is a signal' - that V8 could encode as a stop-out reversal variant of the failed_breakout family. The multiunit tactic (scale out one unit at fixed pip, hold remainder) is a position_scaling lifecycle rule.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Reversal day - trend-resumption reversal bar with trend filter
findings.mechanism: a bar that makes an extreme beyond the prior bar yet closes back through it shows the prior trend's counter-move has failed and the dominant trend is reasserting (bullish = lower low + higher close; bearish = higher high + lower close)
findings.setup_summary: Bullish reversal day = lower low than the prior bar AND closes higher; bearish = higher high AND closes lower. Enter at the close of the reversal bar, hold until the close of the next bar; stop below the bar's low (long) / above its high (short). Filter: take only in the direction of the prevailing trend - the reversal day marks the end of a short-term countertrend correction and resumption of the trend; also usable as a long-term entry (stop = three-bar low from trend analysis) and with the multiunit/quick-profit variant (20-40 pips).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: reversal bar forms. Invalidated when the protective stop (bar extreme) is hit; then the lemonade reversal applies (rare for this method - most reversal-day trades are small winners, losses when stopped are larger than winners).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: close of the reversal bar (bar-close entry). Stop: below the bar's low / above its high, or a three-bar swing low for long-term use. Exit: close of the next day (or 20-40 pip quick profit).
findings.quote: A Reversal Day occurs when a pair makes a lower low than the previous day and closes higher.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, Pattern Recognition, section Reversal Days (pp. 97-101)
findings.notes: Classic key-reversal bar, strongly corroborated across the trading literature. The trend-filtered version (only take reversals in the direction of the dominant trend) makes it a trend-resumption signal rather than a countertrend picker - a useful distinction for V8's behavior family naming. The book notes taking all reversal bars regardless of trend is also net-profitable but doubles the psychological pain; a testable filter hypothesis for V8.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Slingshot - failed-high reversal with measured target and scale-out ladder
findings.mechanism: a failed higher high after a clear key-high/key-low structure shows the bull leg is over; breaking the key low confirms the reversal, and the key-high-to-key-low range projects a measured target with high odds
findings.setup_summary: Identify Key High (any high above the prior high), then Key Low (a 2-3 bar swing low), then Slingshot High (a failed high at least 3 bars from a prior higher bar that is within 20 days - both confirmations required so you are not buying a running top or picking a bottom). Sell on a break of the Key Low with ADX rising; stop = Slingshot High, set as a reversal stop (failed signal is a signal). Profit objective = Key Low minus (Slingshot High minus Key Low); take half off at 1x target, further halves at 2x/3x, trailing stop at 50% of a profit target; final unit exits on stop or Bishop. Mini-slingshot drops the 20-day confirmation, takes 100% off at target, and moves stop to breakeven at the half-way point.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: break of the Key Low after a confirmed Slingshot High. Invalidated when the Slingshot High stop (reversal) is hit or the measured target ladder completes; divergence from the measured projection is not itself an exit.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: sell stop on Key Low break. Stop: Slingshot High (reversal stop, i.e., exit-and-flip). Target: measured projection (Key Low - [Slingshot High - Key Low]); scale-outs at 1x/2x/3x target with a 50%-of-target trailing stop; final unit on stop or Bishop. Requires at least 2 contracts.
findings.quote: The first profit objective is calculated this way. Take the difference between the slingshot high and the key low. Now subtract that value from the key low.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Slingshot, sections Using the Slingshot for Profits / The Mini-Slingshot (pp. 125-130)
findings.notes: The failure-high reversal overlaps V8's failed_breakout / liquidity_sweep_reclaim mechanisms, but its distinctive contributions are the measured-target projection (range-based profit objective) and the scale-out-at-multiples ladder with trailing half-target stop - candidates for a measured-target risk_geometry variant. The two confirmations (min 3 bars from prior higher bar; prior high within 20 days) are falsifiable filters. Complexity is high relative to V8's budget; recommend backlog and simplified variants (mini-slingshot) first.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Maximum Excursion Analysis (MEA) - profit-target calibration from the MFE distribution
findings.mechanism: after any signal, the maximum favorable excursion (MFE) follows a stable distribution; setting profit targets at percentile levels converts uncertain trend follow-through into high-probability partial targets and can turn losing signals profitable
findings.setup_summary: For a given signal type (e.g., 55-day breakout), measure the maximum favorable excursion as a PERCENTAGE of price (not absolute pips) over a window, tabulate into a bell curve, and read off target probabilities - e.g., 'gains 100 pips 90% of the time, 200 pips 62%, 300 pips 32%'. Place a limit profit order at the chosen percentile target while keeping the entry stop. The book claims this principle can turn an unprofitable 5/10 MA-crossover system into a profitable one and generalizes the multiunit 'take a quick 20-pip profit' tactic.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Target-level probabilities are instrument/regime-dependent - the bell curve must be re-estimated per pair and periodically; a target unreachable for the chosen percentile means the signal is a loser under the exit stop.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: original signal trigger. Exit: limit order at the MFE-percentile target; entry stop remains active. No fixed R-multiple - targets come from the empirical excursion distribution.
findings.quote: So now you have adjusted everything to percentages. You will now have a nice bell curve that shows how much the price moves after breaking a key technical pattern.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Slingshot, section Maximum Excursion Analysis (pp. 124-125)
findings.notes: Directly actionable for V8's simulator/lab: compute MFE distributions per expert family and per regime, and let partial targets be calibrated at percentile levels instead of arbitrary R-multiples. This is a methodology input to risk_geometry design, not a new expert family. Note the honest caveat about MEA's viability and the open question of defining the excursion window objectively.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

findings.strategy_name: Fixed fractional sizing with fractional Kelly weighting, correlated-exposure cap, and drawdown time-outs
findings.mechanism: risking a fixed small fraction of equity per trade makes every loss smaller than the last (Zeno-like asymptotic approach to ruin), and because loss sequences are asymmetrical (a wipeout ends the game, a win does not guarantee survival), survival depends on bet size, not edge
findings.setup_summary: Risk a fixed fraction of equity per position: 1% recommended, 0.5% per technique/pair, 0.25% for beginners. Contracts = allowed risk divided by risk-per-contract; never widen the stop to fit more contracts. Treat highly correlated pairs (EUR/USD, USD/CHF, GBP/USD) as one risk bucket - put in all orders and cancel the rest after the first fill. Weight positions by fractional Kelly (half-Kelly F=(bp-q)/b from win rate and avg win/avg loss, only after >=30 trades). Portfolio rules: stand aside or trade smaller on an equity-curve downside break; take a time-out after 2% daily / 5% weekly / 10% monthly drawdown. Coin-flip demonstration: betting 10% of a $100 bankroll 1,000 flips wipes out with >90% probability; 1% bets drop wipeout below 5%.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Risk of ruin is bounded by the fixed fraction; invalidation thresholds are the 2%/5%/10% daily/weekly/monthly drawdown limits that trigger a mandated pause (the 'penalty box').
findings.risk_geometry: Position sizing (account-level), not entry geometry: stop distance unchanged while size = risk-fraction x equity / per-contract risk. Correlated exposure capped to one direction per correlated group.
findings.quote: If you always risk a fixed percentage of your account, you will risk fewer dollars on each trade as you lose money.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, Risk Management, sections Good Risk Management: Fixed Fractional / Highly Correlated Positions / Kelly Formula / Trade Your Equity Curve / Take a Time Out (pp. 108-117)
findings.notes: Maps onto V8's existing RiskGate / risk_geometry framework: fixed fractional sizing refines position sizing; the correlated-exposure bucket is the correlated_exposure_cap starter id (highly relevant to BTC vs ETH correlation); equity-curve-down sizing and 2/5/10% time-out thresholds are lifecycle_rule/max_drawdown_cap candidates; fractional Kelly weighting is a sizing variant that respects the 'no learned component by default' rule only if the stats come from frozen OOS records. The risk-of-ruin asymmetry argument (losses compound downward) is mathematically sound and supports V8's small-risk-per-trade invariant.
findings.book: How to Make a Living Trading Foreign Exchange - A Guaranteed Income for Life 2010

book_title: Harmonic Trading: Volume Two — Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets (Scott M. Carney, 2010), Part 1

findings.strategy_name: 5-0 harmonic pattern (failed-wave first-pullback reversal)
findings.mechanism: A failed final impulse wave (nominally breaching the prior extreme) followed by an extreme 1.618-2.24 extension leg sets up the first pullback of a trend reversal; the 50% BC retracement pinpoints the D point.
findings.setup_summary: On any timeframe: after an extended down move (X), price bounces to A, makes a failed-wave new low at B (XA extension 1.13-1.618, not above 2.24), rallies to C at a 1.618-2.24 extension of AB, then D = 50% retracement of BC converging with a Reciprocal AB=CD equal leg — a long entry at the first pullback of a reversal. Mirror for bearish. If BC never reaches 1.618 the structure is invalid.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: BC leg completes 1.618-2.24 extension of AB, D at 50% BC retracement + Reciprocal AB=CD. Invalid: C never reaches 1.618, XA extension at B exceeds 2.24, or the PRZ is violated (see PRZ-violation continuation finding).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close in the PRZ (50% BC retracement + Reciprocal AB=CD); book defers execution/management to Volume One; violations give a minimum 0.886-retracement target beyond completion; no explicit R-multiple/expiry stated.
findings.quote: the BC leg rallies to at least a 1.618 extension of the AB length, but it does not exceed 2.24. Again, this tight range of 1.618–2.24 is a defining element of the structure.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'The 5-0 Pattern' / Basic 5-0 Requirements
findings.notes: Author claims thousands of cases studied but no statistics; swing-point labeling is the hard dependency. 24/7 crypto (no exchange gaps) makes swing construction cleaner than equities, but ratio-alignments on 1h BTC are noisy; funding applies on the short side.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: RSI BAMM divergence confirmation (complex RSI structure + harmonic PRZ)
findings.mechanism: A complex (W/M-type) RSI structure built entirely beyond the extreme line creates measurable divergence: on the final retest the price makes a nominal new extreme while the RSI holds above/below its prior reading, then the reversal completes at a 1.13 or 1.618 extension of the initial reaction.
findings.setup_summary: With RSI(14): (1) RSI forms a complex W-type entirely below 30 (bullish) or M-type entirely above 70 (bearish); (2) the Trigger Bar is the price bar that closes RSI back above 30 / below 70, and its extreme marks the minimum retest level; (3) RSI must retrace to at least the 50 mid-line; (4) final divergence: price makes a nominal new low/high while RSI at an impulsive retest holds above/below its prior reading; (5) Confirmation Point completes at 1.13 extension (Trigger Bar 2-4 bars from the extreme) or 1.618 extension (Trigger Bar IS the extreme), ideally converging with a harmonic pattern (Bat/Gartley/Butterfly/Crab/5-0) completion.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: complex structure + Trigger Bar + RSI mid-50 retrace + impulsive retest holding the prior RSI reading + price nominal new extreme. Invalid: RSI never tests 50, RSI violates its prior reading on the retest (non-impulsive), price exceeds the prior extreme materially, or extensions are exceeded (beyond 2.0).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close at the Confirmation Point coordinating with the harmonic PRZ; stop: beyond 1.618 for 1.13 setups, beyond 2.0 for 1.618 setups (do-or-die); optional Acceleration Trigger (W-type above 30 after confirmation) as an entry filter; reversal expected quickly after the nominal new extreme.
findings.quote: The RSI reading MUST retrace to at least the 50 level before the final retest can occur
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'RSI BAMM' / Specific Type of RSI Retest
findings.notes: Divergence phenomenon is literature-supported (Wilder cited), but Carney's 1.13/1.618 extension rules are practitioner heuristics with case studies only. RSI(14) is fully computable from bars, deterministic, and cheap in V8's stdlib-first constraint; needs the 'response' feature group. One candidate for an ACTIVE expert if it survives screening.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: BAMM (Bat Action Magnet Move) — CD-leg continuation after B-point break
findings.mechanism: Once the CD leg of a Bat-pattern structure (B point at 50% or less of XA) breaks the prior B point, the unfilled harmonic completion acts as a magnet: price accelerates toward the 0.886 XA retracement PRZ.
findings.setup_summary: Identify a Bat structure with B point at <=50% XA retracement; when the CD leg exceeds the B point (bullish breakout / bearish breakdown), trade the segment from the B-break to the pattern's PRZ completion (0.886 XA retracement) with the direction of the larger trend. Valid situations show decisive continuation; stalls after the trigger are covered.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: CD leg exceeds the prior B point. Invalid: price stalls/lacks continuation after the trigger (cover instead of holding); also AB=CD BAMM variant uses the B-point break of a simple AB=CD.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: breakout/breakdown bar beyond the B point; target: PRZ completion (0.886 retracement typically); management: hold the bias until the PRZ is tested, cover if the move stalls after trigger; no R-multiple or expiry given.
findings.quote: the zone from the point the CD leg is triggered until it tests the completion point of the pattern continually presented a fantastic trading opportunity to capitalize on the predominant trend and the magnet effect of the harmonic price action.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 'BAMM Theory' / The Magnet Effect and Harmonic Breakouts and Breakdowns
findings.notes: Requires harmonic swing-point/pattern infrastructure not yet in V8. The 'magnet' is a narrative label; the falsifiable core is 'CD leg exceeding B point then extending to the 0.886 retracement'.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Alternate Bat (shallow midpoint extension to 1.13 XA)
findings.mechanism: A shallow midpoint (B retraces 0.382 or less of XA) predicts a deeper completion that runs stops beyond the prior extreme to the 1.13 XA extension, where the extreme BC projection (2.0-3.14) converges.
findings.setup_summary: An M/W-type structure whose B point retraces 0.382 or less of the XA leg completes as an Alternate Bat at the 1.13 XA extension (0.886 is the minimum valid level), with BC projections at 2.0/2.618/3.14; a standard Bat completion at 0.886 would have been stopped out, whereas the 1.13 is the actual reversal level.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: structure with B <=0.382 converging at the 1.13 XA extension. Invalid: price exceeds the 1.13 (that is the stop/invalidation); 0.886 is minimum support/resistance so anything shallower than that invalidates.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close at 1.13 XA extension (just beyond the standard Bat PRZ); stop beyond 1.13; target: reversal into the trend; the 1.13 serves as the pattern's validation/violation limit.
findings.quote: the Alternate Bat typically completes in the area beyond the 0.886 retracement, but it should not exceed the 1.13.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Alternate Bat Pattern'
findings.notes: The stop-run dynamic is highly relevant to leveraged crypto (stops cluster at prior extremes and round numbers), but pattern identification needs discretion. The 1.13 invalidation is a clean, deterministic rule once swing points exist.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Reciprocal AB=CD continuation approximation in trend channels
findings.mechanism: In an established trend channel, corrective legs of approximately equal length mark continuation points; the AB leg is often the first corrective leg of a new trend and the CD leg tests the equal-length completion.
findings.setup_summary: Within an established uptrend channel, a bullish Reciprocal AB=CD (lazy Z/S shape, AB and CD roughly equal) completes near channel support and marks a continuation point — entry at the CD completion; mirror for downtrends. The completion is an approximation, not an exact reversal point.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: equal-leg correction completing within a well-defined channel; often the first corrective leg of a new trend. Invalid: CD overshoots the equivalent leg by a wide margin and the channel breaks.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: CD leg test of the equivalent completion point (bar close); complement with channel lines and the reciprocal ratio (e.g., 1.618 AB projection corresponds to ~0.618 AB retracement at D); no explicit stop/expiry given — channel-based.
findings.quote: the completion of the Reciprocal AB=CD pattern is more of an approximation than an exact reversal point.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.4 'Harmonic Patterns Relative to the Trend' / Bullish and Bearish Reciprocal AB=CD within Trend Channels
findings.notes: Explicitly an approximation measure — a candidate 'harmonic retracement convergence' signal feeding the location feature group rather than a standalone expert. Reuses the trend_continuation mechanism of the existing trend_pullback family.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: 1.13 failed-wave stop run (nominal breach of prior extreme then reversal)
findings.mechanism: Nominal breach of a prior extreme to the 1.13 extension of the last leg is a failed breakout/breakdown stop run that reverses; exceeding the 1.13 signals continuation to the 1.27 or 1.618 areas.
findings.setup_summary: After an extended down leg, price bounces quickly then rolls over to a nominal new low at the 1.13 extension of the prior leg and reverses; mirror for tops. The 1.13 defines the sweep depth — if price exceeds 1.13, the rule of thumb is continuation to 1.27/1.618 rather than reversal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price taps the 1.13 extension of a prior leg at a prior extreme and reverses. Invalid: close beyond 1.13 (then the continuation rule applies); reversal candidate requires the failed-wave structure (void of distinct harmonic pattern).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close at the 1.13 extension; stop just beyond 1.13; target: reversal; or flip to a continuation trade toward 1.27/1.618 if 1.13 is exceeded. Author notes this was adopted precisely to avoid stop-outs just before reversals.
findings.quote: It has been my experience that price action that exceeds a critical 1.13 extension level frequently will continue farther to the 1.27 or 1.618 areas.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.2 'Harmonic Impulse Waves' / 1.13 Extension — The Failed Wave
findings.notes: Directly refines the existing liquidity_sweep_reclaim family by quantifying sweep depth (1.13) and adding the exceeding-1.13 continuation rule — a concrete falsifiable addition. High leverage in perps clusters stops at prior extremes, so the mechanism is structurally active on BTC.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Harmonic PRZ violation as continuation (failed pattern, 0.886 target)
findings.mechanism: Violation of a fully-tested harmonic PRZ creates a liquidity vacuum: price accelerates in the primary trend direction to at least the 0.886 retracement beyond the completion point.
findings.setup_summary: After a harmonic pattern's entire PRZ has been tested, a violation — especially on a second test after a nominal first-test reaction — is a continuation trade with the primary trend, targeting at least the 0.886 retracement beyond the pattern completion. The 2000/2008 case studies are the book's core evidence (failed monster bullish Gartley and 5-0 → acceleration of downtrends).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: entire PRZ tested, then price violates it (second test preferred); failure trigger precedes sharp continuation. Invalid (reversal side): strong reversal off the first test with follow-through.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close after PRZ violation; target: minimum 0.886 retracement beyond completion; stop: back above/below the violated PRZ; continuation typically accelerates after brief consolidation.
findings.quote: when the 5-0 pattern fails, the price action typically declines decidedly lower. In many cases, the breakdown in the price action usually declines to at least the relative 0.886 retracement beyond completion of the pattern.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 '5-0 Pattern Violations' + Ch.1 'The Importance of Pattern Violations'
findings.notes: Corroborates the existing V8 failed_breakout expert (liquidity_vacuum_reentry) and adds a concrete measurable target (0.886 beyond completion) and a second-test trigger — a strong refinement candidate. 24/7 crypto with high leverage makes post-violation acceleration follow-through observable on 1h bars.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Harmonic completion pullback in established trend channel
findings.mechanism: A harmonic pattern completing inside an established trend channel is a continuation signpost: the PRZ converging with channel support/resistance gives a high-bias entry with the trend at your back, even very late in the trend.
findings.setup_summary: Within a well-established uptrend channel, a bullish AB=CD (or Gartley/Bat) completing at the lower channel support is a long continuation entry — the pattern's completion is a minimum requirement before the trend resumes; mirror for downtrends. Works regardless of how far the trend has already progressed.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: harmonic pattern completes in the trend direction at channel support/resistance; price reverses after testing all PRZ numbers. Invalid: channel is broken, or pattern completes against the trend and fails (failure = continuation signal for the primary trend).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close at pattern completion within the channel; no explicit stop/expiry — channel-constrained; extension patterns (Crab/Butterfly/Alternate Bat) can poke below/above the channel in volatile completions.
findings.quote: Quite simply, executing a trade in such a manner attempts to put 'the wind to your back' and to capitalize on the continuation of a distinct bullish trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.4 'Harmonic Patterns Relative to the Trend' / AB=CD Patterns as Continuation Signals within Established Trend Channels
findings.notes: Refines the existing trend_pullback family (trend_continuation mechanism): harmonic PRZ completion at channel edge is an entry-timing refinement over the ema-cross trigger. BTC 1h trends are persistent; 24/7 market keeps channels intact across weekends.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Extreme harmonic impulse wave at 0.886 retracement (counter-trend scalp)
findings.mechanism: Confluence of a deep 0.886 retracement of a major leg with an extreme 1.618-2.24 impulse extension produces a precise zone for a sharp but brief counter-trend bounce that requires aggressive profit-taking.
findings.setup_summary: Price reverses at a point where a 1.618-2.24 impulse extension of the final leg converges with a 0.886 retracement of the larger move — a precise short-term bounce zone. Many of these are only brief reactions, so it is a scalp executed on the initial test with tight management.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: convergence of the 0.886 retracement and an extreme impulse extension (minimum 1.618); reversal on the initial test. Invalid: no stabilization and continuation through the zone; a secondary test is often required before the larger move.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: initial test of the confluence zone (bar close); management must be tight with aggressive profit-taking because reactions are sharp but brief; secondary test of the PRZ common before decisive continuation; no R-multiple/expiry given.
findings.quote: The combination of the 0.886 support with the extreme impulse extension frequently provides a brief reversal in most cases.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.2 'Harmonic Impulse Waves' / Extreme Bullish/Bearish Harmonic Impulse Wave at 0.886 Retracement
findings.notes: Brief-scalp character conflicts with V8's 1h fill-at-close simulator (taker costs, funding on counter-trend holds). The confluence zone itself is a usable location feature; as an expert it is lower priority.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Impulsive vs complex RSI extreme filter (extreme readings are not signals)
findings.mechanism: RSI extremes separate into two structures: impulsive (V-shaped, resolves in 1-2 bars) which signal continuation of the trend, and complex (W/M-type persisting at the extreme line) which set up divergence reversals; a raw RSI reading below 30/above 70 is not a signal.
findings.setup_summary: When RSI(14) tags below 30 or above 70, classify the structure: if it snaps back across the extreme line within 1-2 bars (impulsive), treat it as continuation of the predominant trend, not a reversal; only a complex W/M-type structure that persists at the extreme is a valid divergence-reversal starting point.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: RSI extreme reading (structure classification). Invalid: none as a trade — this is a filter; impulsive extremes explicitly do not warrant a reversal trade and may signal continuation.
findings.risk_geometry: Filter only — no entry/stop/target. Applied as a precondition to any RSI-based reversal expert and to avoid fading strong trends on V-shaped RSI extremes.
findings.quote: A Relative Strength reading below the 30 limit does not automatically signify a trade opportunity. In fact, certain extreme impulse structures can signal significant continuations of the predominant trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'RSI BAMM' / Two Types of Bullish Indicator Structures
findings.notes: A cheap deterministic filter on bar data; guards against naive RSI-oversold fading in trending regimes. No existing V8 RSI family — this is a precondition for any future RSI-based expert and a rejection-of-naive-oversold note.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Pattern failures as trend-bias information (signpost methodology)
findings.mechanism: Pattern completions are signposts, not standalone signals: the price action at a PRZ — whether it reverses or fails — is the information; a critical pattern failure signals acceleration of the primary trend, and repeated failures confirm the regime.
findings.setup_summary: Methodology: analyze price action at the PRZ of harmonic patterns within the predominant trend. When a critical bullish PRZ is violated in a downtrend, the failure is a short-side continuation signal (and vice versa); the 2000/2008 case studies show repeated failed bullish setups marked accelerating declines. Also: avoid one-sided bias; analyze both sides relative to the trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Signal: a critical harmonic PRZ is fully tested then violated; the failure itself, not the pattern, is the tradeable continuation signal. Non-signal: a valid reversal off the PRZ (then the completion is the signal).
findings.risk_geometry: Methodological — informs bias/regime rather than a specific geometry; continuation targets described as the next harmonic level (e.g., 0.886).
findings.quote: the failure of long-term bullish patterns led to a substantial downside continuation.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.1 'The Importance of Pattern Violations' and 'It's Not the Pattern's Fault'
findings.notes: Aligns with V8's falsification program: setup failure is evidence, not noise. The operational claim ('violation of a tested harmonic zone → continuation to at least the next harmonic level') is testable on frozen OOS; the narrative parts are retrospectives.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: RSI BAMM extension stop and do-or-die invalidation
findings.mechanism: Setup validity is defined by a hard invalidation beyond the confirmation extension: for 1.13-confirmation setups the stop zone is beyond 1.618; for 1.618 setups beyond 2.0; tandem violation of both the RSI BAMM extension and the pattern PRZ = failed setup.
findings.setup_summary: For any RSI BAMM trade, the stop/invalidation is a deterministic function of the confirmation extension: valid reversals do not exceed the confirmation extension by much; 1.13 setups are invalidated beyond the 1.618 of the final move, 1.618 setups beyond the 2.0. Violations, especially on the first test, flag a strong primary trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Stop: beyond 1.618 for 1.13-confirmation setups; beyond 2.0 for 1.618-confirmation setups. Failure: tandem violation of the extension and the pattern PRZ; early warning = PRZ violation in the upper/lower range before the extension is even reached.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop: beyond the next harmonic extension of the final move (1.618 or 2.0). No target changes — exit at reversal continuation; do-or-die discipline with little discretion.
findings.quote: As a general rule, the 1.13 extension typically employs the area beyond the 1.618 to define its stop loss zone. In comparison, those situations that trigger a 1.618 extension will typically define the area beyond the 2.0 as a violation of the setup.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'RSI BAMM' / Bullish RSI BAMM Violations and Stop Loss Considerations
findings.notes: Concrete, deterministic stop logic usable in RiskGate admission and lifecycle dead-thesis checks. Complements the atr_stop/stop_distance_atr vocabulary with ratio-based invalidation; first-test-violation-flag also functions as a trend-strength signal.
findings.book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

findings.strategy_name: Scheduled-Event Straddle (earnings straddle)
findings.mechanism: Scheduled binary events expand volatility; buying both call and put before the event profits from any large move because the in-the-money leg gains more (rising delta) than the out-of-the-money leg loses (falling delta).
findings.setup_summary: For a stock with earnings 3 trading days away that reports after the bell, trades >1M shares/day, beta >=2.0, price >=$40, and gapped >$1.00 at its last two earnings: if 2-of-3 oscillators (RSI(5)<30/>70, Stoch %K(5)<25/>75, CCI(20)<-100/>+100) show oversold/overbought, buy the anticipated-side option 3 days pre-earnings and the opposite side at earnings-day close (same, nearest strike); otherwise buy both sides before the earnings close. Profit requires a gap >$0.50-$1.00 at the event open.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: event 3 sessions out + 2-of-3 oscillator extreme (or no extreme -> buy both sides). Invalidation: event gap <$0.50 at open (judgment call, smaller returns); quiet market cycle where volatile stocks do not move on earnings; position capped at 5 trading days post-event.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: buy-at-close, nearest same strike, both sides (option premium at risk only, no stop). Target: post-event gap run; exit losing side at open, hold winner, exit at close of 5th trading day after announcement. Expiry: 5 bars hard cap + option expiration rules.
findings.quote: as long as the stock moves big, we should always show a proﬁt on the trade because of the delta factor, and normally that proﬁt is large enough to cover commissions and the spread and still post a solid double-digit-percentage winner
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 13 'Options Strategies: Neutral' - The Straddle (pp. 283-308; file lines 1-294)
findings.notes: Requires options (delta asymmetry) and a scheduled-event calendar; perp crypto has neither earnings nor listed options on most venues. Template could map to macro events (FOMC/CPI) with Deribit options, but is outside the perp-futures scope. Book states this works only in a 12-16 week earnings-season window.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Post-Event Directional Follow-Through Exit (candle-persistence hold)
findings.mechanism: After a scheduled-event gap, the direction of the gap tends to persist while daily candles keep closing in the gap direction; the loser is discarded at the open and the winner is ridden until candle direction reverses or a hard 5-bar cap.
findings.setup_summary: After the event gap, sell the losing side at the open; hold the winning side (calls in a gap-up, puts in a gap-down) for every session whose candle closes in the gap direction (green for longs, red for shorts), and force exit at the close of the 5th trading day after the announcement.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: event gap >$1.00 at open, or $0.50-$1.00 as a judgment extension. Invalidation: first counter-directional close (red candle for a long, green for a short); mandatory exit at day 5.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: exit loser at open, keep winner (frozen at event). Stop: candle direction reversal (red/green flip). Target: none - ride as long as candles persist. Expiry: 5 trading days post-event hard cap.
findings.quote: We will hold our calls for every day the stock puts in a green candle (close is higher than the open) up to ﬁve trading days after the announcement.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 13 'Options Strategies: Neutral' - Taking Off a Straddle (pp. 300-305; file lines 49-205)
findings.notes: Directly transferable as a lifecycle/exit rule: after a scheduled macro event in crypto (FOMC, CPI, ETF decision), hold while hourly/daily bars persist in the gap direction, hard cap at N bars, dead-thesis on first counter close. Crypto has no true gaps, but post-event directional regimes exist. This is the exit companion to the straddle entry.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Fade-the-News Gap Close ('gap and crap')
findings.mechanism: After a scheduled-event gap, 'fade the news' order flow often closes the gap and runs the market opposite to the gap direction; the book warns this is not mechanical and a run in the gap direction must always be anticipated.
findings.setup_summary: After a large event gap (up or down), anticipate partial or full gap closure within a few sessions as post-news flow fades; position counter to the gap with the explicit acknowledgment that continuation ('a run in the direction of the gap') is the alternative scenario.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: large event gap. Invalidation: gap continuation - 'we always have to anticipate a run in the direction of the gap'; the book gives no mechanical entry, calling it a judgment call.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: none mechanical (judgment). Stop/target: not specified. Expiry: within days of the gap.
findings.quote: after the opening gap, what usually happens is that a 'fade the news' mentality takes over, and traders seek to close the gap. This is not always the case, so we always have to anticipate a run in the direction of the gap.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 13 'Options Strategies: Neutral' - Taking Off a Straddle (p. 301; file lines 82-88)
findings.notes: The book itself flags the competing continuation scenario, so this is a regime filter rather than a standalone expert: after crypto macro events, test gap-fade reversion against gap-persistence as a two-arm hypothesis. Crypto retail flow often produces similar post-news reversals.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: No Exposure Through Scheduled Binary Events
findings.mechanism: Scheduled binary announcements create unmodelable overnight event risk; the author's system 'normally requires that we sell prior to an earnings announcement', and his one discretionary override produced a -25% gap-style loss.
findings.setup_summary: Flat positions before a scheduled high-impact announcement unless the strategy explicitly prices event risk: exit at the prior close and re-enter after the event. The book's cautionary case: a position up +12% was held over an earnings announcement and gapped from ~25.48 to below 20.00, booked as 'a very embarrassing loss'.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: scheduled event within the holding window. Invalidation: not applicable - this is an avoidance rule, not a trade.
findings.risk_geometry: Exit at the close before the event; re-entry allowed after the announcement resolves.
findings.quote: my trading systems normally require that we sell prior to an earnings announcement, I decided to hold one of my positions over the announcement in the hope that the company... would beat Street estimates. The company closed trading at a price of 25.48, a full +12 percent over our entry price... I woke the next morning to ﬁnd the same stock trading below 20.00
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 16 'The Bigger Vision' - Trading Teaches You to Be Humble (pp. 319-321; file lines 594-622)
findings.notes: Directly transferable: crypto perps trade 24/7 with high leverage, so scheduled macro events (FOMC, CPI, halvings, large listings) can gap the mark price materially. A RiskGate rule 'no open exposure through scheduled events unless the expert's thesis prices them' is cheap, falsifiable, and consistent with V8's risk-rule layering.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Multi-Oscillator Extreme Confluence Reversal (leg-in trigger)
findings.mechanism: Short-term overextension: when at least two independent oscillators (RSI(5), Stoch %K(5), CCI(20)) simultaneously register oversold/overbought, price tends to move opposite within ~3 days - used here as the pre-event 'leg in' timing device.
findings.setup_summary: On a daily chart, oversold if RSI(5)<30, Stoch %K(5)<25, CCI(20)<-100; overbought if >70, >75, >+100. Requiring agreement from any two registers the extreme condition; then expect the opposite-direction move within roughly three sessions (buy calls if oversold, puts if overbought).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 2-of-3 oscillators at extreme. Invalidation: trend continuing to new extremes (no bounce); the book uses it as a 3-day timing signal, not a hold.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: at the close of the signal day. Stop/target: not stated for the reversal itself (it is a timing filter for the straddle leg-in).
findings.quote: We need agreement from any two of these indicators to register an oversold or overbought condition. If we get such a condition, then we will leg into the trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 13 'Options Strategies: Neutral' - The Straddle Strategy: An 11-Point Review (p. 306; file lines 242-261)
findings.notes: Fully computable on crypto OHLCV; the 2-of-3 confluence is a cheap falsifiable variant of rsi_oversold_reversal. Caveat for 24/7 no-gap markets: oscillator extremes form intraday differently than on exchange-gapped daily bars; the 3-day bounce horizon is testable as a BACKLOG candidate.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Legged / Staged Entry Around a Scheduled Event
findings.mechanism: Staging the entry across days - the anticipated post-event direction leg bought 3 days pre-event, the opposite leg at event-day close - captures pre-event drift and improves average fill versus buying both sides at once.
findings.setup_summary: When 2-of-3 oscillators show oversold 3 days before a scheduled event, buy the calls at that day's close and the puts on event-day close; if overbought, reverse the order. If no extreme, buy both sides before the event-day close. Always leg out: sell the losing side at the event-open gap.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: oscillator extreme 3 days pre-event. Invalidation: no green light - then buy both sides at once; legging assumes pre-event drift toward the anticipated side.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: staged buy-at-close across two sessions. Exit: leg-out at event open (sell loser, keep winner).
findings.quote: We are given a green light to leg into the trade when the stock is either oversold or overbought three days before the earnings announcement.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 13 'Options Strategies: Neutral' - Putting on the Straddle (pp. 299-300; file lines 9-47)
findings.notes: Staged execution is venue-agnostic and expressible in V8 as a sizing/timing lifecycle method (enter first tranche early when a pre-event drift signal fires, second tranche at event). Requires an event calendar; the pre-event drift assumption is testable on crypto macro-event days.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Historical Event-Move Size as Selection Feature
findings.mechanism: Prior event-move magnitude is persistent for an instrument: selecting only stocks that gapped >$1.00 at their last two earnings, and preferring higher-priced, more volatile, high-beta names, concentrates the universe on instruments that actually deliver event moves.
findings.setup_summary: Filter the event-play universe: require >1M shares/day, beta >=2.0, price >=$40, and a gap >$1.00 at each of the last two scheduled announcements; 'the larger the dollar amount of the gap, however, the more proﬁtable the trade will be.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: history of large event gaps + liquidity + beta + price filters. Invalidation: 'quiet market cycles when even the most volatile of stocks do not move that much in response to earnings.'
findings.risk_geometry: Selection filter only - no entry/stop/target.
findings.quote: This is why it is so important to select stocks that are higher in price, are very volatile, and have had a history of multibucker gaps at earnings.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 13 'Options Strategies: Neutral' - Taking Off a Straddle (p. 304; file lines 170-174)
findings.notes: Clean, falsifiable feature input: for crypto macro events, average |price move| around prior FOMC/CPI releases (and prior listing/listing-futures events) as a per-instrument selection feature. Event calendar for crypto is sparser than equity earnings season, hence MEDIUM.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Signal Crowding Degrades Entry (capacity lesson)
findings.mechanism: When many traders run the identical signal, the shared order flow concentrates at one price and the entry degenerates into gap-and-run or gap-and-collapse; edge depends on crowding, so risk and order flow should be diversified across many independent strategies.
findings.setup_summary: Thought-experiment: 20,000 copies of an automated signal all bidding KLAC at 50.00 with 500 shares each = 10M shares aimed at one price vs 5M average daily volume - the stock either gaps up and never looks back or opens at 50, runs, then collapses 'once all that volume is assimilated'. Neither outcome is profitable for the crowd.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not a trade - a design lesson: diversify across dozens of independent strategies rather than one popular signal.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated.
findings.quote: Either KLAC will gap up and over 50.00 and not look back, or it will gap open at 50.00, run up a bit, then collapse once all that volume is assimilated. Neither scenario provides a proﬁtable trading environment.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 16 'The Bigger Vision' - Automated Money Machines (pp. 324-326; file lines 751-778)
findings.notes: Crypto perps are arguably more crowding-sensitive (retail-heavy, funding signals, exchange flow concentration). Lesson maps to V8's registry design: multiple independent mechanism families over one shared scorer/ranker, and awareness that a popular signal's fill quality decays. Corroborates V8 rule 14's preference for simple, diverse baselines.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Commit to a Thesis but Hold It Loosely (dead-thesis discipline)
findings.mechanism: A directional bias is needed to generate a trade, but a bias that is wrong must be dropped immediately: 'Let the markets do what they want to do!' - the market mantra that converts a misread bias into a quick, accepted loss rather than a hope trade.
findings.setup_summary: Every trade enters with a bullish/bearish bias (built from MAs, trendlines, indicators); when price action invalidates the bias, take the quick loss and move on - holding a wrong bias turns small losers into jackpot-sized losses and turns winners into 'paper proﬁts dwindled to nothing'.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: entry bias in place. Invalidation: bias misread - exit immediately ('taking the quick loss and moving on').
findings.risk_geometry: Quick-loss acceptance; no stated stop multiple.
findings.quote: Traders need to hold an initial bias toward the markets and truly commit themselves to it in the form of real-money trades, but they must also refuse to cling to that bias when it proves to be a misread.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 16 'The Bigger Vision' - Trading Teaches You to Hold Your Biases Loosely (pp. 317-318; file lines 493-541)
findings.notes: Reinforces V8's existing design: 'still_valid / dead-thesis' as a separate exit from the stop, and the frozen-thesis pattern in the formalized experts. Market-agnostic discipline lesson, not a new strategy.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Stick to Frozen Parameters - No Discretionary Overrides
findings.mechanism: The trading system is treated as knowing better than the trader; the author's worst recent trade was a discretionary override of a frozen rule ('sell prior to earnings'), converting a +12% winner into a ~-25% realized loss overnight - the failure mode of ad-hoc variance.
findings.setup_summary: Apply the system mechanically: 'there is always room in every trader's toolbox for ingenuity' within parameters, but once a system is established, 'stick with it' - overrides like holding through a scheduled event against the rule are how wins become losses.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not a trade - discipline rule.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated.
findings.quote: for the sake of your trading success, adopt a humble attitude toward both the markets and your various trading disciplines. Both know better than you do.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 16 'The Bigger Vision' - Trading Teaches You to Be Humble (pp. 318-321; file lines 594-622) and Final Thoughts (pp. 329-331)
