findings.notes: Maps directly to V8's versioning discipline: parameter/threshold changes are VARIANTS of one family evaluated on frozen OOS, never in-place discretionary tweaks. Corroborates the challenger + frozen-OOS registry decision model.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

book_title: Trend Trading for a Living: Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living (Thomas K. Carr / Dr. Stoxx, 2007)

findings.strategy_name: Cross-market channel-breakout transfer (Bonds breakout -> S&P entry)
findings.mechanism: A breakout in a leading market transfers directional signal to a correlated follower; the leader's breakout, not the follower's own, carries the information.
findings.setup_summary: Daily timeframe. When Treasury Bonds close above the highest high of the last 14 days, buy the S&P 500 at market on close. Exit either on a trailing stop of the lowest low of the last 17 days in Bonds, or at a $3,000 fixed dollar stop. Reported results: $141,792 profit, average win 2.20x average loss, drawdown <13% of monies earned; a very short-term variant with a same-day '1/1 bailout' won 42 of 49 trades (82% accuracy). Control: the S&P's own 14-day channel breakouts produced a 'miserable track record.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: leader (Bonds) close above its prior 14-day high. Exit/invalidation: leader close below its 17-day low, or fixed $3,000 stop. Thesis dies if leader breakouts stop leading the follower (cross-market relationship regime breaks).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry market-on-close; stop = trailing 17-day low in the leader market or fixed dollar ($3,000); no profit target (let run); short-horizon variant uses a 1/1 same-day bailout.
findings.quote: Thus, when Bonds break out of a 14-day channel, buy the S&P, exit at a dollar loss or a 17-day channel breakdown in Bonds.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 15, 'Just What Does Make the Stock Market Rally?' (pp. 234-237)
findings.notes: Data-blocked until multi-instrument tape exists. The specific bond/stock macro link (interest rates -> equity valuation) is absent in crypto, but the leader-follower mechanism is falsifiable on 24/7 no-gap crypto: e.g., BTC channel breakout leading altcoin entries, or ETH/BTC-ratio breakout as a signal. The book's key evidence point is signal-quality asymmetry: WHICH market breaks out matters more than the breakout rule itself. Also usable as a cross_market feature input.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Buy new highs / sell new lows (X-day channel breakout)
findings.mechanism: Strength follows strength: a market making new X-day highs tends to continue; the public's instinct to sell strength and await pullbacks is the losing habit.
findings.setup_summary: Daily timeframe. When today's high exceeds the highest high of the last X days, buy on close; exit N bars later (13 days in the illustration) or at a fixed dollar stop ($3,500 in the test). Symmetric short on new X-day lows. Falsifiable: new-high breakouts carry positive expectancy; Williams asserts more money has been made buying new highs and selling new lows than with any other technique.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: high > highest high of prior X days. Invalidation: fixed dollar stop hit, or price falls back inside the prior range before the exit date (breakout fails).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on bar close after the new high; stop = fixed dollar ($3,500) or below prior structure; target = exit after fixed N bars (13), no fixed R target.
findings.quote: more money has been made by buying new highs and selling new lows than with any other techniques known to traders.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 15, 'Let's Break Some Bad Habits' — Truth 2 (pp. 239-240)
findings.notes: Classic Turtle-style breakout, heavily corroborated across the library and maps directly to V8's existing trend_pullback complement (buying strength vs buying pullbacks). Note the book's own evidence is split: the same chapter reports standalone S&P channel breakouts as poor with insufferable drawdown, profit concentrated in one large trade — so V8 must treat this as a challenger to test on frozen OOS, not an assumption. 24/7 crypto removes gap-through risk on breakout stops.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Buy strong closes (close in upper portion of the day's range)
findings.mechanism: A close near the high of the range signals demand control and continuation; strength is power a market needs to continue its trend.
findings.setup_summary: Daily timeframe. If the close is in the upper 65% of the day's range, buy at that close and exit 5, 10, 15, or 20 days later with a protective stop. Symmetric: sell closes in the lower 35%. Falsifiable: strong-close momentum shows positive forward returns — reported to make money in all markets tested via System Writer.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close within upper 65% of day's range. Invalidation: protective stop hit within the holding window; strength thesis dead if a subsequent close prints in the lower range.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at bar close; stop = protective (dollar); target = exit after fixed horizon (5/10/15/20 days), no fixed R target.
findings.quote: If price today closed in the upper 65% of the day's range, what would happen if I bought on that close and exited 5, 10, 15, and 20 days later? ... In all markets, this basic strategy made money.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 15, 'Let's Break Some Bad Habits' — Truth 1 (pp. 238-239)
findings.notes: Close-position-in-range is a 'response'-group feature directly measurable on BTCUSDT 1h/4h; the full buy-on-close-exit-N-days strategy is a backlog candidate. Corroborates the general 'buy strength' theme shared with donchian_breakout and with V8's existing failed_breakout (which trades the failure of strength). Williams contrasts this with the bad habit of 'awaiting a pullback' on limit-up-style strength.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Stop distance beyond noise; dollar stops over technical stops; risk-budget sizing
findings.mechanism: Stops are a damage-control shield against unpredictable price; stops placed within random fluctuation get 'gunned' and convert profitable entries into losses. Stop distance is the single largest performance variable in a system.
findings.setup_summary: Always use a stop, placed with the broker, located beyond the market's random fluctuation rather than at tight technical levels; size positions so risk per trade is capped (e.g., 5% of a $100k account). Empirical demonstration on one identical S&P day system: a $500 stop lost $41,750 (26% accuracy); the same entries with a $1,500 stop made +$116,880 (56% accuracy); a $6,000 stop made +$269,525 (70% accuracy) but raised the largest losing trade to $5,920.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A stop is mis-placed if routine noise hits it (too tight) or if per-trade risk exceeds the money-management budget (too wide for the account size).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry not specified by the rule (applies to any entry); stop = dollar-based beyond noise (~$800-$1,200 commodities; $1,750-$2,500 S&P) or a key market turning point; a time stop (end of day) may be coupled with the dollar stop; sizing = risk budget / stop distance (at 5% of $100k, a $6,000 stop allows 1 contract while a $1,500 stop allows 2, doubling profit on the same account).
findings.quote: the closer your stop is the more often you will be stopped out ... stops must be beyond-or past-random fluctuations.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 15, 'Comments on Setting Stops' (pp. 240-243); 'Learning How To Lose Money' (pp. 223-224)
findings.notes: Direct input to V8 RiskGate and stop design: stop distance should be derived from noise/ATR, not fixed tight levels — consistent with V8's stop_r/ATR-ref geometry. Crypto specifics: no gaps means wide stops are not gap-through hazards, and high leverage makes the contracts = risk-budget / stop-distance sizing rule essential; dollar stops should be expressed in volatility terms (funding and fees affect stop-and-reverse frequency).
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Trend systems: no protective stops, no fixed targets — let winners run
findings.mechanism: A trend-following system's payoff comes from catching a few large trend moves; bolting on protective stops or fixed profit targets truncates those big wins and dampens accuracy and profit per trade.
findings.setup_summary: For non-reversal (always-in-market, stop-and-reverse) trend-following systems, do not add money-management protective stops or fixed profit targets; exit only on trend reversal. Empirical claims over 20 years: a money-management stop cuts winning-trade percentage by 10-15% and average profit per trade by up to 1/3; fixed targets dampen system efficiency. Coffee system table: the $1,000 stop had $12,553 drawdown, the $4,500 stop $14,855 drawdown but made almost $30,000 more.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The design is wrong for a given system if the majority of its profit comes from small wins rather than from a few large trend catches.
findings.risk_geometry: Exit only at trend reversal (stop-and-reverse) or when the move tops/bottoms; no fixed R target; stop-and-reverse points intentionally wide.
findings.quote: you cannot improve, appreciably, a good system by using targets ... effective commodity systems do better without a protective stop loss than with one—if they are not reversal systems.
findings.chapter_anchor: 'Secrets of System Developing and Trading' (pp. 229-230)
findings.notes: Directly challenges V8's trend_pullback fixed target_r 1.0 / stop_r 1.0 design; suggests a trailing 'let-run' exit variant as a challenger on frozen OOS rather than accepting the fixed-R geometry. Crypto caveat: long holds pay funding, so the let-profits-run prescription must be weighed against perp funding drag and treated as a falsifiable claim. Reconciliation with 'always use stops': stops are for damage control, but on always-in-market reversal systems a protective stop merely taxes accuracy.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Winners vs losers: stops, money management, and inaction exits
findings.mechanism: The behavioral edge is in discipline, not intelligence: winners enforce stops and money management, exit trades that are 'not doing anything,' and concentrate on a few markets; losers ignore money management, cannot tolerate being flat, and ignore their equity.
findings.setup_summary: Modeling of 20 winning and 30 losing traders: all winners used stops, had a form of money management, were technical traders, could recount one big loss they would not repeat, and 'kicked out trades just because they weren't doing anything'; losers had little money management, were addicted to the rush of being in a trade, never looked at their equity, and hopped markets/newsletters.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The time-based inaction exit is harmful if it systematically cuts trades that were idle but later resolved in profit (exit faster than the system's payoff horizon).
findings.risk_geometry: Stops always used; time/inaction stop for non-performing trades; formal money management; concentrated market focus (one winner traded only Soybeans since 1956).
findings.quote: they use stops and speak of 'kicking out trades just because they weren't doing anything.'
findings.chapter_anchor: 'The Difference between Winners and Losers' (pp. 230-232)
findings.notes: Maps to existing V8 lifecycle machinery: expiry_bars and dead-thesis (still_valid) exits are the mechanical form of the winner's inaction stop; RiskGate and one-exposure-per-direction enforce the money-management separation. The 'being flat is unbearable' loser pattern argues for raising trade-quality bar rather than trading frequency.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Time creates profit — hold through pullbacks; longer timeframes have larger profit potential
findings.mechanism: Large wins require time to mature; shortening the timeframe or exiting on early adverse pullbacks truncates the profit that large trend moves provide.
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable claim: profit scales with holding horizon — 'the longer a system's time frame, the greater the potential for a large profit.' Large trend moves contain substantial adverse pullbacks that must be endured; traders are typically shaken out just before the move resumes. Supporting practice: preframe equity dips and hold until the trend tops/bottoms or reaches major support.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The hold-through-pullback prescription fails in trend-less regimes where adverse pullbacks convert winners to losers (regime dependence).
findings.risk_geometry: Hold until the trend tops/bottoms or price reaches major support; exit on a bail-out indicator/system rather than mental discomfort; preframe equity dips.
findings.quote: never, ever forget that it is time that creates large winnings. The longer a system's time frame, the greater the potential for a large profit.
findings.chapter_anchor: 'Nervous Nellies—Heaven Bound' (pp. 227-229)
findings.notes: For V8 this argues against too-short expiry_bars on the trend-continuation family and is a rationale for a trailing/let-run exit variant (see NEW_let_profits_run). Crypto specifics: holding through pullbacks pays funding; 24/7 markets have no session boundaries to force exits, so hold duration is purely a rule parameter — directly testable on BTCUSDT 1h.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: No perfect system; adaptation over mechanical absolutism
findings.mechanism: Markets contain high random influence; no single mechanical system can fully specify behavior, so systematic rules must be combined with judgment about when conditions fit the rules.
findings.setup_summary: Meta-lesson: 'A perfect system or approach does not exist. Never has, never will.' Use systems for entries, absolute stops, and precise rules, but pass when conditions do not fit the rules; markets carry high random influence from news, weather, and trader outlooks. The chapter also debunks Gann-style 'cosmic' prediction as unfalsifiable marketing (forecasts right about 1 in 20 times).
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (meta-lesson). Implication: any claim of a perfect mechanical system should be treated as unfalsifiable marketing, not evidence.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A.
findings.quote: A perfect system or approach does not exist. Never has, never will.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 16, 'Closing Comments' (pp. 245-248)
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's evidence-bound constitution (no profitability claims; registry experiments rather than promoted systems) and warns against over-adaptation/guru narratives. The 'adaptation when rules don't fit conditions' prescription maps to a possible REGIME_FILTER concept, which per rule 14 enters V8 only through a registry experiment beating the simpler baseline.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

book_title: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading (Larry Williams, 1999) — Part 1 of 2

findings.strategy_name: Volatility breakout (range-expansion entry at period open)
findings.mechanism: An explosive expansion of range sets a trend that persists until an equal/opposite expansion; entering at the next period open + X% of the reference range captures the continuation
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable: when a bar's range exceeds a reference (prior bar's range, or N-bar average range, or a swing-based measure) by a threshold, buy the next bar at open + X% of the reference range (short: open - X%). Williams' tests show adding the expansion to the NEXT bar's OPEN (not close or high) works best ($389 avg/trade across commodities); simple daily-range breakouts on bonds made $73,468 with 80% accuracy on 651 trades; restricting to best trade-days (buy Tue/Thu, sell Wed/Thu) cut trades in half and lifted avg/trade to $173 with 84% accuracy. Buy signals only after down days, sells after up days.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Entry bar fails to extend (no follow-through beyond the entry level); or for longs, price falls back much below the entry-period open — a large-range up day seldom trades far below its open
findings.risk_geometry: entry NEXT_BAR_OPEN + X% of reference range (X≈40-200% by day of week in tests; 50-100% common); stop = 50% of reference range subtracted from entry, or flat dollar stop ($1,500-2,500); target = bailout (first profitable opening) or period close; expiry = close of entry period or next 1-3 bars
findings.quote: I have never seen a more consistently profitable mechanical entry technique than volatility breakouts.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, 'Volatility Breakouts' (pp. 57-73); GSV refinement in Chapter 8 (pp. 123-129)
findings.notes: Chapter 8's Greatest Swing Value is a measurement variant of the same family: use 180% of the 4-day average 'failure swing' (open-to-low on up-close days, open-to-high on down-close days) added to the next open, with a 225% stop. Also consistent with 'don't catch falling daggers / buy when the explosion has begun' (Ch. 2, 12). Could be formalized as an expert consuming volatility+location features.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Range-cycle compression/expansion regime (small ranges beget large ranges) with open-to-close direction law
findings.mechanism: Range sizes oscillate in clusters: compression of ranges precedes expansion; on large-range days, close position vs open carries directional information (up days open near low and close near high)
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable timing/regime rule: after a series of small-range bars (relative to a trailing average) a large-range bar becomes likely — wait for ranges to 'dry up' before entering volatility-breakout trades, and expect contraction after large-range days. Directional law (T-Bond study 1970-98): ~87% of closes are above the open when the open-to-low dip is <20% of the day's range; a positive open-to-close of $500+ occurs 42% of the time and $1,000+ 15% of the time if the dip is <10%; there is near-zero chance of a large up close after a 70-80% dip below the open.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Expansion fails to arrive within the expected window (compression persists); or a would-be large-range day dips far below the open (dip >70-80% of range), making a positive open-to-close near-impossible
findings.risk_geometry: Not a standalone entry — a timing/direction filter over other setups; when applied directly: enter at open, exit at close, stop = reference range fraction
findings.quote: Small ranges beget large ranges. Large ranges beget small ranges.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'The Natural Cycle of Range Change' and 'The Importance of the Open to Low or High of the Day' (pp. 27-36)
findings.notes: Directly usable as a volatility feature (range percentile vs trailing window) plus a regime gate for the volatility_breakout family. Open-to-close statistics map onto per-bar response features in the 1h timeframe.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Hold-to-close / time-as-profit exit methodology
findings.mechanism: Profit grows with holding time; exits before the period close truncate the large-range days that pay for small-range losses; fixed intraday profit targets systematically underperform holding to the close
findings.setup_summary: Comparative, falsifiable: S&P system buying the Monday open after a Friday down close — with a $500 fixed target it lost $8,150; with a $1,000 target it made $13,737; with exit-at-close it made $39,075 ($100/trade avg, smaller drawdown); holding 6 days made $71,600. Rule: never take a winner off before the close of the trading period; use the 'bailout' (exit on the first profitable opening) for fast markets and delay it 1-2 days for slower ones; always keep a dollar stop; exit-and-reverse on an opposite signal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a (methodology; applies to exit selection given any entry)
findings.risk_geometry: exit = period close, or first profitable opening (bailout), or N bars after entry; dollar stop always in force beneath any exit rule
findings.quote: The most profitable short-term trading strategy I know and use is to enter the trade, place my protective stop, then shut my eyes... and wait to get out on the close.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'The Real Secret to Short-Term Trading' (pp. 45-55); exit rules in Chapter 11 (p. 157)
findings.notes: Supports V8's fill-at-close simulator and the principle that expiry_bars / close exits should not be replaced by tight profit targets. In 24/7 perps the 'close' maps to the trading-period boundary.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Oops! gap-overreaction reversal (open beyond prior extreme, reclaimed)
findings.mechanism: An open far beyond the prior period's range is an emotional overreaction (stops run, panic flow); if price then reclaims the prior period's extreme, the overreaction reverses sharply with trapped flow as fuel
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable: LONG — a bar opens BELOW the prior bar's low (a rare occurrence; price almost always opens within the prior range); enter long when price rallies back to the prior bar's low. SHORT — a bar opens ABOVE the prior bar's high; enter short when price falls back to the prior bar's high. Exit next day's open (trade usually lasts ~1.5 days), flat dollar stop. Williams reports S&P 82%+ accuracy (best days except Wed/Thu, $438/trade avg, $42,687) and bonds 86% accuracy ($201/trade); selling into a 9-day overbought filter on Wednesdays netted 79-89% accuracy.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No reclaim of the prior extreme within 1-2 bars, or the gap extreme is exceeded again (gap continuation instead of reversal)
findings.risk_geometry: entry: stop/limit at the prior extreme after the gap open; stop: flat dollar (S&P $2,000 / bonds $1,800); target: next period open (bailout); expiry: 1-2 bars
findings.quote: The precise overreaction we are looking for to give us a buy signal is an opening that is below the previous day's low... The entry comes when, following the lower open, price then rallies back to the previous day's low.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, 'Oops! This Is Not a Mistake' (pp. 113-120)
findings.notes: True daily-boundary gaps do not exist in 24/7 perps, but the pattern maps to period-boundary overextension wicks beyond prior extremes on any timeframe, and to liquidation-cascade stop runs. Conceptual cousin of v8's liquidity_sweep_reclaim family (sweep of a prior extreme + reclaim), but the trigger is an open-gap, not a close-position sweep. Registry candidate under the complexity budget.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Smash-day / specialists'-trap failed breakout of congestion, immediately reversed
findings.mechanism: Public entries on an emotional breakout (naked close beyond a trading range); immediate reversal the next day means the breakout failed and the trapped flow becomes fuel for the opposite move
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable. Smash-day: a bar closes below the prior bar's low, often taking out the prior 3-8 bars' lows (a 'naked close'); if the very next bar trades back above that smash bar's high, the downside breakout failed — buy. Mirror for short. Specialists' trap: in an uptrend, 5-10 bars of sideways congestion break out with a naked close above the whole range; if the breakout bar's true low is broken within the next 1-3 days, the upside breakout was false — short (and vice versa for a buy trap). With day-of-week filtering (any day but Thursday) Williams reports 82-90% accuracy (bonds $420/trade avg; S&P outside-day-down-close pattern 85% on 109 occurrences).
findings.trigger_invalidation: The smash/breakout bar's extreme is not retaken within 1-3 bars — the breakout is real and the thesis is dead
findings.risk_geometry: entry: stop-order at the smash/breakout bar's opposite extreme on next-bar confirmation; stop: flat dollar ($1,500-2,000) or the breakout bar's extreme; target: first profitable opening (bailout); expiry: 1-3 bars
findings.quote: The breakout is a magnet for the public to take action and they do. What kills them is the immediate reversal the very next day.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, 'My Smash Day Patterns' and 'Specialists' Trap' (pp. 101-113)
findings.notes: Refines the existing failed_breakout expert: adds the congestion-window (5-10 bar box) variant, the hidden smash day (close in lower 25% of an up-day's range), and the 1-3 bar immediate-reversal confirmation. Stop-run dynamics in crypto range highs/lows make this a strong REFINE target.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Trade-day-of-week (TDW) and trading-day-of-month (TDM) calendar biases
findings.mechanism: Specific weekdays and trading days of the month carry persistent directional/volatility biases (S&P up Mondays, bonds up Tuesdays, grains up Wednesdays, first-of-month and end-of-month rallies), contradicting a memoryless random walk
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable statistical claims over 17-30 years of data: S&P 500 closes above the Monday open 57% of the time (avg +$109/trade); bonds are best on Tuesdays; grains rally most on Wednesdays (1968-98); both stocks and bonds rally around the first of the month (S&P first-trade-day-of-month buy: 85% accuracy on 129 trades, $73,437); bonds rally into month-end (TDM 18/22 buy, up to 89% accuracy with a gold-downtrend filter) and dip mid-month (TDM 12 sell, 76% accuracy). TDM counts trading days, not calendar days. Williams uses these as stacked filters over other setups, never standalone.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Bias window passes without the expected move; or the stacked filter (e.g., bond trend, gold trend) fails
findings.risk_geometry: entry: open of the bias day (+ X% of prior range as an expansion filter); stop: flat dollar ($1,100-2,500, often only after entry day); target: close, first profitable opening, or exit 3 days after entry
findings.quote: stocks have a proven proclivity to rally on Mondays, Bonds on Tuesdays and virtually all the grains on Wednesday.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, 'The Market Is Not a Coin Flip' (pp. 82-88); Chapter 10, 'Special Short-Term Situations' (pp. 147-156)
findings.notes: Calendar features (weekday, trading-day-of-month, month-end proximity) are deterministic from event timestamps, so they do not violate the no-wall-clock rule. In 24/7 perps the daily open/close framing weakens, but day-of-week volume/vol regimes and CME futures/option expiry (end-of-month/quarter) effects persist.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Ringed/swing-point market structure (nested short/intermediate/long-term highs and lows)
findings.mechanism: A bar with lower highs on both sides is a short-term high (higher lows both sides = short-term low); nesting these produces intermediate and long-term structure; swing points are the only valid support/resistance and their violation signals trend change
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable mechanical definition (ignore inside days): short-term high = bar with lower highs on both sides; short-term low = bar with higher lows on both sides; intermediate = short-term point with higher/lower short-term points on both sides; long-term nested one more level. A short-term low is confirmed intra-period when price trades above the high of a bar with a lower low than the prior bar. Violation of a swing point is the trend-change trigger and stop reference; the (A)-type violation (break of the low preceding a failed new-high rally) is the stronger signal. Inside days (~7.6% of sessions) signal congestion — skip them; outside days (~7%) require intraday open-to-close study.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Acceptance back through a retaken swing level without follow-through
findings.risk_geometry: entry: on break of a swing level (stop order) or pullback to a swing level with trend confirmation; stop: beyond the swing point; target: next swing level; expiry: bar-based
findings.quote: These points are the only valid support and resistance levels I have ever found.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 1, 'Understanding Market Structure' (pp. 15-22); trend-change use in Chapter 9, 'Swing Points as Trend Change Indication' (pp. 133-135)
findings.notes: This is the fractal/swing definition that already conceptually underpins v8's windowed prior-extreme refs. Candidate location feature: labeled swing highs/lows at multiple nesting depths, with inside/outside-day flags.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Three-bar moving-average high/low pullback entry (swing-based variant of trend_pullback)
findings.mechanism: In a swing-point-confirmed trend, buying the pullback to short-term support (3-bar MA of lows) and taking profits at the 3-bar MA of highs harvests mean-reversion-within-trend
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable intraday system (5-60 min bars): compute a 3-bar moving average of the highs and a 3-bar moving average of the lows. Only after the swing-point trend-flip confirms an uptrend, buy at the 3-bar MA-of-lows and take profits at the 3-bar MA-of-highs, awaiting pullbacks back to the low line; in a confirmed downtrend, short the 3-bar MA-of-highs and cover at the MA-of-lows. Pass on signals when the 3-bar low line would itself trigger a trend reversal. Williams reports 30+ consecutive winning trades with this approach.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Swing-point trend flip in the opposite direction, or the 3-bar low line is violated by a trend reversal
findings.risk_geometry: entry: limit at the 3-bar MA of lows (long) / 3-bar MA of highs (short); target: 3-bar MA of highs / lows (fixed structure, not R-multiple); stop: below the swing low / on trend flip; expiry: intraday bars
findings.quote: The strategy is to buy at the price of the 3-bar moving average of the lows—if the trend is positive, according to the swing point trend identification technique—and take profits at the 3-bar moving average of the highs.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, 'The Three-Bar High/Low System' (pp. 136-137)
findings.notes: A swing-based (rather than EMA-based) variant of the existing trend_pullback expert: pullback-to-short-term-structure entry, structural target, trend-gated. Candidate variant under the trend_pullback family multiplicity.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Fade-the-public sentiment filter
findings.mechanism: Short-term public positioning is systematically wrong; when the crowd is excessively long or short, the informed side is the opposite, so extreme public stance disqualifies aligned entries
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable filter, not a standalone signal: use post-close short-term-trader surveys (Jake Bernstein) and newsletter-writer sentiment (Market Vane, longer-horizon) as a disqualifier — never enter a trade with an extreme public stance on the same side; align only against it. Williams: 'If the public is excessive in their selling, I don't want to be a seller along with them.' For crypto perps the survey data does not exist; the analogues are funding-rate extremes and long/short-account ratios, which also act as carry flows.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Sentiment extremes are descriptive; invalidation = crowd being right for a sustained stretch
findings.risk_geometry: Filter only; no standalone entry/stop/target
findings.quote: If the public is excessive in their selling, I don't want to be a seller along with them. I may not always fade the public, but I sure don't want them on my side of the table.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, 'The Theory of Short-Term Trading' (pp. 75-77)
findings.notes: No quantitative test in the book (80%-lose claim is anecdotal). Backlog candidate: funding-rate / long-short-ratio extreme as a participation+flow feature, evaluated against V8's own data before any expert uses it.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Largest-loss-based position sizing: (account balance x risk%) / largest loss
findings.mechanism: Survival is governed by the largest loss, not the average loss; Kelly/optimal-F assume a stable payoff structure (blackjack) and blow up when trade sizes of wins/losses vary as they do in trading; fixed-fraction ramps too fast on winning streaks
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable accounting argument: a 90%-accurate system with $1,000 wins and a $10,000 max loss still ends in the red under contract-scaling once two contracts absorb the large loss. Williams' rule: contracts = (account balance x risk%) / largest system loss, with 10-15% as the sane risk band (drawdown grows faster than profit beyond ~21% risk; >25% is dangerous). Kelly-derived f on his system gave extreme equity gyrations; Ralph Vince's Optimal F and Ryan Jones' fixed-ratio avoid the blow-up but trade off growth. Chapter 14 variant: 'increase one unit following three losing trades' — a drawdown-contrarian scaling rule his system studies supported (>80% win rate after 3 straight losses).
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a (sizing rule, not a market timing claim)
findings.risk_geometry: position sizing = (account x risk%)/largest expected loss; flags largest-loss (max adverse excursion), not average-loss, as the sizing input
findings.quote: Generally speaking, you will want to take 10 percent to 15 percent of your account balance, divide that by the largest loss in the system, or loss you are willing to take, to arrive at the number of contracts you will trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 13, 'Money Management—The Keys to the Kingdom' (pp. 171-183); streak-scaling note in Chapter 14, June 1997 (pp. 198-199)
findings.notes: Directly informs V8's heat cap: size by expected max adverse excursion (MAE) rather than average loss. In leveraged perps this is even more binding — a 1-tick adverse move on a large notional can exceed account equity, echoing Williams' bond 10-tick-open warning ($1,625,000 for 5,000 contracts).
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Will-Spread cross-market regime filter (primary/secondary ratio EMA cross)
findings.mechanism: The spread ratio between a primary market and a causally-linked secondary market (bonds/gold, stocks/bonds) trends ahead of the primary market; an EMA-cross of the ratio across zero, confirmed by next-bar price action, marks the primary's regime
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable alignment tool: compute (primary price / secondary price) x 100; take a 5-period exponential minus a 20-period exponential of the spread (15-min/30-min bars; 3-vs-15 for S&P vs T-bills). Trade long when the oscillator crosses above zero AND the very next bar trades above the crossing bar's high; short on the mirror. Williams uses it to stay aligned with the true trend, not standalone; combined with the first-of-month window it produced 13 month-end trades in 1997 with 10 winners (+99.70 S&P points, $24,925), and it kept traders short through the 1987 crash ($46,000/contract) until the October 20 positive crossing. Underlying claims: higher bond prices are bullish for stocks; gold downtrend is bullish for bonds (gold uptrend impedes bond rallies).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Zero-line crossing without next-bar confirmation = stand aside (unless other gauges align)
findings.risk_geometry: entry: stop-order on next-bar confirmation of the zero-cross; stop: trailing through prior swing/volatility breakout level; target: opposite zero-cross or fixed 2-3 day window
findings.quote: As go Bonds, so go stocks. Always keep in mind Bonds (interest rates) are the dog that wags the tail, which is stocks.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, 'Will-Spread' (pp. 138-146)
findings.notes: Evidence is narrative/case-study (walkthroughs, 1987 crash) rather than systematic backtests. Crypto analogues: BTC vs ETH, BTC vs Nasdaq/equities, BTC vs DXY, and funding/BTC basis as the 'Bond-like' driver. Candidate cross_market feature feeding existing experts' regime gates.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

findings.strategy_name: Out-of-sample instability of time-optimized systems and the simplicity rule
findings.mechanism: Parameters optimized on one sample (moving-average lengths, pure time cycles) fail out-of-sample; chart formations appear in coin flips and temperature data; over-optimization degrades performance — evidence for frozen-OOS evaluation and robustness over perfection
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable OOS evidence: best soybean MA-cross (5/25, 1975-87) made $40,075 but lost $9,100 (drawdown $28,612) forward; the best forward cross failed on earlier data (-$28,725); best British pound cross (5/45) made $135,443 in one decade then gave back a $29,100 losing spell in the next, and the best forward cross (20/40) made only $26,025 on the first period with a $30,000 drawdown. Chartist patterns (head-and-shoulders, flags, etc.) are reproduced by coin-flip and daily-temperature data, so pattern presence is not evidence of causation. Chapter 14: 'The more you tweak and refine them, the more you optimize... the worse the dog performs' — the best newsletters made money on few trades (200-300/year); the busiest letters were consistent losers.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a (methodology / research-protocol lesson)
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: the time or length or cycle of the moving average that worked in one time period does not work in another time period.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'All You Will Ever Need to Know about Cycles' (pp. 23-26); Chapter 14, May 1998 and May 1998 letters (pp. 206-208)
findings.notes: Reinforces V8's frozen-OOS challenger protocol, registry gates, and the ban on in-sample parameter cherry-picking. Also argues AGAINST pure time-based features and chart-pattern mysticism as standalone inputs, and for a few robust filters (volatility, trend, cross-market, calendar) layered rather than a single over-fitted system.
findings.book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

book_title: A Complete Guide to Volume Price Analysis (2013) - Part 2

findings.strategy_name: Volume Climax Reversal (Buying/Selling Climax + Stopping Volume)
findings.mechanism: climax_exhaustion
findings.setup_summary: In a mature trend, a wide-range bar prints on ultra-high volume but fails to follow through (next candles are narrow spread, or a deep-wick hammer forms), showing absorption at the extreme. Confirmation comes as a low-volume test (small hammer on low volume) after the high-volume absorption; enter on next-bar close on the reclaimed side. Sell side analog: narrow-spread up candle on very high volume at a cycle top (buying climax) followed by weak candles.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trend-extreme bar prints on normal (not ultra-high) volume; a low-volume test is followed by a fresh high-volume continuation through the extreme; no stopping volume (rising volume + narrowing spread) appears, so any reversal is not durable.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on bar close on the reclaimed side; stop beyond the climax extreme (wick/high or low); target opposite side of the congestion level; expiry multi-bar.
findings.quote: if this pair were going to sell off sharply, then we would expect this to be a wide spread down candle – it isn't. It's a narrow spread.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10, Fig 10.17 Selling Climax and Fig 10.18 Buying Climax (AUD/USD weekly)
findings.notes: Corroborates V8 backlog family capitulation (capitulation_exhaustion) with explicit stopping-volume/absorption criteria plus a low-volume-test confirmation step. 24/7 crypto perps with high leverage produce frequent climactic volume extremes and liquidation cascades, so the pattern is testable on BTCUSDT 1h. Caveat: aggregated perp volume mixes venues; use a consistent volume source.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Volume-Damped Pullback in Trend (Hold Rule)
findings.mechanism: trend_continuation
findings.setup_summary: While holding a position aligned with the trend, a counter-trend pullback develops on FALLING volume, and no stopping volume (rising volume with narrowing spreads) appears at the pullback extreme. Thesis: the pullback is a pause, not a reversal; hold through it. Applies symmetrically to long (pullbacks down) and short (pullbacks up) positions.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Pullback candles show widening spreads with rising volume (stopping volume / absorption) at the pullback extreme; or a high-volume reversal candle reclaims the position entry zone.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry N/A (position already open); stop beyond the pullback swing extreme; no new target; this rule governs holding, not entry.
findings.quote: If you are short the market and it pulls back against you, but the volume on the upwards moves is falling, then you KNOW that this is simply a temporary pullback and not a change in trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10, Fig 10.16 (AUD/USD 15m spot forex)
findings.notes: Directly refines the still_valid condition of the existing trend_pullback expert: add a volume feature so a pullback on falling volume keeps the thesis valid, while a rising-volume pullback kills it. PIT-safe: all volume bars are available at decision time on the 1h tape.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Volume-Validated Congestion Breakout (Cause and Effect)
findings.mechanism: range_expansion_release
findings.setup_summary: Price builds an extended congestion zone defined by pivot highs/lows; below-average volume confirms the range. Trigger: a bar closes clearly beyond the ceiling (or floor) with above-average, preferably rising volume. Stop below the last pivot low (or above last pivot high) on the entry side. Cause-and-effect: the longer the congestion, the longer the post-breakout trend should last.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Breakout candle closes back inside the range; breakout occurs on low/falling volume (trap); retest of the breached level fails to hold.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after the breakout close; stop beyond the last pivot low/high; target range-height projection or next structure; expiry scaled by congestion duration.
findings.quote: We have a market that has been in congestion, waiting, and gathering itself, when finally the catalyst arrives and the market moves on high volume.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11, Fig 11.10 (GBP/USD 15m)
findings.notes: Corroborates backlog family breakout_retest; adds a mandatory volume-confirmation feature and a time-based cause-effect scaling rule (congestion duration proxies trend duration). 24/7 trading makes congestion zones cleanly defined without session noise; funding can distort volume meaning during range phases.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Low-Volume Trap Move (Fake Breakout)
findings.mechanism: liquidity_trap
findings.setup_summary: After a high-volume reversal or distribution bar, a wide-range move in one direction prints on LOW to average volume (book example: trap-up at the futures session open). The wide spread without volume participation is a trap; enter the opposite direction once the trap move fails and price closes back through its origin. Stop beyond the trap wick.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trap-direction move is followed by expanding volume in the same direction (genuine move); price fails to close back through the trap origin.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry bar close on failure of the trap move; stop beyond the trap extreme wick; target prior congestion on the opposite side.
findings.quote: a classic trap up move by the big operators, a wide spread up candle on low to average volume... Then the selling starts, and down it goes!
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10, Fig 10.20 (ES E-mini 10m session open)
findings.notes: The session-open framing does not transfer to 24/7 perps (no exchange opens), but the core signal - a wide-range move on low volume that reverses - is a general fakeout detector, abundant in crypto at liquidity pools, round numbers, and funding-rate boundaries. Distinct from volume_climax_capitulation: this is the failed push, not absorption at the extreme.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Volume-Collapse Trend Exhaustion (Exit Rule)
findings.mechanism: exhaustion_gravity
findings.setup_summary: In a mature multi-week trend, price keeps printing wide-range bars in the trend direction while volume collapses toward near-zero (market makers pushing price with no participation), OR a volume spike prints with no matching price progress. Either signal means the trend is exhausted; exit the open trend position. The book shows this on AUD/USD weekly (wide bars, near-zero volume) and Coffee 80-tick (ultra-high volume on the 9th bar with insufficient price response).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Volume resumes expanding in the trend direction (genuine re-acceleration); no wide-range low-volume bars appear.
findings.risk_geometry: Exit rule, not an entry; applies to open trend positions; no new stop/target geometry.
findings.quote: What is clear, is that the market makers are moving prices higher with NO volume, and have withdrawn from the market.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10, Fig 10.17 (AUD/USD weekly) and Fig 10.21 (Coffee 80-tick)
findings.notes: Range-without-volume divergence is a falsifiable exit signal and a candidate lifecycle rule for the trend_following family. In crypto, blow-off tops are often funding/liquidation-driven with volume concentrated at the extreme; this rule would exit before the reversal. Complements the volume_climax_capitulation entry side.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Triangle and Pennant Breakout with Volume Validation
findings.mechanism: tension_release
findings.setup_summary: Falling triangle (series of lower highs over a well-defined floor): sustained break below the floor on above-average volume -> short. Rising triangle (rising lows testing a flat ceiling): break above the ceiling confirmed by volume -> long. Pennant (lower highs + higher lows contracting): no directional bias; wait for the breakout and confirm with volume before entering ('coiled spring').
findings.trigger_invalidation: Breakout candle closes back inside the pattern; breakout without volume confirmation.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry bar close beyond the pattern boundary on volume; stop opposite side of the pattern; target pattern-height projection.
findings.quote: each attempt to rally is becoming weaker and weaker in terms of the high of the candles. The floor of the congestion area is very well defined, and any sustained break below here will be signalled with volume.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11, Figs 11.13-11.15 (5m falling triangle, daily rising triangle, monthly pennant)
findings.notes: Pattern geometry adds directional bias on top of the congestion-breakout mechanism (see breakout_retest). Crypto triangles/pennants occur frequently but are noisy; the volume validation gate is what makes the setup falsifiable. Pennant has no inherent direction - breakout-with-volume only.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Triple Top / Triple Bottom Level Reversal
findings.mechanism: level_rejection
findings.setup_summary: Price tests a well-defined resistance level three times, failing each time (triple top), or tests support three times and bounces (triple bottom). Enter on the third-touch failure confirmed by VPA (reversal candle on above-average volume); alternatively, a break-and-hold beyond the level builds a strong platform of support/resistance for a continuation trade.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Price breaks cleanly through the level on strong volume (reversal of the reversal thesis); the third touch succeeds in pushing through on volume.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry bar close on third-touch failure; stop beyond the tested level; target opposite congestion or measured move.
findings.quote: the pair has tested the 1.0600 level on three separate occasions... failing on each occasion.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11, Fig 11.16 (AUD/USD daily triple top) and Fig 11.17 (EUR/CHF hourly triple bottom)
findings.notes: Multi-touch levels are common in crypto because of clustered limit orders and liquidation walls, but 24/7 price discovery makes levels less sticky than in gapped markets. Volume confirmation at the touch is the falsifiable gate. Candidate variant of the supply_demand_zone family.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Multi-Timeframe Trend Alignment Filter
findings.mechanism: timeframe_alignment
findings.setup_summary: Maintain three horizons (slow/benchmark, trading/middle, fast). Take entry signals on the trading frame only when aligned with the dominant trend of the slow frame; counter-trend entries on the fast frame are permitted only as short-duration pullback/reversal trades carrying higher risk. Trend changes ripple fast frame -> trading frame -> slow frame, so the slow frame lags the fast one.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Slow-frame dominant trend flips to the opposite direction.
findings.risk_geometry: Filter rule; does not define entries or stops directly. Trades with the dominant trend are lower risk; against it, higher risk and shorter expected holding time.
findings.quote: If the dominant trend is bullish on the 30 minute chart, and we decide to take a position on our 15 minute chart which is bullish, then the risk on the trade is lower, since we are trading with the dominant trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11, Fig 11.12 (GBP/USD 5/15/30m three time frames)
findings.notes: PIT-safe in V8: aggregate 1h bars into 4h/1d trend features from the same tape with the event clock preserved. This is a regime filter over existing experts, which under V8 rules enters only as a registry experiment beating the simpler baseline on frozen OOS, not as a new Active expert.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Delta / Cumulative Delta Volume (Bid-Ask Order Flow)
findings.mechanism: order_flow_dominance
findings.setup_summary: Per bar, delta = (volume traded at the ask) - (volume traded at the bid); cumulative delta sums per-bar deltas over a window and is displayed as a series to show net buying/selling pressure. Divergence between price and cumulative delta (price makes a new high while cumulative delta fails to) flags weakening buying. Proposed as a feature input for the flow feature group rather than a standalone strategy.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (feature input, not an entry rule).
findings.risk_geometry: Feature input only; no entry/stop/target geometry.
findings.quote: delta volume refers to the difference in volumes between those contracts that trade at the 'ask' and those that trade at the 'bid'... the net difference between the two then displayed as 'delta'.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 12, 'Delta Volume' and 'Cumulative Delta Volume'
findings.notes: The author states she has not used delta/cumulative delta and 'cannot comment on their validity', hence NARRATIVE evidence. Crypto perp venues publish taker buy/sell volume, so the raw data exists, but V8's 1h OHLCV tape would need an additional field (e.g., taker_base_volume) to build this feature. No expert proposed until the feature exists and is screened.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Volume Baseline Calibration (High/Low/Average per Instrument)
findings.mechanism: volume_normalization
findings.setup_summary: Before judging any volume bar as high, low, or average, calibrate the volume distribution for the instrument and session; an extreme volume bar early in a window (e.g., a news spike) distorts the relative reading of all subsequent bars in that session. Compare each bar against a windowed baseline that is robust to such distortion events.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (methodology rule).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - informs feature construction, not trade geometry.
findings.quote: we must try to have an idea of what is considered to be high, low and average volume. So that when these extremes of volume do appear, they do not distort our view of what follows in the remainder of the trading session.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10, Fig 10.21 (Coffee 80-tick) - the 'always remember' caveat
findings.notes: Directly informs how V8 should compute volume features: prefer percentile or robust-window baselines over naive windowed means so extreme bars (liquidation cascades, listing events) do not poison subsequent readings. Relevant to the volume/participation feature groups and any simulator volume model.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: High-Volume Failed Rally (Upthrust) -> Continuation Short
findings.mechanism: liquidity_vacuum_reentry
findings.setup_summary: In a downtrend (after distribution or a selling climax), rally attempts print narrow-spread up candles on very high volume that fail and roll over (upthrust). This confirms further weakness; short on a close back below the rally start, stop above the failed rally high.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rally candles expand in spread with volume and reclaim prior resistance (genuine reversal); the failed rally closes above its starting level and holds.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry bar close below the rally start; stop above the rally extreme wick; target continuation toward prior lows.
findings.quote: the attempt to rally at the right hand edge of the chart. Here we see narrow spread up candles on very high volume, and falling, another very strong signal of further weakness to come.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10, Fig 10.17 (AUD/USD weekly) and Fig 10.21 (Coffee 80-tick)
findings.notes: Corroborates the existing failed_breakout expert (liquidity_vacuum_reentry): the volume of the failed attempt is the key refinement - high volume on a rally that fails identifies the vacuum left by trapped longs, then the reentry short. Common in crypto where leveraged longs get trapped at resistance on high volume.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Equivolume / Candle-Volume Charts - Time as a Cause Dimension
findings.mechanism: time_as_cause_dimension
findings.setup_summary: Equivolume charts replace the time axis with volume (box width = volume, box height = high-low); candle-volume charts overlay equivolume boxes on OHLC candles. The author's own critique: removing time removes Wyckoff's cause-and-effect, the core of trend-power assessment - 'time is the third element of the volume and price relationship' - so the approach becomes two-dimensional.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (presentation technique, no entry logic).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A.
findings.quote: as Wykcoff himself stated, it is the cause and effect which holds the key to the development of the trend. In other words, time is the third element of the volume and price relationship. Remove time, and the approach becomes two dimensional.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 12, 'Equivolume Charts' and 'Candle Volume Charts'
findings.notes: Presentation-layer techniques with no signal logic to port to V8. The lesson is architectural and aligns with V8's determinism rules: keep time (event/available/ingested clocks) as a first-class dimension and never collapse it; a volume-scaled-bar display encodes nothing beyond what OHLCV + volume already carry. DEFER_GATED unless a display feature is ever requested.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

book_title: Trend Trading for a Living: Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living (2008), Part 1 of 2

findings.strategy_name: The Pullback — stochastic-oversold + reversal-candle confirmed pullback in uptrend
findings.mechanism: A dip in an established uptrend is temporary weakness (profit-taking or news noise); traders who missed the prior move re-enter on the dip, reasserting the dominant trend.
findings.setup_summary: Uptrending stock (higher lows over >=3 months; 20MA>50MA both rising) pulls back to touch an upsloping 20 MA (strong trend) or 50 MA (weak trend); stochastics (5,3) drops to/below the 20 oversold line; the current daily candle is a bullish reversal (hammer, engulfing, piercing, or doji). All three conditions register a buy signal on the same day; confluence with an upsloping trendline under the lows improves odds. Daily chart, hold 3-30 days.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the pullback closes below the 50 MA, violates the uptrend trendline, shows bearish indicator divergence, or prints a double top; a red/black candle on the day is a wait-and-see condition (recheck next day).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: stop order $0.02-0.05 above prior day's intraday high (gaps -> limit order; if never hit, scratch); stop: below swing support / 2xATR, max -8% (typ 5-6%); target: 1.5-2.0x stop or 3xATR, or trailing on closing basis; expiry: 3-30 days.
findings.quote: Normally after a period of minor weakness—as measured here by the stochastics indicator reaching an oversold level—the dominant uptrend will reassert itself as traders who missed out on the prior move use the dip to get on board.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9 'The Pullback' (pp. 158-163)
findings.notes: Refines existing V8 trend_pullback (ema_fast>ema_slow, close<ema_slow): adds stochastics(5,3)<=20 oversold confirmation + bullish reversal candle before entry, and pullback depth variant by regime strength (20MA in strong / 50MA in weak). These are parameter/filter variants within the family, not a new family. Full screening rules given (20MA>50MA, close today < close 5 days ago x 1.15, etc.). BTTT-MAX (hourly MA-crossover, fully invested, pp. 21-23) is the cautionary sibling: >500% in 2000 volatility, profits dried when the regime changed — motivates the regime_filter finding.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: The Relief Rally — bearish mirror of the pullback (short rally into MA resistance)
findings.mechanism: A rally in a downtrend is a short-term reevaluation (profit-taking, short squeeze, or news); when it fails at moving-average resistance the dominant downtrend resumes.
findings.setup_summary: Downtrending stock (lower highs over >=3 months; 20MA<50MA both falling) rallies up into a downsloping 20 MA (strong downtrend) or 50 MA (weak downtrend); stochastics (5) rises to/above the 80 overbought line; a bearish reversal candle (doji, engulfing, gravestone, hanging man, evening star) prints. Three factors register a sell-short signal; confluence with a downsloping trendline over the highs improves odds. Best in bearish strongly/weakly trending regimes.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the rally closes above the 50 MA, violates the downtrend trendline, shows bullish indicator divergence, or prints a double bottom / inverted head-and-shoulders; a green candle on the day is wait-and-see.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: stop order $0.02-0.05 below prior day's intraday low; stop: above swing resistance / 2xATR, max -8%; target: 1.5-2.0x stop or 3xATR, trailing stop; QLGC example: 4 signals in 4 months, +50-60% combined while buy-and-holder sat through -55% drawdown.
findings.quote: Here we are looking for a stock that is strongly or weakly downtrending but has rallied up off its lows to reach a major moving average, which should act as resistance.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'The Relief Rally' (pp. 194-197)
findings.notes: Bearish sibling of trend_pullback under the same trend_continuation mechanism family but a distinct behavior family (rally_into_resistance), so a separate Expert file. Carr explicitly calls it 'the inverse of the pullback setup.' V8's trend_pullback is LONG-only; this supplies the SHORT continuation family. Screen: bearish engulfing + 20MA<50MA + close today > close 5 days ago x 1.15.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: The Coiled Spring — bull flag/pennant tightening-range breakout
findings.mechanism: Strong stocks consolidate sideways after a runup instead of selling off; the tightening range (coil) stores energy that releases in a burst of upward momentum when it springs open.
findings.setup_summary: Weakly-to-strongly uptrending stock (20MA>50MA) puts in a new high that is at least a 3-month high within the past 20 trading days, then consolidates in a tightening range lasting 7-20 trading days (coil): sideways-to-slightly-down, trading range getting smaller, no part of the coil extending to/below the 50 MA (tails may poke out if candle bodies stay inside). Pure pattern play — no oscillators needed, only 20/50 MAs and trendlines. Buy signal: close breaks the trendline over the tops of the coil; close below the lower trendline negates.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalidated by a close below the lower coil trendline; coils longer than 20 days signal indecision and are avoided; range must be tightening (lows getting higher and/or highs lower); candle bodies must stay in the coil.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on close above upper coil trendline (or next bar); stop: below lower coil trendline / swing low; target: trailing preferred; examples ALVR +16% in <2 wks, FORD +50% in ~1 month; the longer the coil (within 7-20 days), the higher the spring.
findings.quote: As it does so, price tends to trend inside an ever tighter range—the spring coils up tighter and tighter—until shares are ready to climb again.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9 'The Coiled Spring' (pp. 164-169)
findings.notes: Reuses starter slug tight_consolidation. Continuation-pattern breakout distinct from failed_breakout and from the new-high breakout; sits naturally as a variant within the V8 breakout_retest backlog family (location,volatility,history). ADX screen variant: ADX(14) today < ADX(14) 20 days ago x 0.41 (declining trend strength = coiling).
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Blue Sky Breakout — new-high breakout with OBV confirmation and overextension cap
findings.mechanism: Trends once begun tend to keep trending; new closing highs confirmed by OBV accumulation extend ('buy high, sell higher').
findings.setup_summary: Closing price (not intraday) registers a new significant high — no higher closing high in at least the past 3 months — following a pivot high set within the past 20 trading days (pivot = new high then >=5 bar, <=20 bar consolidation); new-high close / 52-week low <= 3.0 (not overextended); OBV at its highest reading in >=3 months; breakout candle is green/white. All five parameters on the same day = buy signal. Best in bullish strongly trending markets.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Reject if price makes a new high but indicators (OBV/RSI/MACD) do not make new highs (bearish divergence); skip if the stock is overextended (>3x 52-week low); breakout must be on closing basis, not intraday wick.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: next open or stop above prior-day high; stop: below consolidation support / 2xATR, max -8%; target: trailing stop ('let winners run'); examples CREE +22% in 12 days (newsletter pick), +50% on longer hold; AAPL repeated stair-step breakouts.
findings.quote: In a strongly uptrending market, your best bet is to 'buy high and sell higher'. Trends once begun tend to keep trending: this is the essence of trend trading.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9 'The Blue Sky Breakout' (pp. 176-180)
findings.notes: Reuses starter slug donchian_breakout (new-high breakout family); the book adds OBV-3-month-high volume confirmation and an overextension cap (price/52wk-low <= 3.0) as refinement filters, plus the green-candle requirement. Mirror setup 'Blue Sea Breakdown' (Ch. 10, pp. 208-212) is the SHORT equivalent: new closing low after pivot low within 20 days, 52wk-high/new-low <= 2.0, OBV 3-month low, red candle; 'with no immediate support under price, these trades tend to move down quickly and sharply.'
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Bullish Base Breakout — contrarian accumulation-base breakout after downtrend
findings.mechanism: A sideways base at the bottom of a downtrend, confirmed by rising momentum (MACD higher lows) and accumulation (OBV trendline break), flips supply into demand and triggers a rally.
findings.setup_summary: Downtrending stock (lower highs; 20MA below falling 50MA) has traded sideways for >=30 trading days in a consolidation base (flat/falling rectangle or symmetrical/ascending/descending triangle; rising wedge explicitly invalid) at the bottom of the downtrend; MACD prints a series of higher lows within the base; OBV rises above a trendline over its tops. Buy signal = first green candle after the OBV trendline break (or on the OBV-break day if that candle is green). Contrarian: works in bullish-weak, bearish-strong/weak, and range-bound markets; often seen in lower-priced stocks.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A rising wedge base is invalid (usually precedes continuation of the downtrend); no buy without OBV accumulation confirmation — price breaking out of the base without the OBV signal is not a valid entry.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: day of/after OBV trendline break on a green candle; stop: below base low / 2xATR; target: quick +10% burst within days or trailing for +20-30% in 6-7 weeks; examples AKS +20% in 7 days, KLAC +19% (trailing), JNPR +30% in 6 weeks.
findings.quote: To render the setup valid, we need the indicators to tell us two things about price behavior within the base: it has to be gaining in momentum, and there must be evidence that shares are under accumulation.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9 'The Bullish Base Breakout' (pp. 181-189)
findings.notes: Reuses starter slug breakout_retest (V8 backlog family location,volatility,history) but adds participation features (OBV trendline break + MACD higher lows) not currently in the backlog spec — a candidate FEATURE_INPUT for the participation group. Classic antecedent is the Darvas box (Introduction, pp. 3-7): buy break of box top, raise box on new range, exit on break of box bottom. 'OBV often leads price': price frequently follows an OBV breakout.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Bullish/Bearish Indicator Divergence at deep pullback or sharp rally
findings.mechanism: Price making new extremes without oscillator confirmation shows waning momentum; divergence foreshadows a reversal toward the direction of the indicators, which align with the larger trend.
findings.setup_summary: Bullish: stock in a long-range uptrend (50 MA above a RISING 200 MA) trades below the 50 MA and puts in >=2 clear price lows >=5 trading days apart; the last price low pairs with a HIGHER low in >=2 of {MACD, MACD histogram, stochastics, RSI, OBV, CCI}; a bullish reversal candle triggers the buy. Bearish mirror: long-range downtrend (50 MA below a FALLING 200 MA), price above the 50 MA, >=2 higher highs, last high pairs with a LOWER high in >=2 indicators, bearish candle triggers the short. Confluence with 200 MA / trendline / prior support-resistance improves odds. Works in range-bound and weak-trend markets.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Too many lower lows (bullish) eventually negate the long-range uptrend and nullify the setup (likewise too many higher highs bearish); the 50MA/200MA relationship is the regime gate — 50 MA crossing under the 200 MA negates the long-range uptrend even with a rising 200 MA.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: day of bullish/bearish reversal candle, or next day via stop above/below prior day's extreme; stop: below last low / support or 2xATR, max -8%; target: 1.5-2.0x stop or trailing; examples FWLT +25% in 20 days; BRCM +40% over two trades vs +24% buy-and-hold.
findings.quote: Whenever price sets a higher high or lower low without the indicators following suit, we have a setup that often foreshadows large market moves.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9 'The Bullish Divergence' (pp. 170-175) + Ch. 10 'The Bearish Divergence' (pp. 198-203)
findings.notes: Reuses starter slug rsi_divergence (multi-indicator momentum divergence family). Carr calls it 'a real workhorse... we can use it in all sorts of markets, even bearish ones.' Falsifiable spec: 50MA vs 200MA slope defines the long-range regime; >=2 of six oscillators diverging, >=5 bars between lows; strong divergence (much lower price low + much higher indicator low) and >2 diverging indicators favored. Implementable from PIT oscillator history (feature group: history). This is a new V8 behavior family; would enter the registry and compete for one of the 3 active Expert slots.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: The Gap Down — contrarian short after an unfilled gap down in a steady uptrend
findings.mechanism: An unfilled gap down in an uptrend is a trend killer: panic and profit-locking inverts the dynamic; dip-buyers get trapped, and a break below the gap-day low releases them into a sharp drop.
findings.setup_summary: Stock in a steady uptrend (price above a rising 50 MA for at least the past 40 trading days; 50 MA rising without major dips) prints an UNFILLED gap-down candle: at the close, the day's intraday high remains below the prior day's intraday low. Sell-short signal triggers anytime after the gap-down day when price trades below the intraday low of the gap-down candle. Best in bullish-strong, bullish-weak, and range-bound markets; the gap must follow a significant (>=3-month) new high.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Setup negated if price trades up into the gap prior to triggering the sell signal; avoid 'safe-haven' stocks making new highs in a bear market; favor above-average volume on the gap day and prior resistance / bearish divergence at the preceding high.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: stop order below the gap-day intraday low (or next bar); stop: above the gap / swing high; target: trailing stop; examples EBAY (double gap down then breakdown), SWIR (long gap candle, drop resumed after 3 days); warning — never buy a dip to support after an unfilled gap down, 'you are likely to get caught in a bull trap.'
findings.quote: Never underestimate the power of a gap down. It is truly a trend killer.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'The Gap Down' (pp. 203-207)
findings.notes: The unfilled-gap observable is equity-specific (overnight close-to-open discontinuity); 24/7 perp crypto has no exchange gaps, though sudden wick/candle failures (post-funding dumps, flash-crash wicks) are analogs. Gate on whether a 'gap' can be defined on 1h BTCUSDT bars and on V8's simulator gap semantics (the sim models equity-style gaps). The bull-trap warning ('never buy a dip to support after an unfilled gap down') is a transferable RISK filter for the trend_pullback family: do not take pullback longs when the pullback began with a gap-down / high-velocity downside candle.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Rising Wedge Breakdown — distribution-wedge short with OBV/MACD confirmation
findings.mechanism: Narrowing oscillations in an uptrend with slowing momentum (MACD lower highs) and distribution (OBV trendline break) exhaust the rally; the OBV break leads the price breakdown.
findings.setup_summary: Uptrending stock (strong or weak) oscillates in a narrowing wedge: support and resistance trendlines under the lows / over the highs each need >=3 price-point touches (not pivots, just bar touches); MACD makes a series of lower highs inside the wedge; OBV falls below a trendline under its lows. Sell-short signal = first red/black candle after the OBV trendline break (may enter before price itself breaks the wedge). Contrarian; works in bullish-weak/strong and range-bound markets.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No signal without OBV distribution confirmation; fewer than 3 touches per wedge trendline invalid; ascending-triangle (flat-top) wedges are less favored than rising wedges; >2 of RSI/CCI/OBV falling during the wedge favored, and more red than green candles.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: close of the OBV-trigger day; stop: above wedge top / 2xATR; target: trailing stop; NVDA +30% in ~4 weeks (OBV trigger preceded the price breakdown); CSCO +17% over 2 months, entry 20.75 before price closed below the wedge.
findings.quote: MACD must be making a series of lower highs while price is within the wedge... OBV must fall below a trendline placed under the lows of the indicator.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'The Rising Wedge Breakdown' (pp. 213-219)
findings.notes: Short mirror of the bullish base breakout with distribution (not accumulation) confirmation. Consistency note across the book: the rising wedge is explicitly REJECTED as a valid base in the bullish setup (precedes downtrend continuation) but IS the valid pattern here — i.e., rising wedge = bearish in both chapters. The OBV-break-leads-price mechanic ('price often follows an OBV breakout' / 'you often will be in at the very start of a significant trend-down sell-off') is a participation-feature timing signal.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Market Regime -> Setup-Class Selection (five market types from 20/50 MA slope)
findings.mechanism: Market state (strong/weak trend or range, plus how long it has persisted) determines which setup class carries the edge: breakouts in strong trends, continuation/pullback plays in weak trends, reversals in ranges.
findings.setup_summary: Classify the market into five states from the 20/50 MA slope, separation, and pullback depth: bullish-strong (20MA>50MA both rising, distance large/growing, pullbacks only to 20MA), bullish-weak (50MA rising, 20MA fluctuating, pullbacks reach the 50MA), bearish-strong (mirror: 20MA<50MA both falling, rallies only to 20MA), bearish-weak (mirror: rallies reach the 50MA), range-bound (20MA spends about as much time above as below a mostly-flat 50MA, price passes through both). Then trade the matching class: breakout/breakdown plays in strong trends, pullback/continuation in weak trends, reversal plays in ranges. The longer a market persists in its current state, the shorter the intended holding period and targets. General-market gauge: slope of the 50-day MA of the S&P 500.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Regime re-classification on MA slope/cross events (e.g., 20MA crossing 50MA, 50MA rolling over); a 'snakey' fluctuating 20MA with flat 50MA is the range-bound tell; a tight range is next to impossible to profit from except by day traders — in that state move to instruments/stocks showing sizeable moves.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A — regime gate that determines which expert families are admissible per bar (a pre-filter, not an entry).
findings.quote: In weak uptrends and downtrends, you should focus on continuation plays; in strong uptrends and downtrends, you should focus on breakout plays; and in range-bound markets, you should look for reversal setups.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 4 habit 6 (pp. 86-87) + Ch. 7 'Determining General Market Direction' (pp. 113-131)
findings.notes: Directly implementable on 1h BTCUSDT bars from MA slopes — no wall-clock dependency, preserves determinism. This is the missing gating layer in V8: which Expert families are admissible depends on regime state (not a scorer, not a ranker — a deterministic admission filter). Motivation: BTTT-MAX (Introduction, pp. 21-23), a fully-invested hourly MA-crossover system, made >500% in 2000's extreme volatility but profits dried up when conditions changed — pure momentum without a regime gate is regime-dependent. Supporting stat: 'Up to 80 percent of the time, stocks move sideways; they run in trends only about 20 percent of the time' (Ch. 5, p. 100) — range-state must be handled explicitly. Carr's caveat: chart-specific selection trumps market direction ('the vital key is finding the best-looking chart').
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Volatility-scaled stop/target framework (2xATR stop, 3xATR target, -8% cap, RR 1.25-2.0)
findings.mechanism: Correlating per-trade loss tolerance with the instrument's volatility (ATR) bounds risk while allowing reward of 1.5-3x risk; a fixed exact stop price removes discretionary exits.
findings.setup_summary: Every trade requires an exact stop price (not a mental 'area'). Four stop methods: percentage (max -8%, typically -5 to -6%; average loss in the Swing Trade Newsletter ~4.76%), price-pattern (below nearby support / major MA / trendline), ATR (stop at 2xATR, period 14; if 2xATR > 8% from entry the stock is too volatile for a swing trade), parabolic SAR (Wilder price+time stop). Four profit exits: percentage (target 1.5-2.0x the stop distance), price resistance/support, ATR (target 3xATR when stop is 2xATR), and trailing stop (claimed most profitable). Risk/reward minimum: 1.25 with a trailing stop, 2.0+ preferred; scratch any setup that cannot project at least +10% before significant resistance.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — risk layer, applies to every position.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop: max -8% (typ 5-6%) / 2xATR / below structure; target: 1.5-2.0x stop or 3xATR; ATR(14) used both for stops and position sizing.
findings.quote: In most cases, however, due to the relatively short-term nature of these trades, you will want to set a stop-loss no greater than −8 percent on any given trade no matter what you expect to gain from a successful completion of the trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'Entries and Exits' (pp. 229-237)
findings.notes: Maps directly to V8 risk_geometry (entry/stop_r/target_r/atr_ref): 2xATR stop / 3xATR target is a concrete instantiation of stop_r=2 and target_r=3 with atr_ref=14. The -8% cash-cap translates, under perp leverage, into R-multiple position sizing (risk_percent_sizing). Entry mechanics (pp. 227-229): stop order $0.02-0.05 above prior day's high (longs) / below prior day's low (shorts), gaps handled by limit orders; 'the entry is the least important part of trading.' The RR 1.25/2.0 thresholds are a RiskGate admission rule candidate.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: High-watermark trailing stop, never-average-down, and overtrading caps
findings.mechanism: Raising the stop at each new closing extreme locks in gains and lets winners run; proscribing averaging-down and capping trade frequency blocks the two classic loser behaviors (add-to-loser, revenge trading).
