findings.setup_summary: Adjust stops and targets once per day on a high-watermark basis: raise the stop-loss at each new closing high since entry (new low for shorts); lower the target at each new adverse low (raise for shorts). Preferred profit exit is the trailing stop moved on a closing basis ('let your winners run') — the two or three huge winners per year carry the account. Never average down on a losing position (keep the stop, lower the target, wait). Never overtrade: set a daily profit point or trade-count cap and stop for the day when reached; scale back size during a losing streak, increase during a winning streak; beginners cap position at ~1/10 of the account.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — position-management layer; the book allows exceptions only 'as dictated by current market conditions.'
findings.risk_geometry: Stop moved only at end of day on closing basis (avoid intraday whipsaw); in equities, take stops off overnight but keep target limit orders in place; target orders can be broken into small bits one penny apart.
findings.quote: raise your stop-loss price at each new closing high since entry (or new low if the trade is a short)... Never average down on a losing position.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 4 habits 2,3,8,9 (pp. 84-89) + Ch. 11 'Entries and Exits' (pp. 229-239)
findings.notes: For V8: closing-basis trailing-stop raises are a lifecycle/exposure-book rule operating on frozen refs + still_valid (the 'adjust at end of day' becomes a fixed UTC anchor such as the funding hour or session close, never wall-clock inside replay). Never-average-down aligns with rule 16 (one active exposure per instrument/direction) and the no-add-to-loser convention. Trade-count caps and scale-down-after-losses are RiskGate/position-sizing candidates. The trailing stop vs fixed-target tradeoff: fixed targets give steady cash flow but 'you then miss out on those few big runs that, in themselves, can be all the fuel you need to get your account into the big leagues.'
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

findings.strategy_name: Rule of Three (multi-indicator confirmation), divergence-fade, and process habits
findings.mechanism: Requiring >=3 independently-confirming technical reasons filters out confused-market entries and stacks probabilities; price-indicator divergence marks the best reversal points; process habits (journal, chart-first) remove bias and build discipline.
findings.setup_summary: (1) Rule of Three: do not enter any trade unless >=3 technical indicators give confirming reasons — 'conflicting indicators signal a confused market.' (2) Divergence-fade: when price prints a new high/low without indicators following, fade price and trade in the indicator direction (drives the rsi_divergence setup). (3) Trendline hygiene: 'No trend or trading channel exists until a line can be placed on the chart that intersects at least three price points. Two price points can yield a trendline, but no trading decision should be made until a third touch.' (4) Process: keep a journal of every trade (date, symbol, entry/exit, size, P/L, rationale) and analyze monthly; select chart-first, ignoring news/tips/forecasts; trade long setups in bull markets / short setups in bear markets for efficiency, not necessity — 'the vital key to your success as a trend trader is finding the best-looking chart.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — process layer.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A
findings.quote: My Rule of Three says that I will not enter any trade unless I can carefully articulate three reasons from among my list of technical indicators for doing so.
findings.notes: Rule of Three is a soft multi-feature confirmation heuristic — in V8 it argues for multi-feature confirmation thresholds (from different feature groups) rather than single-trigger entries, and is a design note for Expert triggers. The 3-touch trendline rule is a concrete, falsifiable location feature (minimum touches before a line is 'valid' — directly implementable). The 'Amateurs at the open, pros at the close' adage (habit 5, p. 86: enter within the last two hours to be in sync with professional flow) is a time-of-day consideration; in 24/7 perps the analog is session/funding-hour effects (feature group: time) and is weaker. Indicator stack the book standardizes on ('sexy six'): 20/50/200 SMA, MACD 12-26-9, stochastics 5-3, OBV, RSI 5, CCI 20.
findings.book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

book_title: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis (2013) — Anna Coulling, Part 1 (Chs 1-10)

findings.strategy_name: Volume climax reversal (buying/selling climax)
findings.mechanism: a high-volume, wide-range bar at a trend extreme that closes at the open exhausts the dominant side; the deep wick shows the opposite side absorbed the flow, setting up trend reversal.
findings.setup_summary: At the end of an extended trend (after a distribution phase at a top, or an accumulation phase at a bottom), price prints one to three repeated bars with high or ultra-high volume, a deep wick and a narrow body, closing at or near the open. Selling climax (deep upper wick, high volume, top of a bull trend) precedes a fast break lower; buying climax (deep lower wick, high volume, bottom of a waterfall) precedes a march higher. Entry comes only after the climax is confirmed by subsequent price action, never on the signal bar itself.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: climax bar at a trend extreme with well-above-average volume closing at/near the open. Invalidation: volume below average (not a climax), the candle appears mid-trend rather than at an extreme, or follow-through continues in the trend direction on rising volume (no reversal).
findings.risk_geometry: Book gives no stop/target; it stresses the oil-tanker effect - do not enter on the signal bar, wait for follow-through. Natural stops: below the buying-climax low / above the selling-climax high.
findings.quote: Here we will see high volume coupled with a candlestick which has a deep upper wick and narrow body, and is one of the most powerful combinations of price action and volume we will ever see on a chart.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 - The Selling Climax / The Buying Climax
findings.notes: Extends the existing DATA_BLOCKED capitulation backlog family (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion) with the symmetric selling-climax variant and the explicit close-at-open + deep-wick + high-volume bar spec. In crypto perps, liquidation cascades produce the waterfall/climax signature naturally; no exchange gaps means the 'break lower fast' leg is continuous.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Low-volume test of supply/demand (Wyckoff test)
findings.mechanism: after accumulation/distribution, a probe back into the old heavy-volume zone that closes near the open on low volume proves the opposite side has been absorbed, so the campaign can proceed and breakout is imminent.
findings.setup_summary: After an accumulation phase (bottom) or distribution phase (top), price is marked back into the recent heavy-selling/heavy-buying zone (test of supply / test of demand). A successful test: narrow body, deep wick toward the tested zone, closes near the open, LOW volume - residual sellers/buyers are gone and the next move is the breakout. A failed test (high volume, close-through) means the campaign must return into the zone for more mopping-up; no entry.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: test bar into an old high-volume zone after an accumulation/distribution phase closes near the open on low volume. Invalidation: high-volume close-through of the test zone (failed test), or no prior accumulation/distribution phase (test has no meaning).
findings.risk_geometry: Book specifies the candle form (narrow body, deep lower wick, colour unimportant, low volume) but no stop/target; entry is after the successful test is confirmed, before/at the breakout leg.
findings.quote: If the volume remains low, this instantly tells the insiders that there are few sellers left, and that virtually all the selling has been absorbed in the accumulation phase of the campaign.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 - Testing Supply / Testing Demand
findings.notes: Distinct from liquidity_sweep_reclaim: this is a low-volume probe closing near the open, not a wick-through-reclaim. Works on any timeframe; in 24/7 crypto the test can occur without a news catalyst.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Volume-validated congestion breakout with low-volume retest (fake-out detection)
findings.mechanism: moving out of a congestion zone requires effort; a breakout on well-above-average rising volume is genuine and the broken level becomes support/resistance, while a breakout on low volume is an insider trap (fake-out).
findings.setup_summary: Define a congestion zone from isolated pivot highs/lows (3-bar patterns). A valid breakout: a clean close beyond the ceiling/floor (clear water, not an intra-bar touch) on well-above-average, rising volume. After the break, a pullback to test the broken level on LOW/falling volume confirms and is the entry. A breakout on LOW volume is a fake-out/trap - stand aside. Applies to continuation and reversal breakouts alike.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pivot-defined congestion; close beyond the level on above-average rising volume. Invalidation: breakout bar on low/falling volume (fake-out), or retest of the broken level on rising volume (breakdown), or no clean close beyond the level.
findings.risk_geometry: Book: 'any stop loss could then be placed in the lower regions of the price congestion' (the broken zone becomes natural protection); targets are the next volume-dense congestion platforms; a 'clear water' close beyond the level is required.
findings.quote: A break out from such a price area on low volume, is a classic trap move by the insiders, and is often referred to as a 'fake out'.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.7 - Support And Resistance Explained
findings.notes: Refines the DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family with two hard rules the book stresses: (1) volume must be above average and rising on the breakout bar, (2) retest must be on low/falling volume. No-gap 24/7 crypto means breakouts unfold continuously rather than on gapped opens.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Effort-vs-result volume/price anomaly detector
findings.mechanism: Wyckoff's law of effort vs result: wide-range price requires proportionally high volume; when spread and volume disagree (wide spread + low volume, or narrow spread + high volume) the price action is suspect - marked, not genuine.
findings.setup_summary: Single-bar or multi-bar detector: a wide-spread candle on LOW volume is an anomaly (likely a trap/engineered move - insiders testing or marking price, not joining); a narrow-spread candle on HIGH volume is an anomaly (absorption - longs liquidating at a top, buyers absorbing at a bottom; effort without result = market struggling at this level). A valid trend shows rising price with rising volume, and falling price with rising volume; a rising market with falling volume is a classic sign of weakness.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence between spread and volume on a bar or small group of bars. Invalidation: volume normalizes to validate subsequent bars (divergence was a one-off), or divergence appears without trend context (book: get bearings first - location in trend is the first reference point).
findings.risk_geometry: Book-level tool: used to exit existing positions, stand aside, or prepare a reversal entry; no stop/target; it is a confirmation/flagging primitive feeding other setups.
findings.quote: The small price increase has been generated by a huge amount of volume, so clearly something is wrong.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.4 - Examples Of Anomalies; Ch.6 - Wide/Narrow Spread Candles
findings.notes: Propose as a marketstate feature (spread/volume agreement score) consumed by expert still_valid logic and RiskGate: e.g., trend_pullback longs should not be added while effort-result divergence signals engineered price.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Stopping volume / topping-out volume absorption sequences
findings.mechanism: in a fast waterfall the absorbing buying appears as repeated deep-lower-wick candles with high volume that close off the lows, progressively narrowing the spread until a hammer - the brakes applied; the mirror pattern at a top (deep upper wicks, high volume, arcing spreads) is topping-out/distribution.
findings.setup_summary: After a sharp fall on rising volume (price waterfall), look for 2-3 consecutive candles with deep lower wicks, high or rising volume, closing in the upper half of the range, ending in a hammer - stopping volume; reversal/absorption is under way and a move higher is to follow. Mirror: in a mature uptrend, candles with deepening upper wicks, high/ultra-high volume and narrowing spreads (arcing) = topping-out volume; the last candle is a shooting star; distribution then selling climax.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: post-waterfall sequence of deep-lower-wick high-volume candles. Invalidation: volume keeps rising on wide down candles (no absorption; waterfall continues), or a single hammer is treated as a reversal - the book is explicit a single hammer will not halt the move.
findings.risk_geometry: Book: close should be in the upper half of the open-close range for strength; no explicit stop/target (worked examples use the hammer wick as the stop level).
findings.quote: The sequence of candles in Fig 6.17 is an almost perfect example, and if we do see this combination following a sharp move lower, then we would be on full alert for the forthcoming move higher.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 - Stopping Volume / Topping Out Volume
findings.notes: Precursor sequence to the buying climax; in leveraged crypto, waterfall legs from liquidations make the stopping-volume signature (deep wicks + high volume + narrowing spread) frequent and checkable. Distinct behavior family from the single-bar climax.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Low-volume long-legged doji stop-hunt (news/event whipsaw) - stand aside
findings.mechanism: a violently volatile bar (long-legged doji) on LOW volume is anomalous - price is being 'racked' to take out stops and limits with insiders not participating; low volume on a wide move proves it is engineered, not genuine.
findings.setup_summary: During/around a news or event release, price swings violently one way then the other and closes near the open, printing a long-legged doji; if the volume is LOW this is an anomaly and a stop-hunt/trap - the book's instruction is to stay out and wait for later candles. Corollary: any event-driven price move must be validated by rising volume; a wide move on low volume means the insiders are not joining.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: long-legged doji (or wide two-way move) on low volume around an event. Invalidation: doji validated by average-or-higher volume (genuine indecision, watch for follow-through), or subsequent candles confirm a direction on volume.
findings.risk_geometry: None - this is a stay-out filter, not an entry. Book: 'we stay out, and wait for further candles to unfold.'
findings.quote: The most common reason for this is stop hunting, where the market makers and insiders are moving prices violently, first one way and then the other, to shake traders out, and to take out stop and limit orders in the process.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 - The Long Legged Doji Candle
findings.notes: Crypto has scheduled macro releases and event-driven volatility (FOMC/CPI, exchange listings, liquidation cascades) where the same low-volume-whipsaw signature can appear; propose as a RiskGate admission filter (no new exposure while a low-volume whipsaw is active) rather than an expert.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Dynamic pivot trend entry/exit (trend management via isolated pivots)
findings.mechanism: after a volume-validated breakout, an intact higher-high/higher-low sequence of isolated pivot bars defines a live trend; a pivot that fails to exceed the prior one signals the trend is pausing or reversing, triggering exit - enabling entry near the start of a trend rather than after it is obvious.
findings.setup_summary: Following a volume-validated breakout from congestion, hold the position while the market posts isolated pivot highs/lows (3-bar patterns) in sequence: for an uptrend, pivot highs above prior pivot highs and pivot lows above prior pivot lows confirm and hold. Exit when a pivot high posts at or below the prior pivot high (or a pivot low at/below the prior), signalling a secondary congestion phase or reversal. Works symmetrically for downtrends (lower lows/lower highs; exit on a higher pivot low).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: first pivot after a volume-validated breakout. Invalidation: pivots fail to build a sequential pattern (market lacking momentum - 'if these are missing... the market is potentially weak'), or a break the opposite way through the pivot structure (trend reversal, exit).
findings.risk_geometry: Position held through minor pullbacks while the pivot sequence is intact; exit on pivot-sequence failure; no explicit stop/target - pivots themselves are the waypoints. Higher-TF context determines pause vs reversal.
findings.quote: we see a pivot high posted that is lower or perhaps at the same level as a previous pivot, and it is at this point that we are looking at a market that is perhaps moving into a secondary congestion phase
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.8 - Dynamic Trends And Trend Lines
findings.notes: Directly usable as a still_valid/exit rule for trend-following experts (candidate refinement of trend_pullback exit or a new lifecycle rule): the pivot-sequence failure is a deterministic, bar-data-only exit trigger.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Volume-at-price (VAP) density as support/resistance significance
findings.mechanism: the vertical distribution of traded volume at each price level quantifies where supply/demand is dense; high-density price regions act as significant support/resistance, and the depth of the volume platform determines how hard a level is to break and where stops belong.
findings.setup_summary: Compute a VAP histogram over a window; price levels with extreme volume density (especially old, long-lived congestion) act as barriers. A breakout through a high-density platform requires extreme volume; a low-density region takes little effort to penetrate. Price stalled in congestion on ultra-high volume that fails to advance implies selling pressure/weakness. Long-lived congestion with extreme density = strong support platform (stop placement and target guidance).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price approaching or stalling in a high-VAP-density zone. Invalidation: density read without the time component (duration matters - 3 days of congestion is a heavier platform than a few hours at the same visual density); levels treated as rigid rather than elastic.
findings.risk_geometry: VAP depth directly informs stop placement (the book uses the density of the support platform to gauge where stops go) and target selection (next volume-dense platform); no entry-level stop/target stated.
findings.quote: If the concentration of volume was at the bottom, then this is more likely to be buying volume rather than selling volume.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.9 - Volume At Price (VAP)
findings.notes: Crypto perps report real traded volume (unlike the FX tick-volume proxy the book needs), so VAP density is directly computable from the perp tape. Propose VAP-derived features (high-volume nodes, density-weighted S/R levels) for the location feature group; could later seed a volume_profile expert.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Cause-and-effect: consolidation duration/depth scales trend extent
findings.mechanism: Wyckoff's law of cause and effect: the size of the 'cause' (duration and volume of accumulation/distribution congestion) is directly proportional to the size of the 'effect' (the extent of the ensuing trend).
findings.setup_summary: Markets spend roughly 70% of the time in sideways congestion; trends are born from congestion. Measure the duration and depth of a congestion phase (bars and volume density) and use it as a prior for the extent of the following trend: the longer and deeper the congestion, the larger the expected move after the volume-validated breakout (cause large, effect large; cause small, effect small). Also applies across timeframes (nested Russian-doll cycles).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: completed congestion phase followed by volume-validated breakout. Invalidation: congestion that resolves back into the range (no breakout) or a breakout that fails on volume; the proportionality is a tendency, not a guarantee - each market has its own tempo.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated; used for expectation-setting (how far a trend may run) and choosing minor-vs-primary trend, not for stop/target arithmetic.
findings.quote: If the cause is large, then the effect will be large as well. If the cause is small, then the effect will also be small.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.1 - Wyckoff's Laws; Ch.5 - The Accumulation/Distribution Phases
findings.notes: Falsifiable via measurement (consolidation width/duration vs. subsequent trend extent) on perp history; could also inform a simulator prior for trend extent. Corroborated by the Wyckoff line of books in this library.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Trapped-trader congestion zones as persistent support/resistance
findings.mechanism: congestion zones are densely populated with weak, late, emotional traders trapped near the wave tops/bottoms; these trapped populations make the price region act as a self-fulfilling future support/resistance platform, and levels where the market has failed before tend to fail again.
findings.setup_summary: Identify horizontal congestion zones (zig-zag ranges with floors and ceilings, defined by isolated pivots). Zones are elastic (breaks can be fake and price can return inside). A zone that previously failed to break is more likely to fail again; if it eventually breaks on this occasion, the level becomes a stronger platform. Buyers at the top of each wave are weak; buyers at the bottom are strong - the weak population defines the barrier.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price returning to a previously-visited, densely-traded congestion zone. Invalidation: the zone is treated as rigid (the book stresses 'rubber bands', not 'rods of steel'); significance scales with the depth/age of the zone - shallow zones matter little.
findings.risk_geometry: The broken zone becomes a 'natural floor/ceiling' of price protection; stops go below the floor/above the ceiling of the zone; no explicit R-multiple targets.
findings.quote: The buyers at the top of each wave can be considered to be weak, but the buyers at the bottom of each wave can be considered to be strong.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.7 - Fear And Greed Riding The Wave; Support & Resistance - The House
findings.notes: Overlaps location feature work and the liquidity_sweep family but is the zone-formation mechanism (trapped weak positions) rather than the sweep trigger; candidate companion to volume_profile for S/R significance.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: 1% risk rule + stop below signal wick/congestion floor
findings.mechanism: financial risk is quantifiable and capped (1% rule); stop placement follows market-set natural levels (the signal candle's wick or the floor of the volume-backed support zone), so risk is defined by structure rather than by arbitrary distance.
findings.setup_summary: Risk rules stated across the book: cap per-trade financial risk with simple money management such as the 1% rule; place the stop below the wick of the reversal signal candle (e.g., the hammer low) or in the lower regions of the congestion/support zone; use the VAP density/depth of the support platform to judge where the stop should sit; a validated breakout gives a 'natural floor' that protects the position and is where stops belong.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - risk rule, not a signal. Applies to every position: stop below structure, size so the stop distance risks ~1% of capital.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop: below signal-candle wick or below the congestion floor; size: such that the stop-distance loss is ~1% of capital; targets: next volume-dense platform / natural S/R.
findings.quote: Any stop loss by the way would be below the wick of the hammer, with the market setting this level for us.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.4 - risk on the trade; Ch.7 - stop placement; Ch.10 - SLV worked example
findings.notes: Direct input to RiskGate: per-exposure sizing tied to structure-defined stop distance and a per-trade risk cap; the 1% figure is a practitioner heuristic, not an empirical optimum.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Accumulation/distribution phase detection (campaign regime filter)
findings.mechanism: before a major move, large operators accumulate (buying during engineered sell-offs) or distribute (selling into manufactured demand) inside a range; the volume signature of absorbed high-volume moves reveals which campaign is running, so a trend-start can be anticipated from the regime rather than after the trend.
findings.setup_summary: During a sideways range, repeated high-volume sell-offs that close as narrow-spread candles (absorption, not follow-through) followed by quiet recovery = accumulation regime; repeated high-volume up-rallies that stall in a narrow range = distribution regime. These phases precede the next trend, in all timeframes. Regime label (accumulation / distribution / neutral) from volume-absorption patterns gates trend-start expectations and prepares for the low-volume test and breakout.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: range-bound price with absorbing (narrow-spread, high-volume) counter-trend bars. Invalidation: an absorption bar that fails to hold (price breaks the range on rising volume in the campaign direction before the test/breakout), or insufficient duration (a few bars of whipsaw is not a phase).
findings.risk_geometry: None - regime classification; entry still requires the test/breakout triggers (low-volume-test and breakout_retest findings).
findings.quote: These areas are the breeding grounds for trends.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 - The Accumulation Phase / The Distribution Phase; Ch.8 - summary
findings.notes: Propose as a regime filter on the 1h perp tape (range-detection + volume-absorption labels) that gates the breakout/retest and low-volume-test experts; the 'insider' narrative is not testable, but the volume-absorption signature is.
findings.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

findings.strategy_name: Hammer/umbrella-line reversal at support with volume and oscillator confirmation
findings.mechanism: A long lower shadow (rejection wick) at support shows buyers absorbing selling pressure after a decline; the wick marks where bids stepped in
findings.setup_summary: After a decline, a hammer or dragonfly doji forms at a support level (prior swing low, moving average): small real body at the upper end of range, lower shadow >=2x body, no or tiny upper shadow. Confirmation: heavy volume and/or oversold stochastic. Entry at the close of the signal candle or the following bar; target is the opposite structure (e.g., SUN case: up to the April-May resistance). Mirror side: hanging man at resistance after an advance is a short setup (SUN #3 shows a hanging man was 'not significant' right after a move resumed and was negated when price closed above it).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Signal negated when the next candle closes beyond the signal candle's extreme; low significance when it forms immediately after the trend has just resumed (context matters); weak without S/R context or volume/stochastic confirmation.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at signal-bar close or next-bar close; protective stop below support/swing low (sell stop for longs); target = prior resistance structure; case study cites 'an adequate reward-to-risk ratio for a short-term trade up to resistance'.
findings.quote: An entry at the close of the doji session, or the following day, would have provided an adequate reward-to-risk ratio for a short-term trade up to resistance at the April-May highs.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 Case Study 1 (SUN dragonfly doji at 50-SMA, #1/#8 hammer on heavy volume); Case Study 3 (WOLF #1); Appendix A Hammer / Dragonfly doji criteria
findings.notes: Umbrella lines (hammer, hanging man, dragonfly doji) share one rejection-wick mechanism; on 1h BTC candles this is fully observable in OHLC, and 24/7 liquidation sweeps generate frequent long lower shadows at levels.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Bullish/bearish engulfing reversal at support/resistance (tweezer confluence strengthens)
findings.mechanism: Full real-body envelopment of the prior opposite-color body in one bar marks an abrupt control shift from one side to the other
findings.setup_summary: After a decline, a white candle whose real body completely surrounds the prior black real body = bullish engulfing (long); after an advance, a black candle surrounding the prior white body = bearish engulfing (short). The engulfing only envelops the prior real body, not necessarily its shadows. Book's cases: bullish engulfing at 50-SMA support + prior bottoms (FLR Fig 10.7), bullish engulfing at tested S/R with matching lows (tweezer bottom, MEOH #9), bearish engulfing after moves far from the average (WOLF #8).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Pattern only confirmed at bar close (body must fully envelop prior body); mid-range engulfing without S/R context or overextension is 'not very significant' (SUN #3, WOLF #6); the tweezer alone is not significant, it only strengthens a co-occurring engulfing.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at signal-bar close; stop on the far side of the pattern or beyond support; target = prior resistance/structure; the engulfing day's shaven head and bottom show one-sided control (MEOH #9).
findings.quote: It is not necessary that the second candle envelop the prior candle's upper and lower shadows, just the real body. This is a strong reversal pattern that exemplifies an abrupt turnaround in investor psychology.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 Fig 10.7 (FLR bullish engulfing at 50-SMA + prior bottoms); Ch. 11 Case Study 2 (MEOH #9 engulfing + tweezer bottom), Case Study 3 (WOLF #8); Appendix A Bearish/Bullish engulfing
findings.notes: Body-envelopment is a purely candle-geometric test, deterministic and easy to code on 1h candles; the tweezer-strengthening condition is an additional conjunct on matching lows/highs of 2+ consecutive bars.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Piercing pattern / dark cloud cover after a gap-flush open
findings.mechanism: A gap open against the prior move that closes deeply back into the prior body shows the flush was absorbed and control flipped to the counter-move side
findings.setup_summary: After a decline, price gaps down open below the prior black candle's low and closes at least halfway into that black real body = bullish piercing (long). Mirror: after an advance, gap up open above the prior white candle's high and close at least halfway into the white body = dark cloud cover (short). Case studies: MEOH May 30 and July 25 piercing patterns; SUN June 4 near-dark-cloud on heavy overextension. The deeper the penetration into the prior body, the stronger the signal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A close that does not reach the halfway point of the prior body is 'not ideal' and weaker (SUN June 5 close was not half-way and was flagged as non-ideal); the first candle must be a strong opposite-color body; without an underlying trend or S/R the follow-through is uncertain.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at second-candle close; stop below the flush low (second candle's low); target = prior swing structure; penetration depth is the signal-strength scale.
findings.quote: Price gaps down open below the prior candle's low and closes deeply (at least halfway) into the prior candle's black real body. The deeper the second candle's bullish real body penetrates the prior candle's bearish real body, the stronger the signal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 Case Study 1 (SUN #4 near-dark-cloud), Case Study 2 (MEOH #8, #11 piercing); Appendix A Piercing pattern / Dark cloud cover
findings.notes: Crypto perps have no exchange gaps, but a candle that opens below the prior low after a sharp drop (flash-dip / wick flush) is observable on 1h candles; the session-open psychology of the equity 'gap' differs, so treat as an analog, not the same setup.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Morning star / evening star three-candle reversal, strength scaled by third-candle penetration and volume
findings.mechanism: A gapped small-body indecision candle after a strong thrust, followed by a strong opposite body intruding into the thrust candle, marks exhaustion of the move
findings.setup_summary: After a decline: a long black candle, then a small real body or doji gapping down open (the 'star'), then a white candle closing deeply into the first candle's black body = morning star (long). Mirror: evening star after an advance (short). The deeper the third candle's intrusion, the more likely the reversal follows, especially if the third candle is accompanied by heavy volume.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Requires deep third-candle intrusion into the first candle's body; shallow intrusion or low volume weakens the signal; requires a prior trend to reverse.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at third-candle close; stop below the star/low; target = opposite structure; the star's gap creates the exhaustion signature.
findings.quote: The deeper the intrusion, the more likely a reversal will follow, especially if the third candle is accompanied by heavy volume.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix A Morning star / Evening star; Ch. 11 quiz answers (Fig 11.5 B, Fig 11.6 B)
findings.notes: Rarer on 1h BTC than two-candle patterns and needs trend context; could be implemented as a variant of a single candlestick-reversal multiplicity unit (pattern type as a variant parameter) to conserve the active-expert budget.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Support/resistance role reversal: broken level flips and is retested (breakout retest)
findings.mechanism: Once price breaks a level, the old level flips polarity (resistance becomes demand, support becomes supply) and the retest attracts flow in the breakout direction
findings.setup_summary: After a breakout above resistance, a pullback that holds at the old level (now support) is a long; after a break below support, a rally into the old level (now resistance) is a short. Book cases: MEOH May 8 decline back to April peaks where 'support and resistance reversed roles. Buyers stepped in at support'; WOLF June 5-14 where 'Prior resistance had become new support'; S/R is flexible, not a hard line.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Retest fails if price closes back through the flip level (breakout fails / false breakout); the book's glossary defines false breakout as a close beyond a level without momentum to continue, followed by reversal.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the retest rejection candle close; stop beyond the flip level; target = measured move or next structure; the flip level's strength is judged by prior swing history.
findings.quote: As they often do, support and resistance reversed roles. Buyers stepped in at support (6) and pushed price back up to close well off the low as the long lower shadow indicates.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 Case Study 2 (MEOH #6), Case Study 3 (WOLF #5); Ch. 10 Fig 10.7 (FLR support from prior April-May minor peaks); Glossary False breakout
findings.notes: Directly corroborates V8's existing DATA_BLOCKED backlog family breakout_retest (requires location, volatility, history); 24/7 perp trading gives many clean level-flips and liquidation cascades often mark them.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Capitulation / selling climax and blow-off top: extreme-volume thrusts that end moves
findings.mechanism: Extreme volume during a sharp thrust exhausts the move's fuel; the climax is frequently followed by a trend change
findings.setup_summary: Capitulation: a sharp decline on very high volume with panic selling, often followed by a change in trend direction (long). Blow-off top: a sharp upward thrust in an uptrend on heavy volume followed by aggressive selling, often a trend change (short). Selling climax is the mirror of the blow-off. The climax needs genuinely extreme volume to count.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Volume must be truly extreme (climax); if the sharp move continues the climax thesis is invalid; a climax without a subsequent reversal candle is just high-volume continuation.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry after the climax reversal candle closes (e.g., hammer on heavy volume, SUN #8); stop beyond the climax extreme; target = mean/prior range.
findings.quote: True capitulation involves very high volume and a sharp decline as panic selling occurs. Capitulation is often followed by a change in the direction of the trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary (Capitulation, Blow-off top, Selling climax)
findings.notes: Directly corroborates V8's DATA_BLOCKED backlog family capitulation (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion, requires trend, volatility, history); in crypto perps the analog is a liquidation cascade (deleveraging) with taker-volume spike.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Overextension fade: price too far from the moving average + oscillator extreme = vulnerable to pullback
findings.mechanism: Price stretched beyond its short-term mean loses tensile energy; overextension makes counter-move reversal signals valid even when the candlestick is non-ideal
findings.setup_summary: When price has moved 'a good distance away from the moving average' (20-SMA in the cases) with the stochastic at an extreme, reversal signals fire with normal-to-high validity. SUN #4: a non-ideal dark cloud cover after a large run from the 20-SMA with overbought stochastic was 'just as strong as an ideal pattern'. WOLF #6: after moving up from the average price was 'vulnerable to a pullback'. Shrinking real bodies (spinning tops) toward the end of an upswing flagged the same exhaustion (SUN #7).
findings.trigger_invalidation: In a persistent trend, overextension can extend further; the fade thesis requires S/R context and a reversal candle, not distance alone.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the reversal close; stop beyond the overextension swing; target = the moving average / mean.
findings.quote: Since price had moved a good distance away from the moving average, and the stochastic oscillator was in overbought territory, the signal was just as strong as an ideal pattern.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 Case Study 1 (SUN #4, #7), Case Study 3 (WOLF #6); Index 'Overextended stocks, 143'
findings.notes: Best framed as a gating feature (distance-from-mean + oscillator extreme) for the candlestick-reversal families rather than a standalone fade: fading overextension in strong crypto trends without a level is dangerous.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Candlestick reversal candles as exit/lighten warnings for open positions
findings.mechanism: A reversal candle at a stretched point marks thesis weakening; exiting or lightening before the full reversal preserves capital
findings.setup_summary: Swing traders holding longs watch for bearish reversal signals (dark cloud cover, bearish engulfing, shooting star) to lighten or exit; shorts watch for bullish signals. Key constraint: the pattern is only identifiable at the session close, so price may already have moved against the position; mitigation is exiting early on an opening gap after a directional move, or selling part of the position on the gap and holding a protective stop on the balance. Harami signals momentum loss and 'caution' rather than an immediate reversal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Defensive discretion, not a hard rule: the warning candle can be a false signal; the cost of the rule is premature exit, which must be weighed against the protection.
findings.risk_geometry: Exit at bar close on confirmed reversal candle; alternative = partial exit at the gap open plus a protective stop on the remainder.
findings.quote: Another effective way to utilize the candlestick reversal signals is for warnings to lighten up, or exit, an open position... A challenge with utilizing the reversal signals in this manner is that you won't know until the close of the trading session that the pattern is present.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'Reversal Patterns can Provide Warnings'
findings.notes: Deterministic at bar close in V8's fill-at-close simulator; the gap-exit leg is not crypto-relevant (no gaps) but the candle-confirmed exit and lighten-on-warning logic map cleanly to episode exit rules.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Protective stop on every position: sell stop below support (long), buy-to-cover stop above resistance (short)
findings.mechanism: A pre-placed stop at the thesis-invalidating level caps loss per exposure; risk is not inherent to the position side but to failing to protect capital
findings.setup_summary: Every long carries a sell stop below current price at the level where the trader would no longer hold; every short carries a buy-to-cover stop above current price. The book's stance: shorting is not inherently risky ('the bull walks up the stairway but the bear jumps out the window' - prices fall faster than they rise), and 'It is not the practice of shorting that is risky, but rather the actions of the trader who fails to protect his capital.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a (risk rule).
findings.risk_geometry: Stop = structural level below support (long) / above resistance (short); the book gives no ATR-multiple rule, placement is at a level where the position thesis no longer holds.
findings.quote: Just like with a long position, a protective stop order can be used to limit loss on a short position. A protective stop-loss order for a long position is called a sell stop.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'Short Selling' (protective stops)
findings.notes: Foundation for V8's RiskGate stop semantics; in perps, high leverage makes structural stops essential but wick-through-stop risk (liquidity sweeps) is acute, so stop placement must anticipate sweep-and-reclaim rather than sit exactly at the level.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Confluence gating: trade candlestick reversals only where S/R, volume, and oscillators add 'ammunition'
findings.mechanism: Pattern validity is context-dependent: a reversal candle at a level with confirmation has higher follow-through than an isolated signal, so setups are selected, not all patterns traded
findings.setup_summary: Prefer candlestick-reversal trades that form where there is additional ammunition: support/resistance (prior peaks and bottoms, moving averages), volume, and/or the stochastic oscillator. A nonideal pattern may follow through when it forms at a strong ceiling/floor, within a larger Western pattern, or after overextension, 'in spite of falling short of meeting the criteria of an ideal pattern'. Two questions before acting: (1) what price action preceded the event, (2) are there Western technical occurrences affecting direction.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Isolated patterns with no confluence are treated as low quality; visual confluence is partly subjective, which is why the book pairs candlesticks with computable tools (volume, stochastic) for scanning.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a - this is a setup-quality filter applied over entry rules.
findings.quote: As long as there are many trade opportunities to choose from, I'll always gravitate toward the setups that offer a higher likelihood of following through. When I do trade based strictly on the appearance of a candlestick signal, I look for confirmation from other technical tools, such as volume and/or the stochastic oscillator.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'Bullish reversal patterns formed at support' (Fig 10.7 discussion); Ch. 11 validation notes ('nonideal patterns... at a strong ceiling or floor')
findings.notes: This is the book's central thesis and maps to V8 as a gating principle: candlestick-reversal experts should only be admitted to the expert family when location + participation + response features confirm; it also justifies the non-ideal-pattern relaxation at strong levels.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Multi-swing reversal structures (double top/bottom, triple top, head-and-shoulders) confirmed by a close through the pattern
findings.mechanism: Repeated tests of a level accumulate supply/demand; a decisive close through the confirmation line completes the reversal, filtering consolidation that would otherwise resemble the pattern
findings.setup_summary: Double bottom: two prominent near-parallel bottoms in a downtrend, valid on a close above the middle of the 'W'. Double top: mirror, valid on a close below the middle of the 'M'. Head-and-shoulders top (three-Buddha): valid on a close below the neckline connecting the swing lows on both sides of the head. Triple top: valid on a close below the lowest point between the three peaks. The book stresses that many double/triple tops resolve as consolidation, so the close-through confirmation is the validity filter (SUN bonus: peaks 4/7/9 formed a triple top / head-and-shoulders warning).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Pattern is invalid without the close-through confirmation; many such patterns turn out to be consolidation periods, so the confirmation line is the falsification point.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the confirming close through the line; stop back inside the pattern (above the middle); target = pattern projection / prior swing.
findings.quote: It is a valid reversal pattern when it is confirmed by a close below the middle of the 'M'... Remember that many double and triple top patterns turn out to be periods of consolidation.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary (Double bottom, Double top, Head-and-shoulders top, Triple top); Ch. 11 Case Study 1 bonus (SUN triple top at peaks 4/7/9)
findings.notes: Swing detection plus close-through confirmation is implementable on 1h BTC, but base rates of these patterns are contested and require a structural (swing/pattern) feature pipeline; the close-through confirmation is the falsifiable core.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Stochastic oscillator oversold/overbought confirmation at support/resistance for reversal candles
findings.mechanism: An oscillator at an extreme while a reversal candle forms at S/R confirms that the counter-move has a catalyst rather than just a wick
findings.setup_summary: The stochastic oscillator (12-3-3 in the book's chart panels) in oversold territory confirms bullish reversal candles at support (long), and overbought confirms bearish reversal candles at resistance (short). Used consistently across all three case studies: SUN #1 oversold dragonfly doji at the 50-SMA; SUN #7/#4 overbought stochastic with bearish reversal candles; MEOH #7 overbought dark cloud cover; WOLF #1 oversold hammer at the 200-SMA.
findings.trigger_invalidation: In strong trends the stochastic can remain pinned at extremes; oscillator confirmation is only treated as valid at S/R context, and by itself it is a confirmation feature, not an entry.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the confirmed reversal close; stop beyond S/R; target = opposite S/R.
findings.quote: The stochastic oscillator had reached the oversold line as well offering further confirmation of a viable setup for a long position.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 Case Study 1 (SUN #1); Case Study 2 (MEOH #7); Case Study 3 (WOLF #1)
findings.notes: Computable on any bar series; in V8 this is a 'response' feature-group input that gates the candlestick-reversal families, complementary to the overextension feature (distance from mean) rather than a duplicate.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

book_title: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting
Getting Started in Candlestick Charting (Tina Logan, 2008) — Part 1 of 2

findings.strategy_name: Umbrella line reversal (hammer / hanging man)
findings.mechanism: Long lower wick after a directional move shows intraday sellers exhausted and buyers recaptured price to close near the high; short-covering adds fuel for the reversal.
findings.setup_summary: After a multi-bar directional move on BTCUSDT 1h (decline for a bullish hammer, advance for a bearish hanging man), a bar forms with a small real body at/near the top of its range, a lower shadow at least 2x the body, and no or a very small upper shadow (price closes near the range high). The signal is a reversal of the prior move; confirmation = price trades above the hammer's body (or below the hanging man's body), ideally closing there, on the following bar.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Signal negated if the next bar instead moves in the trend's direction (e.g., a hammer followed by a lower close). A reversal pattern forming inside a consolidation has no significance because there is no move to reverse.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on confirmation (next-bar close above body for a hammer); initial protective stop below the pattern's low (failure point); candlesticks give no price target, so target comes from overhead structure or an R-multiple. Book warns that by confirmation price may already be far from the extreme, so reward:risk must be evaluated.
findings.quote: Since short covering equals buying, and bulls will also be buying, it provides fuel for a rally.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3, Hammer / Umbrella Lines, pp.30-35
findings.notes: Hanging man is the exact SHORT mirror after an advance; the book treats the two as one umbrella-line family. The short-covering-fuel mechanism is directly relevant to leveraged perps where liquidation-driven wick extremes and forced covering are core microstructure. Distinct from existing liquidity_sweep_reclaim: it needs no prior extreme reference, only a long lower wick after a directional move.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Opposite-color body engulfing reversal (incl. dark cloud cover / piercing as depth variants)
findings.mechanism: A longer opposite-color body that fully swallows the prior body shows an abrupt intraday takeover by the other side; the deeper the intrusion into the prior body, the stronger the reversal signal.
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h, after a directional move, a bar of the opposite color has a real body that completely surrounds the prior bar's real body (engulfing). Strengthening factors: a steep/long prior move, a tiny first body (spinning top or doji), a long shaven second body, and heavy volume. Dark cloud cover (bearish) and piercing (bullish) are weaker two-bar depth variants requiring the second body to close at least halfway into the first body after a gap-up/gap-down open.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not engulfing if the second body does not fully surround the first body (becomes dark cloud/piercing if at least half); if opens match at both ends the bodies are equal and criteria fail. A prior directional move is required.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry near the close of the engulfing bar or on the next bar's open; stop at the failure point (low of the bullish engulfing bar / high of the bearish one); target at structure (overhead resistance). Book stresses that by confirmation price may already be well off the extreme, so reward:risk must justify the entry.
findings.quote: The engulfing pattern exemplifies an abrupt turnaround in investor psychology.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3, Engulfing Patterns, pp.55-59
findings.notes: Book ranks engulfing as a stronger signal than dark cloud cover / piercing. A single body_intrusion_reversal family parameterized by depth-of-intrusion (>=50% vs full engulf) spans all three, consistent with the V8 variants rule. Heavy-volume strengthening maps to the participation feature group.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Doji reversal after a directional move (northern doji at top)
findings.mechanism: A bar whose open and close are at/near the same price (no body) after a directional move signals intraday equilibrium/indecision that cannot sustain the move, warning of a direction change.
findings.setup_summary: After an advance, a bar forms whose open and close are at or very near the same price (no real body); this is a bearish northern doji, strongest after one or more long bullish bars. After a decline it is a weaker bullish southern doji. Long-legged / dragonfly / gravestone variants encode the same indecision with long shadows and higher volatility.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If the following bar moves in the trend direction the signal is negated; the book cautions a doji is a warning, not a guarantee, and loses potency in declining markets.
findings.risk_geometry: Book recommends waiting for confirmation before entering (especially for southern doji); the doji's high/low acts as near-term resistance/support in the book's own examples (doji high repelled price for several sessions); no target from the pattern itself.
findings.quote: The doji represents indecision, which is not likely to sustain a move.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3, Doji, pp.41-45
findings.notes: The book itself says the doji is over-credited and is more reliable at tops than bottoms. On continuous 24h data, open-close parity is more arbitrary than on session-based markets (book: intraday opens/closes are less significant), so treat as a weak single-bar variant rather than a standalone active expert given the complexity budget.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Three-bar star reversal (morning star / evening star)
findings.mechanism: Staged sentiment flip: a long one-sided body, then a small-body star gapped away from it (momentum stall), then a strong opposite body closing deeply into the first body (control seized).
findings.setup_summary: After a decline, bar 1 is a long bearish body; bar 2 gaps down (bodies do not touch; shadows may overlap) forming a small body or doji star; bar 3 is a strong bullish body that closes deeply into bar 1's body (morning star; evening star is the mirror after an advance). Heavy volume on bar 3 strengthens the signal; a doji star is a stronger variant.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If bar 3 does not intrude deeply into bar 1 the signal is weak/invalid; bodies of bars 2-3 touching or overlapping are acceptable variations; patterns forming inside consolidation have little significance.
findings.risk_geometry: Book flags that a very long bar 3 can leave an inadequate reward-to-risk ratio for entry upon completion (same for evening star); entry after pattern confirmation; stop at the pattern's failure point; targets from Western structure.
findings.quote: The deeper the intrusion of the third candle's white real body into the first candle's black real body, the more likely a reversal, especially if the third session is accompanied by heavy volume.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3, Morning Star, pp.72-75
findings.notes: Requires body gaps between consecutive bars; on continuous 1h crypto these body-gaps are frequent (no session close), so detection is feasible, but the gap semantics differ from session-based stock markets. Overlaps with engulfing when bar 3 fully engulfs the star; lower priority than the single/two-bar families.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Failed breakout at resistance (intraday breach not sustained by the close / upper-wick rejection)
findings.mechanism: Price breaches a level intraday but closes back inside/under it, leaving an upper shadow; the failed attempt reveals insufficient demand at that level and unresolved liquidity to the downside.
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h, price trades above a windowed prior high (or consolidation ceiling) intraday but closes below that level, printing a long upper shadow / shooting star at the level (a failed breakout attempt). The short signal triggers after the failed breakout, with the level frozen as the resistance reference.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If price closes above the level (breakout confirmed), the failed-breakout thesis is invalid. A pattern forming in a long consolidation with no directional move to reverse weakens the signal. The book also shows the mirror: repeated wick tests of a strong visible ceiling get retested until the level is finally broken.
findings.risk_geometry: Existing V8 expert geometry: entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE below the frozen ref, target_r 1.0, stop_r 1.0, expiry_bars 8, atr_ref; still_valid = close stays below ref. Book adds that multiple wick tests of a ceiling strengthen the level and that a 'strong and visible ceiling' will be reacted to repeatedly.
findings.quote: Price actually broke out just slightly above the April high intraday, but closed below it, resulting in a failed breakout attempt.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 5, Tails at Support and Resistance, p.93; Ch 4, Figure 4.1, p.80
findings.notes: Closest match in this book to an already-formalized V8 expert (failed_breakout / liquidity_vacuum_reentry). Refinement inputs: (1) wick-penetration depth vs close-side condition as the trigger, (2) multi-touch ceiling strength, (3) doji-at-resistance variant.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Support-resistance role reversal and retest after breakout/breakdown
findings.mechanism: Once a level is closed through, participants re-anchor expectations on the other side; prior resistance becomes support and its retest is a low-risk continuation entry.
findings.setup_summary: After a close above resistance (breakout) or below support (breakdown), price pulls back and retests the broken level as support/resistance; the retest is the entry. The setup strengthens when the original breakout had heavy volume and the retest occurs on declining volume (acceptance of the new level). Role reversals also occur at broken trendlines and broken 50/200 MAs.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If the retest fails (price closes back through the level), the polarity thesis is invalid and the event is reclassified as a failed breakout/breakdown. The book notes it is ambiguous at the right edge whether a range is consolidation or topping/bottoming until the close-through resolves it.
findings.risk_geometry: Low-risk entry because the stop sits just below the retested level (failure point); the book explicitly says the retest 'offers traders a low-risk opportunity to get aboard the trend rather than chasing'. Breakout strategies often have no fixed target; the book's retest entries use trend continuation as the objective.
findings.quote: It is very common for prior support to be tested as resistance after a breakdown, and vice versa after an upside breakout.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Reversion to the Mean, p.139; Ch 9, Support and Resistance Reverse Roles, pp.191-193
findings.notes: Feeds the existing DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family. Level polarity is observable in 24/7 crypto; retests on low volume map to the participation feature group. Multiple tests of a level strengthen it.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Volume confirmation of breakouts/reversals and price-volume trend relationships
findings.mechanism: Volume is the force behind price moves: heavy volume on a breakout or reversal signal shows real participation and confirms it; a volume-less upside breakout is suspect (false breakout); a pullback on diminishing volume within a trend is profit-taking, not distribution, so the trend resumes.
findings.setup_summary: Add volume features to entries/exits: require volume above its 20-30 period moving average on bullish reversal patterns and on upside breakouts; treat an upside breakout without volume expansion as suspect/false; treat a pullback on declining volume within an uptrend as a continuation opportunity (entry with a closer stop); flag price-volume divergence (price rising, volume declining) as trend weakening. Table 6.1 gives the four systematic states (rising/declining price x rising/declining volume).
findings.trigger_invalidation: The book makes the volume rule asymmetric: downside breaks do not need heavy volume because 'the market can continue to fall under its own weight', so a single symmetric volume threshold would mis-filter shorts.
findings.risk_geometry: Volume is a confirm/filter feature, not a risk parameter; this finding sets no entry/stop/target of its own.
findings.quote: An upside breakout after a period of consolidation is usually accompanied by heavy volume. In fact, the breakout is suspect if not and may be a false breakout.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6, Analyzing Volume Patterns and Trends, p.103-105; Table 6.1
findings.notes: Caution for perps: exchange-reported volume is aggregated and can be inflated or wash-traded, so use relative volume (vs its own MA) rather than absolute thresholds. The price-volume relationship table is a cheap, systematic feature set for the participation group.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Gap classification, fill tendency, and gap zones as support/resistance
findings.mechanism: Markets dislike voids: price tends to return to untraded gap zones; the start of an upside gap (prior bar high) becomes support and the start of a downside gap (prior bar low) becomes resistance.
findings.setup_summary: Detect void gaps between consecutive bars (upside: current low > prior high; downside: current high < prior low). Classify by context: area gap (inside a range, fills fast, little significance), breakaway gap (out of a range, needs heavy volume), continuation/runaway gap (mid-trend, marks roughly the halfway point), exhaustion gap (climax, heavy volume, fills fast, often followed by reversal). Use the gap region or its origin-bar edge as a location zone: a return into an upside gap should find support; a close below the gap breaks that support and turns bearish.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Book warns a continuation vs exhaustion gap cannot be classified at formation time — it takes at least one more bar; a gap is considered filled when most of the void is closed, not necessarily all; some gaps are never filled.
findings.risk_geometry: Gap bottom/top is a stop-relevant level; book example: a stock gapping +35% then pulling back to the gap bottom was a ~24% round trip, which would blow a 15% max-stop; traders must size stops to survive a gap fill or exit into the gap.
findings.quote: The market does not like voids on a chart so there is a strong tendency for gaps to be filled.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8, When Has a Price Gap Been Filled?, p.157; Ch 9, Gaps May Provide Support or Resistance, pp.183-185
findings.notes: The book explicitly states morning gaps occur on stocks 'but not on the charts of continuous 24-hour futures' — the daily-auction gap mechanics do not transfer to perps. What survives is the fill tendency and gap zones as location features between bars (visible on daily/weekly candles in crypto). Low priority; the morning-gap intraday strategy itself is not applicable.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Buy pullbacks in an uptrend / reversion-to-the-mean entry (don't chase overextension)
findings.mechanism: Price deviates from the 20-period MA ('catching air') and tends to revert to the mean; pullbacks and basing within a trend are healthy rest stops, so entries near the MA offer a closer stop than chasing strength.
findings.setup_summary: In an established uptrend (rising swing highs and lows, price mostly above the 20-SMA, a valid rising support trendline), wait for price to pull back to the 20/50-period MA or base sideways rather than buying strength; enter on the pullback so the initial protective stop can sit close. The 50/200-period MAs act as dynamic support/resistance. Inverse for downtrends: sell rallies to the MAs.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If a retracement exceeds two-thirds of the prior trend, the move is technically a trend reversal and the prior trend is unlikely to resume. A pullback that turns into a countertrend move invalidates the continuation thesis.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the MA on a pullback with stop below the pullback swing low (failure point); book recommends max stop distance 10% (swing) / 15% (investor); a trailing stop can ride the trend but expect to be stopped out one or more times during its evolution.
findings.quote: When price moves too far away from that strong moving average, I refer to it as 'catching air.' ... When price has moved too far from the average, the stock may be overextended.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Reversion to the Mean, pp.136-141; Ch 7, Trend Direction, pp.122-123
findings.notes: Directly refines the formalized trend_pullback expert: add a distance-from-EMA / mean-reversion precondition (do not enter overextended) and MA-as-dynamic-S/R references (50/200). In leveraged perps the 'don't chase' discipline is amplified because overextended entries compound liquidation risk.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Oscillator overbought/oversold confluence for candlestick reversal signals
findings.mechanism: When price is overextended (stochastic >80 or <20, and/or far from the MA), a candlestick reversal signal has more fuel because the move is already vulnerable to profit-taking and reversion to the mean.
findings.setup_summary: Score candlestick reversal signals with overextension features: stochastic (14-5-5) in overbought (>80) territory when a bearish pattern forms, or oversold (<20) when a bullish pattern forms; and/or price far from the 20-SMA. The book's rule: either condition alone raises the odds, and requiring both is NOT recommended because they often co-occur but not always — the feature should be additive, not gating.
findings.trigger_invalidation: In strong trends overbought/oversold persists (book: 'it takes a consensus by many market participants to reverse a strong trend'), so these readings are short-term warnings, not trend-reversal signals; the book shows a counterexample where the oscillator gave no confirmation yet the setup still followed through.
findings.risk_geometry: Filter/feature only; it strengthens entries already defined by the candlestick pattern and sets no stop/target of its own.
findings.quote: If a bearish candlestick reversal pattern forms while stochastic is in overbought territory, or if a bullish reversal pattern forms while stochastic is in oversold territory, it strengthens the candlestick signal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Overbought and Oversold Conditions / Enhanced Candlestick Signals, pp.146-149
findings.notes: This is a response-group feature (momentum/oscillator extremes) added to the MarketState for reversal-pattern families, not a standalone expert. In strong crypto trends, overbought persistence is common — consistent with the book's short-term-only interpretation.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Reward:risk >=2:1, stop at failure point with max-distance cap, 2% account risk per trade
findings.mechanism: Protecting capital is paramount: define reward and risk before entry; a stop placed at the technical failure point (not arbitrary) with a max-distance cap, and per-trade risk capped as a fraction of equity, keeps single-trade losses survivable.
findings.setup_summary: Before any entry compute reward:risk = (target - entry) / (entry - stop): require at least 2:1 (ideally 3:1). Place the initial stop at the setup's failure point (pattern low/high or broken level), not to exceed 10% (swing) / 15% (long-term) of price from entry; cap loss per single trade at 2% of total equity; diversify (book model: max ~20% of account per position).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not a signal — applies to all entries. A ratio of 1 is a poor ratio; if the required stop distance exceeds the cap (e.g., ~10% on a volatile name), skip the trade or shift to a lower timeframe.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry near confirmation close; stop at the technical failure point capped at 10%/15% distance; target at structure (S/R) or an R-multiple such that reward:risk >= 2:1; the 2%-of-equity per-trade risk drives position size (inverse of stop distance).
findings.quote: I suggest always trying to select trade setups that will net at least twice as much potential gain as loss. And ideally, that ratio will be 3:1 or better on many trades.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10, Reward versus Risk, pp.207-209; Ch 8, Smart Investor Tip (2% account rule), p.161
findings.notes: Maps to V8 risk_geometry (entry/target_r/stop_r) and RiskGate admission: add a minimum reward:risk gate and a stop-distance cap. The book's percentage caps are stock-world; for perps convert to ATR multiples given volatility. The 2%-of-equity per-trade rule aligns with the existing heat cap / position sizing logic.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Reversal patterns require a directional move to reverse; stand aside in consolidation
findings.mechanism: Reversal signals derive their meaning from reversing a prior move; in a sideways/consolidation regime there is no move to reverse, so patterns there are noise — and trend-following tools whipsaw in ranges.
findings.setup_summary: Gate candlestick reversal families on regime: only fire after an identifiable directional move (up for bearish patterns, down for bullish ones), never inside a long consolidation/rectangle unless at the range extremes (where short swings give something to reverse). A sideways regime (flat/whipsawing 20-SMA, bounded peaks and bottoms) means standing aside for trend-following; false breakouts/breakdowns through range bounds are common. The book also weighs broad-market regime: broad sell-offs break even previously strong support.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The book notes it is ambiguous at the right edge whether a range is consolidation or topping/bottoming base — the gate must not be rigid; the close-through of a range bound is the resolving event.
findings.risk_geometry: Regime gate only; sets no entry/stop/target. It controls which behavior families are eligible (trend-following off in ranges).
findings.quote: If price is moving sideways, referred to as consolidation, and a reversal pattern forms within that congestion area, it has little or no significance.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 4, The Pattern Must Have Something to Reverse, pp.79-81; Ch 7, Sideways (No Trend), pp.125-126
findings.notes: Crypto ranges are frequent and wide; this gate is cheap (swing-structure + MA-flatness features already exist in the trend group) and would cut whipsaw losses across all reversal families. For single-instrument BTCUSDT, the broad-market layer should use higher-timeframe trend/volatility regime rather than cross-asset averages.
findings.book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

findings.strategy_name: Move-significance noise filter
findings.setup_summary: Classify each bar's move relative to the instrument's usual daily percentage change: unless |move| exceeds its usual daily magnitude the event is treated as noise and no signal weight is attached. Significance is nonlinear in magnitude (a 2% move is roughly 4x as significant as a 1% move), so a 1h BTCUSDT bar whose |return| is a small fraction of typical daily range should be ignored for any directional inference.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A move is deemed signal only when |move| > k * (usual daily % change); thesis invalidated if the filter shows no discrimination versus unfiltered signals on frozen OOS (signal subsets do not out-perform chance), or if the move fully reverts inside the significance window.
findings.risk_geometry: Not a trade; a pre-filter. No entry/stop/target. Feeds volatility-normalized feature or regime gating.
findings.quote: Unless something moves by more than its usual daily percentage change, the event is deemed to be noise.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'The Bloomberg Explanations' (p. 166)
findings.notes: Directly transferable to 24/7 crypto where noise dominates a large share of 1h bars. Candidate input for a volatility-scaled significance gate or feature (volatility-normalized move), complementing V8's existing ATR-scaled risk geometry.
findings.book: Fooled by Randomness - The Hidden Role of Chance in Life and in the Markets 2005

findings.strategy_name: Confidence-band (dispersion-first) positioning
findings.setup_summary: Design positions from the width of the uncertainty band around a forecast, not the point forecast: in high-dispersion regimes (wide error band) reduce size, widen stops and extend expiry; in low-dispersion regimes the same point forecast justifies tighter risk. The actionable quantity is variance around the estimate, not the estimate itself.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rule adds no value if dispersion-scaled sizing produces no risk-adjusted improvement versus constant sizing on frozen OOS.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop distance and size scale with the error band (dispersion), never with the point forecast alone; no fixed R target stated.
findings.quote: my activity in the market depends far less on where I think the market is going so much as it does on the degree of error I allow around such a confidence level
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'We Do Not Understand Confidence Levels' (p. 168)
findings.notes: Aligns with ATR-based risk_geometry but adds the normative point: heat/stop/expiry are outputs of dispersion, not of conviction. Reached as DESIGN_INFERENCE; V8 already ATR-scales, so marginal contribution is the sizing-as-output-of-variance discipline.
findings.book: Fooled by Randomness - The Hidden Role of Chance in Life and in the Markets 2005

findings.strategy_name: Threshold-gated strategy evaluation
findings.setup_summary: Do not react to short-run strategy P&L below a significance threshold: performance reports are reviewed only at pre-committed gates (a predetermined P&L/significance threshold), and small-sample outcomes are treated as noise. Taleb calibrates: a $100k gain implies ~2% probability the strategy is genuinely profitable, a $1M gain ~99%.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If threshold-gated review selects different expert versions than continuous review on the same frozen OOS and the gate-selected versions fail to replicate out-of-sample, gating is mis-specified.
findings.risk_geometry: Evaluation protocol, not a trade; no entry/stop/target.
findings.quote: denying myself access to my performance report unless it hits a predetermined threshold
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 (p. 180); calibration example Ch. 12 (p. 180)
findings.notes: Direct design input for the lab/registry screening stage: expert versions are promoted/rejected only at significance-gated evaluation points, never on noisy short-run P&L. Fits V8's frozen-OOS + registry gating.
findings.book: Fooled by Randomness - The Hidden Role of Chance in Life and in the Markets 2005

findings.strategy_name: Path-independent position revaluation
findings.setup_summary: For any open exposure, periodically re-run the entry decision as if flat: if the current MarketState would not generate the same CandidateDraft today, the position is dead regardless of entry P&L ('married to your position'). Soros example: short when market rallied to record highs, then 'covered and went very long' without embarrassment.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalidated when a flat-state re-run would not re-enter; the frozen still_valid check (dead-thesis) is a weaker special case of this rule.
findings.risk_geometry: Exit on thesis-death via fresh-state re-evaluation rather than on P&L target; complements existing still_valid exits in lifecycle.
findings.quote: If you owned no painting, would you still acquire it at the current price? If you would not, then you are said to be married to your position.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 13 'Path Dependence of Beliefs' (p. 187)
findings.notes: Proposed as a lifecycle_rule addition: a periodic flat-state re-entry test layered on top of frozen still_valid logic. No dependence on venue microstructure; fully compatible with deterministic replay.
findings.book: Fooled by Randomness - The Hidden Role of Chance in Life and in the Markets 2005

findings.strategy_name: Spurious-pattern rejection (data-snooping guard)
findings.setup_summary: Before promoting any discovered pattern or expert to the registry, demonstrate it discriminates beyond a data-snooping-controlled null: a pattern must NOT appear at comparable frequency on synthetic/randomized tapes. Skinner's pigeons developed elaborate rain-dance rituals to random food delivery; humans map A->B causation by default.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A candidate pattern/expert is rejected if it fires as frequently on shuffled or simulated random tapes as on the real tape.
findings.risk_geometry: Screening protocol, not a trade.
findings.quote: He programmed it to deliver food at random to the famished birds. He saw quite astonishing behavior on the part of the birds; they developed an extremely sophisticated rain-dance type of behavior
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'The Skinner Pigeon Experiment' (p. 178-179); see note 8 citing Sullivan, Timmermann, White 1999 on data-snooping/bootstrap
findings.notes: Controlled experiment (Skinner 1948) plus the cited data-snooping bootstrap literature make this falsifiable. Mandates a random-tape null in V8's lab screening before any PROPOSED->FORMALIZED promotion.
findings.book: Fooled by Randomness - The Hidden Role of Chance in Life and in the Markets 2005

findings.strategy_name: Negative-skew / blow-up risk cap
findings.setup_summary: RiskGate must cap or reject any strategy whose payoff profile is negative-skew harvest (small frequent gains, rare catastrophic losses), sizing so the modeled worst-case tail (e.g., a deleveraging cascade) never exceeds the per-instrument heat cap. LTCM failed by assigning zero probability to the model itself being wrong.
