findings.notes: Maps to V8's RiskGate heat cap concept; on high-leverage perp accounts with uncapped exposure this is a real blowup guard, and open profits in crypto perps can spike intraday due to leverage.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Overlapping risk layers: position count, per-contract dollar risk, margin-to-equity
findings.mechanism: redundant overlapping risk caps catch concentration that any single measure misses
findings.setup_summary: Admission requires ALL gates to pass: no more than 10 long and 10 short positions simultaneously; futures dollar risk per contract capped at $2,000-2,500 regardless of account size (so 1% of a large account cannot blow up one contract); margin-to-equity kept under 15% (author's comfort level).
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — multi-layer admission gates; a trade is passed if any single gate fails.
findings.risk_geometry: Portfolio-level caps layered on per-trade stop distance; the per-contract dollar cap was added after the author's mistake of risking $5,000/contract on a $500k account.
findings.quote: I will not trade more than 10 markets on the long side and no more than 10 markets on the short side.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 'Additional Risk Measures When Commodity Trading and Forex Trading'; Ch.6 Steps 4-5
findings.notes: The per-contract dollar cap is a direct guard for perp position sizing at high leverage; margin-to-equity maps to a leverage cap. Position-count caps are largely moot for a single-instrument system but inform any multi-instrument expansion.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: MACD zero-line direction gate / 200-EMA market filter
findings.mechanism: the dominant trend direction is confirmed by a momentum indicator; counter-trend breakout candidates are discarded before entry
findings.setup_summary: For longs, require MACD above the zero line and positively increasing; for shorts, below zero and decreasing (on the higher timeframe for retracements, e.g., weekly MACD with daily signals). For broad stock exposure, additionally only go long while price is above the 200-day exponential moving average.
findings.trigger_invalidation: MACD crossing the zero line in the opposite direction cancels pending orders and invalidates the higher-TF trade thesis.
findings.risk_geometry: Filter only — does not alter stops or targets.
findings.quote: I will only consider taking the buy or sell if I am trading in both in the direction of the trend of the MACD.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'Step 3: Trade in the Direction of the MACD'; Ch.5 'As far as the S&P 500'
findings.notes: A cheap, robust feature-based admission gate (trend feature), not a shared ranker. Consistent with V8's existing trend_pullback EMA logic; the 200-EMA line ('above = coast is clear, below = look out') is the canonical long/short regime switch.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Risk-of-ruin geometry ('100 bites of the apple')
findings.mechanism: risk per trade determines how many consecutive losers are survivable; risk above ~1-2% materially raises the probability of ruin over a large trade sample
findings.setup_summary: Assume worst-case streaks (author has personally seen 8-10 consecutive losers and drawdown durations exceeding 24 months; one 2011 loss exceeded the target due to a gap/limit move). Size so ~10 consecutive losers cannot materially dent equity: ~1% risk per trade. Supporting formula given: R = e^(-2a/d), where a = mean return, d = std dev.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — an expectation doctrine; 'your greatest drawdown is always ahead of you' is stated as invariant.
findings.risk_geometry: Account-level doctrine governing per-trade risk %; the 'apple bites' mapping is 100 bites at 1%, 50 at 2%, ~33 at 3%, 20 at 5%, 10 at 10%.
findings.quote: If you are risking 1 percent of your account on a trade, you get to have 100 bites out of the apple.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 'Risk of Ruin'
findings.notes: The single most transferable risk lesson for high-leverage perp crypto: book explicitly warns risk >2% 'increases dramatically' ruin probability, and that drawdowns of 24-30 months are normal for the strategy — a V8 lifecycle/drawdown expectation note. Formula and recovery-from-loss table (20% loss needs 25% to recover; 50% needs 100%) are quantitative.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Higher-timeframe overrule (Don Steinitz laws / Elder triple screen)
findings.mechanism: the higher timeframe defines the tradable trend and its price levels act as 'energy points' that lower-timeframe structure respects
findings.setup_summary: For a daily-bar system, confirm weekly direction before any entry (e.g., weekly MACD above/below zero); the lower timeframe (daily) then supplies the retracement/entry timing. Steinitz laws: every timeframe has its own structure; higher timeframes overrule lower; lower-TF prices respect higher-TF support/resistance energy points; 'what appears to be chaos in one time period can be order in another'.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — a framing doctrine; it does not replace entry/stops but defines which timeframe's trend is tradable.
findings.risk_geometry: None — methodology framing for signal construction.
findings.quote: The higher time frames overrule the lower time frames.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.8 'Don Steinitz's Approach' (and Elder triple-screen reference)
findings.notes: Maps naturally to 1h vs 4h/1d alignment for BTCUSDT: V8's 1h bar should verify a higher-TF regime before admission. Steinitz's 'energy points' language is a precursor to V8's frozen reference-level concept, but the book gives no falsifiable parameters for it.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Pyramiding / scale-in on strength with exit on trend reversal (Mulvaney)
findings.mechanism: a small initial commitment bounds downside while scaling in as the position proves itself compounds winners and rides long trends
findings.setup_summary: Enter very small (Mulvaney: ~0.5% of equity initial commitment per market). If the initial position generates positive returns, scale in; if it hurts the portfolio, reduce and ultimately exit. No profit target — hold until the trend reverses (program average hold ~180 days; wider channel breakout waits to avoid false breakouts).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Scale-out/exit on adverse behavior; a trend reversal (not a price target) ends the trade.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry small; adds on strength; no fixed target; exit on reversal via trailing/ATR stops; author warns pyramiding raises both profits and drawdowns and a drawdown exists that can stop any trader.
findings.quote: If you take our initial position and it starts to generate positive returns, then we'll increase it. If it starts to hurt the portfolio, then we'll reduce it and ultimately exit.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.4 'Paul Mulvaney'
findings.notes: Book presents two valid exit philosophies: Mulvaney (no target, exit on reversal) and Blackwater (strict profit targets + wide stops, no trailing stops). Scaling-in conflicts with V8's 'one active exposure per (instrument, direction)' rule only if scale-ins count as new exposures — needs a registry decision as a variant. Perp funding accrues on scaled size.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: X-day trend breakout with low-risk-bet filter (Donchian)
findings.setup_summary: On any liquid instrument, go long on a breakout above the X-day high and short on a breakdown below the X-day low, but only in markets ranked strong/weak: 'buy the strongest based on the average rate of change and sell the weakest.' A 'low-risk bet' gate compares the initial risk from the X-day breakout to the Y-day low, and the trade is only taken if it fits the fixed equity-risk budget (0.75-1.25% per trade). Entry at the breakout trigger, exit exclusively via the trailing ATR stop. Falsifiable: entry fires on X-day high/low break in a ranked-strong/weak market.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close/price exceeds X-day high (long) or low (short) in a top/bottom-ranked market. Invalidated when price re-enters the X-day range or the trailing ATR stop is hit; no re-entry until a fresh signal.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at breakout trigger; initial stop at Y-day low (long) / Y-day high (short) or via ATR; no fixed target -- exit only by trailing ATR stop; no time expiry; 'low-risk bet' = initial risk (breakout level to Y-day extreme) compared against fixed percent-of-equity risk budget.
findings.quote: I am seeking a breakout, either on the upside or downside. I measure my risk, watch my correlation, watch my open trade equity, and if I can take the trade, I use my two stops as a safety precaution.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, p.169 (rules referenced from Ch.9 pp.96-102)
findings.notes: The book's Conclusion explicitly attributes the core system to Richard Donchian's breakout strategy. The journal gives an empirical distribution over ~100 trades/yr across two models (2009-2012): most trades small losses, few winners carry the year. V8's backlog breakout_retest is a retest variant -- this is the distinct X-day breakout entry and warrants its own family. No exchange gaps in 24/7 perp crypto make breakout trigger fills cleaner; funding is a minor drift term.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Trailing ATR stop as the single exit (Wilder ATR)
findings.setup_summary: Every trade -- long or short, winner or loser -- is exited by the same trailing average-true-range stop, placed immediately on entry and honored the moment it is touched. The stop must be wide enough to let a working trend run (months-long holds are common) and tight enough to keep losses small (typical journal losses 0.2-1.2%). Falsifiable: exit exactly when price touches the trailing ATR stop; no discretionary exit, no 'it will come back' override.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Exit trigger: price closes/prints at or beyond the trailing ATR stop. Invalidation of the trade thesis also occurs when the stop is hit -- stops and dead-thesis are the same exit here.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop = trailing Wilder ATR multiple; target = none (no fixed R target; winners ride until stop); expiry = none (holds run 2 weeks to 5 months in journal); the 'two stops' are protective stops placed immediately upon entry.
findings.quote: My trailing stop has protected me when trades have not worked, and when trades do work the trailing stop gives them enough room to run.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, p.169 (cotton exit); ATR calc ref pp.102-104
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's existing use of atr_ref in trend_pullback/failed_breakout and the distinction between stops and dead-thesis exits. Journal confirms trailing ATR is applied identically on wins and losses (gold, cotton, silver, S&P, yen). In 24/7 perp trading the trailing stop is naturally executable at any hour; funding does not alter ATR-based stops.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Percent-of-equity risk sizing with position scaling by stop distance
findings.setup_summary: Size each position so the maximum loss is a fixed percent of core equity (1.25% on the Global Diversified model, 0.75% on the Diversified model, with per-contract dollar caps of $2,000/$2,500). A tighter stop (or lower volatility instrument) permits more contracts 'for the same risk as a one-lot'; the journal repeatedly attributes enhanced returns to trading two-to-four contracts at identical percent risk. Falsifiable: contract count = floor((fixed_pct * core_equity) / stop_distance_in_dollars).
findings.trigger_invalidation: No entry trigger; sizing rule applied at every admission. Fixed-dollar-per-contract cap (and 1.25% nominal risk) can still be exceeded by gaps/limit moves -- accepted, not preventable.
findings.risk_geometry: Sizing from core equity (excludes open-trade equity); per-trade risk cap 0.75-1.25%; per-contract dollar risk cap; position scaling is a direct consequence of stop distance, not of conviction.
findings.quote: What enhanced my return was that for the same risk I was able to put on two contracts. This underscores the power of position sizing.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, pp.170, 186 (silver, gold, eurodollar entries)
findings.notes: Directly maps to V8 risk_geometry: sizing should be derived from fixed equity-percent risk normalized by stop distance (ATR or swing). With perp leverage this is the standard sizing discipline and prevents the 'bigger size when cocky' failure mode the book warns about (p.158).
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Sector correlation cap (5% per sector, correlation filter within sector)
findings.setup_summary: Cap portfolio exposure at 5% per sector; within a sector, take a new trade only if it does not push the sector's correlation past the threshold (e.g., a 10-year bond long was the last interest-rate trade because the 5% correlation quota was filled; corn+wheat longs were skipped once filled). Falsifiable: no new admission if sector aggregated exposure would exceed 5% of equity, or if pairwise correlation with an open position exceeds a fixed limit.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No entry trigger; an admission is blocked when the sector/correlation quota is full regardless of signal quality -- 'no matter how good a trade looks, follow the plan.'
findings.risk_geometry: Portfolio-level cap (5% per sector), not a per-trade stop; interacts with the heat cap; affects admission, not exit.
findings.quote: I do not want to have more than 5 percent of my portfolio in any one sector. If I allocated heavier in a sector my correlations to risk would increase dramatically.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, pp.166, 180
findings.notes: V8 is single-instrument (BTCUSDT) with one exposure per (instrument, direction) and a heat cap, so a sector cap matters only once multi-asset data exists; for crypto the analog is correlated coin exposure (BTC/ETH alt correlation). The underlying principle -- cap correlated simultaneous risk, skip good-looking trades to respect the cap -- is a confirmed RiskGate admission rule.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Cross-sectional momentum: buy strongest / sell weakest by average rate of change
findings.setup_summary: Over a fixed basket of ~27 liquid markets, rank every market by its average rate of change; take long breakouts only in the strongest-ranked markets and short breakouts only in the weakest-ranked markets ('buy the strongest if I can put on a low-risk bet and sell the weakest'). Falsifiable: the rank filter changes the admitted population, not the entry signal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Ranking re-computed each bar; a market that loses top/bottom rank is not re-entered until it re-qualifies; the breakout signal still governs timing.
findings.risk_geometry: Selection layer only -- entry/exit per the Donchian/ATR rules; ranking constrains which markets get signals traded.
findings.quote: I look to buy the strongest based on the average rate of change and sell the weakest based on the average rate of change.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, p.162 (also pp.186-187, S&P/sugar/Canadian dollar ranking examples)
findings.notes: Requires a multi-instrument perp derivatives tape (data-blocked in V8 today, matching the backlog mechanism of breakout_retest/capitulation). The cross_market feature group exists in the frozen spec, so this is a BACKLOG family, not a new feature group. Crypto perp universe is large enough (dozens of coins) for a relative-strength basket.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Quiet-market compression breakout; avoid high-volatility entries
findings.setup_summary: Best breakout trades originate from quiet/compressed markets: silver's breakout 'came out of a quiet period,' and the book states best trades 'come out of times when the markets are quiet and break out.' Conversely, 'one does not want to jump in on markets that are volatile.' Falsifiable: admit breakout signals only when a volatility/compression measure (e.g., ATR percentile or range compression) is low, and suppress entries during high-volatility regimes.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Filter invalidates admission when volatility is elevated or after the breakout has extended (no chasing after being stopped out -- 'I did not chase the trade').
findings.risk_geometry: Regime gate on admission; interacts with the trailing ATR stop that widens/narrows with volatility.
findings.quote: Actually, some of my best trades come out of times when the markets are quiet and break out. ... One does not want to jump in on markets that are volatile.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, pp.171, 185 (silver quiet-period breakout; cotton giveback)
findings.notes: Maps to V8's volatility feature group and a regime filter on the breakout family. In 24/7 perp crypto, compression-then-breakout is a well-documented pattern and is cleaner to test than in daily futures. Corroborated by the range_compression/volatility_breakout starter vocabulary.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Trend retracement entries (Elder) layered on the breakout core
findings.setup_summary: The system combines two engines: Donchian-style breakouts plus 'the trend retracement ideas of Alexander Elder' -- buying pullbacks within an established uptrend (and shorting retracements within a downtrend). Falsifiable: a retracement entry requires an established trend (per a longer-timeframe trend definition) followed by a pullback to a support/trend point, with the pullback invalidated if the trend structure breaks.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Pullback thesis dead if the parent trend reverses or the retracement exceeds the trend's structure (index refs: trend retracement rules pp.105, 121-127).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on retracement within trend; protective stop under the retracement low; exit by the same trailing ATR stop; detailed parameterization is in Part 1 chapters.
findings.quote: The actual trading is based on Richard Donchian's breakout strategy as well as the trend retracement ideas of Alexander Elder with a strong dose of my personal risk management.
findings.chapter_anchor: Conclusion, p.193 (index: trend retracement rules pp.105, 121-127)
findings.notes: This is a direct corroboration of V8's existing trend_pullback expert family (mechanism trend_continuation, behavior pullback_in_trend). The book's journal shows both engines coexisting; the pullback engine's detailed rules are in Part 1. Strengthens the LITERATURE_SUPPORTED basis for the existing family rather than proposing anything new.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Take every signal; sequential statistical independence
findings.setup_summary: Trade every signal, never skip, and never stop trading a market after a loss streak: the journal documents 9 losses in a row (Dec 2010-Jan 2011), 18 losses in a row (late 2011), and 6-7 loss runs, all taken mechanically; 'the prior trade has absolutely nothing to do with the next trade.' Cherry-picking or quitting a market after losses is described as a guaranteed path to the losing majority. Falsifiable: signal-to-admission rate = 100% with zero discretion.
findings.trigger_invalidation: None -- this is a consistency constraint, not a market trigger.
findings.risk_geometry: No geometry; governs admission consistency across loss streaks.
findings.quote: The prior trade has absolutely nothing to do with the next trade. One must take every trade via one's plan.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, pp.177-178, 188 (nine-loss streak); also p.351 (take every trade)
findings.notes: For V8 this is the anti-tinkering discipline: screening/registry decisions must not react to short loss streaks; the fixed plan is evaluated over many episodes. Directly supports V8's challenger+frozen-OOS registry protocol (no in-place mutation after bad runs). The book explicitly calls streak-following 'no six sigma event.'
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Four-outcome payout: small losses dominate, rare large profits carry returns
findings.setup_summary: There are only four trade outcomes: big losses (prevented by immediate stops), small losses (the majority, typically -0.2% to -1.2%), small profits (0.2-1.2%), and rare large profits (2-14.5% over multi-month holds) which pay for all the small losses. Low win rate is expected and irrelevant. Falsifiable: over a long sample, the PnL distribution is highly right-skewed with a majority of small negative trades and a small tail of large winners.
findings.trigger_invalidation: None; an expectancy property.
findings.risk_geometry: No geometry; defines the expected payoff shape that screening thresholds and expectancy accounting should assume for a trend-following Expert.
findings.quote: There are only 4 possibilities when trading. One can have big losses, small losses, small profits, and rare large profits.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, p.164 (journal-wide confirmation p.192)
findings.notes: Should inform V8's simulator/screening assumptions: an Expert of the breakout family should not be judged on win rate but on the fat right tail; position-scaling that adds contracts when a trade is working amplifies the tail (documented in silver/gold entries). Also justifies tolerance for long drawdown phases (17 months) before any verdict.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Gap/limit-move stop slippage is accepted, un-preventable risk
findings.setup_summary: Even with stops placed immediately on entry, realized losses can exceed the planned per-trade risk because of gaps and limit moves (documented: a cotton long lost 1.5% instead of the planned 1.25% on an adverse gap; Swiss franc fell ~800 points in a day). The book's stance: this is irreducible uncertainty; the only complete prevention is not trading. Falsifiable: stop fills can be modeled with a slippage/overshoot term beyond the nominal stop level.
findings.trigger_invalidation: None -- risk acceptance statement.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop orders placed immediately on entry; nominal risk cap 0.75-1.25% can be exceeded by gap/limit events; no mitigation offered beyond accepting and not trading during unrunnable conditions.
findings.quote: More so, there are periods when there will be limit moves in which one cannot exit. We are dealing with risk and uncertainty. I have accepted the risk and try to mitigate as much as possible, but it is not completely possible.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, pp.163, 183 (cotton gap loss); Swiss franc p.176
findings.notes: Directly relevant to V8's simulator STOP_FIRST + gap semantics. Crypto perps have no exchange gaps (24/7), but wick-throughs and liquidation cascades act as gap-equivalents that can fill stops far worse than the nominal level; the cost model should include overshoot beyond the stop price. Funding is not a gap driver but adds steady-state cost.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Venue/custody counterparty risk (MF Global failure)
findings.setup_summary: MF Global's October 2011 bankruptcy froze cash (a wire never landed) and orphaned positions between two brokers; the author was able to transfer most positions beforehand and keeps accounts at multiple brokers. Falsifiable operational rule: no single venue may hold both all cash and all positions; venue failure must not prevent exit or admission.
findings.trigger_invalidation: None -- operational risk rule.
findings.risk_geometry: No geometry; portfolio/operations-level rule: split venues, keep executable positions transferable.
findings.quote: I was all in cash, and my cash was supposed to have been wired on the Friday before the collapse. This did not happen and my cash at MF Global was frozen.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, pp.191-192
findings.notes: The exact analog for crypto perp venue risk (Mt. Gox, FTX). For V8 this lands as a RiskGate/operational rule once execution exists; in the PRE-EXPERIMENTAL phase it is a standing risk rule for the program's venue/custody assumptions. The simulator's assumption that fills occur at the venue is unaffected but the program must not assume venue solvency.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Data/contract-spec integrity and model synchronization
findings.setup_summary: A natural-gas data/contract mismatch (mini vs full contract) made the system miss a trailing-stop exit signal by 'a tick or so'; the author stayed short, later discovered the position was still open, and skipped a large continuation profit out of prudence. Lesson stated as 'always to get in sync with the model.' Falsifiable: every signal must be computed on the exact same instrument/contract and timestamps the model assumes; a data mismatch must be detectable, not silently actable.
findings.trigger_invalidation: None -- integrity constraint.
findings.risk_geometry: No geometry; data-pipeline constraint: contract identity, price/volatility reference consistency, and exit signals must derive from one synchronized tape.
findings.quote: I realized a couple days later when my system showed me I was still short after realizing I had a data issue. ... The answer is always to get in sync with the model.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, pp.190-191
findings.notes: Directly reinforces V8's determinism invariants: the event/available/ingested clocks must never be collapsed, and PIT data integrity is a first-class concern. Crypto tape has its own hazards (exchange-specific contract specs, funding timestamps, perp vs spot price) that map onto this lesson. The missed-exit cost here (a 'great trade getting away') shows the economic weight of data integrity.
findings.book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

findings.strategy_name: Higher-timeframe trend filter pullback (buy dips in uptrend, sell rallies in downtrend)
findings.mechanism: Buying pullbacks aligned with the higher-timeframe trend has positive skew: a retracement that does not violate longer-TF symmetry is a continuation point, so invalidation is cheap
findings.setup_summary: Define the major trend on a higher timeframe (e.g., daily) as a series of higher highs/higher lows (up) or lower highs/lower lows (down). Take trades ONLY in the direction of that major trend. On the lower timeframe (e.g., 30m/1h), buy pullbacks down to edge-defined support in an uptrend; sell rallies up to edge-defined resistance in a downtrend. All entry and exit signals are computed on the same (lower) timeframe; the longer timeframe is a filter only.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis dies when lower-TF price moves beyond the support/resistance point by more than the predefined stop distance, i.e., the retracement violates the symmetry of the longer trend. Author: there is 'usually very little risk' at these intraday S/R points because you don't need to let price go far beyond them to know the trade isn't working.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at lower-TF support/resistance; stop just beyond the structural level (small distance); profit objective at a longer-TF support/resistance or prior significant high/low; all exit signals on the same timeframe as entry.
findings.quote: The lowest-risk trade, with the highest probability of success, occurs when you are buying dips (support) in an up-trending market or selling rallies (resistance) in a down-trending market.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch11 Thinking Like a Trader / Exercise setup: Time Frame + trend filter
findings.notes: Directly refines the existing trend_pullback expert: adds an explicit higher-TF structural trend filter (HH/HL or LH/LL series) gating lower-TF pullback entries, and a same-timeframe entry/exit rule. In 24/7 perp crypto the daily HH/HL series is computable with no gap artifacts. Caveat: crypto 1h pullback levels get wicked by liquidation cascades, so 'very little risk' at intraday S/R is optimistic; the structural stop must sit beyond the wick zone.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Scale out in thirds with break-even stop (pay yourself as the market makes money available)
findings.mechanism: Harvesting a partial position early converts the remainder into a risk-free state, cutting per-trade loss variance and guaranteeing net profit on tail exposure
findings.setup_summary: Trade a minimum of 3 (or 4) size units. Take the first third off as soon as the market moves a small predefined amount in your favor (author: 4 tics in T-bonds, 1.5-2 full points in S&P). Take the second third at a longer-timeframe support/resistance or a test of a prior significant high/low, and simultaneously move the stop to the original entry (the 'risk-free opportunity'). Leave the last third running with a liquidate order just below a long's / just above a short's likely stopping point on a longer timeframe; do not chase the last tic.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trade is dead at the (initially predefined, later break-even) stop. Last third's thesis dies when price trades beyond the longer-TF stopping point (significant high/low).
findings.risk_geometry: Initial stop predefined (author: ~6 tics on T-bonds); first take at small favorable move; second take at structure with stop moved to break-even; final trailing liquidate just beyond longer-TF significant high/low; author self-reports only ~1 in 10 trades was an immediate loser and 25-30% of losers first moved 3-4 tics favorable.
findings.quote: I always, without reservation or hesitation, take off a portion of a winning position whenever the market gives me a little to take.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch11 / Taking Profits (scale-out regime)
findings.notes: The 'risk-free opportunity' state is the mechanism V8 should formalize in ExposureBook/lifecycle: partial take-profit at small favorable move + stop-to-break-even converts remaining exposure to positive expectancy regardless of outcome. For perp crypto, scaling out also reduces funding-cost drag on open notional. This is position management, not an entry expert.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Minimum 3:1 reward-to-risk ratio per trade
findings.mechanism: With reward:risk >= 3:1, breakeven win rate falls to 25%, so a win rate below 50% still yields positive expectancy - profitability decouples from prediction accuracy
findings.setup_summary: Require target distance >= 3x stop distance on every trade (risk $1 for every $3 of profit potential). Combined with the scale-out regime, a winning-trade percentage below 50% can still be consistently profitable.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rule-level constraint; no thesis. Breakeven win rate for reward:risk R is 1/(1+R).
findings.risk_geometry: target_r/stop_r >= 3.0. Note: V8's existing experts use target_r 1.0, so this is parameter guidance to screen, not a law.
findings.quote: Ideally, your risk-to-reward ratio should be at least 3:1, which means you are only risking one dollar for every three dollars of profit potential. If your edge and the way you scale out of your trades give you a 3:1 risk-to-reward ratio, your winning trade percentage can be less than 50 percent and you will still make money consistently.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch11 / Taking Profits (risk-to-reward)
findings.notes: The arithmetic is verifiable (breakeven WR = 1/(1+RR)); the book evidences no edge with 3:1 skew. For V8: raising target_r from 1.0 trades hit-rate for expectancy - worth an OOS screening variant, not an a priori change.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Market-structure-determined stop, not arbitrary dollar or risk-comfort amount
findings.mechanism: The optimum stop is the level at which the probability the trade will not work is so diminished that closing is better; market structure locates that level better than an arbitrary dollar amount
findings.setup_summary: Define each trade's stop from market structure (the level beyond which the setup thesis fails), never from an arbitrary dollar amount or from risk-comfort. If the dollar risk is uncomfortable, reduce position size; change a risk parameter only when technical analysis warrants it, never to satisfy comfort.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The stop IS the invalidation. Moving the stop (e.g., closer to entry out of fear) is itself classified as an error.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop at the structural point beyond entry-side support/resistance; for pullback entries the distance is small ('usually very little risk'); risk per trade known exactly before entry.
findings.quote: Let the market structure determine where this optimum point is, rather than using an arbitrary dollar amount that you are willing to risk on a trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch11 / Stop-Loss Exit
findings.notes: Consistent with V8's structural/ATR stops and frozen risk_geometry (the book lists moving a stop closer to entry as an error). In perp crypto, structural stops at swing points are known stop-run targets for liquidation cascades, so a pure swing stop is huntable - MEDIUM rather than HIGH; needs a stop-hunt-aware placement or ATR buffer.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Evaluate edges on sample sizes of 20+ trades, never trade-by-trade
findings.mechanism: Per-trade outcomes are random relative to each other; only a committed series reveals the edge's true parameters and their decay
findings.setup_summary: Judge success or failure over a minimum sample of 20 occurrences of the edge, not the last trade. The sample must be large enough to fairly test the variables and small enough that a decay in effectiveness is detectable before an inordinate amount is lost.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Methodology-level; no per-trade thesis. A single edge occurrence is never evidence of anything.
findings.risk_geometry: Know the exact dollar risk per trade and the accumulated worst case (losing all 20) before starting the sample.
findings.quote: Your sample size has to be large enough to give your variables a fair and adequate test, but at the same time small enough so that if their effectiveness diminishes, you can detect it before you lose an inordinate amount of money. I have found that a sample size of at least 20 trades fulfills both of these requirements.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch11 / Trading in Sample Sizes
findings.notes: Directly supports V8's series/registry evaluation and frozen-OOS gating: an expert hypothesis is judged across a candidate-episode series, never per episode; small-sample screening before any registry promotion.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Casino regime: rigid precise variables, take every signal, no subjective filtering
findings.mechanism: Consistent profit requires participating in every event where the odds favor you; picking and choosing trades reintroduces prediction and destroys the probability edge
findings.setup_summary: Entry variables must be absolutely precise, requiring no subjective judgment: if the market aligns to the rigid variables you have a trade, otherwise not - no extraneous factors. Commit to trading the next 20 occurrences of the edge no matter what, and never change the variables mid-sample. This duplicates how a casino operates: fixed odds + participate in every event.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Methodology-level; the commitment is to the full sample. Deviating from the rigid variables is itself the failure.
findings.risk_geometry: The methodology must specify exactly how much is risked to find out if the trade works (the stop), computed in the same timeframe as entry.
findings.quote: The rules are simple: Trade your system exactly as you have designed it. This means you have to commit yourself to trading at least the next 20 occurrences of your edge - not just the next trade or the next couple of trades, but all 20, no matter what.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch11 / Exercise: Learning to Trade an Edge Like a Casino
findings.notes: Mirrors V8's deterministic admission and take-all-signals lab design; argues against any discretionary pre-filter of CandidateDraft absent registry evidence. In 24/7 perp crypto the 'take every signal' rule also removes any temptation to skip trades around funding/volatility events.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Predefine and accept the exact risk of every trade before entry
findings.mechanism: Risk acceptance requires knowing the exact dollar risk before entry; comfort is adjusted by position size, never by changing the technical risk parameter
findings.setup_summary: Before any trade, know exactly the dollar cost of finding out whether the trade will work, and accept it (worst case: losing all 20 trades of the sample). If the dollar amount is uncomfortable, reduce position size (contracts/shares) or use simulated brokerage - never change the technical stop parameter to feel better.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rule-level; a trade taken without a predefined risk is by definition a violation.
findings.risk_geometry: Predefined stop and $ risk per trade before entry; position sized so the accumulated 20-trade worst-case loss is bearable (author's example: S&P 3-point risk x 3 contracts = $2,250/trade, $45,000 for 20).
findings.quote: My risk is always defined before I enter a trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch11 / Accepting the Risk; survey item 5 ('knowing the risk and accepting the risk are two different things')
findings.notes: The psychological counterpart of V8's RiskGate deterministic admission and precomputed risk_geometry: risk is fixed at entry and never renegotiated mid-trade. Maps to the heat cap / risk-per-trade sizing for sizing-down.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Thinking in probabilities (five fundamental truths)
findings.mechanism: Expecting a known outcome makes disconfirming market information threatening and triggers pain-avoidance errors; believing each edge's outcome is unique removes the threat and the error source
findings.setup_summary: Operate from five beliefs: every moment in the market is unique; every edge has a unique outcome; you don't need to know what happens next to make money; potential for loss exists in every trade; outcomes are random relative to each other at the micro level and consistent only over a series. Neutral expectations prevent block/discount/distort/deny perception errors.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Psychological framework, not a market thesis.
findings.risk_geometry: None. The regime-level requirement is predefined risk + accepting any outcome.
findings.quote: To think in probabilities, you have to believe that every moment in the market is unique, or more specifically, that every edge has a unique outcome.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch10 / Beliefs and active contradictions; Ch11 / Thinking Like a Trader
findings.notes: For an automated pipeline this is a design stance, not an executable expert: V8 must not gate execution on per-episode prediction confidence, and the economic verdict is computed over the registry series, not per candidate episode. Belongs in the methodology corpus, not the expert ontology.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Catalog of execution errors (fear/euphoria/self-valuation driven)
findings.mechanism: Loss of objectivity manifests as a specific enumerable set of execution errors rather than analysis failures; the mechanical regime is designed to eliminate exactly these
findings.setup_summary: The book enumerates the error set a trader becomes susceptible to when objectivity is lost: hesitating; jumping the gun; not predefining risk; defining risk but refusing to take the loss (letting it become a bigger loser); exiting a winning trade too soon; taking no profits from a winner; letting a winner turn into a loser; moving a stop closer to entry; getting stopped out then watching price revert; trading too large relative to equity.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Framework; no market thesis.
findings.risk_geometry: None. These are the failure modes the regime structurally prevents (predefined risk, rigid exits, no stop editing).
findings.quote: you become susceptible to committing all the typical trading errors (hesitating, jumping the gun, not predefining your risk, defining your risk but refusing to take the loss and letting the trade turn into a bigger loser, getting out of a winning trade too soon, not taking any profits out of a winning trade, letting a winning trade turn into a loser, moving a stop closer to your entry point...)
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch11 / Objectivity and the error list
findings.notes: Useful as a V8 design checklist: frozen risk_geometry, deterministic admission, STOP_FIRST fills, and the heat cap structurally preclude the stop-moving, hesitation, refusal-to-take-loss, and oversized-position modes. 'Getting stopped out then watching price revert' argues for dead-thesis vs stop being distinct exits.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Edge decay: no static variable set captures shifting market dynamics
findings.mechanism: The set of active participants and their beliefs changes continuously, so the underlying dynamics of market movement change; any rigid snapshot of variables decays in effectiveness
findings.setup_summary: A fixed set of market variables (a snapshot of a fluid system) may work well for an extended period, then its effectiveness diminishes as traders enter and leave with new ideas of high and low. Compensate by trading in bounded sample sizes that detect decay before an inordinate amount is lost, while keeping a consistent approach.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Framework; decay is detected by comparing successive sample blocks, not by market signal.
findings.risk_geometry: None.
findings.quote: No snapshot (rigid set of variables) can take these subtle changes into consideration. You can compensate for these subtle changes in the underlying dynamics of market movement and still maintain a consistent approach by trading in sample sizes.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch11 / Trading in Sample Sizes
findings.notes: Justifies V8's registry evolution (challenger + frozen-OOS, never in-place mutation) and the offline LEARNING_PROTOCOL gate: experts are non-stationary hypotheses whose effectiveness must be re-tested on successive frozen windows, especially across crypto regime shifts (e.g., funding-rate regimes).
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Trend definition: higher-highs/lower-lows series; longer timeframe dominates
findings.mechanism: A trending market is a series of higher highs and higher lows (up) or lower highs and lower lows (down); trend significance scales with timeframe, so the longer timeframe is the major trend and takes precedence
findings.setup_summary: Define the major trend structurally: series of higher highs and higher lows for an up-trend, series of lower highs and lower lows for a down-trend. Longer timeframe = more significant trend (daily trend beats 30-minute trend) and becomes a filter restricting lower-TF trades to the major trend direction.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The trend definition breaks when the series symmetry is violated (a higher-high series no longer makes a new higher high).
findings.risk_geometry: Feature input only; no entry/stop geometry.
findings.quote: A trending market is defined as a series of higher highs and higher lows for an up-trending market and a series of lower highs and lower lows for a downtrending market. The longer the time frame, the more significant the trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch11 / Time Frame (trend filter)
findings.notes: Candidate feature for the trend feature group: a structural HH/HL-series flag over a lookback window, usable as a regime filter or as the trend requirement for trend_pullback/failed_breakout. In 24/7 crypto the series definition is unambiguous (no daily gaps to reset the structure).
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

book_title: Trading in the Zone: Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude (Part 2)
Trading in the Zone: Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline, and a Winning Attitude (Mark Douglas, 2000) — Part 1

findings.strategy_name: Predefine risk before entry
findings.mechanism: unknown outcomes make risk quantification a mandatory precondition for entry; only consistent winners define risk in advance
findings.setup_summary: Before any entry, the stop distance (invalidation price) and the money the trader is willing to spend to find out if the trade works are fixed in advance; entry happens only with this predefinition in place. Claim: traders who predefine risk before entry are the consistent winners, and 'not predefining your risk' is one of the three most common and costliest trading errors; a stop placed in the market is not the same as accepting the risk.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Violated whenever a position is opened without a predefined stop/risk level; the rule is the requirement itself, not a price condition, so any stopless entry invalidates the episode.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: any, but only with a pre-set stop (price level where the edge is considered dead) and a defined max-loss 'spend to find out' amount decided before entry; loss framed as cost of doing business.
findings.quote: only the consistent winners define their risk in advance of putting on a trade
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 2, 'The Safeguards'; reinforced Ch 6 'The Uncertainty Principle'
findings.notes: Unlike blackjack, no exchange rule forces a trader to stake his risk, so risk predefinition must be structural. Maps directly to V8 RiskGate deterministic admission and the risk_geometry {entry, stop, target, expiry} contract.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Preplanned systematic profit-taking
findings.mechanism: a profit exit decided in advance prevents a winning trade from silently reversing into a loser
findings.setup_summary: For every entry the trader fixes in advance the price/point at which profits will be taken, so a winner can never turn into a loser and 'leaving money on the table' is a managed variable. Claim: not having an organized, systematic money-management regimen for taking profits is one of the three most common and costliest trading errors.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Violated when an open winning position is held with no pre-set target or the target is moved to chase the move.
findings.risk_geometry: Target: fixed price/R-multiple known in advance ('in most cases I know for sure at what point I am going to take my profits'); this is V8's target_r.
findings.quote: Why would you ever let a winning trade turn into a loser, or not have a systematic way of taking profits, if you weren't convinced the market was going your way indefinitely?
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, 'Eliminating the Emotional Risk'
findings.notes: Encodes as target_r in V8 risk_geometry; profit exit must be rule-based (pre-set level), not discretionary, which is exactly the frozen-ref style of the existing experts.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Cut losses on thesis invalidation, not on P&L
findings.mechanism: a standing stop alone is not acceptance; the exit must fire when the market invalidates the trade's premise, independent of current P&L
findings.setup_summary: Exit without hesitation whenever the market shows the trade's premise is not working, regardless of entry P&L. Bob CTA anecdote: he placed a stop but bailed at entry when the market ticked against him, then watched the trade run 500 points — the book's point being that a stop in the market is not the same as accepting the risk. Claim: 'cut losses without reservation or hesitation when the market tells them the trade isn't working' is a defining trait of consistent winners.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis is dead when the invalidation condition fires; the error is holding past invalidation while hoping, which the book calls a passive-loser failure mode.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop and dead-thesis are distinct exits: stop is risk geometry (max loss level), dead-thesis (still_valid) is the conditional premise failure; both must be executable without hesitation.
findings.quote: only the best traders cut their losses without reservation or hesitation when the market tells them the trade isn't working
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6, 'The Uncertainty Principle'; Bob CTA journal entry in Ch 7 'Trading in the Moment'
findings.notes: V8 already separates stops from still_valid (dead-thesis) exits; this corroborates that design and adds the human-failure rationale — inside a losing trade the counter-trend is perceptually invisible ('The trend doesn't disappear from physical reality, but our ability to perceive it does', Ch 7), so the exit must be deterministic.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Take every edge signal (casino model)
findings.mechanism: consistent results come from sample size over a fixed edge, never from picking which edges will win
findings.setup_summary: Define an edge as a fixed behavior pattern with a higher probability of one direction; then take every trade that conforms to the edge and never skip or favor edges based on hunches about the next outcome. Two-layer belief: at the micro level each trade is random/statistically independent; at the macro level a large sample converges to the edge's expectancy (casino blackjack 4.5%-edge analogy).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Falsifiable claim: for a fixed edge definition, wins/losses are randomly distributed (no serial dependence in the sequence) and realized outcome converges to expectancy as sample size grows — directly testable in the V8 lab.
findings.risk_geometry: Per-trade risk still predefined (see NEW_predefined_risk); position size constant across edges; every trigger fires an entry.
findings.quote: They have found that by taking every edge, they correspondingly increase their sample size of trades, which in turn gives whatever edge they use ample opportunity to play itself out in their favor, just like the casinos.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, 'Trading in the Moment'; Ch 7 'Probabilities Paradox'
findings.notes: Includes the 'rigid in our rules and flexible in our expectations' paradox (Ch 7 'Eliminating the Emotional Risk'): rules frozen, expected outcome open. This is the epistemic contract behind V8's lab — every trigger produces a CandidateDraft, no discretionary filtering.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: No out-of-parameter information in trade selection
findings.mechanism: adding extra variables to the entry decision corrupts the edge definition and destroys the ability to know what works
findings.setup_summary: The only evidence used to decide whether to take a trade is whether the edge's defining variables are present; gathering 'other' evidence (indicators, friends' opinions, broker tips) adds random variables and makes it impossible to determine what works. The book ties this to traders who plan trades, skip them, and instead act on tips — i.e., unstructured random trading that escapes responsibility.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Violated whenever an Expert's decision path consumes information outside its frozen feature groups.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a — decision hygiene, not entry geometry.
findings.quote: When you use "other" information, outside the parameters of your edge to decide whether you will take the trade, you are adding random variables to your trading regime.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8, 'How the Fundamental Truths Relate to the Skills' (Truth 4)
findings.notes: Directly maps to V8's frozen feature-group spec and the MarketState consumption contract: parameter/threshold changes are VARIANTS of one family, not new discretionary signal sources.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Outcome recency bias: sizing and risk perception invariant to the last few trades
findings.mechanism: the last 2-3 outcomes distort perceived risk — overconfidence after wins drives oversizing and rule violation (euphoria), fear after losses drives hesitation — producing boom-bust equity
findings.setup_summary: A typical trader's perceived risk in any situation is a function of the outcome of his most recent two or three trades: after a win streak he sizes up ('loading up'), stops perceiving risk, and violates rules; after losses he hesitates and skips valid signals. Claim: consistent winners' risk perception and position size are unaffected by recent outcomes; boom-bust cycles end in huge losses caused by euphoria or self-sabotage after winning streaks.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Violated when position size or risk tolerance varies with recent P&L; the guard is fixed sizing independent of the outcome sequence.
findings.risk_geometry: Position size fixed by pre-defined risk per trade, not by confidence; heat cap and one-exposure-per-(instrument,direction) make euphoria-driven sizing structurally impossible.
findings.quote: It's when you're winning that you are most susceptible to making a mistake, overtrading, putting on too large a position, violating your rules
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3, 'Winners, Losers, Boomers, and Busters'; Ch 6 opening
findings.notes: Human emotion is absent in V8 automation, but the same failure can enter through sizing rules conditioned on rolling performance or promotion decisions made after hot streaks; the guard is outcome-invariant risk sizing. The book's 'every loss puts you that much closer to a win' is a psychological reframe that contradicts its own statistical-independence claim — do not encode it as a regime filter or edge modifier.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Entry only on the confirmed signal (no jumping the gun)
findings.mechanism: fear of missing out causes entries before the signal has manifested (jumping the gun); fear of loss causes hesitating past valid signals — both destroy consistency
findings.setup_summary: Enter only when the edge's defining signal has actually manifested in the market, and take every manifestation; anticipating a signal that has not yet formed is evidence the trader is convinced he will miss out. The book lists getting in too early/too late, hesitating at signals, and moving stops closer to entry only to get stopped out as self-generated errors, not market-generated errors.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Violated when an episode enters before the frozen trigger condition (e.g., before bar close) or when a valid trigger is skipped.
findings.risk_geometry: V8 encoding: entry at NEXT_BAR_CLOSE on a frozen trigger; no anticipatory limit orders; the trigger definition itself is the only guard against anticipation.
findings.quote: How could you anticipate a signal that hasn't yet manifested itself in the market, if you weren't convinced that you were going to miss out?
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, 'Eliminating the Emotional Risk'
findings.notes: In 24/7 perp markets there is no session boundary to anchor anticipation, so the bar-close/confirmation semantics of the trigger are the only guard. Encodes as V8's frozen trigger plus NEXT_BAR_CLOSE entry model.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: More analysis is not the path to consistency (black hole of analysis)
findings.mechanism: accumulating more market variables to eliminate risk increases, not decreases, inconsistency, and learning-for-revenge blocks opportunity perception
findings.setup_summary: Trying to eliminate risk by learning about as many market variables as possible is called the 'black hole of analysis'; market analysis does not solve problems of confidence, discipline, or focus. Claim: traders who react to losses by adding analytical tools get worse — the more they learn, the more they expect from the market and the more painful its failure to comply becomes, until consistency is lost.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The lesson is falsified if expanding the variable set on a fixed strategy improves frozen-OOS results — a testable proposition V8 can run.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a — research-program discipline.
findings.quote: market analysis is not the path to consistent results. It will not solve the trading problems created by lack of confidence, lack of discipline, or improper focus.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 1, 'The Shift to Mental Analysis'; Ch 3 'Reacting to Loss'
findings.notes: Supports V8 complexity budget (rule 14: max 3 active experts) and the challenger-variant workflow: refinements are challenger experts on frozen OOS, never in-place variable accumulation.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Collective behavior patterns repeat with statistical reliability (basis for edges)
findings.mechanism: a finite group of traders repeats behavior patterns; groups interacting consistently form collective patterns that are observable, quantifiable, and statistically reliable, giving a pattern-based edge its probability
findings.setup_summary: Edges exist because individuals and groups of traders form behavior patterns that repeat with statistical reliability and occur in every timeframe, so technical analysis can organize collective behavior into patterns that indicate a higher probability of one direction over another. This is the epistemic justification for defining an edge as repeatable pattern + direction, testable via out-of-sample frequency.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Falsifiable: if a candidate pattern's OOS frequency no longer exceeds its base rate, the edge is dead.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a — foundation for edge definition.
findings.quote: These behavior patterns are observable and quantifiable, and they repeat themselves with statistical reliability.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 1, 'The Shift to Technical Analysis'
findings.notes: Asserted without data in the book; V8's lab is the vehicle to test whether any specific pattern repeats OOS. Crypto caveat: participant mix and microstructure (leverage, funding, 24/7) change faster than the equity/futures population the book describes, so pattern stability is an empirical question, not an assumption.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: One trader can negate any edge; hidden variables make every outcome uncertain
findings.mechanism: price is the balance/imbalance of buyers vs sellers, so any unseen trader entering, exiting, or changing size can alter an edge's outcome, making every trade statistically independent and probabilistic
findings.setup_summary: All price movement is a function of what individual traders believe is high vs low; a constant unknown set of hidden variables (sidelined traders, position changes, exit intent) means no single trade's outcome is knowable regardless of pattern quality. Claim: 'it takes only one other trader, anywhere in the world, to negate the positive potential of your trade'; hence no setup is ever exempt from risk predefinition.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a — an epistemic constraint: because no edge can be treated as certain, every setup must carry predefined risk and a defined end.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a — implies risk rules are mandatory regardless of setup quality.
findings.quote: it takes only one other trader, anywhere in the world, to negate the positive potential of your trade
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6, 'The Uncertainty Principle'; Ch 6 'Markets Most Fundamental Characteristic'
findings.notes: Crypto perp amplification: whales, high leverage, no position limits, 24/7 — the 'one trader' force is stronger and faster. Supports V8's probabilistic-expert ontology (expert = falsifiable hypothesis, never a promise).
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Projected support/resistance levels are fragile; one large order can break any level
findings.mechanism: a single large market order can negate any projected level, so level-based invalidation must always be paired with predefined risk rather than trusted as a boundary
findings.setup_summary: Anchored by the soybean anecdote: an analyst projected 'support = low of the day' using the point-and-line method, and a 40-year floor veteran selling 2 million bushels at market broke the level in 30 seconds. Claim: from an individual observer's perspective 'anything can happen, and it takes only one trader to do it'; levels are expressions of belief, not boundaries, and any trader can change them.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a — a risk framing: never rely on a level holding as the sole protection; when a level breaks, the dead-thesis trigger fires and the predefined stop is honored.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop placement: levels are fragile anchors for entries, not guarantees; risk predefinition (NEW_predefined_risk) is the protection, and a level break is a dead-thesis trigger, not an 'impossible' event.
findings.quote: anything can happen, and it takes only one trader to do it
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6, 'The Uncertainty Principle' (soybean support/resistance anecdote)
findings.notes: Related to stop_hunt and liquidity-sweep dynamics: in perp crypto, obvious levels concentrate stop liquidity and leverage cascades break them mechanically. This is the supporting rationale for V8's liquidity_sweep_reclaim (wick through a windowed prior extreme) and for never treating a frozen level as guaranteed.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Self-imposed trade end (expiry/time stop) because the market has no formal ending
findings.mechanism: with no formal market ending, an unfixed trade is a passive loser — the exit must be self-imposed or the market will take everything
findings.setup_summary: Unlike games (blackjack) that force an ending, the market never takes a trader out of a trade: nothing begins, lasts, or ends except by the trader's own decision. Claim: without a self-imposed end — stop, target, or expiry — a losing trade is a passive loser that can consume everything, and 'once you're in a losing trade, you don't have to do anything to keep on losing.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: An episode is invalid if it can run without a defined end condition; every open episode must carry a stop, a target, or an expiry.
findings.risk_geometry: expiry_bars, stop, and target all live in risk_geometry; the trade ends when the first defined condition fires (stop/target/expiry).
findings.quote: Trading has no formal ending. The market will not take you out of a trade. Unless you have the appropriate mental structure to end a trade in a manner that is always in your best interest, you can become a passive loser.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 2, 'The Safeguards'
findings.notes: Directly maps to V8's expiry_bars and STOP_FIRST simulator semantics. In 24/7 perp crypto (no session close) the passive-loser failure mode is amplified: funding and leverage keep bleeding an undefended position, so a time-based end is mandatory, not optional.
findings.book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

findings.strategy_name: Carry trade on interest-rate differential
findings.mechanism: Long the high-yield currency / short the low-yield funding currency to capture the interest-rate spread; trade only while realized volatility is low and the rate differential is wide
findings.setup_summary: On a perp, identify the funding-rate analogue of the interest differential: when the (annualized) funding rate is persistently positive AND realized volatility is low, hold a SHORT perp to harvest positive funding while price stays range-bound; the book's formulation is 'identify a currency pair with a broad interest rate differential and low volatility, sit back, and start collecting interest.' Falsifiable: positive expectancy = funding accrual minus adverse price drift over the hold window, gated on a low-volatility regime.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: wide rate/funding differential + low volatility. Invalidation: sudden volatility spike or differential narrowing forces unwind; risk-appetite collapse causes a violent short squeeze in the funding leg (documented yen +25% in 2007-08).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: time-based (hold to accrue funding/interest), no price trigger; stop: volatility spike or differential narrowing (e.g., funding flips sign); target: accrual over horizon; expiry: funding normalizes. Exit discipline is regime-triggered, not price-triggered.
findings.quote: the carry trade has become one of the most reliable trades in forex... the carry trade tends to thrive when volatility is low and to shrink during crises when uncertainty is high.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.7 'Carry Trade' pp.181-183; Ch.5 'Interest Rate Analysis' pp.96-98
findings.notes: On USDM perps the interest differential is replaced by the funding rate paid between longs and shorts, so the trade is short-perp-when-funding-positive / long-perp-when-funding-negative. Book documents empirical carry returns Aug 2007-Jan 2012 (Figure 7-7) and the yen carry unwind (+25% in the funding leg). DATA_BLOCKED until funding-rate tape exists; this is the V8 'funding_carry' backlog family.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Bollinger-band squeeze breakout with band expansion
findings.mechanism: Tight consolidation compresses volatility; a close through the band with band expansion signals a momentum continuation in the direction of the breach
findings.setup_summary: After a multi-week range with tight recent consolidation (narrow Bollinger bandwidth / low ATR percentile), enter LONG on a bar close above the upper band accompanied by band widening, SHORT on a close below the lower band; 'the steeper the expansion of the band, the stronger the trend.' Book's USD/CAD example: 5 weeks range-bound, tight consolidation, pierce of upper Bollinger = breakout trigger; a volume surge on the break confirms (breakouts 'accompanied by a widening of the band... underscoring the momentum').
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close outside band after compression + band expansion + volume surge. Invalidation: close returns inside the band (false breakout) or band fails to expand; book notes the breakout often begins before bands react (lagging).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar-close after band breach; stop: band midline or recent swing extreme (book example used a hard stop above prior resistance to cap loss at 50 PIPs); target: extension or ride until CCI/MACD cross zero-line (partial exit); expiry ~1 week in book example.
findings.quote: Bollinger bands, then, are especially useful for forecasting breakouts. In general, the steeper the expansion of the band, the stronger the trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'Moving Average Envelopes and Bollinger Bands' pp.151-154; Ch.7 pp.172-173
findings.notes: 24/7 market with no gaps removes the overnight-gap failure mode of squeeze breakouts; high leverage rewards the low-risk entry. Distinct from the backlogged breakout_retest (which requires location/prior-high refs); this family keys on volatility compression + band expansion.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Mechanical MA-cross trend system with momentum confirmation (5x5)
findings.mechanism: Trend initiation is signaled by short MA crossing long MA; confirmation from an oscillator on the same side of its midline; trade until the opposite signal
findings.setup_summary: Fully rule-based and backtestable: 'a so-called 5 x 5 system will generate a buy signal when the close price is above a specified simple moving average (SMA) and the Relative Strength Index (RSI) is above the mid-line 50. A sell signal will be generated when the close price is below the SMA and the RSI is below the mid-line 50.' Book also documents a 5-day/20-day MA cross + MACD variant that held a 1,000-PIP short for 2 months on EUR/USD.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close-side of SMA + RSI-side agreement (or MA cross). Invalidation: whipsaw back across the cross (book shows the rule produced two false signals and missed a 1,000-PIP counter-move); entry after the move has already happened (MA is a following indicator).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: next bar after confirmed cross; exit: opposite cross (system held until reversal signal, no fixed expiry); stop: MA on the opposite side or ATR multiple; target: none (ride until opposite signal) - book warns simple MA rules' edge decayed by early 1990s in liquid majors.
findings.quote: When the 5-day moving average crosses the 20-day average, it heralds a trend reversal... I will enter a position upon the next trend reversal and close it out after the following trend reversal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'Moving Averages' pp.148-151; Ch.7 'Purely Technical Strategy' pp.169-174
findings.notes: Directly expressible as a V8 Expert consuming ema/sma features. The book itself cites Neely & Weller (Fed 2011) that simple MA/filter rules became unprofitable in liquid FX by the early 1990s - this is the key falsification risk to register; treat as a screening candidate, not a default edge.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Extreme positioning contrarian (squeeze fuel)
findings.mechanism: When speculative positioning reaches an extreme against the prevailing price trend, the market is squeezed upon any reversal, amplifying the move
findings.setup_summary: When a positioning proxy reaches an extreme (book: COT short positions at extreme as EUR/USD bottomed June 2010), buy the reversal on trend-confirmation (MA cross), expecting a short squeeze 'potentially catapulting the euro upward by hundreds of PIPs in only a few days.' Related OI signal: NZD's sustained 2011 rise was preceded by OI bottoming.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: extreme positioning (e.g., >2 std dev from its distribution) + price begins reversing. Invalidation: positioning keeps extending with the trend (no reversal); COT/OI is a lagging snapshot, so entry must be confirmed by price action.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar close after reversal confirmation (book used MA crossover as confirmation); stop: beyond the extreme level; target: squeeze extension measured in hundreds of PIPs over days; expiry: a few days to weeks.
findings.quote: the Commitments of Traders data showed that short positions had reached an extreme level. This development alone would be reason enough to buy the euro, since once an uptrend started, it would cause a short squeeze.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.7 'Technical & Fundamental Trend Trading' pp.177-178; Ch.6 'Volume and Open Interest' p.139
findings.notes: No COT exists for crypto perps; the analogues are exchange funding-rate percentiles, open interest, and long/short account ratios (data partially available). Mechanism (crowded-position reversal) is a plausible expert family but DATA_BLOCKED until positioning history is captured in the tape.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Order-flow informativeness (inventory-control / hot-potato microstructure)
findings.mechanism: Completed order flow carries information independent of the news behind it; dealer inventory balancing and large directional client orders move short-term price
findings.setup_summary: Aggregated aggressive (taker) buy minus sell flow over a lookback window is a feature with predictive drift beyond bar direction: 'order flow is itself informative.' Book describes three channels: inventory control effect (dealer adjusts spread to shed unwanted inventory), hot potato effect (unwanted position passed around, price bid up/down repeatedly), and asymmetric information effect (large directional client order read as informed, dealer widens).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Feature, not a standalone entry: signal = sustained flow imbalance in one direction; invalidates when flow flips or price diverges from flow (absorption).
findings.risk_geometry: Feature input only; no entry/stop geometry in the book - it is an informational feature to stack with price-based entries.
findings.quote: Market microstructure analyses have found that order flow is an important variable in exchange rate determination in that it is unique from the information that underlies it. In other words, the order flow is itself informative.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Market Microstructure Analysis' p.77
findings.notes: Book cites empirical microstructure findings (dealer flow as short-term price driver). On perp venues taker-flow imbalance is observable in aggTrades, but V8's canonical 1h OHLCV tape has no order-level data - so this lands as a feature-group proposal (aggregated taker-flow imbalance per bar) contingent on tape extension, not an executable expert now.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Scheduled-news overshoot and pre-release breakout straddle
findings.mechanism: Markets overshoot around scheduled data: expectations are pre-positioned before the release, the print triggers a sharp move, then reaction reverses if the data disappointed relative to consensus
findings.setup_summary: Around a high-impact scheduled release, price consolidates in the hours before; place OCO buy-stop above and sell-stop below the consolidation channel so the breakout direction triggers automatically ('One-Cancels-Other... if the breakout is to the upside, then the buy order will be triggered and the sell order will be cancelled'). Separately, 'buy the rumor, sell the news': fade the extension once the print is in line with (or beats) expectations - a 100-PIP USD rally on a beat reversed within the same day. The book's EUR/USD employment-data example had a 50-PIP pre-release buildup.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: scheduled event + tight consolidation channel. Invalidation: false breakout when bands are set too close (book's own example was stopped by one); a data print exactly matching consensus produces no overshoot.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: OCO stop orders at channel boundaries (or market on release); stop: opposite channel side or beyond the channel; target: 50-100 PIPs in book examples; expiry: same session - event volatility decays within hours.
findings.quote: With both types of news, the market has a propensity to overshoot, hence the expression, 'Buy the rumor, sell the news.'
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'News' pp.81-82; Ch.7 'Trading the News' pp.185-188
findings.notes: BTCUSDT reacts sharply to scheduled macro releases (CPI, FOMC, NFP) even in a 24/7 market. Requires an economic-calendar feature (time group) not currently in the frozen spec. The OCO-straddle variant is concretely expressible as a lifecycle/entry rule once event timestamps exist.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Volatility-led risk-on/risk-off regime filter
findings.mechanism: Volatility spikes precede risk aversion; capital rotates out of risk assets into safe havens, so volatility regime leads directional bias across risk-sensitive assets
findings.setup_summary: When realized (or implied) volatility spikes, treat the regime as risk-off: reduce long-risk exposure and expect flight-to-quality; 'rising/spiking (falling) volatility in the forex markets often precedes an appreciation (depreciation) in the Japanese yen.' Book documents risk-on/risk-off rotations (2008 credit crisis flight to yen/franc/dollar; 2010-11 EUR/USD trading as a risk proxy with S&P 500 moves often preceding, not mirroring, EUR/USD).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Regime feature: RISK_OFF when volatility crosses up a threshold; invalidates when vol mean-reverts without regime change (false alarm - 2011 example: post-earthquake vol spike was followed by intervention, not a persistent risk-off).
findings.risk_geometry: Filter/gate only - modulates exposure and which families are admissible, not an entry geometry.
findings.quote: rising/spiking (falling) volatility in the forex markets often precedes an appreciation (depreciation) in the Japanese yen.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Risk-Driven Trading' pp.84-85; Ch.5 'Sentiment Analysis' pp.115-119
findings.notes: For BTCUSDT there is no intra-market safe haven, but the vol-spike-to-risk-off mapping is usable as a regime gate (equity vol / crypto vol spike precedes deleveraging). Aligns with V8's regime concept: gate admissions by volatility regime rather than by instrument identity.
