findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Session pivot-point support/resistance
findings.mechanism: The prior session's high/low/close average defines objective price levels where the next session's price tends to meet support/resistance; objective calculation makes levels self-fulfilling
findings.setup_summary: Compute pivot = (prior period H + L + C)/3 and three derived support/resistance levels; in the following session fade touches of S1/R1/S2/R2 in a ranging regime (book shows USD/CHF meeting resistance exactly at Support-2); a clean pass through all levels signals unusually strong sentiment - trade with, not against, the break.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: touch of a pivot-derived level. Invalidation: clean close through the level set (trend day) - the book frames level breaks as strong-sentiment signals, so the level trade must be abandoned on a decisive breach.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit at the pivot level; stop: beyond the level; target: next pivot level; expiry: end of the trading session - levels are session-scoped.
findings.quote: A pivot point is simply the average of a currency pair's high, low, and closing prices for a given period of time (typically one 24-hour trading session)... since pivot points are calculated objectively, they will appear the same on all charts and may thus become self-fulfilling.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'Pivot Points' pp.143-144
findings.notes: 24/7 crypto has no natural session boundary; requires a fixed rolling window (e.g., 00:00 UTC or 08:00 UTC daily) to define H/L/C. Self-fulfilling-objectivity argument applies equally to BTC (daily pivots are widely published). Candidate behavior family within a location-based reversal mechanism.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Psychological round-number support/resistance
findings.mechanism: Order clustering and human anchoring at round numbers create self-fulfilling support/resistance; the rounder the level, the stronger the barrier
findings.setup_summary: Price tends to stall or bounce at round price levels ('the rounder the better' - for USD/JPY, 80 is more important than 79, which is more important than 78.5). The level's validity is 'confirmed when rates (repeatedly) bounce off of them upon contact.' Falsifiable as a location feature: proximity of price to the nearest psychological round level, and distance since last clean break.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Feature/setup: approach to a round level with prior bounces. Invalidation: clean momentum break through the level - after a decisive break the level flips role (support becomes resistance).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: at the round level on reaction (or breakout on clean break); stop: beyond the round level; target: next psychological level or prior swing; expiry: not specified in book.
findings.quote: perhaps it's because such levels tend to take place at round numbers - the rounder the better!... That's because humans tend to think in terms of round numbers and develop their forecasts accordingly.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Technical Factors' pp.79-80; Ch.6 'Trend Analysis' pp.140-141
findings.notes: Directly applicable: BTC at 100k/90k/50k and ETH at 3k/4k are heavily watched anchors on perp venues. Land as a location feature (distance to round level) rather than a standalone expert - it is a level-defining input for any location-based family.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Trailing stop for trend protection
findings.mechanism: A stop that ratchets with the favorable extreme lets a winner run while capping giveback: position is closed only if price retraces the trailing distance from its best level
findings.setup_summary: Exit rule: after entry, place a stop trailing N units (book: 100 PIPs) behind the favorable extreme; if USD/BRL falls to 1.84 then rises to 1.85, the position closes at 1.85; if it continues to 1.80 the stop ratchets to 1.81 - 'keep your position open as long as possible (maximizing gains) while continuing to protect yourself from any downside.' Combined with a protective buy-stop above resistance to cap losses (50 PIPs) if the counter-move never comes.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Exit rule, not an entry: always active once in position; the trade-off is stop distance vs. false-exit frequency - tighter stops exit on noise (the book's USD/BRL example set the stop beyond the resistance level to 'give yourself some margin for error').
findings.risk_geometry: Stop: trailing distance from extreme (100 PIPs in book, ~1 ATR in perp terms); target: none (trend rides); expiry: none - exit is purely price-triggered; STOP_FIRST semantics apply.
findings.quote: you can make use of a trailing stop order, which will automatically close your position if the USD/BRL retraces more than a given amount... you can keep your position open as long as possible (maximizing gains) while continuing to protect yourself from any downside.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.7 'Technical & Fundamental Trend Trading' pp.179-180
findings.notes: Trailing stop is directly implementable in V8's lifecycle exits as a ratcheting stop distinct from dead-thesis (still_valid) exits; book's own caveat is that stop distance must exceed noise (use ATR-scaled trailing). Note: the same chapter endorses scaling into losing positions (dollar-cost averaging) for long-horizon trades - that practice conflicts with V8 RiskGate/heat discipline and is NOT adopted.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Inverse-correlation cross-pair hedge
findings.mechanism: Pairing a directional position with an inversely correlated instrument reduces combined variance; the hedge pays off precisely when the primary thesis fails
findings.setup_summary: Book's 'advanced strategy': long AUD/USD hedged with a JPY/EUR position chosen from a correlation matrix (weekly inverse correlation -50.9%); 'while the performance of the AUD/USD and JPY/EUR have varied since 2007, their combined return has always been positive' - i.e., the combination had lower drawdown and still-positive cumulative return across the credit crisis. The book stresses causation vs. correlation: only causation (not mere co-movement) is actionable, and correlations strengthened over time partly due to cross-asset algorithms and index flows.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Hedge thesis invalidates when the rolling correlation breaks down or flips sign (book notes EM currency correlations broke down in H2 2010 as growth/inflation differentials diverged); a stale correlation matrix is dangerous.
findings.risk_geometry: Hedge sizing, not an entry setup: leg sizes chosen so combined exposure is net-neutral on the shared risk factor; no expiry in the book beyond periodic re-correlation checks.
findings.quote: the two pairs exhibited an inverse (weekly) correlation coefficient of 50.9%... their combined return has always been positive. Behold, the perfect trade!
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 'Market Correlations' pp.120-124; Ch.7 'Advanced Strategy' pp.184-185
findings.notes: V8 trades a single instrument (BTCUSDT 1h), so an instrument-pair hedge is out of scope; the transferable lesson is methodology - validate rolling correlation before relying on any correlated/hedged construction, and treat 'correlation is not causation' as a hard rule for any cross-market feature.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Parabolic SAR stop-and-reverse (documented negative result)
findings.mechanism: The claimed mechanism is that trends need rapid momentum accumulation; the Parabolic SAR predicts trend starts/ends via dots, but the book's own worked chart shows it was wrong more often than right
findings.setup_summary: Rejected method: a stop-and-reverse dot signal used to time trend entry/exit. The book applies it to EUR/USD and reports 'the Parabolic SAR was ultimately more often wrong than it was right!', even advising a 3-dot (3-period) delay to build in margin of error. Companion rejection: Elliott Wave Principle, whose waves Fibonacci levels claim to predict, has 'no evidence of it in financial markets' per the economists the book cites.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - method rejected on the book's own evidence; a stop-and-reverse on every signal change would churn through 7 'trends' in one chart window, most of them false.
findings.risk_geometry: None adopted; the book's example shows both entries and stops whipsawed.
findings.quote: If only it were that simple... the Parabolic SAR was ultimately more often wrong than it was right!
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'Parabolic Stop and Reverse' pp.154-155; 'Elliot Wave Principle' pp.144-147
findings.notes: Registered as a rejected option for the V8 registry: a documented practitioner negative result on a stop-and-reverse indicator. Useful as a falsification record - the book itself provides a chart-based counterexample, which is exactly the kind of negative evidence V8 should log before any trend-exhaustion family is proposed.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

book_title: Forex for Beginners: A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets (2012) — Part 1
Way of the Turtle: The Secret Methods That Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders (2007) — Part 2

findings.strategy_name: Turtle System 2 — 55-day Donchian channel breakout
findings.setup_summary: On daily bars, when price trades a single tick above the highest high of the prior 55 sessions, buy 1 unit; when it trades a tick below the lowest low of the prior 55 sessions, sell 1 unit. Entry is executed intraday at the breakout tick (not at the close); if the market gaps through the breakout level, enter at the open. All 55-day breakouts are taken regardless of the prior breakout's result.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Valid while price continues through the channel extreme; thesis invalidated when the System 2 exit (20-day low for longs / 20-day high for shorts) trades through.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: intraday touch (limit) or gap-open. Stop: 2N (2% equity risk). Target: none fixed — held via trailing 20-day channel exit. No expiry.
findings.quote: We entered when the price exceeded by a single tick the high or low of the preceding 55 days. All breakouts for System 2 would be taken whether or not the previous breakout had been a winner.
findings.chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'System 2 Entry', pp. 260-261
findings.notes: Canonical, falsifiable trend-following entry; 24/7 perp market removes futures gap/open complexities and contract rolls, making the channel breakout directly executable on BTCUSDT. Entry-at-touch semantics conflict with V8's canonical fill-at-close simulator, so it needs an explicit fill rule (touch-fill or next-bar-open). Budget-gated: add as backlog family, challenger to trend_pullback via registry experiment on frozen OOS.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Turtle System 1 — 20-day breakout with post-winner skip + 55-day failsafe
findings.setup_summary: 20-day channel breakout entry, but the signal is skipped if the last breakout in that same market was a winner (a breakout counts as a loser if price moved 2N against the position before a profitable 10-day exit; direction of the prior breakout is irrelevant). If a System 1 signal is skipped because the prior trade won, the entry point becomes the 55-day breakout as a failsafe so major moves are not missed.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Entry is suppressed only when the prior breakout in that market was a winner; the 55-day failsafe level always remains as a valid backstop entry.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: intraday tick / gap-open. Stop: 2N. Exit: System 1 10-day low/high (all units). No fixed target.
findings.quote: System 1 breakout entry signals would be ignored if the last breakout would have resulted in a winning trade... this 55-day breakout was considered the failsafe breakout point.
findings.chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'System 1 Entry', pp. 259-260
findings.notes: Mechanism: filtering breakouts that follow a recent winner avoids the whipsaw of repeated breakout attempts, while the failsafe preserves trend capture. Concrete testable variant of donchian_breakout (structural entry-filter difference, not a threshold change, so a distinct family). 'Last breakout outcome' is also a candidate history-group feature. Directly implementable on BTC 1h/daily with continuous data.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Turtle unit pyramiding — add 1 unit per 1/2N favorable move
findings.setup_summary: After the initial 1-unit breakout entry, add 1 unit each time price moves 1/2N favorably from the prior fill price, up to the 4-unit per-market maximum; the add interval is measured from the actual fill, so slippage extends the next add distance. If the market moves fast enough, all 4 units can be added in a single day.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Adds stop at the max-unit cap for that market; each add raises all prior stops by 1/2N (see atr_stop finding).
findings.risk_geometry: Add interval: 1/2N from prior fill; whole-position stop trails 2N from the newest unit.
findings.quote: Turtles entered single-unit long positions at the breakouts and added to those positions at 1/2N intervals after their initial entry.
findings.chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Adding Units', pp. 260-261
findings.notes: Scaling speed is load-bearing: the book warns that adding units slowly (a 'conservative' delay) increases the chance a retracement hits the stops, inverting profitability — a falsifiable claim about build-out cadence inside an episode. Compatible with V8's one-exposure-per-direction rule (units scale within a single exposure). Perp fractional sizing makes 1/2N increments trivially executable; funding cost scales with the added exposure.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: N-based volatility-normalized unit sizing (1% equity per unit)
findings.setup_summary: Size 1 unit = 1% of account equity / (N x dollars-per-point), where N is the 20-day exponential moving average of true range (ATR). One unit therefore moves ~1% of equity per 1N, so a 2N stop risks exactly 2% of equity. This equalizes dollar risk across markets of different volatility, making diversified positions comparable bets. N and unit sizes were recomputed weekly.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — sizing rule, no entry thesis.
findings.risk_geometry: Volatility-derived unit size with fixed risk-per-unit (1%); stop distance 2N implies 2% per-trade risk.
findings.quote: The Turtles used a position sizing algorithm that was very advanced for its day because it normalized the dollar volatility of a position by adjusting the position size on the basis of the dollar volatility of the market.
findings.chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Position Sizing' and 'Volatility: The Meaning of N', pp. 251-255
findings.notes: With 25-125x perp leverage, %-equity volatility-normalized sizing is the critical control; V8's risk_geometry (atr_ref) can directly host this. The 'How much to buy or sell is the single most important aspect of trading' claim and the stated failure mode ('Most beginning traders risk far too much on each trade') are falsifiable design inputs for the RiskGate sizing rule.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Four-tier unit limits: single market / closely correlated / loosely correlated / direction
findings.setup_summary: Portfolio-level heat caps in units: max 4 units in a single market; max 6 units in one direction across closely correlated markets (e.g., crude + heating oil, gold + silver, the currencies as a group); max 10 units in one direction across loosely correlated markets (e.g., gold + copper); max 12 units total in one direction (long or short) across the whole book. Being 'loaded' = at the cap.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — portfolio risk limits.
findings.risk_geometry: Binds aggregate risk across correlated exposures; per the book, even with caps a single gap day (Oct 1987 rate cut) lost 40-60% of equity on a concentrated short book.
findings.quote: Closely correlated markets: ... a maximum of 6 units in one particular direction... The maximum number of total units in one direction long or short was 12 units.
findings.chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Units as a Measure of Risk', pp. 255-257
findings.notes: Direct design input for V8's heat cap, generalized from 'one exposure per direction' to correlated-exposure aggregation (BTC/ETH/majors are highly correlated; simultaneous 24/7 moves are the crypto analog of the 1987 gap). The Oct 1987 anecdote is a regime warning: caps bound but do not eliminate tail-day loss.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Notional-account de-scaling: reduce trading size 20% per 10% drawdown
findings.setup_summary: Trade against a notional account (size set yearly). Each time equity is down 10% from the original account size, reduce the notional by 20% (e.g., $1M down $100k -> trade as $800k; a further 10% off $800k -> $640k), until equity recovers to the yearly starting level. This shrinks position risk multiplicatively as drawdown deepens.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — equity-adaptive sizing rule.
findings.risk_geometry: All position sizes scaled by the reduced notional until recovery; asymmetric (de-scales fast, rescales via yearly reset).
findings.quote: The Turtles were instructed to decrease the size of the notional account by 20 percent each time we went down 10 percent of the original account.
findings.chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Adjusting Trading Size', pp. 257-258
findings.notes: Leverage magnifies drawdowns in perps; a deterministic, pre-committed de-scaling schedule (vs. discretionary cut) is exactly the kind of rule V8's RiskGate can encode. Book acknowledges 'other, perhaps better strategies' — treat as one candidate de-leverage schedule, not the optimum.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Turtle 2N stop with 1/2N unit-tightening; Whipsaw 1/2N-stop re-entry variant
findings.setup_summary: Initial stop is 2N from entry (2% equity risk). Each 1/2N add raises all earlier units' stops by 1/2N so the entire position sits 2N below the newest unit's fill. Stops are pre-defined and nonnegotiable: if price trades through, exit every time. Alternative 'Whipsaw' variant: stop at 1/2N (0.5% risk) and re-enter a stopped unit if price returns to the original entry price — more trades, lower win rate, better profitability.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Stop is a hard exit, not a thesis condition; Whipsaw explicitly re-enters after stop-out on return to entry price.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop: 2N below entry (long) / above entry (short), tightened per add; Whipsaw: 1/2N stop + re-entry at entry. No target (targets are exits, see trailing_stop).
findings.quote: Turtles' stops were set at 2N below the entry for long positions and 2N above the entry for short positions... [Whipsaw] the stops were placed at 1/2N for 1/2 percent account risk. If a particular unit was stopped out, the unit would be reentered if the market reached the original entry price.
findings.chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Turtle Stops' and 'Alternative Stop Strategy: The Whipsaw', pp. 262-266
findings.notes: N-scaled stop placement (volatility-adaptive, equalized risk) is a direct input to V8 risk_geometry. The book's caveat that moving-average systems carry an implicit stop, while explicit stops matter psychologically, maps to V8's separation of stop vs. dead-thesis exits. Whipsaw re-entry (stop then re-enter at entry) is a distinct, testable exit/re-entry behavior. Perp note: no overnight gap risk, but liquidation cascades can trade through stops fast.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Turtle channel exits: full position on 10-day (System 1) / 20-day (System 2) counter-breakout
findings.setup_summary: Exit the entire position when price makes a new N-day low (long) or high (short): 10-day for System 1, 20-day for System 2. Stops are not pre-placed with the broker; the trader watches and exits via limit/market order once the exit price trades through. Most breakout trades lose; profitability depends on a few large winners being held through 20-100% profit give-back.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Exit fires on the counter-channel breakout; theses-invalid and re-entry only on a fresh breakout.
findings.risk_geometry: No fixed target; exit trails at the N-day channel, requiring tolerance for giving back large unrealized profits.
findings.quote: The System 1 exit was a 10-day low for long positions and a 10-day high for short positions... The System 2 exit was a 20-day low for long positions and a 20-day high for short positions. All the units in the position would be exited if the price went against the position for a 20-day breakout.
findings.chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Turtle Exits', pp. 266-268
findings.notes: Trend-end exit by counter-channel breakout is a falsifiable alternative to V8's expiry_bars / still_valid dead-thesis exits; the documented concentration claim ('most of the profits... might come from only two or three large winning trades') is the evaluation-horizon lesson: per-trade stats are the wrong yardstick for such a family.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Buy strength, sell weakness within a correlated group
findings.setup_summary: When correlated markets signal simultaneously, take longs only in the strongest markets and shorts only in the weakest markets within the group, and enter only one unit per contract month. Strength measures: how many N price has advanced since breakout, or (price 3 months ago -> current price)/N, normalized across markets; the strongest group member almost always outperforms the rest to the long side, the weakest to the short side.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Selection applies at signal time; a chosen instrument is invalidated if its own breakout stop/exit fires.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: breakout entry in the selected strongest/weakest instrument; same 2N stops and channel exits per instrument.
findings.quote: If the signals came all at once, we always bought the strongest markets and sold short the weakest markets in a group... The strongest markets had the highest values; the weakest markets had the lowest.
findings.chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Buy Strength, Sell Weakness', pp. 271-272
findings.notes: Not executable as-is in V8 (single-instrument BTCUSDT), but a strong candidate cross_market selection rule if the program expands to alt perps, where BTC/ETH/major correlations and funding divergence make leg selection material. Also a methodology caution: take only the one strongest/weakest leg rather than both sides of a correlated group.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Limit-order bias and fast-market patience (execution tactics)
findings.setup_summary: Prefer limit orders over market orders: place the order at the lower end of the random quote 'bounce' for buys to get better fills and less slippage. In fast markets liquidity dries up, the spread widens, and market orders fill at the extreme of the move; the Turtles waited for some indication of at least a temporary reversal before entering, and exited via limit or market order once the market stabilized even if price had traded past the stop level. Stops were never placed with brokers (position concealment), only tracked as prices.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — execution methodology.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry/exit fill rules only; no stop, target, or expiry changes.
findings.quote: The idea behind using limit orders is to place your order at the lower end of the bounce instead of simply placing a market order... Market orders placed into a fast market usually end up getting filled at the highest price of the run-up, right at the point where the market begins to stabilize as new sellers come in.
findings.chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Tactics' and 'Fast Markets', pp. 268-270
findings.notes: V8's canonical simulator fills at close, so intra-bar bounce/limit execution is not modeled; this lesson informs slippage assumptions in the cost model and any live implementation (perp taker fees make limit fills a real cost edge). The fast-market reversal observation ('new sellers come in, price stabilizes and reverses') is a microstructure claim relevant to liquidation-cascade regimes.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Consistency and rule adherence as the alpha; concentration of yearly profits
findings.setup_summary: A mechanical system covering every decision (markets, sizing, entries, stops, exits, tactics) is followed exactly, because yearly profits concentrate in two or three large trades, so any skipped signal can materially change the year. Turtles with the best records consistently applied the entry rules; those fired or with the worst records failed to enter consistently or changed rules subtly (e.g., slowing unit adds), which inverted the intended effect. Conviction must be built by personally backtesting on historical data, not by others' summaries, so the trader keeps executing through multi-month losing stretches.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — execution/discipline methodology.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A.
findings.quote: Most of the profits in a particular year might come from only two or three large winning trades. If a signal was skipped or missed, this could have a great effect on the returns for the year... I always say that you could publish my trading rules in the newspaper and no one would follow them. The key is consistency and discipline.
findings.chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Consistency' and 'Finally', pp. 261-262, 273-274; 'Mastering Your Demons', pp. 224-233
findings.notes: For V8 this is a research-methodology lesson, not an expert: (1) evaluate families over long horizons because return concentration is extreme; (2) registry/runner must enforce exact rule execution — subtle discretionary 'conservative' tweaks (slower scaling) are a documented failure mode; (3) psychological 'faith' arguments must not be read as edge evidence. In 24/7 crypto, full automation removes the consistency problem mechanically.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Liquidity-first market selection; avoid illiquid instruments
findings.setup_summary: Trade only the most liquid markets: liquidity was the primary criterion for market selection because large positions in thin markets move price so much that entries and exits incur unacceptable losses. Trade a broad enough set to catch trends, but never trade illiquid markets or trade chosen markets inconsistently.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — market-selection rule.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A.
findings.quote: The Turtles traded only the most liquid markets. In fact, market liquidity was the primary criterion Richard Dennis used when determining which markets we were to trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Markets: What the Turtles Traded', pp. 249-250
findings.notes: For perps this is a venue/instrument filter: deep books (BTCUSDT) vs. thin alt perps where funding and liquidation cascades spike impact. V8 is pinned to BTCUSDT, so this is a scope-restriction justification and a caution if the program ever screens additional instruments.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

book_title: Forex for Beginners: A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets (2012) — Part 2 (Ch. 8-11)

findings.strategy_name: EMA crossover trading system (backtested)
findings.setup_summary: On a daily (or per-book 1h-analog) chart, when the fast EMA crosses above the slow EMA, initiate a long; when it crosses below, initiate a short; the book backtests this exact rule on EUR/CHF daily over 6 months and finds it net profitable but with negative Sharpe and risk-to-reward ratios, i.e. profit earned at excessive return variability.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The reverse EMA cross exits the position; the book's own backtest flags negative risk-adjusted return as the invalidation of the naive cross as-is.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at bar close on cross; no stop/target stated in the book (position held through opposite cross); book evaluates with risk-to-reward and Sharpe/Sortino.
findings.quote: each time the EMA crossed over the moving average, the computer initiated a hypothetical buy or sell order.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, Backtesting (EUR/CHF 6-month EMA crossover backtest)
findings.notes: The book's own backtest finding (net profit, negative Sharpe) is itself a falsifiable lesson for V8: naive cross entries on 1h BTCUSDT would whipsaw, and the value of this family is as a baseline competing with trend_pullback, not as an edge. Distinct behavior family (ema_cross) from the existing trend_pullback.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: One-Cancels-Other breakout bracket (direction-uncertain breakout)
findings.setup_summary: When you expect a breakout but not the direction, place a One-Cancels-Other bracket: a buy stop 30 PIPs above the current rate and a sell stop 30 PIPs below; whichever trigger fills first, the other cancels automatically (example: EUR/USD buy +30 or sell -30, whichever happens first).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Neither trigger fills before the order's expiry (one hour, one day, or GTC); after a fill, the thesis dies if price immediately returns through the reference range (failed breakout).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: stop-limit at +/-30 PIPs from current price; order expiry is set by the trader; protective stop on the triggered position placed by the trader (not specified by the book).
findings.quote: you could indicate a One-Cancels-Other order that either executes a buy if the EUR/USD rate increases 30 PIPs or executes a sell if it falls 30 PIPs, whatever happens first.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, Order Entry
findings.notes: Perps have native 24/7 stop-limit orders and no overnight gaps, so the OCO bracket is fully implementable on BTCUSDT 1h. In V8 this is a breakout behavior family over a windowed high/low reference range; V8 rule 16 (one exposure per direction) means the two bracket sides map to two separate candidate episodes rather than one dual-direction expert.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Rollover/carry on the interest-rate differential
findings.setup_summary: Holding a long position in the currency with the higher interest rate earns daily rollover credits; the book quantifies AUD/CAD long at +$7.84 per $100,000 lot/day (~2.9% annualized) and warns that EUR/TRY long bleeds -$58/day (~-21% annualized). Rollover is automatic and continuous (some brokers compute it every second), so it is a standing drag or tailwind on every held position.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Interest rate parity as the stated counter-thesis: 'a positive interest rate differential (i.e., rollover credit) should eventually be accompanied by currency depreciation' - the carry gain can be cancelled by spot depreciation.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop geometry given for carry; hold horizon is the key variable - rollover debits compound on multi-week/month positions.
findings.quote: Now you can understand why the carry trade is such a compelling force in the currency markets!
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, Rollover; Chapter 10, Interest Rate/Rollover Risk
findings.notes: Direct perp analog: funding rate. Long when funding is negative (receive funding) replicates rollover harvest; funding is observable on the derivatives tape. V8 data-blocked until funding history is ingested (same status as breakout_retest/capitulation). The book's IRP invalidation maps to a funding-vs-spot divergence check.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Scale out of losers, scale into winners (add-on-strength)
findings.setup_summary: Risk-management rule: scale out of losing trades and scale into positions that are in profit; Plan 3's behavior rule restates it as 'only add to profitable positions'. Claim: if the scaled position then declines, losses are smaller; if it continues rising, gains are larger.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Adding to a winner that reverses against the add; the rule explicitly prohibits adding to losing positions.
findings.risk_geometry: Adds only on profitable positions; stops maintained on the aggregate position; no R-multiple geometry stated by the book.
findings.quote: scaling out of losing trades and scaling into positions that are in the black
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, Currency Risk; Chapter 11, Table 11-3 (Plan 3 behavior rule)
findings.notes: Averaging-up discipline. In V8 this is a lifecycle rule governing when a candidate episode may be scaled (only on the winning side), living alongside ExposureBook; perps have no lot constraints, so scaling is mechanically trivial and the discipline constraint is what matters.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Fixed per-trade risk cap with R-multiple target (1% stop / 2% target)
findings.setup_summary: Size positions so a fixed stop distance implies a fixed dollar risk: 'if you don't want to lose more than $100 on a single trade and you seek a risk-to-reward ratio of 1% to 2%, then you shouldn't open a position greater than a $10,000 mini-lot.' Breakeven arithmetic: 1% stop / 2% target (1:2 R) is break-even at a 33% win rate; risking 2% instead of 5% per trade dampens the impact of loss streaks.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not applicable - a sizing identity; the 33%-win-rate-at-1:2-R:R breakeven is arithmetic, not an empirical claim.
findings.risk_geometry: stop_distance = 1% (or risk_dollars / notional), target = 2% (2R); the book's rule-of-thumb is R:R = 1:2 with a fixed fraction of account risked per trade.
findings.quote: if you set a stop-loss at 1% and take profits after 2%, you will come out ahead overall, as long as you experience winning trades 33% of the time.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, Risk Management
findings.notes: Directly implementable in V8 RiskGate deterministic admission: fixed fraction of equity risked per episode, stop distance in ATR, target as R-multiple. The book's 2% vs 5% comparison is the classic per-trade risk-cap parameter discussion.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Volatility-calibrated stop distance (stop outside normal noise)
findings.setup_summary: Set stop distance so it exceeds the pair's normal fluctuation range to avoid premature stop-outs: USD/CAD weekly volatility averaged ~100 PIPs (1%) and never exceeded 135 PIPs, so a 100-PIP stop sits inside ordinary noise and 'could automatically lead to your position being closed before the pair has a chance to rebound.' Same data used to gauge worst-case exposure of a planned hold (3-week hold ~= 200 PIPs of risk).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not applicable - calibration guideline; the rule is that stops inside the realized-vol range trigger on noise, not on thesis death.
findings.risk_geometry: stop_distance >= typical range for the hold horizon (e.g. >100 PIPs for USD/CAD at ~1% weekly vol); exposure budget = recent realized vol x hold-period factor.
findings.quote: a fluctuation in the USD/CAD of 100 PIPs would hardly be considered exceptional, and placing a stop-loss at this level could automatically lead to your position being closed before the pair has a chance to rebound.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, Volatility (Figure 10-2, USD/CAD volatility chart)
findings.notes: Validates V8's atr_ref convention (stop distance in ATR multiples) and the separation of stops from dead-thesis exits: a stop inside normal noise exits for the wrong reason. Especially relevant on perps where leverage exaggerates noise around the stop.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Fixed-distance trailing stop on the most recent extreme
findings.setup_summary: A trailing stop sits at a fixed distance below the most recent high (30 PIPs in the example): as price rises the trail ratchets up, superseding the original stop, and executes when price retraces to the trail level (e.g. entry 1.3469, stop trails to 1.3499 after price reaches 1.3519).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Breach of the trail level executes the stop (the intended exit); no other invalidation given.
findings.risk_geometry: trail_distance fixed (30 PIPs example); example also has take-profit +50 / initial stop -20 PIPs; the trail supersedes the original stop once triggered.
findings.quote: my trailing stop will automatically adjust to 30 PIPs below the most recent high, superseding my original stop order.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, Order Entry (Figure 9-7)
findings.notes: In V8 this is a lifecycle stop-update rule (parameterized variant of stop management), not a standalone strategy; ATR-scaled trail distance per V8 convention. 24/7 perps remove the overnight-gap hazard that trailing stops face in FX.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Move stop to breakeven once the position is in profit
findings.setup_summary: Behavior/risk rule from Plan 2: once a position's value is positive, move the stop-loss up to the entry price so the trade can no longer lose money (the cost is that the trade exits at breakeven on any retracement to entry).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Retracement to entry stops the position at breakeven - the intended, bounded cost of the rule.
findings.risk_geometry: stop moves from initial level to entry once position value >= 0; profit target unchanged.
findings.quote: Move stops to breakeven when position value is positive
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, Table 11-3 (Plan 2 risk management rule)
findings.notes: Trivial to implement on perps; V8 nuance - on perps 'breakeven' should be net of accrued funding (a position at entry price after funding debits is not at breakeven). Lifecycle stop-management variant in lifecycle.py.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Consecutive-loss daily stop (circuit breaker)
findings.setup_summary: For traders placing multiple trades per day: establish a mechanical rule that after 3 consecutive losing trades you quit for the day. The book generalizes this into contingency plans for 'a string of losses or a large decline in your account balance' and pairs it with 'avoid seeking revenge after losing trades.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: Mechanical rule: reset on the next day (in 24/7 perp replay, a rolling 24h window).
findings.risk_geometry: 3 consecutive losing trades -> no new entries for the rest of the period; paired with a no-revenge-trading rule.
findings.quote: after 3 consecutive losing trades, you quit for the day.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, Plan Your Trade and Trade Your Plan (behavior rules)
findings.notes: Perp 24/7 trading removes natural daily resets, so an explicit streak-based circuit breaker is more necessary, not less. In V8 this is a lifecycle admission gate keyed off recent consecutive losses in the episode log, distinct from the drawdown math (lose 80% -> need 400% to recover).
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Leverage cap (<=10:1) and leverage-driven equity decay
findings.setup_summary: The book defines leverage above 10:1 as 'excessive' and recommends capping it regardless of broker-allowable limits; Table 11-1 shows equity under consecutive 25-PIP losses: at 50:1, three consecutive losses cut the account to 67% of original, vs 99.25% at 1:1. Worked example: a 100-PIP loss on the same position is 20-25% of capital on 20-25:1 accounts but 2% on a 2:1 account.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not applicable - sizing discipline rule; the equity-decay table is arithmetic.
findings.risk_geometry: notional/equity <= 10:1 (author's rule); account-type choice (micro/mini/standard) is the sizing lever.
findings.quote: if you find that striving to meet your trading goals necessitates the use of excessive leverage (which I define as greater than 10:1), you should scale back your expectations
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, Currency Risk; Chapter 11, A Final Note on Leverage (Table 11-1)
findings.notes: Perps offer 100x+, making the leverage-decay arithmetic directly transferable; the <=10:1 cap is a concrete candidate RiskGate parameter (with the caveat that 1h crypto backtests may warrant tuning). Position-size determination in V8 RiskGate admission.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Reduce/close exposure before scheduled high-volatility news events
findings.setup_summary: Volatility spikes around planned news releases; if you cannot afford the loss a release might trigger, close the position or scale back leverage beforehand. The book also shows how to quantify baseline noise from realized volatility (USD/CAD weekly mean ~100 PIPs, max ~135) so event spikes are distinguished from routine fluctuation.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Event passes without the feared spike (opportunity cost); the rule is a pre-event exposure decision, not a directional call.
findings.risk_geometry: Pre-event action: close position or scale back leverage; no stop geometry given by the book.
findings.quote: volatility may spike around certain planned news releases. If you think that a big move is likely and you can't afford the loss that the news might trigger, close your position or scale back your leverage.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, Volatility
findings.notes: Crypto analog is scheduled macro events (FOMC, CPI) which measurably spike BTC vol, but the calendar is thinner than FX's and crypto-specific news is unscheduled, so this is a regime filter, not a primary strategy. Deterministic in V8 replay: an economic calendar is known ahead of time, so no lookahead.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Overtrading discipline (fewer, longer, higher-conviction trades)
findings.setup_summary: After excessive leverage, 'the biggest strategic mistake committed by novice traders is overtrading' - scalping without preparation, too many simultaneous positions. Remedy is quantitative: 'Instead of trying to earn 50 PIPs twice a day, aim for 200 PIPs once a week,' hold positions longer, and 'there is no rule that says you need to be in the market at all times' - sit out when the market is gyrating or the strategy gives no signal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not applicable - behavioral discipline; the book's attribution example (30 trades in 3 weeks for +253 PIPs) argues fewer trades would have matched the result.
findings.risk_geometry: Raise per-trade profit threshold and hold duration; lower trade count; optional per-day trade cap.
findings.quote: Instead of trying to earn 50 PIPs twice a day, aim for 200 PIPs once a week.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, Poor Strategy; Chapter 11, Risk Management
findings.notes: The 24/7 perp market plus one-click trading makes overtrading friction far lower than in FX, so a frequency cap is arguably more needed on crypto perps. Methodology lesson for V8's evaluation posture (prefer fewer, longer-horizon candidate episodes) and for lab-runner trade-count instrumentation; complements the loss-streak circuit breaker.
findings.book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

findings.strategy_name: Turtle/Donchian channel breakout (System 1 & 2)
findings.mechanism: A breakout of a prior N-day high/low signals a new trend; the edge comes from riding continuation after resistance/support is exceeded
findings.setup_summary: On daily bars (for V8: BTCUSDT 1h): buy when the close exceeds the highest high of the prior N days (N=20 for System 1, N=60 for System 2); sell short on the mirroring low break. Entry sized so the initial stop (2N = 2 ATR) risks 2% of equity; positions pyramided in 1/2-N increments up to 4 units; exit via the 2N stop-loss and, per Chapter 10's Donchian Trend variant, a 10-day breakout exit plus a 25/350 EMA trend filter.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close (or next open) beyond a windowed prior extreme. Invalidation: close falls back inside the channel / hits the 2N stop; the 17-consecutive-losing-cocoa-trades table (Table 4-1) shows long losing streaks are the normal cost of the entry.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: next-bar open after breakout close (Turtles used limit orders); stop: 2N (2 ATR) below/above entry, equivalent to 2% of account at unit sizing; targets: none pre-set - let trend run, exit on 10/20-day breakout in opposite direction (bonus chapter, Part 2) or time; expiry: none (trend-following hold); pyramiding: up to 4 units in 1/2-N increments.
findings.quote: The basic idea was to buy if a market exceeded the highest price for a particular number of preceding days, that is, broke out of its prior price levels.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 The First $2 Million Is the Toughest (pp.38-40, 44-45); Ch.10 Turtle-Style Trading: Step by Step (pp.139-140)
findings.notes: The canonical turtle system and the most likely-corroborated strategy in this library; directly testable on 24/7 BTC 1h (no overnight gaps to stop through). Note the book's own finding that Donchian's edge decayed post-Turtle era (Ch.10: CAGR 29.4%, worst of six systems in 1996-2006) - crowding. V8 budget: would compete for a trend-continuation slot with trend_pullback; propose as new family (registry PROPOSED), not a variant of breakout_retest.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Trend portfolio filter (fast MA vs slow MA direction gate)
findings.mechanism: Filtering entries to the direction of the longer-term moving-average trend removes breakouts against the major trend, which are the moves least likely to continue; market-state selection is a separable source of edge from the entry itself
findings.setup_summary: Compute a fast MA (50-day, or 25-day EMA in the Donchian Trend test version) and a slow MA (300-day, or 350-day EMA). Permit long entries only when fast > slow and short entries only when fast < slow. Book's quantified claim: random entries become edge-bearing under the filter (E70-ratio 1.27 vs ~1.0 unfiltered) and a 20-day breakout entry goes from E70 1.20 to 1.33 with the filter added, E120 reaching ~1.6.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: fast MA crosses to the favorable side of slow MA. Invalidation/filter: no new trades when the two MAs are on the 'wrong' side; the filter also acts as the regime switch for the four market states (trending-quiet vs trending-volatile vs stable states from Ch.2).
findings.risk_geometry: Not a trade geometry - a portfolio/regime gate applied before entries; no stops or expiry of its own.
findings.quote: you can initiate long trades only in markets in which the 50-day moving average is higher than the 300-day moving average and can initiate short trades only in markets in which the 50-day moving average is lower than the 300-day moving average.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 Trading with an Edge, The Trend Portfolio Filter Edge (pp.69-73); Ch.2 market states (pp.25-27)
findings.notes: Strongest quantitative claim in Part 1: the filter is where much of the trend edge lives (70,000-random-entry test, E70=1.27). Maps directly to a V8 regime filter gating existing trend families (trend_pullback, donchian breakout) - fast/slow MA direction on 1h BTC is trivially computable and PIT-safe. The Ch.2 four-market-state taxonomy (stable-quiet / stable-volatile / trending-quiet / trending-volatile) is the underlying regime framework and belongs in the same register decision.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Volatility channel breakout (ATR Channel and Bollinger Breakout)
findings.mechanism: A move beyond a channel defined by a long moving average plus a volatility buffer (ATR or standard deviation) signals volatility expansion and the start of a trend; the wide buffer filters false moves in quiet markets
findings.setup_summary: ATR Channel Breakout: channel top = 350-day MA of close + 7 ATR, bottom = 350-day MA - 3 ATR; enter long at the open if the prior close exceeded the top, short if below the bottom; exit when close crosses back through the 350-day MA. Bollinger Breakout variant: 350-day MA +/- 2.5 std dev of close. Backtests (Table 10-1, 1996-2006): ATR CBO CAGR 49.5%/MAR 1.24; Bollinger CBO CAGR 51.8%/MAR 1.52 - both beat Donchian Trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: prior-bar close beyond the volatility channel. Invalidation: close returns inside the channel (exit at MA) - no stop used in the book's base version; unit limits still apply.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: next-bar open after close beyond channel; stop: none in base version (exit = close crossing back through the 350-day MA); target: none (trend); expiry: none.
findings.quote: The channel is formed by adding 7 ATR to a 350-day moving average of the closing prices for the channel top and subtracting 3 ATR from the moving average for the channel bottom.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Turtle-Style Trading: Step by Step, ATR Channel Breakout & Bollinger Breakout (pp.136-139); Ch.9 building blocks (p.127)
findings.notes: The ATR-channel is effectively the PGO system (Mark Johnson, Ch.10). On 24/7 crypto the long 350-bar MA on 1h needs ~2 weeks of warm-up data; the volatility-buffer width makes the filter robust to regime vol changes. Fits V8 feature groups volatility+trend; a natural new family distinct from donchian (channel vs raw window breakout).
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Fixed-duration time exit (80 bars, no stop)
findings.mechanism: A fixed holding-period exit lets a trade run exactly long enough to capture the trend while mechanically capping drawdown from trend reversal; the book's tests show time exits beat breakout exits and that adding stops makes trend systems strictly worse
findings.setup_summary: Donchian Trend with Time Exit: same 20-day breakout entry with 25/350 EMA trend filter, but exit after exactly 80 days and no stop. It posted the best CAGR of all six tested systems (57.2%, MAR 1.31, Table 10-1) and was the only system whose metrics were unchanged when 5 adverse months were appended (Table 10-2/10-3). Companion finding (Adding Stops, pp.145-147): for Dual/Triple MA and Donchian Time, every stop width from ~0.5 to ~10 ATR made every metric (CAGR, MAR, Sharpe, drawdown) worse; only stops >= 10 ATR matched no-stop.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Exit is calendar-based (N bars after entry) regardless of price; no thesis-based invalidation in the base system.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: next-bar open on 20-day breakout; stop: none; target: none; expiry: fixed 80 bars - the risk_geometry expiry IS the strategy.
findings.quote: uses a time-based exit instead of a breakout exit. It exits the trade after 80 days and does not use any stops whatsoever.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Turtle-Style Trading: Step by Step, Donchian Trend with Time Exit and Adding Stops (pp.140-141, 145-147)
findings.notes: Directly refines V8's expiry_bars risk geometry (trend_pullback already uses expiry_bars=8): this book supports long fixed time exits for trend-continuation families and cautions against entry-based ATR stops for slow systems. In perps, no-gap 24/7 trading removes the gap-through-stop justification for stops, strengthening the no-stop result; the funding cost of holding is the offsetting consideration. The V8 'stop vs dead-thesis (still_valid)' distinction is compatible - the lesson targets entry-based stops, not thesis invalidation.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Volatility-normalized unit sizing (N / ATR = 1% of equity)
findings.mechanism: Sizing every market so that one ATR of adverse movement equals a fixed fraction of equity equalizes per-trade dollar risk across instruments and, critically, equalizes exposure to price shocks regardless of stop distance
findings.setup_summary: Unit size = (1% of account) / (dollar value of 1 ATR per contract). For a $1M account, 1-ATR = $10,000, so units in each market are chosen so daily fluctuations are approximately equal in dollars. The book's evidence: on the Oct 1987 shock, Curtis (1/2-ATR stop) would have lost 4x more if sized by stop-distance alone; volatility-based sizing gave all Turtles identical shock exposure.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - a sizing rule, recomputed each day from the ATR (N) at entry.
findings.risk_geometry: Sizing rule, not entry geometry; pairs with the 2N stop so each unit risks 1% of equity and max 4 units = 4% per market.
findings.quote: Each unit was sized by determining the number of contracts where 1-ATR of price movement would be equal to 1 percent of our account size.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.8 Risk and Money Management, The N Factor (pp.117-120); Ch.3 (pp.32-33)
findings.notes: This is exactly V8's atr_ref/risk normalization principle already in the frozen spec (trend_pullback stop_r 1.0, atr_ref). The book adds two refinements: (a) size by ATR, not by stop distance - stop distance and exposure are decoupled (the 1/2-ATR vs 2-ATR stop story); (b) sizing must be re-frozen at entry and PIT - the 'number of contracts per million' was updated weekly. In perps, position sizing by ATR of the perp is direct since contract value = price x notional.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Turtle unit limits (4/market, 6 correlated, 10-12 per direction)
findings.mechanism: Hard caps on aggregate exposure per market, per correlated basket, and per direction protect against the correlated, simultaneous adverse moves at trend breakdowns; the per-market cap also acts as a filter that keeps out late-signaling lagging markets
findings.setup_summary: Max 4 units per market; max 6 units total across highly correlated markets (e.g., the four interest-rate products, the six currencies); max 10 units long or 10 short overall (12 if positions in uncorrelated markets). Correlated markets naturally cluster: in a real move, all four interest-rate products signal but the Turtles typically held only the first two - the cap filters out markets that signal last and move least.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - a risk gate, not a signal; violations block new units until exposure unwinds.
findings.risk_geometry: Aggregate exposure cap in unit terms (unit = 1% equity risk); the author credits these caps with saving Richard Dennis well over $100M on the Oct 1987 single-day shock.
findings.quote: we could put on a maximum of only 4 units per market; second, we could put on a maximum of only 6 units in markets that were highly correlated; third, we could put on a maximum of only 10 units in any given direction (i.e., 10 long or 10 short).
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.8 Risk and Money Management (pp.119-120)
findings.notes: The 'everything moves against you at once' claim (pp.119, 201-202) is even stronger in crypto, where BTC/ETH/alt perps share funding regimes and liquidation cascades. Maps to V8's ONE-exposure-per-(instrument,direction) rule and heat cap: suggests adding a correlated-basket cap and a net-direction cap (max N units long across the book). The lagging-market filter property is a genuine selection mechanism for correlated alt baskets.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Countertrend fade at support/resistance anchors
findings.mechanism: Anchoring + recency + disposition make recent swing highs/lows sticky anchors: traders sell into rallies to prior highs and buy into prior lows, producing bounces; the short-term edge of betting against a fresh breakout is real because most new-high breakouts fail
findings.setup_summary: Near a recent swing high (resistance anchor), sell short expecting a bounce/fade; near a recent swing low (support anchor), buy expecting a bounce; stop beyond the anchor level. Supporting evidence: the E-ratio for 20-day breakouts is below 1.0 over the first few days after the signal, i.e., price on average moves against a breakout in the very short term, then flips positive only at medium horizons (Figure 5-2).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price approaches a windowed prior extreme with no close beyond it. Invalidation: close breaks the anchor level - the book's heating-oil example (Sept 5, 2006) shows fading a broken support leads to a full wipeout; countertrend traders must exit on the close at or just after the breakdown.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: bar close at/near anchor; stop: ~0.05-0.06 beyond the S/R level (book's example: buy at $2.10, stop 6c below at support breakdown); target: toward the opposite anchor (structure), not an R-multiple; expiry: short (very short-term edge only).
findings.quote: there is generally more movement against a trade taken at a breakout than there is in the direction of the breakout. This is one of the reasons you can make money using a countertrend trading style by betting on the breakout not holding and in favor of a bounce off of the support or resistance.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 Trading with an Edge (pp.68-69); Ch.6 Falling Off the Edge (pp.75-84)
findings.notes: The short-term adverse-breakout data is empirical (E-ratio < 1.0 early), but no full countertrend system is backtested in Part 1 - mechanism rests on the cognitive-bias narrative. Perp caveats: funding keeps price pinned near anchors, liquidation cascades make breakdowns sharper than futures (higher tail risk on the fade), and round-number/ liquidation-level anchors in crypto differ from exchange-made swing anchors. Candidate backlog family (mean_reversion class) alongside V8's existing trend and liquidity families.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Support/resistance breakdown continuation (the trend-following edge at S/R failure)
findings.mechanism: When support/resistance breaks down there is a 'gap in human perception' - holders cling to stale beliefs, no new buyers appear below the level, and selling begets selling, so the market moves farther after a breakdown than at other times (liquidity vacuum below the level)
findings.setup_summary: Buy resistance breakdowns to enter longs, sell support breakdowns to enter shorts: when the close breaks below a windowed prior low that was previously defended (heating-oil example: Sept 5 close below the Aug 30 low at $2.05 after Support 1 and Support 2 held earlier), there is no obvious subsequent anchor, so the move continues long and hard; entry is on/just after the breakdown close. The book asserts a statistically significant tendency for larger moves after S/R breakdowns.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close through a prior extreme after prior tests of that level. Invalidation for the trend side: none beyond the exit rule - this is the continuation edge (failed breakout = entry, not fade); countertrend side must not fight the breakdown.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: bar close at breakdown (or next open, limit orders to avoid adverse fill); stop: ~2N (Turtle) or a small buffer beyond the broken level; target: none (trend continuation); expiry: none.
findings.quote: A breakout occurs when the price 'breaks out' of previous resistance and support levels. As breakout traders, we were buying resistance breakdowns to enter long trades and selling support breakdowns to enter short trades.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 Falling Off the Edge (pp.79-82)
findings.notes: Directly corroborates V8's existing failed_breakout family (mechanism liquidity_vacuum_reentry, behavior failed_breakout_reentry): the book generalizes it to both directions (V8's current expert is SHORT-only) and supplies the psychological mechanism (anchoring/recency/disposition creating the perception gap). The 'statistically significant' claim is asserted, not quantified in Part 1. Perp: liquidation cascades amplify the vacuum, but fill-at-close entry may chase fast moves; frozen prior_high_ref already matches the book's frozen-anchor approach.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Dual / Triple moving-average crossover (always-in-market)
findings.mechanism: A fast MA crossing a slow MA defines trend state; being always in the market removes discretion and captures every sustained move; the book's tests show the simplest version (Dual MA) beat the more complex filtered version (Triple MA)
findings.setup_summary: Dual MA: long when 100-day MA > 350-day MA, short when below; always in the market, exit = flip. Triple MA: 150/250-day crossover gated by the 350-day trend filter; not always in the market. Results (Table 10-1): Dual MA CAGR 57.8%, MAR 1.82 (best MAR of all six systems), Sharpe 1.55; Triple MA 48.1%, MAR 1.53 - complexity did not help. No stops in either; adding stops made every metric worse.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: fast MA crosses slow MA (or the pair crosses the filter MA). Invalidation: the crossing back - the position flips rather than exits to flat.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: next-bar open on crossover; stop: none; target: none; expiry: none - the system is always long or short, so exposure is continuous.
findings.quote: This is a very simple system that buys and sells when a 100-day moving average crosses over a slower 350-day moving average. Unlike the other systems, this system is always in the market, either long or short.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Turtle-Style Trading: Step by Step, Dual & Triple Moving Average (pp.141-144)
findings.notes: Backtested in the book (1996-2006) - falsifiable and corroborated across the trend-following literature. Perp caveat: 'always in the market' means paying (or earning) funding continuously, so net carry drag is a real, testable term that does not exist in futures; on 1h bars, 100/350 MA needs ~2-3 weeks warm-up. The 'simpler beat complex' result reinforces V8 rule 14's simplicity budget and the frozen-OOS screening approach.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Trader effects: visible signal crowding and front-running
findings.mechanism: A rule-based signal that is publicly known (e.g., breakout levels) gets front-run and diluted: other traders trade ahead of the triggering orders, changing what the signal means and eroding or destroying the edge; conversely, unappealing strategies (high drawdown) have long lifetimes
findings.setup_summary: The gold example (pp.154-156): a trader who knows a 1,000-lot buy order sits at $410.50 buys ahead, pushes price to the trigger, sells into the breakout buyers, net +$160K. Mechanism: edges decay as capital flows into them - the popular breakout system in the book drew hundreds of millions in AUM and then produced its worst 20-year drawdown. Mitigations: use limit orders (not market), keep signals private, avoid optimizing to public/illiquid markets; the Turtles varied stops/entry timing to obfuscate.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - a backtest-degradation and execution methodology; relevant when a candidate edge is widely known or machine-monitorable.
findings.risk_geometry: Execution layer: limit/stop orders rather than market orders; entry closer to the touch; avoid illiquid venues (lumber/propane style small markets) where anticipatory orders move price.
findings.quote: If too many traders start to try to take advantage of a particular strategy, that strategy will cease working as well as it did previously.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.11 Lies, Damn Lies, and Backtests, Trader Effects (pp.153-158); also Ch.10 (pp.144, 147)
findings.notes: Most relevant methodology for crypto: Donchian-style levels are public, machine-monitored, and stop-huntable on perp order books, so any formalized V8 expert should assume front-running of visible thresholds (supports V8's point-in-time MarketState and frozen refs - and argues against broadcasting live signal levels). Also explains the book's observation that Donchian's edge decayed vs the Turtle era, and that trader effects can arise without conscious collusion.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: E-ratio: volatility-adjusted MFE/MAE entry-edge measurement
findings.mechanism: An entry's edge can be measured directly before building a full system: average maximum favorable excursion divided by average maximum adverse excursion, each normalized by ATR at entry, over a fixed horizon; random entries give ~1.0, and a real entry must exceed 1.0 over the system's intended holding horizon
findings.setup_summary: For each entry signal, compute MFE and MAE over the next N days (E5/E10/E50/E70...), divide each by ATR at entry, average across signals, and take MFE/MAE. Calibration from the book: 30 random coin-flip tests gave E5=1.01, E10=1.005, E50=0.997; a 20-day breakout entry shows E5=0.99/E10=1.0 (below 1 short-term) but E70=1.20; adding the trend filter lifts E70 to 1.33 and E120 to ~1.6.
findings.trigger_invalidation: An entry with E-ratio <= 1.0 over its intended horizon has no edge; an entry whose edge is positive only at horizons mismatching the system's exit is a system-design mismatch.
findings.risk_geometry: No trade geometry - a pre-trade screening/validation statistic; horizon parameter is the key choice (edge must be measured over the actual holding window).
findings.quote: The E-ratio is the average volatility-adjusted MFE divided by the average volatility-adjusted MAE.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 Trading with an Edge, The Edge Ratio (pp.66-69)
findings.notes: Directly usable in V8's registry/screening pipeline: measure a proposed expert family's E-ratio on BTC 1h over its intended horizon (e.g., trend_pullback's 8-bar expiry -> E8) before formalizing, and to test whether entry edge exists at all. ATR normalization is PIT-safe. Also supports the book's core thesis (Ch.5): entry edge is horizon-specific, and exits should be matched to the horizon where the entry has edge - relevant to V8's risk_geometry design.
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

findings.strategy_name: Drawdown clustering: correlated bad days at trend ends (Monte Carlo with chunk scrambling)
findings.mechanism: At the end of large trends, markets that are usually uncorrelated move against everyone at once and bad days are serially correlated; Monte Carlo that scrambles individual trades (or single-day changes) destroys this clustering and understates drawdowns, so validation must scramble in multi-day chunks
findings.setup_summary: When simulating alternative equity paths, trade-scrambling MC removes the date-link between correlated markets (gold+silver+sugar all down mid-May to mid-June 2006) and understates drawdown magnitude/frequency; equity-curve scrambling with 20-day chunks preserves the serial correlation of daily net changes. The Oct 1987 eurodollar gap and the 'everything moves against you at once' behavior are the motivating evidence. Robust measures (RAR%, R-cubed = RAR%/(length-adjusted avg of 5 largest drawdowns)) are also introduced as less luck-sensitive alternatives to CAGR/MAR/Sharpe.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Validation result invalid if: test period covers only 1-2 market states (like polling only Democrats, Ch.12), sample < ~100 trades (rule triggers with <5 occurrences are uninformative), or parameters sit on a 'cliff' (1% parameter change flips result, e.g., 45.7% to -0.4%).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - validation and performance-measurement methodology; informs simulator and registry gates rather than trade geometry.
findings.quote: at the end of a large trend when it breaks down and reverses, it seems that everything moves against you at once; even markets that normally do not seem correlated become so on those volatile days when a large trend disintegrates.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.12 On Solid Ground, Monte Carlo Simulation (pp.200-205); Ch.8 (p.119); Ch.11 cliffs (pp.173-176)
findings.notes: Crypto perps make this worse, not better: BTC/ETH/alt perps share funding, leverage, and liquidation cascades, so simultaneous bad days are the norm at breakdowns - any V8 Monte Carlo / bootstrap validation must preserve cross-market date alignment and serial correlation (scramble in chunks), or it will understate drawdown. Also supports V8's canonical-L1 simulator retaining correlation structure and its frozen-OOS gates (the optimization paradox - optimized parameters overstate future - is directly relevant to V8's challenger-vs-frozen-OOS rule).
findings.book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

book_title: Way of the Turtle: The Secret Methods That Turned Ordinary People Into Legendary Traders (2007) - Curtis M. Faith, Part 1 of 2
Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques, 2nd Edition (2001) - Part 1 of 2

findings.strategy_name: Hammer and Hanging Man (Umbrella Lines)
findings.mechanism: A long lower shadow with a small real body at the top of the range shows sellers pushed price down during the session but buyers reclaimed the close near the highs; after a downtrend this is seller exhaustion (hammer), after an extended rally it is buyer entrapment that needs confirmation (hanging man).
findings.setup_summary: After a downtrend, a bar whose real body sits at the upper end of the range, lower shadow at least 2x the real body height, and no or very short upper shadow (hammer) is a LONG setup completed at bar close. The identical candle after an extended rally (preferably at an all-time high) is a hanging man: a SHORT setup only once the next bar closes under its real body.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: bar close completes the shape (lower shadow >= 2x body, tiny/absent upper shadow) in the correct trend context; hanging man additionally requires a confirming close under its real body. Invalidation: close under the hammer's low voids support; absence of confirmation after a hanging man keeps the bull trend entrenched (new-high closes negate).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at hammer close or limit near the lower-shadow support zone; stop under the hammer's low (swing point, ~$5 below in the worked example); candles give no price targets so targets come from Western structure; hanging-man short stop above its high.
findings.quote: It has a long lower shadow that should be at least twice the height of the real body... A hammer must come after a decline. A hanging man must come after a rally.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, Reversal Patterns - Umbrella Lines / Hammer / Hanging Man, pp. 32-42
findings.notes: Wick-rejection semantics transfer directly to leveraged BTC; a stop under the wick low is a natural risk_geometry. Overlaps V8's liquidity_sweep_reclaim when the hammer wick takes out a prior extreme; this family covers the pure shape-plus-trend variant. The book's own risk/reward example shows the entry-refinement lesson (buy the correction into the shadow, not the close).
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Bullish/Bearish Engulfing Pattern
findings.mechanism: The second opposite-color real body fully enveloping the prior body shows buying (bullish) or selling (bearish) pressure overwhelming the prior session's force; the pattern's low/high becomes a frozen support/resistance anchor.
findings.setup_summary: In a clearly definable trend (even short-term), a second candle whose real body engulfs the prior real body and is the opposite color is a reversal signal: bullish engulfing after a decline (LONG), bearish engulfing after a rally (SHORT). Importance rises when the first day is a spinning top, the second body is very long, the move was protracted/fast, or volume is heavy on the second body.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close of the second bar completes the engulfing (body wraps prior body, opposite color, trend required). Invalidation: close below the low of a bullish engulfing pattern voids its support; a black body wrapping a white body after a decline is NOT a bearish engulfing (context-dependence - same shape after a rally only).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the second-candle close or on a correction to the pattern low; stop below the lowest low of the bullish pattern / above the highest high of the bearish pattern (pattern acts as support/resistance - frozen refs); targets from Western tools since candles give none.
findings.quote: Two candles comprise the engulfing pattern. The second real body must engulf the prior real body... I use the high of the two candle lines that make the bearish engulfing pattern. That high becomes our resistance... the lowest low of that pattern should become support.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, Reversal Patterns - The Engulfing Pattern, pp. 42-49
findings.notes: Engulfing is the most machine-recognizable candle signal and heavily used in crypto. The pattern-as-support/resistance ref gives a deterministic risk_geometry in V8's frozen-ref style, closely analogous to how failed_breakout freezes prior_high_ref.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Dark-Cloud Cover / Piercing Pattern (body-penetration reversals)
findings.mechanism: After a strong one-directional body, the next session opens beyond the prior extreme (gap/opening extension) then closes deep inside the prior body: the extension failed, trapping momentum participants who entered at the open/close and reversing control.
findings.setup_summary: Dark-cloud cover (top): after a strong white body, a black body opens above the prior session's high and closes more than 50% into the white body. Piercing pattern (bottom): after a strong black body, a white body opens below (ideally under) the prior low and closes more than 50% into the black body. Less than 50% penetration is a weaker on-neck/in-neck/thrusting pattern needing next-session confirmation.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: second-bar close penetrating >50% of the first body; dark-cloud's second bar should open above prior high. Invalidation: close back above the pattern high (dark-cloud) / below the pattern low (piercing) voids the reversal; penetration <50% is only a weak signal, not a reversal.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at pattern-completion close (or wait for bounce to the dark-cloud resistance / pullback to the piercing support for better risk/reward); stop above the highest high of the dark-cloud cover (its resistance anchor) or below the piercing low; greater penetration = higher confidence.
findings.quote: The second day's price opens above the prior session's high... the market closes deeply within the prior day's white body. The greater the degree of penetration into the white real body, the more likely this is a top. Some Japanese technicians require more than a 50-percent penetration.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, Reversal Patterns - Dark-Cloud Cover and Piercing Pattern, pp. 49-59
findings.notes: The 'open above prior high' leg maps to gap/opening wicks seen in crypto around liquidation cascades and funding spikes; the >50% body-penetration threshold is a crisp falsifiable parameter. Book admits definitional variance (open above close vs above high) and that non-classic variants can be read by 'how and where' they formed - a subjectivity caveat for machine recognition.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Morning/Evening Star (three-candle trend exhaustion)
findings.mechanism: A small-body star (gap away from a long one-directional body) reflects a stalemate where the prior trend's force dissipates; the third body closing deep into the first body confirms control has switched.
findings.setup_summary: Morning star (bottom): after a decline, a long black body, then a small real body that does not touch the first body, then a white body intruding deeply into the first body. Evening star (top): mirror after a rally; the star's small body is the first hint of a top. Ideal versions have non-touching real bodies; a doji middle candle = doji star (stronger); double-gap abandoned baby variants are rare but strongest.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close of the third candle completing the pattern after a trend. Invalidation: a close under the morning star's lowest-low support ref voids the reversal; no preceding trend to reverse = no signal; second and third candles overlapping does not invalidate (gap between them not required).
