findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the third-candle close or on a correction back to the pattern's lowest-low support; stop below that low; the book explicitly flags poor risk/reward buying at pattern completion and recommends waiting for the pullback to the support anchor; evening-star resistance = its highs.
findings.quote: The concluding candle of the morning star is a white real body that intrudes deeply into the first session's black candle... The lowest low of the three lines that form this pattern should be support.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, Stars - The Morning Star and Evening Star, pp. 62-70
findings.notes: Three-bar patterns complete late (book's own admission), so the operationally actionable part is the pullback-to-support entry, not the completion close. The 'three-river' historical note frames a close over the evening-star resistance / under morning-star support as the confirmation event.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Doji as Top-Reversal Signal (Northern/Southern doji asymmetry)
findings.mechanism: An open-equals-close session reflects complete bull/bear balance; in an overbought rally this indecision means the buyers' scaffolding gives way (top), but in a downtrend it is a weak bottom signal because an ambivalent market can fall of its own weight.
findings.setup_summary: A doji (open ~= close, any shadows) after a rally, especially after a tall white candle or in an overbought condition, is a potential top: take the highest high between the doji and the prior tall white candle as close-based resistance and require a confirming close under it. Doji in a trading range ('box') has no forecasting implications because there is no trend to reverse.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: doji bar completes in a trending/overbought context. Invalidation: close above the doji-resistance ref negates (market 'refreshed', bullish breakout); a Southern doji (in a decline) is not a bottom signal unless it confirms other support evidence; doji in a box range = no trade; doji with a new high close needs next-session bearish confirmation.
findings.risk_geometry: Resistance = highest high of the doji and prior tall white candle (frozen ref, close-based); stop above it; confirmation = next-session close under the doji's close; doji in a box at range edges merely confirms the range.
findings.quote: The doji is a distinct trend change signal, especially during rallies... as successful as doji are at calling tops, they tend to lose some reversal potential in downtrends... doji have little forecasting implications if they are in a trading range environment since there is no trend to reverse.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, The Magic Doji, pp. 155-170
findings.notes: The falsifiable cores are the top/bottom asymmetry claim and the box-range regime filter ('no trend to reverse = no signal'), which doubles as a REGIME_FILTER lesson for all reversal experts. Long-legged/gravestone/dragonfly doji variants are shape refinements of the same family.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Windows (Gaps) as Support/Resistance with Close-Based Invalidation
findings.mechanism: A price vacuum between two bars (no overlapping shadows) leaves a zone where corrections stop: the window acts as support (rising) or resistance (falling), so the trend continues until the window is closed on a close, not an intraday touch.
findings.setup_summary: A rising window (prior bar's high below current bar's low, shadows not overlapping) in an uptrend is a continuation signal: buy dips toward the window; the whole window is a support zone, critical support is its bottom. Mirror for falling windows (sell bounces, resistance at the top). Trend stays intact - even across many windows - until a close under the last rising window's bottom (or over the last falling window's top); if one window's support breaks, step down to the next window below.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: window bar completes (gap between shadows, size irrelevant - even 4 cents). Invalidation: close under the bottom of a rising window voids the uptrend; close over the top of a falling window voids the downtrend; intraday pierce without a close does not invalidate.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: buy dips at/near the rising window (aggressive traders may buy near its top); stop: mental or physical on a close under the window bottom; falling-window shorts stop on close over the window top; targets from Western structure.
findings.quote: It is said by Japanese technicians to 'go in the direction of the window'... 'corrections stop at the window.'... If the pullback closes under the bottom of the window, the prior uptrend is voided.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, Continuation Patterns - Windows, Tasuki, Gapping Plays, pp. 126-141
findings.notes: Literal gaps between consecutive 1h bars are rare in 24/7 crypto (mostly liquidation/exchange-outage events), lowering signal frequency; but the close-not-intraday invalidation semantics and broken-structure support transfer to V8's lifecycle/simulator rules. Nison himself downplays tasuki/side-by-side variants: 'It is the window that is critical.'
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Springs and Upthrusts (Wyckoff false breaks / stop hunts)
findings.mechanism: liquidity_vacuum_reentry - a false break below support (spring) or above resistance (upthrust) runs the stops and traps the momentum participants on the wrong side; the reclaim on a close proves the defending side (bulls at support, bears at resistance) is victorious.
findings.setup_summary: Spring (LONG): price breaks under a tested horizontal support and then closes back above it (new lows could not hold); buy the reclaim. Upthrust (SHORT): price penetrates a tested horizontal resistance and then closes back under it; sell the failure. Ideal volume: light on the break, heavier on the reclaim.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close back above the broken support (spring) / close back under the broken resistance (upthrust). Invalidation: a close back through the most recent swing low (spring) or recent swing high (upthrust) voids the thesis and the target; a beachhead maintained (holding above broken resistance) means bulls keep control.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop = most recent swing low (spring, preferably on a close); target = the high before the spring was made or the top of the trading range; upthrust target = recent low or bottom of range; entry on the reclaim close.
findings.quote: a spring develops when the market breaks under a horizontal support area and then springs back above that previously broken support... If the market is solid, it should not get back to the most recent lows. That would be a stop level (preferably on a close).
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, Candles with Trend Lines - Springs and Upthrusts, pp. 199-205
findings.notes: Direct, named support for the V8 failed_breakout and liquidity_sweep_reclaim families - stop hunts above/below ranges are endemic to leveraged crypto. Adds a participation refinement (light break / heavy reclaim volume) and explicit target semantics (pre-spring high or range top) to the existing frozen-ref design.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Change of Polarity (old support becomes new resistance)
findings.mechanism: trapped_position_gravity - traders who bought near old support (or were stopped out there) are emotionally attached to their entry price; rallies back to that level trigger their break-even exits, converting old support into supply and old resistance into demand.
findings.setup_summary: After a tested support breaks, the first rally back into the old support zone should stall and reverse (SHORT); after tested resistance is cleared, pullbacks to the old resistance zone should hold (LONG). The level should be tested a few times before applying the principle, and it works as a zone, not an exact price.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price re-enters the flipped zone after the break. Invalidation: a close back through the zone in the breakout direction (old support re-conquered on a close) voids the flip thesis.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the reaction into the flipped zone, ideally with a confirming candle (e.g., hammer confirming polarity support; bearish engulfing at polarity resistance); stop beyond the flipped zone; target toward the next structure; old support zone can be a band (e.g., $116-$117.50) rather than one line.
findings.quote: Old support becomes new resistance and old resistance becomes support. This is what I call the 'change of polarity' principle... The most important price on any chart is the price at which you entered the market.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, Candles with Trend Lines - The Change of Polarity Principle, pp. 205-211
findings.notes: The psychological mechanism (break-even exits by trapped longs) transfers directly to crypto, where prior range extremes, round numbers and liquidation clusters are heavily traded. Natural frozen-ref design: ref = previously tested support/resistance level. This also supplies the 'why' behind V8's failed_breakout still_valid rule (close stays below the old level).
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: RSI Divergence + Overbought/Oversold with Candle Confirmation
findings.mechanism: momentum_divergence - price making new highs while RSI fails to follow shows the move lacks internal force; the oscillator is only a warning that becomes actionable when a candle pattern confirms the turn.
findings.setup_summary: Negative divergence (price new high, RSI lower than at the prior price high), especially with RSI in the overbought zone (>70) and confirmed by a top candle (e.g., dark-cloud cover), is a SHORT setup. Positive divergence (price new low, RSI higher) with oversold RSI (<30) plus a bottom candle is a LONG setup. Divergence is more meaningful when RSI is in the overbought/oversold region.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: confirming candle after the divergence forms. Invalidation: price continues to new highs/lows with RSI following (divergence resolved); a candle signal without the oscillator warning (or vice versa) is a weaker signal.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the confirming candle, not the oscillator alone; stops beyond the extreme of the move; use the candle anchor (e.g., dark-cloud cover high) for stop placement.
findings.quote: A negative, or bearish, divergence occurs when prices are at a new high, but the oscillator is not... I view an overbought or oversold oscillator as only a warning, a clue, with final confirmation coming with a candlestick pattern.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 14, Candles with Oscillators - The Relative Strength Index, pp. 226-229
findings.notes: Oscillator state (RSI band, divergence flag) is a natural response-group feature; the book insists on candle confirmation, so V8 should consume it as a filter/confirmation feature (convergence input) rather than a standalone expert. An oscillator trendline break adds a second negative signal (Exhibit 14.1).
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Moving Average as Support/Resistance with Candle Confirmation
findings.mechanism: trend_continuation - a moving average that repeatedly holds price becomes a live support/resistance ref in a trend; pullbacks to it resume the trend, but only when a candle signal confirms the bounce.
findings.setup_summary: In an uptrend, pullbacks to a previously-validated moving average (popular lengths: 5/9/30/40/65-day; 9-period EMA common in FX) that hold on a close and form a bullish candle (hammer, bullish engulfing) are LONG entries. A close below the MA is bearish; a validated MA broken on a close becomes resistance (polarity).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: candle confirmation at the MA (e.g., hammer at MA support) after the MA has been validated. Invalidation: a close through the MA in the breakout direction voids the pullback thesis; an unvalidated MA should not be traded as the sole reason.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the confirming candle at the MA; stop below the MA or below the candle low; target from Western structure; only trade MAs that have already proven to hold price.
findings.quote: we can then turn our attention to this particular moving average with the idea that retracements should hold the moving average as support... It is much more important to have a candlestick signal confirming a moving average's support or resistance.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 13, Candles with Moving Averages - Using Moving Averages, pp. 217-224
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's existing trend_pullback (ema_fast > ema_slow, close < ema_slow): adds the conditions that the MA be previously validated and that a candle signal confirm the bounce. Golden/dead cross terminology (dual MA crossover) also documented; 'slope up' refinement noted.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Reversal Signals Only Trade in the Direction of the Major Trend
findings.mechanism: regime_trend_alignment - a reversal signal against the major trend merely liquidates the trend-side position; entering counter-trend risks being run over by the larger flow even if eventually right ('the market is never wrong').
findings.setup_summary: In a bull market, a top-reversal candle signal is used to liquidate longs and to wait for a bullish signal on the correction, not to initiate a short. In a bear market, bottom-reversal signals are buy-candidates only once the major trend turns. This is an admission filter applied before any reversal-signal entry.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Applies as a filter: the major-trend definition must be explicit (price vs MA, higher lows/higher highs); invalidation of the trend itself re-enables counter-trend signals. Combined with the book's 'If...then system' discipline - stay in the position only if the market behaves as anticipated, otherwise exit.
findings.risk_geometry: NONE - an admission/exit filter (RiskGate style), not a directional strategy; also covered by the book's DISCIPLINE rules (stops always, lose the opinion not the money, pace trades to market environment).
findings.quote: An important principle is to initiate a new position (based on a reversal signal) only if that signal is in the direction of the major trend... This bearish signal would not warrant a short sale... It would, however, signal a liquidation of longs.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, Reversal Patterns - introduction, pp. 31-32; DISCIPLINE rules, p. 185
findings.notes: Maps directly onto V8's risk/lifecycle layer (RiskGate admission, one exposure per direction, dead-thesis exits) and the 'market is never wrong' discipline: a stop/exit rule rather than an entry generator. Corroborates the protective-stops sidebar ('A stop should be placed at the time of the original trade... There is no room for hope in the market').
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Cluster of Candles / Convergence of Signals at One Price
findings.mechanism: signal_convergence - several independent candle and Western signals stacking at the same price area (support or resistance) magnify the significance of that area, because each signal is an independent estimate of the same supply/demand boundary.
findings.setup_summary: At a support/resistance area, count the independent candle signals (engulfing patterns, hammers, doji, piercing patterns, shooting stars, windows) and Western signals (trend lines, MAs, retracements, change of polarity) landing at the same price: the more that converge, the higher the probability the area holds. Location matters more than signal shape - a buy pattern completed at a resistance area is not a buying opportunity.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: >=2 independent signals at the same ref. Invalidation: a close through the convergence zone voids the cluster; a signal formed at the wrong location (buy signal at resistance, sell signal at support) is not actionable regardless of shape.
findings.risk_geometry: Not an entry by itself; upgrades the confidence/weight of a zone that then uses its own candle anchors for stops and targets; the 'cluster' technique (e.g., four bearish signals stacked at $38-$39.50 resistance) is the canonical example.
findings.quote: I define convergence as 'a cluster of technical signals converging at, or near, the same price.' Convergence is a pivotal concept. This is because the more signals that join at a support or resistance area, the more likely a reversal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 2 introduction and Chapter 10, A Cluster of Candles, pp. 181-191
findings.notes: Central Part 2 thesis: candle signals are confirmatory, not standalone; 'where' a signal forms outweighs 'what' it is. For V8 this is a methodology lesson on the feature side (location/context weighting of CandidateDrafts) and a design note that single-family drafts should be context-weighted - a lab/registry question, not an expert behavior. Also the book's repeated 'candles give no price targets' point justifies pairing candle signals with Western targets.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

book_title: Trading ETFs: Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis (2nd ed., 2012) by Deron Wagner — Part 1 (Ch.1-10)

findings.strategy_name: Sector relative-strength rotation (top-down ETF selection)
findings.mechanism: Persistent relative strength is created by institutional sector rotation; sectors that resist broad-market drawdowns are the first to new highs on a bounce and the last to fall, so buying relative strength and shorting relative weakness both raises upside and lowers downside.
findings.setup_summary: On 60-min or daily percentage-change overlay charts vs a benchmark, find instruments that diverge persistently: sector holds sideways or higher while the broad market drops and outpaces it on bounces (longs), or vice versa (shorts). Never trade instruments moving in lockstep with the benchmark. Confirm with 'relative strength to itself': close in the upper 30% of the intraday range for longs, bottom 30% for shorts; the middle 40% is the 'danger zone'. Buy the leaders, not the laggards within the strong group.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Entry requires persistent divergence plus %-range close position; thesis invalid when the instrument closes in the danger zone (middle 40% of range) or reverts to benchmark parity.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: bar close or final-hour after divergence confirmed; stop below support; target not fixed - trail or sell into resistance; hold weeks to months (book average: several weeks).
findings.quote: Sectors with relative strength often generate double-digit percentage gains even while the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite are mostly unchanged.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.4 'Finding Indexes with the Most Relative Strength' + Ch.3 top-down summary; Ch.5 'Buy the Leaders, Not the Laggards'
findings.notes: Cross-coin relative strength (e.g. ETH/BTC leadership, alt rotation) is testable on perp pairs as a cross_market feature, but V8 currently trades a single instrument (BTCUSDT 1h), so this lands as selection methodology and feature input, not a standalone expert.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Broad-market trend confirmation before directional exposure
findings.mechanism: Roughly 85-90% of individual instruments move with the broad market, so trading against an unclearly-defined market regime is the surest way to lose; confirmed-trend regimes favor directional trading while range regimes chop accounts apart.
findings.setup_summary: A trend exists only when the reference index shows 2 higher highs + 2 higher lows (3 anchor points) for an uptrend (or 2 lower highs + 2 lower lows for a downtrend) AND price trades above both 20- and 50-day MAs with the 20-day closer to price and above the 50-day (mirror for downtrend). Multiple recent MA crossovers, or the 50-day trading closer to price than the 20-day, signal a choppy range - declare range-bound and avoid broad-market instruments. For multi-instrument books, require >=2 of 3 major indexes in confirmed trend before trading the broad market; otherwise trade only independently-trending sectors.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Uptrend invalid when a lower low forms below the trendline; trend stability invalid when 20/50 MA crossover clusters appear (range warning).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - admission gate: determines whether directional exposure is allowed at all, not a per-trade geometry.
findings.quote: Approximately 85 to 90 percent of stocks and ETFs move in the same general direction as the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite. Therefore, failure to clearly identify the direction of the broad market's trend before even considering which ETFs to buy or sell short is a surefire way to lose capital.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Determining the Direction of the Broad Market Trend' (trendline test + 20/50-day MA confirmation)
findings.notes: BTC is its own broad market, so the trendline (3-anchor, 2HH/2HL) + MA-alignment filter is directly implementable on BTCUSDT 1h and maps cleanly to a deterministic V8 regime gate on expert admission.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Volume confirmation of breakouts and distribution-day counting
findings.mechanism: Institutions cannot hide their footprint in volume; breakouts and trends lacking volume confirmation fail to follow through, volume leads price (not lags), and 'volume is the one indicator that never lies'.
findings.setup_summary: Require breakouts out of consolidation bases to spike to 200-300% of the instrument's own average daily volume (relative-to-itself, not absolute). Track accumulation days (up on higher volume) vs distribution days (down on higher volume): healthy markets absorb a couple of distribution days per month, but 5+ distribution days end even strong uptrends. Treat trends formed on light volume with caution and expect support breaks without volume confirmation to fail.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Breakout thesis weakens if volume does not confirm; >=5 distribution days in a month invalidates aggressive long exposure; a break of support that fails to follow through on volume is a bear trap (book's Feb-2003 E-mini example).
findings.risk_geometry: entry: breakout bar/session with 2-3x average volume; stops unchanged from setup; no explicit target.
findings.quote: As a rule of thumb, you want to see ETFs breaking out of bases of consolidation on at least 200 percent to 300 percent of their average daily volume levels.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 'Analyzing Volume' (accumulation/distribution days, 5-day vs 50-day volume MAs, intraday volume comparison)
findings.notes: Perp volume data exists; the relative-volume (vs its own average) framing is the correct 24/7 analog. Feeds the participation feature group and refines breakout-family volume gates.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: 200-period MA 'brick wall' and support/resistance polarity flip
findings.mechanism: The long-term MA acts as a magnet that initial tests rarely pierce; each subsequent test weakens it; after a firm break the level flips polarity (prior resistance becomes new support and vice versa).
findings.setup_summary: When price tests the 200-period MA (as support from above or resistance from below), the first test generally holds (book shows 1-5 failed attempts, e.g. $SOX tried 5 times against its 200-week MA); each retest raises the odds of a firm break; a break with confirmed volume signals a trend change and the level becomes the new support/resistance. Used as both entry trigger (MZZ long on 200-day-MA breakout of the inverse ETF) and exit/target (sell first test of 50-day MA resistance, e.g. GLD July-2006 exit).
findings.trigger_invalidation: A decisive high-volume break through the 200-period MA invalidates the 'wall holds' thesis; repeated failed reclaims after a break confirm real reversal (XHB: 4 failed 50-day-MA breakout attempts then success after an undercut).
findings.risk_geometry: entry: on break with volume, or on bounce off level; stop beyond the level; target: next major MA or prior high/low; timeframe-agnostic.
findings.quote: the 200-day MA simply acts like a brick wall whenever a stock, ETF, or index runs into it... Unless the dominant trend is really strong, it generally requires multiple tests of the 200-day MA before a position bursts through.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'The 200-Day Moving Average Brick Wall' (IWM, $SOX weekly, MZZ, ONEQ examples)
findings.notes: Level polarity and multi-test weakening are timeframe-agnostic and directly testable on BTCUSDT 1h; belongs in the location feature group and as an exit-target rule for trend families.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Pullback to the fast MA (10-day / hourly 20-MA) in an established strong trend
findings.mechanism: In strong established trends, institutional buying resumes at fast MAs; the strongest instruments pull back only to the fastest MA (often converging with the uptrend line) and power to new highs, rarely reaching slower MAs.
findings.setup_summary: Require an established trend (2 higher highs + 2 higher lows, 3 anchors). Buy the first test of the 10-day MA in a strong uptrend (or the hourly 20-MA as short entry resistance in a downtrend, book's IWM short), especially when the MA converges with the uptrend line; do not buy the very first touch - wait for confirmation on the next-lower timeframe (break of the hourly downslope / prior-day high). Stop below the 20-day MA. If price gaps to the 10-day MA but fails to close the session above it, scratch the trade.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A firm close below the fast MA invalidates the pullback (expects the leg to the 20-day); a firm close below the 20-day MA precedes a steeper correction to the 50-day; entries on the first touch without confirmation stop out frequently.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: test of 10-day MA with confirmation (next-bar or prior-day-high break); stop: below 20-day MA (or below retracement low); target: prior highs / upper trend channel or overhead resistance; expiry: days to weeks.
findings.quote: The strongest ETFs in the market typically pull back to their 10-day MAs and then power ahead to new highs... if an ETF gaps down to the 10-day MA on the open, but fails to close the session above it, you usually want to scratch the trade because the likelihood of a further correction down to the 20-day MA is high.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'Ten-Day Moving Average in Strong Trends' (FXI, INP) + Ch.7 'Pullbacks' (XLB 20-day-MA pullback, IWM short at hourly 20-MA)
findings.notes: V8's trend_pullback expert (ema_fast>ema_slow and close<ema_slow) is corroborated; this refines the entry to a faster-MA pullback with a scratch rule on close below the fast MA and stop below the slower MA.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Breakout above a downtrend line with retest-of-new-support confirmation
findings.mechanism: A prior resistance level becomes support after a break; a first retest that holds the broken line confirms the reversal, while a retest that breaches it exposes a 'fakeout'; longer-term trendlines dominate shorter-term ones.
findings.setup_summary: Wait for the first break of a clearly defined downtrend line (long side), then wait for the first minor retracement; enter above the prior day's high only if the pullback holds above the broken line (new support); stop below the retest low. Canonical book variant: instrument bounces off a long-term (weekly/monthly) uptrend line, then breaks the intermediate-term downtrend line; entry on the break (often converging with the 50-day MA), stop below the break day's low; exit into resistance of the 50-day MA or a prior high (GLD, SMH, IBB, PBW trades).
findings.trigger_invalidation: A retracement that pierces back below the broken line invalidates the reversal (fakeout); avoid first-break entries without retest confirmation ('blindly buying the first break').
findings.risk_geometry: entry: above prior day's high after a holding retest, or on the break with MA convergence; stop: below retest low / break-day low; target: prior highs (reward/risk often 3-4:1, min 2:1); hold days to weeks.
findings.quote: wait for the first minor retracement that follows. The idea is to make sure that the pullback does not breach new support of the prior downtrend line. If it does, the reversal attempt was likely a 'fakeout' to reel in the bulls.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.7 'Breakouts above Downtrend Lines' (GLD) + trade examples SMH (Ch.9), IBB (Ch.9), PBW (Ch.9), RKH short (Ch.10)
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family; trendline polarity is directly testable on 24/7 perp data and cleanly separable from the failed-breakout SHORT family.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Failed breakout to a new high -> reversal short
findings.mechanism: A breakout that fails to hold traps breakout buyers; forced exits by trapped longs plus new shorts create a fast downside vacuum that often falls to the 50-day MA quickly.
findings.setup_summary: Instrument makes a new high (ideally from a consolidation base) but holds it only briefly (book examples: 2 days) and closes back below the pivot; short the breakdown, or short the break of the 50-day MA after a one-day unconvincing bounce (XME). Intraday management: if a breakout entry is positioned to close the day below its pivotal resistance (wick above, body below on a daily candle), exit the same day - this marks a short/intermediate-term top, often after a stop hunt; a failed intraday breakout that follows through the next day can be reentered above the prior day's high. Gap-down below the pivot (DIA) is an especially bearish confirmation.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Reclaim of the pivot (or rally above the head in the H&S analog) invalidates the short; failed breakouts in strongly-trending markets fail at higher rate and should be sized/held shorter.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: break below pivot or below 50-day MA after failed bounce; stop: above pivot/head or above candle high (XME $65.82 above 10-day MA and down-candle high); target: prior low (e.g. June-14 low for MDY) or 50-day MA; short hold 1-5 days ('right or right out').
findings.quote: Not only must all the bulls who bought the consolidation close the position, but those who bought the breakout must as well. This sudden exodus triggers a wave of downward momentum that, in turn, attracts the attention of short sellers.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.7 breakout-failure discussion, Ch.8 'Strategies for Closing Losing Positions' (IWM Oct-2007, intraday rule), Ch.10 XME and DIA short trades
findings.notes: Directly corroborates V8's failed_breakout expert (SHORT, close below windowed prior high); book adds the intraday close-below-pivot rule and the failed-breakdown mirror (bear trap) as refinements.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Shakeout probe below support precedes successful breakout
findings.mechanism: A brief probe below an obvious support level or trendline shakes out weak hands and absorbs overhead supply; reclaiming the level within a few days leaves less supply to block the next breakout, so the probe-reclaim is structurally bullish.
findings.setup_summary: In the days before a successful breakout, the instrument undercuts a prior low or trendline support by a small margin, holds below for no more than a few days, and snaps back above it (FXI July-2005 gap below its base then reclaim, XHB Sept-2006 undercut of prior low then breakout 3 days later, SMH Jan-2005 one-week probe below weekly uptrend line, OIH inverted-hammer shakeout before breakout). Buy the subsequent breakout of the consolidation. Note the book also uses stop hunts to explain why entry orders placed only a few pennies above a prior high trigger prematurely - market makers/specialists push price just past the level to grab shares before reversal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Failure to reclaim above the probed level within a few days means the break was a real breakdown (trend reversal), not a shakeout; do not blindly buy every dip below support - wait for reclaim confirmation.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: breakout above the consolidation high after probe-reclaim (or reclaim above trendline); stop: below the probe low; target: new highs; expiry: days.
findings.quote: When an ETF moves marginally below a pivotal level of support for no more than a few days, and then promptly zooms back above it, it has the effect of shaking out the weak hands... This has the corresponding effect of absorbing a large amount of what would have been overhead supply.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.9 FXI, SMH, XHB trade examples + Ch.7 'stop hunts' (probes past highs/lows by market makers)
findings.notes: This is the V8 liquidity_sweep_reclaim mechanism; wick-based sweeps of liquidations/stop clusters are native to 24/7 leveraged crypto. The perp venue has no specialist, but clustered stop levels and liquidation cascades play the same role.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Head-and-shoulders top short with right-shoulder entry
findings.mechanism: Traders trapped long at the head and left shoulder sell into the next rally (preventing a higher high and forming the right shoulder); when price returns to the neckline the trapped positions capitulate and the neckline break draws shorts into a momentum collapse. The predicted drop equals the head-to-neckline distance below the neckline.
findings.setup_summary: Bearish H&S top (left shoulder + head + right shoulder + neckline) on any timeframe. Short during the right-shoulder formation (tight stop above the head, better reward/risk) or after a definitive neckline break (better confirmation, wider stop). Volume confirmation: lighter volume on the right shoulder than the left increases follow-through odds; rising right-shoulder volume is a warning. Target = head-to-neckline distance projected below the neckline (SPY 2002: ~10 points below ~$87 -> $77, hit exactly). Failure: rally above the head after the right shoulder = failed H&S with a powerful upward move (short squeeze + re-entry by shaken-out bulls) - a long setup. Timeframe-dependent completion: daily H&S takes weeks; hourly is more reliable in short-term bear phases. Book corroborates with a cross-market confirmation (hourly $OSX H&S + crude-oil lower high).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rally above the head invalidates the pattern (failed H&S -> strong counter-move); rising volume on the right shoulder warns of failure; stops must be respected until head/neckline levels are definitive.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: mid-right-shoulder formation or neckline break; stop: just above the head (short) / below the head (inverse long); target: head-to-neckline distance below neckline, or next support (book covered OIH at 50-day MA support, $139, instead of the $133 target); expiry: timeframe-dependent (daily H&S = several weeks).
findings.quote: My most profitable ETF short sales were often the result of capitalizing on this pattern... a relatively tight stop can be placed just over the top of the head, thereby creating much greater profit potential on a downward move than the risk of getting stopped out.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'Short Selling the Head-and-Shoulders Chart Pattern' (SPY 2002, IWM 2007) + Ch.10 OIH short (hourly $OSX H&S with crude lower high)
findings.notes: Recognizable on 1h crypto charts but H&S reliability on 24/7 leveraged markets is unproven; the more robust, falsifiable sub-claims are the failed-H&S counter-move (connects to failed_breakout) and the neckline-measured-target rule.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Swing-high/low trailing stops with 2:1 minimum reward/risk
findings.mechanism: Trailing stops just beyond swing highs/lows (with padding against stop hunts) lock in the bulk of a move without giving it all back; a 2:1 minimum reward/risk makes a 50% or lower batting average net profitable.
findings.setup_summary: For winners, especially breakouts to new highs (which have no overhead resistance to target), trail the protective stop below each successive swing low (longs) or above each swing high (shorts); move to breakeven after the first structure confirms (OIH: break of May low -> stop to breakeven, then trail above each bounce high). Never set stops exactly at swing levels - add padding (~15-20c intraday, ~1 point daily) against stop hunts. For short-term setups the minimum reward/risk is 2:1 on every entry. Exception: parabolic high-volume exhaustion moves (upper trend-channel probe + volume spike, e.g. IYR Feb-2007) - sell into strength rather than trail, because such moves mark at least a short-term top. Exit basis: trendline breaks on the trade's timeframe (hourly for short-term, daily/weekly for longer holds); a legitimate break shows a volume spike with a large down candle, minor probes without volume get more leeway.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A high-volume, big-candle break of the trailing line/structure = legitimate reversal, stop should have been hit; double-bottom or double-top structure near the stop warrants tightening (lock in gains).
findings.risk_geometry: entry: per setup; stop: padded swing extreme then trailing structure; target: none for new-high trades (stop-managed), prior high/low for others; expiry: none (stop-managed).
findings.quote: you always set the stop about 15 to 20 cents above on an intraday chart, or a point above on a daily chart, which prevents the stop from getting triggered before you want it to by the specialists and market makers.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.8 'Trailing Stops' (OIH trailing example, IYR parabolic), Ch.6 reward/risk rule (SPY H&S ~2:1 'minimum ratio to look for with all long and short setups')
findings.notes: Swing-high/low trailing with padding is directly implementable on BTCUSDT 1h and aligns with V8's risk_geometry (stop/target/expiry) and lifecycle exits. Padding rationale survives venue transfer: stop clusters at round numbers and swing extremes exist in perps even without designated market makers.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Opening-gap entry and stop rules
findings.mechanism: Gaps reflect overnight supply/demand imbalance; entering immediately at a gapped trigger price is higher-risk because the gap often marks the day's extreme, so confirmation (first-20-minute range resolution) is required, and gapped stops should be re-anchored to the 20-minute extreme.
findings.setup_summary: Four rules, all anchored to a daily session clock: (1) If a trigger is hit by an opening gap, enter only after the instrument trades through its first-20-minute high (longs) / low (shorts) by >=10 cents; ignore gaps under 10 cents. (2) If an open position gaps beyond its stop, hold the first 20 minutes then re-anchor the stop to 10c below the 20-min low (longs) / 10c above the 20-min high (shorts). (3) Gap >=2% in the trade's favor overnight: sell half at the open to lock gains, keep half with a tightened stop. (4) Gap >=2% against overnight: wait 5 minutes, cut if the 5-minute low breaks, else sell into the 9:50-reversal bounce near the 20-minute high.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Failure to break the 20-minute extreme after a gap usually means the gap was the day's extreme - stand aside; rule 4 exists to minimize (not avoid) the loss on adverse gaps.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: 20-minute range break with 10c padding; stop: 20c below morning low (gap-up longs) or re-anchored at 20-min extreme for gapped stops.
findings.quote: ETFs that gap open beyond their trigger prices. For a long setup, buy the ETF only if it subsequently sets a new high after the first 20 minutes of trading.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.7 'The Opening-Gap Rules' (rules 1-4; 9:50 a.m. reversal period); applied in Ch.10 DIA short
findings.notes: The rules depend on a daily close-to-open discontinuity and a fixed session clock (20-minute opening range, 9:50 reversal). Crypto perps trade 24/7 with no exchange-level gap, so the trigger mechanism does not exist; perp analogs (funding-induced jumps, weekend session boundaries) are separate phenomena with their own structure.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Contango/rollover and leveraged-ETF daily-reset decay
findings.mechanism: Rolling expiring futures into dearer forward months (contango) and daily re-leveraging of leveraged/inverse products both impose a structural, compounding drag on buy-and-hold, so the vehicle systematically underperforms the index it tracks.
findings.setup_summary: Quantified decay: USO fell ~48% from inception (2006) to mid-2011 vs -30.1% for E-mini crude (~18% underperformance in 5 years); UNG similarly underperformed natural-gas futures; over H1-2009 the S&P 500 returned +3.16% while a 2x long returned -0.68%, a 1x inverse -8.91%, and a 2x inverse -21.68% - all from daily resets/rolls, not from index direction. Commodities with easy physical delivery (gold, silver) escape the roll drag. Front-running speculators and 'rollover' each month mechanically guarantee the loss. Lesson for V8: funding on perps is the structural analog - persistent positive funding is a roll-like drag on longs; the simulator's Binance USDM cost model must price funding and basis, and any multi-leverage or inverse construction must not be treated as a 1x underlying.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - vehicle-structure lesson, not a trade trigger.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A
findings.quote: Unless the fund is able to take delivery of the physical commodity, the ETF is virtually guaranteed to underperform its index due to the effects of rollover, contango, fees, and front running.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.2 'The Hazards of Contango' (USO/UNG/GLD/SLV figures) and 'Unraveling the Leveraged ETF Mystery' (Table 2.2 daily-reset returns)
findings.notes: The only finding with quantified empirical tables (Morningstar-sourced daily-reset returns, multi-year USO/UNG/GLD/SLV vs continuous-contract comparisons). Transfers to perps as funding/basis cost modeling in the simulator; no economic claim is made about funding trading.

book_title: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques, 2nd Edition (Steve Nison, 2001) — Part 2

findings.strategy_name: Box range breakout with measured-move target
findings.mechanism: consolidated box stores pent-up energy; a close-breakout projects a move at least equal to the vertical height of the box
findings.setup_summary: Price trades inside a well-defined horizontal box range (Japanese 'box range', e.g., $50-$53) for an extended period; enter when a bar CLOSES outside the box (intraday penetration that does not close through leaves the level intact). Target = box height added to the broken boundary on the upside ($56) or subtracted on the downside ($47). Invalidation: a close back inside the box voids the target (change of polarity).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close outside a multi-touch box boundary. Thesis invalidated when price closes back inside the box (e.g., 'if the index had closed back above 3600, it would have voided my downside target of 2750'); mere intraday tag of the boundary does not break it.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at bar close on the breakout; target = box height projected from the broken boundary; invalidation = close back inside the box; targets are not stop/entry levels in their own right.
findings.quote: When a breakout from box range unfolds, the market has good potential continuing in the direction of the breakout.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 16, 'Breakouts from Boxes' (pp. 250-255, Exhibits 16.1-16.5)
findings.notes: Corroborates and extends the DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family with a falsifiable target rule (range-height projection) and a close-based invalidation. Crypto is dominated by lateral ranges; 24/7 no-gap closes make the close-break rule clean, but false breaks/liquidity sweeps are frequent, so the close-reclaim invalidation is load-bearing. Ascending/descending triangles (same chapter) are trended variants sharing the height-projection measurement.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Measured-move price targets used for exits only
findings.mechanism: Western measured objectives (box height, flagpole, triangle height) forecast reversal extent; they offset existing positions, never initiate new ones
findings.setup_summary: Compute a measured objective from a completed Western pattern (box breakout, swing target, flag/pennant flagpole, triangle height) and use it to exit or trim an existing position. A price target is not synonymous with support/resistance, does not guarantee the price will stop there, and does not predict the extent of a reversal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — an exit methodology, not an entry trigger. Reaching a target does not justify a counter-position without independent reversal confirmation.
findings.risk_geometry: Target-based exit: box-height/flagpole/triangle-height projected from the broken level; conservative variant projects flag objectives from the bottom of the flag rather than the top ('I prefer to err on exiting too early').
findings.quote: one should not look at a price objective to initiate a new position, but to offset an outstanding position.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 16 intro (p. 249)
findings.notes: Directly informs V8 risk_geometry target semantics: measured objectives are exits, and target != level (no auto-fade at target). Reinforces that stops and dead-thesis are distinct exits in the lifecycle.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Stochastic oversold + positive divergence + %K/%D cross with candle confirmation
findings.mechanism: close near range low + divergence + fast/slow cross flags momentum turn; a candlestick pattern confirms the turn
findings.setup_summary: After a decline: %D <= 20 (oversold), positive divergence (price lower low while stochastic makes a higher low), %K crosses above %D, and a bullish candlestick (e.g., hammer) confirms. Mirror for tops: %D >= 80, negative divergence, %K crossing under %D.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: %D<=20 + positive divergence + %K/%D bullish cross + candle confirmation. Invalidation: close below the confirming candle's low ('if the stock had pulled under the hammer's low then, in spite of the positive stochastic reading, one should consider vacating longs').
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the confirmed candle's close; stop under the signal candle's low; book gives no target or expiry (open-ended mean reversion).
findings.quote: to get a buy signal, the market must be oversold (20% or less for %D), there is positive divergence, and the %K line is crossing above the %D line.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 14, 'Using Stochastics' (pp. 233-237, Exhibits 14.6-14.7)
findings.notes: Mean-reversion family — no active expert today; complexity budget caps at 3 actives, so this is a backlog candidate. Crypto 1h trends persist and oversold can stay sticky (liquidation cascades); must be gated by a trend-regime filter (see regime_filter) before screening.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Oscillator divergence confirmed by a reversal candle (exit/trim signal)
findings.mechanism: price makes a new extreme while the oscillator (MA oscillator, stochastic, MACD) fails to confirm = momentum failure; a reversal candle converts divergence into an actionable signal
findings.setup_summary: At a resistance/support area: price makes a new high (low) while the oscillator makes a lower high (higher low); a confirming bearish (bullish) candle (bearish engulfing, hanging man, shooting star) makes the signal actionable. Primary stated use: when a stock is overextended and a candlestick confirms a turn, exit or lighten longs; mirror for shorts.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence + confirming candle. Invalidation: no candle confirmation = no signal ('we would not look to sell' on oscillator alone); hanging man requires a close under its real body next session for bearish confirmation.
findings.risk_geometry: Exit/trim rule applied at overbought/oversold oscillator readings; confirmation and level breaks are close-based.
findings.quote: at the time of that pattern the stock had made a new high and the moving average oscillator had made a lower high. This formed bearish or negative divergence.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 14, Exhibit 14.5 (pp. 232-233); MACD section (pp. 237-239)
findings.notes: Primary V8 value is an oscillator-divergence feature (windowed price extrema vs smoothed momentum extrema) in marketstate, consumed by other families as confirmation; the exit framing supports a lifecycle rule for trimming overextended positions. Divergence is noisy in crypto 1h and is treated here as confirmation, not a standalone entry.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Relative-volume confirmation of candle patterns and breakouts
findings.mechanism: 'Volume is like water pressure in a hose': heavier volume on the confirming candle/breakout validates the price signal, while the setup candle should be relatively light
findings.setup_summary: For any reversal/continuation candle pattern, check relative volume vs preceding sessions: a bullish engulfing/piercing pattern should show lighter volume on the first candle and heavier volume on the confirming candle; a hammer or rising-window break gains significance with a volume spike. Upside breakouts to new highs should be accompanied by a volume push — a low-volume new high is a reason to be circumspect. Volume should increase in the direction of the trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not a standalone trigger — a confirmation overlay. Adds no value on flat volume; low-volume breakout warrants caution but not a fade.
findings.risk_geometry: No independent entry/stop/target; modulates aggressiveness (a high-volume hammer allows buying the close more aggressively because retracement to the hammer low is less likely).
findings.quote: a bearish engulfing pattern should have a lighter volume on the first candle (the white) and a heavier volume on the second candle (the black) to increase the bearish engulfing pattern's significance.
findings.notes: Maps to the 'participation' feature group. Crypto perp volume includes wash/manipulation noise and liquidation-driven spikes; use relative volume (quantile vs lookback), never absolute, exactly as the book advises. High value as a confirmation filter on candlestick families (engulfing, hammer, failed_breakout).
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: High-volume doji/spinning top at extremes — supply absorption / exhaustion
findings.mechanism: heavy supply during a decline absorbed by equally aggressive demand (small range on huge volume = absorption); after an extended advance, huge volume meeting the bulls' drive = possible top
findings.setup_summary: After a steep decline into a support area, an unusually high-volume doji or spinning-top bar forms: the high volume proves heavy supply while the small range proves demand absorbed it, increasing the odds of a turn vs a normal-volume session. Mirror: a very high-volume doji/spinning top after an extended advance is a possible top reversal (the bulls' drive met with enough supply to stall).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: relative volume spike on a doji/small real body at a support area (decline) or after an extended advance. Invalidation: the high-volume bar has a large directional body (no absorption) or price closes through the support area.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry after a confirming candle; stop under the signal bar's low; support reference often anchored to prior pattern lows (e.g., engulfing lows); target not specified in the book.
findings.quote: A very heavy-volume doji or small real body during a steep decline shows that heavy supply is being taken by the equally aggressive demand.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 15, 'Integrating High Volume with Spinning Tops or Doji' (pp. 246-247, Exhibit 15.4)
findings.notes: Feeds the DATA_BLOCKED capitulation backlog family (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion). On crypto perps, liquidation-cascade volume spikes make this observable on 1h, but the same spikes can be self-fulfilling; require the absorption (small real body) condition, not volume alone.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Flag/pennant and swing-target continuation with flagpole projection
findings.mechanism: sharp impulse + short lateral/countertrend consolidation + resumption; measured target = flagpole height projected from the consolidation
findings.setup_summary: A clean sharp advance (flagpole A to B) is followed by a short congestion band (flag = horizontal box; pennant = lower highs and higher lows), then price resumes the prior trend by breaking the consolidation. Target = flagpole height projected from the bottom of the band for longs (conservative) and from the top for shorts. Swing-target variant projects the first-leg channel height from the correction low/high.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: resumption break out of the consolidation following a defined impulse. Invalidation: the band resolves against the prior trend (e.g., bull flag breaks below flag support) or price closes back into the band.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the resumption break; target = flagpole height from the bottom/top of the congestion band; stop = opposite side of the band.
findings.quote: the height of the first leg is a rally from A to B. There is then a correction to C. Once the market ascends from C, we would 'swing' the initial channel height of A to B onto the correction low at C.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 16, 'Swing Targets, Flags, and Pennants' (pp. 255-260)
findings.notes: Continuation family. On crypto 1h the flagpole/consolidation structure is fuzzy; the falsifiable core is impulse -> range -> resumption with a projected target. Overlaps trend_pullback in spirit but differs by requiring a defined consolidation band and a measured objective.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Spring and Upthrust — false break and reclaim (change of polarity)
findings.mechanism: false breakdown/breakout through a horizontal congestion boundary that fails to hold, then reclaim through the 'broken' level = trap; target back to the opposite end of the range
findings.setup_summary: Spring (long): prices break under horizontal congestion support then spring back above the 'broken' support — bullish, with a measured target to the upper end of the congestion band. Upthrust (short): prices break above a resistance line from a lateral zone, fail to hold, and pull back under the 'broken' resistance — target is a retest of the lower end of the recent trading zone.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: penetration of a horizontal boundary that fails to hold (close reclaims the boundary). Invalidation: the break holds on a close (a genuine breakout — see the donchian_breakout family).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the reclaim close; stop on the failed-break extreme (below the spring low / above the upthrust high); target = opposite end of the congestion band; old support converts to resistance (change of polarity).
findings.quote: Spring When prices break under the support of a horizontal congestion band and then springs back above the 'broken support' area. This is bullish and there is a measured price target to the upper end of the congestion band.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary B, 'Spring' and 'Upthrust' (p. 283); change-of-polarity principle
findings.notes: Corroborates the FORMALIZED liquidity_sweep_reclaim expert (wick through windowed prior extreme reclaimed by close) and the failed_breakout family; adds the polarity-target semantics (retest of the opposite end of the range). Crypto's sweep-heavy microstructure (stop clusters above/below ranges) makes this directly testable on 1h.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Trend-regime gate on candle reversal signals
findings.mechanism: a reversal candle's meaning is conditional on the larger trend regime; a bullish signal in a bear market is not a buy signal
findings.setup_summary: Gate all candlestick reversal signals by the prevailing trend regime: a bullish candle pattern in a major bear market is not a buy signal, while a bullish formation confirmed by other technicals within a bull market is a buying point. 'Where you stand in relation to the overall technical evidence may be more important than an individual candle pattern.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — a filter. Long setups with a bearish regime are skipped (or flagged for counter-trend study only); single-pattern signals without regime confirmation are not traded.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target of its own; modulates admission at the RiskGate.
findings.quote: a bullish candle signal in a major bear market should not be used as a buy signal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Conclusion (p. 268); Ch 17 convergence discussion (pp. 263-265)
findings.notes: Directly supports a RiskGate/regime admission rule for counter-trend candle experts (e.g., stochastic/hammer mean-reversion setups). A 1h trend-regime classifier (EMA stack, higher-timeframe slope) is computable offline and deterministic.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Signal convergence at a price level strengthens reversal calls
findings.mechanism: multiple independent signal families (candles + Western) converging in a narrow price zone raise the probability of a reversal; convergence does not project the extent of the move
findings.setup_summary: A reversal is more credible when several independent signals cluster in the same price area. Example: shooting star + bearish engulfing + falling window + high-wave candle + rising resistance line + oscillator divergence all converging in one zone called a major NASDAQ top. Candles frequently give the turning signal ahead of Western indicators (dark-cloud cover preceded MACD reversal by almost a week).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Confidence is graded by how many independent families agree at the same level; no single-family signal is sufficient on its own, and even strong convergence does not forecast correction depth.
findings.risk_geometry: No standalone risk geometry; informs confirmation strength for other families.
findings.quote: This cluster of signals converging in the 5050-5150 area greatly strengthened the prognosis that the NASDAQ had reached a ceiling.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 17 (pp. 263-265); Ch 14 MACD example (pp. 238-239)
findings.notes: Evidence is a single case study (NARRATIVE), so treat as a design hypothesis to be tested, not a finding. In V8 this argues for per-expert confirmation counting across feature groups; the shared scorer/ranker stays ABSENT by default (rule 14) until a registry challenger beats the simpler baseline on frozen OOS.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Close-based confirmation for reversal candles and S/R levels
findings.mechanism: reversal candle signals require a close-based confirmation bar; support/resistance is defined by closes, not intraday extremes
findings.setup_summary: Hanging man requires a close under its real body the next session for bearish confirmation; inverted hammer requires a higher open and especially a higher close. Pattern-derived resistance/support holds on closes: pushing above an evening star's resistance intraday without closing above it leaves the level intact. A doji confirming hesitation needs a close under the nearby window to damage the trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A candle signal without close-based confirmation is not actionable; an intraday tag of a level without a close-through is not a break.
findings.risk_geometry: The confirmation bar defines the entry reference and the invalidation level (e.g., close under the hammer's low voids the bullish stochastic read).
findings.quote: for bearish confirmation of a hanging man, we need a close under the hanging man's real body.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 14, Exhibit 14.5 (p. 232); Ch 16 evening-star resistance (pp. 258-259)
findings.notes: Validates V8's existing NEXT_BAR_CLOSE entry semantics and close-based still_valid exits; the close-defined S/R rule is a natural close-relative location feature (not wick-relative) for the location feature group.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Windows (gaps) as support/resistance
findings.mechanism: a price void (window) acts as support (rising) or resistance (falling); closing the window damages the trend thesis
findings.setup_summary: A rising window (gap up, entire range above the prior bar) is a bullish signal and should act as support; a falling window is a bearish signal and acts as resistance. High-volume windows are stronger levels. A close through the window confirms damage to the trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The window level survives until price closes back through it; a close through voids it.
findings.risk_geometry: Window = frozen level (support/resistance); break-and-close through it invalidates.
findings.quote: When the market opens a window to the upside, it is a rising window. It is a bullish signal and the rising window should be support.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary A, 'Windows' (p. 278); Ch 15 (Exhibit 15.3)
findings.notes: 24/7 perp trading has no exchange gaps, so literal windows are rare (only whole-bar range discontinuities, e.g., around funding/listing events). The survivable core — prior session extremes as S/R — is already covered by the supply_demand_zone and sweep families. Reject the gap mechanic itself; optionally salvage a 'session-extreme level' feature.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

findings.strategy_name: Failed breakout short (overhead resistance)
findings.mechanism: a failed breakout above a consolidation with overhead resistance leaves trapped bulls and a liquidity vacuum that pulls price back down through the level
findings.setup_summary: Daily: after price breaks above a multi-week consolidation/prior high, it closes back below that level (breakout failure), ideally making a lower high; enter short on the break of a confirmatory level such as the 50-day MA or the prior day's low. Target is the prior swing low; stop above the failed-breakout extreme.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close below the 50-day MA or prior day's low after a failed breakout above overhead resistance. Invalidation: price reclaims back above the broken level/MA.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar-close break below confirmatory level (FXI: short 30-40 cents below the Feb 23 low). Stop: just above the failed-breakout high / prior day's high. Target: prior swing low, cover on test of support. Expiry: days to weeks.
findings.quote: breakouts above consolidations often fail when there are prior levels of overhead resistance
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'Ten ETFs Sold Short' (IWM, FXI, DIA)
findings.notes: Multiple worked examples corroborate the existing V8 failed_breakout expert; adds MA-break and prior-day-low as alternative entry triggers for the same family.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Failed reclaim of broken 50-day MA (bounce into resistance)
findings.mechanism: after a breakdown below a pivotal MA, the broken MA flips to resistance; a retracement that fails to reclaim it confirms downtrend resumption
findings.setup_summary: Daily: price closes below its 50-day MA for the first time in months (also breaking the primary uptrend line), then retraces up to the MA and fails to reclaim it on two separate tests; short the following day on a break below the prior day's low.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: two failed tests of the broken-MA resistance, then break below prior day's low. Invalidation: close back above the 50-day MA.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: break of prior day's low below established MA resistance. Stop: above the MA-resistance test high. Target: prior swing low, cover into weakness on the test. Expiry: days to ~2 weeks.
findings.quote: In both tests, new resistance of the 50-day MA perfectly marked the highs of each day's rally
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'Bounce into Resistance of a 50-Day MA' (OIH)
findings.notes: Distinct from failed_breakout: the reference level is a broken MA now acting as resistance and the setup is a failed reclaim of broken support (S/R flip), not a failed upside breakout of a prior high.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Symmetrical triangle / volatility-compression expansion
findings.mechanism: prices oscillating in a tightening range compress volatility; resolution is a large expansion, and a failed breakout on one side accelerates the move against the trapped side
findings.setup_summary: Daily: several weeks of tightening highs/lows form a symmetrical triangle (volatility contraction). The book's variant: price first rallies above the upper channel (drawing in bulls) and fails, then short the break of the lower channel below the 20/50-day MAs; the long mirror applies on the upper-channel break.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: break below the lower channel (or above the upper channel for longs). Invalidation: close back inside the triangle.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: short ~30-40c below the failed-breakout low / below MAs. Stop: above the failed-breakout high. Target: prior swing low. Expiry: short, days.
findings.quote: It is merely a pattern that predicts a large expansion of volatility
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'Break of a Symmetrical Triangle Chart Pattern' (FXI)
findings.notes: Direction-neutral compression-to-expansion mechanism; book trades the failed-breakout variant. Compression is measurable as a declining ATR/range ratio in the window.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Intraday relative-strength momentum (top-down)
findings.mechanism: instruments showing the largest gap-adjusted strength from the open while trading in the top third of their intraday range tend to lead the session; buying the strongest into strength captures continuation
findings.setup_summary: Intraday: rank sector indexes by % change at open+5min and open+30min; keep the one with the largest move since the open (gap-adjusted), still in the top (bottom) third of its intraday range, with first-30min volume >= its 5-day average; buy the strongest ETF within the sector on a 0.382 Fibonacci retracement of the first-30-min range or on a break above the first-30-min high.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 0.382 retracement fills or opening-range breakout; if no retracement by open+45min, 'correction by time' -> enter at market. Invalidation: index falls out of the top/bottom third of its intraday range.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit at 0.382 retracement or market on breakout/time-correction. Stop: below intraday swing or the preplanned multiweek stop. Target: day-trade via 5/15-min MAs and trendlines, or the multiweek target.
findings.quote: sectors that don't fall with the broad market will be the first ones to rally to new highs when the major indexes eventually bounce
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'Identifying Relative Strength Intraday'
findings.notes: The 9:35/10:00 session anchors do not exist in a 24/7 market, but the cross-sectional relative-strength core ('buy the leaders, not the laggards') is testable with trailing-window strength across perp instruments.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: ATR-relative position sizing (Size Ratio)
findings.mechanism: sizing position size and stop distance as a function of volatility relative to price keeps per-trade dollar risk constant across instruments
findings.setup_summary: Size Ratio = 10-day average close / 50-day ATR. Baseline exposure (e.g. 5% of capital); if Ratio < 50, cut position size 25% and widen the protective stop 25%; if Ratio > 75, raise size 25% and tighten the stop 25%.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (sizing rule, not an entry signal).
findings.risk_geometry: Stop distance scaled inversely with the Size Ratio so net dollar risk stays constant per trade.
findings.quote: Average closing price of last 10 days / 50-day ATR = Size Ratio
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'Position Sizing'
findings.notes: Author is explicit these are experience-derived guidelines, 'not derived from any high-tech mathematical algorithm'. Directly transferable to perp volatility targeting.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Minimum 2:1 reward/risk gate with extension filter
findings.mechanism: only take trades whose structural target is at least twice the stop distance, and skip entries too far extended from their breakout pivot where downside risk outweighs upside
findings.setup_summary: Before entry require (target - entry) / (entry - stop) >= 2. Do not buy after a large quick extension (e.g. >20% in three days) or at an extended 52-week high; prefer the breakout-then-tight-consolidation base over the extended move.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Skip the trade if R:R < 2:1 or entry is beyond the breakout pivot by more than a few percent.
findings.risk_geometry: Risk = points entry-to-stop; reward = points entry-to-projected target.
findings.quote: If the downside risk outweighs the profit potential, don't make the trade... especially if the reward is at least double the risk (2:1 reward/risk ratio)
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'Always Use Reward/Risk Ratios'
findings.notes: The extension filter is especially relevant on leveraged perps where late entries into extended moves face deep pullbacks.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Stop wiggle room below obvious levels (withstanding stop hunts)
findings.mechanism: stops clustered at the obvious trendline/MA level are run first; a volatility-scaled buffer below obvious support avoids false stop-outs while keeping risk bounded
findings.setup_summary: For 1-3 week holds, draw the 60/120-min uptrend/downtrend line and place the stop below it by a volatility-scaled buffer (~0.2x ATR; 10c on a 50c ATR) rather than at it; never place a break-even stop exactly on an obvious trendline (OIH's breakeven coincided with the hourly uptrend line and was probed).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Placement rule; thesis-invalidation remains a clean close beyond the buffer level.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop ~1 point below the 20-day EMA or ~0.2x ATR below trendline support; looser stop paired with smaller share size.
findings.quote: Is my stop placement too obvious? If it is, you can be assured that you will be stopped out, only to watch the stock or ETF reverse in the right direction
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'Withstanding Stop Hunts'
findings.notes: Crypto has no specialist/market-maker, but liquidation clusters and MEV bots target obvious stop levels; the buffer principle transfers while the manipulator narrative is venue-specific.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Sitting-on-hands (SOH) no-trade regime filter
findings.mechanism: in regimes where breakouts fail, breadth diverges, volume dries up, or big news looms, edge is absent and standing aside preserves capital
findings.setup_summary: Stand aside when: (a) major indexes diverge (one breaking down, another at new highs), (b) an elevated share of breakouts fail within a day or two, (c) aggregate volume runs well below its 50-day average, or (d) highly anticipated macro news is pending.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Activate on any listed condition; deactivate when conditions normalize.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry; cash is a valid position.
findings.quote: The most consistently profitable professional traders are actually out of the markets more than they are in the markets
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'Know When to Be in SOH Mode'
findings.notes: Measurable crypto analogs: BTC/ETH divergence, failing breakout breadth, declining perp volume, FOMC/CPI event windows.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Round-number trigger and stop placement
findings.mechanism: orders cluster at psychologically salient whole numbers, so price probes just beyond them before reversing and clustered stops at round levels get run
findings.setup_summary: Set buy triggers just below the whole number and sell/exit limits just above it (e.g. sell at 48.98, not 49.00); never set protective stops exactly at whole numbers.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Placement rule, not an entry signal; ignore if fills prove unreliable.
findings.risk_geometry: Trigger/exit offsets of a few cents from round numbers improve fill odds.
findings.quote: both buy triggers and protective stops should not be set exactly at whole numbers
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'Support and Resistance at the Whole Numbers'
findings.notes: Round-number order clustering is observed in BTC (e.g. 100k); the specialist-exploitation driver is venue-specific, but placement discipline transfers.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Evaluate decisions, not outcomes
findings.mechanism: judging trades by P&L alone reinforces habits formed by lucky or undisciplined winners; evaluating by whether the same decision would be repeated builds the right long-run habits
findings.setup_summary: Post-trade, ask 'would I do the same thing again, knowing what I now know?' - a yes means the trade was correct even if it lost. Keep a trading journal of honest observations and statistics ('performance measured is performance gained').
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (evaluation methodology).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A
findings.quote: Would I do the same thing again, knowing what I now know?
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'Assessing Your Trades'
findings.notes: Reinforces V8's separation of decision quality from outcome in the offline learning protocol.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Breakout trigger discipline: confirm with an ATR-scaled buffer
findings.mechanism: false breakouts are common at obvious levels; requiring price to exceed resistance by a volatility-scaled buffer makes the breakout self-confirming and filters fakeouts
findings.setup_summary: The entry trigger is always above resistance / below support by a buffer (~0.2x ATR: QQQQ 3-day high 47.87 + 10c on a 50c ATR -> trigger 47.97-48.02) and is never pre-empted; if the trigger is not hit, there is no trade.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger must be touched/cleared; missing it means no entry (QQQQ probed only 5c above the 3-day high before reversing).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: break of level + ATR buffer; stop below/above the level; target: structure. Paying a slightly worse price for a higher confirmation probability.
findings.quote: It's always better to pay a slightly higher price for entry, in exchange for a better chance of not getting sucked into a false breakout
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'Proper Trigger Prices' + QQQQ example
findings.notes: Refines the backlog breakout_retest family; wick-throughs above resistance are frequent on 24/7 crypto, so the buffer is a practical fakeout filter.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

findings.strategy_name: Target-and-exit at structural level (take the gift)
findings.mechanism: covering at the predetermined structural target (test of prior support/resistance) captures the bulk of the move with minimal risk even when continuation is possible; greed invites giving it back
findings.setup_summary: Set the target at a prior swing low/high and cover on the test of that level regardless of whether further move is likely (IWM target = January low; FXI target = Jan 10 low; OIH covered on the test of its prior low). If the exit looks premature, the resulting bounce offers a better reentry.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Exit at the predetermined structural target; a reversal before target is handled by the protective stop.
findings.risk_geometry: Target = structural prior extreme; exit on the test; reentry on the subsequent bounce.
findings.quote: I covered on the test of the prior low, the original downside price target having been satisfactorily achieved
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 IWM short (also FXI, OIH)
findings.notes: Supports structural (S/R-based) targets over pure fixed-R targets in V8 risk_geometry.
findings.book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

book_title: Trading ETFs: Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis (2nd ed., 2012) by Deron Wagner — Part 2

findings.strategy_name: Trading-range mean-reversion with boundary invalidation
findings.mechanism: range containment breaks are the only thesis killers; reversion to the mean-reversion price/area inside a bounded range is the entry
findings.setup_summary: Define a trading range on the 1h chart from at least two reaction highs (resistance) and two reaction lows (support) plus the mean-reversion price/area (the level price keeps returning to while meandering). When price reverts to the mean-reversion area, enter expecting containment inside the range; the trade thesis is dead the instant price breaks a key support/resistance boundary.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Entry zone = mean-reversion price/area inside the range. Thesis invalidated on a break through the range boundary (support or resistance) - exit immediately regardless of P&L - or when the projected time in the range expires. More touches at a level make it 'stronger'.
