Wang 2001 (buy spec sentiment >80% + fade hedger sentiment <20%) is the empirical anchor, annualized 18.9-43.8% across 2-8 week holds.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: COT Movement Index rate-of-change surge
findings.mechanism: The RATE of change of positioning toward an extreme marks when a counter-trend reaction has exhausted itself; a surge that then fails to restart the prevailing trend is a regime-change alert.
findings.setup_summary: Weekly: Movement Index = COT Index(t) - COT Index(t-6 weeks). A +40 point buying surge during a correction in an uptrend marks the end of the pullback (re-buy); a -40 point selling surge during a bounce in a downtrend marks the end of the reaction (re-sell). If a +/-40 point surge fails to restart the prevailing trend, expect a major trend change - this is the signal's most valuable mode.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: +/-40 points in a 6-week window while a counter-trend reaction is underway. Invalidation: the surge does not resume the prevailing trend - that failure is itself the tip-off to a major trend change (e.g., pound rallying straight through a -40 point reading ended the major downtrend).
findings.risk_geometry: No stop/target stated. Signals time entries in the direction of the prevailing trend; in flat ranges +/-40 signals replace COT climaxes as the useful trigger. Wang 2003's 1-standard-deviation net-position-change rule is the statistical analog and generates a high percentage of simultaneous signals.
findings.quote: A ±40 point surge in the COT Index within a six-week period frequently marks the end of a counter-trend price reaction.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, COT Movement Index, pp. 75-81
findings.notes: The +/-40 point / 6-week threshold is a practitioner heuristic (cross-validated by Wang 2003's 1-sigma rule), and it needs a weekly positioning series that crypto does not natively have; funding/OI rate-of-change could stand in but the weekly cadence and commercial proxy are both weak.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Fund capacity exhaustion breakout failure
findings.mechanism: Trend-following funds fuel breakouts; when their net long is already at its record/prior capacity while price retests a prior high, there is insufficient remaining speculative buying power to force a breakout, so the retest fails.
findings.setup_summary: Weekly: price approaches its prior high while the large-speculator (fund) net position has already matched its prior record net long - i.e., buying capacity reached its previous limit. Expect the breakout to fail. The entry is not at the failed high but on the break below the prior reaction trough (support), once it is obvious funds are not buying and are liquidating.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: fund net long at its prior-high capacity while price retests the high. Invalidation: fund net position shows it has NOT exhausted buying capacity (new buying power available) - then a breakout attempt may succeed; also a lack of buying INTEREST (not capacity) can fail a breakout, which is less predictable.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on break below prior support trough (swing point); the failed-breakout top itself is not the entry level; book implies stop above the failed high.
findings.quote: If a breakout relies on speculative buying (and most do), fund net positions can tip off their remaining buying power.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 5, Net Positions, pp. 47-61 (Figure 5.7)
findings.notes: Directly refines V8's existing failed_breakout family (liquidity_vacuum_reentry): add a crowding-exhaustion precondition, proxied in crypto by funding-rate percentile + OI blow-off at highs. Crypto 1h is momentum-dominated, so a failed-breakout-with-positioning-exhaustion filter is falsifiable on the existing tape. Positive-feedback-fund premise is literature-supported (Ch 8 studies); the capacity-exhaustion prediction is chart-based inference.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Fund selling exhaustion divergence bottom
findings.mechanism: Funds are positive-feedback traders; when price makes a new low but the fund net position refuses to make a new low (higher bottom), speculative selling is provably subsiding - exhaustion - tipping a major bottom.
findings.setup_summary: Weekly: during a downtrend, price prints a new low while the large-speculator net position forms a higher bottom than its prior extreme. This is a momentum-style non-confirmation but on positioning data, and the book calls it 'proof positive' that speculative selling is subsiding: bank short profits and take an early long entry into the new uptrend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price new low + fund net position higher bottom. Invalidation: fund net position also makes a new low (no divergence); also, trend changes at D/Z only count when funds stop short of their previous extremes.
findings.risk_geometry: Early long entry at the divergence; stop and target not specified; Ch 10 adds: if funds hold a near-record net position in the trend direction, tighten the trailing stop rather than trying to pick the exact top/bottom.
findings.quote: In the case of the fund net position, it is not just a sign; it is proof positive that speculative selling is subsiding.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 5, Net Positions, Figure 5.8 (Fund Selling Exhaustion Marks a Major Bottom)
findings.notes: Refines the existing capitulation backlog family (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion) with a positioning-divergence variant: in crypto, OI/funding divergence at a price low (e.g., funding deeply negative while OI falls / long interest already flushed) is observable on the 1h tape. Caveat: crypto 'selling exhaustion' is often liquidation-cascade-driven, a different causal texture than COT fund behavior.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Abrupt sentiment reversal regime rule
findings.mechanism: A sudden 180-degree flip in the net position of the crowd that had been fueling the trend means the current trend has overshot; anticipate a reversal regardless of which direction the new signal points.
findings.setup_summary: Weekly: after an extended move, the group that drove the trend reverses its net position sharply within one report (e.g., commercials swinging from record long to record short - the S&P 500 in 1987, NASDAQ in March 2000). Treat the current trend as suspect and anticipate reversal, even if the COT signal itself looks confusing or is directionally 'wrong'. Corollary: in an uptrend, the failure of a minor COT buy signal to rebound prices is a strong warning of a major downturn.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: abrupt net-position flip after an extended move, or a minor-trend-direction signal failure. Invalidation: the flip/signal produces follow-through (no reversal); the book stresses this is a warning to protect/exit existing trend exposure, not a standalone reversal entry.
findings.risk_geometry: Used as a regime/turn warning: cut or hedge trend-direction exposure and stand ready to reverse with technical confirmation; no price-based stop/target given.
findings.quote: When you see an abrupt reversal in trader sentiment, anticipate a reversal in the current price trend, regardless of the direction of the COT signal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10, Chart Pattern Validation, p. 109 (NASDAQ top); Ch 9, pp. 101-103
findings.notes: Transferable to V8's lifecycle machinery as a dead-thesis/regime rule: a sharp flip in the crowding proxy (funding sign flip, OI blow-off, long/short ratio reversal) after an extended 1h trend flags overshoot. In crypto the flip is often liquidation-driven (flush-and-recover), so the 'reversal' outcome is less certain than in COT data - hence MEDIUM, and the rule should gate risk, not force entries.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Two-MA crossover on fund COT Index (mechanical COT system)
findings.mechanism: Trend-following speculators' positioning leads price; a mechanical two-moving-average crossover on the speculator net-position index generates trend-following entries from an external, non-redundant dataset.
findings.setup_summary: Weekly COT data stamped to daily bars: fast MA of the large-speculator COT Index crossing above the slow MA = buy on next day's open; crossing below = sell short; the model is always in the market with no stop. Tested on 35 futures markets 2000-2007, all positive gross (best pair per market, ~14 trades/year). The author explicitly warns it is not trade-ready: no stop-loss, no statistical verification, and drawdowns would be excessive.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: MA cross on the fund COT Index. The model is always-in so has no invalidation; the binding constraints the book documents are (a) the 3-10 day release lag (results were only marginal on pre-2000 bimonthly/monthly data) and (b) the need for a stop-loss fail-safe and a backup trend-catch option when the COT signal never comes.
findings.risk_geometry: Always-in, no stop - explicitly flagged as the system's flaw; entries/exits at the open of the day following the signal; no roll cost included.
findings.quote: Although such a simple set of trading rules might not be very effective if applied to price, hypothetical performance is quite impressive when applied to the Commitments data.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 9, View from the Pits, pp. 97-103
findings.notes: Methodology lessons for V8: (1) an external positioning dataset can produce signals comparable to price-based ones - in crypto, funding/OI percentile series could feed a mechanical cross; (2) data release lag is the dominant backtest bias - crypto has no equivalent lag (real-time data), which changes the edge structure; (3) always-in trend systems without stops bleed in crypto's volatility; (4) mandatory gating signals can make you miss the few big moves that make a year's profit.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Backwardation roll yield / funding carry
findings.mechanism: Hedgers pay a risk premium to speculators (hedging pressure); in backwardation, long positions earn a roll yield as deferred futures converge up to spot, while contango guarantees a roll loss for longs - carry is a return source independent of price direction.
findings.setup_summary: Observable weekly/monthly: term-structure sign (backwardation vs contango) or funding-rate sign determines whether longs (backwardation/negative funding) or shorts (contango/positive funding) earn carry while holding. The book documents that roll profit/loss must be accounted separately from price-based signal P&L, and that carry (not forecasting skill) explains a large share of speculator profitability in the academic record.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Carry is a passive return stream, not an entry trigger; the invalidation is sign reversal - backwardation flipping to contango flips the sign of the roll profit; the book notes seasonal commodities can move between contango and backwardation as supply tightens.
findings.risk_geometry: Holding-period cost model item: roll profit enters the simulator cost/PnL model separately from the signal; in crypto perps this is the funding settlement line.
findings.quote: Prices in contango, on the other hand, drop during the holding period, guaranteeing a rollover loss (which can only be offset through successful market forecasting).
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8, View from the Gallery, pp. 83-96 (Keynes's Theory of Normal Backwardation; de Roon 2000; Tien 2001)
findings.notes: Funding rate is the direct 24/7-perp analog of the roll yield and is observable in real time per funding window. Two V8 uses: (1) a funding-rate percentile/rolling-carry feature in marketstate feeding the positioning-exhaustion mechanisms; (2) a simulator cost-model line for expected funding P&L. Literature anchor: Keynes normal backwardation; de Roon et al. 2000 (hedging pressure explains significant price movement); Tien 2001 (hedging pressure ~45% of FX variation).
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Containment breakout (pent-up speculative demand)
findings.mechanism: When the counter-trend crowd must sell (or buy) aggressively just to hold a price inside a range, the effort itself signals pent-up speculative demand on the other side; once containment lifts, the breakout is explosive.
findings.setup_summary: Weekly: a prolonged trading range in which the counter-side sustains persistent selling (or buying) pressure to hold the boundary - visible as extreme normalized positioning (COT pinned below 50%) and repeated failed breakout attempts. The tell: when the counter-side begins covering shorts and accumulating (a rate-of-change buying surge inside the range), anticipate a breakout of the opposite boundary. OJ 2005: a year of aggressive commercial selling to contain prices presaged an explosive speculative bull move.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: containment effort + a positioning rate-of-change surge by the counter-side inside the range. Invalidation: containment relaxes without a surge (no pent-up flip), or prices break on the containment side first; also, in a sideways market a COT selling climax before a breakout is the exit-long / consider-short signal.
findings.risk_geometry: Book recommends buying with commercials near the range bottom (COT buying climax) so you are aboard for the breakout; exit longs on a selling climax before the breakout; retest of the broken boundary after breakout = additional entry opportunity (90% buying climax).
findings.quote: The excessive commercial selling pressure here was really a sign of pent-up speculative demand.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7, COT Movement Index, Figure 7.4 (OJ 2005 trading range), pp. 78-79; Ch 14 gold sideways tactic p. 155
findings.notes: Crypto ranges are frequently resolved by liquidation cascades rather than containment-then-breakout, and the 'who is containing' side is opaque without commercial segmentation. The mechanism is plausible and falsifiable if a containment proxy (sustained funding-rate pressure + range-bound volatility) is formalized, but it is chart-case-based in the book.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Fading small traders (rejected scheme)
findings.mechanism: Claim: small traders are 'dumb money' and should be faded. Verdict: the small-trader (nonreportable) bucket is a mixed bag of small commercials and speculators whose composition varies by market and trend, often moves too little to signal, and is not published separately - so the naive fade is not robustly executable.
findings.setup_summary: Rejected practice: take positions opposite the small trader net position. The book shows small-trader patterns are a 'real mishmash' - sometimes fund-like, sometimes fading the trend (2005-2007 example) - and the group's net position is often near-flat. Only in specific markets (livestock, where commercials dominate the small totals) does the small-trader net position show structure, and there it mirrors commercials (fade-able in the opposite sense) rather than acting as a reliable dumb-money fade.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a - strategy rejected; any retail-positioning fade must first establish the composition of the retail proxy.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: The small speculator may be the 'dumb money,' but he is not stupid enough to come out from hiding among commercials in the small trader category.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 4, Fading Small Speculators and Other Half-Baked Schemes, pp. 39-45; Ch 5 Small Trader Patterns pp. 59-60
findings.notes: The literature premise (small traders are net losers; Ch 8 studies) is supported, but the actionable fade rule is rejected on data-composition grounds. For crypto: exchanges publish retail long/short ratios and funding, which tempt naive retail fades; this finding argues those proxies must be validated for composition (who is actually in the bucket) before any fade behavior is formalized.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Seasonal hedging composites (rejected scheme)
findings.mechanism: Claim: comparing current hedging to the multi-year seasonal average of commercial hedging reveals whether commercials are more or less bullish than usual. Verdict: the seasonal composite is a smoothing artifact - year-to-year variance swamps the mean, so deviations from the 'seasonal average' carry no forecast value.
findings.setup_summary: Rejected practice: average weekly net commercial positions by calendar week across years (easy to sum and divide) and compare the current year's hedging against that 'seasonal norm'. The book shows the annual lines scatter wildly around the composite (corn example: short hedging peaks at week 11, long hedging at week 40 on average, but individual years diverge massively), so a current-year deviation is not statistically meaningful.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a - rejected; the test the author applied was whether a statistically reliable seasonal bias exists (it does not).
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: To be of any help, there would need to be a statistically reliable seasonal bias. I have done the math; it is not there.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 4, pp. 43-45 (Seasonal vs Actual Graph of Commercial Hedging)
findings.notes: No crop cycle in crypto; the transferable lesson is a caution against calendar-averaging ANY positioning/funding series and reading deviations as signal without a variance test - directly relevant to any time-of-day or funding-cyclicality feature V8 may propose.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Positioning data segmentation integrity and indicator kill-switch
findings.mechanism: Classifying long-only index/swap-dealer positions as 'commercials' fogged the true insider signal; when a structural change contaminates the segmentation, the indicator produces systematically invalid signals - and you must know your system well enough to recognize when it is not working and stop trading it.
findings.setup_summary: The copper episode: in the record 2005-2007 bull market, commercials kept buying instead of scaling out, so the COT Index's signature pattern broke and it generated buy signals all the way up - because nontraditional commercials (index funds) were exploiting hedge exemptions and were being classified as commercial. Rule: when a signal generator starts producing wacky, pattern-breaking outputs under an identifiable market-structure change, pull the plug on the indicator until it re-establishes a reliable, interpretable pattern.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: observable divergence of the indicator's behavior from its modeled signature coincident with a structural/data segmentation change. Invalidation: the pattern re-establishes after the structural change passes; note the CIT contamination was judged tolerable only because CIT net-long is near-flat (a constant rather than a variable).
findings.risk_geometry: n/a - a model-health/kill-switch rule, not a trade geometry.
findings.quote: When you see this (or any other indicator you may use) begin to produce wacky signals, it is time to pull the plug on the faulty indicator.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 14, Test of Metal, pp. 157-159 (The Copper Caper); Ch 1 pp. 9-13; Ch 2 pp. 25-26
findings.notes: Maps onto V8's registry QUARANTINED mechanism and the frozen feature-group audit: crypto perp microstructure changes (venue shifts, OI composition, institutional entry, new contract listings, exchange-of-record changes) can silently break the calibration of funding/OI-based features. A model-health rule - detect when a family's signal signature diverges from its modeled behavior and quarantine it - is directly actionable.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Synthetic/composite positioning series construction
findings.mechanism: For instruments without direct positioning data, construct a pseudo series by combining the sign-adjusted positioning of related, highly-correlated markets; a thin futures venue can still proxy global positioning because inter-dealer FX turnover is mostly offsetting 'hot potato' flow, not directional demand.
findings.setup_summary: Methodology: build the target series' net position / COT percentile from correlated components - USD Index from inverted IMM currency positions (open interest 2800% of the native NYBOT contract), COT Cross Indexes for dollar-free pairs (multiply quote currency by -1, then add), gold/silver ratio pseudo-positions from notional-normalized gold minus silver, oil complex composite, stock index composite. Validate the synthetic series against any thin native series (the EUR/JPY pseudo-COT matched the actual NYBOT series closely), and monitor correlations regularly since they drift and are not causal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a - methodology; the book's cautions: correlations do not establish causation, and spurious links (e.g., Yahoo vs yen) must be checked before reliance.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: When you start making things up, there is no end to the concoctions possible. But there is one additional category of pseudoindicator that is worthy of discussion.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 12, Crossing Currencies, pp. 129-132; Ch 14 Gold/Silver ratio p. 157; Ch 15 oil composite pp. 168-173
findings.notes: Since no CFTC COT exists for crypto, synthetic positioning proxies (funding-based, OI-based, cross-venue and cross-asset composites) are the only route to import the whole positioning family. Klitgaard & Weir's 'microcosm' argument is literature-supported: a dominant perp venue's positioning can proxy global crypto flow despite small relative size, because dealer turnover is mostly offsetting.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Commercial Net Position Climax Contrarian Signal
findings.mechanism: commercials (hedgers) are structurally contrarian; when their net position reaches a historical climax the market is near a major turn
findings.setup_summary: On the weekly COT release, rank the commercial net position against its multi-year look-back range (COT Index, stochastic formula). A buying climax (index >= 90) or selling climax (index <= 5), confirmed when the index backs off the extreme, marks a major turn; take the commercial side (buy climax -> long, sell climax -> short). NASDAQ selling climax Oct 8 2007 flagged the stock-index top ~3 days before it, and the author carried 13 consecutive weekly warnings before the January 2008 break.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: index backs off the extreme (confirmation). Invalidation: index holds at the extreme while price continues — major sell signals can be premature inside bull trends (e.g., Nov 2004), so the claim is a success-ratio edge, not a certainty.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the next weekly open after the COT release applying the correct release lag; the book's Part 2 gives no stop/target — V8 must assign atr_ref stop, 1R target, expiry in bars.
findings.quote: Commercial selling reported in last Tuesday's Commitments report triggered a major COT sell signal in the NASDAQ.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue, 'COT Signals Stock Market Top' (Fig. E.1); Glossary 'climax'
findings.notes: No CFTC COT per-type breakdown exists for most perp venues (only CME BTC/ETH futures have COT). Funding rate and open interest can proxy for the positioning gauge but lack trader-type labels and are real-time, which removes the stale-data edge the book exploits.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Failed COT Signal Explosive Counter-Move
findings.mechanism: when commercials fail to defend a level after their positioning climaxed against a direction, the unresolved positioning unwinds explosively in the opposite direction
findings.setup_summary: After a COT sell (buy) signal, if price does not decline (rise) and instead closes back through the level commercials were defending, expect an explosive move in the opposite direction. Gold 2007: a successful commercial selling climax in July was followed in September by the failure of commercials to hold resistance at the same price level (a 'COT sell signal failure'), and the ensuing move pushed gold to record highs.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close back through the failed level after a positioning climax. Invalidation: the original signal resolves in its own direction (price keeps declining after a sell signal).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE beyond the failed level; stop on the far side of the failed level; target is trend-following (ride the explosive move); no explicit R-multiple stated.
findings.quote: the failure of commercials to hold resistance at the same price level in September created a COT sell signal failure (point C). Following typical form, the ensuing move was quite explosive, pushing gold prices to record levels.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue, 'Gold Responds to COT Buy Signal' (Fig. E.2)
findings.notes: Single-case pattern in this part; 'typical form' implies repetition but only one example is shown here. Conceptually adjacent to V8's liquidity_sweep_reclaim / failed_breakout dynamics but conditioned on a positioning-climax signal.

findings.strategy_name: COT Signal Retry After Fake-Out
findings.mechanism: a prior invalidated signal (fake-out) does not kill the thesis; a fresh major COT signal coinciding with a developing top/bottom formation warrants a second entry attempt
findings.setup_summary: After a COT short (long) signal was faked out and price kept rising (falling), take the second short (long) attempt when a fresh major COT signal appears together with a developing top (bottom) formation. Copper, Oct 1 2007: the first major COT sell signal in ~4 years plus a developing top formation justified another short entry attempt despite the earlier fake-out during the record-breaking rally.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: fresh major COT signal + top/bottom formation. Invalidation: no formation develops or price makes a new trend extreme.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at formation confirmation (new short/long); stop beyond the formation extreme; no explicit R-multiple or expiry given.
findings.quote: Bears should not let the prior fake-out prevent another short entry attempt if a top formation develops.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue, 'Copper Flashes a COT Sell Signal' (Fig. E.3)
findings.notes: Structurally similar to V8 sweep-and-retry / failed-breakout retry logic, but the confirmatory input here is a positioning-climax signal rather than pure price structure.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Sector Lead-Market COT Signal Propagation
findings.mechanism: positioning extremes in the strongest/leading market of a sector carry information for correlated sector members; a signal in the reference market warns of hidden selling/buying pressure in the laggards
findings.setup_summary: Monitor COT signals on the strongest, most-commercial-crowded market in a sector; when it flashes a major buy/sell signal, treat the whole sector as at risk of the same turn. NASDAQ was the only index strong enough to draw a commercial selling climax in Oct 2007; the author inferred 'overwhelming commercial selling pressure just above the recent highs' in the S&P, Russell, and Dow, and any rally became a selling opportunity.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: reference market major COT signal. Invalidation: laggard sector members fail to follow; prematurity is common during trends.
findings.risk_geometry: Used as a sector regime filter rather than a per-market entry; no stop/target specified.
findings.quote: if the S&P, Russell, and Dow futures had performed as strongly as the NASDAQ, they too would have triggered COT sell signals.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue, 'COT Signals Stock Market Top'
findings.notes: Crypto analog: BTC funding/positioning extremes as a lead for ETH and altcoin perps; sector coherence in crypto is looser and regime-dependent, so a lead-market filter needs its own falsification.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: COT Movement Surge (±40 Points in Six Weeks)
findings.mechanism: a rapid +/-40-point swing in the positioning index over six weeks marks short-term exhaustion of the crowd, flagging minor tops and bottoms
findings.setup_summary: Compute the COT Movement Index (rate of change of the COT Index over ~6 weeks, range -100 to +100). A +40/-40 surge flags a minor top/bottom; use it as reversal timing near extremes rather than a standalone trend signal. Index cross-references it as flagging minor tops and bottoms and as a market-correction timing tool.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: +/-40 point movement within ~6 weeks. Invalidation: no price response within the surge window; surges can be premature during strong trends.
findings.risk_geometry: Reversal-timing input; the detailed rule set lives at pp. 75-79 (Part 1) — not restated in this part, so no stop/target/expiry here.
findings.quote: surge A +/-40 point move in the COT Index within a specified period (usually six weeks).
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary 'surge'; Index '40-point COT surge rules, 75-79' and 'surges indicating minor tops and bottoms, 108'
findings.notes: Scale is in COT Index units (0-100); a crypto analog would need re-parameterization on a funding-based gauge, where the same 'velocity of crowding' idea is measurable intraday.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Stochastic Normalization of Net Positions (COT Index)
findings.mechanism: ranking a trader-group net position within its historical range via the stochastic formula yields a 0-100 gauge that is scale-insensitive to open-interest growth, making positioning comparable across eras
findings.setup_summary: Construct a positioning gauge by ranking the group net position against its historical range (stochastic formula): 0 = most bearish historical extreme, 100 = most bullish. Ratio variants (percent-of-total and percent-of-group) are insensitive to large OI swings from quarterly contract rollovers, unlike the raw subtraction form, which visibly widens during OI surges (Appendix A, Fig. A.2). Look-back period choice changes signal frequency.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — methodology. Caveat: the subtraction form's pattern changes with OI growth; ratios give scale-stable patterns.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A
findings.quote: COT index Based on stochastics, a formula that compares the current net position to its historical range and ranks it on a scale of 0 percent (most bearish) to 100 percent (most bullish).
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary 'COT index'; Appendix A 'Alternative Net Position Formulas' (Examples 1-5)
findings.notes: The rank-vs-range normalization transfers directly to a funding-rate or long-open-interest gauge in crypto; V8 feature construction should prefer ratio/rank normalization over raw levels.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Point-in-Time Release-Lag Discipline in COT Backtests
findings.mechanism: signals are only actionable when the data existed and was released; using compilation dates instead of release dates, or applying a different lag in testing than live, invalidates backtests
findings.setup_summary: COT files carry Tuesday compilation dates but were released later: 6-business-day lag pre-1990, 3-day nominal/10-day skip-week lag from Oct 1992, weekly Friday release of prior-Tuesday positions only since Oct 9 2000, and Options+Futures Combined-report publication parity only since Jan 18 2002. Any backtest that enters on the next weekly open after a COT signal must apply the contemporaneous release lag; results generated without it are, in the author's words, 'imaginary.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A
findings.risk_geometry: N/A
findings.quote: If you see system testing that took a position on the next weekly open after a COT signal was generated, you will know that the testing prior to 2002 is invalid. (Those kinds of results are not just hypothetical, they are imaginary.)
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix B, 'Data Periodicity and Lag'
findings.notes: Directly mirrors V8's PIT invariant (event/available/ingested clocks never collapsed); crypto venue ingestion lags (funding timestamps, OI snapshot times, exchange maintenance gaps) must be modeled the same way in the simulator.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Contract-Spec Continuity Back-Adjustment
findings.mechanism: positioning series are discontinuous at contract-specification changes; back-adjusting or combining overlapping contracts preserves a homogeneous series for testing
findings.setup_summary: Before any COT backtest, detect and repair discontinuities: multiply S&P data x2 for pre-Nov-1997 (contract halved $500->$250); grains x0.20 pre-1998 (bushels->5,000-bushel contracts); NYBOT dollar index x0.5 pre-May-1992; combine overlapping old/new contracts during transitions (hogs 1996, copper 1989, RBOB 2006); ignore markets with negligible OI that never persist. A database 'beginning 19830101' is a watermark of the author's curated series and a red flag for other sources.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A
findings.risk_geometry: N/A
findings.quote: My solution is to backadjust the historical data to the new specification, where possible, so that a continuous data base can be maintained.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix B, 'Contract Specification Changes' and 'When Not to Adjust Historical Data'
findings.notes: Perps have no contract-size changes, but venue OI-definition changes, delisting/relisting, and exchange-roll do create analogous discontinuities worth auditing in V8 feature construction.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Hedging Pressure / Normal Backwardation Risk Premium
findings.mechanism: commercial hedgers pay a risk premium to speculators for bearing price risk; aggregate hedger net positioning therefore embeds a forecastable return component (normal backwardation / hedging pressure)
findings.setup_summary: Long futures exposure earns the backwardation/risk premium paid by short hedgers; the book's reference base (Chang 1985 'Returns to Speculators and the Theory of Normal Backwardation'; Bessembinder 1992 'Systematic Risk, Hedging Pressure, and Risk Premiums'; Bessembinder & Chan 1992 time-varying risk premia; De Roon-Nijman-Veld 2000 'Hedging Pressure Effects') ties commercial net short positions to expected returns. This is the theoretical justification for treating commercial net-position extremes as turn signals.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — theory; the premium is time-varying (convenience yield, contango/backwardation regimes, pp. 84-85).
findings.risk_geometry: Structural long-carry exposure; no explicit stop/target in the book.
findings.quote: Keynes Theory of Normal Backwardation
findings.chapter_anchor: Index (pp. 84-85); References (Chang 1985; Bessembinder 1992; Bessembinder & Chan 1992; De Roon et al. 2000)
findings.notes: Perp analog is funding: longs pay or receive funding depending on positioning crowding, a carry whose sign is observable in real time — but the commercial-hedger supply of risk that drives normal backwardation is absent in crypto perps.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

findings.strategy_name: Trader-Group Behavioral Role Asymmetry
findings.mechanism: the three COT groups play stable, opposite behavioral roles — commercials counter-trend (negative feedback), large speculators/funds momentum-follow (positive feedback), small traders are systematically wrong-sided — so a group's net position is only interpretable through its role
findings.setup_summary: Build separate positioning features per trader group with role-appropriate semantics: fade commercials at climaxes (counter-trend/negative feedback), confirm trends with large-speculator fund net direction (momentum/positive feedback), and treat small-trader net positions as a contrary indicator (index: 'fading of small traders'). Academic support cited in the book: Houthakker 1957, Wang 2001/2003, Hartzmark 1987, Leuthold-Garcia-Lu 1994, Kearns & Manners 2004.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A — feature construction. Caveat: classification can blur — commodity index traders are reported inside the commercial counts and distort 'hedger' semantics (pp. 34-36), and swap dealers hold large long index-replication positions.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A
findings.quote: positive feedback A trader that adds positions as the market moves favorably to existing positions (momentum or trend-following).
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary 'positive feedback'; Index 'Trading styles' (pp. 51-59); References (Wang 2003; Kearns & Manners 2004)
findings.notes: Crypto perps lack trader-type classification; the retail-crowd-vs-smart-money split is cruder and observable only via funding-rate sign, open-interest concentration, and liquidation data — so role semantics must be inferred, not read off a report.
findings.book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

book_title: The Disciplined Trader: Developing Winning Attitudes (1990) — Part 1 (Chs 1-13, Mark Douglas)

findings.strategy_name: Intraday zone-touch reversion (preplanned S/R scalping)
findings.mechanism: mean reversion at predefined support/resistance: price touching a mapped zone reverts toward the opposite zone level
findings.setup_summary: Predefine intraday support and resistance levels (in the case study a 7-10 tick range). Buy at support / sell at resistance, target the opposite level, and exit on the rotation to objective. Stop is a fixed 2-3 ticks beyond entry, sized to the assessed reliability of the S/R levels; thesis is invalidated if price trades more than 2-3 ticks through entry.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price touches a pre-mapped support (LONG) or resistance (SHORT) zone. Invalidation: price trades >2-3 ticks through entry in the adverse direction, or the zone fails to hold.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit-style at the predefined zone (wait for price to hit the level); stop: 2-3 ticks beyond entry (fixed tick, chosen from reliability of the S/R levels); target: opposite zone level; expiry: no explicit bar count — 'wait for the market to rotate' to objective.
findings.quote: The plan was for him to stand in the pit and wait for the price to hit his target (buy support or sell resistance), execute the trade, wait for the market to hit his objective, and then exit the trade. If the market traded through his entry point in the opposite direction by more than two or three ticks, he was supposed to execute the loss without hesitation.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, The Three Stages to Becoming a Successful Trader (pp. 67-68, floor-trader case study)
findings.notes: Single case study, not a statistical claim; evidence-class NARRATIVE. Transfer to BTCUSDT 1h is indirect: the pit-session 'rotation within a day' rhythm does not exist in a 24/7 perp, and the 7-10 tick scalping frame is sub-bar at 1h. The falsifiable core (zone-touch reversion with a structurally-sized stop and opposite-zone target) is a candidate mean-reversion family distinct from all currently formalized V8 experts. Coordinate with the sibling part-2 reader: same book may reprise this in Ch. 15 (Psychology of Price Movement).
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Passive-loser lifecycle rule (no natural game end -> mandatory predefined exit)
findings.mechanism: unlike casino games, an open market position has no automatic end; doing nothing continues the loss, so every position must carry a pre-set loss limit, objective, and expiry enforced actively
findings.setup_summary: Rule, not a signal: at entry, define the loss limit, the profit objective, and the conditions that end the position, because the market will not end it for you. A trader in a losing position must actively participate to stop the loss; inaction is a passive continuation of loss (down to liquidation).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any open position. Invalidation: position is closed only by the preplanned stop/target/expiry or dead-thesis exit, never by hope that the market 'comes back'.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: none (rule); stop: predefined loss limit set at entry; target: predefined objective; expiry: mandatory — no natural game end exists.
findings.quote: In the market environment, you have to actively participate to get into a trade and actively participate to end your losses. If you do nothing, the potential exists to lose everything you own.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, The Three Stages to Becoming a Successful Trader (p. 61); Ch. 5, Prices Are in Perpetual Motion (p. 45, 'passive loser' vs gambling)
findings.notes: Directly justifies V8's lifecycle design: one active exposure per (instrument, direction), mandatory stop/target/expiry in risk_geometry, and dead-thesis exits. In 24/7 perps with leverage this is the highest-urgency structural rule — a position never auto-closes and unfunded size decays via funding.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Fear-driven asymmetric exits (cut profits short / let losses run)
findings.mechanism: fear of losing biases attention: in winners it focuses on profit being taken away (early exit), in losers it blocks loss-confirming information (hold) — producing the classic asymmetric P&L
findings.setup_summary: Behavioral mechanism explaining why discretionary exits degrade: the same trader holds a losing position while cutting a winning one short, purely from fear-driven attention allocation. The falsifiable claim is that discretionary exit decisions under an open position diverge from pre-committed rules in a systematic (asymmetric) direction.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any open position where exit is left to discretion. Invalidation: system-determined exits (stop, target, still_valid) remove the discretion that fear exploits.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated; the lesson is that exit decisions must be mechanical, not emotional.
findings.quote: What you have just been given is an example of why the vast majority of traders cut their profits short and let their losses run. In a winning trade, the fear of losing will cause us to focus our attention on information that the market is going to take our profits away, compelling us to get out early. In a losing trade we will focus our attention on just the opposite information—anything other than that which would indicate the trade is a loser.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 10, How Memories, Associations, and Beliefs Manage Environmental Information (p. 103)
findings.notes: Design justification for V8's deterministic stops/targets and frozen-reference still_valid checks: they exist precisely because discretionary exits under position bias are systematically wrong. Corroborates existing_family_refinement: no expert may re-evaluate its own exit emotionally; exit logic is pre-committed.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Revenge-trading block (last trade is irrelevant to the current opportunity)
findings.mechanism: after losing more than intended risk, the trader seeks to 'get back', rejecting valid current profit opportunities and enlarging targets/size until the recoup target is met
findings.setup_summary: Rule: the previous trade's P&L must never enter the current trade's decision. The book's concrete example: after a 20-tick loss with 5-tick intended risk, the trader rejects a valid 10-tick profit because 'getting back' demands 15-20 ticks — a target that no longer reflects market potential. Adversarial framing ('it's me vs the market') leads to giving money back.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: recent loss exceeding intended risk. Invalidation: any target or size adjustment keyed to recouping a prior loss is a rule violation.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated; the rule caps discretionary adjustment of target/size by prior outcomes.
findings.quote: For example, is a 10-tick profit enough in the trade you are currently in if you lost 20 in the last trade?... If you believe in 'getting back,' 10 won't be enough regardless of what the market is doing or telling you. You will need at least 15 and preferably 20 to make you whole.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 5, Prices Are in Perpetual Motion with No Defined Beginning or Ending (p. 47)
findings.notes: For 24/7 perps with high leverage and instant execution, revenge size-ups/target-inflation execute within seconds. In V8 terms this is a RiskGate-adjacent admission rule: candidate generation and risk_geometry must be a pure function of point-in-time MarketState, with no path-dependence on the equity/outcome of prior episodes (consistent with rule 15: outcome data never mutates an active Expert).
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Skill-bounded position sizing (risk comfort level; size-up after wins predicts give-back)
findings.mechanism: position size must stay within the trader's demonstrated skill/objectivity level; sudden size-ups — especially after winning streaks, to 'prove' success — predict giving back all profits plus more
findings.setup_summary: Rule: identify a 'risk comfort level' and expand it only as fast as the trader can maintain objective perception. Falsifiable pattern from the case study: a trader who ran a streak of 1-2 tick winners then jumped to 20 contracts lost ~$3,000 the next day — all profits plus more, in one session.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: risk/size increase beyond the level at which objectivity has been demonstrated. Invalidation: size-up driven by self-image ('prove I have arrived') is the failure signature; sizing must be a monotonic function of validated skill, not of recent wins.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated; sizing rule only — risk per trade held at the fear-free comfort level, expanded gradually.
findings.quote: he was reasoning that by trading a larger contract size he would make enough money to prove to himself and everyone else that he had finally arrived... The next day he lost almost $3,000.00 trading 20-contract positions. He gave back to the markets all his profits, plus more.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, The Three Stages to Becoming a Successful Trader (p. 69, 20-contract case study); Ch. 2, Skills to Be Acquired (p. 28, risk comfort level)
findings.notes: V8 mapping: heat cap and per-exposure risk are frozen constants; the lesson is that a live/learning system must not let recent win streaks expand its own size. Corroborates V8 rule 15 (registry-gated learning) and the complexity budget — sizing must not be a learned, path-dependent quantity.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Price behavior over reasons (market is always right; post-hoc narratives are not predictive)
findings.mechanism: price is the consensus belief of all participants acting as force; movement follows greatest force; 'reasons' given by traders after the fact are justifications/excuses with no predictive value
findings.setup_summary: Methodology rule: build signals from observable price behavior and structure, never from post-hoc news narratives or trader-provided 'reasons'. The market is never wrong 'in what it does'; being 'right' with superior reasoning is irrelevant unless price agrees. Irrational crowd behavior is nonetheless predictable because it is driven by shared fear of scarcity and fear of missing out.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: a narrative-based or expectation-based reason to act that price does not confirm. Invalidation: if the collective force of traders moves price against the thesis, the thesis is dead regardless of its logical quality.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated (methodology layer, not a trade geometry).
findings.quote: If you want to learn to predict price movement, you don't need to pay attention to reasons. What you need to do is determine how the majority of traders perceive the external conditions in relationship to either their fear of scarcity, or their fear of missing out, or both. ... The market is never wrong in what it does; it just is.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 7, In the Market Environment, Reasons Are Irrelevant (p. 60); Ch. 3, The Market Is Always Right (p. 40)
findings.notes: Foundational for V8's behavior-driven ontology: an Expert is a falsifiable hypothesis over observable MarketState behavior, and candidate episodes are validated on tape, not on narrative. In crypto perps, intraday 'reasons' (news, FUD, narratives) are abundant and cheap — this rule keeps signal construction venue-agnostic and evidence-bound.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Participant-group fear-flow anticipation (groups act in unison under shared fear)
findings.mechanism: participant groups (locals, commercials, retail) share price objectives/timeframes and act in unison under fear of loss and fear of missing out; their collective behavior is predictable to an observer outside the same fear cycle
findings.setup_summary: Mechanism for anticipating crowd behavior: identify which participant groups are under pressure (fear of missing out on the upside, fear of loss on the downside) and what conditions confirm or disappoint them; when groups act in unison they upset equilibrium and force prices one direction. Falsifiable proxy in perps: positioning/funding extremes and liquidation cascades as group-fear footprints.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: observable conditions under which a participant group must act (e.g., margin/liquidation pressure, extreme funding skew). Invalidation: if the hypothesized group does not act in unison (price fails to follow), the flow thesis is dead.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated in the book; this is a mechanism candidate, not a concrete trade geometry.
findings.quote: under certain market conditions large groups of traders will all be trying to do the same thing—because of what they fear will or won't happen—upsetting the equilibrium, forcing prices to move in one direction. If you haven't yet learned to identify these conditions, you naturally won't perceive them when they exist.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 10, How Memories, Associations, and Beliefs Manage Environmental Information (p. 94); Ch. 7 (p. 57, locals/commercials/retail groups)
findings.notes: The 1990 pit taxonomy (locals/commercials) does not map cleanly to crypto perps; the analogue is retail vs. whales/permanent holders with funding as the flow signal. Needs the derivatives tape (funding, open interest, liquidations) before any formalization — data-blocked in the same sense as breakout_retest/capitulation. Would consume participation/flow/time feature groups, which V8 has not yet built.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Uncommitted probability assessment (evaluate market as if no position is open)
findings.mechanism: opportunity assessment must be recomputed from current point-in-time state independent of the open position and its P&L; releasing the demand that expectations be fulfilled lets the market say when to enter and exit
findings.setup_summary: Methodology rule: compute the opportunity as an 'uncommitted assessment of the probabilities' — the same signal logic applied whether or not a position is open. In V8 terms this is exactly the point-in-time MarketState read: candidate generation and the still_valid (dead-thesis) check are recomputed from the frozen state, never anchored to entry price or open P&L.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any state evaluation while holding a position. Invalidation: if the assessment requires the trader's hope that price returns, the thesis is already dead; the assessment must be re-runnable as if flat.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated (methodology layer).
findings.quote: Releasing yourself from the demand your expectations be fulfilled exactly the way you expect them to be. Releasing yourself from the demand will allow you to shift your perspective to perceive whatever opportunities exist in the market now, as if you didn't have a trade on at all.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, You Create Your Experience of the Market (p. 63); Perceiving Opportunity (p. 64, 'uncommitted assessment of the probabilities')
findings.notes: Direct architectural validation of V8: no wall-clock, frozen refs, still_valid recomputed from state, and outcome data never mutating an active expert — all implementations of 'evaluate as if you didn't have a trade on'. This is the strongest methodology anchor in Part 1 for existing design.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Defined conditions are the precondition for repeatable wins (random winning / random losing)
findings.mechanism: a win produced by undefined conditions cannot be repeated or prevented; only exactly definable behavior (own and market's) enables learning to repeat wins and stop losses
findings.setup_summary: Methodology rule: any signal or edge must be expressible as exact, observable conditions so that episodes can be reproduced and validated. The failure mode 'random winning and random losing' occurs when a trader cannot define what produced the last win, making the next trade a gamble and breeding fear/anxiety.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: a signal or outcome that cannot be restated as exact observable conditions. Invalidation: an undefined 'win' is not evidence of edge; a candidate episode must be reproducible from a point-in-time state snapshot.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated (methodology layer).
findings.quote: If you can't define your own behavior and that of the markets, you can't learn how to repeat your wins or prevent your losses.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, The Market Is an Unstructured Environment (p. 53, 'random winning and random losing')
findings.notes: Maps to V8's evidence-bound structure: an Expert is one falsifiable hypothesis with exact trigger/invalidation/risk_geometry; without this, no registry progression (SCREENING->REPLICATION->SHADOW) is meaningful. Reinforces why the economic verdict stays NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM until episodes are reproduced on frozen OOS.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Expanded timeframe for big-picture perception; objective set by market structure
findings.mechanism: expanding the timeframe of observation increases the number of usable distinctions and the quality of opportunity assessment; profit objective should be set by what the market offers, not by personal value ('how much is enough')
findings.setup_summary: Methodology: assess a candidate opportunity within a broader timeframe context, and let the market's structure define the profit objective ('let the market tell you how much is enough') rather than a personal target. Narrow tick-level focus serves any illusion; expanding the perspective is a component of disciplined perception.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: opportunity evaluation using only the immediate bar/context. Invalidation: a profit objective anchored to personal expectations (desired win size) rather than observable structure is a rule violation.
findings.risk_geometry: None stated; supports setting targets from market structure instead of fixed personal goals.
findings.quote: It will be extremely difficult to learn how to develop a perspective for the 'big picture,' by expanding your time frame perspective... You can learn how to trade where you won't be using information to justify your beliefs but rather to perceive the most likely possibilities in any given moment.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, You Create Your Experience of the Market (p. 63); Ch. 5 (p. 43, 'how much is enough')
findings.notes: Supports the existing trend_pullback design (trend context on a longer frame, targets from structure not personal expectation) and the 'let the market tell you how much is enough' objective-setting principle. Relevant to perp specifics: no daily close boundary to anchor 'enough', so structure-based targets (levels, R-multiples) matter more than calendar-based targets.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Stops do not cap worst-case loss (gap/slippage through stop)
findings.mechanism: a stop order caps nominal risk only if price trades through the stop level; gaps/slippage mean realized loss can exceed the stop distance, so risk sizing must price worst-case slippage, not the nominal stop
findings.setup_summary: Risk-model rule: even a disciplined stop does not bound realized loss, because the market can gap through the stop level. The simulator and risk sizing must model worst-case fill beyond the stop, not assume stop-level execution.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any stop order. Invalidation: a fill assumed exactly at the stop price is a modeling error; worst-case slippage must be a parameter.
findings.risk_geometry: Stops: exit triggered at stop level, filled at the gap-through price (worst-case slippage must be modeled); this is a fill/cost-model rule, not an entry geometry.
findings.quote: You don't ultimately know what your risk is, even if you are disciplined enough to use stops, because the market could gap through your stops.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, The Three Stages to Becoming a Successful Trader (p. 61)
findings.notes: In crypto perps there is no exchange-session gap (24/7), but liquidation cascades, thin order books, and mark-vs-last dislocation produce stop-through slippage that is the perp analogue of a gap. Validates V8's canonical L1 simulator's STOP_FIRST + gap/slippage semantics and the Binance USDM cost model; confirms gap semantics must be retained even though 'no exchange gaps' is often claimed.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Big-trade mentality block (honor the objective even when it is 'too small')
findings.mechanism: rejecting a valid, structure-signaled profit objective because its size feels insulting relative to expectation; over-holding winners past the objective in the belief a bigger move is coming, then giving the profit back
findings.setup_summary: Rule: the profit objective must be honored when taken — the book's own confession: refusing $500-$750 profits 'even when I knew that's all there was to be made' because the market felt insulting. The falsifiable claim: over-holding past a valid objective (expecting a 'big trade') systematically converts wins into give-backs.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: position at objective where remaining potential is judged by the book's observation to be exhausted. Invalidation: the decision to hold past objective must be thesis-based (structure says more), never expectation-based (the amount is 'too small').
findings.risk_geometry: Target: set and honored per the structure; over-holding past target without a fresh thesis is the violation.
findings.quote: my big-trade mentality was so pervasive that I would refuse to take profits of $500 or $750 in many trades even when I knew that's all there was to be made... it felt as if the market was insulting me by offering such paltry sums compared to what I needed or expected.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 1, Why I Wrote This Book (p. 19)
findings.notes: With leverage, over-holding a winner past the objective compounds the give-back. In V8 terms this is a risk_geometry discipline rule: target_r is a frozen constant of the expert variant; letting 'expected size' mutate the target is a discretionary violation. Related to but distinct from the revenge-trading rule (that one keys targets to prior losses; this one keys holding to expected win size).
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: leverage_cap
findings.mechanism: high leverage converts a normal adverse move into a forced liquidation; capping notional at a small multiple of equity bounds loss before the liquidation engine fires
findings.setup_summary: Account-level risk rule: notional per position is capped at a small multiple of equity (the book's institutional benchmark is 2:1; retail was 100:1-400:1). A stop must be in place so max loss is bounded far below the point where available margin is consumed and the broker force-closes the position (the book's loss was $2,000+ on a $1,700 account because $20/pip with no stop outran the $1,200 of free margin).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: notional-per-unit (per pip) is large relative to equity, or no stop is set. Invalidation: the exposure's worst-case loss would exhaust free margin before the stop distance; a stop distance that exceeds free-margin headroom invalidates the trade.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: N/A (risk gate). Stop: mandatory; must be closer than the margin-call distance. Sizing: the book states only 'we might use 2-to-1 leverage' at the institutional desk; $10/pip on $1,000 account vs. $20/pip on $1,700 account was the fatal scaling. No % rule stated.
findings.quote: At Ernest Wellington, we might use 2-to-1 leverage. That's it. We don't mess around with crazy leverage. We'd all wash up... When your losses reached $1,200, you had used up all the available margin. So we closed your trade automatically as a service to you.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'Lessons Learned' p.34 (leverage); Ch. 7 'You Never Forget Your First Margin Call' p.58-60
findings.notes: Directly transferable to perp crypto where 100x+ leverage and a hard liquidation engine are native: the RiskGate admission rule should size notional so a 1-ATR adverse fill cannot approach the liquidation price, and every exposure must carry a stop. V8 already mandates stops in risk_geometry; this finding makes the sizing-vs-free-margin bound explicit. The counterfactual hazard — Harry held a 100+ pip adverse move with no stop and survived only via broker force-close — is the exact liquidation-cascade setup perp markets exhibit.
findings.book: Adventures of a Currency Trader - A Fable about Trading, Courage, and Doing the Right Thing 2007

findings.strategy_name: profit_target_at_prior_support_resistance
findings.mechanism: price repeatedly stalls at established prior support/resistance; a pre-committed target at such a level plus holding through pullbacks captures the full trend move that emotion-based early exits would truncate
findings.setup_summary: After entry in the direction of an established move, set the target at the next major prior S/R level (round number or a level that stopped price in multiple prior years), frozen before entry, and hold through adverse pullbacks until price reaches it. Exemplars: EUR/JPY long at 119.00 (a barrier hit in Jan 2002 that took 9 months to break) targeting 131.00 (stopped in 1997/1998/1999); GBP/USD long after FOMC targeting 1.8600, 470 pips away, 'I made up my mind before I took the trade.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade entered on a thesis (technical barrier + macro confluence) with a pre-frozen structure target. Invalidation: target level is broken and closed beyond it (thesis dead); until then, pullbacks are not invalidation — exiting early on fear was the documented error ('I had let my emotions ruin the trade').
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: market (bar close). Stop: not specified beyond thesis invalidation (break of the support thesis). Target: structure level, not fixed R — 131.00 vs. entry 119.00 was ~12R of stated move; 1.8600 was 470 pips on a 40-pip quick scalp thesis. Expiry: months (two months to exit in the fable), no bar-based expiry.
findings.quote: Ride your profits, Harry. That's the lesson here... I have a profit target at a previous level of support and resistance, where price stopped cold several times this year, and as recently as just a week ago... 470 pips away, but it can get there. I made up my mind before I took the trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'Craig's Ten-Million-Dollar Lesson' p.35-38; Ch. 8 p.63
findings.notes: Refinement candidate for the existing trend_pullback / failed_breakout experts: both currently hardcode target_r 1.0 and expiry_bars 8, which this lesson argues truncates winners. A variant that replaces fixed-R targets with frozen structure targets (prior swing high/low, round number with multi-touch history) and extends expiry until the frozen target or thesis break is a legitimate family variant, not a new family. The frozen-ref discipline matches V8's 'still_valid' dead-thesis exit.
findings.book: Adventures of a Currency Trader - A Fable about Trading, Courage, and Doing the Right Thing 2007

findings.strategy_name: macro_release_avoidance
findings.mechanism: the first minutes after a scheduled macro release are dominated by reactive/slippage-prone flow and headline-chasing; waiting for the actual number and planning on higher timeframes yields decisions based on fact rather than reaction
findings.setup_summary: No new exposure during / immediately after a scheduled macro release (FOMC minutes, NFP, CPI) — the book's stated risk is that 'even no decision can move the dollar 100 points in sixty seconds.' After the number is known, plan on daily/weekly/4h charts ('You need to watch the longer term charts'), not 1-minute/tick charts, and let the trade play out over days-to-weeks, not minutes.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: scheduled high-impact release within the next few bars. Invalidation: rule is about entry suppression, not direction; it lapses once the release has printed and a plan is formed on longer timeframes.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: none during the avoid window (suppressed). Timeframe: the book prescribes daily/weekly/4-hour charts for planning ('the young guys are all looking at the five-minute charts, or God help them, the one-minute charts, or lower'), explicitly rejecting sub-hour planning.
findings.quote: You don't trade the day of the report—you make longer term bets after it's out... They can just wait to see what the number is, then make a rational plan... What really matters isn't what happens in the next five minutes. What matters is what happens by the end of the day and then next week.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8 'Charlie Flank Goes to U.S. National Bank' p.69-70
findings.notes: V8-friendly: the suppression window can be expressed on the event clock (release print event), not wall clock, preserving determinism. Perp crypto relevance is partial — BTC reacts to USD macro (FOMC/CPI/NFP) and crypto-native scheduled events (funding, unlocks, upgrades), but there is no session open/close and no one-minute data monopoly; the lesson transfers as 'suppress new entries around scheduled macro prints and prefer higher-timeframe planning after the print,' not as a literal NFP-day rule.
findings.book: Adventures of a Currency Trader - A Fable about Trading, Courage, and Doing the Right Thing 2007

findings.strategy_name: fomo_cockiness_guard
findings.mechanism: early wins inflate perceived skill and trigger FOMO/oversizing, converting a profitable run into ruin; the two documented failure modes are believing one's own B.S. and the fear of missing out
findings.setup_summary: Behavioral guard: after a short winning streak (the book's exemplar: one $10M winner -> 'I lost on my next 13 trades... a fourteen-million-dollar hole'), position size must stay flat and no discretionary size increase or 'trade the opposite of the signal because it worked once' reversal is allowed. 'Making money on my first trade... was probably the worst thing that I could have done.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: consecutive wins or a single outsized win in the account history. Invalidation: any account-level rule cannot invalidate psychology, but the guard lapses only via registry-gated size review after a frozen-OOS sample; there is no market invalidation for this finding.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target geometry; the lesson is a cap on notional escalation and a prohibition on signal-reversal trades driven by one prior lucky opposite-side fill.
findings.quote: Rule Number One: Don't Become Cocky... the fear of missing out was the second greatest mistake that I could ever make. And the first? Believing my own B.S... I lost on my next 13 trades. All of them... I got bold when I should have sat on my profits.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 p.38-39 (13 losses) and p.44 (napkin rule); Ch. 6 'A Turn for the Worse' p.47-54 (doubling up against the signal at FOMC)
findings.notes: Not directly codifiable as an entry signal, but it motivates two concrete V8 gates: (1) the RiskGate should reject size escalation that is keyed to recent win count, and (2) the registry protocol already prevents an Expert from being 'promoted' on a short win-streak sample — this fable is the canonical cautionary tale for the small-sample gate. FOMO behavior in 24/7 perp markets manifests as chasing momentum after a big candle or doubling after a flush; rule 16 (one exposure per direction) partially neutralizes the revenge-double.
findings.book: Adventures of a Currency Trader - A Fable about Trading, Courage, and Doing the Right Thing 2007

findings.strategy_name: pyramiding_position_build
findings.mechanism: scaling into a position in tranches on favorable pullbacks reduces entry risk versus all-in entry and lets confirmed winners compound; adding only to positions already in profit converts a small probe into a large winner
findings.setup_summary: Initiate with a small position (the exemplar opened 5M EUR/JPY at 119.00), then add tranches on each favorable pullback (119.50, 120.00, ... building to 500M) as long as the position remains in profit, exiting only at the pre-planned structure target. The stated contrast: 'I took oversized positions... instead of building the position over time' was the mistake that followed.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: existing exposure in profit and price pulling back within the trend toward the frozen entry-thesis. Invalidation: thesis break (pair cannot hold above the support/entry thesis) — 'I couldn't buy the pair at 119.00 anymore! When I closed the big trade, I lost the right to hold the EUR/JPY at a super-duper discounted price.'
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: market on pullback, tranche-by-tranche. Stop: thesis-level invalidation; the book never pyramids into a losing position. Target: single frozen structure target for the whole pyramid. Expiry: months; no bar expiry.
findings.quote: I didn't put all my trading capital into the first position. Instead, I built it up over time... with any pullback, even slight ones, I added to the winning position... I bought more after that at 119.50. Five million more Euros worth. And then ten million more at 120.00.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'Craig's Ten-Million-Dollar Lesson' p.36-39
findings.notes: Directly conflicts with V8 rule 16 (one active exposure per instrument/direction), so this must be a backlog candidate, not a live family: lifting rule 16 for a pyramiding variant would require a registry experiment beating the single-exposure baseline on frozen OOS. The mechanism is falsifiable in the V8 simulator (fill-at-close tranche adds on pullbacks, single frozen target), and the book's stated failure mode — re-opening at a worse price after closing a winner, then oversizing — is exactly the behavior the lifecycle ExposureBook should gate against.
findings.book: Adventures of a Currency Trader - A Fable about Trading, Courage, and Doing the Right Thing 2007

book_title: The Disciplined Trader: Developing Winning Attitudes (Mark Douglas, 1990, annotated)

findings.strategy_name: Support/Resistance range fade with stop-and-reverse
findings.mechanism: A repeatedly-tested support/resistance level concentrates opposing expectations; the disappointed side is forced to liquidate, so the edges of a balance area are high-probability fades until one side proves dominance.
findings.setup_summary: In an established trading range (book example: a two-week band between 94-10 and 95-25), place resting orders a few ticks inside each boundary: sell near resistance, buy near support, with a stop-and-reverse order beyond the boundary. The weight of each level grows with the number of failed penetration attempts. On 1h BTCUSDT: a defined high/low zone rejected at least 2-3 times with a similar pullback magnitude each time.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = price trades into the resting zone at a range edge. Thesis invalidated when price stops-and-reverses through the boundary by the book's ~6-tick margin (the market defines itself by penetrating), converting the fade into a breakout trade in the penetration direction.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: resting limit orders INSIDE the range edges, not at the exact extreme (early anticipators of the failure sell/buy first and you miss the fill); stop: stop-and-reverse beyond the boundary by a small margin; target: opposite side of the range; no bar expiry stated.
findings.quote: put your orders in a place where the highest probability is that it will continue in the direction of your trade
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'The Psychology of Price Movement' - Support and Resistance / trading range, pp.160-162
findings.notes: Self-fulfilling-prophecy logic ('All beliefs eventually become self-fulfilling prophecies'): S/R works because enough traders act on it. 24/7 perp crypto has clean level tests (no gaps) but high leverage makes liquidations at range edges push ranges through; needs a range-definition feature (location + history) plus a small-margin reverse trigger.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Old resistance becomes support (polarity-flip retest)
findings.mechanism: After a breakout through old resistance, the traders who sold there are either trapped (they bail out near break-even, becoming buyers) or too psychologically pained to sell at that price again, so the level's seller pool empties and old resistance acts as support on retest.
findings.setup_summary: After price convincingly breaks a previously tested resistance and later returns to it, expect old resistance to hold as support: buy the retest. On 1h BTCUSDT: a level that stopped rallies 3+ times, a decisive close through it, then a pullback back to the level.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = retest of the flipped level after a decisive breakout. Thesis invalidated if price trades back decisively through the old level (the flip failed) or if the retest attracts no buying.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: retest at the flipped level; stop: just beyond the flipped level to the downside ('where the market shouldn't be'); target: continuation toward the next significant reference point; no expiry stated.
findings.quote: Hence, old resistance becomes support, and old support becomes resistance for the same reasons.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'Support Becomes Resistance and Resistance Becomes Support', pp.162-163
findings.notes: Supplies the causal mechanism (trapped-seller bail-out + seller-pool depletion) for the backlog breakout_retest family, currently DATA_BLOCKED with requires=location,volatility,history. Distinct from the range fade: this is trend-continuation after a breakout, not mean-reversion at the edge.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: High-retrace-lower-high failure then break of prior low (distribution breakdown)
findings.mechanism: When a second rally fails to exceed a prior high, buyers' expectations are disappointed; if price then penetrates the intervening swing low, disappointed bulls liquidate en masse and there is no one to buy from them, so price falls sharply.
findings.setup_summary: Market makes new highs, sells off; on the second approach the rally fails to exceed or equal the prior high (lower high); entry once price penetrates the prior swing low between the high and the retrace. On 1h BTCUSDT: prior high, lower-high failure, then a bar close below the swing low.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = penetration of the prior swing low after a lower-high failure. Thesis invalidated if the second attempt makes new highs (buyers validated) or the swing low holds on repeated tests.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on break of the prior low; stop: above the failed high / where the market shouldn't be; target: continuation until buyers re-enter at some 'cheap' reference point; no expiry stated.
findings.quote: If prices penetrate that low, watch for buyers to bail out en masse. For them to get out of their position, who is going to buy it from them? ... Fall like a rock.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'High à Retrace à Rally to a Lower High', pp.163-164
findings.notes: Directly corroborates and refines the formalized failed_breakout expert (SHORT, close below windowed prior high after a failed breakout) by adding the prior-swing-low breakdown trigger and the disappointed-expectation liquidation-cascade mechanism. HIGH perp applicability: high leverage turns the 'no buyers to absorb' step into liquidation cascades at the support break.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Trendline break continuation (balance-shift)
findings.mechanism: A trend has a rhythm/flow sustained by imbalance between buyers and sellers; a break of the trendline signals the balance of forces has shifted, and the market tends to keep going in the direction of the break.
findings.setup_summary: In an established trend with a clear trendline and a recognizable ebb-and-flow rhythm, a decisive close beyond the trendline signals a balance shift; enter in the break direction. On 1h BTCUSDT: a multi-day trendline with at least 3 touches broken by a bar close beyond it.
