findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = break beyond the significant trendline. Thesis invalidated if the break stalls and price returns through the trendline (the balance shift did not gain hold) or if no follow-through appears.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: pre-placed order at the price that would confirm the balance change; stop: 'where the market shouldn't be' (just beyond the trendline); target: trend continuation; no expiry stated.
findings.quote: markets that break trendlines have a tendency to keep on going in the direction of the break, because it signals a significant shift in the balance of forces.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'Trends and Trendlines', pp.162-163
findings.notes: Book itself cautions 'trends are a function of time' and the rhythm is a session ebb-and-flow concept; in 24/7 perp crypto the rhythm is weaker and trendlines are noisier, though the balance-shift logic is the same mechanism behind many crypto trend-break continuations. Corroborated across the library's trend-following books.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Aggressor conviction: paying up to buy / selling below last price initiates momentum
findings.mechanism: A trader willing to buy above the last price or sell below it has stronger conviction than the passive side; aggressive initiative makes the last price a new bottom/top, forces prior losers to liquidate, and can gather momentum.
findings.setup_summary: When trades occur beyond the last posted price (takers crossing the spread), treat it as conviction flow that can gather momentum: 'who is paying up to get in or get out?' In perps this is measurable as taker-buy vs taker-sell aggressor volume at the top of the book.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = sustained aggressive buying/selling (price bid/offered to new levels with insufficient counterparties). Thesis invalidated when the aggressor side's conviction runs out, the passive side takes the initiative, or momentum stalls at a significant reference point.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: momentum-following with the aggressive side (no precise entry type given); stop: below/above the aggressor's last defended level; no target or expiry stated.
findings.quote: a trader willing to buy high or sell low instead of buy low or sell high has to have a stronger conviction in his belief in the future value... he is making the last price a bottom.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'The Psychology of Price Movement', pp.152-154
findings.notes: The 'last price becomes a bottom/top' reference-point logic is directly observable in perp order books, but V8's canonical 1h-bar MarketState has no trade tape, so this is a feature-group input gated on tick/agg-trade data (derivatives tape), not an active expert. Mechanism also underlies the failed_breakout and liquidity_sweep_reclaim experts.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Buy/sell away from value (balance-area extremes)
findings.mechanism: Most trading activity clusters in a comfort balance area (bell-curve distribution of price-time); trades away from value have the fewest participants because traders fear being alone there, so the extremes of the balance area are where the best opportunities are.
findings.setup_summary: Identify the value/balance area where the majority of trading activity clusters; trade the first departure of price from its edge back toward value. On 1h BTCUSDT: a high-volume cluster zone; enter on the first test beyond the zone's edge, fade back toward the zone interior.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = price departs from the value-area boundary. Thesis (reversion to value) invalidated if the departure is forceful enough to set off chain reactions - new participants joining the break side and old position-holders liquidating in the break direction.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: at the departure from the value-area edge; stop: beyond the departure point; target: back into the value area; no expiry stated.
findings.quote: to 'buy or sell away from value'... these are the scariest trades to make because the trader who can make them is all alone; there is no safety in numbers.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'Balance Areas', pp.157-158 (citing Steidlmayer & Koy, Markets and Market Logic, 1987)
findings.notes: The book's balance-area concept is the value-area/TPO idea (majority of activity in a bell-curve range) with a psychological twist: traders cluster at 'comfort' (the middle), not fair value. Requires volume-by-price / TPO-style distribution beyond V8's canonical L1 bars; the reversion-to-value trade needs a defined value boundary feature.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Last buyer / public participation exhaustion (distribution top)
findings.mechanism: A bull market requires continual infusion of new buyers; when participation broadens to the least risk-tolerant public and professionals begin distributing into them, the supply of marginal buyers runs out and the market has nowhere to go but down.
findings.setup_summary: Near the end of a sustained rally, watch for participation broadening to the most risk-averse, latest-arriving traders - in perps, observable as extreme funding, crowded longs, surging new accounts and open interest. The professional 'knows the end is near' when the public buys en masse and starts taking profits while buyers still exist.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = broad late/public participation at price highs. Thesis (distribution top) invalidated if new buyers keep being drawn in and price keeps extending - the marginal-buyer pool is not yet exhausted.
findings.risk_geometry: No mechanical entry/stop/target given; a sentiment/flow-based distribution signal, not a bar-level setup.
findings.quote: When the last buyer has bought, the market has no place to go but down.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'High à Retrace à Rally to a Lower High' (public-participation discussion), pp.164-165
findings.notes: The finite-buyer premise is structurally weaker in 24/7 global perp markets where new participants can enter at any hour, but retail crowding is directly observable in crypto via funding rate, long/short ratios and OI. Usable as a participation feature (input to risk/regime), not a standalone entry.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Trading Rule 1: predefine what a loss is in every trade
findings.mechanism: Predefining the market condition that invalidates a trade removes weighing and judging at exit time, letting a loss be executed as an automatic function of the strategy instead of negotiated under pain.
findings.setup_summary: Before entry, specify exactly what the market must look like or do to prove the trade no longer represents an opportunity in the trading timeframe; the loss is defined by an observable market condition, not by dollar pain. This is the book's first formal trading rule.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The predefined invalidation condition IS the thesis-killer: if it occurs, exit. The book warns that failing to execute it on a winner reinforces inappropriate behavior that 'will inevitably lead to disaster'.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry; a pre-entry loss definition. Maps to V8 risk_geometry invalidation and the still_valid dead-thesis exit (a separate exit from the stop-loss).
findings.quote: Predefine what a loss is in every potential trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.16 'Step Two: Dealing with Losses - Trading Rule 1', p.170
findings.notes: This is the book's clearest articulation of V8's dead-thesis/still_valid concept and its separation from the stop-loss: the loss is defined by what the market does, not by price distance. Corroborated across the psychology/craft books in the library.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Trading Rule 2: execute losing trades immediately upon perception
findings.mechanism: Hesitating on a predefined loss either reinforces bad behavior (when it recovers) or starts a pain spiral (when it worsens); immediate execution keeps the trader available for the next opportunity and prevents compounding errors like skipping the next trade or chasing tips.
findings.setup_summary: Upon perception that a trade is a predefined loser, exit immediately with no consideration, weighing, or judgment; if you find yourself weighing, the loss was either not predefined or not being executed. Book's second formal trading rule.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Exit rule, not a setup. Failure modes the book names: letting the loss worsen, then not taking the next opportunity ('which invariably is always a winning trade'), then anger-driven tip-taking ('which invariably is always a loser').
findings.risk_geometry: Exit discipline complementing the stop-loss with a dead-thesis exit; no entry or target; 'keep your contract size light' until flawless execution is second nature.
findings.quote: Execute your losing trades immediately upon perception that they exist.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.16 'Step Two: Dealing with Losses - Trading Rule 2', pp.170-171
findings.notes: In perp crypto with high leverage this discipline is what separates a controlled loss from liquidation; the book frames it as protecting future decision-making, not just capital. Maps to V8 RiskGate/deterministic admission and the simulator's STOP_FIRST semantics.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Expertise in one repeating behavior pattern before broadening
findings.mechanism: More information is not better in trading; limiting awareness to one mechanical behavior pattern builds confidence and accuracy, while information overload from many patterns leads to confusion and losses.
findings.setup_summary: Choose one simple, preferably mechanical, trading system that identifies one behavior pattern that repeats with some degree of frequency; understand every relationship between its components and its profit potential; avoid all other information and opportunities; trade one market, at most two.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Methodology guidance, not a market setup. Book: stay with the exercise until it becomes 'second nature', then and only then broaden.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: become an expert at just one particular type of behavior pattern that repeats itself with some degree of frequency
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.16 'Step Three: Becoming an Expert at Just One Market Behavior', pp.171-172
findings.notes: Independent corroboration of V8's expert ontology: one Expert per behavior family, the complexity budget (max 3 active), and the absence of a shared scorer/ranker. Also notes perception and execution are separate skills - a thesis can be perceived and still not executed.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Take all system signals; think in probabilities; don't outguess the system
findings.mechanism: Trading systems mathematically quantify past collective-behavior relationships into statistical odds; outguessing them destroys the trade sample and blocks the experience needed to believe in probable outcomes, and 2-3 consecutive losses are normal for most systems.
findings.setup_summary: Commit to trading a well-defined-entry/exit system exactly by its rules for a set learning period, taking every signal including the losing ones; risk per trade must be an amount completely within tolerance so pain does not shut down learning; only after flawless execution becomes habit can contract size grow.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Methodology guidance. The book's Catch-22: you won't believe in the system's odds unless you execute it long enough to internalize them, and you can't execute it long enough without the belief - the resolution is discipline, not discretion.
findings.risk_geometry: Position sizing: risk per trade must be fully comfortable ('amount of money you risk per trade should be an amount that you are completely comfortable with'); 'keep your contract size light'.
findings.quote: taking all the signals generated by your system is the only way you can get the firsthand experience you need to establish a belief in probable outcomes
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.16 'Step Four: Learning How to Execute a Trading System Flawlessly', pp.173-176
findings.notes: Supports V8's frozen-OOS / registry discipline: the lab must consume all candidate episodes of a family, not select favorable ones, and a family's short run of consecutive losses is not itself evidence of failure. Also: 'Any identified pattern may or may not be repeating itself' - no pattern is valid until it completes.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

findings.strategy_name: Go with the flow: align with the dominant force until the balance shifts
findings.mechanism: Prices move in the direction of the greatest force - traders fulfilling their beliefs about future value; identifying and aligning with the dominant side, then re-aligning when significant reference points show the balance shift, is the easiest way to make money.
findings.setup_summary: Identify which side is establishing dominance (who is paying up, who is passive and liquidating); trade with that side; when price reaches significant reference points where the dominant side could be disappointed, watch for the balance to shift and re-align with the new dominant side.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Alignment invalidated when the dominant force loses conviction at a significant reference point (sellers return in force / buyers stop paying up) and the balance shifts; the book's Step Five question set (who is paying up, how much strength, is momentum building, what would disappoint the predominate force) is the monitoring protocol.
findings.risk_geometry: No mechanical entry/stop/target given; principle-level guidance.
findings.quote: The greatest number with the strongest belief will always be right. The easiest way to make money is to go with the flow.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.16 'Step Five: Learning to Think in Probabilities', pp.177-179
findings.notes: Foundational trend-following rationale, heavily corroborated across the library's trend-following corpus. In V8 terms it supports the regime/flow filter concept and the 'trade with the side that has established dominance' logic behind trend_pullback, rather than a standalone entry.
findings.book: The Disciplined Trader - Developing Winning Attitudes 1990 - annotated

book_title: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques: A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East (1991), Part 1 (Ch.1-14)

findings.strategy_name: Springs and Upthrusts (Wyckoff false-breakout return)
findings.mechanism: unsustained penetration of a range extreme creates a vacuum: price returns to the opposite side of the congestion band
findings.setup_summary: In a lateral range, price momentarily pierces a prior low (spring) or breaches a prior high (upthrust) but the penetration is unsustained (no durable close through). Spring: buy on reclaim above the old lows, objective is retest of the upper band, stop under the spring-day low. Upthrust: short once the new high fails to hold, objective is retest of the lower band, stop above the new high. The book explicitly states the target (opposite end of the trading range) and protective stop (the new high/low of the false breakout) for both. Confluence with a candlestick signal (shooting star on the upthrust day, hammer on the spring day) strengthens the entry.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: intraday breach of a prior extreme that does not hold on a close basis (the book's beachhead rule: bulls must CLOSE above resistance and then hold old resistance as new support; intra-day pushes are not enough). Invalidation: sustained close through the level, or (for upthrust) the market establishing camp in enemy territory.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on the reclaim/close back inside the range (book: buy if prices push back above the old lows). Stop: under the spring-day low (spring) or above the new high made on the false breakout (upthrust). Target: the opposite end of the congestion band. No expiry stated.
findings.quote: Trading springs and upthrusts is so effective because they provide a clear target (the opposite end of the trading range) and protective stop (the new high or low made with the 'false breakout').
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'Candlesticks with Trendlines - Springs and Upthrusts' pp.193-200 (also scouting-party/beachhead discussion p.199-201)
findings.notes: This is direct corroboration of two existing V8 families: the spring is liquidity_sweep_reclaim (wick through prior low reclaimed by close) and the upthrust is failed_breakout (close below windowed prior high after failed breakout). The book adds explicit, concrete risk geometry: stop beyond the false-breakout extreme, target = opposite side of the range. In leveraged 24/7 crypto, stop-run sweeps of prior 1h/4h highs and lows are pervasive, so the close-based beachhead confirmation ('it is a close above' - Ch.1 p.7) is the load-bearing rule to keep.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Hammer / Hanging-man long-shadow reversal
findings.mechanism: a long lower shadow with a tiny body at the range top shows sellers failed to hold the low; the same line is bullish or bearish purely by trend context
findings.setup_summary: On the chosen timeframe, a bar has (1) real body at the upper end of the range, (2) lower shadow at least twice the body height, (3) no or very short upper shadow. After a downtrend this is a bullish hammer (bottom reversal); after an uptrend the identical line is a bearish hanging man (top reversal) that REQUIRES next-bar confirmation (open below the hanging-man's real body, or a black close below its close). Confidence scales with shadow length / smallness of body; white hammer body slightly more bullish, black hanging-man body slightly more bearish.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: hammer/hanging-man shape in a defined trend. Hanging man invalidated if next bar opens higher / gaps up (book: 'if the market opens lower the next day, those who bought... are now left hanging'); hammer invalidated if bears make new lows without reclaiming (hammer 4 case in Ch.4).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar close (book Ch.1: patterns complete on the close). Stop: 'the hammer's low could be used as a protective stop out level' (stated for trendline-test hammer, Ch.11) or under the support line. Target: not stated in book - use structure/opposite trend. No expiry.
findings.quote: The longer the lower shadow, the shorter the upper shadow and the smaller the real body the more meaningful the bullish hammer or bearish hanging man.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 4 'Reversal Patterns - Hammer and Hanging-Man Lines' pp.28-38
findings.notes: Single most falsifiable candlestick rule in the book (three crisp criteria + confirmation requirement) and it is the closest candlestick cousin to V8's liquidity_sweep_reclaim (the hammer's lower shadow IS a wick through a low that gets reclaimed). Proposed new family candidate with registry decision; hammer is LONG after downtrend, hanging man SHORT after uptrend with mandatory next-bar confirmation - the confirmation gate should be a hard variant rule, not advisory.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Engulfing / dark-cloud cover / piercing (body-penetration reversal continuum)
findings.mechanism: reversal strength scales with how deeply the second opposite-color body penetrates the first body - partial (dark-cloud/piercing) vs full (engulfing) solar eclipse
findings.setup_summary: Two-bar pattern in a clearly definable trend: (a) bullish/bearish engulfing - second real body of opposite color engulfs the prior real body (shadows need not be engulfed); (b) dark-cloud cover at tops - second bar opens above the prior high and closes >50% into the prior white body; (c) piercing at bottoms - second bar opens under the prior low and closes >50% into the prior black body. Penetration depth is the ordinal strength signal (engulfing > dark-cloud; piercing must exceed the midpoint, on-neck/in-neck/thrusting below-midpoint variants are bearish). Strength factors: small-then-large body pair, after protracted or very fast move, heavy volume on second bar.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pattern forms in a definable trend. Invalidation: 'If a long, white real body closes above the highs of the dark-cloud cover, or the bearish engulfing pattern, it could presage another rally'; closing under the lows of a bullish engulfing/piercing via a long black candle resumes the downleg.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: after second-bar close / next bar. Stop: for dark-cloud, 'a benchmark to place a stop - at the new high of the second day of the dark-cloud cover pattern'; for the engulfing pair, beyond the engulfing bar's extreme. Target: not stated. No expiry.
findings.quote: The greater the degree of penetration of the black real body's close into the prior white real body, the greater the chance for a top.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 4 'Engulfing Pattern' pp.38-43, 'Dark-cloud Cover' pp.43-48, 'Piercing Pattern' pp.48-54
findings.notes: Key V8-relevant nuance: engulfing can flag a top WITHOUT a new high being made (the book shows this repeatedly - 'it may give a reversal signal not available using the criteria for a reversal day'), i.e. the pattern is not dependent on gapped opens which are rare in continuous 24/7 markets. The >50% midpoint penetration threshold is a clean, testable parameter. Book notes the bullish engulfing at a downtrend bottom is one of its strongest signals - comparable to failed_breakout but in the opposite (bottom) direction.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Doji after a rally (top-calling indecision with bottom asymmetry)
findings.mechanism: a session that opens and closes at the same price signals buyer indecision; an uptrend needs buyer conviction to persist, so doji breaks the scaffolding; in downtrends a falling market can continue by its own weight so doji loses reversal power
findings.setup_summary: A doji (open==close within a few ticks) after a long white candle in an uptrend - especially after a prolonged/overbought rally - warns of a top; the more conservative the trader, the more confirmation is required (next black candle, hanging man, or long black session). Falsifiable asymmetry claim: 'as good as doji are at calling tops... they tend to lose reversal potential in downtrends' - doji need more confirmation to signal a bottom than a top. Doji shadows can become support/resistance; doji are only meaningful in markets where doji are not already frequent (do not use intra-day charts under 30 minutes).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: doji (or near-doji at an important junction) after an uptrend. Invalidation: no confirming follow-through; a doji at the middle of a trading band or in doji-dense markets is noise; doji star bearishness negated if the next bar gaps higher.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on confirmation bar close. Stop: beyond the doji extreme or below the supporting trendline. Target: structure-based. No expiry.
findings.quote: Yet, as good as doji are at calling tops, based on experience, they tend to lose reversal potential in downtrends.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8 'The Magic Doji' pp.149-164 (esp. 'Doji at Tops' pp.150-153, 'Doji after a Long White Candlestick' pp.154, 'Doji as Support and Resistance' p.161)
findings.notes: The top/bottom asymmetry is a directly falsifiable directional claim on BTCUSDT 1h (top-calling doji + next-bar confirmation vs bottom doji with more confirmation required). The 'doji becomes support/resistance' idea feeds the location feature group. The near-doji tolerance ('a few ticks') needs a volatility-relative (ATR) threshold in V8, not an absolute tick.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Change of polarity (old support becomes resistance / old resistance becomes support)
findings.mechanism: traders are emotionally attached to their entry price; when a tested level breaks, trapped buyers become sellers on retests, flipping the level's polarity
findings.setup_summary: Old support, once broken, converts to new resistance and old resistance converts to new support; potency is proportional to the number of times the level was tested and the volume/open interest at each test. The mechanism is explicitly psychological: three buyer groups (bargain hunters, stopped-out longs seeking vindication, adders) all re-enter at the old level; once it breaks, those same groups become sellers at the level. Tradeable form: a flipped level retested with a confirming candlestick (hammer at old-resistance-now-support; the book's silver example: support A,B,C,D broke, rallies to ~$5.33 were used to exit longs).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: a historically multi-tested level that price closes through, then returns to. Invalidation: a clean close back through the flipped level in the direction of the old trend (e.g., old resistance re-taken above re-bullishes).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on the retest with candlestick confirmation. Stop: beyond the flipped level or the signal-candle extreme. Target: next structure; book pairs polarity with 50% retracements to set targets (orange-juice example: support expected at $1.65 = 50% correction AND prior resistance).
findings.quote: The most important price on any chart is the price at which you entered the market.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'The Change of Polarity Principle' pp.201-207 (psychology explanation p.204-205)
findings.notes: This is the core location-family feature for V8: a 'tested-level count' and 'prior-support-flipped' feature belong in marketstate's location group, and it upgrades stop/target placement for failed_breakout and liquidity_sweep_reclaim (old level = new magnet). The potency claim (number of tests + volume at tests) is falsifiable. Heavily corroborated across the rest of this library (Edwards & Magee, Murphy, Wyckoff), making it a strong candidate for a formalized location feature rather than a new expert.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Windows (gaps) as continuation, support/resistance, and pullback magnets
findings.mechanism: a gap in the direction of the trend marks a discontinuity in available supply/demand; corrections are expected to travel back to the window, which then acts as a floor or ceiling
findings.setup_summary: A window is a gap between the prior and current session's price extremes. In an uptrend a window implies further rise and should be a floor on pullbacks: 'corrections go back to the window', so buy pullbacks into the window while it holds. If the window closes and selling pressure continues after the close, the prior uptrend is voided (and vice versa for downtrends). Corollaries: windows from a congestion zone or a new high deserve special attention; three windows in one trend imply a top/bottom is near (especially with a turning-point candle after the third); a window in a rising market not closed within three days predicts a rally.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: window formed in a trending market; pullback into the window holds. Invalidation: window closes AND opposite-direction pressure continues through it (trend voided) - the book's Dow-crash example required both closing the window AND continuation of buying force.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on pullback into the window (buy zone) / short into window-as-resistance. Stop: under/over the window. Target: not stated (trend resumption). No expiry.
findings.quote: Traditional Japanese technical analysis (that is, candlesticks) asserts that corrections go back to the window.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 7 'Continuation Patterns - Windows' pp.119-129
findings.notes: True price gaps are structurally rarer in 24/7 perps than in the 1990s futures this book covers, which caps applicability at MEDIUM. But the window concept survives in crypto as daily/weekly-candle gaps and as the 'fair-value gap / imbalance' level that price retests - the pullback-to-window behavior is observable. DATA_BLOCKED until a gap-definition feature (prior-candle extreme vs current extreme on the bar close) is added to marketstate.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Morning/evening star and doji-star (three-bar gap-stalemate reversal)
findings.mechanism: a star (small body not overlapping the prior body) represents a deadlock in the bulls-vs-bears tug of war; the prior trend's power has dissipated and the market is vulnerable to reversal once the third bar confirms
findings.setup_summary: Three-bar patterns: morning star (bottom) = tall black body, small body gapping lower (star), then a white body closing well within the first bar's black body; evening star (top) = mirror with black third bar intruding into the first white body. Doji stars (star is a doji) are more potent but demand next-session confirmation; a doji star in an uptrend is negated if the following session gaps higher. Evening star needs only the star's body low above the first body high (weaker requirement than a Western island top). Factors: gaps before/after the star, third bar closes deeply into first body, light volume on bar 1 and heavy on bar 3.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pattern completion (third bar close well into the first body). Invalidation: no confirmation the session after a doji star; doji-star bearishness voided if next bar gaps higher white; third-bar white that closes only shallowly into the first black body (on-neck/in-neck/thrusting) is bearish not bullish.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: after third-bar completion (close-confirmed). Stop: beyond the pattern's extreme (e.g., under the morning star's low). Target: not stated. No expiry.
findings.quote: The star's small real body represents a stalemate in the tug of war between the bulls and bears.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'Stars' pp.55-70 (Morning Star p.56, Evening Star p.59, Doji Stars p.64, Shooting Star p.70)
findings.notes: The star's defining feature is a body that does NOT overlap the prior body - in continuous 24/7 trading this 'gap-away' condition is less frequent than in gapping futures/equities, hence MEDIUM. The load-bearing, crypto-robust core is the third-bar-close-deeply-into-first-body confirmation gate, which is fully observable on 1h bars. The evening-doji-star 'negated if next bar gaps higher' rule is a clean trigger/invalidation pair.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Oscillator divergence (RSI/stochastics) with trend-conditional use
findings.mechanism: price making new extremes while momentum (RSI/stochastics) fails to confirm shows the move is internally weak; divergence warns the trend is stalling
findings.setup_summary: Negative/bearish divergence: price at a new high while the oscillator does not make a concurrent high (more meaningful when the oscillator is in overbought territory, RSI>70/80). Positive/bullish divergence: price at a new low while the oscillator prints a higher low. Entry requires confirmation: RSI moving back above its prior high, slow %K crossing back above %D (book's two-step stochastic rule: oversold <=25 for %D + positive divergence + %K crossing %D). Hard directional gate from the book: use oscillator signals only in the direction of the dominant trend; 'overbought markets usually should not be shorted' - overbought is a defense signal for longs, not a short trigger.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence in an overbought/oversold region with a crossover/confirmation signal. Invalidation: price keeps making records (divergence without confirmation is only a warning); a new major trend starting from a congestion-breakout can keep the oscillator pinned overbought.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on the confirmation crossover or a coincident candlestick signal (the book shows candlesticks can give the signal a few days earlier than RSI confirmation alone). Stop: beyond the recent swing extreme. Target: not stated. No expiry.
findings.quote: Do not short on a bearish oscillator signal unless the prevailing trend is heading south.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 14 'Candlesticks with Oscillators' pp.227-236 (RSI pp.228-232, Stochastics pp.232-234)
findings.notes: The trend-gate rule (oscillator signals only with the dominant trend; overbought is not a short trigger) is the anti-naive-mean-reversion lesson and aligns with V8's behavior-driven design: divergence is a trend-stall warning, not an unconditional reversal. RSI/stochastics are cheap to compute PIT on 1h closes. Divergence is corroborated across the library; candidate is falsifiable with fixed 14-period RSI and a 'new price extreme without new oscillator extreme' scan.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Retracement levels (50%/38%/62%) as confluence resistance/support for candlestick entries
findings.mechanism: retracements of the prior swing act as psychological magnets; resistance/support is expected at the level and is confirmed when a bearish/bullish candlestick forms there
findings.setup_summary: Compute 38%/50%/62% retracements of the last swing (50% is the most-widely-monitored). Expect resistance in a bear market / support in a bull market at the level, and require a candlestick reversal indicator at that level to act (book's gold example: 50% retracement of A-B at $464 -> bearish engulfing at $469 within $5 -> next leg lower; crude oil: 50% of rally at $29.05 -> hammer at $28.30 -> $5 rally). When the trend is strong and a level is pierced, escalate to the next deeper retracement (50% of the larger move) - the book shows a 50% of the whole 1987-89 decline at $430 stopping gold at $425 with harami + hanging man. Confluence with old levels (change of polarity) and moving averages increases reliability.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches a retracement level and a bearish/bullish candlestick pattern forms there. Invalidation: a close through the level (the book would then escalate to the next retracement of the larger move).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: on the candlestick confirmation at the level. Stop: beyond the level (e.g., past the $464 zone in the gold example). Target: retracement levels can also project targets (measured move from double bottom). No expiry.
findings.quote: Thus, at $464 you look for resistance and confirmation of resistance with a bearish candlestick indicator.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 12 'Candlesticks with Retracement Levels' pp.209-214 (50% rule p.210, 'a 32% retracement is where first resistance is sometimes seen' p.175)
findings.notes: Retracement levels are best treated as a feature (level-distance feature in the location group: distance to 50/38/62% of a frozen swing) consumed by entry confirmation, not as an expert - the book itself frames them as 'look for resistance AND confirmation with a bearish candlestick indicator', i.e. the candlestick is the trigger. MEDIUM for crypto: levels are magnets but heavily arbitraged; the 50%-of-larger-move escalation is a useful regime nuance.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: 'Stomach 80% full' - correction after ~8-10 consecutive new highs/lows
findings.mechanism: extended runs of record highs/lows without a meaningful correction concentrate longs/shorts and exhaust fuel; after about eight to ten records the odds of a significant correction are strong
findings.setup_summary: Count consecutive 'record highs' (new highs for the move) or 'record lows' without a meaningful correction. After about 8-10 such records the odds are strong that a significant correction will unfold; at 8+ records the Japanese say 'the stomach is 80% full'. The book's gold example: 8 new higher highs reaching a window-resistance area was a double caution (record count + resistance confluence). A meaningful correction resets the count.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 8-10 consecutive record highs (or lows) with no meaningful correction. Invalidation: a meaningful correction resets the count; a persistent new-leg up past ~10 records (the rule is a probability statement, not a barrier).
findings.risk_geometry: Risk-rule/filter, not an entry: use as a caution signal to trail stops, take profit on longs (or shorts), or gate new long entries near resistance; the book pairs it with resistance confluence (window 2) for stronger tops.
findings.quote: Candlestick theory states that after about eight to ten new highs or lows, without a meaningful correction, the odds are strong that a significant correction will unfold.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 7 'Continuation Patterns - Windows' (Eight New Record Highs, gold example) p.128
findings.notes: Extremely falsifiable counting rule on BTCUSDT 1h: a 'consecutive record count' feature in the history group is trivial to compute PIT, and leveraged crypto trends commonly run 8-10 1h records before violent corrections (funding accumulates). Best mapped as a risk/regime feature (reduce long aggression, raise stop-trail sensitivity) rather than a standalone expert - the book itself presents it as caution confluence, and a correction is not necessarily a reversal.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Protective stops at trade initiation + expectation-based (dead-thesis) exit
findings.mechanism: stops placed at the time of the original trade (when most objective) cap losses; a position is held only while price action confirms the entry thesis, so a contradiction or failure to confirm is an exit trigger
findings.setup_summary: Methodology rule: place the stop when the trade is initiated (objectivity is highest then); define risk/reward parameters with the technicals before entry; stay in the position only if the market performs according to expectations - if subsequent price action contradicts or fails to confirm, exit ('Lose your opinion, not your money'). Stop placement guidance throughout the book: under the signal-candle low (hammer's low), under the supporting trendline, above the false-breakout high, or at the new high of the dark-cloud cover day. Two mottos: 'all long-term trends begin as short-term moves' and 'there is no room for hope in the market'.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a - this is the risk gate itself.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop: at trade initiation; below the signal-bar low, below the trendline, or above the false-breakout high (structure-based, not % or ATR-based in this book). No fixed target or expiry - exit on contrary price action or on a new opposing candlestick pattern (Ch.1: 'Some Japanese candlestick practitioners place a trade based on a candlestick signal and stay with that trade until another candlestick pattern tells them to offset').
findings.quote: Stay in the position only if the market performs according to expectations. If subsequent price action either contradicts or fails to confirm these expectations, it is time to exit.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 sidebar 'The Importance of Protective Stops' pp.188-189; also Ch. 1 pp.7-10 and Ch. 9 p.165
findings.notes: Directly maps to two V8 mechanisms that already exist: (1) RiskGate deterministic admission with stops in risk_geometry, and (2) the dead-thesis (still_valid) exit in lifecycle - the book's 'stay only if the market performs according to expectations' IS V8's still_valid semantic, and the 'another candlestick pattern tells them to offset' rule is a lifecycle exit trigger. 'There is no room for hope in the market' is the anti-hold-and-hope justification for deterministic stop execution. V8's STOP_FIRST simulator and frozen risk_geometry comply.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Rule of Multiple Technical Techniques (confluence at one price area)
findings.mechanism: the more technical indicators that assemble at the same price area, the greater the chance of an accurate forecast; the coincidence is a marker of an important market juncture
findings.setup_summary: Methodology principle (Arthur Sklarew): confluence of independent technical indicators at the same price area raises forecast accuracy. The book's canonical example: gold resistance at $425-433 derived from four independent devices (50% retracement of 1987-89 move = $430; double-bottom measured move = $425; late-1988 high = $433; Elliott 4th-wave constraint = $425) - gold peaked at $425 and the bear market resumed. Also demonstrated with candlestick clusters (Ch.10: hanging man + harami + shooting star + tweezers top within three sessions at the same highs = a short-term top). A falsifiable corollary in the book: there is always a price where the thesis is wrong (for gold, a close above $433).
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a - methodology. Note the book's built-in falsification rule: 'there is always a price where I will say my market view is wrong.'
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: The more technical indicators that assemble at the same price area, the greater the chance of an accurate forecast.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part 2 intro 'The Rule of Multiple Technical Techniques' pp.172-176 and Ch. 10 'A Confluence of Candlesticks' pp.177-183
findings.notes: For V8 this supports a registry-gated confluence/filter concept, but it must not become the absent-by-default router/shared scorer: the constitution (rule 14) keeps those out unless a registry experiment beats the single-expert baseline. The safe reading is (a) require independent confirmation before acting on a marginal candlestick signal, and (b) encode the 'price at which the thesis is wrong' as an explicit invalidation - which V8 already does via frozen refs and still_valid. The 4-indicator gold example is a strong pedagogical anchor for feature-group 'location' confluence.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Spring (false breakdown) and upthrust (false breakout) at congestion bands
findings.mechanism: stop-run under/over a congestion band creates a vacuum; close-based reclaim signals the trapped side is wrong
findings.setup_summary: In a lateral congestion band, prices undercut band support and then close back above it (spring = bullish), or push above band resistance and close back below it (upthrust = bearish). The reclaim must hold on a close; the book repeatedly requires close-based hold of the broken level before acting (corn: hammer holding $2.65 support on a close).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close back on the reclaimed side of a broken congestion-band edge after an undercut/overthrow. Invalidated if price closes back through the reclaimed edge toward the failed side.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on reclaim-bar close (book buys next session after confirmation); stop beyond the undercut low (spring) or failed high (upthrust); target = opposite side of the congestion band or the prior range boundary.
findings.quote: Spring—when prices break under the support of a horizontal congestion band and then springs back above the 'broken support' area. This is bullish.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary B 'Spring'/'Upthrust' (pp. 303-307); Ch. 20 corn Exhibit 20.4, p. 285; Ch. 20 crude/silver examples
findings.notes: Directly corroborates V8's formalized liquidity_sweep_reclaim family. Adds two refinements: (1) congestion-band context (sweeps are traded only at band edges, not at arbitrary extremes) and (2) close-based hold confirmation before the reclaim is trusted (matches V8's still_valid/reclaim semantics).
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Trend-context filter and confluence requirement for candlestick signals
findings.mechanism: a pattern's meaning is conditional on the dominant trend; single-pattern signals without independent confirmation are weak
findings.setup_summary: Candlestick signals are only actionable in the direction of the prevailing higher-timeframe trend (a bullish hammer in a bear market is not a buy; a bullish signal in a bull market, especially confirmed by an independent oscillator/volume signal, is a buying point). Reversal patterns are also context-conditional (doji is more significant as a top than a bottom).
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - this is a gating methodology, not a tradeable setup. V8 should apply it as a regime/admission filter before any single-pattern setup is allowed to emit.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A
findings.quote: Be flexible about chart reading. Where you stand in relation to the overall technical evidence may be more important than an individual candlestick pattern. For example, a bullish candlestick signal in a major bear market should not be used as a buy signal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 14 'The Rule of Multiple Technical Techniques' (pp. 172-176, 236); Conclusion (pp. 287-288)
findings.notes: The book states this as its central operating principle and repeats it (Ch. 14, Conclusion, and the trade examples in Ch. 20 where the author refuses a bullish hammer in a downtrend). For V8 this argues against context-free candlestick triggers: pattern emissions should be gated by a trend/regime feature, and confluence (oscillator or volume) should be a strength signal. Corroborates the plan's regime-filter concept.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Oscillator divergence (price extremes not confirmed by momentum) with candlestick confirmation
findings.mechanism: when price makes a new extreme but momentum does not, the driving force is decelerating, so the trend is at risk
findings.setup_summary: Price prints a new low (high) while stochastics/RSI/momentum print a higher low (lower high) - a positive (negative) divergence; when a candlestick bottoming (topping) signal (hammer, dark-cloud cover, evening star) appears in the same zone, the prior trend is treated as ended. Exhibits: S&P 1990 stochastics divergence at hammer cluster; gold momentum divergence at long-legged doji.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence extreme + candlestick reversal in the same zone. Invalidated if price prints a further new extreme without a reclaiming close (divergence persists but trend resumes).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on confirmation bar close; stop beyond the divergence extreme (swing low/high); target = prior range or polarity level. Book gives no fixed R-multiples.
findings.quote: If prices reach new highs and stochastics do not, this is a negative divergence and is bearish. If prices establish new lows and stochastics do not, this is a positive divergence and is bullish.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 14 'Candlesticks with Oscillators' (Exhibits 14.5-14.8, pp. 232-239); Glossary B 'Divergence'
findings.notes: Oscillators are computable continuously on 1h perp bars. Caveat for crypto: divergences are frequent in hard-trending perps and the book itself only treats them as meaningful with the candlestick confirmation - so the divergence alone is a weak feature; the confirmed variant is the backlog candidate.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Oscillator overbought/oversold extreme with candlestick confirmation
findings.mechanism: at market-specific oscillator extremes, continuation is unlikely; a candlestick reversal at the extreme raises the odds of a top/bottom
findings.setup_summary: When momentum/stochastics reach a market-specific overbought (heating-oil example: 10-day momentum ~+200) or oversold (~-400) level, the market should stall or back off; the odds of a reversal increase if a bearish (evening star, harami cross) or bullish (hammer) candlestick pattern appears at the same extreme. Stochastics: a %K/%D cross from under 25% is a stronger signal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: oscillator extreme + candlestick reversal in the same zone. Invalidated if the oscillator re-extends to a new extreme with price following (extreme levels are sticky, so a level alone is not a signal).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on candlestick confirmation close; stop beyond the extreme swing; target = retracement of the prior move. No fixed R-multiples stated.
findings.quote: At the 200-point overbought level, continuation of the prior rally is unlikely and the market should either trade sideways or backoff. The odds of a top reversal with an overbought momentum reading are increased if there is bearish candlestick confirmation.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 14, Exhibit 14.9 heating oil (p. 238); stochastics oversold cross, Exhibit 14.5 (p. 235)
findings.notes: Key methodological point: the book calibrates extremes per-market (not fixed 80/20) - a variant-counting argument for V8. In crypto, extremes are sticky in trending regimes, so the candlestick-confirmation leg is load-bearing.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Light-volume test of a prior high or support level
findings.mechanism: a retest of a level on shrinking volume shows the aggressive side's force is drained, raising double-top/double-bottom odds
findings.setup_summary: A retest of a prior swing high on volume lower than the first test signals draining buying power (bearish, raises double-top odds - bonds example: 379k vs 504k contracts); a retest of support on light volume signals draining selling force (bullish - bonds doji-tweezers bottom, 234k vs 448k). Usually paired with small real bodies, doji, or tweezers at the level.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price returns to a windowed prior extreme on volume below the first test's volume. Invalidated if the level breaks decisively on expanding volume (rejection was wrong; the level was not defended).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on next-bar confirmation; stop beyond the tested level; the double-top example gives a minimum measured target (bonds: 'double top gave a minimum measured target of 90').
findings.quote: A light volume test of a support level suggests a diminution of selling force and is, consequently, bullish. Conversely, a light volume test of a previous high is bearish since it demonstrates a draining of buying power.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 15 'Candlesticks with Volume and Open Interest', Exhibits 15.1-15.3 (pp. 241-245)
findings.notes: The book's stated limitation - futures volume is reported a day late (p. 241) - does not apply to perps, where volume is real-time; this is one of the cleanest transfers in the book. Measured-move targeting on a confirmed double top is a falsifiable target rule.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Two-bar candlestick reversals (engulfing, harami, hanging man, doji) with next-bar confirmation
findings.mechanism: the reversal bar only becomes a signal when the next session confirms by closing in the reversal direction
findings.setup_summary: Pattern definitions are precise: bullish engulfing = white body engulfs prior black body in a downtrend; bearish engulfing = black body engulfs prior white body in an uptrend; harami = small body inside a large prior body ('truce'); a hanging man or hammer only becomes bearish/bullish with next-session confirmation (e.g., a black session with a lower close). Doji after a long white body is a top warning; doji is more significant at tops than bottoms.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pattern at an extended zone (uptrend/downtrend location). Hanging-man/doji/hammer variants require next-bar confirmation before acting; invalidated if the confirmation session does not follow through or if the pattern's extreme is violated.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the confirmation bar close. Book example (corn): buy at $2.68 with stop under support at $2.64, target downward-sloping resistance at $2.79; earlier example moved stop to breakeven when a nearer resistance stalled the move.
findings.quote: A hanging man... signals the market has become vulnerable, but there should be bearish confirmation the next session (i.e., a black candlestick session with a lower close or a weaker opening) to signal a top.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary A (engulfing, harami, hanging man, doji, pp. 289-301); Ch. 20 corn/coffee trade examples (pp. 284-286); Ch. 15 bonds doji-tweezers bottom (p. 243)
findings.notes: Representative of the book's whole reversal-pattern family (engulfing/harami/doji/hammer/morning-evening star are all precisely defined in Glossary A). The distinct falsifiable claims: (1) pattern + next-bar confirmation beats pattern alone, and (2) patterns are context-conditional ('doji days are usually more significant as reversals in uptrends than in downtrends'). Part 1 likely covers the pure pattern definitions; this finding anchors the confirmation and context requirements.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Change of polarity - old support becomes resistance (and vice versa)
findings.mechanism: a defended level that breaks leaves both a vacuum and a positional memory; price that returns to the level finds the former defenders as counterparties
findings.setup_summary: A zone that acted as support acts as resistance once broken (and conversely). Coffee example: late-March/May lows near $0.92 broke on June 14; the brief rally stopped exactly at $0.92, confirming the flipped zone, and a short was taken on June 21 when price failed to clear the window resistance, with a stop above $0.9175 and a $0.8675 objective.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price stalls/rejects at a former-support-now-resistance (or former-resistance-now-support) zone, preferably with a bearish (bullish) candlestick at the zone. Invalidated if price closes back through the zone to the prior side (flip failed).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on rejection at the flipped zone (close/confirmation); stop beyond the zone/reference extreme; target = the next prior support level. Book uses a window high as the stop reference.
findings.quote: Remember the axiom that old support can become resistance. The late March and May lows were near $.92... This level became resistance.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 20 coffee example (pp. 283-284); Glossary B 'Change of polarity' (p. 303); Ch. 7 references (pp. 201-207)
findings.notes: Cleanly transferable: perp price levels are not distorted by overnight gaps, so polarity-flip zones are a natural 'location' feature for MarketState. Could later form a standalone location-based expert (entry on rejection at a flipped zone), but the book's evidence is case-study only.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Structural stop/target placement off swing reference points
findings.mechanism: the stop is placed beyond the nearest defended reference so a close through it falsifies the thesis; targets are structural, not fixed-R
findings.setup_summary: From the Ch. 20 trade journal: stops go beyond the defended reference (neckline, window, support line, hammer low) and targets go to structural levels (prior-year support, range boundary, retest of hammer lows). Position is moved to breakeven when price stalls at a nearer resistance and the short-term objective is not reached; entry direction is gated by the dominant trend (bear market => short rallies only).
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - risk methodology, not a setup.
findings.risk_geometry: Soybeans: short $6.27, stop above neckline $6.35, target $5.90 support. Corn: buy $2.68, stop under support $2.64, target $2.79 resistance. Crude: short, stop above window $17.65, target retest of hammer lows. Silver: stop moved to breakeven when $21.75 resistance stalled the move.
findings.quote: On June 13, I recommended a short at $6.27. The stop was above the neckline at $6.35. The target was $5.90 (this was based on a support area earlier in the year).
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 20 'How I Have Used Candlesticks' (pp. 281-286)
findings.notes: Direct input to V8's risk_geometry: the book's stops are structural (beyond a defended reference) rather than fixed R-multiples - motivates a structural-stop variant of the existing stop_r parameter. Also demonstrates break-even management when a nearer objective fails and 'trend context gates direction' (refuses a bullish hammer in a downtrend).
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Open-interest trend confirmation, high-OI stop cascade, and trapped-longs supply
findings.mechanism: rising OI shows new participants financing the move; falling OI during a rally means short covering; unusually high OI at highs turns stop-losses into a cascade and traps late longs as future supply
findings.setup_summary: (1) Rising OI confirms the trend (new longs aggressive in up-moves, new shorts in down-moves); a rally on declining OI is short covering and vulnerable. (2) Unusually high OI coinciding with new price highs presages trouble: sell-stops clustered along the advance trigger a chain-reaction cascade once price turns (sugar 1990), and longs who survived are trapped overhead, so any rally meets their exit supply.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger for the cascade: OI at unusual highs concurrent with new price highs. Invalidated if OI rolls over before price breaks (bears exit first) or if price keeps making highs on still-rising OI (genuine new-money trend).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - flow/participation feature; the cascade leg is a short-side timing input and a risk flag for existing longs.
findings.quote: If there is unusually high open interest coinciding with new price highs it could presage trouble... a chain reaction of triggered sell stop loss orders can cause a cascade of prices.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 15 'Candlesticks with Volume and Open Interest' (pp. 248-251, cotton and sugar exhibits)
findings.notes: Open interest is published in real time for crypto perps; the stop-cascade mechanism maps directly to liquidation cascades (the perp-native version of this). The 'trapped longs in pain become rally supply' element is an overhead-supply/positioning feature, analogous to the existing flow vocabulary. Doji clusters at the OI plateau top (sugar, bonds) provide the candlestick confirmation leg.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Value area and initiating-vs-responsive order flow (Market Profile)
findings.mechanism: price probes advertise for the opposite side; initiating flow outside the prior value area predicts where value moves, and shrinking value areas show declining trade facilitation
findings.setup_summary: Volume-by-time (TPO) profile defines the value area (~70% of session volume). Initiating selling - range extensions and extremes under the prior day's value area on expanding volume - should be bearish; buying below prior value is 'responsive' (expects return to value), selling below it is 'initiating' (expects value to move down). Shrinking value areas during an advance indicate the market is failing to accept higher prices as value, a top warning.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: initiating selling (extreme + range extension) under the prior value area on expanding volume. Invalidated if price is quickly rejected back into value (the initiating group is wrong; responsiveness wins).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - market-structure feature; profile-derived levels (value area bounds, extremes) can serve as stop/target references.
findings.quote: Thus, if there is initiating selling activity (extremes and/or range extension), under the previous day's value area on expanding volume, it should have bearish implications.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 17 'Candlesticks with Market Profile' (pp. 259-265)
findings.notes: Crypto perps have no designated daily open, so value-area analysis requires defining a session boundary (e.g., 00:00 UTC); the 'initial balance' concept maps to an opening-range concept. TPO-style volume-by-time is computable from trade data. The initiating-vs-responsive classification is a falsifiable auction-theory flow feature that corroborates the flow vocabulary.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Candlestick reversal signals as volatility-regime timing
findings.mechanism: a candlestick 'truce' reversal in a strong trend at high volatility marks the shift from trend to lateral, hence volatility contraction; a reversal at low volatility in a range forecasts a new trend with volatility expansion
findings.setup_summary: In a strong trend that has pushed volatility unusually high, a candlestick reversal indicating a bull/bear truce (harami, counterattack lines, doji after a long white body) flags the end of the trend and an expected volatility contraction. Conversely, a candlestick reversal at low volatility in a lateral band flags a new trend and rising volatility. The author notes the shifts are shorter-term, and that signals work better against historic than implied volatility.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: reversal pattern at a high-vol trend extreme (or low-vol range). Invalidated if the trend resumes and volatility keeps expanding.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - regime/feature signal; could inform a volatility regime filter in V8 or the simulator's vol modeling.
findings.quote: If a strong trending market has pushed volatility levels to unusually high levels, the emergence of a candlestick reversal indicator may provide an attractive time to sell volatility or to offset a long volatility trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 18 'Candlesticks with Options' (pp. 267-274, silver and sugar exhibits)
findings.notes: The contraction-after-truce claim is a falsifiable volatility feature: expected-vol decline conditioned on a reversal pattern at a high-vol trend extreme. Implied vol requires an options chain (Deribit) which V8's perp data does not include; realized/historic vol is directly computable, and the author explicitly says candlesticks work better with historic vol.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

findings.strategy_name: Window (gap) continuation - 'the market goes to the window'
findings.mechanism: an unfilled window in the direction of the trend acts as a magnet: price pulls back to it, the window holds as support/resistance, and the trend resumes
findings.setup_summary: A window (gap) opens in the direction of the trend; price is expected to pull back to the window, which acts as support (up-gap) or resistance (down-gap), then the trend resumes. In the author's trades the window is used as a continuation leg and as a stop reference (crude: short with stop slightly above the June 15-18 window at $17.65, target retest of the hammer lows; coffee: failure to clear the window's resistance area triggered the short).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pullback into an open window in the trend direction. Invalidated if the window is filled (closed) and price continues through it - the support/resistance premise is dead.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on rejection at the window edge; stop beyond the window's far edge (author: stop slightly above the window high); target = retest of the prior extreme (hammer lows).
findings.quote: When the market rallies and opens a window, there should be a pullback to that window. The window should be support... The Japanese expression is that 'the market goes to the window.'
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary A 'Window' (pp. 300-301); Ch. 20 crude-oil and coffee examples (pp. 284-285)
findings.notes: BTCUSDT perps trade ~24/7 with no overnight/weekend gaps, so the gap mechanism is structurally N/A; the simulator's existing gap semantics do not apply to the perp tape. The residual 'pullback to a broken zone' behavior is already captured by the supply_demand_zone finding. Recorded as a rejection so no future V8 family resurrects gap-based triggers on a gap-less market.
findings.book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques - A Contemporary Guide to the Ancient Investment Techniques of the Far East 1991

book_title: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques (Nison, 1991) — Part 2 (Ch. 14-20, Conclusion, Glossaries)

findings.strategy_name: Correlated simultaneous setup risk reduction
findings.mechanism: simultaneous same-direction setups on highly correlated instruments share one underlying risk factor, so capping aggregate correlated exposure prevents a correlated drawdown that would breach the weekly cap
findings.setup_summary: When several correlated instruments (pairwise correlation >= 0.65) print same-direction setup signals in the same bar window, halve per-trade risk (e.g., 1% -> 0.5%) so the aggregate correlated cluster stays under the weekly drawdown cap even if all signals fail together. Example given: six yen pairs all printing daily kangaroo tails -> 6 x 0.5% = 3% at risk, leaving 2% of weekly budget.
findings.trigger_invalidation: correlation measured on a recent window; if pairwise correlation drops below the 0.65 threshold, full per-trade risk is restored
findings.risk_geometry: per-trade risk halved to 0.5% for a correlated cluster; weekly drawdown cap 5%; aggregate cluster risk <= remaining weekly budget
findings.quote: For simultaneous trades with a correlation of 0.65 and above, the risk is reduced to 0.5 percent per trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 13, Risk Rules: Correlated Trades (pp. 217-218)
findings.notes: Directly extends V8's ONE-exposure-per-(instrument,direction) rule to a correlated-cluster heat cap in RiskGate. BTC/ETH/major-alt perp returns are highly correlated and a liquidation cascade hits all BTCUSD-margined positions at once. Caveat: correlation is non-stationary and must be windowed; threshold (0.65) and halving factor are practitioner defaults, not measured.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Period maximum drawdown cap with first-day sizing constraint
findings.mechanism: a hard drawdown cap on a fixed period bounds the ruin path, and per-trade sizing is derived so a single day's worst case cannot consume the whole period's budget
findings.setup_summary: Fix a period cap (example: 5% per trading week, or per day/month depending on timeframe). Derive per-trade risk so that the worst case of all same-day signals cannot exhaust the cap on day one: with 6 signals on the first day, risk 0.65%/trade (total 3.9%), not 1%. Stop trading for the period once the cap is hit.
findings.trigger_invalidation: cap resets at the period boundary; a cap breach halts new entries until the next period
findings.risk_geometry: per-trade risk <= cap / max-same-day-signal-count; example cap 5% weekly; stop-trading trigger at cap breach
findings.quote: If you have a 5 percent drawdown rule per trading week, and you have six trading signals in one day, perhaps instead of risking 1 percent per trade you risk 0.65 percent per trade for an overall risk of 3.9 percent.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 13, Risk Rules: Maximum Drawdown (pp. 215-216)
findings.notes: This is V8's heat cap + drawdown circuit breaker. The numeric example is directly lab-falsifiable. For 24/7 crypto the 'day' boundary must be defined deterministically (UTC), since there are no exchange sessions.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Worst-case planning with fixed fractional risk
findings.mechanism: constant percentage risk per trade normalizes equity volatility across trades and builds position-size discipline (trading tolerance)
findings.setup_summary: Size every position so the dollar loss if the stop is hit equals the same fixed percentage of account (1-2%). Compute worst case = dollar loss at the stop, add 20% buffer, and assume that amount of risk for every trade. This keeps the emotional amplitude of any single trade constant so execution quality stays stable.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a (sizing rule, not an entry trigger)
findings.risk_geometry: position size = (risk% x equity) / (stop distance + ~20% buffer)
findings.quote: First, calculate your worst-case scenario. This should be the dollar loss if your stop loss is hit. Second, add 20 percent to this amount... assume this (percentage) risk for all of your trades.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 16, Worst-Case Planning / Trading Tolerance (pp. 254-255)
findings.notes: With 5-50x leverage available on perps, fixed-% risk sizing is the only sane default; ties position size to stop distance (V8's stop_distance_atr analog). The +20% buffer covers slippage/funding on high-volatility perps. The 'trading tolerance' psychological claim is not falsifiable; the sizing formula is.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Three-bar exit (time-stop runner exit)
findings.mechanism: if price has not delivered in the expected direction within N bars, the edge is not materializing and time value is being lost; exit at the close
findings.setup_summary: For runner-style trades where stop loss and profit target are one and the same, if the trade has not moved in the expected direction within three bars of entry, exit at the close of the third bar. Consistently applied (Molly's mechanical big-shadow system), accepting small winners and occasional large winners.
findings.trigger_invalidation: trade closed at target, at stop, or at the close of the third bar whichever comes first
findings.risk_geometry: exit at close of bar 3 on non-delivery; stop = entry risk; target = swing point/nearest zone
findings.quote: If you are a runner, your stop loss and your profit target may be one and the same (for example, if you are using the three-bar exit).
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 13, Managing Stops and Profits (pp. 219-220); references Ch 11 exits
findings.notes: Full definition lives in Ch 11 (Part 1); Part 2 confirms usage as a runner exit where stop and target coincide. Bar-count time stops are directly implementable in V8 (existing expiry_bars; current experts use 8 bars, this suggests a tighter variant as a lifecycle variant).
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Cancel pending entry if the stop level is traded before the trigger
findings.mechanism: if price trades to the would-be stop level before the pending entry trigger fires, the setup's location premise is invalidated pre-entry
findings.setup_summary: For a pending stop-entry (e.g., buy stop placed above a bullish kangaroo tail's high with a stop below the pattern), if the market first trades down through where the stop loss would sit, cancel the pending buy stop. The setup is dead before it triggers.
findings.trigger_invalidation: pending order cancelled if stop level is traded before entry trigger fires; entry otherwise triggers as planned
findings.risk_geometry: entry: buy/sell stop above/below pattern extreme; stop: beyond pattern low/high; trigger: opposite extreme
findings.quote: If the market pushes through where the stop loss would be, it may make sense to cancel the trade. This is using market information to manage your trades, even before they occur.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 13, Using Market Information (pp. 220-221, Fig 13.1)
findings.notes: Falsifiable: conditional P(profit | entry triggered after stop level breached) should be worse than unconditional. Perps have no gaps so stop levels can be touched intra-bar; this adds a real pre-entry invalidation path to V8 breakout/sweep experts, distinct from post-entry dead-thesis (still_valid).
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Exit on opposite-direction signal (reversal-signal exit policy)
findings.mechanism: an opposite-direction setup printing in the trade's location invalidates the directional thesis and should close the trade before target or stop
findings.setup_summary: Pre-commit to an exit policy before entry: either close on any opposite-direction signal, or close only when a counter-signal prints at a zone. Example: daily NZD/USD bearish kangaroo tail short; market falls to the next zone at 0.7430 where a bullish 'almost kangaroo tail' candle prints; the naked trader closes the short there.
findings.trigger_invalidation: exit when opposite-direction signal prints (policy-dependent: any counter-signal or counter-signal-at-zone); target/stop otherwise in force
findings.risk_geometry: manual exit on counter-signal; stop and target still active
findings.quote: Some naked traders will only close a trade if the market prints a reversal signal on a zone. Other naked traders will simply close a trade as soon as price action offers a counter signal, a signal in the opposite direction of the trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 13, Using Market Information (pp. 220-222, Fig 13.2)
findings.notes: This is exactly V8's dead-thesis (still_valid) exit semantics: a counter-direction expert firing at a location should terminate the opposing exposure. Candidate refinement for failed_breakout and liquidity_sweep_reclaim still_valid logic, or a cross-expert lifecycle rule (one active exposure per direction already enforces this at admission; here it is the exit trigger).
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Rolling win-rate decay check (system potency monitoring)
findings.mechanism: if recent-window win rate diverges from the historical win rate, the edge may be decaying; this separates a bad-luck streak from a dead system
findings.setup_summary: Track the system's historical win rate. When a losing streak or concern arises, compute the win rate of the last 50 trades and compare it to the historical win rate; if they differ greatly, the system may be losing potency and must be re-validated on recent market data (e.g., last 3 months) before being trusted again. If the rates agree, the streak is variance.
findings.trigger_invalidation: recent-50 win rate close to historical -> treat streak as variance, keep rules unchanged
findings.risk_geometry: n/a (monitoring rule); re-test on a recent window before re-trusting
findings.quote: compare your historical win rate to the win rate of the past 50 trades. If the historical win rate differs greatly from the current win rate, the trading system may be losing its potency.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 15, The Bad Market Theory (pp. 246-247)
findings.notes: 'Differs greatly' is undefined - to be falsifiable it needs a statistical test (e.g., binomial CI on the 50-trade window vs historical p). Aligns with V8 frozen-OOS and registry discipline: this is the natural rule for moving an expert toward QUARANTINED/REJECTED. Also the chapter argues naked setups are psychology-based and persist because retail is ~1% of volume.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Candlestick pattern validity by close position within bar range
findings.mechanism: the close's position within the bar's range determines whether a candlestick pattern is valid; the open and early-bar path matter less
findings.setup_summary: A candlestick setup is valid only if the close lands in a specific position: bearish big shadow closes near the low, bullish big shadow closes near the high. Molly's mechanical version: shadow larger than the prior five candlesticks by at least 15% and close within ~15 pips of the extreme; trigger on the next bar; target the nearest zone; three-bar exit.
findings.trigger_invalidation: close outside the required position -> pattern invalid, no signal
findings.risk_geometry: entry: next-bar close; stop: beyond pattern extreme; target: nearest zone; exit: three-bar rule
findings.quote: If the closing price for a bearish big belt is not near the low, but rather near the middle of the candlestick, is it a valid sell signal? The closing price is absolutely critical to the naked trader.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 14, A Simple Trick (pp. 236-238); Ch 13 subjectivity example (Molly, pp. 224-225)
findings.notes: Close-position-in-range is computable per bar and consistent with V8's NEXT_BAR_CLOSE trigger semantics; pip-based filters need translation to ATR/volatility units for 1h BTCUSDT. The candlestick-snapshot exercise itself is expertise-building, not a strategy; the load-bearing falsifiable content is the close-position validity rule plus Molly's mechanical filters.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Transaction-cost ratio scales inversely with target size
findings.mechanism: spread/slippage is roughly fixed per trade while target size shrinks on lower timeframes, so short-horizon small-target trades carry disproportionately high transaction cost
findings.setup_summary: Before choosing a timeframe, compute total round-trip cost / expected target. Worked example: 2-pip spread on a 10-pip scalp = 16% commission, versus 1.9% on a 100-pip daily target; a 3-pip slippage on a 10-pip target is a 30% profit cut that can tip a system into unprofitability.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a (methodology constraint)
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
