findings.quote: The spread on the EUR/USD is likely to be quite tight, perhaps two pips, so you must make 12 pips to bag 10 pips of profit. This is a commission of 16 percent... Longer-term trading is not only cheaper, it is easier to execute successfully.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 13, Choosing Your Playing Field (pp. 225-226)
findings.notes: Direct input to the V8 Binance USDM cost model and lab reporting: a per-trade cost/target ratio metric should gate which (target_r, expiry_bars) variants are viable on 1h BTCUSDT. Taker fees + funding + slippage are a fixed per-trade drag that eats small-target, short-expiry strategies.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Pre-planned drawdown retreat sequence (avoid revenge trading / cycle of doom)
findings.mechanism: a drawdown triggers a pre-committed recovery routine instead of rule changes; mid-drawdown system redesign destroys edge and amplifies risk
findings.setup_summary: After hitting the maximum drawdown, execute a fixed 5-step sequence: (1) step away from the trading station, (2) back-test a predetermined sample (e.g., 200 trades or a fixed date range), (3) evaluate the trading statement to separate bad luck from rule violations, (4) decide if the system still works by re-testing on recent data (e.g., last 3 months), (5) rebuild confidence slowly, demo trading if needed. Never redesign the system inside the drawdown.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: Without a strong structure, without rules designed to keep you from emotional revenge trading after a drawdown, you're almost certain to fall into undisciplined trading and to take on excessive risk.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 13, Maximum Drawdown (pp. 216-217)
findings.notes: Corroborates V8 rule 15 (offline, registry-gated learning; no in-place mutation of active experts) and the registry's quarantine path. Revenge-trading risk is amplified by 24/7 market availability; the protocol is a discipline/process constraint, not a falsifiable strategy.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: One-edge focus: boring trading is expert trading
findings.mechanism: concentrating on one edge reduces decision variance and system-switching waste; repeated system-switching is the primary cause of retail failure (cycle of doom)
findings.setup_summary: Become expert at one setup and trade it repeatedly until boring; add a second system only after ~8 months of the first, and only a complementary (low-correlated) one so profits in one system tend to offset drawdowns in the other. Back-test -> forward-test demo -> small live account -> full account progression, risking 2% or less throughout.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: The real secret of expert traders: They focus on one market, one trading system, one edge, and they use this edge in their trading repeatedly. Profitable trading is boring.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 14, The Secret of the Experts / Boring Trading Is Expert Trading (pp. 230-231, 235-236)
findings.notes: Decision-relevant: supports V8 rule 14 complexity budget (max 3 ACTIVE experts, no router/shared scorer) and discourages expert proliferation. The diversification-via-complementary-system rationale also supports gating new families behind a registry experiment that beats the simpler baseline on frozen OOS.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: No-trade patience and market-mood regime selection
findings.mechanism: profitability comes partly from not trading; forcing trades when price action is not aligned with the current market mood (trending vs drifting/choppy vs transition) degrades edge
findings.setup_summary: Naked trading spends most of its time waiting for price to reach strong zones; each catalyst (kangaroo tail, last kiss, big shadow, trendy kangaroo) is suited to a particular market mood. Falsifiable test offered: back-test one year of a high-frequency setup on a short timeframe and a low-frequency setup on a long timeframe and compare profitability; when neither setup is present, the correct action is no trade.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: Sometimes making money is easier when you do not trade. Sometimes avoiding trades is just as important as taking trade opportunities when they arise.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 14, Step One: Get in the Comfort Zone (pp. 231-232)
findings.notes: Market moods are defined in Ch 9 (Part 1); Part 2 asserts the mood-catalyst fit and gives the back-test comparison as the test. 24/7 crypto spends much of its time drifting or ranging, so a regime/no-trade admission gate over the expert pipeline is implementable; the hard falsifiable part is a deterministic mood classification from trend/volatility features.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

book_title: Naked Forex: High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators (Nekritin & Peters, 2012) — Part 2 of 2

findings.strategy_name: Last Kiss breakout-retouch confirmation
findings.mechanism: True breakouts retouch the broken zone and hold; fake-outs snap back inside the box, so entry is deferred until a retouch plus a continuation candle in the breakout direction.
findings.setup_summary: Identify a consolidation box (support + resistance zones, at least two touches on each side). Wait for price to break beyond one zone, then wait for the market to return and retouch the box edge; enter via a buy/sell stop beyond the high/low of the first strong candle in the breakout direction printed at the retouch. Emergency stop at the midpoint of the box (support + box width/2); if a candle closes back inside the box the thesis is dead and the trade is exited. Target = nearest zone.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: breakout beyond one zone, retouch of the box edge, strong directional candle at the retouch. Invalidation: any close back inside the box exits (usually a smaller loss than the emergency stop); emergency stop at box midpoint.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: stop order beyond the retouch candle extreme (buy stop above high for up-breaks, sell stop below low for down-breaks). Emergency stop = midpoint of consolidation box. Dead-thesis exit: close back inside the box. Target: nearest zone. No fixed expiry stated.
findings.quote: the last-kiss trade is based on the retouch principle. The market will often come back to a significant zone once the market has expanded beyond the zone
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 'The Last Kiss' — retouch principle pp.82-93 (rules p.92-93)
findings.notes: Directly refines V8's DATA_BLOCKED backlog family breakout_retest with the retouch-confirmation filter and the 'close back inside box' dead-thesis exit (maps to still_valid). In 24/7 crypto perps the consolidation-box construct is clean because there are no exchange gaps to skip over the box edges.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Big Shadow zone-reversal engulfing
findings.mechanism: A zone-printed engulfing candle whose range dwarfs the prior candles signals exhaustion: the market over-extended into a price-memory level and was rejected.
findings.setup_summary: On a support/resistance zone, two candles form a big shadow: the second candle has a higher high and lower low than the first, a wider range than the prior 5-10 candles, and closes near its extreme (bullish close near high, bearish close near low). Best set-ups have 'room to the left' — the market has not printed on the zone for at least 7 candles. Enter via a stop beyond the big-shadow candle; stop a few pips beyond the opposite extreme; target the nearest zone.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: engulfing two-candle formation on a zone with close near the extreme and range > prior candles. Invalidation: stop a few pips beyond the big-shadow candle extreme; set-ups whose close sits near the candle midpoint, or that print where recent price action exists at the zone, are skipped.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: buy stop a few pips above the big-shadow high (bullish) / sell stop below the low (bearish). Stop: a few pips beyond the opposite extreme of the big-shadow candle. Target: nearest zone (with cushion). Expiry: none stated; 'room to the left' >= 7 bars is the quality gate.
findings.quote: Big shadows must print on the zones. Big shadows print at extreme highs or extreme lows... The very best big-shadow candlesticks have room to the left.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'The Big Shadow' pp.95-110 (rules p.109, optimizers p.110)
findings.notes: Distinct from V8's formalized failed_breakout (SHORT reentry below a failed high) — this is a two-candle zone-rejection reversal. The falsifiable differentiators are the close-near-extreme condition and the >=7-bar room-to-the-left filter (an exhaustion gate).
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Kangaroo Tail zone sweep-reclaim
findings.mechanism: A long wick through a zone that closes back on the zone's other side shows the level was probed and rejected, sweeping resting stops and leaving reversal fuel.
findings.setup_summary: Single candle on a zone with open and close in the extreme third of the candle (top third bullish, bottom third bearish), a long tail relative to the body, open and close inside the previous candle's range (market not in a runaway phase), and ideally a range greater than the previous 10 candles. Most such candles penetrate the zone intra-bar, then close back on the other side. Enter via a stop beyond the tail end; emergency stop a few pips beyond the tail; target the next zone.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: extreme-third open+close, long tail, open/close inside prior candle range, printed on a zone. Invalidation: stop a few pips beyond the tail; the book also recommends closing early if the drawdown reaches 75% of the way to the stop. Red flags: short tails, no zone, giant candles immediately prior, or open/close outside the prior candle's range.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: buy stop a few pips above the high (bullish) / sell stop below the low (bearish). Stop: a few pips beyond the tail (maximum loss). Optional early exit at 75% of the distance to the stop. Target: next zone.
findings.quote: Most kangaroo tails will push through the zone and then come back and close on the other side of the zone.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.8 'Kangaroo Tails' pp.131-150 (tips and red flags pp.149-150)
findings.notes: Nearly identical to V8's formalized liquidity_sweep_reclaim (wick through windowed prior extreme reclaimed by close, frozen ref, stay-on-reclaimed-side still_valid). The book's tail-vs-body length, extreme-third open/close, and prior-range filters are concrete candidate variant refinements; 'room to the left' supports the windowed-extreme reference.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Wammie/Moolah double-touch zone reversal
findings.mechanism: Two touches on a zone with a higher low (or lower high) and enough separation show momentum dying out; the second touch failing to extend the zone test flips the balance toward reversal.
findings.setup_summary: Double bottom (wammie) on a support zone where the second touch is HIGHER than the first, with at least 6 candles between touches; enter on the first strong bullish candle at the second touch via a buy stop above its high; stop below the first (lower) touch; target the next zone. Moolah is the mirror: double top with a lower second touch, sell stop below the bearish candle at the second touch, stop above the first touch, target the next zone below.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: two distinct zone touches with a higher low (wammie) / lower high (moolah), >= 6 bars between touches, strong candle on the second touch. Invalidation: stop beyond the first touch; fewer than 6 bars between touches implies the market is coiling for a breakout THROUGH the zone (do not trade).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: buy stop above the strong bullish candle at the second touch (wammie) / sell stop below the bearish candle (moolah). Stop: a few pips beyond the first touch — deliberately placed so a third touch of the zone does not stop the trade. Target: next zone. No expiry stated.
findings.quote: a wammie formation is identified by a second touch that is higher than the first touch on the zone... A wammie trade is only valid if there are at least six candlesticks between the first and second touches.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.7 'Wammies and Moolahs' pp.111-129 (characteristics pp.125-128, tips p.128-129)
findings.notes: The six-bar separation rule is the distinctive falsifiable filter; rapid repeated touches signal imminent breakout rather than reversal. In leverage-driven crypto, zones break more often than in spot FX, so the higher-low/lower-high discriminator and the stop-behind-first-touch geometry are the load-bearing parts.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Trendy Kangaroo pause-breakout continuation
findings.mechanism: In a strong trend, a tight 3-10 candle pause builds a minor zone; a kangaroo-style candle that sticks beyond the pause in the trend direction shows the pause is a rest stop, not a reversal.
findings.setup_summary: During a strong uptrend (or downtrend) the market pauses with 3-10 candles in a tight consolidation; then a kangaroo-style candle prints with open/close in the extreme third and a tail that sticks out beyond the consolidation range in the trend direction. Enter via a stop beyond the candle's extreme in the trend direction; stop on the other side of the candle; target the next zone. Not ideal if printed right after a large correction (may signal trend end).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: established trend + small pause + kangaroo candle sticking beyond the pause range. Invalidation: stop on the other side of the candle; set-ups after a large correction may signal trend exhaustion; a candle that does not stick beyond the pause range is not valid.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: buy stop above the high (bullish) / sell stop below the low (bearish) of the trendy kangaroo. Stop: a few pips beyond the opposite extreme. Target: next zone. No expiry stated.
findings.quote: The market pauses and several candlesticks print in a small consolidation range... A trendy kangaroo prints below the consolidation range.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.10 'The Trendy Kangaroo' pp.163-175 (characteristics pp.173-175)
findings.notes: Behavior-family sibling of V8's trend_pullback under the same trend_continuation mechanism, but a different behavior: entry is a stop-order breakout beyond the pause range, not a pullback re-entry into the trend. Regime-gated to trending tape — the book is explicit it fails in directionless markets.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Big Belt week-open key-reversal candle
findings.mechanism: Weekend-reopening excitement overshoots the fair price; the reversal candle prints on a zone with the open beyond the prior close and the close at the opposite extreme, marking an exhaustion high/low.
findings.setup_summary: On a zone, a candle opens beyond the previous candle's close and closes at the opposite extreme: bearish belt opens near the high and closes near the low; bullish belt opens near the low and closes near the high. In forex these nearly always surface on the first trading day of the week. Enter via a sell stop below the low (bearish) / buy stop above the high (bullish); stop on the other side; target the next zone. Book claims an 'exceptionally high win rate' on daily charts and recommends the daily timeframe.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: zone + open-beyond-prior-close candle with the close at the opposite extreme; room to the left preferred. Invalidation: stop beyond the opposite extreme; trade never triggers if the market does not trade beyond the belt's entry level.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: sell stop below the low (bearish belt) / buy stop above the high (bullish belt). Stop: a few pips beyond the opposite extreme. Target: nearest zone. Timeframe gate: daily recommended.
findings.quote: bearish big belts nearly always surface on the first trading day of the week. The market opens much higher than the closing price of the previous week and then steadily trades lower
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.9 'The Big Belt' pp.151-161 (characteristics pp.160-161)
findings.notes: The week-open gap premise does not exist in 24/7 crypto perps (no weekly close). The candle-shape reversal at a zone could feed the candlestick family, but the catalyst trigger (first day of the week after a weekend pause) is forex-specific and the 'high win rate' claim is untested narrative.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Three-Bar trailing exit
findings.mechanism: Trailing the stop behind the extreme of the last three closed bars locks in trend profit while giving the market a bounded cushion.
findings.setup_summary: For a long, once three bars have closed the stop trails below the lowest low of the three most recent closed bars; for a short, above the highest high of the three most recent bars. The stop is adjusted only when a bar closes and never moves against the position. Works best when the market accelerates into a strong trend; in non-trending tape it exits for minimal profit (the book shows a 13-pip win).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Applies from 3 bars after entry; stop adjusted at bar close only; exit when the trailing stop is hit.
findings.risk_geometry: Trailing stop = lowest low / highest high of the last 3 closed bars plus a few pips. Candle must close before the stop moves. No target or expiry (pure trailing).
findings.quote: the exit is based on the price action of the most recent three bars... the lowest low of the previous three candlesticks (for buy trades), or the highest high of the previous three candlesticks (for sell trades)
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.11 'Exiting the Trade', Three-Bar Exit pp.188-199
findings.notes: Deterministic and clock-free, uses only closed bars — directly expressible as a V8 lifecycle/risk rule and complementary to the fixed R-multiple geometry. Matches crypto's sustained trending periods; gives back profit in chop, which is the mechanism to test.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Zone, split and ladder exits
findings.mechanism: Zones act as price magnets as well as barriers, so zone levels are natural profit targets and trail anchors.
findings.setup_summary: Zone exit: target the nearest zone, placing the take-profit a few pips short of the zone as a cushion. Split exit: half the position targets the first zone and half targets the next zone; after the first target is hit the stop moves to breakeven. Ladder exit: as each successive zone is reached, trail the stop to the previous zone, giving a one-zone cushion and letting the market breathe in trends.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Targets and trails are mechanical; a trade ends when a zone target or the trailed stop is hit.
findings.risk_geometry: Targets = zone levels with a few-pip cushion. Split exit moves the stop to breakeven after the first target. Ladder trail moves the stop zone-by-zone. All zone-based — requires a live, point-in-time zone map at every bar.
findings.quote: Zones are also magnets: The market tends to be attracted to these places on the chart. In other words, zones are simultaneously price barriers and price magnets.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.11 'Exiting the Trade', Zone/Split/Ladder exits pp.180-188
findings.notes: Depends on the zone-map feature (see zone-ontology finding). In crypto, liquidation cascades can overshoot zone targets, so the cushion, the split-exit breakeven step, and the ladder give-back are the specific mechanisms to falsify.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Support/Resistance zone ontology and price memory
findings.mechanism: Price reverses repeatedly at the same levels because markets have memory; a zone's importance grows with its touch count and age, and it survives across years.
findings.setup_summary: Define a zone as the AREA where price has reversed repeatedly (not a line). Find zones on a higher-timeframe line chart — bends in the line mark zones. Zone strength scales with the number of touches; ignore minor zones (those visible one timeframe lower). Zones recycle across years. A zone is not broken until price CLOSES beyond it: intra-bar penetration ('touches deep into the beer belly') does not count as a break.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a — feature-definition methodology; supplies the location feature, the close-beyond-zone break rule used by every zone-based setup, and the room-to-the-left rule for windowed extremes.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a (location feature ontology). Zone levels drive targets, stops, and confirmation across all zone-based setups.
findings.quote: If the market trades beyond the zone it does not mean that the market has broken the zone... most of the time if the market touches a zone, it may trade beyond the zone, but it will not close beyond the zone.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.4 'Identifying Support and Resistance Zones' pp.39-70
findings.notes: Directly informs V8's location feature group: zone-as-area, touch-count weighting, higher-timeframe zone discovery, the close-based break rule for frozen refs, and 'room to the left' for windowed extremes. The close-beyond rule is point-in-time safe.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Stop-gated entries filter failed set-ups
findings.mechanism: Failed reversal set-ups retrace but almost never take out the set-up's own extreme; gating the entry on a stop beyond that extreme filters out most losers.
findings.setup_summary: Across every naked catalyst (big shadow, kangaroo tail, big belt, last kiss, wammie/moolah), enter only with a buy/sell stop beyond the set-up candle's extreme rather than on a retracement or at market. If the market never reaches the stop level, the trade never triggers — the majority of failed-set-up losers are never entered. This is also the book's rationale for earlier entries and tighter stops than indicator-lagged signals.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Entry is never taken on retracement into the set-up; if the entry stop is not touched, the trade is skipped (a no-trade, not a loss).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry type = stop order beyond the set-up extreme (not market/limit). This is a risk_geometry entry-type lesson; it must be modeled against V8's STOP_FIRST and fill-at-close simulator semantics.
findings.quote: if you decide to use buy stops and sell stops to enter your trades, you will eliminate many losing trades from your record
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'The Big Shadow' pp.99-100; Ch.8 pp.146-148; Ch.9 p.152
findings.notes: Transfers well to crypto, where wicks and stop-runs are frequent: a failed set-up's extreme is rarely taken out, so stop-gated entry is a cheap loss filter. The book repeats this argument in four chapters, making it a load-bearing methodology principle.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Setup-to-regime matching (choppy vs trending)
findings.mechanism: Markets alternate between choppy/drifting and trending states; each naked system exploits one state and underperforms in the other.
findings.setup_summary: Classify the tape as drifting/choppy or trending and apply trend-following set-ups (trendy kangaroo) only in trending tape, and transition set-ups (last kiss) only at the choppy-to-trending transition. The book's operational trend test is a line chart assessed 'mostly up, mostly down, or mostly up and down' — falsifiable as a lookback slope or range-relative drift measure.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a — a regime gate overlaid on set-up eligibility; the supporting claim is documented underperformance of trend systems in directionless markets.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a (regime filter on set-up eligibility, not on risk geometry).
findings.quote: Most trading systems will perform exceptionally well during either the choppy market or a strong trending market, but never in both types of market moods.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 'The Last Kiss' pp.73-75; Ch.10 'The Trendy Kangaroo' pp.163-175
findings.notes: Supports a regime filter / expert-eligibility gate in V8: keep trend-continuation experts gated to trending tape. Relevant to crypto's pronounced alternation between range and trend regimes; the 'mostly up/down' measure is a candidate deterministic regime feature.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Back-testing integrity: no future data, few variables
findings.mechanism: Hindsight bias, postdictive error, and parameter overfitting make backtests look profitable while the same system fails live.
findings.setup_summary: Whether manual or automated, testing must trade only from the right-hand edge of the chart: never advance the chart and then return to take a trade; automated tests can silently leak future data (postdictive error); adding too many rules/indicators over-fits the historical data and breaks on new data. Simple systems are robust across markets and timeframes.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a — methodology for the V8 lab: point-in-time MarketState, no wall clock, frozen refs, registry-gated variants.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a (testing methodology).
findings.quote: Seasoned traders understand how simple trading systems are robust... Using too many variables often implies that there are too many indicators in the trading system.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Back-Testing Your System' pp.25-38 (hindsight bias p.32, postdictive error p.36)
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's determinism rules (no NOW(), point-in-time state, append-only logs, sha1_hex) and the complexity budget (max 3 active experts). 'Trade from the right-hand edge' is the book's phrasing of point-in-time discipline.
findings.book: Naked Forex - High-Probability Techniques for Trading Without Indicators 2012

findings.strategy_name: Trendline / Moving-Average Pullback Bounce
findings.mechanism: A valid trend slope persists; a pullback that touches and bounces off the rising trendline (or MA support) is a continuation entry because buyers step in at proven support, and the more times the line is tested the more significant it is.
findings.setup_summary: In a defined uptrend (rising peaks and troughs, price above an up trendline drawn under at least two rising reaction lows, preferably touched 3 times), buy when price pulls back to the trendline and closes back above it. Mirror in downtrends: short bounces to a falling down trendline. Same logic applies to moving-average support (e.g., close below 50-day warns of drop toward the 200-day). Falsifiable on 1h BTCUSDT by defining trendline support as a frozen line through prior reaction lows and entry on a confirming bar close.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A decisive close below the up trendline (or below MA support) invalidates the bounce; in downtrends a decisive close above the falling trendline invalidates the short. Failure of price to hold a previously-tested trendline is itself an early reversal warning.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at bar close after the trendline touch; stop below the trendline or below the recent reaction low; target = prior high (resistance); no R-multiple or expiry stated (book trades from daily/weekly bar closes).
findings.quote: Retests of up trendlines often present excellent buying opportunities.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.2 'Trendlines' (p.31) and Ch.4 moving-average-as-support (pp.78-82)
findings.notes: Directly refines the existing trend_pullback expert (ema_fast>ema_slow and close<ema_slow). Book adds the trendline-touch mechanism and the 'more touches = more significant' validation rule as variants. Crypto perp 24/7 continuous data has no exchange gaps, so trendline/MA support is unbroken and computable.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Percentage / Fibonacci Retracement Entry (1/3, 1/2, 2/3)
findings.mechanism: Corrections in a trend retrace predictable fractions of the prior move (min 1/3, typically 1/2, at most 2/3); support at these levels in an uptrend attracts resumption buying, while a move beyond two-thirds implies the correction is actually a full trend reversal.
findings.setup_summary: Measure a completed swing (e.g., 20 to 40). In an uptrend, buy the pullback when price reaches the 50% retracement level (or the 38%-62% zone, commonly 38/50/62) of the prior advance and resumes higher; in a downtrend, sell bounces into the one-third-to-half retracement area. Levels act as support in uptrends and resistance in downtrends; a retracement beyond two-thirds switches the thesis to full reversal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A move beyond the two-thirds (66%) retracement level invalidates the continuation thesis and indicates a total trend reversal.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the retracement level on a bar close; stop below the two-thirds level (or below the swing low); target = the prior extreme; no expiry stated. The book notes Fibonacci levels (38/62) derive from the Fibonacci number series.
findings.quote: A stock that's traveled from 20 to 40 will often retrace about 10 points (50 percent) before resuming its advance.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.2 'Retracing Our Steps by One-Third, One-Half, and Two-Thirds' (pp.34-37)
findings.notes: Distinct mechanism from trendline pullback: structural percentage levels rather than a slope line. Fully computable on continuous crypto perp data; the two-thirds-overrun rule gives a clean dead-thesis condition. Corroborated widely in this library's TA canon.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Weekly Key-Reversal Bar
findings.mechanism: A wide-range bar that opens with trend-extension (breaks a support level) and closes back through the prior week's range shows absorption of the losing side's flow (exhaustion), with width of the bar and heaviness of volume scaling significance.
findings.setup_summary: On a weekly chart during a decline: the stock starts the week with heavy selling and breaks below a support level, then closes by week's end above the previous week's price range — an upside weekly reversal (LONG setup). Mirror: prices open the week sharply higher and collapse at week's end — a downside reversal (defensive/short). Wider weekly bar and heavier trading volume increase significance; more meaningful when occurring near historic support/resistance. Daily version = key reversal day but carries less weight.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Book states the downside reversal 'isn't usually enough to turn the chart bearish' alone — it warrants defensive action, so treat as a caution signal pending confirmation rather than an immediate short.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the weekly close (bar close); no explicit stop or target given; volume and range act as a strength filter.
findings.quote: A stock starts the week with a lot of selling and usually breaks under some type of support level. By week's end, however, prices have turned dramatically upward and close above the previous week's price range.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.2 'Weekly Reversals' (p.38)
findings.notes: Weekly bars exist on 24/7 crypto (Sunday 00:00 UTC close) and the pattern is objectively definable (week open near lows, week close above prior week high). No gap mechanics on perps so 'breaks support' is a continuous move; volume data available, though wash-trading caveats apply.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Head-and-Shoulders Neckline Break
findings.mechanism: After an extended trend, a final push beyond the prior extreme (head) flanked by two lower highs (shoulders) exhausts the driving side; a decisive close through the neckline (line through the intervening troughs) completes the reversal, with the head-to-neckline distance projecting a minimum move.
findings.setup_summary: In an uptrend, price forms three peaks: two shoulders near the same level flanking a higher head; draw the neckline through the two intervening troughs. A decisive close below the neckline signals a new downtrend (target = neckline-break price minus head-to-neckline vertical distance). Mirror for the inverse head-and-shoulders bottom (three lows, middle lowest; upside neckline break = new uptrend). Volume/OBV should confirm the break.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Pattern incomplete until neckline breaks; measurements are approximate minimums, not precise targets. Upside volume (heavier volume more critical on upside than downside) absent at the break weakens the signal.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at neckline break on bar close; stop above/below the neckline or at the head; target = pattern height projected from break point; no expiry stated. Book cites the NY Fed staff report (Osler & Chang 1995) that the pattern produces statistically and economically significant profits in currencies.
findings.quote: The final conclusion of the report was that the head and shoulders pattern produces statistically and economically significant profits when applied to currency trading.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Head and Shoulders Pattern' and 'Even the Fed Is Charting' (pp.60-65)
findings.notes: Only finding in this part with an explicit statistical citation (NY Fed Osler-Chang). Neckline break is objectively definable at bar close. Subjective identification risk (which swings are shoulders) argues for a tight formal definition if formalized.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Triangle Continuation Breakout
findings.mechanism: Sideways consolidation between converging trendlines within an established trend is a pause; resolution usually occurs in the direction of the prior trend about two-thirds to three-quarters into the pattern, with the vertical height projecting the move.
findings.setup_summary: After a trend, price narrows into a symmetrical triangle (each trendline touched at least twice, often three times); on a decisive break of one side in the direction of the prior trend (with volume pickup, especially on upside breaks), trade continuation. Ascending triangle (flat top, rising bottom) = bullish; descending triangle (flat bottom, falling top) = bearish. Target = triangle's widest height projected from the breakout point; the longer the pattern has formed, the more significant the move.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Breakout that fails / price re-enters the pattern; an upside breakout not accompanied by a noticeable volume increase is immediately suspect.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the bar-close break of the trendline; stop back inside the pattern (beyond the opposite line); target = projected height; pattern duration scales significance.
findings.quote: Usually, about two-thirds to three-quarters of the way into the pattern, prices will break out in the direction of the prior trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'The Triangle' (pp.65-69)
findings.notes: Continuation variant distinct from reversal patterns; overlaps starter vocabulary tight_consolidation / range_compression. No gaps on crypto perps remove gap-fill complications around consolidation ranges; volume confirmation available.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Volume / On-Balance-Volume Trend Confirmation and Divergence
findings.mechanism: In a healthy trend volume flows with the trend (heavier on rallies than pullbacks); when price and volume/OBV diverge the trend is losing momentum, and OBV often breaks out before price, giving an early participation signal.
findings.setup_summary: Confirm trend health: OBV line rising with price = healthy; price at new highs while OBV makes lower highs (or OBV falls) = negative divergence, warning the trend is in trouble. Volume rule: in a healthy uptrend volume bars are larger on up days and smaller on pullbacks; heavier volume on pullbacks than on rallies is an early warning. At important bullish breakouts a noticeable increase in volume is essential; an upside breakout without it is suspect. OBV line often breaks out before price does.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Price and OBV/volume line diverging → treat trend as weakening; signal is a filter/reduction cue rather than an entry.
findings.risk_geometry: Not an entry setup; acts as a confirmation/filter on entries and as an early-exit warning; no stops or targets stated.
findings.quote: An upside breakout in any market that is not accompanied by a noticeable increase in trading activity is immediately suspect.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Volume Analysis' and 'Granville's On-Balance Volume' (pp.50-54)
findings.notes: OBV and volume-based divergence are directly computable on perp/SL 1h data and belong in the participation feature group (marketstate). Caveat for crypto: reported volume can include wash/fake volume on some venues — prefer aggregated trusted-feed volume. This feature should also gate the backlogged breakout_retest family.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: ADX Trend/Range Regime Filter
findings.mechanism: The ADX line (derived from +DI vs -DI) classifies market mode: rising ADX = trending (favor trend-following tools), falling/flat ADX = range (favor oscillators); ADX>40 then dropping = trend exhaustion.
findings.setup_summary: Compute +DI, -DI and ADX (Welles Wilder directional movement). ADX below 20 = low volatility, no trend (use nontrending/oscillator tools); ADX rising above 20 = beginning of an important trend (use trend-following); ADX well above 40 then starting to drop = trend exhausted, switch back to range tools. Use weekly ADX for primary regime determination (weekly more significant than daily).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Regime classification flips when ADX direction reverses; the rule only selects which tool class to use, it does not by itself enter positions.
findings.risk_geometry: None — a tool-selection filter (moving averages vs oscillators), not an entry/stop/target system.
findings.quote: A rising ADX line tells us that a market is in a trending mode. A falling or flat ADX line reflects a trading range environment.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'The Average Directional Movement (ADX) Line' (pp.131-135)
findings.notes: Directly implementable as a V8 regime gate on 1h BTCUSDT: gate which expert families (trend vs mean-reversion) are admissible per MarketState. ADX is a trend/volatility feature computed in marketstate; threshold params (20/40) become variants.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Stochastic Oscillator Reversal with Longer-Timeframe Trend Filter
findings.mechanism: Oscillator extremes flag overextension; the fast-timeframe (daily) overbought/oversold cross is only traded in the direction the longer timeframe (weekly, then monthly) points, producing 'buy dips in uptrends, sell rallies in downtrends'.
findings.setup_summary: Slow stochastics (14,3,3): %K = (close-low14)/(high14-low14)*100, %D = 3-period MA of %K. >80 overbought, <20 oversold. As long as weekly stochastic lines are positive (%K above %D), take only daily buy signals from oversold (<20) with %K crossing above %D (preferably with a positive divergence) and ignore daily sell signals; when weekly lines are negative, ignore daily buy signals and take daily overbought (>80) crosses for shorts. General rule: always use the next-longer timeframe (14h→14d→14w→14m) to set direction.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Weekly stochastics flip against the open position; in strong running markets oscillator stays pinned >80/<20 and should not be faded; daily signals alone are premature (needs weekly confirmation).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on daily bar close after the cross; no explicit stop/target; book shows combined RSI+stochastic confirmation improves reliability (stochastics earlier but less reliable; wait for RSI 70/30 confirmation).
findings.quote: always use the next longer time period to determine the direction of the market you will be trading from
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 'The Stochastics Oscillator' and 'Weekly Signals Determine Position' (pp.110-117)
findings.notes: The multi-timeframe trend-filter principle is a core methodology lesson for V8 lifecycle: longest-admissible timeframe sets the exposure side. Stochastics computable on 1h bars; weekly/monthly candles form naturally on 24/7 data.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: RSI Overbought/Oversold with Divergence and Failure Swing
findings.mechanism: Price making new highs while RSI fails to confirm (divergence) and then breaks its own intervening trough (failure swing) signals trend exhaustion even while price still rises; the RSI double top above 70 / double bottom below 30 is the trigger.
findings.setup_summary: RSI(9 or 14): >70 overbought, <30 oversold, 50 acts as trend midpoint (support during uptrend corrections, resistance to downtrend bounces). Sell setup: price at new high while RSI forms a double top above 70 (or descending RSI peaks), then RSI breaks the trough between its two peaks — a failure swing gives a sell signal even though price is still rising; often coincides with RSI falling back below 70. Buy setup is the mirror below 30. Most potent buy: daily AND weekly RSI both turning up from below 30.
findings.trigger_invalidation: In strong trends RSI can stay above 70 for weeks — do not fade while pinned; divergence without the failure-swing confirmation is only a warning, not a signal. If weekly RSI is dropping while daily turns up, the daily buy signal is weak.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on bar close after the failure-swing confirmation; no explicit stop or target stated; 70/30 and 50 crossings themselves generate trend signals.
findings.quote: If the RSI line then drops below the trough, a failure swing has been given.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.5 'Welles Wilder's Relative Strength Index' / 'RSI Divergences' (pp.100-109)
findings.notes: Distinct from stochastic finding: single-line divergence/failure-swing mechanics vs two-line cross with timeframe filter. RSI is computable on 1h data and widely corroborated. The failure-swing trigger is the falsifiable, objectively definable part.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Bollinger-Band Support/Resistance and Band-Width Squeeze
findings.mechanism: Price tends to meet resistance at the +2-sigma band and support at the -2-sigma band around a 20-period MA (95% containment); unusually narrow band width (low volatility) is usually followed by high volatility, so band contraction is a volatility-expansion precursor.
findings.setup_summary: Bollinger bands = 20-period MA with bands two standard deviations above/below. In an uptrend prices hold above the middle line (support) and rallies stall at the upper band; corrections find support at the 20-day line or the lower band. In a downtrend, the 20-day line is resistance and prices bounce off the lower band. Band width (contraction/expansion) tracks volatility: unusually narrow bands usually precede a high-volatility move; unusually wide bands warn of trend slowing or a return to a range. Works on daily, weekly, and monthly charts (20-period scaled to each).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Bands are tendencies, not hard barriers; a strong trend can ride the band. The squeeze signal gives no direction (book leaves resolution unstated).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry near a band on bar close with reversion expectation; target = middle line or opposite band; no explicit stop or expiry stated.
findings.quote: Unusually narrow bands (reflecting low volatility and a quiet market) are usually followed by a period of high volatility
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.4 'Or Put Bands around It' and 'Band Width Is Important, Too' (pp.87-95)
findings.notes: Band-width squeeze is a natural FEATURE_INPUT for the volatility feature group and a setup precursor for the existing volatility_breakout concept. The book also covers fixed-percentage envelopes (3% around 20-day, 5%/10% around 10-/40-week) as the simpler predecessor.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Relative Strength Ratio Rotation (Top-Down Leadership)
findings.mechanism: Money rotates among competing assets; the relative-strength ratio (asset/benchmark) trend reversal identifies which side is taking leadership, so investors buy rising-RS assets and avoid/underweight falling-RS assets.
findings.setup_summary: Compute the RS ratio = asset price / benchmark (stock vs S&P 500; sector vs market; commodity vs bond; for crypto: coin vs BTC or an index). Apply trendline or moving-average analysis to the ratio: a break of a long down trendline in the ratio (e.g., CRB/S&P in 2002) signals new leadership; a downside violation of the ratio's 50-day MA (China/world ratio, Q4 2007) signals underperformance. Top-down process: establish market trend first, then the strongest sector/asset, then the leader within it — but require both relative strength AND an absolute uptrend (relative strength in a falling asset only means losing money more slowly).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Ratio trendline/MA violation flips the rotation; diversification benefits diminish in global bear markets (all fall together).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry only when the asset is in an absolute uptrend and its RS ratio is rising; no explicit stop/target or expiry stated.
findings.quote: the relative strength ratio is the single most valuable tool in the asset allocation process
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.7 'The Relative Strength Ratio' (p.142) and Ch.9 'Relative Strength and Rotation' (pp.185-203)
findings.notes: For V8, a coin/BTC (or altcoin/market-cap) RS ratio is a cross_market feature usable for selection and regime work; supported by extensive multi-year case studies but no formal statistics in this book. Crypto caveat: 2022-style regime shifts and stablecoin/benchmark composition changes need a frozen benchmark definition.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Market Breadth Divergence (AD-Line and Percent Above 200-Day)
findings.mechanism: Index gains driven by fewer and fewer constituents are fragile: when the cumulative advance/decline line or the percent of assets above their 200-day average fails to confirm a new index high, breadth is diverging negatively and the rally is on weak footing, leading major indexes down at tops.
findings.setup_summary: Track breadth over the asset universe: a cumulative advance-decline line and/or the percent of assets trading above their 200-period average (crypto analog of the NYSE % above 200-day). Healthy = index and breadth rise together. Warnings: index makes a new high while breadth fails (negative divergence); % above 200-day exceeds 70-85% (overextended) then breaks below 70%; a drop below 40% signals a bear regime (first such break in 4+ years was significant in 2007), and only a recovery above 60% signals a new bull. Breadth turns down before major indexes, especially at tops, because cap-weighted indexes hide widespread weakness.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Breadth re-confirms (both lines rising together) → uptrend healthy; a rebound setup appears only when readings drop below 30% and then turn up.
findings.risk_geometry: A filter/early-exit tool rather than an entry; the book uses it to take profits or defensive action ahead of the index decline; no stops/targets stated.
findings.quote: While the NYSE was hitting a new high, only two-thirds of its stocks were still in uptrends.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.8 'Market Breadth', 'Percent of NYSE Stocks Above 200-Day Average', 'NYSE Bullish Percent Index' (pp.163-182)
findings.notes: Directly computable on crypto: percent of the top-N liquid coins above their 200-day MA is a widely used altcoin-regime indicator; advance-decline over the same universe is computable from index data. Belongs in participation/cross_market feature groups and can gate broad-market regime for V8.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Electronic front-running via fragmented order flow (signal leakage)
findings.mechanism: Large-order intent leaks when an order is split across multiple venues; fast participants detect the first arrival and trade ahead on the remaining venues, moving price against the sender.
findings.setup_summary: A large order is fragmented and routed to several venues at once. The first venue to receive it (e.g., BATS, physically closest) fills ~100% of displayed size while aggregated multi-venue fill collapses to a fraction; the price pops/plunges within milliseconds of entry as fast traders buy/sell ahead of the order on the other venues. Falsifiable on any timestamped multi-venue tape: fill rate falls as venue count rises, and the first venue's fills are systematically fuller (Brad observed 100% fills on BATS regardless of how many other exchanges he sent to).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: large order entry into a fragmented, thin market. Thesis (fragmentation leaks intent) is invalidated if simultaneous-arrival orders still produce partial fills and adverse price moves - which the book shows is NOT the case (synchronized arrival restored full fills).
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target stated; this is an adverse-selection (implementation shortfall) mechanism, not a directional setup. For V8: relevant as a flow/participation feature (aggressive-order footprint, fill-quality warning) rather than an entry rule.
findings.quote: some other trader was, in effect, noticing his demand for stock on one exchange and buying it on others in anticipation of selling it to him at a higher price
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2 (Brad's Problem) - the AMD/Intel live demo and Thor discovery
findings.notes: Victim-side lesson of the book's central mechanism. In crypto, a single dominant venue (Binance) removes 13-venue fragmentation arbitrage, but large-order footprint is still observable in the trade print and cross-exchange/index latency games exist; the transferable V8 seed is a large-aggressive-order feature. The predator-side detection vehicle (resting 100-share sentinel orders on BATS used 'to tease information out of investors'; latency tables used to fingerprint brokers) is a distinct flow-intelligence tactic that is DATA_BLOCKED for a bar-level tape - flagged in this finding rather than emitted as a separate expert.
findings.book: Flash Boys - A Wall Street Revolt 2015

findings.strategy_name: Liquidity-thickness-conditioned order slicing (Rob Park's algo)
findings.mechanism: Participating only when displayed depth exceeds its trailing historical average prevents the order itself from moving the market (thick books absorb flow without revealing intent).
findings.setup_summary: Execution rule for a large order: slice it into fixed tranches on a schedule (the book's example: 100,000 shares carved into 5,000-share pieces every five minutes, never above a price cap), but only transact a child order when the displayed offer size exceeds its trailing historical average - the market is 'thick'. Refrain when the book is thin, because a smart trader will not tip intent into a thin market. Falsifiable: fills obtained on thickness-gated tranches are better than un-gated participation.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: displayed size > historical-average offered size at the child-order price. Thesis (thick books absorb flow without adverse move) invalidates if thickness-gated fills are statistically no better than thin-book fills, or if the price cap is hit repeatedly.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit child orders gated by depth-vs-historical-average; fixed tranche schedule with per-tranche price cap; no stop/target stated (it is a participation/execution rule, not a P&L setup).
findings.quote: It only bought stock if the amount on offer was greater than the historical average of the amount offered.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2 (Brad's Problem) - description of Rob Park's RBC algorithm
findings.notes: Practitioner heuristic, falsifiable but not statistically validated in the book. For V8: a candidate liquidity-feature-group input (offered-size vs trailing-average depth) and a caution that thin books punish large participation - relevant to fill-quality reasoning even at 1h-bar granularity.
findings.book: Flash Boys - A Wall Street Revolt 2015

findings.strategy_name: SIP-latency / stale-price arbitrage (public vs private quote feed)
findings.mechanism: The public consolidated quote (SIP) lags private feeds built inside exchanges; fast traders buy at a stale public bid or sell at a stale public offer, and the value of the early view scales with volatility because volatility creates new prices to see first.
findings.setup_summary: Trade the gap between the public consolidated quote (NBBO via the SIP) and a faster private feed: buy when the fast feed shows a higher price than the public bid, sell when it shows a lower price than the public offer. Edge per window scales with realized volatility and with the feed-latency gap (up to ~25ms in the book's example). Empirical anchor cited in the book: UC Berkeley researchers counted 55,000 SIP-vs-fast-feed price divergences for Apple in a single day, each a potential stale-price exploitation.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence between public and private feed prices exceeding the latency*volatility product. Thesis (stale prices are exploitable by speed) invalidates if the latency advantage yields no consistent positive fill differential, or once the SIP is modernized to private-feed speed.
findings.risk_geometry: No stop/target stated; per-window arbitrage with inventory and latency as binding constraints; not executable at bar-close frequency.
findings.quote: That's why volatility was so valuable to high-frequency traders: It created new prices for fast traders to see first and to exploit.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4 (Tracking the Predator) - Reg NMS / SIP loophole and the UC Berkeley 2013 study
findings.notes: Falsifiable empirical case (cited 2013 UC Berkeley study with a concrete daily divergence count) for an intra-millisecond latency strategy. Not executable on BTCUSDT 1h bars or on a single-venue bar tape; retained only as market-structure context (why microstructure edges are speed- and volatility-dependent, and why 'public' aggregated feeds can lag reality).
findings.book: Flash Boys - A Wall Street Revolt 2015

findings.strategy_name: Event-granularity evidence rule (causality requires timestamped event data)
findings.mechanism: Causal attribution of a market event is unfalsifiable unless records exist at the timescale of trading; when trading happens at microsecond scale but records are kept by the second, competing causal stories cannot be distinguished.
findings.setup_summary: Methodological rule drawn from the 2010 flash crash: the SEC blamed a single erroneous futures sell order, but the market traded in microseconds while exchange records were second-granular (Brad's search of the SEC report: 87 hits for 'minute', 63 for 'second', 4 irrelevant hits for 'millisecond', 0 for 'microsecond'). Any causal claim built on coarser-than-event data ('someone hit a button') is unfalsifiable - 'the data didn't exist'. For V8 this is the justification for the event/available/ingested three-clock discipline and hash-bound deterministic replay.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any causal claim about an event made from data coarser than the event timescale. Thesis (granularity determines falsifiability) invalidated only if a coarse record can be proven to uniquely determine the causal chain.
findings.risk_geometry: Not a trading setup; a data/evidence-quality rule. V8 enforcement: append-only logs, no wall clock in replay, three never-collapsed clocks.
findings.quote: The unit of trading was now the microsecond, but the records kept by the exchanges were by the second.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4 (Tracking the Predator) - flash crash and Brad's word-count audit of the SEC report
findings.notes: Directly reinforces V8's deterministic-replay and PIT rules: episode attribution is only as good as the event clock, and collapsed clocks make findings non-reproducible. Also a caution against accepting 'official' single-cause explanations for large adverse moves without microstructure-scale evidence.
findings.book: Flash Boys - A Wall Street Revolt 2015

findings.strategy_name: Hidden execution-cost tax measured by controlled counterfactual experiments
findings.mechanism: Hidden transaction costs ('the tax') are real, systematic, and invisible at the per-trade level; they are measurable only by controlled experiments that compare realized fills against a counterfactual where the mitigating mechanism is applied.
findings.setup_summary: Measure implementation shortfall as the difference between the pre-trade quoted market and realized execution, using matched controlled trades (RBC traded 'not to make money but to test theories', with an allowed daily loss budget). Results cited: buying 10 million Citigroup shares with synchronized (front-run-proofed) arrival saved ~$29,000, under one-tenth of 1% of notional - 'the tax' - which scaled to ~$160M/day market-wide; one $9B hedge fund estimated the cost of not trading at stated prices at ~$300M/yr (~3.3%). Falsifiable: the measured saving is either above noise or it is not.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: fills on the same order with vs without the mitigating mechanism (synchronized arrival / thickness gating). Thesis (hidden costs are real and systematic) invalidates if the measured differential is within noise of zero across a large representative sample.
findings.risk_geometry: No directional setup; a cost-model calibration lesson. Entry/target/stop not stated. For V8: the simulator's Binance cost model should include implementation shortfall / adverse selection beyond the raw fee schedule, because hidden costs materially change per-trade economics.
findings.quote: we bought 10 million shares of Citigroup, then trading at roughly $4 per share, and saved $29,000 - or less than a tenth of 1 percent of the total price. 'That was the tax,' said Rob Park.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2 (Brad's Problem) - Thor experiments and the presentation to T. Rowe Price; corroborated in Chapter 3/4 (the $300M hedge-fund estimate)
findings.notes: The book's explicit evidence-methodology contribution: (a) run controlled counterfactual experiments with a bounded loss budget rather than trusting broker cost reports; (b) hidden costs are amplified by market structure (maker-taker kickbacks, routing distortions) and scale with volume; (c) extrapolating a small measured saving to market scale is a legitimate order-of-magnitude argument. Feeds V8's simulator cost model and the 'the economic verdict stays NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM' discipline (costs must be modeled, not assumed away).
findings.book: Flash Boys - A Wall Street Revolt 2015

book_title: Flash Boys: A Wall Street Revolt (2015)

findings.strategy_name: Relative strength ratio rotation (buy leaders, avoid laggards)
findings.mechanism: relative strength ratio trend identifies leadership; concentration in leaders and rotation out of laggards captures the rotational drift that indexes hide
findings.setup_summary: Compute the instrument/benchmark ratio (e.g., a sector or alt contract divided by the broad market). LONG the market or instrument whose RS ratio is above its rising trendline / making relative new highs while the benchmark is flat; exit and rotate when the RS ratio breaks its support trendline. Falsifiable: RS-ratio leaders persist over weeks-to-months and rotation into leaders on ratio-confirmation beats equal-weight.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: RS ratio above a rising trendline or breaking out vs benchmark. Invalidation: RS ratio closes through its support trendline (leadership loss) or the instrument's own trend turns.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar close once ratio confirms. Stop: RS-ratio trendline break. Target/expiry: none stated; book notes sector trends may last only a few months so they must be monitored frequently.
findings.quote: Relative strength analysis allows you to identify market sectors that are outperforming (leaders) and those that are underperforming (laggards). The main idea in doing that is to buy leading sectors and avoid the laggards.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 12 Summary (Exchange-Traded Funds); also Ch 11 figs 11.6-11.7 (Consumer Staples RS high; Retail ratio support break)
findings.notes: Direct analog in crypto perps: BTC/alt ratio and perp-vs-perp leader rotation (e.g., BTC vs ETH or sector contracts) as a cross_market feature. In 24/7 perp markets there are no exchange gaps to distort ratios, and funding regimes make the ratio the cleaner leadership gauge than absolute price. Requires the cross_market feature group and a benchmark series; single-instrument BTCUSDT 1h scope limits it to a candidate family.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: 200-day moving average major-trend regime filter
findings.mechanism: price below/above a very long MA defines the major trend; the MA's own slope adds regime confirmation
findings.setup_summary: Track close relative to a long MA (book: 200-day). Close below the (rising) 200-day = major sell/risk-off; close above = major buy/risk-on; a turning-down 200-day is an additional bearish sign. Falsifiable: being flat or short while below the long MA and long while above it outperforms unconditional exposure.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close crosses the long MA. Invalidation: close returns through the MA (whipsaw) or the MA flattens into a range so the filter stops separating regimes.
findings.risk_geometry: Used as a bias/regime gate, not an entry: no entry order, stop or R-target stated. In V8 terms it is a candidate RegimeFilter input that gates experts rather than a standalone expert.
findings.quote: The fund fell below that major support line during July which flashed a major sell signal. ... It's a bad sign when the 200-day line turns down as it did near the end of that year.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11, '200-Day Moving Average and Housing' (fig 11.1); Ch 11 fig 11.10 (Fidelity Intl Real Estate); Ch 12 fig 12.2 (QQQQ)
findings.notes: On V8's 1h bars a 200-day MA is ~4,800 bars; book uses daily. Suggest mapping by calendar time (e.g., rolling 200-day close series from 1h closes) so the regime filter is comparable to equities research. 24/7 markets remove weekend-gap artifacts that plague daily MA signals in equities, so the filter is cleaner here; but crypto's long, deep trend reversals make MA-turn confirmation worth testing as a separate feature.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: 50/200-day moving average crossover trend flip
findings.mechanism: a shorter MA crossing a longer MA signals the intermediate trend has flipped; the cross filters noise that single-MA price violations cannot
findings.setup_summary: Bullish cross: 50-period MA crosses above 200-period MA -> long bias; bearish cross: 50-period crosses below 200-period -> short bias. Book documents the bearish 50/200 cross as the second-stage sell signal (after the 200-day violation) that avoided two-thirds of a 30% drawdown. Falsifiable on BTCUSDT: cross-defined bias flips capture the major trend turns better than single-MA violations.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 50 MA crosses 200 MA. Invalidation: immediate counter-cross (whipsaw) or price stalling in a range where MAs converge.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar close after cross confirmation. Exit: opposite cross. No R-multiples or stops stated; book treats it as a position bias tool.
findings.quote: The second is the downside crossing of the 200-day average by the 50-day (down arrow) a month later. From its summer 2007 top to its spring 2008 bottom, this fund lost 30 percent of its value. The visual trader who spotted the bearish moving average crossing could have avoided two-thirds of those losses.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11, 'Bear Crossing Sinks Chips' (fig 11.4); also 'Bullish 50/200-day MA Crossovers' scan rows in Appendix A fig A.2
findings.notes: In perp crypto, funding and 24/7 trading produce more choppy MA crossovers than in daily equities; expect higher whipsaw. The 50/200 on 1h (~1,200/4,800 bars) is slow but maps directly to the trend feature group. Keep as a backlog family; low priority versus faster trend features, and it is effectively a variant of the long-MA regime filter.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Old resistance becomes new support (breakout retest hold)
findings.mechanism: after an upside breakout of prior resistance, the first pullback to the breakout level acts as support; a hold-and-resume confirms genuine demand at the level
findings.setup_summary: Price closes above a prior windowed high (breakout), then pulls back to the old-resistance/new-support level; if the close holds above the breakout level and price resumes the uptrend, continue LONG. Falsifiable: retest-holds above the breakout level are followed by continuation more often than retests that close back below.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: breakout close above prior high; retest close stays above breakout level. Invalidation: retest closes back below the breakout level (failed retest / vacuum reentry).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close above resistance, or the retest-hold close. Stop: below the breakout level (retest low). Target: not stated (continuation, book gives no R-multiple).
findings.quote: the fund dipped right back to its breakout point during August (see circle) before resuming its uptrend. That confirmed the old adage that 'old resistance becomes new support.'
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11, 'Natural Gas Breakout' (fig 11.2)
findings.notes: This directly corroborates V8's existing DATA_BLOCKED backlog family breakout_retest (location, volatility, history) and its old-resistance->new-support mechanism. Perp 24/7 markets have no gap-throughs of resistance levels, so breakout-level retests are cleaner and more testable; high leverage makes the stop below the breakout level a natural 1R geometry.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Rate-of-change zero-line crossing as trend confirmation
findings.mechanism: ROC crossing zero after a long stretch on one side signals the trend has lost or regained momentum
findings.setup_summary: Compute ROC(N) (book: 13-week ROC on weekly). A zero crossing after the ROC has been on the opposite side for an extended period (e.g., first time below zero in 16 months) confirms the trend change and is the tradeable signal. Falsifiable: ROC zero-crosses, especially after a long one-sided stretch, precede trend continuation in the cross direction.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: ROC(N) crosses zero after >=N bars one-sided. Invalidation: ROC re-crosses zero within a few bars (failure) or the move is range-bound.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar close after zero-cross. No stop/target stated; used as a confirmation feature rather than a standalone system.
findings.quote: A sell signal occurred in December 2007 (down arrow) when the rate of change fell below zero for the first time in 16 months.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11, 'Negative ROC Hurts Technology' (fig 11.5); ROC also indexed under 'Rate of change' usage in Ch 11 and Appendix A scans
findings.notes: The 'first time in N months' qualification is the falsifiable part: a prior-context ROC zero-cross is stronger than a raw one. On 1h perp data, ROC over ~equivalent windows is cheap and deterministic. Add as a trend/response feature; the 'extended one-sided stretch' condition makes it a candidate regime-confirmation input, not an expert.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Multi-touch trendline break as high-conviction support violation
findings.mechanism: a support line touched multiple times concentrates order flow; a decisive close through it is a major regime signal, not a noise event
findings.setup_summary: Fit an up-trendline to at least three swing lows; a decisive close below the multi-touch line is a major sell signal (book example: break of a four-year, three-touch support line caught the consumer discretionary decline one-third in). Falsifiable: breaks of >=3-touch trendlines lead larger and longer moves than breaks of 1-2 touch lines.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close below a >=3-touch rising trendline. Invalidation: close reclaims the trendline side within K bars (trap) or the trendline was fit on <3 touches.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close through the trendline. Stop: trendline reclaim / swing extreme. Target: not stated; book notes the break occurred only a third into the decline, implying large residual move.
findings.quote: The more times a trendline is touched, the more reliable it becomes. A good trendline should be touched at least three times as this one was. That's why the decisive break of that four-year support line during October 2007 (circle) was so important.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11, 'Consumer Discretionary Breakdown' (fig 11.3); also Ch 11 fig 11.11 (RTPIX trendline breaks)
findings.notes: The '>=3 touches' reliability rule is a concrete, testable feature for the location feature group and for supply_demand_zone-type logic. Trendline fitting is subjective; V8 would need a deterministic fit (e.g., anchored least-squares or pivot-based). In 24/7 crypto, hourly trendlines are noisy and high leverage makes stop placement sensitive to fit method.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Engulfing reversal at support with volume confirmation
findings.mechanism: an engulfing candle at a support location shows aggressive directional absorption; heavier volume and support confluence raise its significance
findings.setup_summary: A bullish engulfing candle (white body fully engulfs prior black body) that forms at a chart-support location (prior low, trendline, or moving average) with above-average volume is a short-term reversal signal; bearish engulfing is symmetric at resistance. Falsifiable on 1h BTC: engulfing-at-support on rising volume precedes short-term reversals more often than engulfing in mid-range on average volume.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: engulfing candle closing at a support/resistance location on above-average volume. Invalidation: next bar closes back through the engulfing body (failed reversal).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: close of the engulfing bar (bar-close entry). Stop: below engulfing low (bullish) / above engulfing high (bearish). Target: not stated; book presents it as a short-term turn tool to be combined with other criteria.
findings.quote: If that short-term upside reversal takes place in an area of chart support (like a previous low, a trendline, or a moving average), it takes on even more significance. Heavier upside volume also adds to the significance of the pattern.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix B, 'Bullish Engulfing Pattern' (figs B.3-B.5); candlestick reversal list indexed under 'Bullish Reversal Patterns'
findings.notes: V8 has no candlestick family yet. The book's core falsifiable contribution is the three-way confluence (location + volume + engulfing body), which fits the location/participation/volatility feature groups. 1h 24/7 perp candles make engulfing common, so the location+volume filters are what would separate signal from noise. Entry at bar close keeps it simulator-compatible.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Point-and-figure column breakout with box-size sensitivity scaling
findings.mechanism: recording only box-size price moves strips intra-column noise; a new column exceeding prior column tops/bottoms is an unambiguous breakout, and exceeding more columns is a stronger signal
findings.setup_summary: Build a point-and-figure chart with a percent box size (book recommends 1% default; 0.5% for short-term, 2% for long-term). Buy signal: new X column exceeds the prior column's top (double-top breakout; triple/quadruple for exceeding 2-3 columns). Sell signal: new O column falls below prior bottoms. Falsifiable: the box-size-filtered column breakouts have higher follow-through than raw tick-by-tick breakouts, and triple/quadruple signals outrank double.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: column exceedance of prior column extreme. Invalidation: immediate column reversal (X->O or O->X) right after the signal.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: at the column-break signal price. Stop: at the box level where the column reverses (box size sets stop granularity). Target: not stated in Part 2; book notes P&F software computes price objectives.
findings.quote: the triple-top breakout is considered to be a stronger signal. The same is true of the triple-bottom breakdown. And, as you might expect, the quadruple-top breakout is even stronger because three previous X columns are exceeded.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix C, 'Triple and Quadruple Signals' (figs C.1-C.3, C.6); box-size guidance in 'How to Vary P&F Charts'
findings.notes: The percent box size is effectively a volatility/ATR-style filter, which is exactly what 1h perp noise needs. Implementable deterministically from OHLC without wall-clock dependence. The column-break is a location feature (prior column high/low). The P&F 'Bull Trap / Bear Trap' alert classes in fig C.3 corroborate V8's failed_breakout mechanism (breakout then reversal) and could be a REFINE_EXISTING input rather than a new family.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Bullish percent breadth regime thresholds (BPI + McClellan momentum)
findings.mechanism: the proportion of a market's constituents on buy signals measures internal participation; thresholds separate bull/bear/oversold regimes that single-instrument price cannot show
findings.setup_summary: Compute the percent of universe instruments on buy signals (book: NYSE Bullish Percent Index). Below 50 = bear territory, back above 60 required to confirm bull, below 30 = oversold; sector BPI dispersion identifies the weakest and strongest groups. McClellan oscillator (19/39 EMA cross of net advances) gives short-term breadth momentum. Falsifiable: breadth thresholds separate regimes that price alone does not.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: BPI crosses 50/60/30 thresholds, or 19-EMA breadth crosses 39-EMA. Invalidation: rapid threshold back-crossing (bounding in the 40-60 band).
findings.risk_geometry: Regime gauge only: no entry, stop, target, or expiry stated. Used to filter group participation and confirm 'bear market rallies'.
findings.quote: readings in the NYSE Bullish Percent Index ($BPNYA) well below 50 percent put it in bear market territory; and that a move back over 60 percent was necessary to put it back into a bull market.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix A, 'Bullish Percent Indexes' (figs A.4-A.5) and 'McClellan Breadth Indicators' (fig A.6)
findings.notes: Requires an instrument universe (many perp contracts) for breadth; V8 currently runs a single instrument (BTCUSDT 1h), so this is universe-gated, not single-instrument. In perp crypto the closest analog is breadth of a perp basket (e.g., % of top contracts above their own long MA, or funding-weighted breadth), which is a real sentiment/flow input once a multi-instrument tape exists.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Negative-correlation flight-to-safety hedging (bonds/gold vs stocks)
findings.mechanism: in stress, money rotates out of equities into Treasuries and gold, producing persistent negative cross-asset correlation that can hedge or replace equity exposure
findings.setup_summary: During equity market stress, bond ETFs and gold rise as stocks fall; inverse funds mirror the index so a sell signal on the long vehicle is a buy signal on the inverse. Falsifiable: cross-asset correlation between the risky asset and its hedge turns strongly negative in stress regimes and can be traded directly rather than via hedged net exposure.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: risk-off regime where the counter-asset rallies while the risky asset falls. Invalidation: correlation flips positive (flight-to-safety breaks down; central-bank backstop).
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target given in Part 2; presented as a portfolio-construction and instrument-selection method (mutual fund/ETF rotation), not a per-trade geometry.
findings.quote: During the second half of 2007, bond ETFs rose sharply as stocks fell. So did gold. ... This is because money rotating out of stocks during a period of economic stress usually moves into the relatively safety of Treasuries.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 12, 'Using ETFs to Hedge' (figs 12.1, 12.10); also Ch 11 'Inverse Stock Funds' (fig 11.14)
findings.notes: In perp markets there is no need for inverse vehicles - SHORT is native, so the mirror-image trick is moot. The transferable piece is cross-asset correlation as a feature group input (e.g., BTC vs equity index, BTC vs gold, or BTC vs ETH) for regime detection. Out of scope for the single-instrument program; would need multi-asset data feeds.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Methodology: prices lead fundamentals; use the tape as the discounting mechanism
findings.mechanism: market price is a leading indicator that discounts fundamentals; lagging fundamental data should be predicted FROM price, not the reverse
findings.setup_summary: Do not overweight lagging fundamental or media narratives against price action: 'if the technicals are bad, the fundamentals are probably just as bad'. The stock market leads the economy by 6-9 months, so a leading indicator cannot be predicted from a lagging one. For V8 this validates a behavior/tape-driven program and explains why expert inputs are price, order-flow and regime features rather than fundamentals.
