findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a - methodology principle, not a tradeable signal.
findings.risk_geometry: none stated; principle-level guidance.
findings.quote: Rather than using fundamental data to predict the trend of a market, it makes more sense to use the price trend to predict the fundamentals.
findings.chapter_anchor: Conclusion, 'Prices Lead the Fundamentals' and 'The Stock Market Leads the Economy'
findings.notes: Also supports the book's recurring 'keep it simple' rule - 'the best market moves are usually fairly obvious. The real trick is to make sure that you see them' (Ch 11 'Keep It Simple') - which maps to V8's complexity budget (rule 14) and its preference for a few clean features over esoteric indicators. Reinforces why media/retrospective explanations ('the media will always tell you why later') are not a valid evidence source.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

findings.strategy_name: Lifecycle rule: bearish/inverse exposure is cyclical, not a long-term holding
findings.mechanism: bearish (inverse) positions are valid only inside the bear regime; the regime is cyclical, so short exposure must be closed when the regime flips rather than held indefinitely
findings.setup_summary: Book states stocks spend 3 of every 4 years in uptrends, so bear funds/inverse exposure are unsuitable as long-term holdings and 'should be sold' once the bear market or correction ends - 'that's where market timing comes in'. Falsifiable lifecycle rule for V8: SHORT experts should be expiry/regime-bound; a SHORT exposure whose regime condition (e.g., price below the long-MA, downtrend intact) flips must be closed, mirroring how bear-market tools are wound down.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: SHORT exposure active; regime flips bullish (e.g., price reclaims the long-MA or the 50/200 cross turns bullish). Rule fires: close short exposure. Invalidation: regime flip fails (whipsaw re-entry below MA reopens the short case).
findings.risk_geometry: Exit rule only - the book gives no entry/stop/target; its contribution is the lifecycle constraint on short/hedge exposure.
findings.quote: a bear fund isn't suitable as a long-term holding. As the name implies, a bear fund is suitable during a bear market (or a severe downside correction). Once the bear market (or correction) has ended, the bear fund should be sold. That's where market timing comes in.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 12, 'Using a Bear ETF' (fig 12.1); also Ch 11 'Inverse Stock Funds' (fig 11.14) and Ch 12 'Inverse Sector ETFs' (fig 12.5)
findings.notes: Directly actionable for V8: it argues SHORT-direction exposure should be regime-bound with an explicit exit on regime reversal, rather than held to a fixed R-stop or indefinite expiry. Perp specifics strengthen this - funding paid on short positions bleeds a stale short, and 24/7 reversal risk makes a regime-flip exit rule (via the long-MA/50-200 cross) a natural lifecycle clause for any SHORT expert. Corroborates the two-way/cyclical view in the book's ETF chapters.
findings.book: The Visual Investor - How to Spot Market Trends 2nd edition 2009

book_title: The Visual Investor: How to Spot Market Trends (2nd Edition, 2009) - Part 2 (Ch 11-12, Conclusion, Appendices A-C)

findings.strategy_name: Multiple Time Frame Momentum Strategy (dual-timeframe momentum alignment)
findings.mechanism: larger-timeframe momentum direction conditions the market; a smaller-timeframe momentum reversal in that direction is the highest-probability re-entry point
findings.setup_summary: Trade only in the direction of the higher-timeframe momentum (e.g., 4h/1d trend feature); wait for a lower-timeframe (1h) momentum oscillator bullish/bearish reversal; enter with a stop-based trigger and initial stop one tick beyond the swing made prior to the reversal. Falsifiable: count entries that occur within N bars of a higher-TF bullish/bearish momentum state and a lower-TF cross.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = lower-TF momentum reversal in direction of higher-TF momentum, cancelled if the lower-TF momentum makes an opposite reversal before fill. Thesis invalid if the higher-TF momentum reverses or reaches OB/OS (see regime_filter finding); the book states a higher-TF bearish reversal from OB implies weeks of sideways-to-down, not a long.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry via stop one tick above/below the last completed bar or swing; initial protective stop one tick below/above the swing prior to the reversal; ST unit target = minor corrective retracement, LT unit target = trend continuation.
findings.quote: The basic strategy is to trade in the direction of the larger time frame and execute the trade following a smaller time frame momentum reversal in the direction of the larger time frame momentum.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary 'Multiple Time Frame Momentum Strategy'; Ch.2 rules; Ch.7-8 trade campaigns
findings.notes: The book calls this 'the best trade filter I've discovered in over 20 years'. V8's trend_pullback already encodes single-timeframe trend alignment; a dual-timeframe (4h/1d trend, 1h momentum reversal) variant is the natural refinement. Momentum = ROC-style oscillator, computable PIT. Requires a trend feature evaluated on a second timeframe bucket.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Momentum reversal trailing one-bar-high/low (Tr-1BH/L) stop entry
findings.mechanism: entry only fills when price takes out the prior bar extreme in the trade direction, avoiding catching a knife and confirming momentum continuation
findings.setup_summary: After the lower-timeframe momentum reversal condition is met, rest a stop order one tick above (long) or below (short) the last completed bar; re-arm the order on each new bar at the new bar extreme until filled; initial stop one tick beyond the swing low/high prior to entry. Falsifiable: entry fills only if the bar extreme is taken out; measurable fill rate and subsequent outcome.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Order is cancelled if the smaller-timeframe momentum makes a reversal in the opposite direction before the fill; thesis invalid if the swing used for the initial stop is breached at fill time.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop-entry at prior-bar extreme +1 tick; initial protective stop at swing low/high -1 tick; exposure = entry-to-stop distance (the book repeatedly computes initial capital exposure in pips and judges setups by it).
findings.quote: If the trade entry order is executed, the initial protective stop is placed one tick below/above the swing low/high made prior to entry.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 / Glossary 'momentum reversal trailing one-bar-high/low entry strategy'; applied throughout Ch.7-8
findings.notes: This is a different fill semantics from V8's current NEXT_BAR_CLOSE: it requires a resting-stop fill model in the canonical L1 simulator (fill if bar high/low reaches the order price), or a conservative approximation (enter next bar only if the prior bar extreme was broken). Also feeds the one-exposure lifecycle entry ordering.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Swing breakout entry strategy
findings.mechanism: a defined reversal/continuation condition plus price taking out a recent swing extreme confirms the new section has begun
findings.setup_summary: Once minimum setup conditions are met (higher-TF momentum alignment, correction position), enter go-long one tick above the recent swing high (or go-short one tick below the recent swing low); initial stop one tick beyond the swing made prior to entry. Falsifiable: define swing via windowed pivot rule; entry triggers on breakout bar.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid if setup conditions (momentum/pattern position) are no longer true before price reaches the swing level, or if price reverses below/above the prior swing after entry.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop-entry above/below recent swing extreme; initial stop at the prior swing +1 tick buffer; no target stated by this strategy (targets come from price projection methods).
findings.quote: initiate a go-long or go-short entry at a price one tick above/below the recent swing high or low
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.6 / Glossary 'swing breakout entry strategy'; swing-entry examples pp.150-158 (referenced)
findings.notes: Distinct from the existing failed_breakout expert (which is SHORT on re-entry after a failed break). This is the long-side (and symmetric) breakout trigger. Candidate for the backlog breakout_retest family; swing definition must be a deterministic windowed pivot rule.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Two-unit / multiple-unit exit management
findings.mechanism: splitting one thesis into a short-term and long-term unit lets the trader bank a profit on a minor corrective target while keeping a wide-stop unit alive for the larger trend
findings.setup_summary: Every trade taken with at least two units. Unit 1 (ST) is exited at a minor corrective target (e.g., the 50% retracement) or trailed at the one-bar-low after a lower-TF momentum reversal; Unit 2 (LT) is held for a trend target with a wide stop adjusted only on swing structure. Falsifiable: compare (a) two-unit exit scheme vs (b) all-in/all-out on the same entries.
findings.trigger_invalidation: ST-unit exit triggers on minor-target touch or trailing 1BL; LT-unit exit triggers on trend target, higher-TF momentum extreme reversal, or swing-based stop; thesis invalid when the correction extends past its price/time targets (implies complex correction or reversal).
findings.risk_geometry: ST unit: exit ~50% retracement or trailing 1BL after momentum reversal, then stop moved to breakeven; LT unit: stop kept far, adjusted one tick below/above swing prior to each momentum reversal; capital exposure measured per unit.
findings.quote: Every trade should be taken with at least two units. One unit is considered short-term and is exited if the market reaches a minor corrective target. The second unit is considered long-term and is exited at a trend target.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.7 / Glossary 'multiple-unit trading'; executed by Adam Sowinski (p.202-206), Jagir Singh (p.207-213), Jaime Johnson (p.231-235)
findings.notes: Partial exits are compatible with V8's one-active-exposure rule (rule 16) since they scale one exposure rather than opening a second. The book also contains a scale-IN example (add to short below a minor Wave-b low); that conflicts with the one-exposure rule and would need explicit lifecycle treatment if ever pursued.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Wide-stop structure-based stop trailing (momentum-reversal stop adjustments)
findings.mechanism: keeping the stop far from price early protects the trade from noise; tightening only on a technical event (momentum reversal, target touch) avoids being shaken out of a valid trend position
findings.setup_summary: Initial stop one tick beyond the swing prior to entry; do not move it until a defined technical event occurs (target reached, or the next lower-TF momentum reversal). Then adjust to one tick beyond the swing low/high made prior to that reversal. Do not trail to every minor swing. Falsifiable: a rule 'adjust stop only on momentum-reversal events' versus 'trail at every N-bar swing' compared on outcome and stop-out rate.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger for each adjustment = momentum reversal event in trade direction (or structure change: consolidation breakout, gap, two-day selloff); thesis invalid if price exceeds the swing levels that define the stop chain (dead thesis).
findings.risk_geometry: Stops at swing points +1 tick, not ATR multiples; the book's examples keep the LT stop so wide it only adjusts a handful of times over a multi-week trade (e.g., EUR/USD LT unit: stop moved ~3 times in 6 weeks).
findings.quote: Unsuccessful traders often trail the stop much too close to the market and get stopped out for a relatively small profit when they could have held for a much larger profit.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.8 Robert's Follow-Up on Adam Sowinski (p.205); also Ch.7 LT-unit management (p.193-196)
findings.notes: Directly informs V8's dead-thesis (still_valid) vs stop distinction and the RiskGate stop model: the rule is that stops are adjusted on structure/momentum events, not continuously. In high-leverage perps this must be paired with the exposure cap (risk_percent_sizing finding) since wide stops mean large absolute risk.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Momentum OB/OS dual-timeframe regime filter (exhaustion block)
findings.mechanism: when higher-timeframe momentum is overbought/oversold, the remaining move is limited and a higher-timeframe reversal is imminent, so new entries are blocked and existing stops tightened
findings.setup_summary: Only long trades considered when higher-TF momentum is bullish UNLESS it is bull OB; only shorts when bearish UNLESS bear OS. When the higher-TF momentum reaches OB, expect at most a couple of lower-TF reversals before a higher-TF high/reversal; after a higher-TF bearish reversal from OB, expect sideways-to-down for several weeks (no new longs). Falsifiable: measure forward returns after higher-TF momentum extreme vs non-extreme, and after higher-TF reversal-from-extreme.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Filter blocks new entries (RiskGate admission) at OB/OS extremes; once a higher-TF reversal from extreme occurs, the thesis 'trend continues' is invalid and existing positions are trailed tightly.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry at extremes; existing LT positions trailed close (one tick below swing prior to next lower-TF reversal) once the dual-timeframe extreme position is made; anticipated high within a couple of higher-TF bars.
findings.quote: Only long trades would be considered if the momentum is bullish unless the momentum is bull OB. ... The weekly momentum made a bearish reversal from the OB zone, which is typically followed by a sideways to down trend for several weeks, which is not a time to hold a long position.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary 'bull OB, momentum'; Ch.2 strategy rules (referenced); Ch.7 p.196-197
findings.notes: Crypto momentum extremes can persist (OB stays OB during sharp trend legs), so the 'imminent reversal' claim is the falsifiable part to test on BTCUSDT 1h with 4h/1d higher-TF momentum. As a RiskGate admission block it is cheap and testable.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: ABC-correction confluence-zone pullback entry (multi-Fib target cluster)
findings.mechanism: corrections are at least three swings; their end is bracketed by a confluence of independent price projections (internal retracements, APP, external retracements) and time retracement, so the pullback low is a location feature rather than a guess
findings.setup_summary: In an established trend, after a three-swing (ABC) correction, enter in trend direction when price reaches a zone where multiple Fib levels cluster (e.g., 61.8/78.6% internal retracements, 100% APP of Wave-A, 127/162% external retracements) with lower-TF momentum oversold (for a long) and time retracement in the 38.2-61.8% band. Falsifiable: define the confluence zone by counting overlapping projection levels; test touch-and-reversal frequency.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid if price breaks beyond the confluence zone toward the Wave-A extreme (simple ABC) or past 162% Ex-Ret / 100% time retracement (complex correction or trend reversal). A confirmed three-wave decline that reverses above the Wave-A low implies the correction is over and the advance continues (used as an exit in the GBP example).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry via momentum-reversal/1BH trigger after the zone touch; initial stop below the confluence/support (e.g., below regression channel line); ST target = Wave-C target zone (61.8-100% APP); LT target = continuation beyond the prior extreme.
findings.quote: Most corrections end at or very near one of the four key internal retracements.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary 'retracement, internal price'; Ch.4 (referenced); Ch.8 Derrik Hobbs soybean setup (p.223-224)
findings.notes: Refines trend_pullback: adds a location feature (confluence zone of windowed-Fib levels) as the expected pullback terminus, plus the time-retracement band. The three-swing assumption ('the assumption is always that a correction will make at least three sections') is the falsifiable core.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: 2-standard-deviation linear regression channel reversion/continuation
findings.mechanism: in a trend, price oscillating around a 2-sd regression channel mean reverts at the channel edges, so the bottom of the channel locates the trend-continuation entry and the top locates the exit
findings.setup_summary: In an established uptrend with weekly/daily momentum oversold, buy when price reaches the bottom of the 2-sd linear regression channel and a momentum bullish reversal fires; initial stop below the channel support; exit half at the channel median, the rest at the top of the channel. Falsifiable: measure reversion at the channel band and the median/top objective hit rate.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid if price closes below the regression channel support line (stop at a structural low under the line); a 'at least two-day sell-off before considering a swing low' rule governs which structure points count for stop adjustment.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at momentum reversal near channel bottom (767'25, stop 743'75 in the example); stop below regression support; exit half at channel median, half at channel top; the author admits this yields small losses in choppy, non-trending conditions and large gains in runaway trends.
findings.quote: My objective in a strong trending market is to take half the profits at the median of the regression channel and to take the rest of the profits at the top of the regression channel.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.8 Derrik Hobbs soybean trade (p.225-227)
findings.notes: A 2-sd regression channel is the linear analogue of Bollinger bands; computable deterministically on bar closes. Crypto trends routinely overshoot channel edges during funding-driven squeezes, so the reversion assumption is the falsifiable part. Candidate backlog family; requires volatility (std-dev window), trend, and location features.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Session/participation filter - avoid low-activity noise
findings.mechanism: low-participation sessions produce quick but meaningless swings and volatility, so signals generated there are noise, not information
findings.setup_summary: Filter trade consideration to periods with adequate participation; ignore or down-weight moves made in low-volume sessions. The author trades only pit-session data for ES because overnight volume is low and produces 'quick but meaningless swings'. Falsifiable: compare signal quality (forward return given a signal) by participation bucket / hour-of-week.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Filter is admission-side: signals formed in low-participation windows do not trigger entries (or are marked lower-confidence).
findings.risk_geometry: None stated; purely an entry-qualification filter.
findings.quote: I generally only look at pit session data because the volume is so low overnight and there are often quick but meaningless swings and volatility overnight.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.8 Robert's Follow-Up on Kerry Szymanski ES trade (p.221)
findings.notes: Crypto is 24/7 with no exchange close, but participation and volatility cluster by UTC session (Asia/Europe/US) and around funding timestamps (00/08/16 UTC), so a time/participation feature group is directly constructible from perp tape (hour-of-week + rolling volume percentile). Not a strategy by itself; feeds feature-group spec.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Fixed-percent capital exposure cap (max 3% per trade)
findings.mechanism: capping initial capital exposure (entry minus initial stop, times units) as a fraction of equity keeps any single thesis from materially damaging the account regardless of leverage
findings.setup_summary: Position size is chosen so that the per-trade capital exposure (|entry - initial stop| x units) is at most 3% of account equity; the book also uses a two-unit split so the effective exposure per unit is smaller. Falsifiable: an account-level risk metric computed per trade; sizing rule is deterministic.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trade not taken (or size reduced) when the structure-based stop implies exposure > 3% of equity; the book notes a wide-stop setup may be traded via a less-leveraged instrument (SPY instead of ES) rather than skipped.
findings.risk_geometry: Sizing cap on (entry - stop) distance x units; this is the cap that makes the book's wide structure stops tractable.
findings.quote: The maximum position size should represent capital exposure of no more than 3 percent of the account.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary 'position size'; Ch.6 position-size section (referenced, pp.158-162)
findings.notes: Complements V8's RiskGate heat cap. On leveraged perps the 3% capital-exposure cap is the binding constraint (liquidation distance = |entry - stop|), so the RiskGate should compute exposure in the same way: stop distance in price terms times notional leverage.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Leverage discipline: prove edge unleveraged before trading leveraged; trade for points, not ticks
findings.mechanism: leverage multiplies an unproven method's losses faster than its wins; point-capture (swing/position timeframes) has a higher success floor than tick-capture (day trading) because it avoids high-frequency decision stress
findings.setup_summary: Do not deploy leverage (in perp terms: high leverage / margin) until the strategy is demonstrably profitable on an unleveraged proxy or small size; prefer swing/position timeframes that trade for points; the book asserts 70-95% of retail accounts lose within months, more so for day traders. Falsifiable in V8 only as a program-level gate, not a market strategy: OOS evidence precedes any leverage/execution claims.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not a market signal; a research-program governance rule.
findings.risk_geometry: None; account-level discipline.
findings.quote: If you can't make money with unleveraged trades, you'll never make money with leveraged trades.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.9 'Trade for Points, Not for Ticks' and 'Technology, Trading Time Frames, Markets to Trade, and Leverage' (p.242-244)
findings.notes: Reinforces V8's own constitution (NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM without authority receipt; evidence gates before promotion). Corroborates the choice of 1h bars / point capture over tick-level day trading, and argues for gating leverage and execution studies behind frozen-OOS evidence.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Time Band / alternate time projection (cycle-based timing)
findings.mechanism: if the market's recent time-cycle rhythm continues, the next high/low is made inside the overlap window of recent cycle ranges
findings.setup_summary: Project the window for a trend high/low as the overlap of recent high-high and low-high cycle ranges (bull) or low-low and high-low ranges (bear), with outliers excluded; Alternate Time Projections at 62/100/162% of prior same-direction swing durations complement it. Used to time exits near price targets (e.g., gold top projected to mid-March 2008, actual high March 17 at the projected price).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Time window is advisory for exit timing only; the book's own example exited a long near a corrective low before the trend resumed - time projections carry no thesis-invalidating power by themselves.
findings.risk_geometry: Exit-window overlay on price targets; no stop or entry semantics.
findings.quote: In a bull trend, the overlap of the recent high-high cycle range and the recent low-high cycle range. If the recent time cycle rhythm continues, the assumption is the next high will be made in the Time Band (overlap) range.
findings.chapter_anchor: Glossary 'Time Band'; Ch.5 (referenced); Ch.8 Cees van Hasselt gold trade (p.216-218)
findings.notes: Cycle counting (H-H/L-L ranges, outlier exclusion) is subjective; 24/7 crypto data removes the session cadence that anchors intraday cycles; and V8 determinism requires any timing feature to be bar-count based, not wall-clock. Defer behind a gated, deterministic reformulation if ever pursued.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

book_title: High Probability Trading Strategies: Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets (Robert Miner, 2008) - Part 2 (Ch.7-end, 8, 9, Glossary)

findings.strategy_name: Dual Time Frame Momentum Strategy (direction + execution filter)
findings.mechanism: When rate-of-change momentum on a larger time frame defines trade direction and a smaller time frame momentum reversal aligns with it, the market is positioned for the largest price moves with minimal capital exposure; momentum and price trends often diverge, so a single-frame momentum signal is not a trade signal.
findings.setup_summary: On any two time frames (e.g., daily+60m, or 4h+1h for crypto), only consider trades in the direction of the larger time frame momentum indicator trend. The setup condition is a smaller time frame momentum reversal (fast line crossing slow line) in the direction of the larger time frame. Four higher-timeframe states with distinct rules: bull-not-OB (longs on smaller-TF bullish reversal below OB zone), bull-OB (no new longs, shorts possible on bearish reversal), bear-not-OS (shorts on smaller-TF bearish reversal above OS zone), bear-OS (no new shorts, longs possible on bullish reversal). Setup is a precondition, not an execution signal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Setup voided if smaller time frame momentum reverses against the larger time frame before execution; smaller-TF bullish reversal made inside the OB zone (or bearish reversal in the OS zone) is not a valid long (short) setup. A higher time frame OB/OS position is never a reason to exit an existing position, only to avoid new entries.
findings.risk_geometry: Filter only: no entry/stop of its own; entry is handled by a separate objective entry strategy (e.g., trailing one-bar or swing). Higher-TF oversold/overbought lowers expected downside before the next reversal, reducing required capital exposure.
findings.quote: Trade in the direction of the larger time frame momentum. Execute the trade following the smaller time frame momentum reversals.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, Multiple Time Frame Momentum Strategy (esp. 'The Basic Dual Time Frame Momentum Strategy' and 'Dual Time Frame Momentum Strategy Rules', Table 2.1)
findings.notes: The author's core claim ('most powerful approach I've discovered in over 20 years'), fully objective (four momentum states, no interpretation). Book shows honest losing setups and divergences. In V8 terms this is a universal direction gate; because routers/shared scorers are ABSENT by default (rule 14), it must enter either as a per-expert feature requirement (e.g., trend_pullback already requires trend+volatility) or through a registry experiment beating a simpler baseline on frozen OOS. Crypto note: 24/7 tape makes two-frame momentum alignment well-defined with no session/gap artifacts, and the book's own 'momentum hangs in OB during strong trends' rule anticipates crypto's strong-trend behaviour.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Trailing One-Bar High/Low (Tr-1BH/L) stop-entry
findings.mechanism: Requiring the market to take out the last completed bar's extreme before entry filters out entries that would immediately reverse, and puts the initial stop close to the reversal for small known capital exposure.
findings.setup_summary: Once the high-probability setup conditions are met (DTF momentum reversal at a price/time target zone), place a resting buy-stop one tick above the high of the last completed bar (long) or sell-stop one tick below the low (short); re-place it bar-by-bar on the new last bar until filled. Initial protective stop is one tick beyond the swing extreme made prior to entry. If the smaller time frame momentum reverses against the intended direction before fill, the order is cancelled.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Cancel the resting order if the smaller time frame momentum makes a reversal against the trade direction, or (for shorts) reaches the oversold zone, before execution. If the swing extreme taken as the stop level is violated, the reversal thesis is voided.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: stop order 1 tick beyond last completed bar extreme (takeout, not bar-close). Initial stop: 1 tick beyond the prior swing high/low. Capital exposure = entry minus stop, known exactly before fill (book example: 24.75 pts on ES, judged too large, mitigated by dropping to a smaller time frame or an unleveraged ETF). No fixed expiry; entry order lives while the setup conditions hold.
findings.quote: trail the buy-stop or sell-stop to enter the trade one tick above the high or below the low of the last completed bar. Place the initial protective stop one tick beyond the swing high or low made prior to entry.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, 'Entry Strategy 1: Trailing One-Bar Entry and Stop'
findings.notes: Completely objective entry with known pre-fill exposure; 24/7 perps have no gaps, so takeout entries and one-tick-beyond stops are executable as a matter of course. In V8, this is a candidate refinement of the entry semantics of existing experts (trend_pullback currently enters NEXT_BAR_CLOSE): modeling a resting stop-order entry requires a simulator fill-model decision (canonical L1 is fill-at-close), so flag as an explicit simulator_model variant before adoption.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: ABC correction overlap + Wave-B-takeout continuation entry
findings.mechanism: When a pullback section overlaps back into the range of the prior section, the market is most likely in a correction (not a new trend); a move beyond the Wave-B extreme confirms the correction is complete and price resumes the pre-correction trend to a new extreme.
findings.setup_summary: In an established trend, label a pullback as at least three swings (A-B-C). Setup signal: price trades back into the range of Wave-A (the overlap guideline) - minimum conditions for a correction are complete. Entry: trade/close beyond the Wave-B extreme (a swing entry) - 'all-out go long or short signal' - with the initial protective stop no further than the potential Wave-C extreme. Minimum expectation: a new extreme beyond where the correction began. On the opposite side, a trend is the five-wave non-overlapping structure.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If price takes out the extreme that began the prior trend (the correction thesis level), the correction interpretation is voided. Book is explicit that overlap is not always a correction and a correction is not always overlapping (two shown failure figures), so stop discipline at the Wave-C extreme is mandatory.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: 1 tick beyond Wave-B extreme (swing takeout). Initial stop: 1 tick beyond potential Wave-C extreme (the swing low/high prior to entry). No fixed target: minimum reward is the new extreme beyond the correction start; 100% alternate price projection is the usual reward assumption. No fixed expiry.
findings.quote: If a market overlaps a section, more than likely it is making a correction. ... A trade beyond the Wave-B extreme is a pattern signal that the correction should be complete, with a stop no further than the potential Wave-C extreme.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Trend or Correction: The Overlap Guideline' and 'ABC and Away We Go'
findings.notes: Structure-based and timeframe-agnostic, so it transfers to 1h/4h crypto, but requires reliable swing labeling (the book's own failed-example Figure 3.17 shows a 'correction' that broke down to new lows) and the author admits 'most corrections do have a swing overlap and most overlaps are a part of a correction' without statistics. New family means a registry decision + CHANGELOG per D-032/D-033; complexity budget (rule 14) is full at 3 active experts, so this must start in backlog (like breakout_retest and capitulation).
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Five-wave trend stage identification ('fifth waves are the key')
findings.mechanism: Trends typically complete in five non-overlapping sections; once four sections conforming to guidelines are confirmed, the next new extreme is probably a final Wave-5 and the trend is near exhaustion, so the countermove should be at least greater in time and price than any correction within the trend.
findings.setup_summary: Count trend sections; when four completed sections meet the guidelines (Wave-2 does not trade beyond the start of Wave-1; Wave-3 is not the shortest of waves 1, 3, 5; Wave-4 does not close into the closing range of Wave-1 - author's modification allows intraday wick overlap), a new extreme is a probable Wave-5. A smaller time frame momentum reversal at the probable Wave-5 extreme is an early signal the trend is complete. A trade beyond the Wave-4 extreme confirms five waves done and implies a countermove at least greater in time and price than any prior correction in the trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Count invalidated (recount) if Wave-2 exceeds the Wave-1 origin, Wave-3 is the shortest, or Wave-4 closes into the Wave-1 closing range. The book shows overlapping bull 'trend' waves (Figure 3.28) where the structure never conformed - so this is a heuristic stage cue, not a rule.
findings.risk_geometry: Exit/stage rule rather than entry: when the four-wave guidelines are met and momentum reverses at a probable Wave-5, tighten or trail stops instead of adding; reversal entry only after Wave-4 extreme takeout with a stop beyond the Wave-5 extreme.
findings.quote: The most valuable piece of information regarding trends is that once waves 1 through 4 are confirmed, the trend should be in the final stages.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Trends and Five-Wave Patterns' and 'Fifth Waves Are the Key'
findings.notes: For V8 this is best used as a lifecycle/exit-side rule for existing trend experts (a 'trend near exhaustion' state that flips the still_valid or stop-trailing policy) rather than a standalone entry, consistent with the book using it to avoid adding longs near the end of a trend. In 24/7 high-leverage perps, extended fifth waves and liquidation cascades are common, and the author's own modification (allow wick overlap of Wave-1) plus the overlapping-trend example argue for keeping it a probabilistic stage cue.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Dynamic Price Strategy: In-Ret + APP + Ex-Ret confluence zones (EOW targets)
findings.mechanism: Corrective and trend highs/lows tend to occur at proportions of prior sections; a narrow price zone where independent projections from different sets (internal retracements, alternate price projections, external retracements) coincide marks a high-probability reversal zone for a correction or trend end.
findings.setup_summary: Internal retracements: 38.2/50/61.8/78.6% of a trend section (50/61.8 end most corrections; 78.6 is the max - a close beyond it voids the correction thesis). Alternate price projections: for a correction, APP of Wave-A at 61.8/100/162 projected from the B extreme (100% APP is the most frequent target); for a five-wave trend with four sections complete, APP of waves 1-3 at 38.2/61.8 from the Wave-4 extreme and 100% APP of Wave-1. External retracements: 127/162/262% of Wave-B (correction) or Wave-4 (trend) to locate the final section. A high-probability zone contains one projection from each of the three sets (minimum: one In-Ret plus one APP).
findings.trigger_invalidation: If price reaches the zone without a momentum/pattern reversal, the zone is not the end of the structure. A close through the 78.6% internal retracement voids the correction thesis (trend continuing). Corrective sections rarely exceed the 162% APP.
findings.risk_geometry: These are pre-identified take-profit/reversal zones, not entries - the book insists entries still require confirmation (never buy/sell at a target price). Reward estimation rule: the minimum reward is a new extreme beyond where the correction began, or the 100% APP; 'risk/reward' ratios are called a best guess and deprecated.
findings.quote: if an In-Ret and an APP are near each other, they form a relatively narrow-range zone from where a corrective trend reversal is probable.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, 'Beyond Fib Retracements' (Internal Retracements, Alternate Price Projections, External Retracements, Pattern Price Targets / EOW-C and EOW-5)
findings.notes: Ratios are price-agnostic and computable on 1h bars, but in leveraged 24/7 perps projected zones are frequently swept by stop-runs and liquidation cascades, so the book's own prescription - zone reached is only a condition to stand ready for a momentum/pattern reversal, never a standalone trade - is the load-bearing part. For V8 these zones are natural 'location' feature-group inputs (distance-to-confluence-zone features) rather than a new expert, and could later feed take-profit placement as a refinement of the fixed target_r 1.0 convention.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Dynamic Time Strategy: time retracements + alternate time projections + Time Bands
findings.mechanism: Reversals cluster at harmonic proportions of prior sections measured in time units (time retracements, alternate time projections) and at the overlap of recent cycle ranges (Time Bands); several independent time factors inside a narrow window raise the probability of a reversal there, so a trader is prepared in advance for when to expect the turn.
findings.setup_summary: For a potential three-section correction, project (1) time retracements of the prior trend at 38.2/50/61.8/100/162% (simple ABC corrections usually complete in the 38.2-61.8% zone; complex corrections by the 100% time retracement), (2) alternate time projections of the Wave-A time range at 61.8/100/162% from the B extreme (62% = minimum, 100% = most frequent, 162% = max for a Wave-C), and (3) the recent 100% low-low (or high-high) cycle; the narrow overlap window (+/- 1-2 bars) is the probable correction-completion time. Time Bands: overlap of the recent high-high count range and low-low/low-high count range (5-6 repetitions, outliers trimmed) projected forward.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A new low/high before the 38% time retracement is not a completion (only temporary support/resistance). If price makes a new extreme beyond the 100% time retracement for a complex correction, the time thesis is void (book shows the failed IBM example where the correction high came well after all time factors).
findings.risk_geometry: Time-only readiness tool: no entry or stop of its own; used to be prepared to act on a price-plus-momentum confirmation inside the window. Book repeatedly notes time factors 'warn what is probable and not probable' rather than pinpointing bars.
findings.quote: Most simple three-section, ABC corrections are complete in the 38.2% to 61.8% time retracement zone.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, 'Beyond Traditional Cycles' (Time Retracements and Corrections, Alternate Time Projections, The Time Target Zone, Time Bands)
findings.notes: Bar-count projections are fully compatible with V8 determinism (no wall clock; time in bars) and with a 24/7 tape (no session structure to distort counts). Reliability of cycle regularity in high-leverage crypto is questionable - the author himself presents a clean failure - so for V8 this is a 'time' feature-group input (bars-to-window) used as a readiness/regime cue, never a standalone trigger; requires PROJECT_EVIDENCE before any formalization.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Two-unit position: short-term take at minor-correction completion, long-term unit rides the trend
findings.mechanism: Splitting a position into two units hedges the uncertainty of the larger trend call: exiting the first unit at a probable minor-correction completion banks a profit even when the 'major trend' thesis is wrong, while the second unit is held with a wide stop to capture a developing trend.
findings.setup_summary: Every position is taken in at least two units. Short-term unit: once price reaches the 61.8% retracement of the prior trend section OR after the second smaller time frame momentum reversal against the position (two reversals because even a corrective rally makes an ABC with two momentum highs), trail the stop at the 1-bar low and take the unit out on the trailing stop. Long-term unit: hold with a relatively wide stop (e.g., below the potential Wave-B low / out of the typical 38.2-50% Wave-4 retracement) until the higher time frame momentum reaches its overbought/oversold extreme or a probable Wave-C / Wave-5 price target is reached, then trail the 1-bar low; adjust to breakeven once two sections of a potential ABC are complete.
findings.trigger_invalidation: ST unit exits on the trailing 1-bar low after its trigger (61.8% retracement or second momentum reversal). LT unit exits on the trailing 1-bar low after higher-TF momentum OB/OS or the projected Wave-C/Wave-5 target zone; the book's example also shows a logical mid-campaign stop advance after a minor swing high was taken out.
findings.risk_geometry: Two exits per position: unit-1 target is a structural retracement/momentum condition, unit-2 target is trend-exhaustion (higher-TF momentum extreme or pattern/price target), both executed as trailing 1-bar-low stops rather than fixed-price limits. Aggregate capital exposure still capped at 3% (see risk_percent_sizing).
findings.quote: For every trade, there must be at least two units. ... one unit is usually exited relatively quickly for a relatively small profit. The second unit is held with the intention of capturing the longer-term trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, 'Multiple-Unit Trading' and 'Trade Management' (XAU and S&P campaigns)
findings.notes: Partial takes fit perp trading well: they harvest the fast initial move, cap losses when the 'trend' call is wrong, and cut exposure (and funding cost) on the second unit. In V8, rule 16 allows one exposure per (instrument, direction) - a two-unit position is a within-exposure sizing variant, not two exposures, so this is a lifecycle refinement requiring a registry decision, not a new expert family.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Let-the-market-take-you-out: trailing stop, never exit at a fixed price target
findings.mechanism: Fixed take-profit exits forfeit the tail of trends (markets often blow through price targets); trailing a protective stop keyed to structure and momentum captures the majority of a trend while capping the give-back, because the stop is always placed at the price that voids the trade thesis.
findings.setup_summary: After entry, never place a take-profit at a predetermined price; instead trail the protective stop at the trailing 1-bar low or below the most recent minor swing structure, advancing it only on a logical structural event: a new minor swing extreme taken out, the second smaller-TF momentum reversal against the position, price reaching a 61.8% retracement or a projected target zone (as a stop-adjustment trigger, not an exit price), or the higher time frame momentum reaching OB/OS. Exit is the stop being hit by market action. Exception allowed: when you cannot monitor the market (e.g., vacation), leave a protective stop plus a take-profit limit.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The stop is never placed at an arbitrary dollar distance from price; it is always at the price that voids the entry thesis. The four exit concepts: (1) let the market take you out, (2) exit factors = entry factors (momentum/pattern/price/time), (3) plan both units' exits before entry, (4) adjust as new information arrives, each change a logical consequence of the new bars.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop = 1 tick beyond trailing 1-bar low or the relevant swing structure; no fixed target; expiry = while the thesis holds, exits are structural. Gives back a small amount beyond each swing to avoid premature exits ('trailing a stop too close' is named the top reason traders get shaken out before trend completion).
findings.quote: Always let the market take you out by moving against the position. Do not exit at a predetermined price target.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, 'Exit Strategies' and 'Exit Strategy Concepts'
findings.notes: Directly applicable to perps, where early-profit-taking is the dominant retail habit and trends are extended; one caveat the book does not address: funding costs on a held long mean an 'always hold to trend end' bias must be tempered by expected funding carry. For V8 this argues for making still_valid/dead-thesis exits structural (already the design: stops and dead-thesis are different exits) and for refining target_r handling so projected zones are stop-tightening triggers rather than hard take-profits.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Capital exposure limits: 3% per trade, 6% aggregate, 10% monthly stop
findings.mechanism: Capping per-trade and aggregate capital exposure keeps the account alive through losing streaks - the book states successful traders run only ~30-40% win rates, so small losses and large wins are the only path to survival; the drawdown math (20% loss needs 25% gain, 50% needs 100%) makes preservation decisive.
findings.setup_summary: Maximum capital exposure on any single trade = 3% of available account equity; maximum exposure on all open trades = 6%; maximum acceptable monthly closed-trade loss = 10% (stop trading for the balance of the month once hit). Position size = (available capital x 3%) / (per-unit capital exposure), rounded down, where per-unit exposure = entry price - initial stop price times contract/share value. Example: $20,000 account, $325 per-contract exposure -> 2 contracts max.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a - sizing rule applied to every candidate trade; if per-unit exposure is so large that even 1 unit breaches the 3% cap, pass the trade or move to a smaller timeframe (or an unleveraged instrument) to shrink exposure.
findings.risk_geometry: The sizing formula consumes whatever risk_geometry the setup produces (entry and initial stop determine per-unit exposure); the author's framing - 'we don't determine the entry, stop, or exposure; the market does' - matches V8's design where exposure is a deterministic function of entry/stop.
findings.quote: Three percent maximum capital exposure on any one trade and 6% maximum exposure on all open trades is the accepted standard.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, 'Position Size'
findings.notes: Directly maps to V8 RiskGate deterministic admission and the heat cap; perps' high leverage and 24/7 operation make these caps more, not less, important (monthly 10% caps can be hit in hours). The book also records a meta-lesson: Gann's traditional 'never risk more than 10%' was found by the author to be far too much - a reminder that sizing rules need project evidence, not just authority.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Momentum lookback selection: variants, not one magic setting
findings.mechanism: An indicator's lookback period sets the tradeoff between signal lag and whipsaw false reversals; the useful setting for a market/timeframe is the one where reversals originate from the OB/OS zones near price extremes with few mid-range fakes, and settings must be re-tuned when volatility/momentum cycles change.
findings.setup_summary: For a chosen momentum indicator (Stoch/DTosc/MACD are shown to give nearly identical reversal timing - 'most price indicators represent about the same thing'), test a few lookback periods (e.g., 8 vs 13 vs 21) on recent data: the 13-period example beat 8 (mid-range whipsaws) and 21 (lag + reversals missing the OB/OS zones). Choose the period meeting three criteria: (1) both lines reach the OB/OS zone before most reversals, (2) reversals fall within a couple bars of price swing extremes, (3) few whipsaw reversals between zones. Re-test when momentum cycles change (e.g., when the indicator stops reaching the OS zone on corrections in a stronger trend, shorten the lookback).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Settings drift: when the indicator makes two or more oscillations without reaching the OB/OS zones on corrections, the lookback is no longer matched to the current momentum cycle and should be revised on recent data.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a (parameter selection); the author explicitly rejects the idea of one universal best setting and of market-condition-dependent rule sets (never know a trading range/trend in advance), arguing for one chosen setting held until compelling evidence of drift.
findings.quote: Test a few settings on recent data and see which best meets the criteria for a useful indicator.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'What Are the Best Indicator Settings to Use?'
findings.notes: This validates V8's rule that parameter/threshold changes are VARIANTS of one family (one multiplicity unit) rather than new experts, and warns that crypto's volatile regime changes will invalidate fixed lookbacks - re-tuning must be done on frozen OOS with a registry decision (per rule 15), never in-sample or on live data, to respect V8 determinism and the no-overfit gate.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Four-factor confluence: momentum + pattern + price + time alignment
findings.mechanism: When several independent market dimensions (multiple time frame momentum, pattern structure, projected price zone, projected time window) all indicate the same reversal, the setup has a higher probability outcome and smaller capital exposure than any single factor alone, because the odds stack rather than add.
findings.setup_summary: For each candidate reversal, score four independent factors: (1) multiple time frame momentum position and smaller-TF reversal, (2) pattern position (ABC completion / overlap / five-wave stage), (3) price projections confluence zone reached, (4) time projections window reached. Trade only when multiple factors point to the same reversal; the book's worked campaigns (XAU, S&P, OIH) always list Momentum/Pattern/Price/Time summaries before the Trade Strategy. Minimum expectation rule used throughout: after a completed correction/trend, price resumes to a new extreme at least greater in time and price than the prior section.
findings.trigger_invalidation: When factors conflict, treat the setup as lower probability - pass or reduce size; never take a trade on a single factor. The book is explicit that any single indicator or technique alone is insufficient and that all four together still lose sometimes (objective is 'high probability outcome and acceptable capital exposure', never certainty).
findings.risk_geometry: Confluence lowers initial capital exposure because the entry sits at the alignment point with a close structural stop (book example: ~2-3 points risk against 35+ points reward). The reward side is always a best guess (minimum = new extreme beyond correction start, or 100% APP).
findings.quote: it is when several completely independent factors all indicate the same position that the best setups with the highest probability outcome and smallest capital exposure are made.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Momentum and Pattern Position'; thesis restated in Chapters 4-5 summaries and every Chapter 7 trade campaign
findings.notes: The confluence thesis is coherent with V8's multi-feature-group experts (each setup already requires several feature groups), but the independent contribution of each factor in 24/7 leveraged crypto is unknown and must be validated per factor (e.g., feature-gate ablation on frozen OOS). This is a methodology lesson for how setups are composed in MarketState, not a new expert or a router - the absence-by-default rule (rule 14) means a shared confluence scorer would have to win a registry experiment.
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

findings.strategy_name: Rejected: momentum-divergence reversal systems and 'trading range' strategies
findings.mechanism: The author's falsification stance: price-momentum divergence and trading-range patterns are selected-after-the-fact artifacts; divergence occurs when a trend merely slows (momentum reverses while price continues), so most divergence-setup 'reversals' are losses, and a trading range can never be known to be a range in advance.
findings.setup_summary: The author challenges any single-indicator or divergence-based system: 'I've never seen one of these plans that actually made money' despite many well-chosen published examples, because on the same data there were identical divergence setups that lost. Likewise, 'trading range strategies' are declared fiction since the market can never be known in advance to be entering a range - the book shows the same pattern position (overlap) failing to a new low. Explicit caution to ignore educators selling divergence or range-specific rules.
findings.trigger_invalidation: n/a - rejection stance; the relevant test is that any divergence/range rule must survive PROJECT_EVIDENCE on frozen OOS before V8 ever formalizes it.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a
findings.quote: I've never seen one of these plans that actually made money... For every price-momentum divergence example that resulted in a trend reversal, I can just about guarantee there were one or two and probably a lot more that did not result in a trend reversal on the same data.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'Momentum and Price Trends Often Diverge'; trading-range remarks in Chapters 2-3
findings.notes: This is the author's skeptical argument, not empirical evidence - hence NARRATIVE - but it is a valuable screening gate for V8: divergence-based reversals (rsi_divergence and similar) and range-regime rules should not be adopted from literature alone; they need PROJECT_EVIDENCE_SUPPORTED before any registry movement. It also corroborates V8's core stance that trend indicators alone are unreliable for reversal timing ('for every trend indicator example I will show you two where it quickly failed').
findings.book: High Probability Trading Strategies - Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets 2008

book_title: High Probability Trading Strategies: Entry to Exit Tactics for the Forex, Futures, and Stock Markets (Robert C. Miner, 2009) - Part 1 (Ch 1-7)
The Warren Buffett Way (2nd Edition, 2005) — Part 2

findings.strategy_name: Contrarian at sentiment extremes
findings.mechanism: Pessimism is the most common cause of low prices; crowd fear/greed extremes push prices away from fair value, then revert
findings.setup_summary: When crowd sentiment reaches an extreme (observed proxies in perps: funding rate extremes, record open interest, lopsided long/short skew), fade the crowd direction. 'Be fearful when others are greedy and greedy only when others are fearful.' Falsifiable: entry opposite the sentiment extreme, hold for reversion toward the pre-extreme level.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: participation/flow extremes at record percentiles. Invalidation: sentiment extreme persists and deepens (no reversion within window), i.e., the crowd is right.
findings.risk_geometry: Book specifies no entry/stop/target; holding horizon years, not bars. For V8: needs bar-close entry, ATR or swing stop, expiry bars; the book's own warning is that a panic can stay extended in a leveraged venue.
findings.quote: We simply attempt... to be fearful when others are greedy and to be greedy only when others are fearful.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11 The Psychology of Money (Mr. Market), pp. 180-181
findings.notes: Proxies (funding, OI, long/short skew) are directly observable 24/7 on perps, making this testable; but crypto has no intrinsic-value floor, so a pure sentiment fade without a value anchor can be killed by a leverage cascade (see deleveraging_cascade starter vocabulary). Gate as a sentiment feature input until participation/flow feature groups are formalized.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Overreaction reversal on discrete news shocks
findings.mechanism: Investors overreact to bad news and react slowly to good news, fixating on the most recent information; the overshoot reverts once the extrapolation exhausts
findings.setup_summary: After a sharp price move on a discrete event (scandal, earnings miss, hack), enter opposite the shock once the recent-information extrapolation has run its course. Exemplar in text: American Express dropped nearly 50% on scandal while the business thesis was intact; the price recovered within ~2 years (author's framing). Falsifiable: shock-overshoot reversal to pre-event level within a defined window.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: large adverse move on an idiosyncratic, news-identifiable event while thesis/conditions are unchanged. Invalidation: the thesis is actually broken (the event changed the fundamentals), so price does not revert.
findings.risk_geometry: Book gives no stops/targets; the AE case held ~2 years and exited on recovery. For V8: bar-close entry after shock, swing/ATR stop, expiry in bars, thesis-invalidation exit via still_valid.
findings.quote: people tend to overreact to bad news and react slowly to good news. Psychologists call this overreaction bias.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11 The Psychology of Money (Overreaction Bias), pp. 184-185
findings.notes: Chapter cites academic behavioral studies (Thaler) for the overreaction regularity. On 24/7 perps news shocks happen intraday and carry no gap protection, so overshoots can be violent and reverts delayed by funding/leverage; the slow-to-good-news half of the claim implies a drift continuation variant worth separating in screening.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Crowding gate: consensus empties the edge
findings.mechanism: When everyone makes the same choice for the same reason, no one is left to profit from it and the crowded position is vulnerable to a sharp unwind
findings.setup_summary: When positioning/consensus becomes one-sided (mob influence, institutional imitation), the edge on that side evaporates and unwind risk rises. Falsifiable as a risk gate: block new entries on the crowded side when participation/flow extremes are present, or fade the crowded side; crowding proxies for perps are funding rate, open interest, and long/short skew.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: crowding metric at extreme percentile. Invalidation: consensus positions continue to be rewarded (crowding is not mean-reverting in this regime).
findings.risk_geometry: Book specifies no geometry. As a gate: no entry on the crowded side; if used as an entry, contrarian with ATR/surplus stop, because the unwind move can be a liquidation cascade.
findings.quote: when everyone is making the same choices because 'everyone' knows it's the thing to do, then no one is in a position to profit.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11 The Psychology of Money (temperament / mob influence), p. 179; institutional imperative referenced pp. 96-102
findings.notes: Munger's institutional-imperative/herding claim. Highest perp relevance of the book: funding/OI/long-short crowding is measurable, and crowded perp positioning is exactly what produces liquidation cascades; this complements the existing liquidity/participation feature-group direction rather than a new price expert.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Concentrated low-turnover portfolio construction
findings.mechanism: High turnover erodes net returns through transaction costs, and concentration forces deeper analysis that raises decision quality
findings.setup_summary: Empirical claim from the book (Mauboussin 1992-2002 study): market-beating funds averaged ~30% annual turnover vs ~110% for all equity funds, held 37% of assets in top-10 names, and espoused intrinsic-value selection. Focus investing limits the portfolio to ~10-20 names with 0-20% turnover and 5-10 year holding.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (portfolio construction rule, not a trade signal).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A; stated holding periods 5-10 years, turnover 0-20%.
findings.quote: As a whole, the market-beating mutual funds had an average turnover ratio of about 30 percent. This stands in stark contrast to the turnover for all equity funds—110 percent.
findings.chapter_anchor: Afterword (Mauboussin study), pp. 208-209; Ch 10 Managing Your Portfolio, pp. 160-163
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's complexity budget (max 3 ACTIVE experts, rule 14) as a deliberate concentration decision, and argues against expert proliferation. On perps the turnover penalty is worse (taker fees + funding), so low-frequency, higher-conviction signals are structurally favored; also a cost-model input for the simulator.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Uncertainty-scaled margin of safety
findings.mechanism: The required discount/edge before entering scales with the uncertainty and economic risk of the situation; higher risk demands a greater margin of safety
findings.setup_summary: Entry-admission rule: required edge (discount, or in V8 terms required R / edge threshold) is a monotone function of uncertainty/volatility of the candidate. Falsifiable: compare per-entry outcomes across volatility buckets and require a larger edge threshold in high-uncertainty regimes.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: candidate passes thesis screen. Rule application: demanded edge rises with uncertainty proxy. Invalidation: edge-threshold scaling does not improve risk-adjusted outcome.
findings.risk_geometry: Book states no prices/stops; concept only. Maps to RiskGate admission thresholds and interacts with heat cap; in V8 terms, higher-vol regime -> larger required edge or smaller size, not a wider stop.
findings.quote: to protect against higher economic risk, demand a greater margin of safety in the purchase price.
findings.chapter_anchor: Afterword (Bill Miller section), p. 207; margin-of-safety principle pp. 13, 25, 131
findings.notes: Directly portable: in perps the uncertainty axis is realized vol/regime and the 'margin of safety' becomes a required-edge or sizing gate. Cleanly falsifiable in the V8 lab by bucketing entries on volatility and testing whether a scaled admission threshold improves risk-adjusted outcome.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Pre-committed invalidation exits against loss aversion
findings.mechanism: Loss aversion is asymmetric (~2x), so humans hold losing positions far too long hoping for a turnaround; mechanical pre-committed exits are the countermeasure
findings.setup_summary: Behavioral claim: investors need roughly twice as much positive to overcome a negative (Thaler experiments), causing them to hold bad choices too long and to defer realizing losses ('the loss doesn't become real until they act on it'). Rule: invalidation exits must be pre-committed and mechanical, not discretionary.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (exit-discipline rule).
findings.risk_geometry: Book gives none; the V8 analog is the dead-thesis (still_valid) exit, which must fire independently of current PnL.
findings.quote: investors feel twice as bad about losing money as they feel good about picking a winner
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11 The Psychology of Money (Loss Aversion, Mental Accounting), pp. 185-186
findings.notes: Refines existing lifecycle semantics: V8 already separates stops from dead-thesis exits; this finding supplies the behavioral rationale for why still_valid must be thesis-based and state-frozen, and why holding a loser through funding accrual on leveraged perps is doubly costly (funding + liquidation risk + the psychology the book documents).
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Best-alternative threshold gate
findings.mechanism: Every new candidate must beat the best alternative you already know to be available; applying the threshold screens out most of what you see
findings.setup_summary: Munger's measuring stick: 'the best thing you already have should be your measuring stick.' A new candidate is admitted only if it is better than the current best available alternative; this screens out 99% of candidates. Falsifiable at the program level: registry admission requires the candidate to beat the simpler baseline on frozen OOS before status advance.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (admission methodology).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A.
findings.quote: If the new thing you are considering purchasing is not better than what you already know is available, then it hasn't met your threshold. This screens out 99 percent of what you see.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10 Managing Your Portfolio (The Decision to Buy), p. 173
findings.notes: Directly corroborates V8's challenger + frozen-OOS + registry gate (rule 14: learned components enter only by beating the simpler baseline). Argument for keeping candidate admission competitive rather than absolute-threshold-based.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Horizon-dependent odds
findings.mechanism: Short-horizon price prediction is a coin toss; extending the horizon, given a sound thesis, shifts the odds in the holder's favor
findings.setup_summary: Methodological claim: predicting price direction over a short period has roughly coin-flip odds; with a sound purchase and a multi-year horizon the odds shift meaningfully in favor. V8 corollary: next-bar-close entries on 1h data are noise-dominated; prefer structural signals that are evaluated over longer horizons.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (framework lesson).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A; implied holding horizon years.
findings.quote: if you extend your time horizon out to several years (always assuming that you have made a sensible purchase), then the odds shift meaningfully in your favor.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10 Managing Your Portfolio (Buffett's View of Risk), p. 165
findings.notes: In perps the horizon extension is bounded by funding cost and leverage maintenance; the lesson transfers as: signal horizon should be long relative to entry noise, and funding carry is the explicit price of holding. Supports the design preference for slower, thesis-anchored experts over tick-noise signals.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Evaluation-frequency myopia
findings.mechanism: More frequent price observation degrades allocation decisions because recent losses loom larger (myopia amplifies loss aversion)
findings.setup_summary: Thaler experiment in the text: subjects shown high-frequency volatile returns allocated 40% to equities; subjects shown only 5-year periodic returns allocated ~70%, same underlying data. Lesson: evaluate performance on long windows and avoid reacting to short drawdown windows.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (evaluation methodology).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A.
findings.quote: The group that had been bombarded by lots of information... allocated only 40 percent of its money to the stock market; the group that received only periodic information allocated almost 70 percent of its portfolio to stocks.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11 The Psychology of Money (Overreaction Bias), pp. 184-185
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's frozen-OOS / long-window evaluation and no-wall-clock determinism: decisions about expert promotion/demotion must be made on the frozen long-window record, never on a live short drawdown. Counterweight against reacting to recent OOS underperformance with in-place parameter changes.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Risk as thesis failure, not price volatility
findings.mechanism: Risk is the possibility of harm from misjudging the value/thesis, not the volatility of the price; a price dip on an intact thesis reduces risk
findings.setup_summary: Risk-definition lesson: 'the academics' definition of risk' (volatility) is rejected; risk = possibility of harm, a function of misjudging the business/thesis plus uncontrollable effects. For V8: thesis-failure risk should govern invalidation, and volatility should not be the sole basis for risk gating or sizing.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (risk-definition framework).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A; conceptual. ATR-based stops remain execution tools, not the definition of risk.
findings.quote: Buffett has a different definition of risk: the possibility of harm. And that is a factor of the intrinsic value of the business, not the price behavior of the stock.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 10 Managing Your Portfolio (Buffett's View of Risk), pp. 165
findings.notes: Cautions against vol-normalized sizing or vol-only gating as the risk model: the operative risk in V8 is dead-thesis (still_valid) persistence. In perps the thesis anchor is thin (no intrinsic value), so thesis-failure risk concentrates in event/liquidity risk, which supports the existing regime and liquidation-aware risk rules.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Overconfidence as the source of excess counterparty flow
findings.mechanism: Overconfident participants trade too much on overstated certainty; their turnover is the inefficiency a disciplined process can harvest, and a standing warning against overconfidence in one's own results
findings.setup_summary: Book cites the classic overconfidence evidence (most people rate themselves above-average drivers; doctors claim 90% diagnostic confidence with ~50% accuracy) and concludes 'If all the players think that their information is correct... the result is a great deal of trading.' Discipline, not IQ, is the differentiator.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (market-structure/behavioral claim).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A.
findings.quote: If all the players think that their information is correct and they know something that others do not, the result is a great deal of trading.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 11 The Psychology of Money (Overconfidence), pp. 183-184
findings.notes: Two uses for V8: (1) a structural argument that a disciplined, non-participating system harvests the flow of overconfident retail (relevant to funding/flow harvesting on perps); (2) a program-level guard — treat frozen-OOS results with epistemic humility and require registry-gated replication before promotion.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Market quotes as opportunity screen, not signal source
findings.mechanism: The market exists only as a reference point to see if anyone is offering to do something foolish; decisions are anchored to the thesis, not to live price action
findings.setup_summary: Behavioral method: 'turn off the stock market' — check quotes periodically only to spot foolish offers, not to derive signals; 'After we buy a stock, we would not be disturbed if markets closed for a year or two.' For V8: entry logic should be anchored to pre-committed, state-frozen thesis conditions; no intra-episode re-optimization from live price movement.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (process discipline).
findings.risk_geometry: N/A.
findings.quote: The market is there only as a reference point to see if anybody is offering to do anything foolish.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 12 The Unreasonable Man (Step One: Turn Off the Stock Market), pp. 192-193
findings.notes: Supports V8's determinism rules: no wall clock, no live re-optimization, thesis invalidation only via pre-committed still_valid. In 24/7 perps this is doubly important because continuous quotes invite continuous re-deciding; the analog of 'checking periodically' is the frozen event/available/ingested clock discipline.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Fixed-risk (percent-of-equity) sizing normalized by stop distance
findings.mechanism: Sizing inversely proportional to per-trade stop distance equalizes dollar risk across all trades so no single trade dominates portfolio variance.
findings.setup_summary: Risk a fixed percent of current account equity on each signal: dollar risk = pct x equity, contracts = floor(dollar_risk / stop_distance_in_dollars). On the Donchian 56-commodity system 1980-2011, raising the percent risked from 1% to 4% scaled average annual return 90.6%->503.4% with max DD 39.8%->84.5%, and gain-to-pain rose monotonically (5.17->11.21). The large-account conclusion: fixed-risk sizing delivered nearly all the risk improvement, leaving little for other money-management overlays (5.17->5.37).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis fails if gain-to-pain does not rise monotonically with risked percent, or if per-trade risk is not actually equalized (e.g., sizing floor/granularity breaks on small accounts). Once sizing normalizes risk, entry-risk caps and open-risk caps become redundant (Ch.14 finding).
findings.risk_geometry: entry: per signal (Donchian breakout); stop: 3-standard-deviation volatility catastrophic stop (dollar risk = distance entry-to-stop x value); target: none stated here; fractions rounded down to whole contracts in the book.
findings.quote: a fixed percentage of equity is risked on each trade. It is implemented by multiplying the fixed percentage by account equity on the day of the trade to determine the dollar amount to be risked. Then, the strategy's trade risk is used to determine the number of contracts that should be traded.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.14 'Fixed-Risk Sizing', pp. 221-223, Tables 14.1, 14.10
findings.notes: Crypto perps permit fractional sizes, removing the book's whole-contract floor problem. V8 currently sizes to a fixed stop_r (1.0R) per Expert; this supports a variant where size = (pct x equity)/stop_distance so risk is equalized across BTC, ETH, and alt perps. Funding is not priced in the book's sizing and must be added to the perp cost model.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Limit trade risk on entry (high entry-risk bypass)
findings.mechanism: Bypassing entries whose initial stop distance exceeds a dollar cap keeps worst-case per-trade loss bounded and improves return-per-unit-risk in one-lot portfolios.
findings.setup_summary: On each signal compute dollar trade risk = distance(entry, catastrophic stop) x contract value; if it exceeds a fixed cap (e.g., $2,000), bypass the trade. On the 56-commodity one-lot system, a $2,000 cap raised gain-to-pain from 7.93 to 9.11 (15% improvement) while an overly tight $1,000 cap hurt (7.02). The effect vanishes under fixed-risk sizing (Ch.14: 5.35 vs 5.36 baseline) because a 10-lot at $2,000 risk equals a 5-lot at $4,000 risk.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The cap only helps when per-trade risk is NOT normalized by sizing. In a sized book it is redundant; in a one-lot/one-exposure book it acts as a volatility admission filter that should be re-validated per regime.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: bar close; stop: 3-SD volatility catastrophic stop (relative to recent volatility); bypass decision made at entry only; no expiry.
findings.quote: trades with a high trade risk are bypassed... bypassing trades with an initial stop greater than $2,000 away from the entry price increases the gain-to-pain ratio from the baseline 7.93 to 9.11, a 15 percent improvement.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.12 'Limit Trade Risk on Entry', pp. 195-197; Ch.14 pp. 224-226
findings.notes: BTCUSDT 1h ATR varies by an order of magnitude across regimes, so a per-entry risk cap in R or USD is implementable in RiskGate admission. The Ch.14 normalization caveat must be recorded: in a fixed-R, one-exposure-per-direction V8 book this caps to a volatility-regime filter rather than a sizing rule.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Limit open-trade risk (open-equity give-back cap, profit-taking exit)
findings.mechanism: Exiting when distance from current price to the stop reaches a dollar/percent threshold harvests the trade's peak-to-date profit, converting open give-back into realized equity.
findings.setup_summary: While a trade is open, monitor dollar open-trade risk = distance(current price, stop) x value; when it exceeds a threshold, exit the trade. On the 56-commodity system, exiting at >$6,000 open-trade risk beat no-exit (gain-to-pain 8.94 vs 7.93) but a tight >$4,000 cap hurt (6.66) - a U-shaped response. The percent-of-equity variant (Ch.14, capped at 8%-5% of equity) did not help the sized large-account system.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Tight caps destroy upside (book's own >$4,000 result) and the rule is redundant where profit targets already exist (Ch.15 stock system kept a '$300 scalping profit-target' and rejected both open-risk limits).
findings.risk_geometry: entry: as per base system; stop: catastrophic stop; exit: fixed dollar open-trade-risk threshold acting as profit-taking at peak-to-date profit; no expiry.
