findings.quote: This money management technique closes the trade when a certain dollar amount of open-trade risk is reached. Note that this can also be looked at as a form of profit-taking.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.12 'Limit Open-Trade Risk', pp. 196-197, Table 12.8; Ch.14 pp. 226-227
findings.notes: On perps there are no exchange gaps to absorb give-back and markets run 24/7, so open-equity give-back is real and measurable. In V8 taxonomy this is a THIRD exit type distinct from stops and dead-thesis (still_valid) - an episode-level give-back cap. Threshold must be frozen and is equity/leverage dependent.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: First-N-in-a-group correlated-exposure cap
findings.mechanism: Capping concurrent positions per correlated group prevents correlated losses from stacking into one drawdown event; group-capped diversification beats concentrating risk in fewer correlated instruments.
findings.setup_summary: Group instruments by pairwise correlation (book uses 0.40 as significant); allow at most N concurrent signals per group, bypassing the newest when the group is full. Adding second-tier commodities under first-in-a-group raised gain-to-pain from 4.09 to 5.17; trading one-lot of the augmented basket beat two-lots of the top-tier only (gain-to-pain 7.56 vs 4.09, max DD $17,180 vs $34,568). Large-account version: cap of 7 per group was the optimum (5.36 vs 5.32 baseline).
findings.trigger_invalidation: If correlation regimes shift (groups re-correlate in stress), a static group structure breaks; membership must be computed on frozen windows, not full-sample, or the cap misallocates.
findings.risk_geometry: portfolio-level bypass rule; no per-trade change.
findings.quote: It's better to diversify with second-tier commodities than to double-up on the top-tier set... the gain-to-pain ratio for the augmented portfolio is almost 85 percent higher than the baseline portfolio when trading two lots of the best commodities.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.12 'First-N-in-a-Group', pp. 193-196; Ch.14 pp. 224-225
findings.notes: BTC/ETH/alt perps are highly correlated and correlation spikes in stress (the 2008 analog the author describes in Ch.12). V8's one-exposure-per-(instrument,direction) is per-instrument; this extends it to per-correlated-group, a strictly stronger claim worth testing once cross_market feature data exists.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Short correlated-surrogate hedge overlay (beta hedge)
findings.mechanism: A short position in a highly correlated market proxy offsets the systematic beta component of a basket of longs, cutting drawdowns more than it cuts returns when the longs' edge is idiosyncratic.
findings.setup_summary: Against N long signals in a correlated basket, hold a fixed number of short positions in a market surrogate (SPY ETF). On the Nasdaq-100 Donchian long basket, 5 longs / 2 SPY shorts raised gain-to-pain 1.78->1.90 and cut max DD $7,520->$6,589; adding 'hedge on only when >=2 active basket trades' lifted it to 2.09. The hedge only pays because the basket longs compound ~1%/2 days while the surrogate declines only marginally.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The hedge must be gated on basket activity: when the 70-day trend filter collapses the basket to few trades the hedge bleeds (Ch.13). On perps, perpetual funding on the short leg is a recurring carry cost, and hedge beta must be re-estimated as basket composition changes.
findings.risk_geometry: hedge legs sized like longs ($5,000 each); fixed hedge count (e.g., 2); no stated stop on hedge; hedge removed when active basket trades < threshold.
findings.quote: let's try adding a downside hedge... sell short one or more $5,000 positions of a market surrogate like the exchange-traded fund (ETF) for S&P 500... with five longs and two shorts, profitability is reduced by about $450 per year, but average max draw-down and max draw-down are reduced even more.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.13 'Position Hedging', pp. 217-218, Tables 13.2-13.3; Ch.15 pp. 235
findings.notes: Natural perp analog: short BTCUSDT perp against a long basket of alt perps - directly executable with no borrow, but funding on the short leg erodes P&L and 24/7 trading means no overnight-gap protection benefit. Requires the cross_market feature group and a beta proxy series; gate hedge on active-exposure count per the book's finding.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Bundle uncorrelated strategies on combined equity
findings.mechanism: Combining strategies with low-correlated equity curves reduces portfolio drawdown more than it dilutes return because their loss events rarely coincide; diversification credit appears mainly as DD reduction, then as optional leverage.
findings.setup_summary: Run two structurally different strategies (short-term counter-trend Nasdaq scalper + mid-term commodity trend-follower) off one combined equity pot, each at half its standalone risk fraction. 2000-2011: combined gain-to-pain 4.25 vs 2.61 (stock alone) and 2.42 (commodity alone); average annual max DD 6.0% vs 9.0%/11.0%. Best allocation 0.45 commodity / 0.55 stock (4.29); a leverage multiplier 1.0-1.5 scales return 25.3%->39.2% at near-flat gain-to-pain (4.29->4.51).
findings.trigger_invalidation: If the two equity curves become highly correlated (regime convergence), the benefit disappears; the book conditions the edge on strategies being 'different enough' in equity-curve correlation, not just instruments.
findings.risk_geometry: each strategy keeps its own stops/targets; allocation weights sum to 1; optional global leverage multiplier on the fixed-risk base.
findings.quote: The key, of course, is that they need to be different - not necessarily in the instruments they trade, but different enough that the resultant equity curve is not highly correlated with the equity curves of your current systems.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.16 'Trading the Stock and Commodity Strategies Together', pp. 241-244
findings.notes: Direct implication for the registry: PROPOSED experts should be screened partly on equity-curve correlation to the 3 ACTIVE experts (max budget, rule 14), and combined-equity (not segregated) allocation halves each strategy's risk fraction. This is a portfolio-level methodology note, not a new Expert.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Cap concurrent open-trade count
findings.mechanism: Capping the number of concurrent positions bounds peak portfolio exposure; the benefit concentrates in drawdown control and only materializes for longer-holding systems with large open-equity give-back.
findings.setup_summary: When open trades reach a cap, bypass new signals until one closes. Commodity one-lot book: capping at 20 trades cut max start-trade DD monotonically ($64,996->$55,932) at gain-to-pain cost (7.93->6.83); large-account sized book: cap of 30 was marginal (5.37 vs 5.36); stock book: cap 45 best (2.80). The author notes clusters of many concurrent trades carry the biggest risk/reward, so aggressive caps forfeit reward.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Caps hurt when they bypass high-conviction cluster signals; the technique only helps strategies that hold longer with higher profit-per-trade and larger open give-back (Ch.14), and does little for fast scalpers.
findings.risk_geometry: portfolio-level admission bypass; no per-trade change.
findings.quote: the biggest risk/reward opportunities occur when you have a relatively large number of trades on... this money management tactic works best with longer-term trend-following strategies; those that hold trades longer and consequentially have a higher profit-per-trade as well as a larger open-equity give-back.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch.12 'Limit Total Number of Open Trades', p. 198, Table 12.10; Ch.14 pp. 226; Ch.15 pp. 234
findings.notes: V8's one-exposure-per-(instrument,direction) already caps per-instrument; an aggregate count/heat cap adds a portfolio bound. Because signal clustering in trending crypto regimes is common, a regime-dependent cap (higher cap in strong trend, lower in chop) is a falsifiable variant.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Correlated-pair divergence reversion (pairs trade)
findings.mechanism: When a persistently correlated pair diverges, short the rising leg and long the falling leg, betting on spread re-convergence; the pair's idiosyncratic spread has bounded variance, keeping risk small and market-neutral.
findings.setup_summary: Select pairs with average Pearson correlation > 0.40 over their lifetime from a liquid universe (~300 pairs from 1,300 stocks); on divergence, sell the rising member and buy the falling member; exit when the spread re-syncs. Development looked good but live trading was disappointing; redeveloped correctly (every pair ever-correlated during its lifetime, not only pairs correlated at sample end) the strategy was 'no longer tradeable'.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The book's own thesis-invalidation: full-sample pair selection is look-ahead curve-fitting - pairs that lost correlation wandered independently and produced mostly losers. Any V8 version must select pairs on frozen out-of-sample windows only.
findings.risk_geometry: entry: both legs market on divergence; exit: on re-convergence; no stated stop/target; author expects small risk from market-neutrality.
findings.quote: When the normally correlated pair started to diverge in price, I'd sell the one going up and buy the one going down, and then wait until they got in sync again and exit with a profit... the strategy was no longer tradeable.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix D 'Case 1: Stock Pairs Trading', pp. 273-274
findings.notes: Perps enable clean market-neutral pairs with no short-borrow, but funding on both legs is a carry cost and the selection-bias failure mode is directly reproducible on crypto (e.g., BTC-ETH or index-perp spreads). The primary transferable content is the selection-bias curve-fit lesson; gate any proposal on frozen-OOS pair selection.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Limit-order fill probability and slippage modeling
findings.mechanism: Backtests that assume every resting limit order fills at the limit when price trades through it overstate performance; real fills are partial (~8/10) and fill price is worse than the limit (slippage inside the limit-to-open range).
findings.setup_summary: A long-only stock system entered on pre-open limit orders; backtests kept everything that hit the limit on the open and randomly selected post-open fills. Live trading diverged immediately: only ~8 of 10 open fills (and missing fills were historically the better trades), and fills priced between the limit and the actual open rather than at the limit. 'The hypothetical performance numbers were astronomical.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: Applies only where limit entries exist; V8's canonical fill-at-close L1 is unaffected. If any Expert proposes resting-limit entries, the model must discount fill probability and price fills at worst-of(limit, touch).
findings.risk_geometry: n/a - methodology constraint on the simulator for any limit-entry variant.
findings.quote: My real trading didn't get all the trades that my hypotheticals said I should get on the open, even when price clearly traded below the limit order entry price. I got about 8 out of 10... I'd sometimes get the 99, but mostly I'd get somewhere between 99 and 100.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix D 'Case 2: Using Limit Orders on Daily-Bar Stock Data', pp. 274-275
findings.notes: BTC 1h candles routinely wick through levels, so intrabar limit-fill assumptions are the highest-risk fill modeling error. Record as a simulator constraint: keep canonical fill-at-close; if limit entries are ever added, model partial fills + inside-the-range slippage as a documented variant, never assume limit fills.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Closed-trade-only signal attribution (no open P/L look-ahead)
findings.mechanism: Using open-trade mark-to-market P/L in any scoring or feature feeding entries leaks information about trades already entered into future signals, inflating in-sample performance.
findings.setup_summary: Bar-scoring using average profit over the last 10 trades dramatically raised top-score profitability; the cause was that some of the last 10 trades were still open and their running daily P/L was fed into the scoring matrix. Restricting scoring to closed trades made the profit-per-trade criterion 'only marginal'. This is the book's canonical example of subtle look-ahead bias.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Any feature built from trade outcomes must use only closed, realized outcomes with full outcome lag; frozen-OOS evaluation must expose the inflated signal before live use.
findings.risk_geometry: n/a - methodology.
findings.quote: I was keeping the profit each day for the trades that hadn't closed out and these numbers were being used in the scoring matrices. They skewed the whole matrix... I fixed the problem by only using closed trades.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix D 'Case 3: Bar-Scoring Using Profit-per-Trade', pp. 275-276
findings.notes: Concrete instance of the look-ahead class V8's LEARNING_PROTOCOL forbids: outcome data must never mutate an active Expert, and no feature may incorporate open-trade P/L. Codifies a deterministic invariant for the lab/lifecycle: only closed-trade outcomes, lagged, may enter any state an Expert can read.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Directional-volatility measurement (close-SD vs average range/ATR)
findings.mechanism: Standard deviation of closes captures directional (trending) volatility that average range/ATR misses; two streams with identical average ranges can have very different SD, so volatility filters and stop distances must be computed on a measure matched to the intended risk.
findings.setup_summary: Given two 18-bar streams with identical high-low ranges each bar, one trending (closes drifting) and one ranging, average range is equal but SD of closes is far higher for the trending stream. The book's catastrophic stops are 3-SD of closing price (not ATR), and the author 'always checks both measures' when using a volatility filter; he also notes the 40-day SD of closes varies within a commodity by an order of magnitude (e.g., Nasdaq 100 from $1,140 to $46,500), which is why stops must be relative to recent volatility.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Switching volatility measures changes stop-distance distributions; any change must be a frozen, audited feature-group decision and re-validated OOS.
findings.risk_geometry: feeds stop placement: stops relative to recent volatility; book's canonical catastrophic stop = 3 SD of closing price.
findings.quote: standard deviation accounts for directional volatility, while average range doesn't... I always check both measures when I use a volatility filter.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix A 'Volatility Measures and Comparison', pp. 246-247; Appendix B 'Relative Contract Risk', pp. 252-255
findings.notes: V8's atr_ref uses ATR (non-directional); this supports adding a close-SD-over-window volatility feature to audit whether directional-volatility regimes (trend segments) behave differently for stop placement. Adding a feature-group member is a frozen-spec, audited change per D-031/D-032.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Leverage to drawdown tolerance, not margin adequacy
findings.mechanism: Exchange margin is a lagging indicator of risk - raised only after volatility has already hurt the account; sizing should target a maximum drawdown the trader can sustain, because fully-leveraged positions can lose more than account equity.
findings.setup_summary: Fully-margined commodity positions can wipe an account: with $1,000 equity controlling two fully-margined corn contracts, a $0.15 adverse move turns the account into a $500 debit. Experienced traders ignore margin and size by fixed-risk percent so expected max DD stays inside personal tolerance; risked-per-trade 0.25%->1% scales max DD 11.8%->37.4% (Ch.14 Table 14.10). The book's cautions: only a small fraction of traders can sit through a 40-50% drawdown, and margin changes always arrive after the volatility.
findings.trigger_invalidation: In high-leverage perps, liquidation and funding make the book's 'many adverse trades from a margin call' buffer much thinner; a sizing rule anchored only to margin/liquidation distance is insufficient - it must be anchored to a tolerable max-DD percentile.
findings.risk_geometry: leverage multiplier scaled to DD tolerance; fixed-risk percent x equity / stop distance defines size.
findings.quote: Most experienced commodity traders don't even consider margin requirements when trading. Their money management considers risk from a draw-down probability standpoint, and they leverage to experience draw-downs within their personal risk tolerance, not to margin requirements... Margin requirements are no help because they are a lagging indicator of risk.
findings.chapter_anchor: Appendix B 'Margin', pp. 262-263; Ch.14 Table 14.10, p. 230
findings.notes: Perps offer 20-125x leverage with instantaneous liquidation and deleveraging cascades, so anchoring risk sizing to a sustainable max-DD budget (per-trade risk fraction + heat cap) rather than liquidation distance is directly actionable and consistent with V8's deterministic RiskGate and NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM stance.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

book_title: Building Reliable Trading Systems: Tradable Strategies That Perform as They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals (Keith Fitschen, 2013)

findings.strategy_name: Margin of safety asymmetry gate
findings.mechanism: requiring a large discount between price and independently-estimated value buffers the entry against estimation error and adverse value moves
findings.setup_summary: Before any entry, form an independent estimate of expected value and require the entry price to clear a minimum discount (roughly 25-33%) to that estimate; the setup must remain adequate even if the estimate subsequently declines by ~10%. Operates as a pre-entry admission gate overlaid on any candidate setup, not as a standalone signal.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: candidate setup where entry price is at least ~25% below (long) / above (short) the value or edge estimate. Thesis-invalidation: the discount compresses below threshold before entry, or the value estimate itself deteriorates by more than the buffer.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at bar close once the discount threshold is met; book gives no explicit stop/target - the margin buffer substitutes for a stop (a 25% discount survives a 10% adverse value move); holding horizon is long-term, not bar-based.
findings.quote: There are two rules of investing, said Graham. The first rule is don't lose. The second rule is don't forget rule number one.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 2 'The Education of Warren Buffett' (margin-of-safety doctrine, p.14-15); Ch 8 'Value Tenets' (75%/-10% example, p.131)
findings.notes: Transfers to perp crypto as a reward:risk admission gate (e.g., require minimum expected edge above funding + fees), since BTC perp has no definable intrinsic value; the 25%-discount/10%-value-decline logic is a directly falsifiable asymmetry requirement. Corroborates the margin-of-safety concept across the value-investing library.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Fear-collapse quality-asset buy (capitulation)
findings.mechanism: fear-driven selling overshoots intrinsic value on intact assets, and the correction of that misappraisal delivers the return
findings.setup_summary: After a severe fear-driven collapse in which a fundamentally intact asset loses a large fraction of its value while the crowd extrapolates zero (GEICO -97% from $61 to $2; Wells Fargo down ~49% in a year on a regional real-estate panic), buy in size and accumulate over months-to-years. The market has misappraised the asset, not the business.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: extreme price collapse combined with economics that are intact (temporary problem, not structural). Invalidation: the intact-economics premise is disproven (Fruit of the Loom-style structural decline, GEICO's near-bankruptcy from reserve mispricing), or the discount to assessed value is never achieved.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at market during depressed conditions, accumulated over years (GEICO bought over five years, Washington Post over 1973); no bar-level stop or target; exit = value realization; Buffett: 'a year like that... would not distress us.'
findings.quote: Great investment opportunities come around when excellent companies are surrounded by unusual circumstances that cause the stock to be misappraised.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8 'Value Tenets' (quote p.131); Ch 3 GEICO (p.32); Ch 4 Wells Fargo (p.57-58); Ch 1 American Express (p.3)
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's DATA_BLOCKED capitulation family (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion, requires trend,volatility,history). In 24/7 perp crypto the 'temporary problem' filter is critical: deleveraging cascades produce many cheap-but-broken assets, and V8's tape cannot directly measure fundamental intactness - the main transferable observable is fear-extreme overshoot followed by reclaim.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Avoid turnarounds / severe structural change
findings.mechanism: assets undergoing major restructuring or directional change carry a high probability of major errors, so the expected return of such trades is impaired
findings.setup_summary: Do not initiate positions in assets undergoing fundamental restructuring, turnaround, or major change; 'severe change and exceptional returns usually don't mix.' Prefer unchanged, consistent assets ('very much profiting from lack of change'). This rule constrains contrarian entries to temporary setbacks only and excludes broken or regime-changing assets from the universe.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger for avoidance: announced restructuring, turnaround, hostile-change, or structural regime shift in the candidate. Invalidation of the avoidance: the change completes and a consistent post-change track record re-establishes the asset as eligible.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry by construction - acts as a pre-filter on the candidate universe; substitutes 'one-foot hurdles' selection over 'seven-footers' (no stop needed because the trade is never taken).
findings.quote: Severe change and exceptional returns usually don't mix.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 5 'Business Tenets' (p.68, 'turnarounds seldom turn' p.67); Ch 3 textile turnaround lesson (p.30)
findings.notes: For perp crypto: avoid catching falling knives in assets with structural breaks (chain hard-forks, regulatory bans, stablecoin de-pegs, exchange collapses). Complements the capitulation family by excluding broken assets - the two rules together define which fear-collapses are buyable. Buffett's Berkshire textile experience (closed 1985) is the canonical failure case.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Institutional imperative / crowd-imitation avoidance
findings.mechanism: crowd beliefs are not evidence - herding transfers the errors of the many to the follower, and contrarian conviction is only right when data and reasoning, not agreement, justify it
findings.setup_summary: A trade thesis that depends on the continuation of a widely-shared crowd belief is suspect. Thirty-seven failed investment-banking firms were run by hard-working, high-IQ people undone by 'mindless imitation of their peers.' Before entry, verify with independent data and reasoning; 'you are right because your data and reasoning are right,' not because the crowd agrees.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: thesis relies on crowd consensus continuation (e.g., entry only justified if 'everyone keeps buying'). Invalidation: objective crowding measures show the position is not actually crowded, or independent data confirms the consensus.
findings.risk_geometry: None - decision-process rule applied before entry; feeds thesis design, not entry/stop arithmetic.
findings.quote: How could they get a result like that? I'll tell you how... mindless imitation of their peers.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'Management Tenets' - institutional imperative (p.96-99); Ch 2 Graham on fear/greed mispricing (p.16)
findings.notes: Directly relevant to perp crypto where crowding is extreme and measurable via funding rate, open interest, and long/short ratios; can inform a crowding filter (participation feature group) or a lifecycle rule, and justifies contrarian families whose edge comes from herding-driven overshoot.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Consistent operating history as regime filter
findings.mechanism: a long steady track record of the same behavior is a relatively reliable predictor that the behavior continues, while discontinuous change destroys predictive confidence
findings.setup_summary: Admit only instruments/regimes with a long, consistent record of the same behavior; a steady record is a relatively reliable predictor that results continue. Buffett evaluates four-to-five-year averages rather than single years, and excludes assets whose plans failed and who are fundamentally changing direction.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: candidate passes the consistency test (same behavior, comparable results, over a multi-year lookback). Invalidation: behavioral discontinuity or structural change breaks the record; single-year noise should not trigger exclusion.
findings.risk_geometry: None - regime/selection filter applied before setup evaluation; lookback in years, not bars.
findings.quote: very much profiting from lack of change. That's the kind of business I like.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 5 'Business Tenets' - Consistency section (p.67-70); Ch 7 (four-to-five-year averages, p.109)
findings.notes: For perp: BTC/USDT regime consistency (persistence of trend/volatility characteristics over multi-year windows) can gate which behavior families are admitted per window; aligns with V8's frozen-OOS methodology and the regime_filter starter id, and with Buffett's 'consistent operating history' tenet.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Focus investing / conviction-scaled big bets
findings.mechanism: concentrating capital into a few high-probability bets, sized by conviction, beats thin diversification because it forces deeper research and lets the highest-conviction edge carry the portfolio
findings.setup_summary: Concentrate rather than diversify thinly: Berkshire put 35% of its common-stock portfolio into Coca-Cola and 40% of the partnership's assets into American Express; more than 75% of holdings are often in five securities. Scale position size up when the probability of success is assessed very high, and down when unsure. Fisher: too many baskets make it impossible to watch all the eggs.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: probability of success assessed at the top of the conviction range. Invalidation: new adverse evidence drops conviction, or the thesis breaks - then exit/trim regardless of price.
findings.risk_geometry: No fixed stop/target; size = f(conviction); entry at attractive price; long holding horizon; concentration is a research-quality mechanism, not a leverage mechanism.
findings.quote: When the probabilities of success are very high, make a big bet.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8 'Value Tenets' - Coca-Cola at 35% of portfolio (p.135); Ch 1 American Express 40% (p.3); Ch 2 Fisher focus (p.19)
findings.notes: For V8: exposure per family/instrument could scale with frozen-OOS evidence strength rather than equal-weight. Caution - interacts with rule 16 (one exposure per instrument-direction) and the heat cap; the lesson is concentration on thesis quality, not leverage. Buffett: 'twelve investments decisions in his forty year career have made all the difference.'
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Leverage avoidance / heat cap
findings.mechanism: leverage converts ordinary drawdowns into ruin - highly leveraged positions are vulnerable during economic slowdowns, so unleveraged sizing is what makes returns survivable
findings.setup_summary: Do not use leverage to manufacture returns: 'good business or investment decisions will produce quite satisfactory economic results with no aid from leverage,' and highly leveraged entities are vulnerable during economic slowdowns. Standing rule: position size must be survivable without liquidation under adverse conditions, with a heat cap.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rule violation (rejection trigger): any position whose survival depends on leverage beyond what the thesis needs, or aggregate heat above the cap. Invalidation: none - standing admission rule.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry mechanics; constrains size so stop and heat levels are reachable without forced liquidation; 'vulnerable during economic slowdowns' maps to deleveraging-cascade regimes.
findings.quote: Good business or investment decisions will produce quite satisfactory economic results with no aid from leverage. Furthermore, highly leveraged companies are vulnerable during economic slowdowns.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 7 'Financial Tenets' - return on equity without debt (p.110-111)
findings.notes: Directly corroborates V8's heat cap and RiskGate: on 24/7 perp with 100x+ available leverage this is the single most transferable risk rule; also connects to the deleveraging_cascade starter id, since leveraged vulnerability is the mechanism of liquidation cascades.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Float economics / being paid to hold (funding carry)
findings.mechanism: when the cost of holding capital is zero or negative - premiums exceed payouts - the holder is literally paid to hold, so carry turns a hold position into a positive-yield position
findings.setup_summary: Insurers win when the cost of float is zero or negative; Berkshire's reinsurance group ran a negative 3% cost of float in 2003 (underwriting gain > $1B). Applied to perp: enter/hold positions only when expected edge clears funding + fees; when funding strongly favors the position side, carrying is itself a positive yield. Never 'write dumb policies' (negative-EV trades taken just to stay active).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: funding rate pays the position side and expected price move clears remaining costs. Invalidation: funding flips or carrying costs exceed edge - exit or refuse the position.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry only if edge > funding + fee; holding favored while being paid; exit when carry turns negative relative to edge; no bar-level stop stated.
findings.quote: The insurer is literally being paid to hold the capital.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3 'Our Main Business Is Insurance' - float economics (p.35-37); 'dumb insurance policies' quote (p.38)
findings.notes: Unique perp-crypto transfer: the funding rate is the direct analog of float cost. Two V8 landings: (1) funding as a mandatory cost in the simulator cost model and as a feature-group input (flow/time), and (2) funding-tailwind holding as a carry-family backlog candidate. Caution: funding is a small term vs. 1h price risk.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Probability-weighted worst-case scenario analysis
findings.mechanism: enumerating the specific scenarios that would ruin a position and requiring the worst plausible case to be survivable at the entry price is how risk gets priced into the trade
findings.setup_summary: Before entry, enumerate the 3-5 specific scenarios that could ruin the position, assign probabilities, and verify the worst plausible case is survivable and that the entry price compensates. Wells Fargo: even if 10% of all loans (not just real estate) became problem loans at 30% loss severity, the bank still broke even - so the position was survivable.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: all enumerated catastrophic scenarios are rated low-probability AND survivable at the current price. Invalidation: any plausible scenario breaches the survivability threshold, or the probability of a ruin scenario is not negligible.
findings.risk_geometry: No fixed stop; a survivability buffer substitutes for a stop in the worst case; entry price must compensate for weighted risk; 'A year like that - which we consider only a low-level possibility, not a likelihood - would not distress us.'
findings.quote: Consider some mathematics... If 10 percent of the bank's $48 billion in loans... were problem loans in 1991 and produced losses, including interest, averaging 30 percent of the principal value of the loan, Wells Fargo would still break even.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8 'Value Tenets' - Wells Fargo risk analysis (p.129-130)
findings.notes: For perp: the scenario library should include liquidation cascade, funding blowout, exchange/wallet risk, flash-move slippage (no exchange gaps but fast wicks), and correlated-asset cascade; pairs with the max_drawdown_cap and correlated_exposure_cap starter ids.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Circle of competence universe restriction
findings.mechanism: investing outside the boundary of understood mechanisms makes it impossible to interpret developments and therefore impossible to decide wisely, so the defined boundary itself is the edge
findings.setup_summary: Only trade instruments and setups whose mechanism you fully understand, and define the boundary explicitly: 'it's not how big the circle is that counts, it's how well you define the parameters.' Buffett passes on Microsoft/tech not because it is unprofitable but because he cannot project its cash flows; success is doing very few things right while avoiding big mistakes.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: the setup is inside the defined competence boundary. Invalidation: a new mechanism/industry is traded before the understanding is developed, or the boundary is left undefined.
findings.risk_geometry: None - universe filter applied before any setup evaluation; 'An investor needs to do very few things right as long as he or she avoids big mistakes.'
findings.quote: Invest within your circle of competence. It's not how big the circle is that counts, it's how well you define the parameters.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 5 'Business Tenets' - simple and understandable business (p.63-64)
findings.notes: Maps directly to V8's expert ontology: an Expert is one falsifiable hypothesis about one understood behavior family; the circle-of-competence discipline justifies the cap on active experts and the registry gate (rules 6, 14).
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Buyer's strike / no-trade is a position
findings.mechanism: inactivity is itself a decision with a positive expected value when no candidate clears the required threshold - holding capital beats doing something stupid
findings.setup_summary: When no asset clears the required discount, do nothing: Buffett's multi-year inactivity ('buyer's strike' in the late 1990s-2000s) was a decision, not a miss. Underutilized capital is 'a painful condition to be in but not as painful as doing something stupid.' The default state is no-position, and the strike lifts only on price.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: no candidate passes the value/edge threshold (no-trade state). Invalidation: a qualified setup appears - the strike lifts only when the discount is achieved.
findings.risk_geometry: None - inactivity rule; keeps dry powder; reinforces that the market 'is there to serve you, not instruct you.'
findings.quote: Our capital is underutilized now. It is a painful condition to be in but not as painful as doing something stupid. (I speak from experience.)
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 9 'Investing in Fixed-Income Securities' - 2003 letter (p.142); Ch 1 buyer's strike (p.7-8)
findings.notes: Aligns with V8's evidence-bound posture and no-trade baseline: candidate episodes that fail admission should not be forced into activity; also argues for low-trade-frequency expectations in backtests and guards against overfitting to activity.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

findings.strategy_name: Share repurchase below value as accumulation signal
findings.mechanism: when an issuer repurchases its own securities below intrinsic value, each dollar spent buys more than a dollar of intrinsic value, creating value for remaining holders and signaling rational capital allocation
findings.setup_summary: When an issuer repurchases its own securities at a price below assessed intrinsic value, accumulate alongside: each repurchase acquires more intrinsic value per dollar spent and signals management rationality. Coca-Cola repurchased 32% of shares outstanding (since 1984) at an average $12.46 - worth ~$60B a decade later; the Washington Post repurchased 43% of its shares at an average $60.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: buyback program announced/executed below assessed intrinsic value. Invalidation: repurchase above value (destroys value per dollar), or the repurchase is financing-constrained (Fruit of the Loom-style over-leverage, 128% debt/equity).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at or below the repurchase price; no stop/target; hold through value realization; horizon is years.
findings.quote: If a company's stock price is $50 and its intrinsic value is $100, then each time management buys its stock, they are acquiring $2 of intrinsic value for every $1 spent.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'Management Tenets' - rationality / share repurchase (p.89-92); Coca-Cola buyback (p.90)
findings.notes: Crypto analog is token buyback-and-burn / treasury repurchases below fair value as a supply-flow signal. DEFER_GATED because V8's tape lacks on-chain supply-flow data; would enter via a flow feature group (with cross_market) only if on-chain data is added to the pipeline.
findings.book: The Warren Buffett Way 2nd edition 2005

book_title: The Warren Buffett Way (2nd Edition, 2005)

findings.strategy_name: Frictional cost drag
findings.mechanism: active turnover silently taxes returns via spreads, commissions and fees; aggregate investor returns equal business gains minus marketplace-imposed costs, so a hyperactive market is a pickpocket of the patient
findings.setup_summary: Any strategy's live return equals gross backtest return minus per-unit costs (taker fee, funding, slippage) times turnover. Rule: before any family is promoted it must clear a cost hurdle computed as (fee + funding + slippage) x expected turnover; high-turnover families must show edge several multiples of per-unit cost. Falsifiable in V8 by charging full Binance USDM fees plus funding on every fill and re-evaluating frozen OOS.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If an expert's OOS edge collapses to at-or-below its measured cost burden, the family is cost-drag-bound and must be gated or rejected.
findings.risk_geometry: Not an entry geometry; cost accounting applied at fill: taker fee + funding accrual + slippage over the L1 fill-at-close model.
findings.quote: the aggregate pre-tax rewards to our owners will equal the business gains achieved by the company less the transaction costs imposed by the marketplace—that is, commissions charged by brokers plus the net realized spreads of market-makers
findings.chapter_anchor: Part III.A The Bane of Trading: Transaction Costs (1988), pp. 119-121
findings.notes: Crypto perps are the worst-case environment for this: taker fees, 8h funding and slippage compound over 24/7 turnover. Directly corroborates V8's Binance USDM cost model and the 'hyperactive stock market is the pickpocket of enterprise' warning (p. 129).
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Forced-selling cascade exhaustion
findings.mechanism: mechanical stop-losses and forced liquidation selling beget further selling; once the forced-seller population is exhausted, the non-leveraged patient side can buy the dislocation
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: a sharp collapse amplified by forced selling (liquidation cascade - OI purge, forced-long liquidation spike, price sweeping a cluster of prior stops) followed by a bar-close reclaim back above the cascade extreme = long setup. The buyer who is not forced to sell can wait out the volatility.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis is that the decline was forced-selling-driven, not structural. Invalidated if price keeps printing new cascade lows with fresh liquidation waves (secular decline, not exhaustion) - ties to the value-trap rule.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on bar close reclaim of the cascade low; stop below cascade extreme (swing/ATR); target prior congestion; expiry in bars; dead-thesis if new cascade lows.
findings.quote: this strategy—which is simply an exotically-labeled version of the small speculator's stop-loss order—dictates that ever-increasing portions of a stock portfolio, or their index-future equivalents, be sold as prices decline
findings.chapter_anchor: Part II.C Debunking Standard Dogma (1987), pp. 81-82 (portfolio insurance / Brady Report $60-90B on a hair trigger)
findings.notes: Refines the DATA_BLOCKED capitulation backlog family: distinguishes forced-selling exhaustion from secular decline. Perp-specific: no circuit breakers, 24/7, liquidation engines, and high leverage guarantee forced sellers exist on every crash.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Survive-to-finish leverage cap
findings.mechanism: a small probability of forced distress or ruin is never acceptable regardless of expected upside; size so the worst case cannot force liquidation
findings.setup_summary: Standing RiskGate rule: reject any exposure whose sizing implies non-trivial probability of forced liquidation or breach of the drawdown cap under historical worst-case adverse excursions. In perp terms: notional must be sized so a worst-case cascade flush (multi-ATR) does not liquidate or breach the heat cap; no expected-value maximization that risks ruin (the book explicitly rejects 99:1 leverage odds).
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - standing gate, not an episodic setup.
findings.risk_geometry: Sizing rule: notional bounded by drawdown/ruin tolerance, not by expected value; one exposure per instrument-direction; heat cap.
findings.quote: A small chance of distress or disgrace cannot, in our view, be offset by a large chance of extra returns.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part II.F Cigar Butts and the Institutional Imperative (1989), pp. 96-97; cf. Owner-Related Principle 7, pp. 34-35 ('To finish first, you must first finish')
findings.notes: Perps offer extreme leverage and 24/7 liquidation; a 99:1 expected-value trade still loses the account if the 1% is a liquidation cascade. Corroborates V8's heat cap and ONE exposure per (instrument, direction).
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Cheapness/value-trap rejection
findings.mechanism: cheapness relative to recent history is not a reversal trigger; in a structurally deteriorating asset one problem surfaces after another, eroding any initial discount
findings.setup_summary: Standing rule: an entry triggered mainly by 'price is cheap vs its own recent range/history' (deep drawdown from highs, oversold oscillator, large discount to a slow anchor) is rejected unless an independent structural-reversal condition is present. Perp crypto analog: structurally declining assets (persistent lower highs, net outflows, weakening funding) that look 'cheap' keep printing lower lows.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (standing rule). A long is only admitted with a separate reversal thesis (e.g., forced-selling exhaustion), never on cheapness alone.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry refused on cheapness-only signal; if admitted via another thesis, stop at structure, modest R target, short expiry.
findings.quote: In a difficult business, no sooner is one problem solved than another surfaces—never is there just one cockroach in the kitchen.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part II.F Cigar Butts and the Institutional Imperative (1989), pp. 93-95
findings.notes: Crypto is full of chronically 'cheap' assets that keep declining (structural dilution, fading usage). Guards the capitulation family: only exhaustion, not cheapness, is the trigger. SHORT-side implication: persistent structural decline is a valid short thesis even when the asset 'looks cheap'.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Fear/greed sentiment extreme
findings.mechanism: emotional extremes (fear/greed) push prices far from any fair anchor; the patient side enters against the emotional crowd
findings.setup_summary: When measurable crowd sentiment reaches an extreme (perp funding rate at extreme percentile, long/short ratio, OI/participation blow-offs), price is dislocated and mean-reverts as the emotion fades; multi-day/multi-week horizon on BTCUSDT 1h. Requires a value/anchor estimate to distinguish dislocation from trend.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Extreme alone is insufficient - without an anchor, extremes can persist. Invalidated if the dislocation is fundamentals-driven rather than sentiment-driven.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on exhaustion signals at the extreme (bar close after a vertical move, funding blow-off); stop beyond the extreme; target reversion to slow anchor; long expiry (bars-to-days).
findings.quote: we simply attempt to be fearful when others are greedy and to be greedy only when others are fearful.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part III opening (1986), pp. 118-119; Part II.A Mr. Market (1987), pp. 64-65
findings.notes: Buffett's version needs an intrinsic-value anchor that perp price data does not have; candidate proxies are funding-rate / OI / long-short positioning (feature groups flow, participation). Backlog until sentiment-derived features exist. Reversion-to-value is NOT price mean-reversion.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Loss-based risk measurement
findings.mechanism: risk is the possibility of loss, not price volatility; volatility/beta-style measures mis-rank assets and mis-measure strategy risk
findings.setup_summary: Methodology rule: V8 risk evaluation must use loss-based quantities (per-episode drawdown, probability of hitting stop, expected adverse excursion) rather than price volatility as the primary risk metric. A strategy that lost money is 'riskier' at the lower equity level, not safer; beta-like metrics cannot distinguish a structurally declining asset from a stable one.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (methodology).
findings.risk_geometry: Risk gates expressed in R-units and drawdown, not vol-normalized metrics; stops and dead-thesis exits remain the risk surface.
findings.quote: It is better to be approximately right than precisely wrong.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part II.C Debunking Standard Dogma (1993), pp. 75-77; 'equating beta with investment risk makes no sense' p. 78
findings.notes: Perp crypto is high-vol by construction; vol-based risk measures would drown in noise. Loss/ruin framing matches V8's stop, dead-thesis (still_valid) and per-episode R accounting.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Probability-weighted event evaluation
findings.mechanism: only trade events with publicly announced outcomes, sized by P(event) x payoff vs (1-P(event)) x loss plus time cost
findings.setup_summary: Pre-trade checklist for any announced-outcome event: (1) probability the event occurs, (2) time funds are tied up, (3) upside if something better transpires, (4) downside if the event fails. Take only where probability-weighted gain clearly exceeds weighted loss plus opportunity cost; participate only in publicly-announced events, never rumor.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Abstain/exit when terms change, financing falls through, or the re-estimated probability drops below the required edge.
findings.risk_geometry: Few large positions with wide diversification across mutually-independent events; never one huge bet ('refuse to accept a single, huge bet' - roulette-wheel outlook, p. 79).
findings.quote: To evaluate arbitrage situations you must answer four questions: (1) How likely is it that the promised event will indeed occur? (2) How long will your money be tied up? (3) What chance is there that something still better will transpire—a competing takeover bid, for example? and (4) What will happen if the event does not take place because of anti-trust action, financing glitches, etc.?
findings.chapter_anchor: Part II.B Arbitrage (1988), pp. 66-73
findings.notes: Perps have no announced-price merger spreads; nearest analogs (listings, unlocks, halvings, governance) lack a fixed spread to capture, so direct applicability is LOW. The four-question probability-weighted framework is still the correct pre-trade evaluation template. The 63-year ~20%/yr record with stated fair-test conditions (pp. 72-73) is the book's closest empirical claim.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Focused high-conviction concentration
findings.mechanism: concentration reduces risk when it raises analysis intensity and conviction thresholds; over-diversification spreads thinking thin and multiplies per-trade costs
findings.setup_summary: Portfolio/expert design rule: maintain a small number of high-conviction, deeply-understood exposures rather than broad diversification; add capital to top-conviction setups instead of the 20th-best idea. Corroborates V8's max-3-active-experts complexity budget, the registry experiment path, and one-exposure-per-direction.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A.
findings.risk_geometry: Few positions, large size per conviction, long holding, no forced churn.
findings.quote: a policy of portfolio concentration may well decrease risk if it raises, as it should, both the intensity with which an investor thinks about a business and the comfort-level he must feel with its economic characteristics before buying into it.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part II.C Debunking Standard Dogma (1993), p. 75; Keynes 'few enterprises' letter, p. 81
findings.notes: Conflicts with the statistical-power needs of backtesting (few families = few episodes); for V8 the lesson supports the deliberately narrow expert set rather than diversification-driven family proliferation. Note: arbitrage is the exception requiring wide diversification (p. 78-79).
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Margin-of-safety entry threshold
findings.mechanism: only act when price offers substantial expected value over cost; a marginal edge is not worth the exposure
findings.setup_summary: Standing admission rule: an expert emits a CandidateDraft only when expected edge (probability-weighted payoff minus all costs including funding and fees) exceeds a required margin multiple, e.g. EV >= 2x per-unit cost; setups whose edge barely clears cost are skipped. Raises the bar as costs rise.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A (standing threshold); a trade that is only 'slightly better than cost' is rejected by construction.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry only at prices giving margin; a geometry whose wider stop / tighter target shrinks margin below the threshold is rejected.
findings.quote: If we calculate the value of a common stock to be only slightly higher than its price, we're not interested in buying. We believe this margin-of-safety principle... to be the cornerstone of investment success.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part II.D 'Value' Investing: A Redundancy (1992), p. 87; cf. Junk Bonds p. 101 ('Margin of Safety' as the three-word secret)
findings.notes: Without an intrinsic-value anchor, margin-of-safety becomes a required edge-over-cost multiple - which binds strongly in perps given funding and taker fees.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Institutional herding and signal crowding
findings.mechanism: organizations mindlessly imitate peers; individually rational actions neutralize collectively, so crowded strategies self-erode and herd behavior creates synchronous exits
findings.setup_summary: Methodology warning: a signal's edge decays as adoption spreads; backtests on already-crowded signals are suspect, and synchronous crowd exits (stops clustered at common levels) amplify drawdowns. V8 should track crowding proxies (OI positioning, funding, perp-vs-spot flow) for its own families and prefer uncrowded triggers.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A.
findings.risk_geometry: Extreme crowd alignment is itself a warning (see sentiment_extreme); avoid stop placement at the obvious shared level.
findings.quote: The behavior of peer companies, whether they are expanding, acquiring, setting executive compensation or whatever, will be mindlessly imitated.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part II.F Cigar Butts and the Institutional Imperative (1989), pp. 95-96; toe-stand parable, Part I.C pp. 45-46
findings.notes: Crypto signals crowd within weeks (copy-trading, groupchats, fund flows). The textile toe-stand ('individually rational, collectively irrational' capital spending, p. 46) is the alpha-decay parable for the quant arms race.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Capital-retention value test
findings.mechanism: retained capital must create at least $1 of value per $1 retained or be returned; capital that cannot clear the bar is misallocated
findings.setup_summary: Lifecycle rule: each active expert/parameter variant must demonstrate, on frozen OOS, that deployed capital (per-episode R after funding and fees) returns at least $1 of value per $1 of exposure cost, evaluated on a rolling window; otherwise the variant is deactivated and capital returned to the pool. Mirrors V8's registry gating (PROPOSED -> FORMALIZED -> SCREENING -> REPLICATION -> SHADOW -> PROMOTED).
findings.trigger_invalidation: A variant fails when its OOS per-episode net value is below the cost of the capital it retains, sustained over the rolling window.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A (capital allocation, not entries).
findings.quote: We test the wisdom of retaining earnings by assessing whether retention, over time, delivers shareholders at least $1 of market value for each $1 retained.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part I.A Owner-Related Business Principles #9 (1996), p. 35; cf. Dividend Policy (1984), pp. 124-126
findings.notes: Also warns against 'core-business camouflage' (p. 126): a star family's wins can hide persistent losers elsewhere, so per-family P&L must be evaluated separately - which V8's one-file-per-family layout already enables.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Commodity-market edge structure
findings.mechanism: in a commodity market no participant is much smarter than the dumbest competitor; returns are set by cost structure and patience, not analysis brilliance
findings.setup_summary: Methodology lesson: BTCUSDT perps are the most commoditized market on earth, so price-superiority ('smarter' analysis) is not a durable edge. Edge must come from structure: lower costs (fee/funding discipline, maker execution), asymmetry (sizing, forced-selling exploitation), and patience (not being forced to sell). Falsifiable: experts whose edge claim rests on analysis superiority alone should be gated; structure-based edges prioritized.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A.
findings.risk_geometry: Cost discipline: maker/rebate execution, funding-timing; avoid being the counterparty with the highest cost.
findings.quote: In a business selling a commodity-type product, it's impossible to be a lot smarter than your dumbest competitor.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part II.I Preferred Stock (1994), p. 115 (USAir); cf. Part I.C Plant Closings, p. 46 (Burlington $3B capex, stock flat over 20 years)
findings.notes: Corollary of the same essay: capital-reinvestment races in commodity markets neutralize everyone (airline/textile examples) - the quant arms race in crypto means V8's edge must be cost/risk-structural, not informational.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

book_title: The Essays of Warren Buffett: Lessons for Corporate America (1998), Part 1
Building Reliable Trading Systems: Tradable Strategies That Perform as They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals (Keith Fitschen, 2013) — Part 1 of 2

findings.strategy_name: Donchian channel breakout trend-following (20-bar)
findings.mechanism: trend persistence after channel breakout; entry at channel extreme gives momentum continuation with long-side profit 2-3x short side
findings.setup_summary: Go long when price exceeds the highest close of the previous 20 bars; short when price breaks below the lowest close of the previous 20 bars; entry on a stop order at the breakout level; reversal exit when the opposite extreme is broken. On BTCUSDT 1h this maps to a 20-bar channel close breakout with reversal exit.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close above prior 20-bar highest close (long) / below prior 20-bar lowest close (short). Thesis invalidates if the longer-term trend filter (close vs close ~200 bars ago) no longer agrees with the entry direction.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on stop order at channel extreme; 3x 20-day standard-deviation catastrophic stop (avg ~$1,910/contract) triggered on close with exit next open; reversal exit otherwise; no time stop (trends have no time constraint).
findings.quote: Long entry: If flat or short, and trading exceeds the highest close of the previous x days, then exit the short position and go long. Entry is on a stop order.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 5, Trading System Elements: Exits (Commodity Example)
findings.notes: The book's entry-power analysis (Ch. 4) ranks Donchian and standard-deviation breakouts as the two best trend entries across 56 commodities, with profit push and persistence proportional to lookback. Long trades earned ~2x short profit-per-trade ($514 vs $250) - a long bias V8 must re-test on BTC (funding can flip this). Distinct from V8's backlogged breakout_retest (a retest variant) and from failed_breakout (SHORT, liquidity-vacuum mechanism).
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Path-of-least-resistance tendency analysis
findings.mechanism: each market class and timeframe has a persistent tendency to trend or to mean-revert; trading the direction of least resistance dominates blindly assuming a strategy style
findings.setup_summary: Three-step monthly test on the target instrument: (1) baseline buy-and-hold; (2) buy instruments one std-dev above their 20-bar average (trend-following side); (3) buy instruments one std-dev below (counter-trend side). The side that beats baseline is the path of least resistance. For BTCUSDT 1h this decides between trend-following and mean-reversion expert families before any strategy development.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not an entry; a pre-development regime diagnostic. Its output is only valid for the tested timeframe - the book found stocks counter-trend on daily bars but trend on hourly bars, so a 1h result does not transfer to 4h/1d.
findings.risk_geometry: No trade geometry; output is a per-timeframe tendency classification used to seed the entry-family choice.
findings.quote: I believe stocks are primarily counter-trend-following tendency instruments on daily data; commodities are primarily trend-following instruments on daily data; and overall, FX pairs are primarily counter-trend-following tendency instruments.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 3, Summary of Daily-Bar Tendencies
findings.notes: The single most important pre-development lesson for V8: run the tendency test on BTCUSDT 1h before formalizing any mean-reversion family. BTC has a commodity-like fundamental (mining cost floor) and stock-index-like sentiment; the book's evidence shows hourly-bars stocks trend, which raises the prior that 1h BTC trends too - a testable hypothesis, not an assumption.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: One-day pullback entry filter on an existing trend setup
findings.mechanism: most trend signals fire on up-close bars; waiting one adverse close after confirmation yields a better price and prunes entries at the top of the move that would go straight to the stop
findings.setup_summary: If the long setup exists, wait for a down close; if the setup still exists, enter long on the next open. For shorts, wait for an up close. On BTCUSDT 1h: a valid long signal (e.g., Donchian breakout with trend filter) followed by one down bar, then entry at the next bar open.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: setup exists AND today's close is down (long) / up (short). Invalidation: the base setup no longer satisfies its conditions after the adverse close, or the longer-term trend filter flips.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry next-open after the adverse close; no additional stop specified - inherits the base system's volatility stop; the standalone day-filter test (down-close day -> buy next open) made +$19/trade long, +$7/trade short across 56 commodities.
findings.quote: If the long setup exists, we wait for price to go down one day, and if the setup still exists, we enter the long position. For shorts, we wait for price to rally for one day.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Trading-Day-of-the-Week Filter (Commodities)
findings.notes: Directly corroborates V8's formalized trend_pullback expert (ema_fast>ema_slow + close<ema_slow, NEXT_BAR_CLOSE entry). Caveat from the book's own full-system test: the filter raised profit-per-trade 378->430 but LOWERED gain-to-pain (1.14->1.08) because it cut trade count - so the refinement must be evaluated on risk-adjusted metrics, not profit-per-trade.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Longer-term trend alignment filter (close vs close N bars ago)
findings.mechanism: only taking entries aligned with the longer-term trend direction removes counter-trend noise trades; a 70-bar lookback maximized gain-to-pain on both the stock and commodity systems
findings.setup_summary: Gate every entry: long entries allowed only if today's close > close N bars ago (N=70 selected); short entries only if close < close N bars ago. On BTCUSDT 1h, a 70-bar regime gate. This filter alone kept the stock system out of most of the 2008 crash.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger condition is a monotonic close-vs-close comparison; invalidation is the trend comparison flipping against the open position's direction (dead-thesis exit source).
findings.risk_geometry: No stop change; in the commodity system the 70-bar filter raised profit-per-trade 378->545, cut max drawdown 474k->355k, gain-to-pain 1.14->1.23.
findings.quote: We only take trades if they are in the same direction as the longer-term trend, as determined by a comparison of today's close with that of x days ago.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Longer-Term Trend Filter (Commodities)
findings.notes: The single highest-impact, cheapest rule in the book (close-vs-close-N-ago is computable from OHLC history alone, no indicator state). For 24/7 perps this is directly transferable; 70 on daily bars is a longer horizon than 70 on 1h - the analogous parameter should be re-estimated on 1h data, not imported.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: High-volatility entry gate and vol-spike exit
findings.mechanism: volatility clusters; when recent average range is extreme, noise-to-signal is too high for entries and open equity is at risk, so bypass entries above a threshold and exit live trades when the range blows past a limit
findings.setup_summary: Bypass entries when the 20-day average range (scaled to dollars) exceeds a threshold ($700 selected); as an exit, if the 20-day average range exceeds a limit on the close, exit on the next open. On BTCUSDT 1h: gate entries and exits on average true-range relative to price percentile.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Entry bypass when avg-range > threshold; exit trigger when avg-range > limit at close. No independent invalidation - it is a volatility-regime gate, not a thesis condition.
findings.risk_geometry: Exit at next open when triggered; the range filter on commodities cut max drawdown from $354,671 to $86,296 and lifted gain-to-pain 1.23->2.11 (entry gate) then 2.44 (with exit variant).
findings.quote: Table 6.15, which showed that we should bypass entries with a 20-day average range greater than $700. But suppose we enter a trade and things heat up. Maybe the same filter should signal a trade exit if a certain volatility limit is exceeded.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Volatility-Based Filters (Commodities)
findings.notes: Caveat for crypto: volatility spikes often coincide with the largest trends (2017, 2020, 2021), so a naive high-vol exit can cut off the best trades; the book's own low-vol filter and std-dev variants did not help. V8 should test the gate as a distribution-aware percentile (vol relative to its own recent history) rather than an absolute dollar threshold, which does not exist for BTC.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Volatility-scaled catastrophic stop, triggered on close with next-open exit
findings.mechanism: trade risk should scale with recent volatility because dollar stops are simultaneously too tight for volatile instruments and too loose for quiet ones; a stop is a risk-control measure, not a profit enhancer
findings.setup_summary: Place the catastrophic stop at 3x the 20-day standard deviation of closes from entry (best variant; dollar stops, Donchian-midpoint stops, and average-range stops all underperformed it). If the stop level is breached on a close, exit at the next open - the book shows next-open exit beats intraday resting-stop exit.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Stop trigger: close through the 3-SD level. Thesis: stops cap drawdown but systematically lower profit-per-trade; they should be adopted on risk grounds only.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry-price +/- 3 x 20-day SD of closes; triggered on close, executed next open; the book's repeated finding is 'a stop loss doesn't increase your total profit' yet cuts max drawdown - accept the profit-per-trade tax.
findings.quote: the best risk/reward solution usually lies with a stop executed at either the close or the next open
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 5, Exit Stops (Stock Example)
findings.notes: Corroborates V8's atr_ref stop geometry. The next-open execution finding matters for crypto: 24/7 markets mean resting stops DO fill (unlike overnight commodity sessions), but liquidation-engine wicks and stop-runs argue for the same close-triggered/next-bar-open execution to avoid wick fills. V8's STOP_FIRST simulator already encodes order priority; this book's evidence justifies the close-trigger/next-open execution path.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Momentum divergence at channel extremes - fade, not trade
findings.mechanism: in trending instruments, price/momentum divergence at a Donchian extreme is exhaustion, not continuation - trading divergences lost on stocks and commodities, while fading them on commodities won +$451/trade at 30 bars
findings.setup_summary: 14-day Donchian high higher than the prior high, with a 14-bar momentum reading lower than at the prior high, and today's close below yesterday's (divergence short setup). Fade it: enter short on the next open instead of buying; hold 5-30 bars. Mirror for the long side at Donchian lows. On commodities the fade earned $136/trade at 5 bars rising to $451 at 30 bars.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence setup at a 14-bar channel extreme. Invalidation of the fade thesis: momentum moving back in the same direction as price (the book's alternative ruleset 'New price buy/sell setup' removed the opposite-momentum requirement and lost money).
findings.risk_geometry: Market entry next open; fixed hold of 5-30 bars; no stops in the test - a crude exit that still won, so the entry is the load-bearing element.
findings.quote: I think we can conclude that divergence trading doesn't have a significant edge in either stock or commodity trading; in fact, for commodities you'd be much better off trading in the opposite direction on each divergence signal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, A Divergence Is a Strong Signal
findings.notes: This is a falsification of the popular rsi_divergence entry as a trend signal plus evidence for its contrarian mirror on trending instruments. BTC trends like commodities per the book's tendency analysis, so the fade carries counter-trend risk and a funding headwind that the book's zero-cost commodity test did not face - the fade variant must be funding-adjusted in any V8 test.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Bar-scoring: expected forward return conditioning by criteria bins
findings.mechanism: each bar's profit potential is characterized by binning criteria (e.g., SD of close, SD of volume, range/price, bar type) and assigning each bin its average forward return; the summed score is an expected-value ranking across candidates
findings.setup_summary: For each bar compute several criteria (20-day SD of close position, 20-day SD of volume, 10-day SD of range/price, 8-category bar type), bin each into 20 equal-size bins, and tag each bar with its N-bar forward return (N=2-5). Sum bin-expected-returns into a bar score; trade the top-x scored bars each day (entry next open, exit after N bars). BRAC test showed ~10-15% inherent curve-fit inflation.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: bar score in the top-x of the day. The methodology invalidates if bin separation (top-bin vs bottom-bin expected return) is small - the book's own diagnostic for criterion quality.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry next open; fixed 2-day hold in the developed system; equal-size position = equity/x; 50-trades/day variant returned 47.2%/yr with 18.2% avg of top-20 drawdowns.
findings.quote: Bar-scoring assigns a profit expectation to each bar by using a large set of similar setups and their average return over the expectation period.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, Conclusion (Bar-Scoring)
findings.notes: Bar-scoring is cross-sectional (best when there are thousands of instruments); V8 is single-instrument BTCUSDT, so the cross-sectional ranking does not transfer, but the time-series analogue (conditioning 1h bars by SD-of-close, SD-of-volume, range bins and measuring forward expected return) is a direct, falsifiable feature-group study that can inform which feature groups carry predictive signal before any expert is formalized.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Fixed-fractional risk sizing (1-3% per trade) over Kelly/optimal-f
findings.mechanism: compounding with equalized per-trade risk grows equity fast while capping ruin probability; over-betting (Kelly's 20% stake, optimal-f) produces 77-99% drawdowns and bust
findings.setup_summary: Size every position so the distance to stop represents a fixed small fraction (1-3%) of equity; the book's simulation of a 60%-winning even-money game shows Kelly's 20% stake yields a 77.3% average max drawdown with 2% bust, while 1-2% stakes keep max drawdown under 40% with zero busts. Fixed-fractional risk beat both optimal-f and fixed-ratio in the commodity system (gain-to-pain 7.27 vs 5.70 vs ~2).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not a strategy trigger; sizing rule. Its validity is bounded by the account-size constraint the book stresses: small accounts cannot risk a small fixed percentage because one contract already exceeds it.
findings.risk_geometry: Position size = (equity x risk%) / stop-distance; compounding uses open+closed equity; stop distance is the 3-SD volatility stop from the stop_distance_atr finding.
findings.quote: There's a reason most money managers use a fixed-risk trading approach. It's because it is a very fast way to build equity, and risk is equalized on every position by the sizing.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 11, Sizing Summary
findings.notes: With perp leverage 20-100x, position sizing is where over-leverage does its damage; the book's simulation (Kelly = 20% stake, 77% drawdown, 2% bust) is the strongest available argument for V8's RiskGate heat cap and per-trade risk limits. Also a methodological warning: optimal-f ignores open-equity giveback and concurrent-trade overlap, so its TWR math is unusable for a system with open positions - V8's heat cap should be equity-fraction based, not TWR-based.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Diversification across uncorrelated groups; cap same-group exposure
findings.mechanism: instruments within a group move in tandem, so concentrated group exposure multiplies drawdown; spreading across uncorrelated groups keeps profit roughly constant while cutting drawdown ~20-25%
findings.setup_summary: Trade instruments from different groups rather than several members of one group; 'first-N-in-a-group': take the first N signals from each group and cap group count. The book's 8-commodity test: all-currencies vs diversified portfolios made near-identical profit ($528,888 vs $517,983) but the diversified set had ~25% lower average and ~20% lower max start-trade drawdown.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Risk-portfolio rule, not a market trigger; it caps how many correlated exposures may coexist.
findings.risk_geometry: Portfolio-level: max simultaneous exposures per correlated group = N; apply start-trade drawdown as the small-account survival metric.
findings.quote: These results illustrate the diversification advantage. The average max draw-down is about 25 percent lower in the diversified set, and the maximum draw-down is about 20 percent less than the non-diversified portfolios', but the total profit is about the same.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 12, Diversification (beginning of Part 1)
findings.notes: For single-instrument BTCUSDT the cap is trivial; it becomes load-bearing if V8 expands to ETH/alt perps, where the entire crypto market is effectively ONE correlated group - BTC, ETH and majors would count as same-group exposures (beta ~0.8+), so naive multi-coin 'diversification' would not reduce drawdown the way this book's diversified commodity basket did. Funding-basis and BTC-dominance structure are the crypto-specific group dimensions.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: BRAC test and minimum trade-sample requirements
findings.mechanism: curve-fit severity is proportional to too-few trades in the development sample; standard error of mean profit-per-trade shrinks with sample size, and the BRAC (Build-Rebuild-Compare) test quantifies parameter persistence by withholding the last year, rebuilding with the same selection logic, and comparing
findings.setup_summary: Require many hundreds to thousands of trades in any development sample (the book's gold-file experiment shows standard error ~$200 at 90 trades and still ~$100 at 300 trades on a $32.80 mean trade); after building, withhold the final year, rebuild with identical selection steps, and compare on the withheld period. A moving-average system across 37 commodities passed BRAC with identical parameter picks; the Swiss-franc 1980s fit failed out-of-sample (from $8,500/yr to $1,500/yr).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not a market rule; a development gate. A candidate system that does not pass BRAC is not tradeable regardless of backtest PnL.
findings.risk_geometry: Development-level: trade counts, standard error bands, and withheld-period comparison replace single-chart 'spectacular' curve fits.
findings.quote: for most trading systems (I won't say all, but I'm thinking all) you need many hundreds to thousands of trades in your back-test to minimize the effects of curve-fitting and gain the confidence that real trading will match the parameters of your back-test
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 2, Testing for Curve-Fitting
findings.notes: Directly supports V8's frozen-OOS and registry-gated evolution rules: parameter stability ('the best parameter set doesn't flop around from year to year' once trade counts are high) is the falsifiable claim behind not re-optimizing in place. The book also refutes the '30 trades is enough' myth and warns against out-of-sample-by-withholding as inferior to BRAC (withholding shrinks the dev sample). V8's single BTC 1h tape can reach thousands of trades for fast families but not for slow ones - that asymmetry should gate which families are formalizable at all.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

findings.strategy_name: Limit-order adverse selection: backtests overstate fills on resting orders
