findings.mechanism: a resting limit order fills only when the book on the other side at that price is consumed - which is precisely when price is moving through your level against you; it is missed when price would have come back, so real fills are winners-missed/losers-caught
findings.setup_summary: Any strategy that enters on limit orders, or exits via limit profit-targets, will realize worse fills than a fill-guaranteed backtest: the book's emini-S&P 5-minute scalp backtested at $15.90/trade with a straight-line equity curve (928 wins/330 losses), and in live auto-trading 'just about all of the losing trades would occur, but you'd only get about half the winners.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not a market rule; a fill-modeling rule. Its scope is any V8 candidate whose risk_geometry uses limit entries or limit profit-targets.
findings.risk_geometry: Simulator-side: penalize limit-order fills with an adverse-selection model (fill probability that depends on which way price is moving through the level), and scale the penalty inversely with profit-per-trade - small-profit scalps are killed, large-profit systems merely degrade.
findings.quote: I missed some of the best fills, but always got filled on the ones that traded down to my price, and kept going down from there. In other words, I missed some big winners, but always seemed to get the losers.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 2, Limit Order Mania
findings.notes: V8's canonical L1 simulator is fill-at-close with STOP_FIRST - it currently has no representation of limit-order fill bias. For perps, maker orders are the cost-efficient execution (rebates), so any future candidate using maker entries inherits this exact bias, amplified by leverage. Also relevant: the book's dual-orders-in-a-bar and assuming-every-point-in-a-bar-is-a-trade-point warnings argue for keeping V8's fill-at-close L1 rather than intra-bar path assumptions.
findings.book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

book_title: The Big Short: Inside the Doomsday Machine (Michael Lewis, 2011)

findings.strategy_name: Credit-extension-by-instrument erosion (watch the lenders, not the borrowers)
findings.mechanism: When the credit-supply side progressively degrades underwriting/leverage standards to grow loan or volume throughput, hidden fragility accumulates in the system that later converts into defaults; the top is dated by lenders losing restraint, not by any single price statistic.
findings.setup_summary: On any market state, treat measurable easing of credit/leverage availability (in crypto perps: rising max-leverage tiers, relaxed margin/collateral rules, launch of higher-risk leveraged products, sustained positive-funding leverage build-up) with static aggregate risk metrics as a rising-fragility regime rather than a neutral condition. Burry flagged the top from the 'extension of credit by instrument' — lenders inventing new instruments to lend to people who could not otherwise afford it — while FICO/LTV aggregates stayed flat.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: observable expansion of credit/leverage availability without compensating quality. Invalidated: if the same provider subsequently tightens (raises margins, cuts leverage tiers), or if actual defaults/liquidations do not rise after the standard erosion.
findings.risk_geometry: Not a trade; a regime filter feeding RiskGate admission and long-side still_valid logic. No entry/stop/target of its own.
findings.quote: What you want to watch are the lenders, not the borrowers. The borrowers will always be willing to take a great deal for themselves. It's up to the lenders to show restraint, and when they lose it, watch out.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'In the Land of the Blind' (Michael Burry)
findings.notes: The underwriting-standard mechanism transfers to perps as venue leverage policy (exchanges raised max leverage in bull phases) and funding/collateral regimes, but there is no underwriting analog and no teaser-reset; the proxy is leverage availability, OI structure, and funding. Root incentive is the originate-and-sell moral hazard: 'Any business where you can sell a product and make money without having to worry how the product performs is going to attract sleazy people.'
findings.book: The Big Short - Inside the Doomsday Machine 2011

findings.strategy_name: Hidden composition deterioration (decompose aggregates; forced flow masks quality)
findings.mechanism: Headline aggregates stay statistically static while the composition inside them shifts toward lower quality (rising share of interest-only/negative-amortizing instruments, rising share of forced flow disguised as voluntary), so deterioration is invisible until it is terminal.
findings.setup_summary: Measurement discipline for feature engineering: do not read aggregate flow/OI/participation stats at face value; decompose into forced vs voluntary components. In perps the 'involuntary prepayment' analog is liquidation/forced-close volume as a share of total volume and OI split by leverage bucket; Burry's static-FICO/rising-IO-ARM analog is static aggregate credit metrics with a rising high-risk instrument share. Vinny proved the method: sifting pool data revealed 'stunningly high delinquency rates' and no real earnings.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: rising forced-flow share or high-risk composition share while headline volume/OI is flat. Invalidated if the decomposition reverts, or if the predicted default/liquidation surge does not follow within the observation window.
findings.risk_geometry: Not a trade; an evidence discipline for feature-group construction (which ratios enter marketstate).
findings.quote: 'Involuntary prepayment' sounds better than 'default.'
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 1, 'A Secret Origin Story' (Vincent Daniel's pool analysis)
findings.notes: Directly implementable: perp venues publish liquidation volumes and OI breakdowns. The lesson generalizes Burry's observation that 'these measures could stay roughly static, but the overall pool ... was worsening in quality.'
findings.book: The Big Short - Inside the Doomsday Machine 2011

findings.strategy_name: Common-factor correlation cap (diversification illusion under one factor)
findings.mechanism: Positions in nominally different instruments that load on a single common factor are not diversified; the factor event hits them all simultaneously, so a 'diversified' book collapses as one position.
findings.setup_summary: RiskGate rule: before admitting a book of positions, aggregate exposure by common factor rather than by instrument count. The 2007 CDO error was treating 100 subprime pools (same floodplain: US home prices) as a diversified portfolio and re-rating 80% of the triple-B pile as triple-A; the perp analog is a multi-alt book that is one BTCUSD-beta position, or a short book that is one liquidation-cascade factor.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Cap rule, not a trade: if correlated exposure under any single factor exceeds the heat cap, admission is denied. Continuously validated; no thesis to invalidate.
findings.risk_geometry: Risk rule only; interacts with the RiskGate heat cap and the ONE exposure per (instrument, direction) lifecycle rule.
findings.quote: By assuming that one pile of subprime mortgage loans wasn't exposed to the same forces as another—that a subprime mortgage bond with loans heavily concentrated in Florida wasn't very much like a subprime mortgage bond more concentrated in California—the engineers created the illusion of security.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'How Can a Guy Who Can't Speak English Lie?' (CDO/synthetic CDO explanation)
findings.notes: Historically confirmed by the AIG FP failure (insured pools went from 2% to 95% subprime without anyone flagging it). Reuses starter slug correlated_exposure_cap. The rule is the direct precedent for V8's correlated-exposure caps.
findings.book: The Big Short - Inside the Doomsday Machine 2011

findings.strategy_name: Momentum-stall leverage fragility (price need not fall, only stop rising fast)
findings.mechanism: Leveraged credit is only solvent while the collateralizing asset keeps appreciating; deceleration of appreciation — not a decline — is sufficient to trigger defaults and cascades, because payments and margins were built on the extrapolated appreciation.
findings.setup_summary: Falsifiable regime claim from Lippmann's quant evidence: when price appreciation decelerates from an extended fast-appreciation regime while leverage (OI, funding-heavy positioning) is high, treat as a fragile regime. The empirical anchor: since 2000, homes appreciating only 1-5% defaulted at nearly 4x the rate of homes appreciating >10%; first-year subprime defaults had already risen from 1% to 4% while prices still rose, and 8% pool losses zeroed the triple-B tranches.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: measured deceleration of appreciation below the prior regime rate with elevated leverage. Invalidated if a sustained price stall does not produce rising forced liquidation/default rates within the observation window.
findings.risk_geometry: Regime filter for RiskGate admission and long-side still_valid gating; no entry/stop/target of its own.
findings.quote: Home prices didn't even need to fall. They merely needed to stop rising at the unprecedented rates they had the previous few years for vast numbers of Americans to default on their home loans.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'How Can a Guy Who Can't Speak English Lie?' (Lippmann's 'Shorting Home Equity Mezzanine Tranches' pitch)
findings.notes: The book makes a falsifiable statistical case (specific 4x multiplier, 1%->4% first-year default, 7%/8% pool-loss thresholds zeroing BBB-/BBB). Perp leverage is marked continuously, so the stall-to-cascade mechanism is the core of crypto liquidation cascades and transfers more directly than the mortgage reset mechanics. Reuses starter slug deleveraging_cascade.
findings.book: The Big Short - Inside the Doomsday Machine 2011

findings.strategy_name: Defined-downside tail protection with counterparty survival and MTM collateral
findings.mechanism: A tail bet with capped premium and many-x upside only pays off if the party you bought protection from survives the very event you are insured against; demanding mark-to-market collateral posting on the contract preserves the payoff.
findings.setup_summary: Burry's CDS construction lesson: when tail risk is structurally mispriced (buyers paying 250bp for protection on the worst triple-B pools while a triple-A seller charges 12bp on the same bonds re-rated through a synthetic CDO), place the defined-loss bet before the market reprices it, then wait through mark-to-market pain. Two execution constraints: (1) buy protection only from counterparties that will survive the insured event — Burry never bothered calling Bear or Lehman because they were most exposed; (2) demand MTM collateral posting so the hedge's value is not destroyed by counterparty failure. 'I'm not making a bet against a bond. I'm making a bet against a system.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: structural mispricing of tail risk (wide gap between what sellers charge and what odds imply). Invalidated if the mispricing reprices before the position is fully on, or if the counterparty cannot post collateral / is itself at risk from the event.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: premium stream (book: ~2.5%/yr on triple-B for up to ~6 years of an expected 30-year loan). Stop: none; loss capped at the premium stream. Target: many multiples of premium on the event (odds felt like 2:1, offered at 6:1 to 10:1). Collateral/MTM posting on the contract is mandatory.
findings.quote: There was no point buying insurance from a bank that went out of business the minute the insurance became valuable.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'In the Land of the Blind' (Burry's first CDS trades, May 2005)
findings.notes: The CDS instrument itself does not exist in perps (no options/insurance tape), so the trade construction is DEFER_GATED. The transferable risk rules are venue-level: cap single-venue exposure, model exchange/liquidation-engine failure in the simulator, and treat any hedge's counterparty survival as part of the hedge's value. Direction of the underlying trade was SHORT, but the extracted rule is direction-neutral.
findings.book: The Big Short - Inside the Doomsday Machine 2011

book_title: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis: Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing (2011), Paul Ciana — Part 1 (Ch 1-5)

findings.strategy_name: Momentum divergence as trend-exhaustion warning
findings.mechanism: price making a new extreme while momentum fails to confirm indicates the trend is decelerating/exhausting
findings.setup_summary: On the trading timeframe, price prints a higher high while RSI(14) prints a lower high (bearish divergence) or price prints a lower low while RSI prints a higher low (bullish divergence). Divergence must be anchored on confirmed swing extremes (peak preceded and followed by opposite bars), allow ~2-3 bars tolerance between price and momentum peaks, and be invalidated if momentum re-pierces its prior extreme before price confirms.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Divergence is null if the momentum indicator re-makes its prior peak/trough before the price peak/trough is confirmed; peaks offset by 4-5+ bars do not count; Kase: the setup becomes a usable exit/danger sign only when the divergence completes on a confirming closing bar.
findings.risk_geometry: Book gives no entry/stop/target for this signal; used as a warning of trend change or (Kase) as an exit signal — pull stops to Dev2/Dev3 or warning line on divergence completion; OBOS levels are trend-conditional (uptrend: overbought 75-80 / oversold 35-40; downtrend: overbought 55-60 / oversold 20-25).
findings.quote: Bearish divergence (an opportunity to sell) occurs when price is making higher highs and RSI is making lower highs.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 1, 'Applying the Most Popular Technical Indicators — Relative Strength Index' (pp. 19-21); Chapter 4, 'Kase Momentum Divergence Algorithm' (pp. 177-187)
findings.notes: KaseMDA supplies the falsifiable definition needed to test this: swing-based peaks, 2-3 bar tolerance, null-divergence rule, 1-2% peak filters, 89-bar max span. Trend-conditional OBOS thresholds are a regime lesson in their own right.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Kase DevStops volatility-quantile trailing stop
findings.mechanism: stop distance is set at skew-corrected quantiles of the two-bar true-range distribution so stop-out probability is known in advance and scales with volatility AND its variability
findings.setup_summary: Trailing stop follows the highest high (long) / lowest low (short). Warning line = mean TrueRangeDouble (TRD); Dev1/Dev2/Dev3 = 1 / 2.2 / 3.6 std devs above mean TRD, skew-corrected because range distributions are right-skewed. Dev3 is the permanent emergency stop; Dev2 in choppy regimes; front-end MA crossover defaults which side's stops plot.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Stop-out probabilities from empirical hit-hit tables (most active futures, 150k+ bars): Warn->Dev1 ~80%, Dev1->Dev2 ~80%, Dev2->Dev3 ~70%, Warn->Dev3 ~45%; a stop at the warning line has ~50% noise stop-out probability, at Dev1 ~15%, at Dev2 ~2.5%.
findings.risk_geometry: Trailing; stop at TRD quantiles; risk amount pre-calculable (KaseRevAmounts) so position size = risk budget / stop distance; no target; stop widens with volatility and vol-of-vol; 'logical and predictable' versus swing stops which are logical but not predictable in magnitude.
findings.quote: we use 1, 2.2, and 3.6 standard deviations over the average TRD for Kase DevStops Dev1, 2, and 3
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, 'Kase DevStops' (pp. 169-177)
findings.notes: Crypto perps trade 24/7 with no overnight gaps, so TrueRange equals the high-low range on most bars; the transferable core is the volatility-quantile stop with a stated stop-out probability plus the hit-hit cascade used for scaling out. In V8 this refines stop_r in risk_geometry: replace a fixed ATR multiple with a volatility-percentile stop.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: KaseSwing higher-low swing-midpoint breakout
findings.mechanism: after a higher swing low forms, a close above the intermediate swing high confirms the higher-low sequence and captures the next swing leg
findings.setup_summary: Identify swing highs/lows with KaseSwing (swing size = N bars up/down, 1-3 typical; inside-bar and extreme rules defined). When the second swing low is >= the first swing low, go long on the bar that closes above the middle swing high between the two lows; mirror for shorts (second swing high <= first, close below middle swing low).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Entry invalid if price breaks the prior swing low before the midpoint is reclaimed; open position exits when the trailing swing stop is broken.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close above the swing midpoint (fill-at-close compatible). Stop: prior swing low, ratcheted up at each new higher swing low; no target — exit on swing-stop break. Book caveat: swing stops are logical but not predictable in size, so cap the stop using the recent average of swing magnitudes or switch to DevStops.
findings.quote: if there are two swing lows where the second swing low is equal to or higher than the first, then when prices exceed the middle swing high, a long trade may be taken
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, 'Using KaseSwing for Market Timing' (pp. 163-168)
findings.notes: Distinct from breakout_retest and trend_pullback: entry is anchored to swing structure, not moving averages; the ratcheting swing stop is a concrete lifecycle rule. Clean swings form on BTCUSDT 1h, and the inside-bar/extreme conventions make the algorithm fully mechanical.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Bollinger bandwidth-regime band trade (fade wide, ride narrow)
findings.mechanism: bandwidth regime determines whether a band touch reverts to the mean (wide bands) or precedes a directional break to be ridden (narrow bands)
findings.setup_summary: When bandwidth is above its average (vol expansion), sell the close above the +2sd band and buy the close below the -2sd band, targeting the middle band (mean). When bandwidth is narrow (compression), do NOT fade band touches — instead a close beyond a band signals a new trend direction and the trade is to ride the band while bandwidth expands.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Reversion thesis invalid if price keeps closing beyond the band while bandwidth is expanding; the 'riding' trade is only valid while bandwidth expands from compression.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: bar close beyond the +/-2sd band (20-period MA, 2sd). Target: the middle band / mean reversion. Book specifies no stop or expiry; implies hold until mean; riding trades held while bandwidth expands (can persist several periods).
findings.quote: wider bands offer better opportunities than narrow bands for a mean reversion trade. Narrow bands are more useful for determining the future direction of trend.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 1, 'Applying the Most Popular Technical Indicators — Bollinger Bands' (pp. 25-28)
findings.notes: The load-bearing lesson is regime-conditioning one indicator's signal (fade vs ride) on a bandwidth state; the narrow-band ride side maps to range_compression / volatility_breakout. Crypto vol-regime switching makes bandwidth a natural regime feature.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: ADX/DMI trend-strength directional gate
findings.mechanism: when ADX>25 the market trends in the DMI-dominant direction and only that direction should be traded; below 25 the market is range-bound
findings.setup_summary: Trade long only when +DMI > -DMI and ADX > 25; short only when -DMI > +DMI and ADX > 25. ADX rising through ~15-23 flags a trend developing; ADX falling from ~32 toward 25 flags a trend ending. ADX below 25 = range-bound, no directional edge.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Directional thesis invalid when ADX drops back below 25 (trend weakening/ending — not necessarily reversing) or when the DMI pair flips.
findings.risk_geometry: Regime gate, not an entry; no stops/targets specified; pairs with any entry system; usable as higher-timeframe bias.
findings.quote: the ADX line suggests that the market is trending in the direction of the greater DMI line if it is above 25. If it is below 25, it suggests that the trend is weak or range bound.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 1, 'Applying the Most Popular Technical Indicators — Directional Movement Indicator' (pp. 29-31)
findings.notes: Directly reusable as a trend-regime gate on BTCUSDT 1h using the trend feature group; ADX transitions (15->23 forming, 32->25 ending) provide regime-change hints usable in lifecycle rules.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Price-volume confirmation with time-normalized volume (VAT)
findings.mechanism: a price move is more credible when volume agrees, and time-of-day-normalized volume (VAT) removes calendar skew that hides the true level of participation
findings.setup_summary: Rising price + rising/above-average volume = bullish, trend supported; rising price + falling volume = top/consolidation warning; falling price + rising volume = bearish; falling price + falling volume = bottom warning. Volume spike at market lows = accumulation; at market highs = distribution. Compare volume to its same-time-of-day average (VAT — average of that hour/day over prior X days), not a plain moving average, because a plain MA is skewed by stale and by time-of-day structure.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Confirmation feature only; no independent invalidation — its failure (price up, volume light) is itself a warning flag used to fade the move.
findings.risk_geometry: Feature/confirmation input; book specifies no entry, stop, or target for volume rules alone.
findings.quote: Price is rising and volume is rising and/or above average = bullish market; the uptrend is being supported by market participants.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 1, 'Volume at Time' and 'Intraday Volume at Time' (pp. 36-43)
findings.notes: For perps, volume is notional and taker-split based, traded 24/7; hour-of-day and day-of-week normalization is implementable from the tape, but wash trading and venue fragmentation distort absolute volume — normalize relative to a venue-consistent baseline. Volume features belong in the participation group.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Relative-strength rotation across a universe (RRG)
findings.mechanism: cross-sectional relative strength and its momentum rotate clockwise around a benchmark; long the strong-and-strengthening, short/avoid the weak-and-weakening
findings.setup_summary: For each element in a universe compute RS ratio vs benchmark (JdK RS-Ratio) and RS momentum (JdK RS-Momentum). Long/overweight elements crossing into the top-right quadrant (ratio>100, momentum>100); short/underweight elements crossing into the bottom-left quadrant (ratio<100, momentum<0). Ignore elements circling near the benchmark (100,100) — those are not where the moves are. Rotation trails confirm direction and pace.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rotation thesis invalid if momentum crosses back through 100 without the ratio following (rotation within a quadrant, RS>100 or <100 stays); exit when the element rotates into the opposite quadrant.
findings.risk_geometry: Weekly/monthly hold for institutions or intraday (RRG works on any timeframe); trails of 3-17 weeks confirm rotation; book gives no stops/targets; the long top-right / short bottom-left pair is cited as the 'least risk' variant because both RS states are confirmed.
findings.quote: the average excess return of the underperform recommendations was significantly higher than the excess return of the outperform recommendations.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'The JdK RS-Ratio and JdK RS-Momentum' and 'Relative Rotation Graphs' (pp. 65-82)
findings.notes: Self-reported backtest (1987-2003, 3,456 sector-months) claims significant outperformance; the asymmetric result — avoiding the underperformers contributed more excess return than picking outperformers — is the durable lesson. For crypto: alt-vs-BTC cross-sectional rotation across perps; feed cross_market features into single-instrument experts rather than building a router (rule 14).
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Validated seasonal cycle activated by a price trigger
findings.mechanism: a seasonal cycle is only tradable if validated by out-of-sample correlation (Cycle-R) of exogenous data halves, and only executed when price confirms the direction via a trigger
findings.setup_summary: Build a calendar-year seasonal cycle by compositing prior years; accept it only if Cycle-R (correlation between cycles built on the first vs second half of history, or across look-backs) is positive/meaningful (example given: 0.76 for SBUX); trade only the strongest (long) and weakest (short) zones of >=14 days and only in the cycle's direction, and only when a price trigger (e.g., close through the daily DMA channel) confirms the move. Seasonal heat (consistency across prior years' cycles) weights zone reliability.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Setup invalid if Cycle-R is negative or seasonal heat is dark/inconsistent; trade invalidated when price closes back through the trigger level (e.g., the DMA channel).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry/exit = close vs DMA channel. Worked example: AXP long entry $39.72, exit $45.86 (+15.46% in 38 trading days); short entry $42.30, exit $39.09 (+7.00% in 11 days); no ATR stop — channel-cross exit. Dow 30 tables show W/L improving 0.59->1.55->2.50->7.00 as validity and bias filters stack.
findings.quote: it is wise to act on shifts in the seasonal patterns only if a price trigger indicates a move in the new direction of seasonality.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Testing for a Valid Seasonal Cycle' and 'Applying Cycles as a Strategy' (pp. 85-100)
findings.notes: Evidence is single-year Dow 30 tables plus a correlation validity test — statistically presented but narrow. Calendar-year seasonality transfers weakly to crypto (no equity calendar, ~13y BTC history); the transferable methodology is (a) the Cycle-R out-of-sample validity gate before trusting any periodic pattern, and (b) the rule that a setup is only acted on with a price trigger. Hour-of-week / funding-cycle effects could be tested with the same validation discipline.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Higher-timeframe trend permission filter (bias before trigger)
findings.mechanism: lower-timeframe entries are gated by a higher-timeframe trend state; short-bar moves that contradict the larger timeframe are mostly noise and should not be acted on
findings.setup_summary: Choose a bias interval larger than the trigger interval: e.g., monthly/weekly DMA channel (6-period high/low averages displaced 4 bars) as bias for daily DMA triggers; weekly ENS/EROC as bias for daily signals; Kase Permission Stochastic builds synthetic bars (e.g., 5 daily bars rolled into one synthetic weekly) so permission is granted ~2 bars earlier than waiting for the natural higher-timeframe close. Take only long triggers when bias is long, only short triggers when bias is short; when the filter grants opposite permission, require stronger bar-pattern confirmation before entry.
findings.trigger_invalidation: A bias flip reverses the permissioned side and warrants reevaluation of open positions; Kase's trend-direction principle: each smaller cycle is a test of the next larger cycle.
findings.risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target of its own — it gates which signals are admissible. Kase prefers the filter at ~3x the traded bar length (synthetic). Dow 30 study: adding monthly-DMA bias to daily DMA triggers raised W/L from 0.59 to 7.0 and return per trade from 0.29% to 7.40%; GE study: moving-with-bias 168.88% vs ignoring-bias -66.42%.
findings.quote: Bias indicators are primarily set to intervals larger than those used to trigger in and out of trades.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Strategic Step #1: Determining Bias' and 'Displaced Moving Average Channel' (pp. 111-121); Chapter 4, 'Kase Permission Stochastic and Screen' (pp. 199-201)
findings.notes: The highest-value transferable rule in this book for V8: gate Expert emission by a higher-timeframe trend state, implementable without wall-clock dependence via synthetic bars or the natural higher bar. Also pairs with Kase's KEES rule that when permission is contrary, multiple confirming bars are required.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Squeeze-play: extreme sentiment as setup, price as trigger
findings.mechanism: extreme bullish/bearish positioning (options ratios, short interest) creates reversal fuel that only fires when price confirms; an overcommitted crowd leaves no one left to continue the trend
findings.setup_summary: Setup: excessive bearish options betting (high put/call median) or excessive bullish (high call/put median); high short interest in an uptrend (short-squeeze fuel) or depressed short interest in a downtrend (long-squeeze fuel). Trigger: price closes through the daily DMA channel in the setup's direction. Both sentiment and price must agree; a sentiment setup is never traded without a price trigger.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Setup invalid if sentiment is not extreme or if price fails to trigger; position exits on the reverse DMA-channel cross. 'We always use a price study to activate the sentiment setup.'
findings.risk_geometry: Entry/exit on DMA-channel cross. Worked examples: BBY long triggered on close above DMA after mid-March put/call extreme; DIA short triggered on drop below DMA in early May after April call/put extreme. No ATR stop given.
findings.quote: For a short squeeze situation, we are looking for those stocks that have an excess of negative sentiment but are in an uptrend—these are situations where the market is telling us that the negative bettors are wrong.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Erlanger Put/Call Ratio' and 'Monitoring' (pp. 141-146)
findings.notes: Perp analogs: funding-rate extremes (excessive long/short leverage), open interest, taker-buy/sell ratio. Put/call and short-interest series do not exist for most perps, so funding is the closest flow feature; the general mechanism (extreme positioning + price trigger) is the transferable core and is corroborated across the Squeeze-Play framework.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Intraday value-line and opening-range bias
findings.mechanism: prior-session value levels (pivot/support/resistance) and the opening range define the day's bias; price breaking them reveals who is in control and the day's momentum
findings.setup_summary: At session start, set resistance/pivot/support value lines from prior-day structure plus the first-hour (or first 5-min) opening-range high/low. Price above the resistance line => long-only bias; below the support line => short-only bias; between them => neutral. Break of the opening-range high => positive near-term bias; break of the opening-range low => negative. Clusters of value lines (e.g., prior-day last-2h high + pivot + 60-min opening low) are stronger levels. Support broken then reclaimed above the pivot = sellers failed (positive recovery); resistance taken then lost = buyers failed.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Bias flips when price crosses the defining level; a broken level retested as the opposite side is the strong continuation pattern; levels expire at session end.
findings.risk_geometry: Intraday, expires at session end; bias determines admissible side; value lines act as targets and pivot breaks as triggers; no ATR stop specified. Flash-crash day cited as case where a disciplined value-line approach keeps the trader on the right side.
findings.quote: If price breaks above the first-hour high, the near-term bias turns positive. If price breaks below the first-hour low, the near-term bias turns negative.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Erlanger Value Lines' (pp. 126-133)
findings.notes: 24/7 perps have no natural session open; UTC-midnight or funding-hour boundaries can define synthetic sessions, but the mapping is imperfect. The prior-day value-line cluster concept (last-2h high/low, pivot) transfers as session-anchored location features for a time feature group.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Phase-consistent tactics: horizontal vs vertical market
findings.mechanism: eliminate the low-probability side first: in an uptrend the short side has near-zero probability of prevailing, so only long tactics are admissible; range phases require range-edge tactics
findings.setup_summary: Classify the market as uptrending, downtrending, or sideways. Uptrend: only buy higher price pivot lows. Downtrend: only short lower price pivot highs. Sideways: only buy range lows / short range highs, or stand aside. If no admissible entry appears, do not trade — standing aside is often the best choice. Most losses come from being on the wrong side of the phase or using the wrong tactic for the phase.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The tactic table is re-evaluated when the phase changes; a phase change requires reclassification before any new entry.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at pivot lows/highs or range edges on the allowed side; framework-level tactic table (Table 5.1), no explicit stops/targets.
findings.quote: The highest possible high-probability trade starts with the mind-set and very basic rules of: In an uptrend, don't be short; in a downtrend, don't be long.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, 'Technical Analysis Is Simple in Theory—Difficult in Practice' (pp. 218-220)
findings.notes: Corroborates the regime_filter and NEW_higher_timeframe_permission findings from a different angle; adds the explicit tactic-per-phase table (pivot-low entries in trends, range-edge entries in sideways). The chapter's rationale — losses concentrate on being on the wrong side of the phase — is the falsifiable claim V8 can test as a regime discipline.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Balance/imbalance phase regime (fast follows slow)
findings.mechanism: balance leads to imbalance: horizontal low-volatility phases and vertical high-volatility phases alternate, so the end of a slow phase precedes the next directional move; the two phases are mutually exclusive and are traded differently
findings.setup_summary: Classify each BTCUSDT 1h window as horizontal (balanced: narrow range, overlapping bars, fat volume-at-price profile) or vertical (imbalanced: wide non-overlapping bars, skinny profile). Trade only the vertical phase; enter directional trades as horizontal ends (profile transitions fat->skinny) and prefer trading the fast-to-slow side; stand aside when slow becomes slower (fat->fatter profiles, 'multiple consecutively slower and slower profiles often lead to very fast vertical moves').
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: profile shape transition fat->skinny after a slow phase, or price exiting the value area with non-overlapping bars. Invalidation: price re-enters balance without directional follow-through (fast probe fails quickly, e.g. V-pivot); correct phase identification is the whole premise, so the phase classifier itself must be falsified on frozen OOS.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on bar close of the directional break out of balance; stop beyond the balance extreme or probe extreme; target at the next horizontal-development area (far side of the move); the chapter demands >=4:1 reward-to-risk for any trade taken in the phase.
findings.quote: Fast vertical market movements follow slow horizontal market movements. This is an either/or state.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 222-240) 'Balance versus Imbalance' / Figures 5.4-5.9, 'Relative Balance Leads to Relative Imbalance'
findings.notes: The 24/7 perp tape has no opening gaps, so profile/horizontal-development continuity is cleaner than in index futures, making the fat/skinny profile classifier computable from 1h bars + volume-at-price. Maps to a marketstate regime feature (horizontal vs vertical phase + maturity) that gates trend_pullback/breakout families; the fast-to-slow position guidance (stay while profiles skinny, tighten stops while fatter) is a lifecycle management companion.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Probe and Pullback (breakout-retest from balance)
findings.mechanism: a probe beyond a balance extreme exhausts resting orders; a pullback that holds the balance extreme/HVA then reasserts in the probe direction
findings.setup_summary: After a defined horizontal balance (>=2 relatively equal pivot highs and lows), price probes beyond one extreme, then retraces back to or into the balance area. Entry in the probe direction on a stall in the retest zone, i.e. between the broken balance extreme and the HVA boundary; expectation is that the retest of the balance extreme or HVA leads to reassertion in the probe direction and a directional move.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: retest of the broken balance extreme or HVA after a probe, with a stall signal (smaller-degree balance/support indication) in the zone. Invalidation: retracement through the entire HVA of the balance area - 'a retrace through the entire HVA of the balance area invalidates the setup'; a full retrace converts the trade to the Reversal-and-Retest premise.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on bar close anywhere between the retested balance extreme and the HVA limit (long: extreme-to-HVA lower limit; short: extreme-to-HVA upper limit); stop beyond the opposite extreme of the HVA; first target the probe extreme, then far side of the next low-volume hole / beyond the balance area on phase transition.
findings.quote: The retest of the balance area after the 'probe' outside of balance should not retrace any further than the HVA of that balance area.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 267-273) 'A Trading Plan for Trade Locations, Entries, Stops, and Targets' - Probe and Pullback, Figures 5.31-5.32
findings.notes: This is a concrete, fully-specified spec for the existing V8 backlog family breakout_retest (currently DATA_BLOCKED, requires location/volatility/history): the book supplies the retest-zone definition (balance extreme to HVA boundary), the invalidation (full HVA retrace), and stop/target convention. No-exchange-gaps means balance extremes and HVA refs stay PIT-valid in crypto.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Reversal and Retest (failed probe -> reversal on retest)
findings.mechanism: when a probe fails and price pierces the HVA of the balance area aggressively, the imbalance has flipped; the reversal is confirmed by a retest of the balance range or HVA
findings.setup_summary: When a Probe-and-Pullback fails - the pullback shows no stall and price trades through the entire HVA of the balance area in an aggressive/persistent (initiative) fashion - the setup reverses: enter on a retest of the balance range or HVA in the direction opposite the failed probe. Fading extremes of smaller-degree balances once the HVA is broken, or once the opposite balance extreme is broken, is also valid.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: initiative piercing of the HVA followed by a retest of the balance extreme/HVA. Invalidation: price reclaims the far side of the broken HVA and re-engages the original direction (no vacuum formed); per V8, still_valid = close stays on the reversal side of the frozen reference.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on retest after the pierce; stop beyond the opposite extreme of the HVA (often beyond the extreme of the balance reversed through for smaller structures); first target from smaller structures/balances to the left, with the best setups targeting the far side of a low-volume-at-price hole.
findings.quote: The key to this setup is the piercing of the HVA of the balance area in an initiative way. Once broken, entries into this type of trade can be taken upon a retest of the range or of the HVA.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 269-273, 1919-1934) 'Reversal and Retest', Figures 5.33-5.34
findings.notes: Corroborates and refines the existing V8 failed_breakout expert (liquidity_vacuum_reentry): the book's Reversal-and-Retest is the HVA-pierce variant of that family and adds the retest-entry rule, a frozen-reference invalidation, and the low-volume-hole target. A variant parameterization (retest-zone width, HVA-vs-balance-extreme reference) rather than a new family.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Trading into profile holes (minus development)
findings.mechanism: low-volume-at-price regions (holes, 'minus development') between areas of horizontal development lack technical support, so price traverses them fast and with high reward-to-risk
findings.setup_summary: Build a rolling volume-at-price distribution over a lookback window; identify holes = price ranges where volume did not accumulate (no horizontal development). When price breaks from a balanced area toward a hole, expect a rapid vertical traversal to the far side (next high-volume area). Long: enter near the unfair low only when a short-timeframe pause forms (new small Dynamic VAP = supporting volume); Short: enter on a break below the balance support with stop above the breakdown bar.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price breaks the edge of a balanced area toward a profile hole. Invalidation: quick probe failure inside the hole - the book's 'Probe' bars fail fast, so a failed probe allows a tight stop; reversal back into the balance area invalidates.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the hole edge (pause-confirmed) or on the break bar close; stop just beyond the breakdown level / above the breakdown-bar high; targets = far side of the hole (opposite HVA), then the far end of that HVA; reward-to-risk is claimed higher than horizontal trades provided you are on the correct side.
findings.quote: These rapid vertical moves are caused by supply/demand imbalances and, in profile terms, this leaves a hole in the profile that, when revisited, has a high probability for fast price movement.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 240-245) 'Vertical Nondevelopment (Minus Development)', Figures 5.16-5.17; Trading Application #1 (pp. 275-278, Gold)
findings.notes: Crypto perps trade 24/7 with venue aggregate volume available, so volume-at-price profiles are computable, but aggregate-tape noise (HFT wash, funding-driven flow) makes the 'hole' definition venue- and lookback-sensitive - hence MEDIUM. The mechanism (vacuum traversal) is closely allied to the existing liquidity_vacuum_reentry family; new-family registry decision required. Feature input: volume-at-price sparsity in a price band.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Coiling breakout from a narrowing value range (Dynamic VAP)
findings.mechanism: progressively narrowing Unfair-High/Unfair-Low value ranges compress volatility; a wide-range bar breaking the top with a near-high close triggers directional expansion through prior low-volume structure
findings.setup_summary: Track a rolling value-range box (Unfair High / POC / Unfair Low) per timeframe. Consecutive narrowing boxes = market coiling (volatility decreasing, approaching horizontal development); wider boxes = volatility increasing (watch for trend exhaustion). On BTCUSDT 1h, a breakout occurs when price closes above the Unfair High (below Unfair Low) with a wide-range bar closing near its extreme; long entries on the 15m retest at the 15m box bottom (provided price stays >= POC of the VAP map).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close beyond the value-range boundary with an expanding bar after a period of narrowing ranges, and 8+ consecutively higher boxes followed by a pause box. Invalidation: close back inside the value range (breakdown of the breakout); failure to accelerate through a hole / prior POC zone.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry on the breakout bar close or the 15m retest; initial stop just below the top of the daily value range (tight), moved up via the 60m as price advances; targets = prior POCs to the left; exit when a new consolidating box forms at a prior POC (supply absorption).
findings.quote: The narrower the price range between an Unfair High and an Unfair Low--and the tighter the area of support and resistance--the more coiled the market is becoming.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 265-267) 'Refining Market Analysis and Trading Using TAS PRO Dynamic VAP'; Trading Application #2 (pp. 278-280, S&P e-mini)
findings.notes: The coiling concept is directly computable on 1h BTCUSDT (rolling value-range width percentile as a volatility feature) and the stop/target scheme (below box top, prior POCs) is PIT-safe. Maps to the range_compression strategy slug; candidate new expert family (volatility compression breakout) distinct from trend_pullback.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Fast-Trigger momentum turn with time-expiry (ATM FT)
findings.mechanism: a fast momentum oscillator turning up from oversold / down from overbought biases price in the turn direction for ~7.58 bars (empirically 66.32% of closes in the turn direction)
findings.setup_summary: With a higher-timeframe trend present (TSB trend-strength line present / multi-timeframe monthly->weekly->daily alignment), buy when the fast momentum line turns up from oversold (short when it turns down from overbought). Expect price to move in the turn direction or sideways for ~7.58 bars (rounded to 8). If no favorable movement or condition change occurs within ~8 bars, exit before the price stop.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: FT turn from overbought/oversold aligned with the higher-TF trend background. Invalidation: no movement in the turn direction within ~8 bars (the new trend may not be developing); the longer-timeframe FT turning against the position adds pressure.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the oscillator turn (bar close); time-stop at ~8 bars if no movement (half-cycle); initial stop outside the near-term volatility band; backtest claim: closes in the turn direction 66.32% over an average 7.583 bars (INDU, 10 years).
findings.quote: when the ATM FT turns up or down, price will move in the direction of the turn or sideways 66.32 percent of the time for a period on average of 7.583 bars.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch6 (pp. 291-300, 303-305) 'ATM Trigger', 'Trade When the Odds Are in Your Favor', Figures 6.3-6.19
findings.notes: The one genuinely empirical claim in Part 2 (a backtest, hence LITERATURE_SUPPORTED). The ~8-bar time-expiry independently corroborates V8's trend_pullback expiry_bars=8 and gives a momentum-oscillator entry alternative; the proprietary FT is proxy-able with any fast oscillator (e.g. stochastic/ROC) - transfer to perps is MEDIUM because INDU futures frequency and 24/7 BTC regime differ.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Preset-time no-movement exit (time-stop)
findings.mechanism: a position that produces no favorable price movement or no market-condition change within a preset time window is a dead thesis; exit before the price stop is hit
findings.setup_summary: For every new position define a preset movement deadline (half-cycle of the momentum oscillator ~= 8 bars, scaled by dividing the max holding period by ~8-9 to choose the trading timeframe). If the position makes no significant favorable price movement, or (for exhaustion entries) the market condition does not change in the trade's direction, by the deadline - exit regardless of stop distance. Re-establishing the position later is always permitted.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: deadline elapses without significant favorable movement / without condition change. Known cost: sometimes you exit and the market then moves in your original direction; the rule is accepted to improve overall performance.
findings.risk_geometry: Time-based exit independent of the price stop; stop remains as backstop; timeframe chosen so that holding period = 8-9 bars (e.g. 45-minute holding -> 5-minute bars).
findings.quote: New positions must make some price movement in your favor within a preset amount of time. Should you not get any significant price movement within that time limit, exit.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch6 (pp. 302-307) 'Using Time as Part of Your Risk Management', 'The Hardest Part of Any Strategy Is the Exit'
findings.notes: Directly implementable as a V8 lifecycle/dead-thesis rule: dead-thesis is already distinguished from stop exits in V8, and this adds a third exit - time-invalidation. Deterministic and cheap; no wall clock needed (bar-count based). Corroborates the time_stop starter slug.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Volatility-band stop placement (ATM Trade Velocity)
findings.mechanism: initial stops must sit outside the market's near-term volatility distribution, otherwise normal oscillation stops them out; profit/risk are quantified over fixed horizons (risk ~8 bars, profit ~34 bars)
findings.setup_summary: At entry, project a volatility funnel (standard-deviation confidence lines drawn outward from the entry, based on current volatility). Do not place initial stops inside the 1-2 standard-deviation band - price can and often does trade within it. Expect price to reach the projected profit line; if price hangs below the profit line over time, the position is weak (reduce/exit); above the strong line, consider adding.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Rule applies at entry and during management; a stop placed within the band is mislocated, not a trade trigger. The underlying position logic is invalidated by time (no progress to the profit line within the projected horizon).
findings.risk_geometry: Initial risk quantified over ~8 bars; profit expected over ~34 bars; stop outside the vol band (>=2 std dev), trail as the trade matures; distinct from a fixed ATR multiple in that it is distribution-based.
findings.quote: Be sure you don't place initial stops within these two areas, as price can and often does trade within it.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch6 (pp. 304-305) 'ATM Trade Velocity', Figure 6.16
findings.notes: Refines V8's stop_distance_atr / atr_stop concept: instead of a fixed ATR multiple, the stop distance is set to the 2-sigma band of a volatility forecast, which is directly computable on perp data (and leverage-appropriate). Candidate RiskGate admission check for existing experts' risk_geometry.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Minimum 4:1 reward-to-risk admission rule
findings.mechanism: only take trades with measured technical reward-to-risk >= 4:1, computed with a smaller-timeframe stop and a larger-timeframe target; fixed R-multiple exits are rejected in favor of expectation/time management
findings.setup_summary: Before entry, measure R:R from the chart: identify an Area of Opportunity in the larger timeframe, then use a smaller timeframe to locate a defined-risk setup - stop level from the smaller-timeframe setup, target from the larger timeframe. Do not take any trade below 4:1; if none exists on the timeframe, drop down a timeframe or two until a 4:1 opportunity appears. Do not manage trades to a fixed 3:1 target ('myth'): winning trades are managed by expectation, time, and market condition.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Admission gate, not a trigger: any candidate with R:R < 4:1 is rejected at admission (or moved to a lower timeframe where 4:1 exists).
findings.risk_geometry: Mixed-timeframe R computation (small-TF stop, large-TF target); R:R >= 4:1 required at admission; management is dynamic (time/condition based), not fixed-R.
findings.quote: Measure the technical reward to risk from the charts and do not take any trades that are less than 4:1 reward-to-risk ratio (R:R).
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 275, 280-281) 'Reward-to-Risk Considerations' & 'Conclusion: Trading Rules'; Ch6 (p. 305) 'The 3:1 Risk/Reward Myth'
findings.notes: Candidate RiskGate admission rule (V8's RiskGate currently uses target_r/stop_r fixed geometry). Note the 4:1 gate targets pre-transition balance-area setups with phase-transition upside; a fixed minimum-R gate interacts with V8's 1.0R targets and would need registry evaluation. Also the book's rejection of fixed 3:1 management argues for keeping V8's dynamic exits.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Exhaustion countertrend with condition-change confirmation
findings.mechanism: at trend extremes, momentum exhaustion (fast and slow triggers concurrently overbought/oversold against the trend) can mark a reversal, but only if the overall market condition changes within ~8 bars; otherwise the trend resumes
findings.setup_summary: At a mature vertical move (slowing price movement, decreased slope, overlapping retracements, divergence), look for momentum exhaustion (both fast and slow momentum lines concurrently oversold against the trend, then the fast line turns up). Enter countertrend only if the trend-condition coloring (trend bars / trend line) flips to the countertrend direction within ~8 bars, preferably before the fast line reaches the opposite extreme. If no condition change occurs within the window, the trend resumes - exit and do not add.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: exhaustion signal at an extreme (FT+ST concurrently against trend + FT turn). Confirmation: market condition change within ~8 bars. Invalidation: no condition change within ~8 bars -> trend resumes; the book explicitly warns most exhaustion signals are only a pause, and warns against reversing off a single timeframe unless price moves very fast (6-8 bars).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at the extreme (bar close); stop beyond the extreme/top; time-stop ~8 bars for condition change; typically used to trade around large positions (exit 20% in and out), not to reverse.
findings.quote: If you are buying/selling exhaustion, the condition of the market must change to the direction of your position within a preset amount of time. Should no change in condition occur within that time limit, exit.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch6 (pp. 297-307) 'ATM Exhaustion Alert', 'ATM Divergence Alert', 'Don't Fight the Trend', Figures 6.10-6.12
findings.notes: Countertrend at extremes is dangerous in high-leverage perps because funding and liquidation cascades can extend trends well beyond an exhaustion signal; the condition-change confirmation within ~8 bars is the essential falsifiable guard. MEDIUM for perps. Distinct from the with-trend momentum-turn finding (that entry requires trend background present; this entry fades an ending trend).
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Range balance fading (buy pivot lows / short pivot highs)
findings.mechanism: in a balanced (supply-constrained) market, fading the range extremes with a higher-timeframe bias captures rotation back toward the opposite extreme; the HVA acts as a magnet in balance
findings.setup_summary: Define a sideways range (>=2 relatively equal pivot highs and lows). Long only at range pivot lows with a higher-timeframe long bias; short only at range pivot highs with a higher-timeframe short bias (or both if undecided). In a mature balance, fade tests of the HVA favoring the POC side (long above POC, short below POC). In early-stage balance, fade only first or second tests of new range extremes (needs supporting confluences/divergences); do not trade the middle of a developing balance - most random, highest noise.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches a range extreme / HVA test. Invalidation: the extreme breaks (range expansion) - stop beyond the extreme; a transition to vertical phase kills the fade premise (the HVA 'magnet' begins repelling price).
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at range extremes / HVA tests (fade); stop beyond the opposite extreme of the HVA (or beyond the range extreme for early balance); first target = opposite extreme of the balance/range; beyond-range targets only in anticipation of a phase transition.
findings.quote: We trade sideways, nontrending markets as follows: Long: Buy only the price pivot lows of the range if you have a higher-timeframe long bias. Short: Sell/short only the price pivot highs of the range if you have a higher-timeframe short bias.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 224-226, 271-275) 'Trading Horizontal Markets', 'Mature Balance Trades', 'Early Stage Balance Trades', Figure 5.6
findings.notes: A complete range-fading spec for the mean_reversion_band slug: HTF-bias filtering, mature-vs-early balance maturity distinction, first/second-test fade rule, and the 'no middle of developing balance' rule. MEDIUM for perps because ranges break violently under funding/liquidation cascades; the HTF-bias and maturity filters are the load-bearing parts.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Five-player breakout liquidity accumulation
findings.mechanism: on a range breakout the four participant groups respond asymmetrically (novice sellers panic-cover at any cost, pro-sellers' tight stops convert to buying, pro-buyers add), so volume-at-price becomes one-sided and each successive prior pivot extreme taken out adds more one-sided flow - a self-reinforcing liquidity run
findings.setup_summary: On a breakout from a balance area, expect volume to become one-sided in the breakout direction (all or most of the volume moves to one side). Feature proposal: measure volume-at-price asymmetry at the breakout edge and the accumulation of one-sided volume as each successive prior pivot high/low is exceeded; wider-range non-overlapping bars confirm the flow. This fuels breakout follow-through and is the mechanism behind fast vertical moves.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Feature/mechanism input, not a standalone trigger. If volume does not become one-sided on breakout (balanced volume, quick failure), the breakout lacks the fuel for vertical continuation - a confirmation filter for breakout-family entries.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A (feature) - feeds the liquidity_sweep_reclaim / failed_breakout / hole-traversal mechanisms and breakout follow-through confidence.
findings.quote: The most remarkable part of this breakout is what is significant: all (or most) of the volume in this timeframe moves to one side of the market; in this example, to the upside.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 228-231) 'Four Market Participants--and Then a Fifth', Figure 5.11
findings.notes: In perps the counterpart of 'novice sellers panic-covering' is liquidation cascades + stop-runs, so the mechanism maps strongly, but one-sidedness must be measured on venue aggregate volume with wash-trade noise - hence MEDIUM. Proposed feature: breakout-direction volume share (volume-at-price asymmetry) as a participation-group feature usable by liquidity families.
findings.book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

findings.strategy_name: Pivot Support-2 reversal (buy near S2, target R1)
findings.mechanism: Pivot-derived support/resistance levels are the market's equilibrium reference; a multi-day decline into an oversold condition at the Support-2 level reverts toward Resistance-1, and price reversion toward the pivot is the causal bet.
findings.setup_summary: After a multi-day decline (the book's example: 5 days down) with an oversold oscillator (daily stochastics %K=66/%D=75 in example, described as 'oversold'), place a limit buy near the pivot-derived Support-2 level; stop below S2 at a fixed price distance; target Resistance-1 / just below the prior day's high; move the stop to breakeven once price advances a defined amount. Falsifiable on any timeframe with pivot levels computed from prior OHLC.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Invalidated if price closes through Support-2 (stop below S2); after a favorable move the stop is moved to breakeven, so thesis dead if price returns to entry.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit order at S2; stop: fixed price distance below S2 (10 points in the bond example); target: R1 (structure); breakeven stop after favorable move; short-horizon expiry (intraday/swing).
findings.quote: Look to buy near Support 2 since the primary support is projected to be lower than the previous day's low... Risk ten points... Profit objective: Look to sell near 101-10 (near today's price from Resistance 1 and below yesterday's high...).
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, Fig. 11.1 daily trade worksheet (p.195)
findings.notes: Pivot levels computed from rolling OHLC anchor cleanly on 24/7 perps (no exchange gaps), so S2 tags are mechanical. But 24/7 flow plus funding and leverage raise adverse-excursion risk at support, and the book's 'oversold' trigger is loose. Candidate family requires location features (pivot S1/S2/R1/R2) in marketstate; bars-anchored pivot window is a variant question.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Stop placement away from round-number levels
findings.mechanism: Round-number and quarter-fraction price levels concentrate resting orders and act as intraday support/resistance; stops placed exactly at them are preferentially run, so offset stops from these levels.
findings.setup_summary: Do not place buy stops exactly on round levels (bond/note fractions 08/32, 16/32, 24/32; grains 0.5/1.0; meats 0.25/0.50/0.75); place buy stops above and sell stops below those levels because they act as intraday support/resistance and collect stop orders. Crypto analogue: avoid stops exactly at psychological round prices (e.g., 100,000).
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - a stop-placement risk rule, not a trade thesis.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop price offset by a small buffer from the round level; applies to both entry stops and protective stops.
findings.quote: You generally want to put your buy stops above these levels and your sell stops below those levels as those prices can act as support and resistance on an intraday basis.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 12, 'Other Tactics and Techniques' (p.214)
findings.notes: Well-corroborated across the library (stop-run/stop-hunt literature). Crypto perps show strong clustering at round figures; no gaps makes fills at these levels more likely to be stopped exactly, and high leverage magnifies the cost of being run. Implementation: RiskGate offset for stops near integer/round price deciles.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Fractional risk-capital sizing (50% margin, 20% per-trade risk)
findings.mechanism: Capping deployed margin and per-trade risk to fractions of equity preserves the account through losing streaks; risking the full account on one position is ruin-concentrated.
findings.setup_summary: Trade only risk capital (money you can afford to lose). Use at most ~50% of investment capital as margin for any one trade, and risk at most ~20% of initial capital on a single trade; do not deploy 100% of margin capacity into one position, which a small adverse move can wipe out. Position size is a function of stop distance and the risk budget.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - a sizing rule; violated if per-trade risk exceeds the fixed equity fraction.
findings.risk_geometry: Position size = per-trade risk budget / stop distance; account-level margin cap (50%) and per-trade risk cap (20%).
findings.quote: Some money managers suggest using only 50 percent of your investment capital in any one trade and then risking 20 percent of your initial capital in that trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, 'A Dose of Reality' (p.196)
findings.notes: Directly feeds RiskGate deterministic admission: per-trade risk cap and heat cap on notional exposure. With perp leverage (10-125x), the 20% per-trade risk cap becomes even more binding. Book also stresses never risking the whole account ('It's okay to lose your shirt, just don't lose your pants...').
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Scale out half at profit, breakeven stop on the remainder
findings.mechanism: Booking partial profit transfers the risk on the remaining position to zero (breakeven stop), making it structurally hard to turn a winning trade into a loser while still participating in continuation.
findings.setup_summary: Enter with multiple contracts; when the market gives a decent profit, exit half the position; immediately move the stop to breakeven on the remainder; let the remainder ride for the continuation move. Falsifiable as a lifecycle rule: after first target, stop relocates to entry, remainder position persists.
findings.trigger_invalidation: If the market fails after the first exit, the breakeven stop exits the remainder at zero; the trade cannot become a net loss.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: multiple units at one level; partial target at ~1R (decent profit); stop moved to breakeven after partial exit; remainder runs with no fixed target.
findings.quote: Trade in multiple contracts, and get out of half of your positions when the market gives you a decent profit... If the market fails, then move your stop to breakeven so you have a chance to break even on the other half of the trade.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 12, 'Other Tactics and Techniques' (p.214)
findings.notes: Trade-management rule, venue-agnostic; maps to ExposureBook episode rules (partial close + stop re-peg to entry). Compatible with V8's one-exposure-per-direction rule if the position is scaled within a single exposure. This is the same 'move stop to breakeven' mechanic as the worksheet example in Ch. 11.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Pyramiding - add to winners at fixed price increments
findings.mechanism: In a trending move, adding units at fixed favorable increments compounds gains while using open-market profit as the risk base; early adds carry the most risk and later adds are funded by unrealized gains.
findings.setup_summary: Take a base position near a perceived low; add one unit every fixed price increment (book: every 20 cents, equal to one margin unit) as price advances, using resting limit buy orders; trail stops up with each add based on prior support or accrued profit; exit the full book at a defined top/level. Explicitly avoid the 'reverse pyramid' of adding larger sizes at higher prices, where a small setback wipes out all profit.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis dead if the first stop is hit before any add (risk = first add); a reverse-pyramid structure is identified as ruin-prone.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit orders at fixed increments (e.g., 20c apart = one margin unit); stops trailed below prior adds; initial risk = first position's stop distance; target = analyst-defined top.
findings.quote: You add positions every 20 cents higher... This tactic virtually trades using money made from the market rather than your own capital.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 12, 'Pyramiding' (pp.205-210)
findings.notes: Book itself warns it is 'leveraging leverage using more leverage', exposed to margin-raise and reverse-pyramid risk. In perps, funding paid on the full growing notional and high leverage make the 'market money' framing hazardous; treat as a position-scaling variant within one exposure, gated on regime, rather than a standalone expert.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Scale trading - averaging down near historical lows without stops
findings.mechanism: For physical commodities, production-cost and historical floors imply an eventual rebound; buying more in tranches at descending levels lowers average cost and pays off on the rebound.
findings.setup_summary: Set a base price near historical lows; buy tranches at fixed increments below the base as price falls; use NO stops; keep buying until price bottoms and turns up, then sell the accumulated position back to the market. Requires large reserve capital; margin calls and large drawdowns can blow out undercapitalized accounts before the rebound.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis only fails permanently if the asset never rebounds; interim invalidation is margin-call/undercapitalization, not a price stop.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: limit buys at descending fixed increments; no stop; exit on rebound (sell accumulated tranches); open-ended holding period with roll/expiry risk in futures.
findings.quote: You do not use stops. You keep buying on the way down until prices hit a bottom and begin to turn back up.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 12, 'Scale Trading' (pp.210-212)
findings.notes: The causal floor (production cost / physical demand) does not exist for a BTC perp, and the no-stop mandate directly conflicts with V8's RiskGate admission and stop-first risk framework. Funding accrues on a growing losing notional, and leverage converts the intended averaging-down into deleveraging-cascade exposure. Reject; the only transferable piece is tranche accumulation as a regime-gated variant of a value extreme - not worth a family.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Pre-weekly-close trend continuation (S&P Friday 10:30 a.m. rule)
findings.mechanism: Position-squaring and 'don't hold the bag over the weekend' behavior drives the trend formed mid-session to persist into the weekly close; margin-call and central-bank flow windows concentrate this effect.
findings.setup_summary: US equity futures: the intraday trend formed between 10:30 a.m. and noon on Fridays becomes the trend into the Friday close; day-trade with that established trend rather than fighting it. Book shows 12 weekly closes near the daily high/low, all but two exceptions being holiday sessions. Crypto analogue would be trend persistence into the weekly candle close (Sunday 00:00 UTC) or into funding boundaries.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Pattern broke on holiday/shortened sessions (2 of 12 examples); expects exceptions when the session structure differs.
findings.risk_geometry: Intraday entry with the established mid-session trend; exit at close; no stated stop/target.
findings.quote: The trend from 10:30 a.m. until 12 noon will be the trend going into the close of business on Fridays.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 12, 'Other Tactics and Techniques' (pp.212-213)
findings.notes: The exact 10:30-noon Friday window is US-session and weekly-close specific; perps have no Friday close. A falsifiable crypto analogue (trend persistence into the Sunday 00:00 UTC weekly close, or the last hours before an 8h funding payment) could be tested, but requires defining session boundaries that V8's replay does not currently model. Gate until a time/session feature group exists.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Stop-reversal when the setup is too obvious (fade crowded consensus)
findings.mechanism: When a setup is so universally recognized it 'can't fail', the information is already priced; its failure produces reversal momentum, so a reversing stop on the failed side converts the stop-loss into the entry.
findings.setup_summary: When a signal accumulates many confirmations (book: '10 different indications') and looks unable to fail, do not enter one-sided; use a stop reversal - place a reversing stop so that if the market stops you out, you are filled in the opposite direction, letting failure momentum offset the original loss. Conceptually adjacent to the failed-breakout family (liquidity vacuum reentry): the 'everyone sees it' breakout that fails is exactly the crowded-signal case.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Reversal thesis fails if the original side continues; risk is double-sided exposure at the reversal moment.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: reversing stop beyond the obvious level; risk = original stop distance; no stated target (momentum continuation).
findings.quote: Whenever you have a signal that is so strong that you think it can't fail... then use a stop reversal... What everyone else knows isn't worth knowing sometimes.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 12, 'Other Tactics and Techniques' (p.214)
findings.notes: Anecdotal rule of thumb; hard to feature 'crowdedness' from OHLC tape alone. Natural fit is as a refinement/variant of the existing failed_breakout family (crowded breakout -> reversal) rather than a new family. The reversing-stop mechanic also needs lifecycle work (flip direction on stop-out), which conflicts with V8's single-exposure rule; keep in backlog.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Buy-stop entry on channel/resistance breakout
findings.mechanism: Price trading through a defined channel/resistance point is the market 'proving' upside; a resting buy stop converts that proof into an entry, avoiding pre-trigger commitment.
findings.setup_summary: When price is contained in a channel/range, place a buy stop above resistance (or sell stop below support) and enter only if price trades through it; the market must prove direction by surpassing the level. This is a stop-triggered (intrabar) breakout entry rather than a bar-close entry.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No fill unless the level is traded through; a triggered stop fills at next available price with slippage.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: stop order beyond the level, fill at or near stop with slippage; protective stop on the opposite side of the channel; target beyond the opposite boundary.
findings.quote: you might place a buy stop above that area to enter a long position if the market moves that high. In other words, you are waiting until the market proves that it may go higher by surpassing a certain price or chart point.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, 'Stop Orders' (p.181)
findings.notes: Relevant to V8's entry-type modeling: current experts enter NEXT_BAR_CLOSE; the stop-entry variant fills intrabar when price trades through the level (market-if-touched semantics with slippage). Perps have no gaps, so stop fills are cleaner than in futures, but fast 24/7 moves can still gap the fill. Add stop-entry fill semantics (trigger at level, fill at next price) to the canonical simulator before screening breakout families.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Proportional time stop - half-and-half thesis check
findings.mechanism: A position's value decays with time if the thesis does not pay; re-evaluating at the halfway point of the expected horizon (or when half the premium/time value is gone) prevents holding a wasting position to full expiry.
findings.setup_summary: Enter with an explicit expected time horizon for the thesis to pay (e.g., 6 months for the coffee call). At the halfway point of that horizon - or when half the time/premium value has eroded - re-evaluate: exit, trim/salvage, or re-commit; do not silently hold a position whose time thesis has decayed.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - a time-management rule; triggers re-evaluation, not a hard exit by itself.
findings.risk_geometry: Expiry set at half the expected horizon (proportional time stop); exit/trim if no confirmation by then.
findings.quote: If half of the time value or half of the premium value erodes, reevaluate the position. Either get out of the options or salvage some premium by liquidating a portion of your position.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 13, 'Options Trading Steps' (p.224)
findings.notes: Framed for options time decay, but the general rule - check the thesis at a fixed fraction of the expected horizon - transfers to perps and refines V8's expiry_bars: expiry becomes a proportional-thesis check (e.g., by expiry/2 the trade must be within X of target) instead of a fixed bar count. Corroborates the 'time stop' starter concept.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Pre-committed mechanical order execution (plan then trade)
findings.mechanism: Placing entry and protective orders ahead of the session removes in-the-moment hesitation, fear, and greed from execution; the process runs mechanically regardless of the trader's emotional state.
findings.setup_summary: Do the analysis in a calm, undisturbed state (the author writes entries/exits on the weekend); place GTC entry and stop-loss orders before the session; then sit back - winners run, losers get stopped, and un-hit orders are cancelled at the horizon end. The book's worksheets add a defined risk factor and profit objective to every pre-placed order.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - an execution methodology rule.
findings.risk_geometry: Pre-placed entry + stop + target as a bracket; orders cancelled at period end if unfilled.
