findings.quote: On Monday mornings I place open orders (GTC) for clients based on that research, both entry and stop-loss orders. The next step is to sit back and wait. The process is all mechanical; no emotions hinder me.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, 'Your Trading To-Do List' (pp.198-199)
findings.notes: Execution methodology, corroborated across the library's psychology chapters. In 24/7 perps resting orders are the only way to trade unattended sessions, so pre-committed entry/stop/target brackets are the practical analogue of this rule. Reinforces V8's pre-planned risk_geometry (entry/target/stop/expiry fixed at proposal, not ad hoc).
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Close-confirmed entry/exit (stop-close-only basis)
findings.mechanism: Requiring the closing range (not an intrabar tick) to breach a level filters whipsaw by making the market 'prove' the move on the close before acting.
findings.setup_summary: Use stop-close-only semantics: exit only if the closing price/range breaches the stop level, and enter only if the market closes above/below a defined point. The book flags the danger: price can close well beyond the intended level, so adverse excursion is larger on the close.
findings.trigger_invalidation: N/A - an execution-basis rule; closes beyond the level are accepted with adverse-excursion cost.
findings.risk_geometry: Trigger evaluated at bar close (final range); entry/exit price may be far from the level on volatile closes.
findings.quote: This is a specific order that some traders use to make the market prove they are wrong when exiting a trade. It can also be used for entering a trade if the market is closing above or below a certain point.
findings.chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, 'Stop Close Only' (pp.181-182)
findings.notes: Direct corroboration of V8's NEXT_BAR_CLOSE entry convention (close-confirmed trigger) and of close-based dead-thesis checks: the market must prove on the bar close, not on an intrabar tick. The adverse-excursion caveat is a simulator-model note (close basis can fill far from the trigger level in volatile bars).
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

book_title: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics: How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators (2004), John L. Person - Part 2
The Essays of Warren Buffett: Lessons for Corporate America (1998) — Part 2 (IV Mergers & Acquisitions; V Accounting & Taxation; Epilogue)

findings.strategy_name: Leverage fragility / empty-sack risk gate
findings.mechanism: Extreme financial leverage converts a sound position into a fragile one; levered structures profit in booms but are destroyed in adversity, so the leveraged operator's 'easy success' is not evidence of a good business.
findings.setup_summary: RiskGate rule: reject or scale down any CandidateDraft whose effective leverage (notional/margin) or stop distance relative to liquidation price breaches a fragility cap. In the simulator, forced-deleveraging and liquidation cascades must be modeled as real costs, not ignored as tail events. Falsifiable: compare net OOS results of an expert family with vs. without the leverage cap at identical gross setups.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = candidate leverage or liquidation-proximity above the fragility cap; thesis-invalidation = a position whose margin is so thin that a normal ATR-sized adverse move forces liquidation is structurally rejected regardless of setup quality.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry/sizing rule, not a price geometry: stop distance must clear the liquidation price with margin, else no entry; heat cap per (instrument, direction) tightened when volatility is elevated.
findings.quote: It is hard for an empty sack to stand upright.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part IV.C Leveraged Buyouts, p.149 (Wesco letter, C.T. Munger)
findings.notes: The LBO discussion shows leverage-based gains are mostly tax/reshuffling effects plus a long-boom beta, not acquisition skill ('easy success in such transactions does not imply that success is easy in ordinary corporate acquisitions'). For perps the analog is explicit: leverage multiplies funding and liquidation fragility; a backtest family must be gated so leverage cannot manufacture apparent edge. Refines V8's existing heat cap in src/v8/risk.py.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Buy when macro-fear is at a peak (contrarian accumulation, ignore forecasts)
findings.mechanism: Fear peaks create price discounts that the fundamentalist exploits; macro forecasts are an expensive distraction, and the best purchases are made exactly when apprehensions are maximal.
findings.setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h, after a sharp drawdown accompanied by a realized-volatility spike and elevated participation (the observable fear proxy), enter LONG while apprehensions are at a peak rather than deferring; ignore all macro/political forecasts. Falsifiable: define fear proxy = drawdown depth percentile AND realized-vol percentile over a window; enter only when both are extreme.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = fear proxy at extreme (deep drawdown + vol percentile); invalidation = price fails to reclaim the prior swing low or fear persists beyond expiry without stabilization, indicating capitulation exhaustion did not occur.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE; stop below the fear-swing extreme (structure); target R-multiple; long expiry given slow sentiment repair.
findings.quote: we have usually made our best purchases when apprehensions about some macro event were at a peak. Fear is the foe of the faddist, but the friend of the fundamentalist.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue, pp.207-208
findings.notes: Directly extends the existing backlog family capitulation_exhaustion (src/v8/experts/capitulation.py, DATA_BLOCKED pending derivatives tape). Crypto is sentiment-driven 24/7 with funding and long-liquidation cascades that make fear peaks mechanically observable (negative funding, long liquidation sweeps), so the proxy is more concrete than in equities. No statistical case is made in the book (anecdotal), hence NARRATIVE.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Buy below intrinsic value (margin-of-safety discount entry / repurchase logic)
findings.mechanism: When market price sits at a wide discount to an independently-estimated fair value, buying returns $2 of present value for $1; the auction nature of security markets lets the buyer acquire value at a fraction of negotiated-acquisition prices.
findings.setup_summary: Define an anchor independent of price — for perps, a synthetic fair value such as a funding/carry-adjusted equilibrium or a realized-volatility-based valuation band. When price trades below anchor by a margin-of-safety threshold, enter LONG; when above by the same threshold, enter SHORT. Falsifiable: fixed discount threshold, fixed convergence horizon, stop below the discount-defining structural extreme.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger = discount-to-anchor exceeds the margin-of-safety threshold; invalidation = the anchor itself is repriced (fair value revision, e.g., funding regime change) or price fails to converge to anchor within the holding horizon, proving the discount was not a mispricing.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at bar close or limit at the discount level; stop beyond the structural extreme defining the discount; target = reversion to anchor (structure, not fixed R); long expiry because convergence is slow.
findings.quote: major repurchases at prices well below per-share intrinsic business value immediately increase, in a highly significant way, that value. When companies purchase their own stock, they often find it easy to get $2 of present value for $1.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part IV.A Sensible Stock Repurchases Versus Greenmail, p.147
findings.notes: Only genuinely actionable strategy family in this part. Crypto perps have no DCF intrinsic value, so the strategy is implementable only with an explicit synthetic anchor (funding/carry equilibrium or vol band); absent an anchor it is unfalsifiable. The 'auction market vs negotiated price' point maps to perp microstructure: continuous two-sided auction lets a patient buyer accumulate at auction-clearing discounts that a negotiated (market-order) purchase cannot get.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Investor gains equal business gains in the end (closed-system conservation)
findings.mechanism: Aggregate investor gains must equal the underlying business gains over time; price/value divergence only redistributes between buyers and sellers, and 'generally, the sophisticated have an edge over the innocents'.
findings.setup_summary: A falsification frame for V8: in perpetuals the closed system is even stricter than equities — there is no earnings accrual, and funding makes the market explicitly zero-sum minus fees. Therefore any claimed edge is a redistribution from the less-sophisticated side, and the baseline expectation is that the average participant loses to costs. Falsifiable: an expert family's net OOS return must exceed the cost drag (fees+funding+slippage) of simply holding exposure, or the 'edge' is illusory.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Applies to V8 verdicts, not to entries: no economic claim can be registered unless net-of-cost OOS return beats the passive-exposure baseline; this is a precondition for any registry promotion.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - evaluation frame; use the simulator's Binance USDM cost model to compute the passive baseline.
findings.quote: in the end, investor gains must equal business gains.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part V.E Intrinsic Value, Book Value, and Market Price, pp.189-190
findings.notes: Also: 'When the stock temporarily overperforms or underperforms the business, a limited number of shareholders receive outsized benefits at the expense of those they trade with.' This is the strongest structural caution in the book for any V8 claim and supports the existing NO_ECONOMIC_CLAIM default and frozen-OOS verification discipline.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Hold to compound; churn pays a transfer tax every cycle
findings.mechanism: Realizing gains periodically pays a tax/transfer cost on each cycle; a single internally-compounding holding beats a sequence of equal-return round-trips by a huge factor (book's $1 doubling example: ~$25,250 vs ~$692,000 over 20 years). Every asset switch incurs a 'transfer tax'.
findings.setup_summary: For the V8 simulator: quantify the compounding drag of turnover the way the book quantifies tax drag — taker fees, funding, and slippage paid on each round-trip compound against a family's gross edge. Falsifiable: simulate two variants of the same family at identical gross per-trade edge but different turnover and show net results diverge by the cost compound, matching the book's arithmetic.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Methodology check, not a trade: a high-turnover expert family must beat the low-turnover variant on net OOS after costs, or its gross advantage is a measurement artifact.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - cost-model lesson for src/v8/simulator.py (fill-at-close, Binance USDM cost model, funding accrual).
findings.quote: this deferred tax liability is equivalent to a very large transfer tax that is payable only if we elect to move from one asset to another.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part V.G Deferred Taxes, pp.195-196; Part V.J Taxation and Investment Philosophy, pp.205-206 (Li'l Abner tale)
findings.notes: Perps have no capital-gains tax, but funding + taker fees + slippage are the perp 'transfer taxes' paid on every position switch, and they compound identically. The 27:1 arithmetic is exact and reproducible, hence DESIGN_INFERENCE rather than NARRATIVE.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Owner earnings: net of maintenance costs, not 'cash flow'
findings.mechanism: Sustainable economic earnings = reported + non-cash charges - required maintenance reinvestment; quoting 'cash flow' (a)+(b) without subtracting maintenance (c) overstates sustainability, because 'over a five- or ten-year period, they must make the investment - or the business decays'.
findings.setup_summary: For V8 backtest economics: compute net edge = gross PnL - mandatory costs to stay in the market (funding paid while holding, rollover, borrow). A family that looks profitable on gross PnL may be net-negative once these maintenance costs are netted, mirroring the (a)+(b)-(c) formula. Falsifiable: re-rank expert families on net-after-maintenance edge and compare registry decisions.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Methodology check: any family whose edge depends on omitting persistent maintenance costs (funding on a 24/7 market) is rejected or re-evaluated on the net basis.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - evaluation/attribution lesson; funding accrual belongs in the simulator cost model and lifecycle hold accounting.
findings.quote: the company or investor believing that the debt-servicing ability or the equity valuation of an enterprise can be measured by totalling (a) and (b) while ignoring (c) is headed for certain trouble.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part V.D Owner Earnings and the Cash Flow Fallacy, pp.185-186 (Scott Fetzer example)
findings.notes: Funding is the perp maintenance cost par excellence: a long held through positive funding pays it continuously. The book's warning that EBITDA-style presentation is used to 'justify the unjustifiable' parallels promotional backtest reporting that omits funding and fees.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Accounting numbers are the beginning, not the end (source-integrity audit)
findings.mechanism: Reported figures can be 'as pliable as putty'; certified numbers carry false precision, so investors must reconstruct economic reality from primary facts rather than accept reported earnings at face value.
findings.setup_summary: For V8's marketstate and data pipeline: treat any vendor-reported or pre-computed series (funding rate, open interest, volume) as an 'accounting number' to be audited against the primary tape before it enters a PIT MarketState. Falsifiable: any feature group consumed by an expert must be reproducible from raw event-level data in the append-only store; series that cannot be reconstructed are excluded.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Data-governance rule: a feature source that fails reconstruction from the primary tape is quarantined, regardless of how much edge it appears to add.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - pipeline discipline for src/v8/marketstate.py and the PIT builder; supports the three-clock (event/available/ingested) rule.
findings.quote: investors must always keep their guard up and use accounting numbers as a beginning, not an end, in their attempts to calculate true 'economic earnings' accruing to them.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part V.B Look-Through Earnings, p.168; V.G Deferred Taxes (the $1.1B liability-vs-trade-creditor contrast, p.194)
findings.notes: Exchange-reported perp metrics (funding, OI, wash-inflated volume) are exactly the 'pliable putty' figures the book warns about; the look-through principle (judge by reconstructed economics, not reported line items) maps to V8's PIT reconstruction and source-integrity audit.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Beware the horse that walks fine (seller-timed quality)
findings.mechanism: The counterparty/seller knows more than the buyer and times the transaction for when the asset 'walks just fine'; buying into the most flattering presentation of quality is inherently adversely selected.
findings.setup_summary: A psychological guardrail for V8: when a setup's public justification is at its most consensus-flattering (peak open interest into highs, euphoric narrative), treat entry as adversely selected against the crowd and require independent verification instead of seller/crowd-supplied optimism. Falsifiable as a filter: reject candidates whose triggering narrative is consensus-positive at the moment of entry.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Filter, not a trade: candidates admitted on the strength of apparent quality at the point of maximum flattery are rejected; the filter is validated by comparing OOS results with the filter on vs off.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - psychology/filter lesson; pairs with the failed-breakout and liquidity_sweep families' reliance on frozen refs rather than narrative.
findings.quote: the seller of a business practically always knows far more about it than the buyer and also picks the time of sale - a time when the business is likely to be walking 'just fine.'
findings.chapter_anchor: Part IV.D Sound Acquisition Policies, p.151; also On Selling One's Business (financial-maneuverer buyer type, pp.155-156)
findings.notes: In perps the 'seller' is the retail crowd and liquidity providers; the book's warning that apparent quality at sale-time masks adverse selection maps to buying momentum at the point where everyone already knows the story. Also relevant: the ailing-horse anecdote ('when he's walking fine, sell him').
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Only swing at pitches in the happy zone
findings.mechanism: Disciplined selectivity: a hitter who swings at everything outside his zone drops from a .344 hitter to a .250 hitter; infrequency of acceptable opportunities is a sign of discipline, not of failure.
findings.setup_summary: For V8 expert screening: enforce a quality bar so a family only emits candidates meeting a minimum evidence threshold; the rarity of qualified candidates is expected ('infrequency of business acquisition may safely be predicted'). Falsifiable: a family forced to trade all near-threshold setups underperforms the same family trading only above-threshold setups on frozen OOS.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Methodology check: any family whose edge vanishes when the quality bar is tightened is evidence that the bar, not the setup, was the source of apparent edge.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - selection policy for the lab runner and registry screening gates.
findings.quote: If I have to bite at stuff that is out of my happy zone, I'm not a .344 hitter. I might only be a .250 hitter.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue, pp.208 (Ted Williams quote); also infrequency-of-acquisitions passage, p.151
findings.notes: Perp markets present near-infinite 'pitches' 24/7, so the selectivity lesson is directly testable: does the V8 family emit candidates selectively or does it trade every setup? The book frames patience as productive (dealing 'from strength').
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: The fat wallet is the enemy of superior results (capacity decay)
findings.mechanism: Capacity limits and base effects: high growth rates self-destruct as the base balloons ('in a finite world, high growth rates must self-destruct'), and a minimum-deployable size shrinks the opportunity universe.
findings.setup_summary: For V8: every candidate edge must be evaluated at a realistic deployment size, because perp depth and slippage scale with notional; a family that looks good at small notional may show decaying per-unit edge as size grows. Falsifiable: simulate each family at increasing notional and show net edge per unit declines beyond a capacity threshold.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Methodology check: registry promotion requires the frozen-OOS net edge to survive at the deployment-size simulation, not just at minimal notional.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - capacity/slippage lesson for src/v8/simulator.py and lab sizing.
findings.quote: A fat wallet ... is the enemy of superior investment results.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue, pp.207-208 (Sagan bacteria passage; $100M minimum-deployable rule)
findings.notes: The book's '$100 million minimum' shrinks the universe; the perp analog is that the exploitable depth of BTCUSDT at a given time window bounds how much of a backtest edge is real. Base effects (Sagan's bacteria) warn against extrapolating early-family results.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Double-dip decomposition: fundamental gain + one-time re-rating
findings.mechanism: Past returns came from two components: gains in intrinsic value plus a one-time bonus from market 'correction' of valuations; the re-rating component is not repeatable, so future returns have a single-dip.
findings.setup_summary: For V8 attribution: decompose each family's realized PnL into underlying-move capture vs. microstructure/funding timing vs. level-correction effects. A family whose edge is mostly a one-time 'correction' of a stale level (e.g., a mean-reversion to an anchor that has itself repriced) must not be extrapolated. Falsifiable: split OOS PnL by source; a family whose edge is dominated by non-repeatable correction components is not registry-promotable.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Evaluation frame, not a trade: verdicts on a family must be based on the repeatable component of its PnL, not the total.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - attribution lesson; supports the lab's per-episode logging and frozen-OOS verdict discipline.
findings.quote: our performance to date has benefited from a double-dip: (1) the exceptional gains in intrinsic value that our portfolio companies have achieved; (2) the additional bonus we realized as the market appropriately 'corrected' the prices of these companies.
findings.chapter_anchor: Epilogue, pp.207-208
findings.notes: For perps, the decomposition is directional-move capture vs. funding accrual vs. liquidation-timing; funding-heavy profits are the analog of the one-time re-rating bonus and should not be extrapolated as an independent edge (funding is a transfer, not a source).
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Evaluate on look-through drivers, not the short-term scoreboard
findings.mechanism: Performance should be judged by the economic driver (business value) rather than by short-term market price; the scoreboard (price) is the final arbiter in the long run, but decisions are made by watching the playing field.
findings.setup_summary: For V8: an expert should be evaluated on whether its causal behavior/mechanism actually occurred and its MarketState inputs were valid, not on short-window PnL; price outcome is the final arbiter at OOS time, but evidence gates and registry decisions are mechanism-based. Falsifiable: an episode is scored on mechanism validity (setup conditions, still_valid holds) before PnL is examined.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Evaluation frame: verdicts that flip purely with short-window PnL noise are rejected in favor of mechanism-based scoring.
findings.risk_geometry: N/A - evaluation methodology for the lab runner and registry gates.
findings.quote: In investing, just as in baseball, to put runs on the scoreboard one must watch the playing field, not the scoreboard.
findings.chapter_anchor: Part V.B Look-Through Earnings, p.170 (portfolio goal: maximize look-through earnings a decade out)
findings.notes: Also in this part: 'we search for situations in which both approaches give us the same answer' (faith + analysis agreement, p.159) — i.e., conviction (behavioral) and analysis (mechanism) should converge before acting. Reinforces V8's falsification stance that an expert is one falsifiable hypothesis about a behavior family, judged on mechanism before PnL.
findings.book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

findings.strategy_name: Pivot point S1/R1 reaction with candle confirmation (P3T)
findings.mechanism: prior-period equilibrium P=(H+L+C)/3 with derived S1/S2/R1/R2 levels act as reference points where price reacts; prior support/resistance reverse roles after a breakout
findings.setup_summary: Compute P,R1,R2,S1,S2 from the prior period HLC (daily/weekly/monthly; for 24h markets use the full-session range and combine all sessions). When price trades at or near weekly or monthly S1/R1 (strongest when weekly and monthly numbers converge), wait for a confirming reversal candle (hammer at S1, shooting star/harami/engulfing at R1), then enter next-bar-open in the reaction direction. Trade only the FIRST test of the level. Target the opposite pivot level; stop beyond the swing extreme.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches S1 or R1 within a small tolerance and a confirming candle completes. Thesis invalidation: a decisive close beyond the pivot level (level fails as reaction point); also abandon after repeated tests of the same level ('if you go to the well one too many times, the well will run dry').
findings.risk_geometry: entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after reversal candle at pivot; stop = swing extreme beyond the level (below the established low / above the high, often close-only); target = opposite pivot (R1 after S1 bounce) or R2/S2; expiry = one pivot cycle (intraday for daily numbers, swing for weekly/monthly).
findings.quote: Trading for the day will usually remain between the first support and resistance levels as these professional floor traders make their markets. As a general rule, I usually will only take a trade based off the first test of the S1 or R1 pivot number.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 6, 'Finding Equilibrium' and 'P3T Signals'
findings.notes: Book gives many worked cases (sugar monthly S1 6.09 vs low 6.11; S&P weekly S2 781.67 vs 771.30) but no statistics - practitioner heuristic. Weekly/monthly pivots are computable on 24/7 BTCUSDT with no gap distortion, and the book explicitly handles 24h markets by using the full-session range. Caveat: self-fulfilling following is a concentration risk, and high-leverage perps attract stop-hunts near round/pivot numbers. Core of the book's P3T = pivot + candle + oscillator multi-verification ('verify, verify, verify').
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Reversal candlesticks at support/resistance after extended moves (hammer, shooting star, doji, engulfing, harami cross)
findings.mechanism: single or multi-candle rejection at a prior price extreme reveals order-flow exhaustion and a reversal of short-term direction; the more prior candles a benchmark candle engulfs, the stronger the signal
findings.setup_summary: After an extended trend or near prior S/R/pivot levels require a reversal candle: hammer (lower shadow at least 2x body, body at upper end, little/no upper shadow) at support; shooting star (long upper shadow, body low, little/no lower shadow) at resistance; doji after a long white candle near a top; bearish/bullish engulfing covering the prior body; bearish harami cross (long white candle then doji inside its body) after a long advance. Enter on next-bar confirmation; tops need more confirmation than bottoms ('tops take longer to form than bottoms' - look for a SECOND bearish candle at resistance).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: reversal candle completes within 1-2 bars of a prior extreme; bullish patterns require next-candle validation (e.g., inverted hammer needs a white candle opening above it). Thesis invalidation: close beyond the pattern extreme; failure of next-bar confirmation.
findings.risk_geometry: entry NEXT_BAR after confirmation; stop beyond the candle extreme (for hammer below the low, close-only per book); target = prior structure (pivot S1/R1, trendline, or candle midpoint as first support for 'pillar of strength'); expiry = 2-3 bars intraday, longer on weekly charts.
findings.quote: The lower part, or the shadow, should be at least twice the length of the real body... The more candles that are engulfed, the more power behind the signal!
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 4, 'Candle Patterns' and 'Reading Candle Charts'
findings.notes: Nison-style practitioner patterns, anecdotal evidence. On 1h BTCUSDT these shapes are computable and common; high leverage manufactures long wicks (sweeps) that form hammer/shooting-star shapes, which cuts both ways (patterns fire on liquidity sweeps that may continue). Best consumed as a behavior family on top of location features (prior extreme / pivot).
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Climax volume + open-interest decline reversal (blow-off top / capitulation bottom)
findings.mechanism: after an extended trend, an unusual volume spike with declining open interest (longs liquidating, shorts panic-covering) signals a climaxing market and a major trend reversal
findings.setup_summary: In an established trend, price makes wider-than-normal daily swings with unusually strong volume while open interest declines. Three characteristics required for a climax top or bottom: (1) wider-than-normal range/volatility, (2) heavy volume, (3) declining open interest. Rising price + falling OI indicates short-covering rather than new longs (weakening, potential reversal). Treat as a major reversal warning and do not add to trend positions.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: volatility expansion + volume spike + OI decline over the same window at the end of a long trend. Thesis invalidation: OI resumes expansion while price continues in trend direction (new money entering = trend intact).
findings.risk_geometry: entry after confirmation (not on the spike bar itself); stop beyond the extreme made during the climax; target = prior range/trendline; expiry = swing (days-to-weeks).
findings.quote: if a substantial daily market price increase or decrease occurs after a long steady uptrend or downtrend and has an unusually high volume period, it is considered to be a blow-off top or bottom and can signal a market turning point or trend reversal
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 5, 'Volume' and 'Putting the Data Together'
findings.notes: Refines the existing DATA_BLOCKED capitulation backlog family. Advantage over the book's futures: perp open interest is real-time (the book laments OI is published next-day), so the OI condition is directly testable; funding adds a pressure gauge the book lacks. Caveat: perp OI mixes hedgers and leveraged specs and direction is not visible in raw OI, so OI decline alone is ambiguous.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Inside bar / range-compression breakout
findings.mechanism: range compression (current bar wholly inside the prior bar's range) concentrates resting orders; a breakout of the range releases them directionally with continuation
findings.setup_summary: Current bar's high and low both within the previous bar's high-low (inside bar; close is not important). Place a buy stop above / sell stop below the inside bar's range and enter on the breakout, expecting continuation. Generalizes to triangles/pennants as continuation patterns: the time the consolidation took to form is the measuring distance, and breakouts are strongest when the pattern does NOT coil all the way to the apex.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: a bar closes whose range is fully inside the prior bar, then the next bar trades through either bound. Thesis invalidation: false breakout closing back inside the range (then treat as failed breakout); note the longer a triangle takes to form, the less power the breakout usually has.
findings.risk_geometry: entry stop-order beyond the inside-bar extreme; stop = opposite side of the inside bar, or below the first low point forming the support line for triangles; target = measured move (formation height projected from breakout, flagpole distance); expiry = 3-5 bars intraday.
findings.quote: The whole current range is within the previous bar's range... A breakout either way of the inside bar range gives a buy or sell signal, based on the theory that there is a continued price move in the direction of the breakout.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 3, 'Bar Charts' (inside bar) and Ch 5, 'Triangle Chart Patterns' and 'Flag Formations'
findings.notes: 1h BTCUSDT produces frequent inside bars and tight consolidations; 24/7 trading with no close-gaps makes the range bounds unambiguous. High leverage raises the cost of the false-breakout branch, so the failed-breakout exit semantics matter. This is the volatility-contraction family V8 can formalize cleanly.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Oops gap-fade (stop-entry through the prior extreme after a gap open)
findings.mechanism: a gap open beyond the prior extreme is an emotional overshoot of the chasing crowd; when price trades back through the prior extreme it traps those orders and reverses, so entering via a stop through the extreme exploits the trapped flow
findings.setup_summary: When a market gaps below the prior session low, place a BUY stop a few ticks above the prior low; when it gaps above the prior high, place a SELL stop a few ticks below the prior high. The stop triggers on reclaim of the prior extreme. Larry Williams' method; works best in countertrend conditions (e.g., sell-oops in an uptrend). The stop entry also protects against a true breakaway gap (new valuation).
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: gap open through a prior session extreme, then price trades back through the extreme triggering the stop. Thesis invalidation: the gap is a genuine breakaway (no reclaim); price reclaims but fails to follow through (double-invalidation).
findings.risk_geometry: entry = stop order just beyond the prior extreme (buy stop above prior low / sell stop below prior high); stop = a few ticks on the far side; target = gap fill / countertrend distance; expiry = intraday, at most 1-2 sessions ('If you were to hold this position more than one day without proper stop or risk management, a nice short-term trade could have resulted in a loss').
findings.quote: When a market opens lower than the previous day's low, a trader should place a buy stop a few ticks above the previous day's low... These reactions tend to work better in countertrend conditions.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 5, 'Oops Signal'
findings.notes: True session gaps are rare in 24/7 BTCUSDT (no overnight close), so raw applicability is limited; however the mechanism - price opens beyond a prior extreme then reclaims it, trapping the chasers - is exactly the existing failed_breakout / liquidity_sweep_reclaim family. Recommend treating the oops as a gap-open VARIANT of those experts (an entry-with-stop refinement), not a new family.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Fibonacci retracements, extensions and projected targets (confluence with pivots)
findings.mechanism: price corrections and extensions cluster at Fibonacci ratios (0.382/0.50/0.618/0.786 retracements; 1.272/1.618 extensions) because orders concentrate there; projected targets = move length x ratio added to the retracement point
findings.setup_summary: After an initial A-to-B move, a pullback to C: ratios 0.382/0.50/0.618/0.786 of the A-B move define support/resistance zones. Upside projections = A-B length x (0.618 / 1.00 / 1.618 / 2.618) added to point C (or retracement level). When a Fibonacci target coincides with a pivot R1/S1 or a prior MA crossover, the confluence is treated as a high-probability reaction/exit point. 100% retracement = double bottom retest; 1.272/1.618 extensions project support below a broken initial low.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price pulls back into a ratio zone with reversal-candle or momentum confirmation. Thesis invalidation: ratio zone fails - price exceeds the 0.786 retracement (trend likely over) or breaks the 1.272 extension.
findings.risk_geometry: entry at the ratio zone with confirmation; stop beyond the ratio (below 0.786 retracement / above 1.618 extension); target = the projected extension or a coincident pivot level; expiry = swing.
findings.quote: If you apply a Fibonacci ratio multiplier of 1.272 percent or 1.618 percent of the initial move, you can determine potential support beneath the market once it has taken out the initial low.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8, 'Fibonacci Numbers'
findings.notes: No statistical backing in the book (anecdotal; author notes 'uncanny coincidence' with pivot calculations). Best role in V8: a location feature-group input that enriches the existing location features with ratio-derived S/R candidates, and as confluence for the pivot_reversal family - not a standalone expert. Difficulty flagged by the book itself: identifying the peaks and troughs to measure from.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Contrarian sentiment extremes (bullish consensus / VIX / put-call / COT -> funding + positioning for perps)
findings.mechanism: when positioning is one-sided at an extreme, the marginal buyer/seller is exhausted and price is vulnerable to reversal; volatility and fear gauges are contrarian - extreme complacency marks tops, extreme fear marks bottoms
findings.setup_summary: Bullish consensus near 75-85% after a prolonged uptrend, or a low fear/volatility gauge while price is at highs, or extremely one-sided positioning (COT: small specs extreme one way, commercials/large specs opposite at an extreme price) -> anticipate a correction. Extreme put-to-call readings signal bottoms; extreme low readings signal tops. Crypto analogs: funding rate at sustained extremes, extreme long/short positioning, high perp OI at highs, margin-requirement changes. Always confirm with price action before fading.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: sentiment gauge reaches its historical extreme band while price sits at a corresponding price extreme. Thesis invalidation: sentiment stays extreme and price keeps trending (extremes persist in leverage-driven markets); the book itself warns 'never get bearish in the hole' and that a low VIX does not always mean price will drop (volatility can rise from rallies).
findings.risk_geometry: entry only after price confirmation (candle/pivot signal) since sentiment alone is timing-weak; stop beyond the swing extreme; target = prior support/mean or pivot level; expiry = swing.
findings.quote: The bottom line: When everyone is bullish, don't join them... 'Buy it when nobody wants it, and sell it when everybody has got to have it.'
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 9, 'Market Vane', 'Commitments of Traders', 'Put-to-Call Ratio', 'VIX', 'Summary'
findings.notes: Perp crypto has real-time funding rate, OI and long/short ratios - closer analogs to COT/VIX than equity data. But positioning data persists extreme in strong trends and perp leverage makes contrarian timing expensive; the book's own caveats (media lag: 'by the time it gets on the news, the move is probably over') support using this as a regime/confirmation overlay rather than a standalone entry.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: MA crossover (golden/dead cross) and test-of-crossover as support/resistance
findings.mechanism: short-term vs long-term moving average crosses mark trend transitions, and the crossover point itself acts as a future S/R reference because it is the price where signals were generated
findings.setup_summary: With 3/9/18-period EMAs (or 5/10/20 weekly): golden cross (short crosses above long) = buy, dead cross = sell. Distinctive claim: markets often test the crossover point rather than the prior high/low, so a retest of a prior crossover level is a trade reference. Confluence with weekly/monthly pivots at the same price is a strong reversal setup (crude oil $31 example). Fails in ranges - the book states markets are trending only ~1/3 of the time.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: cross occurs or price returns to a prior crossover level. Thesis invalidation: whipsaw in a trading range (signals fire on every gyrating cross) - requires a trend/regime filter; exit if price crosses back.
findings.risk_geometry: entry at cross or at retest of the crossover level; stop beyond the swing low or just past the level (silver example: buy $4.45-4.49, stop below $4.38 prior low); target = trend continuation, scale out where MAs act as support; exit discipline: at 100% of initial margin return, take half off and trail the stop on the remainder above the 3-day and 9-day MA.
findings.quote: A lot of time you will see that a market does not rally to test the old highs but, instead, goes up to test the point of the moving average crossover.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8, 'Moving Averages'
findings.notes: Directly relevant to V8's existing trend_pullback family (already consumes ema_fast/ema_slow). The distinct refinement is the 'test-of-crossover as S/R' behavior and the pivot/MA confluence gate. Standalone cross trading on 1h BTCUSDT would whipsaw in ranges; use as a trend filter / existing-family variant rather than a new active expert.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Oscillator divergence (MACD / stochastic) - false-extreme reversal
findings.mechanism: price makes a new extreme while the momentum oscillator makes a weaker extreme - the move lacks participation and is a false/fragile extreme prone to reversal
findings.setup_summary: Bullish divergence: price makes a lower low vs a prior low while stochastics/MACD makes a higher low (false bottom). Bearish divergence: price makes a higher high while the oscillator makes a lower high (weak top). Stochastic rules: %K crossing below %D above 70 with both pointing down = hook sell; %K crossing above %D below 30 with both pointing up = buy. Works in volatile/choppy conditions; oscillators give false signals in steady trends. Confirm with pivot target or candle pattern before acting.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence forms at a pivot S/R or after an extended trend. Thesis invalidation: in strong trends oscillators stay overbought/oversold and keep generating false signals (book: during a whole downtrend stochastics kept printing buy signals; only the >75% cross was the classic sell).
findings.risk_geometry: entry after price confirmation (%K/%D cross or confirming candle); stop beyond the extreme of the divergent bar; target = prior extreme or pivot; expiry = 1-2 days for swing use.
findings.quote: This is a condition where the market price makes a low that is lower than a previous low but the underlying MACD pattern makes a higher low. This divergence indicates that the low is weak or a false bottom... and signals a potential price reversal.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8, 'Stochastics' and 'Moving Average Convergence/Divergence'
findings.notes: Computable on 1h BTCUSDT but premature in strong perp trends; fits the existing V8 vocabulary as a response feature (oscillator response to price). Backlog candidate whose edge must be tested against trend-following baselines before formalization.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: 8-to-10 new records exhaustion (consecutive new-high/new-low streak + reversal candle)
findings.mechanism: after 8-10 consecutive new highs or new lows the trend has run its course; a reversal candle appearing within 1-2 bars of the 8th-10th record confirms exhaustion
findings.setup_summary: Count consecutive sessions (bars) that print a new high (uptrend) or new low (downtrend). When the count reaches the 8-10 band and a reversal candle (hammer, doji, shooting star) appears within one or two bars, fade the trend: after the 8th-9th new low, buy with a close-only stop below the lowest low; after the 8th-9th new high, sell with a close-only stop above the highest high. The stop is close-only because 'if the market truly is ready to turn around, it should not close below the established low.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: streak count in the 8-10 band AND reversal candle within 1-2 bars. Thesis invalidation: bar closes beyond the extreme (close-only stop); streak extends past ~10 records; also the inverse pattern can recur (book shows the 8-10 setup repeating on the dollar index downtrend).
findings.risk_geometry: entry NEXT_BAR after confirmation candle; stop = close-only below the lowest low / above the highest high; target = prior consolidation or trendline; expiry = swing; 'the longer the time period, the longer the trade signal may work' (weekly charts give longer trades than daily).
findings.quote: when the market price either advances or declines by making eight to ten new highs or lows, it can signal that the advance or decline should subside... put a stop close-only order below the lowest low
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 4, 'Reading Candle Charts' (8 to 10 new records)
findings.notes: Novel, fully quantifiable (streak counter is deterministic) and frequent on 1h BTCUSDT. The close-only stop maps exactly to V8's bar-close semantics. Falsifiable: measure whether streaks in the 8-10 band with a reversal candle precede reversals more often than baseline. Candidate for screening as a counter-trend family with tight heat cap.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: 1-2-3 W-bottom / M-top swing breakout (confirmed by close through the reaction extreme)
findings.mechanism: a failed retest of a prior extreme (higher low on retest) followed by a close through the reaction high confirms accumulation and triggers a reversal breakout; measured objectives come from the head-and-shoulders neckline projection
findings.setup_summary: W bottom (1-2-3): after a downtrend, price makes a low (1), rallies to a reaction high (2), retests the low WITHOUT undercutting it (3 = higher low), then closes above the reaction high (2) -> buy signal. Inverse M top: price makes a high (1), falls to an interim low (2), rallies below the prior high (3 = lower high), then closes below the interim low (2) -> sell. Head-and-shoulders variant: entry on neckline break; measured objective = distance from shoulder highs (or head) to the neckline projected from the neckline.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close through the point-2 reaction extreme (not an intraday spike). Thesis invalidation: retest undercuts the prior low (higher-low premise broken, becomes continuation); close back through the breakout level.
findings.risk_geometry: entry NEXT_BAR after the confirming close; stop below point-1 low (or point-3 low) / above point-1 high; target = measured objective (leg distance, or H&S neckline projection); expiry = swing.
findings.quote: the price falls back again to retest the low but does not go as low as the previous low (point 3), followed by another price rally that goes beyond the first reactionary high, generating a buy signal
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 5, 'M Tops, W Bottoms, or 1-2-3 Patterns' and 'Head-and-Shoulders Tops or Bottoms'
findings.notes: Structurally matches the existing DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family. Close-based confirmation suits V8's bar-close model and avoids intraday fake breaks. The H&S measured-move is a secondary pattern (more subjective; lower priority).
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

findings.strategy_name: Scale-out and stop-management rules (half-off at 100% margin return, trailing stops, close-only stops)
findings.mechanism: locking in half the position at a target and trailing the stop on the remainder converts a winner's R:R asymmetry into guaranteed partial profit while preserving upside; close-only stops filter intraday noise so a correct thesis is not stopped out
findings.setup_summary: Exit/risk rules extracted from the book: (1) if a trade makes 100% of the initial margin requirement, liquidate half the position (single contract: take the whole trade off) and trail the stop on the remainder above/below the 3-day and 9-day moving averages; (2) do NOT move a stop to breakeven while price is still at breakeven - wait until price has actually advanced, or you get stopped out prematurely on a correct thesis; (3) use close-only stops when a thesis depends on the close ('a regular stop could be triggered on an intraday move, and then the market could snap right back up and take me out of the trade'); (4) always use stops and know the loss objective before entry; (5) risk/reward plan from entry ('a trading plan should include the initial entry position, the risk management loss objective, and the targeted profit objective').
findings.trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches the scale-out target (100% margin return) -> reduce half, trail stop. Never trigger: moving a stop to breakeven prematurely; holding without a stop.
findings.risk_geometry: exit-first design: stop = close-only beyond structure (below low / above high); target = opposite pivot or MA level; expiry = bars; scale-out = 1/2 at first target, remainder trailed.
findings.quote: Rule of thumb: If you make 100 percent of your initial margin requirement, get out of the trade if you are a one-contract trader. Multiple position traders should move stops down and get out of half of their positions.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch 8, 'Moving Averages' (rule of thumb); Ch 6, cotton P3T trade (close-only stop at 32.20); Ch 1, 'Holding Penalty'
findings.notes: Directly actionable in V8's RiskGate and lifecycle: a 'reduce-at-100%-margin-return' lifecycle rule, a 'close-only stop' option (already aligned with bar-close fills), and the 'no premature breakeven stop' rule. The 100%-of-margin threshold is a specific, testable parameter. Also contains the book's core psychology lessons ('when you are wrong, know when to get out'), which support existing risk rules rather than new mechanics.
findings.book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

book_title: University of Berkshire Hathaway: 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting (Part 1: 1986-2009)

findings.strategy_name: Margin of Safety (large discount between price and estimated value)
findings.mechanism: a dramatic gap between price and a conservatively estimated value absorbs miscalculation and worse-than-average luck; the asymmetry protects the buyer over time
findings.setup_summary: Act only when price sits at a large discount to a conservatively estimated value: Buffett estimates an asset at X to 3X and attempts to buy at 1/2X ('the gap should be dramatic, not a dollar of value for 97 cents'). Translated to a perp trade: require a minimum reward:risk asymmetry (target R clearly above stop R, ideally >=2:1) so the position survives miscalculation, and reject any entry where price is near the thesis value.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Thesis is invalid if the estimated value itself falls (the underlying business/catalyst deteriorates) rather than the discount merely closing; a discount that only closes because price rises toward value is a win, not an invalidation.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry at a large discount to a frozen estimate of value; the margin itself is the protection (no stop specified by the book); requires target R > stop R with a minimum asymmetry buffer.
findings.quote: When you build a bridge, you insist it can carry 30,000 pounds, but you only drive 10,000-pound trucks across it.
findings.chapter_anchor: 1986 'Value Investing' section; 1989 'Intrinsic Business Value (IBV)' ('if he and Munger get a value of X to 3X for an asset, then they attempt to buy it at 1/2X')
findings.notes: BTCUSDT has no fundamental cash-flow value, so the transferable core is the asymmetry gate: require reward:risk >1:1 in risk_geometry so miscalculation is survivable. Current V8 experts use target_r 1.0 / stop_r 1.0; this argues for a required asymmetry floor on formalized experts.
findings.book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

findings.strategy_name: Crisis Dislocation Buying (buy when forced sellers are price-insensitive)
findings.mechanism: forced sellers (margin calls, redemptions, panic, 'the electronic herd') sell regardless of price, pushing price far below value; the buyer with dry powder captures the reversion when selling exhausts
findings.setup_summary: After a violent forced-selling dislocation, buy while the market is paralyzed and hold for reversion: 1974 equities, 2002 junk bonds at 35-40% YTM (back to 6% in 18 months), Feb-2008 auction-rate munis at 10% yields (back to 4%), Korean stocks at 3x earnings. In perp crypto this maps to buying after liquidation cascades / deeply negative funding flushes where price has overshot; 'any calls you get on Sunday, you're going to make money' - seriously distressed sellers signal the opportunity.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Dislocation persists and never reverts because the underlying thesis was genuinely broken (credit/default event, not a liquidity event) - the muni episode was a liquidity dislocation, the subprime collapse was both, and Buffett refuses to catch a fundamentally broken asset.
findings.risk_geometry: Buy only where price is dramatically below a frozen value estimate; no fixed stop given - the margin of safety is the protection; the constraint is having dry powder at the moment of panic (Berkshire keeps a minimum cash reserve).
findings.quote: The key is to buy when others are paralyzed. Stocks in 1974. Junk bonds in 2002.
findings.chapter_anchor: 2006 'Opportunity Cost'; 2008 'Municipal Bond Dislocations'; 2005 'Hair Trigger'
findings.notes: Strongly corroborates the existing liquidity_sweep_reclaim family and the backlogged capitulation family; proposes behavior_family_candidate cascade_exhaustion_buy (mechanism forced_selling_dislocation) as a lower-frequency variant: buy the flush once the forced seller is exhausted rather than the wick-reclaim form.
findings.book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

findings.strategy_name: Stop-Run Cascade (clustered stop-loss logic becomes a doomsday machine)
findings.mechanism: when many participants share identical stop-loss logic, triggering one stop auto-triggers the next - the shared logic converts a small move into a self-feeding cascade ('pouring gas on a fire')
findings.setup_summary: Identical stop/automated-selling logic across many players creates cascades: Black Monday's portfolio insurance was 'a bunch of stop/loss orders, but done automatically... they created a doomsday machine that kept selling and selling.' In perp crypto the analogue is liquidation cascades and stop clusters below key levels. Two implications: (a) do not place your own stop in the obvious cluster where it becomes the harvested liquidity; (b) the cascade itself manufactures the overshoot a liquidity-sweep buyer wants.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The cascade stalls once the automated/forced sellers are exhausted (all stops and liquidations consumed); price reclaims the swept level - the sweep is a harvesting event, not a change in trend.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop location is itself a risk decision: stops should sit at structural levels and outside the crowd's cluster, not in the obvious pool; stop placement must assume the stop may be swept before thesis invalidation.
findings.quote: They created a doomsday machine that kept selling and selling.
findings.chapter_anchor: 2007 'Derivatives and the Crowded Trade' (Black Monday / portfolio-insurance analysis)
findings.notes: Corroborates the liquidity_sweep_reclaim expert (wick through prior extreme, reclaimed by close). Mechanism_family_candidate stop_run_cascade, behavior_family_candidate clustered_stop_harvest. The risk-rule output is the more actionable piece for V8: stop geometry must avoid the obvious cluster.
findings.book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

findings.strategy_name: Hidden Correlation = Unrecognized Concentration
findings.mechanism: exposures that look independent all correlate in a stress event; if you do not price the correlation you carry an unrecognized concentration of risk
findings.setup_summary: Assume correlations go to 1 in a crisis before taking the book: 'when telecom debt collapsed, people found that all of it was correlated'; the subprime mortgage mess correlated across instruments Berkshire had never linked. For a perp book this means BTC/ETH/alt longs, funding carry, and basis positions are ONE risk in a crash, and heat must be capped as if one instrument - never by per-instrument or per-direction limits alone.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Standing rule, not an episodic setup; it binds continuously and is strongest exactly when single-instrument risk measures look lowest.
findings.risk_geometry: Aggregate book exposure cap computed under a correlation->1 stress assumption; do not rely on per-instrument diversification to reduce heat in the tail.
findings.quote: When things go bad, all kinds of things correlate that you wouldn't think of. If you are not aware of these correlations, you have an unrecognized concentration of risk.
findings.chapter_anchor: 2003 'Correlation'; 2005 'Correlation of Risk'
findings.notes: Reuses starter slug correlated_exposure_cap. Strengthens the existing V8 one-exposure-per-(instrument,direction) rule and the heat cap: the cap must aggregate under the assumption that all open exposures are one exposure in a cascade.
findings.book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

findings.strategy_name: Ruin Avoidance - Anything Times Zero Is Zero
findings.mechanism: one event that zeros the account destroys the entire compounded record no matter how good every other year was; leverage is the typical cause because a single margin-call day converts an open position into forced liquidation
findings.setup_summary: Design the book so no single event can wipe it out: 'anything times zero is zero... if there is just one year with a zero, it's all over'; 'throughout history, it is leverage that wipes people out'; 'there only has to be one day you cannot meet a margin call.' Buffett cites LTCM (25x net worth), Gen Re post-9/11 (collateral calls on shrunken capital), and GEICO's $94M loss on $72K of premium as the failure mode. For V8: leverage is capped so a worst-case gap/cascade/liquidation move cannot breach the wipeout boundary; 'you cannot farm-out risk management.'
findings.trigger_invalidation: Standing constraint; it binds only when sizing and leverage decisions are being made, and it is the reason Buffett accepts lower returns ('Why expose the company to ruin and disgrace for an extra percentage point of return?').
findings.risk_geometry: Position size and leverage capped so a maximum-adverse-excursion scenario cannot force liquidation; keep a reserve so a forced-seller moment finds you with dry powder, not under margin.
findings.quote: Anything times zero is zero. No matter how good the record was in every other year, if there is just one year with a zero, it's all over.
findings.chapter_anchor: 2007 'Stewardship: Brains Plus Caution'; 2004 'Last Man Standing'
findings.notes: Directly supports V8's no-leverage core simulator and the RiskGate heat cap; implies a stress-scenario check (max adverse excursion under cascade) as an admission gate on every candidate episode.
findings.book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

findings.strategy_name: Be Greedy When Others Are Fearful (sentiment-extreme contrarian)
findings.mechanism: extreme sentiment marks price far from value because the herd's emotion, not economics, drives the extreme; fading the extreme reverts when the emotional driver exhausts
findings.setup_summary: Take the opposite side of emotional extremes: 'be fearful when others are greedy and greedy only when others are fearful'; Buffett and Munger bought through every crisis (2008, 2002 junk, 1974) while 'euphoria prevails' marked the tops. In perp crypto the measurable extremes are deeply negative funding, capitulation volume, flushed open interest, and record-low sentiment - a contrarian long setup that should be validated against the existing capitulation backlog family.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The extreme does not revert while the reason for fear remains fundamentally valid - distinguish a liquidity/sentiment flush (tradeable) from a genuine thesis break (not tradeable); Buffett's 2008 muni dislocation reverted, the subprime mortgage decline did not.
findings.risk_geometry: No stop given by the book; the margin of safety substitutes for a tight stop, so the setup requires the price-vs-value gap to be large before the extreme is faded.
findings.quote: We simply attempt to be fearful when others are greedy and to be greedy only when others are fearful.
findings.chapter_anchor: 1987 'On the Market' (annual-report quote); 2008 subprime/crisis commentary
findings.notes: Reuses starter slug sentiment_extreme. Corroborates the DATA_BLOCKED capitulation backlog family (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion); proposed behavior_family_candidate extreme_fear_reversal. Note: sentiment is not in the V8 feature-group vocabulary, so it must be proxied through participation/liquidity/flow features (volume climax, flushed OI, funding).
findings.book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

findings.strategy_name: No Cost-Basis Anchoring (the stock does not give a damn)
findings.mechanism: the market outcome is independent of the price you paid, who recommended it, or your entry reference; anchoring hold/exit decisions to cost basis or P&L produces irrational continuation of losing exposures
findings.setup_summary: Exit and hold decisions must be functions of the thesis and the market, never of entry price or unrealized P&L: 'a stock does not know you own it, the price you paid, who recommended it, the prices someone else paid... the stock does not give a damn.' 'You do not have to make it back the way you lost it' - do not extend a losing exposure to claw back a loss (the USAir preferred write-down).
findings.trigger_invalidation: The rule itself is the guardrail: a position whose thesis is dead must exit regardless of whether P&L is negative or positive, and a position whose thesis is alive must be held regardless of how good the entry looks now.
findings.risk_geometry: Stop and target are derived from structure and thesis, not from entry price; dead-thesis (still_valid) exit is computed independently of unrealized P&L.
findings.quote: A stock does not know you own it, the price you paid, who recommended it, the prices someone else paid . . . the stock does not give a damn.
findings.chapter_anchor: 1995 'Stocks' (USAir write-down: 'you do not have to make it back the way you lost it')
findings.notes: Directly supports V8's separation of the stop exit from the dead-thesis (still_valid) exit and mandates that lifecycle exit conditions never reference entry price or P&L.
findings.book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

findings.strategy_name: The Past Is Not Prologue - Anti-Extrapolation of Historical Statistics
findings.mechanism: historical statistics, especially recent historical performance, are a weak basis for projecting future edge because the conditions that produced them do not persist; reliance on the past rewards correlation, not causation
findings.setup_summary: 'If investors only had to study the past, the richest people would be librarians.' 'The danger of relying on historical statistics or formulas is that you end up betting on a 14-year-old horse with a great record but now ready for the glue factory.' Munger: 'It's stupid the way we extrapolate the past. Not just stupid, massively stupid.' For a research program: a backtested edge is a hypothesis, not a fact - it must survive frozen out-of-sample and regime change, and the recent past is the least reliable window to project from.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not an episodic setup; it is the discipline that any in-sample-validated pattern be treated as provisional until it survives frozen OOS and an unseen regime.
findings.risk_geometry: None - this is an evaluation-protocol constraint, not a trade geometry.
findings.quote: If investors only had to study the past, the richest people would be librarians.
findings.chapter_anchor: 1989 'Past Is Not Necessarily Prologue'; 1993 'Value Investing: A Mispriced Gamble'; 2001 'Extrapolating the Past: Massively Stupid'
findings.notes: Fully consistent with V8's evidence-bound constitution: frozen OOS, challenger-versus-frozen-baseline evolution, no in-place learning. Methodological support for treating any backtested edge as falsifiable, and for discounting extrapolations of the recent bull/bear window.
findings.book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

findings.strategy_name: Opportunity-Cost Selection (every trade competes with the best alternative; omission is the biggest cost)
findings.mechanism: each commitment is justified only if it beats the best available alternative; mediocre opportunities are costly because they consume the capacity to act on great ones, and the largest cost is failing to act on an understood high-conviction idea ('thumb-sucking')
findings.setup_summary: 'Life is a whole series of opportunity costs' - 'to measure opportunity cost, take your best available opportunity versus all other options.' In trading, with one exposure per direction, every candidate episode competes and only the best fills the slot; a filled slot must beat the next-best idea (rank by expected value). Symmetrically, errors of omission dominate: Buffett stopping Wal-Mart at $23 cost shareholders $10B; Munger's Belrich Oil refusal cost $200M. Not acting on a high-conviction understood setup is the most expensive mistake.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Standing selection discipline; it binds at every admission decision and every capacity allocation.
findings.risk_geometry: Capacity discipline is the mechanism: one active exposure per direction makes the next-best idea the explicit opportunity cost of filling the slot.
findings.quote: Life is a whole series of opportunity costs.
findings.chapter_anchor: 1997 'Filters' (Opportunity Cost); 2006 'Opportunity Cost'; 2001 'The Biggest Mistake: Opportunity Cost'; 2004 'Errors of Omission'
findings.notes: Supports V8's one-exposure-per-direction rule as a selection engine: the next-best candidate must be scored and compared, and 'understandable risks properly priced without undue aggregation; the ability to say no is crucial' (2002) is the same selectivity principle for the RiskGate.
findings.book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

findings.strategy_name: Circle of Competence - In / Out / Too Hard
findings.mechanism: edge exists only inside a known perimeter; classifying most ideas as 'too hard' concentrates effort where genuine understanding exists and avoids 'seven-foot bars'
findings.setup_summary: Maintain an explicit in/out/too-hard classification: 'there are three boxes - in, out and too hard.' Buffett's five-minute acquisition answer comes from pre-built filters plus a strict perimeter; 'a large part of his success has come from knowing how to recognize and step over one-foot bars and to recognize and avoid the seven-foot bars.' For V8: a behavior family is formalized only where the causal mechanism is specifiable as a falsifiable hypothesis; 'too hard' is a legitimate disposition (registry status) for behaviors that cannot be turned into an executable expert.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Not an episodic setup; it is the perimeter rule that governs which behaviors may become experts at all.
findings.risk_geometry: None.
findings.quote: There are three boxes--'in,' 'out' and 'too hard.' It is important to know what is too hard for you and stick to what you do best.
findings.chapter_anchor: 2006 'In/Out/Too Hard'; 1993 'Key to Successful Investing' ('stay within your circle of competence (and know where the perimeter is)'); 2007 'Buying Businesses'
findings.notes: Supports V8's registry discipline (PROPOSED->FORMALIZED->...->REJECTED) and the rule that 'too hard' behaviors are not forced into experts; formalize only behaviors with a coherent, specifiable mechanism.
findings.book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

findings.strategy_name: What vs. When - No Macro Timing
findings.mechanism: predicting which side of an edge wins (the 'what') is tractable; predicting the timing of market swings (the 'when') is not - 'we're predicting how people will swim against the current. We're not predicting the current itself.'
findings.setup_summary: Buffett and Munger refuse market-timing and macro forecasts ('you can't dance in and out of businesses based on forecasts'), keep cash as a default option when nothing is cheap, and concentrate on individual opportunities. 'To think about what will happen versus when is a far more efficient way to behave.' For V8: regime filters and macro-timing components should stay absent by default; edge hypotheses are conditional on observable microstructure, not on forecasts of the direction or timing of the market.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Standing design constraint - it excludes an entire class of components (market-timing and regime-forecast models) rather than defining an episodic trigger.
findings.risk_geometry: Cash is the default option when no asymmetric setup exists; there is no obligation to hold a position in every regime.
findings.quote: We're predicting how people will swim against the current. We're not predicting the current itself.
findings.chapter_anchor: 1992 'On Market Timing'; 1988 'On Predicting Business Cycles'; 1994 'What vs. When'; 2005 'Be Out of Step' ('Berkshire does no asset allocation')
findings.notes: Consistent with V8's default-absence of regime filters. Counterpoint to keep honest: in crypto, funding/positioning data makes some regime state observable at the microstructure level - but the book's lesson is that predicting market direction/timing is not where edge lives.
findings.book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

findings.strategy_name: Volatility Is Not Risk (risk is probability of permanent loss, not price variance)
findings.mechanism: risk is the probability of permanent loss of capital, not the size of price jiggles; measuring risk by beta/volatility misprices lumpy opportunities and teaches the wrong stop behavior
findings.setup_summary: 'Volatility is no measure of risk to us' - Buffett buys farmland after a 70% price collapse (which beta theory would call maximally risky) and writes supercat insurance that loses in a given year but wins over a decade; a lumpy 20-80% return is not riskier than a smooth 5%. Real risk is the nature of the economics and 'not knowing what you're doing' - the probability and size of thesis failure, not variance. For V8: risk gates should be driven by scenario loss of capital (thesis death, liquidation) rather than by volatility alone; volatility may size a position but should not be the definition of risk.
findings.trigger_invalidation: Standing philosophy; it binds when risk measures and stop sizing are designed.
findings.risk_geometry: Size by worst-case scenario loss of principal, not by volatility-scaled distance alone; a stop may be wide (structure-based) while the position remains small in scenario-loss terms.
findings.quote: Volatility is no measure of risk to us.
findings.chapter_anchor: 1994 'Modern Portfolio Theory Described'; 2007 'Comments on Risk'
findings.notes: Design principle for the RiskGate: in perp crypto the true tail risk is liquidation and thesis death, not ATR-sized wiggles; V8 should separate volatility-based position sizing from permanent-loss-based risk admission.
findings.book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

findings.strategy_name: Line of least resistance regime gating
findings.mechanism: trade only in the direction of the dominant market trend; stand aside in cash when the market is consolidating sideways
findings.setup_summary: First classify the market regime from price structure on a multi-bar/swing horizon: uptrend, downtrend, or sideways consolidation. Take longs only when the line of least resistance is up, shorts only when it is down; when the market is sideways, hold cash and wait for a clear direction to establish. Entry comes only after the trend is visible in price action, never in anticipation.
findings.trigger_invalidation: No trade is taken while the market is sideways and undecided; a position's thesis dies if the regime classification flips against it (trend breaks).
findings.risk_geometry: No explicit stop/target stated for this rule; risk is controlled by refusing to trade against the regime plus the separate 10% per-position loss cap.
findings.quote: Always evaluate and appraise general conditions first, and determine the line of least resistance. Is it an upward-trending market or a downward-trending market? Or is it consolidating—moving sideways, trying to make up its mind?
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 3 'The San Francisco Earthquake Rumbles in New York' (pp. 53-54); codified as rule 1 in Ch. 4 'The Crash of 1907' (p. 66)
findings.notes: Maps to V8's absent-by-default regime filter: it enters only through a registry experiment beating the simpler baseline on frozen OOS, never as a permanent gate. For BTCUSDT 1h the up/down/sideways classification is directly computable from OHLC structure with no lookahead.
findings.book: Jesse Livermore - World's Greatest Stock Trader 2001

findings.strategy_name: Probe-and-confirm pyramiding (position scaling on confirmation)
findings.mechanism: build a pre-planned position in tranches, adding size only after price confirms the thesis by moving in the intended direction
findings.setup_summary: Before the first trade, fix the total intended position size. Enter 20% as a probe; add the next 20% only if price moves in the intended direction (proof the judgment is correct), another 20% at a further-extended confirming level, then after a normal countertrend correction holds at the prior add level take the final 40%. If the probe moves against you, close it or wait; never sustain a loss above 10% on the position.
findings.trigger_invalidation: An adverse move after any tranche invalidates the confirmation: no further adds until the price again confirms; the probe itself is cut or frozen rather than averaged down.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: staged tranches (20/20/20/40%) at successively confirming prices (higher for longs, lower for shorts); stop: 10% against original purchase price; target: ride the swing, no fixed R-multiple; expiry: none stated, position held while trend holds.
findings.quote: The first probe or transaction is crucial; it is the key to this technique. After the first transaction, do not make a second until you have confirmed that your judgment is correct.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 4 'The Crash of 1907' (pp. 64-65)
findings.notes: The inverse rule is stated in Ch. 5 (Cotton King): Livermore's $2.7M loss came from dollar-averaging DOWN into losing cotton instead of cutting it - i.e., adds are only permitted on confirmation, never against the thesis. V8's rule 16 (one active exposure per instrument/direction) and complexity budget mean this lands as lifecycle/methodology scaling guidance, not a new active expert.
findings.book: Jesse Livermore - World's Greatest Stock Trader 2001

findings.strategy_name: 10% per-position hard stop
findings.mechanism: a fixed percentage of the original purchase price is the maximum tolerable loss per position, enforced mechanically regardless of the position's story
findings.setup_summary: Any long or short position is closed if it loses more than 10% against the original purchase price, unconditionally - even if the underlying judgment later proves right. Livermore framed this as his lifelong bucket-shop inheritance: all he ever wanted to lose in any one stock is ten percent.
findings.trigger_invalidation: The cap is unconditional; the rule itself has no invalidation. Livermore's catastrophic losses (e.g., holding losing cotton) came precisely from breaking this rule.
findings.risk_geometry: Entry: any; stop: fixed 10% of original purchase price (not ATR-scaled, not swing-point); target/expiry: not specified by this rule.
findings.quote: All I ever want to lose in any one stock is ten percent... If he lost more than 10 percent against his original purchase price, then he covered his position.
findings.chapter_anchor: Ch. 2 'The Back Story' (pp. 33-34); restated in Ch. 3 'The San Francisco Earthquake Rumbles in New York' (p. 56)
findings.notes: On BTCUSDT 1h a fixed 10% price stop is roughly 7-20 ATR units depending on regime - very wide next to V8's 1R ATR-based stops, and the leverage of perps multiplies the account impact. The structural lesson (deterministic per-position loss cap, enforced even when the thesis is 'right') transfers to RiskGate; the 10% constant needs regime-aware recalibration, not blind adoption.
findings.book: Jesse Livermore - World's Greatest Stock Trader 2001

findings.strategy_name: Ride the big swing; sell the loser, keep the winner
findings.mechanism: expected value concentrates in long-trend continuation; banking small profits early and funding losers by cutting winners destroys the edge
